english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu haa mi-aduawai lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning gives the plant roots time to soak up moisture before the sun gets too hot, preventing the water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛmuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ tsɔ. Enɛ ji koni nu akatsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water sits on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, so when water covers the land for too long, the roots drown and soil germs easily make them decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu ha he ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under harsh sun, so fast-growing plantain leaves act as natural umbrellas that provide shade and keep the air cool for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, plantain tso lɛ baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding underneath and sucking out the plant's juice, or that a disease has entered the leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites, kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi ni amɛmiinu tso lɛ nu. loo hela yɛ baai lɛ amli

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water, because it tries to save its energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato baajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ejaakɛ eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and crooked in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand downward under the ground, so if the soil is hard and packed, the tuber cannot easily push through and gets bent or stops growing big.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni ebaanyɛ ebɔle loo ekpa dalɛ.

english: Plantain roots do not go deep into the soil, so when the tree bears a heavy bunch of fruit, the top becomes heavy and wind can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo lɛ, Yiteŋgbɛi lɛ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted to quickly snatch up water and soil food before domesticated farm crops can even get started.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe oya koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ dani okwaayeli nibii ni akɛwoɔ shia lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves are thin and delicate. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them from heat and help them retain moisture until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ naa ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves from drying out.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely rich soil without balanced nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves on top instead of storing starch in its roots below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: High daytime temperatures or sudden dry spells stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to conserve water and energy rather than trying to nourish new fruit.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomatoi lɛ aba amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai heei lɛ aná hewalɛ

english: Why do my yam seeds take so long to sprout after I plant them in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. They will not sprout until this internal biological clock finishes, regardless of how much water or soil you give them.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Amɛkwɛŋ kɛyashi nɛkɛ mligbɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ baagbe naa. Ekɔɔɔ he eko nu loo sũ babaoo ni okɛbaahã lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants curling up and showing small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and tiny holes are usually caused by fall armyworms or heat stress. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss, while pests feed on the tender central shoots inside.
ga: Baai kɛ buji bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fall armyworms loo heat stress. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mligbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my hot pepper leaves roll inwards and stay small instead of spreading out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in peppers is often a reaction to tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus spread by them, which disrupts the leaf's normal growth tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni gbalaa fãji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ mli

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. Without wooden prop poles or windbreaks, heavy fruiting bunches and wet soil make them top-heavy and easy to blow down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji tso tso loo kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne ko bɛ Yibii akui ni tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baaha amɛfee tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa amɛ shi oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I do not harvest them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers reach full maturity, extra moisture in the soil and naturally occurring soil fungi begin breaking down the stored starch, causing root rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli baa lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ ŋmei ni ato lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my next crop of maize grow greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the legumes die, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei gboi Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Is it safe for me to cut my plantains in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo plantains yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to cut plantains in the cool early morning or late evening. Harvesting during the hot afternoon causes the fruits to heat up, lose moisture rapidly, and spoil much faster before reaching the market.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo plantain lɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adɔ. Efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya Ni efiteɔ oya kwraa dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is mature enough to harvest for the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛha jara?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits look full, plump, and lose their sharp corners or ridges, becoming rounded.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko jeɔ kpo akɛ eyi obɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshishigbɛ loo eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ elaaje koni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Where should I store my harvested plantains on the farm while waiting for buyers?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ ato yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: You should store harvested plantains in a cool, shaded area, such as under a tree or inside a thatched shed. Keep them raised off the bare soil on dried leaves or wooden pallets to prevent rot and sunburn.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, tamɔ tso shishi loo jwɛi tsũ ko mli. Wo amɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ tso nɔ. Enɛ ji koni akafite kɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do my plantains ripen and turn yellow so quickly after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a plantain is cut, it naturally produces a ripening gas called ethylene. Heat speeds up this process, so keeping the cut plantains cool slows down the gas and keeps them green longer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo plantain lɛ Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ baa. Dɔlɛ haa nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha plantains ni afo lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni gas lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I cover my cut plantain bunches with leaves after harvesting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ baai aha mi-plantain ni mifo lɛ he yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, covering harvested plantains with loose leaves protects them from direct sunlight, reduces heat buildup, and stops the fruit skin from getting sunburned and scorched.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ baai ni etse ehe lɛ tsu nii ni akɛha plantains ni akpa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha dɔlɛ ni abua naa lɛ aba shi ni otsi aduawai ahewolo lɛ naa koni hulu akashã ni ekashã

english: Does dropping or rough handling damage my cut plantains even if the skin does not tear?
ga: Ani efiteɔ mi plantain ni afo lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ehewolo lɛ etseee moŋ?

english: Yes, rough handling bruises the flesh inside the skin. Bruised areas turn soft, turn black quickly, and lower the price buyers at the depot will be willing to pay.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ. ha fãji ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ He ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. fast black ni ekɛ jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ nitoohe lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I keep my plantains from getting ruined when transporting them to distant markets like Kumasi?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi plantains lɛ anaa koni akafite beni mikɛyaa jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tamɔ Kumasi lɛ?

english: Stack the bunches carefully on soft bedding, such as straw or dry leaves, in a well-ventilated vehicle. Transporting them during the cooler night or early morning hours prevents thermal damage.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo saatso ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ tsɔne ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli Kɛ́ otsi ohe yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo akafite nii.

english: Will a plantain variety that performs well in Kumasi also do well on my farm in another region?
ga: Ani plantain henɔi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Kumasi lɛ hu baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ?

english: Most Ghanaian plantain varieties perform well across the forest zones, provided your field has fertile soil, adequate rainfall, and good protection against strong winds.
ga: Ghana dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa. ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I encourage my plantain trees to produce bigger and heavier bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi plantain lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo jwɛi wuji ni tsii?

english: To get larger bunches, prune away extra suckers so only two or three stalks grow on one stem mat, and apply compost or manure regularly to feed the crop.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná kuu agbo lɛ, Kpãa ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli koni ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ ahi ŋmeii kome nɔ. ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii daa kɛye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain tree turn yellow and dry up before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Early yellowing of leaves is usually caused by leaf spot diseases or lack of water and nutrients. Healthy green leaves are necessary to feed the plant so the fruit bunch can grow fully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hela loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ mra. Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ he miihia waa yɛ tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ mli bɔni afee ni aduawai akui lɛ anyɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning yellow and dry up during the August dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ August mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the mid-year dry spell in August, the drop in rainfall makes it hard for plants to absorb nitrogen from the soil. Without enough water and nitrogen, the lower leaves turn yellow as the plant tries to save energy.
ga: Yɛ afi ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ August mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato he lɛ.

english: How does heavy rain in the wet season affect my flowering yam crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ saa sweet potato tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain during flowering can wash away pollen, prevent proper tuber formation, and waterlog the soil, which leads to root rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen lɛ. Etsiɔ yitso ni feɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu Enɛ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantains next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantain yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso hee lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that create living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field where I grown maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This naturally enriches the soil, giving your maize free nutrients to grow taller and produce larger ears.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha o-corn nutrient free lɛ ada ni ehiɛ toi wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden change in temperature. Regular watering during hot periods helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo dɔlɛ tsakemɔi trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What makes the leaves of my tomato plants curl upwards during the day?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism tomato plants use to protect themselves from losing water during intense afternoon heat, or it can be a sign of sap-sucking insects like whiteflies.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ ahe okadi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong storm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. When heavy fruit bunches form and rain softens the ground, strong winds easily pull the roots out of the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai babaoo feɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why does the ground in my farm become very hard and cracked after rain stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa beni nugbɔ ekpa enɛ gbii komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or compost. Organic matter acts like a sponge, keeping the soil loose and helping it hold moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your young plants desperately need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei, ni ebaaju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: How can I tell underground crops like cassava are ready for harvest without digging everything up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni mifooo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli?

english: Cassava is generally ready when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, the main stem turns brown, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the dirt where roots cannot reach it, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps turn the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Which way should I point the stem cutting when I am planting cassava in my field?
ga: Kɛji oodu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, nɛgbɛ esa akɛ atsɔɔ ŋmei ni akɛfoɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small raised buds or 'eyes' on the cassava stem stem stick. These buds must point upward toward the sky so the shoots can grow up easily into the air instead of struggling inside the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bumps loo ‘buds’ ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli mlɛo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers that end up falling off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi egbeeɔ shi ni edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without making pods if the tree lacks water, if tiny pests like mirids attack them, or if there are not enough beneficial insects in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ Mirids tutua amɛ, loo kɛji kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the internal water channels inside the plant stem. Rotating your field with non-vegetable crops like maize helps starve and clear the bacteria from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee aduawai tamɔ ŋmãa tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, ehaa hɔmɔ baa shi ni ejieɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Do my yam plants really need tall wooden stakes to grow properly?
ga: Ani mi sweet potato tso lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines off the ground on wooden stakes lets the leaves catch direct sunlight and fresh air, which helps the plant generate the energy it needs to grow large tubers under the dirt.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ.

english: Should I cut away the small shoots that sprout up around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many young shoots causes them to fight the main tree for food and water. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain tree yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛwu amɛshi tso titri lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha niji agboi ni tsii aba dumɔwu titri lɛ nɔ.

english: How do plants like groundnuts and cowpeas make my farmland better for next season?
ga: Te tsei tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ aha midumɔ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is making the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by microscopic insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves and passing on viruses. Controlling these insects early with organic or recommended sprays stops the leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwieɔ mɔ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Is it safe to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is risky because the first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell. If the soil dries out before regular rains begin, the newly germinated seeds will dry up and die beneath the ground.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi dani nugbɔ nɛ daa Dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crops full access to the soil's nutrients so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why should I plant tree seedlings alongside my normal food crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ daa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ masɛi?

english: Trees help protect your food crops from strong winds, hold moisture in the soil, and improve soil fertility over time, giving you both seasonal food and long-term timber or fruit income.
ga: Tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oniyenii nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ shika ni onáa kɛjɛɔ tso loo aduawai amli be kakadaŋŋ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some crops grow well under heavy tree shade while others die out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like cocoa and ginger naturally prefer shade because their leaves handle lower light, whereas crops like maize and tomatoes need direct, full sunlight to generate energy and grow properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei sumɔɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ la fioo pɛ shɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes timber trees grow straight and tall instead of growing short and bushy?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ daraa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ shi moŋ fe kukuji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji?

english: Trees grow straight and tall when they compete with nearby trees for sunlight, which pulls them upward, and when low side branches are regularly pruned during early growth.
ga: Tso lɛ daa linear ni ekwɛɔ ŋwɛi beni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. ni baagbala tso lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛ be mli ni afoɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni edaa oya lɛ

english: Why do tree crops take many years to produce yield while food crops only take a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛduɔ nii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Trees spend their early years building deep root systems and strong trunks to gather water from deep underground, whereas food crops spend all their energy quickly on seeds and fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ kɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa ni akɛbuaa nu naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi niyenii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii oya yɛ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the crop is receiving either too much or too little water at its roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my newly planted seedlings are getting enough water during a dry period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Check the soil two inches deep around the base of the plant; if it feels dry and hard, or if the leaves start wilting and curling inward, the seedling needs deep watering early in the morning.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ 2 inches ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he kɛji enuɔ he akɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ baai lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni awo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu waa leebi.

english: How does leaving proper space between my plants help them grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Proper spacing stops plants from competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, and allows air to flow freely, which prevents leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ahe lɛ haaa amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni foliar helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it better to plant my crops immediately after the first rain or wait a bit longer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo ooomɛ fioo?

english: It is best to wait for the rains to become consistent so the seeds get continuous moisture to sprout and establish strong roots without dying from sudden dry spells.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa ni amɛgbooo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli.

english: How does following a planting calendar prevent my crops from failing?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔ kalanda ni mikɛnyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite?

english: A planting calendar aligns your land clearing, sowing, and weeding with local rainfall patterns, ensuring crops get water when they need it most and avoiding peak pest seasons.
ga: Kalanda ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ, ni aduɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ akpã gbee. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii náa nu yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ waa lɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ be ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he.

english: What guidelines should I follow when clearing land so I do not ruin the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi esa akɛ atsu he nii beni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni akafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Avoid burning all cleared vegetation; instead, leave slashed weeds to decompose as organic mulch, which protects soil organisms and keeps moisture in the ground for your crops.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei fɛɛ ni ajie lɛ ashãmɔ he. Mohu ɔ, a ngmɛɔ jwɛi nɛ a fo ɔ blɔ nɛ a puɛɔ nɛ a peeɔ jwɛi nɛ a peeɔ jwɛi nɛ a ngɛ mi ɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why are the young cocoa trees on my farm turning yellow and burning when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates living shade umbrellas that protect delicate cocoa leaves from burning while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together with my maize make my maize grow taller and greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpaaa gbee lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes collect nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ebuaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing tiny tubers underground even though the leaves above look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or get excessive nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing tall leaves instead of storing energy in the roots below ground.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen fa babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crop have ragged holes eaten into them almost overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ nɔ lɛ fee buji ni etse ehe lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the daytime and feed heavily on the leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and preventing fruit from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi yibii anaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit viruses to the crop, stunting its fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni kɛ hela lɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread across the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines must climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce large tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and improving tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha tuber yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when weather conditions get too hot or when water supply is irregular. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve moisture and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔi ahe.

english: Why should I avoid planting my crops immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell that can scorch fragile new sprouts. Waiting until the rains become consistent ensures the soil holds enough moisture for young seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the stems of my crops help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from evaporating soil moisture and protects plant roots from extreme heat.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho. ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their delicate leaves from harsh direct sunlight and retain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei adɛŋ. Koni akɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why does leaving cleared weeds on top of my field help my crops survive the dry season better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dead leaves or weeds, known as mulching, acts like a protective cover that keeps the soil cool and prevents moisture from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light green and yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the tips down when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off the plant without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, sudden dry spells, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to turn flowers into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Trukaa hulutsoo be Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔii afee aduawai lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the afternoon sun even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: On very hot afternoons, leaves release water faster than roots can draw it up from the soil, especially if the soil lacks organic matter that helps hold water near the roots.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ jieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does planting cassava stems at a slant make any difference compared to planting them straight up?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ko yɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant places more stem nodes under the soil surface, which encourages the plant to produce a higher number of heavy root tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava tsei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha stem nodes babaoo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ woɔ shishifãi babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant them on raised earth mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds loosen hard soil so plant roots can spread easily, improve water drainage so roots do not rot during heavy rains, and keep plant nutrients concentrated around the base.
ga: Gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ekwɛ tsei amli niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛbɔle shishitoo lɛ he

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat the inner leaves of my maize plants before the ears even show?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on young leaves and crawl deep into the leaf center where the tissue is soft and easy to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai bibii anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni fãji lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni eyeɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring nutrients that maize crops take away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ kɛtsu nii lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce smaller yields than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent crops for high yield, but the seeds harvested from them lose those high-yielding traits in the next generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant oil palm trees inside my cocoa farm to get extra income?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mu tsei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni maná shika kroko?

english: It is not recommended to plant oil palm near cocoa. Oil palm trees absorb a lot of water from the soil and create heavy shade, which weakens nearby cocoa trees and lowers your cocoa yield.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu mu tso yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo. Mu tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo be ni tsii baa. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni ehaa kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Which trees should I avoid planting close to my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You should avoid water-heavy trees like oil palm, as they draw large amounts of moisture out of the ground and block the light your cocoa trees need to stay strong.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ mu tsei, ejaakɛ amɛjieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛtsiɔ la ni he hiaa o-cocoa tso lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Is it better to keep my oil palm plantation separate from my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaagbala ŋmei ŋmɔji amli kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli?

english: Yes, you should always plant oil palm and cocoa on separate plots because oil palm competes aggressively for soil water and reduces cocoa productivity.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ odu mu kɛ kookoo yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mu tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni ehaa kookoo ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees drying up even when I plant them near other tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miiho lɛ? ni midu yɛ tsei kakadaji krokomɛi ahe lɛ

english: Certain tall trees draw away most of the underground water in the area, leaving the soil dry and causing neighboring cocoa trees to lose their strength.
ga: Tsei kakadaji komɛi gbalaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ babaoo kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni ehaa kokoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How do I know if another plant is stealing water from my cocoa soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei krokomɛi miiju nu kɛmiijɛ mi-kookoo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If a nearby crop takes up too much water, you will notice the ground around your cocoa drying out quickly and the cocoa trees becoming weak or losing vigor.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛ nu babaoo tsuɔ nii Obaayɔse akɛ he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Okookoo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni kookoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbɔjɔɔ loo amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do some crops stay green during dry times while nearby cocoa trees suffer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ naa amanehulu lɛ?

english: Some crops, such as oil palms, have strong root systems that pull available water from deep in the soil for themselves, leaving little water left for cocoa trees.
ga: Nibii komɛi ni aduɔ, tamɔ mu tsei, yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni gbalaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa cacao tsei lɛ.

english: Does too much shade from tall palm trees affect how my cocoa trees grow?
ga: Ani hulutsoo babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, heavy shade from trees like oil palms can block required light, and when combined with root competition for water, it makes cocoa trees weak.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo ni mli wa ni jɛɔ tsei tamɔ mu tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ la ni he hiaa waa lɛ naa. ni kɛ akɛ nu he akaŋshii ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ lɛ fata he lɛ Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why does the oil palm tree grow so tall and cast a big shadow on other plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛwoɔ tsei krokomɛi anɔ ŋmɔlɔ wuji lɛ?

english: Oil palm directs its energy upwards toward the sun as it grows, which creates a high canopy that casts heavy shade over crops underneath it.
ga: Mu tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo ni tsii baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: How does the way a tree grows affect the crops planted next to it?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni tso ko daa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ ahe?

english: Trees that focus their energy on tall upward growth create broad shade and draw heavy amounts of water from the surrounding soil, which slows down neighboring crops.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara lɛ feɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni amɛjieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: What makes a mature cocoa tree lose its strength and stop producing well?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛkpaa yibii kpakpai womɔ?

english: A cocoa tree loses its strength when neighboring trees steal the moisture from its soil and block out the sunlight it needs to stay healthy.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛ́ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ju nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛtsi hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily and lose moisture fast. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains gives them the shelter and humidity they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa wɔɔhe kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cocoa trees very close to each other so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their tops block sunlight from reaching lower branches and their roots fight over nutrients, resulting in weak trees and smaller overall yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cassava right next to my young cocoa seedlings to get food while waiting for cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ cacao tsei bibii ahe koni maná niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava has large, aggressive root systems that suck heavy nutrients and moisture from the soil, which will starve and stunt young cocoa trees. Plantains or cocoyams are safer intercrops because they share soil better and provide good shade.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifã agbo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Plantains loo cocoa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ amɛjaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kpakpa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping many of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ baai babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves in hot, dry weather to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Maintaining shade trees and keeping soil covered with mulch helps slow down water loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Tsei ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo.

english: Why do many small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers but naturally drops most of them because it lacks the energy to carry them all. Lack of insect pollination or dry spell stress can also increase flower drop.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi bɔ ni eji lɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛbɛ fɔfɔi hewalɛ fɛɛ. Kplukai ni bɛ loo dry haomɔ hu baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they mature during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning low branches and clearing thick growth allows air and sunlight in to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Will cutting off lower branches from my cocoa trees reduce how many pods I harvest?
ga: Ani cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Pruning lower and overcrowding branches actually increases yield. It encourages the tree to direct food to healthy pod-bearing branches and improves airflow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi kɛ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii yaa niji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akaye tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: Why do weeds growing near the base of my cocoa seedlings slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Weeds have quick-growing roots that steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients right from your young cocoa trees, while also hiding pests that eat young leaves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ teeɔ.

english: Does riding a motorbike repeatedly along a narrow path close to my crops harm their growth?
ga: Okpɔŋɔ nɔ nyiɛmɔ shii abɔ Nyiɛmɔ gbɛ bibioo lɛ nɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni mibɛŋkɛɔ lɛ yɛ oshara kɛha amɛdalɛ?

english: Constant heavy traffic packs the soil tightly around tree roots, making it hard for rainwater and air to soak in, which can stunt the roots of nearby crops over time.
ga: Gbɛfaa babaoo ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akɛ amɛaabote mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my mature cocoa trees turning pale green even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Pale green leaves usually show that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen. Applying organic manure or balanced fertilizer helps bring back healthy dark green leaves and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun because their roots are shallow and leaves are delicate. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides protection from direct heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahewɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ fataa he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. As the maize grows, it pulls stored nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed new growth at the top, showing that the soil needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni ŋmãa lɛ da Ejieɔ nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋmãa hee ni eda yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I see small worms eating holes in my maize leaves early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli leebi?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the plant leaves during the hot daytime to escape heat and come out to feed on the tender leaves during the cooler morning and evening hours.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛjo hulutsoo be lɛ naa foi, ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛye baai bibii yɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why should I move my cabbage seedlings to the main field late in the afternoon instead of the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ cabbage dumɔwui lɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli shwane mli moŋ fe leebi lɛ?

english: Transplanting seedlings late in the day allows them to recover from root disturbance during the cool night. If planted under hot morning sun, the seedlings quickly lose water and can wilt or die from heat shock.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni haoɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ leebi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil moisture. The plant sheds its blossoms to survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking plant juices and spreading a leaf curl virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ baai lɛ ahe hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã

english: Cassava is usually ready 8 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil around the stem base as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crop to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and small or poorly filled cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni ehiɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Harvesting crops repeatedly without feeding the soil drains away its natural nutrients. Rotating crops like maize with beans or groundnuts, or adding compost, restores plant nutrients to the soil for better future yields.
ga: ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa shii abɔ Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ekɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hoɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii kpakpai wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops need different types of fertilizer at different times instead of just one type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ekome pɛ lɛ?

english: Just like humans need a balanced diet of different foods to grow strong, crops need different nutrients at different stages. They need Nitrogen early on to build green leaves, and Phosphorus and Potassium later to develop strong roots and heavy cobs.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii ni ja he hiaa adesai koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Niyenii srɔtoi he miihia tsei yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Nitrogen he miihia amɛ mra koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli. ni sɛɛ mli lɛ ehe miihia ni ená fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Can I spray liquid food directly on my pepper leaves, or does fertilizer always have to go in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ niyenii ni ji nu afɔ pepper baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be?

english: You can spray liquid fertilizer directly on the leaves. Crops can drink nutrients quickly through tiny pores on their leaves, giving them immediate food if the dry soil cannot transport fertilizer to the roots fast enough.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei baanyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ anɔ, ni enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya shishifãi lɛ amli oya bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does animal manure take longer to make my vegetables grow compared to chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi heɔ be babaoo dani aduɔ aduawai fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is like ready-made fast food that plants can drink immediately, while manure is slow-release food. Soil organisms must first break down the manure before plant roots can consume its nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii ni afee oya ni afee klalo ni tsei baanyɛ anu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Manure ji niyenii ni shwieɔ shi blɛoo. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ agbala ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ kɛ emli niyenii lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Groundnuts are special crops that extract nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which restores balanced nutrients to your soil naturally for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or water. When a plant feels hungry, it pulls food out of its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top so new growth can survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ hɔmɔ miiye amɛ lɛ Egbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni tsei heei ni eda lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: On hot afternoons, water evaporates from tomato leaves faster than the roots can pull moisture out of the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its pores and save water, usually recovering once temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ nu akafite. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant food. If the crop does not have enough energy or water, it sheds flowers to save itself.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ loo nu ni fa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni ekɛkwɛ ehe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains above them to act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops if there is enough sunlight on the farm for all of us?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha wɔ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds steal the balanced food and water stored in the soil before your crop's roots can reach them. They also overcrowd your plants and attract crop pests and diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni sa ni ato yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani tso shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Amɛhaa otsei lɛ hu eyiɔ ohe fe nine ni amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai.

english: Will I get more maize if I plant my seeds very close together in the line?
ga: Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for limited food, water, and light. This results in weak, thin stalks with tiny cobs rather than a healthy, high-yielding harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ niyenii, nu kɛ la fioo he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Mohu ɔ, o ma ná ngma nɛ hi nɛ e woɔ yiblii babauu.

english: How do I know when the rains are steady enough for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Do not plant after just the first heavy rain, as the ground underneath may still be dry. Wait until you get two to three consistent rains within a week so the soil stays moist enough to help seeds germinate and grow strong roots.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ pɛ. Ejaakɛ ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. Enɛ ji koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and curling up during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water in hot sun, and yellowing usually means the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Giving the crop water or applying fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and make food for the crop.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden sticks to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for sunlight to make energy for growing tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the dark ground into the sun and prevents soil-borne diseases from ruining the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ kɛha amɛ adebɔɔ mli tuber dalɛ. Ankɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli kɛjɛɔ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa hulu la mli lɛ haaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get enough water. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save its strength until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots near the soil surface. When heavy stems bear large fruit bunches, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi kuɔ we nɛ e kɛ zugba ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Kɛ́ tso lɛ tso lɛ tsii lɛ, ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya

english: Why does my land yield smaller harvests every year if I keep planting the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly sucks out the exact same nutrients from the soil every season until the ground becomes exhausted. Rotating different crops, like beans or peanuts, restores nutrients back into your land.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. be mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my pepper roots to turn soft and rot when heavy rain pools on my land?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Roots need air just like humans do. When water stands on the field for too long, it drowns the roots by blocking air, allowing fungi in the wet soil to attack and rot the root system.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi tamɔ adesai pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees like plantain or forest trees shields young cocoa leaves from scorching heat until the plants are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei lɛ to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first. By the time cassava needs more space, the maize is already harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Kɛ́ be lɛ shɛ lɛ, he ko babaoo he miihia ŋmei. Agbɛnɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my vegetable leaves more frequently during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-vegetable baa lɛ shii abɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects reproduce much faster when temperatures rise, and hot weather stresses crops, making leaves softer and easier for bugs to bite and feed on.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ oya waa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi bibii ni amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: I want to start planting cocoa, but people tell me I should plant plantain on the farm first. Why is that?
ga: Miisumɔ ni madu kookoo, shi mɔ ko kɛɛ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Mɛni he je nɛ e ba jã a?

english: Young cocoa shoots are very sensitive to intense heat. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and cool soil environment they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I plant maize on the same plot of land where I am growing young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ cacao tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with young cocoa is a good practice during the first season because maize grows quickly, provides temporary shade, and yields early food for your family while the cocoa develops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni oha oweku lɛ nibii ni baa oya be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Does cocoa grow better in direct, bright sunlight or under the shade of bigger trees?
ga: Ani kookoo daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ tsei wuji ashishi?

english: Cocoa plants prefer partial shade, especially during their early years. Constant direct sunlight scorches their young leaves and dries out the topsoil, which slows down crop growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo, titri lɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Hulu la ni yaa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why is it important to plant my plantains in straight rows instead of scattering them around the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu plantains yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every crop gets enough sunlight and root space, while making it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ ooonyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when planting them alongside other crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe?

english: Plantains need enough room for their large leaves to spread out without blocking too much sunlight from neighboring crops, so spacing them roughly 3 meters apart allows good air movement and light balance.
ga: Plantains he miihia he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛbaai wuji lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsiii hulu la babaoo naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi gbɛ ni miihe ashɛ mitai 3 yɛ tsei nɛɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni la lɛ hu ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize growing tall and thin without producing healthy cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and weak when it is planted too close together or under heavy shade because it is competing aggressively for sunlight rather than using energy to develop strong cobs.
ga: Abele daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛye hulu la he akaŋ moŋ fe hewalɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: Will growing plantains and maize together with cocoa wear out my soil quickly?
ga: Ani plantains kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afite oya?

english: Heavy feeders like maize and plantain draw nutrients rapidly from the topsoil, so while companion planting is beneficial, you must replenish the soil using organic manure or fertilizers to keep the land fertile.
ga: Nibii ni haa niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he moŋ, shi ehe miihia ni okɛ humus loo organic fertilizer awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time of year to start planting my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje kookoo dumɔwui ashishi?

english: You should plant cocoa seedlings at the beginning of the main rainy season so that the frequent rains help the young roots establish deep in the soil before the dry season arrives.
ga: Esa akɛ odu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli koni nugbɔ anɛ shii abɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa.

english: How can the government cocoa extension services help me as a beginner farmer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli lɛ kookoo he nitsumɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi akɛ okwaafonyo hee lɛ?

english: Cocoa extension officers offer technical guidance on correct planting distance, disease prevention, pruning techniques, and can connect you with certified seed sources and farm inputs.
ga: Cocoa extension nitsulɔi haa ŋaawoo yɛ gbɛ ni ja ni esa akɛ adu lɛ he. Helai atsimɔ he ŋaai ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ bo abɔ dumɔwui ahe jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ odaseyeli kɛ ŋmɔ mli saji ahe.

english: Should I rely on the advice of old local farmers in my community or wait for extension officers before I plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ okwaafoi onukpai ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ŋaawoo nɔ loo mamɛ extension officials lɛ dani madu?

english: Experienced local farmers understand the local soil and rainfall patterns, while extension officers bring scientific methods; combining traditional practical knowledge with extension advice gives your crops the best chance to thrive.
ga: Akutsoŋ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ nuɔ akutsoŋ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛjianɔtoi shishi. Yɛ be mli ni shweremɔ he nitsulɔi kɛ jeŋ nilee gbɛi tsuɔ nii Kusum nilee ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii kɛ shweremɔ he ŋaawoo ni akɛaafata he lɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I treat or coat my crop seeds with medicine before planting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa atsu dumɔwui ahe nii loo mikɛwo amɛhe dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ mli lɛ?

english: Coating seeds with protective chemicals or fungicides before planting shields them from soil insects, fungal decay, and diseases, allowing more seeds to sprout safely and grow into healthy plants.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ mɔ he loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Fungi, fitemɔ, kɛ helai yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning pale white instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: White or pale leaves on maize are usually a sign of nutrient deficiency, such as a lack of zinc or nitrogen in the soil, or damage from microscopic pests that prevent the leaves from producing food.
ga: Baai yɛŋ loo eyɛŋ yɛ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa, tamɔ zinc loo nitrogen ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do insects keep attacking my maize crops even after I spray chemical pesticides on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ moŋ?

english: Pests can become resistant if the same chemical is used repeatedly. Spraying at the wrong time or right before rain can also wash the medicine away before it has a chance to kill the insects.
