ga: Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni nyɛɔ ewuɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ tsofa lɛ he dani ená hegbɛ egbe kooloi bibii lɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight, well-spaced rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ, ni gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows gives every crop equal access to sunlight, water, and nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I protect my crop stalks from falling over when strong winds and heavy rain hit my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ashishifãi anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Moulding soil high around the base of your crop stalks—known as earthing up—gives roots extra support. Planting tall trees along farm borders also acts as a windbreak to protect your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ebɔle Otso lɛ shishitoo Ale lɛ hu akɛ grounding. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aye abua amɛ babaoo. Tsei kakadaji ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why do my crops easily catch rot and fungal sickness when hot sunny days are mixed with sudden rain showers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ, kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ futu mli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures combined with high humidity create the perfect breeding environment for fungal spores to bloom rapidly on wet crop stems and leaves.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ fɔmɔ oya yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes small insects to destroy my harvested maize after I put the dried grains into storage sacks?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ewo nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Storage pests like maize weevils hatch from tiny eggs inside the grain or crawl into sacks through small gaps. Properly drying your grains and treating them with approved storage dust keeps them safe.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa bibii amli. yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli Aloo okɛ ohe awo kotoku mli kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli. Kɛ́ ogbala odumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility and breaking pest cycles for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. ni ofo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so that the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the plants are actively growing and the soil is slightly moist, ideally early in the morning or late afternoon when heavy downpours are not expected.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tso lɛ miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ. Esa akɛ awo lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. ni akpaaa gbɛ akɛ ebaaha nugbɔ anɛ waa

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so the grains do not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmaa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, the husks open slightly, and the grains become hard with a visible dark layer at the point where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Kpoji lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe fioo. ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni anaa yɛ he ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if it rains continuously for over a month?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fe nyɔŋ kome?

english: When rain falls constantly, the soil becomes waterlogged and starves root systems of oxygen. This turns maize leaves yellow, stunts overall plant growth, and can cause roots to rot because they cannot breathe or absorb food properly.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ Ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbo ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow after weeks of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa otsii komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous heavy rain washes key plant nutrients like nitrogen out of the topsoil and drowns root tips. Without air and nutrients, the cassava plant pulls energy from its lower leaves, causing them to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ eshishi baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do white spots and mold appear on my crop leaves when the weather stays dark and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Fungi spread very fast in warm, moisture-rich conditions. When cloudy and wet days last for a long time without sunshine to dry the leaves, fungal spores land on the crop, multiply, and cause leaf spots, blights, and rot.
ga: Fuŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ latsaa babaoo mli. Yɛ gbii ni atatu kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu la bɛ ni baaha baai lɛ agbi Fungal spores lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe, amɛshwereɔ ni amɛkɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Will heavy rainfall wash away the fertilizer I put around my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Yes, excessive or heavy rain can flush chemical fertilizer below the depth where roots can reach or wash it entirely off the farm field. It is best to apply fertilizer in smaller amounts during moderate weather and gently cover it with topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛyashɛ he ni shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ shishi. loo okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ afɔ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko awo mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseee lɛ, ni okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aha nɔ blɛoo.

english: How can I stop water from settling and rotting crop roots in low areas of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa nu ni shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ tsei shishifãi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can dig narrow drainage ditches across your farm to channel standing water away from your crops. Planting crops on raised soil mounds or ridges also keeps sensitive roots elevated above waterlogged ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ mli nubu bibioo ko. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ koni okɛjie nu ni ekã shi kɛjɛ onibii amli lɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does enrolling in government programs like Planting for Food and Jobs help my farm?
ga: Nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi amli ni oookɛ ohe awo mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nitsumɔi Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Programs like Planting for Food and Jobs give farmers reduced-cost access to high-quality seeds, fertilizers, and training from extension officers, helping you achieve bigger yields and protect your crops against local stresses.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ niyenii ni aduɔ kɛ nitsumɔi Ehaa okwaafoi lɛ naa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsɔsemɔ kɛjɛɔ extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ yɛ be mli ni ebaa shika ni he hiaa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa yibii babaoo ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli haomɔi ahe.

english: Why should I buy subsidized seed bags instead of planting grain saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa lɛ kotoku ko yɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Subsidized seeds are specially selected and certified to grow stronger, produce larger yields, and resist diseases better than seeds saved from old crops, which gradually lose their strength and yield potential over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa lɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni ahaa amɛ odaseyeli koni amɛdara waa. amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ fe dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ tsei momo amli, ni fiofio lɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: Why are government-supported fertilizer bags cheaper than regular market prices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni maŋ nɔyeli lɛ kɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ jara waaa fe jara ni akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Government subsidies pay for a portion of the actual cost per bag to make plant nutrients affordable for farmers, encouraging proper soil feeding and boosting overall harvest production across the region.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ woɔ shika diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛwoɔ kotoku kome mli lɛ fã ko koni eha tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni okwaafoi baanyɛ ahé. Wo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa he hewalɛ. ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ he hewalɛ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without making fruits during long cloudy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ atatu be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food for flowering and fruit production. When sunlight is hidden by long rainy or cloudy periods, crops stretch upward to search for light, making them weak and unable to set grain or fruit.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. Beni hulu lɛ tsiɔ ehe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo atatu be mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛtao la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui loo ewo yibii.

english: Is it safe to harvest my corn or beans while it is still raining every day?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa ŋmãa loo ŋmãa be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lolo daa gbi?

english: Harvesting in heavy rain keeps grains wet, leading to rapid mold growth, rotting, and insect damage in storage. It is safer to wait for dry weather or use raised drying platforms under protective shelter immediately after harvest.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Ekɛ fungal lɛ daa oya baa. fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo okɛ nɔ ko ni awo nɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ atsu nii yɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a canopy, protecting the seedlings from heat and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantain ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before any pods grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed, but dropping too many flowers is usually caused by stress from dry soil, extreme heat, or lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and well-nourished helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. Shi bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli haomɔ, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni fa fe nine baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Why do some cocoa trees produce pods all year round while mine only bear fruit during the main rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Trees that bear fruit year-round usually have continuous access to soil nutrients and water, often through irrigation or shaded moisture retention. When a tree gets steady food and water, it does not stop flowering and fruiting after the primary rainy season ends.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa shĩa mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ ná niyenii kɛ nu daa Ekpaŋ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ naagbee sɛɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning dark brown or black and rotting before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shaded, and unventilated farms. Letting sunlight and air into the farm by trimming excess leaves and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from destroying the rest of your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekafite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough nutrients to grow healthy cocoa without buying expensive tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha manyɛ makwɛ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni miheee nibii ni jara wa ni akɛkaa hela lɛ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft, holds moisture without staying muddy, and has earthworms present. If your cocoa leaves look pale yellow or the trees grow very slowly, the soil is likely lacking nitrogen and other essential plant foods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa henumɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaaa efee muji Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo tso lɛ miida blɛoo waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ tsei ahe nibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is burning the bush before planting cocoa better than letting weeds rot on the field?
ga: Ashãa jwɛi lɛ dani aduɔ kookoo Ani ehi fe ni aaaha jwɛi lɛ agbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Slashing weeds and letting them rot on the field is much better than burning. Burning destroys helpful organisms in the soil and burns away natural organic food, whereas letting vegetation rot creates natural compost that keeps the soil rich and moist.
ga: Jwɛi ni aaafolɔ ni aha egbo yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi kwraa fe ni ashãa. Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni ekɛ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect my crops, and how can I protect my soil?
ga: Te Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture out of the air and soil, causing plant leaves to dry out and young pods to drop early. Covering the soil around the base of your crops with dry leaves or grass (mulching) locks in moisture and keeps the soil cool during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off branches from my cocoa trees when they are already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji amli be mli ni amɛhiɛ kã shi lolo lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni kookoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning removes non-producing branches and parasitic plants that suck energy away from the main trunk. It allows sunlight to reach lower branches and helps the tree focus all its food into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ loo afoɔ tsei lɛ ajieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii kɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni ená ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my new cocoa plants to make extra income?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ kookoo tsei heei ateŋ koni maná shika kroko?

english: You can plant food crops alongside young cocoa, but heavy feeders like cassava should not be planted too close to cocoa roots because they compete fiercely for water and soil nutrients. Plantains or food crops with shallow roots are safer options for young farms.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Shi kɛlɛ, kaadu tsei ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Plantains loo niyenii ni shishifãi bɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ kroko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔji bibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pluck my cocoa pods so the beans don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akafite?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvesting when their skin turns completely yellow or orange, depending on the variety. Plucking them green means the beans inside are undeveloped, while leaving them on the tree too long causes the beans inside to sprout and ruin.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Edamɔ tso lɛ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ Green plucking tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eshɛko lolo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise us to plant tougher crop varieties instead of the soft, common ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Tougher crop varieties are specifically bred to withstand harsh weather, pests, and poor soils, ensuring you still get a reliable harvest even when weather conditions get bad.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa oyaa nɔ onine shɛɔ nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli wa po.

english: Is there any real difference between growing a yellow variety of a crop and a white one?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko diɛŋtsɛ yɛ tsei ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, color differences often point to different nutrient levels. Yellow varieties usually contain higher amounts of natural vitamins like Vitamin A compared to white ones, even if both grow similarly.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ kɔlai amli lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ adebɔɔ mli vitamini tamɔ vitamin A ni fa babaoo kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔŋ henɔi lɛ ahe. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: How do I know if a crop variety that is popular overseas will grow well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko ni ehe gbɛi waa yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Not all foreign crops adapt well to local soils and hot sun. An extension officer can tell you if that variety has been tested locally and whether it is tough enough for Ghana's climate.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ tsei komɛi nyɛɛɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akɛɛ bo kɛji aka tsofai srɔtoi lɛ akwɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Ni ani ewa bɔ ni sa kɛha Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ?

english: What should I do if local buyers in my area refuse to buy yellow crop varieties because they prefer white ones?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ maŋbii ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kpoo akɛ amɛbaahe ŋmɔŋ henɔi ejaakɛ amɛsumɔɔ ŋmɔŋ henɔi?

english: You can teach local buyers about the health benefits and taste of the yellow variety, or look for alternative buyers and export markets where yellow varieties are in high demand.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsɔɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ safron henɔ lɛ he kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo ha lɛ. Aloo taomɔ mɛi krokomɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ jarayeli hei ni mɛi biɔ ŋmɔŋ srɔtoi babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do buyers in foreign countries seem to prefer yellow crop varieties over white ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔŋ henɔi fe ŋmɔŋ henɔi lɛ?

english: Consumers in foreign markets often associate yellow crop varieties with higher nutritional value and specific flavors that fit their cooking and eating habits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni yeɔ jara yɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔŋ henɔi ni yɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto ni sa amɛ nihoomɔ kɛ niyeli su lɛ toɔ he.

english: How can we get our local communities to accept and start eating new crop varieties that look different from what they know?
ga: Wɔbaahã wɔ akutsei lɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ ni amɛje ŋmɔshi nibii heei yeli shishi. Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ efee srɔto yɛ nɔ ni amɛle lɛ he?

english: Community cooking demonstrations and public awareness about the health benefits help people overcome their fear of new crops and build a habit of eating them.
ga: Akutsoŋ niyenii homɔ he nɔkwɛmɔnii kɛ maŋbii ni amɛleɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ gbeyeishemɔ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ahe lɛ nɔ kunim. ni okɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayeli afee su

english: Why should I consult an agricultural expert before buying seeds for the new planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nilelɔ ko dani mahe dumɔwui kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ?

english: Agronomists know which specific seed varieties match your soil type and weather, helping you avoid spending money on seeds that will fail to produce good yields.
ga: Agronomists le dumɔwui ni kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ henɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okafiteɔ shika yɛ dumɔwui ni wooo yibii kpakpai ahe.

english: Why is it a good idea to set aside a small portion of my land to test a new crop variety first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oooha he bibioo ko lɛ? mi lɛ koni maka tsei srɔtoi heei akwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Using a small training plot lets you learn how the crop behaves and how to care for it under your farm's conditions without risking your main source of income.
ga: Tsɔsemɔ shikpɔji bibii ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa okaseɔ bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni oookwɛ amɛ nɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishi. ni okɛ oshika jɛɛhe titri lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Do tougher crop varieties stay fresh longer after harvest than standard varieties?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni wa lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei srɔtoi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, tougher crop varieties often have stronger skins or firmer flesh, which helps them resist damage during transportation and stay fresh longer in storage.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni wa lɛ fɔɔ hewolo ni wa loo loo ni mli wa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ nɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ, ni amɛhiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Does the color of a crop variety change how resistant it is to sun and heat?
ga: Ani tso ko su tsakeɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛdamɔɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ naa lɛ?

english: While color itself mainly reflects nutrients, many yellow or darker varieties are intentionally bred alongside tough traits that help the plant tolerate strong sunshine and heat.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ su jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kpo titri moŋ, shi srɔtoi babaoo yɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo ediŋŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛná sui ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Can I plant plantain and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, growing maize and plantain together is a good practice. Maize grows quickly and can be harvested in a few months, while plantain takes longer to mature, allowing you to make full use of your land while waiting for the plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni plantain heɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni adu nii lɛ.

english: Why do officers encourage farmers to mix different crops on one field instead of planting only one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu ŋmɔ kome mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Mixing crops helps protect your farm against total loss. If bad weather or a specific disease affects one crop, the other crop can still survive to provide you with food and income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baabu oŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekafite kwraa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo hela pɔtɛɛ ko ye ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu baanyɛ ahi shi koni amɛha bo niyenii kɛ shika.

english: Why do destructive insects attack my farm less when I mix plantains with other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blighters fioo ko pɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ plantains futu tsei krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Mixing different types of plants creates physical barriers that confuse pests, making it much harder for specific insects to spread rapidly from plant to plant.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛfeɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni futuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa kooloi komɛi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ.

english: What is the difference between foreign or improved seeds and the traditional seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛ shishijee dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Improved or foreign seeds are developed to produce higher yields, grow faster, and resist common local pests and dry conditions better than traditional saved seeds.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo ni yɔɔ srɔto koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. edaa oya ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: Will foreign plant varieties grow well in my local soil?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mimaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Many foreign or improved crop varieties are tested to perform well in Ghanaian soil, provided they receive the right spacing, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Aka maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi babaoo loo tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ nɔ. Esa akɛ amɛná he ko ni sa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How many months does it take for improved maize to be ready for harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa ni asaa lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ?

english: Most improved maize varieties mature quickly, usually taking between 3 to 4 months from planting to harvest, depending on the specific variety.
ga: Abɛi ni atsake lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa oya. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli. Edamɔ henɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Adding manure or balanced fertilizer will restore nutrients and help plants grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titri, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How do large crops like plantain trees protect the soil around them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he?

english: Plantain trees have broad leaves that shade the ground, which reduces moisture loss from the hot sun and keeps the soil moist for surrounding plants.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: How can government initiatives like Planting for Food and Jobs assist me on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli nifeemɔi tamɔ niyenii ni aduɔ kɛ nitsumɔi baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Initiatives like Planting for Food and Jobs support farmers by offering access to subsidized quality seeds, affordable fertilizers, and expert advice from agricultural officers.
ga: Nibii ni afeɔ tamɔ niyenii adumɔ kɛ nitsumɔi ni afeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara waaa kɛ ŋaawoo ni he esa ni jɛ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ

english: Where can I safely buy high-quality improved crop seeds for my planting season?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mahe dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha midalɛ be lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: You can get genuine improved seeds from registered agricultural input dealers, district agriculture offices, or through official government farming support programs.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui ni asaa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Kpokpaa nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ loo kɛtsɔ nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil naturally. Rotating them with maize restores soil fertility so your next crop grows stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: What is making small holes in the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing center of young corn plants. Checking your field early and applying ash, neem extract, or safe pesticides directly into the plant center can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni sũ, neem mli nu, loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The best solution is to plant disease-resistant stem varieties recommended by agricultural officers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow big leaves and produce large yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa wuji kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily when exposed to direct, hot sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to survive on their own.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ,.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Consistent watering and balanced soil nutrients help flowers stay on and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients away from your plants. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks of growth allows your crops to consume those nutrients and grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ naa nakai niyenii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the early morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering in the early morning is best because the cooler temperatures allow the plant roots to absorb the water deep in the soil before the hot sun causes it to evaporate.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshwieɔ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I protect my cut yam tubers from rotting before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mifo lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dani madu?

english: Rubbing dry wood ash over the fresh cut surfaces of yam setts creates a protective barrier. This prevents fungal infections and rot in the soil, helping the setts sprout healthy leaves faster.
ga: Tso mli sũ ni egbi ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni afo ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he baa. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers if I want to expand my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni magbɛ mihe lɛ mli?

english: Plantain plants need plenty of room to stretch their leaves and roots. Spacing them about 3 meters apart gives each plant enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce heavy, healthy bunches.
ga: Plantains he miihia he ko babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Aaafee mitai 3 ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛyibii lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant is hungry for nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, or it is experiencing drought. Removing old yellow leaves helps the plant send its energy directly to the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen. aloo amɛmiikpe hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni egbɔ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots thin and woody instead of fat and full of starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ fɔ kɛ starch najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if the soil is too hard for them to expand or if the soil lacks potassium. Planting in loose, well-drained soil and harvesting at the right age keeps the roots soft and full.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa loo kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Ni kɛ́ akpa yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi bibii ni amɛye emuu.

english: How can I stop my cassava from rotting in the soil if I do not harvest it right away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa kɛji mikpaaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Cassava rots when water sits around the roots for too long. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots safe in the ground longer.
ga: Cassava fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale green and yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pale or yellow leaves on young maize are a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps the leaves turn deep green and make food for the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni eha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: What makes some of my maize cobs have empty gaps instead of full rows of corn?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Empty gaps on a cob happen when the maize flowers are not fully pollinated, often due to hot, dry weather or planting stalks too far apart. Planting maize in blocks rather than single rows helps wind carry pollen to every silk.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baa beni ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ eshɛko amɛhe kwraa lolo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. aloo dumɔ tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ Abele ni aduɔ yɛ blɔki mli moŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ pollen yaa siliki ŋmei fɛɛ ŋmei ŋmei mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before producing any pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding mulch around the base protects the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes black rotten spots at the bottom of my tomatoes, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or uneven watering. Watering your plants regularly and adding lime or organic manure to the soil prevents this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa. Nu ni oooha otsei lɛ daa ni okɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Is it good to plant maize and cassava together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together is a great practice. Maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving the space open for the slower-growing cassava to spread out and mature later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be lɛ mli sɛɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a new piece of land is fertile enough for crops before I clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko nɔ baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii dani mafo mli?

english: Look at the wild plants growing there; dark green, thick vegetation and earthworm activity usually mean good soil. If the soil feels soft and dark when you dig, it will support healthy vegetable and crop growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ, tsei ni eyi obɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii anitsumɔ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ duŋ beni otsuɔ nii lɛ Shikpɔŋ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai kɛ tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to protect their delicate leaves from heat while their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Can I plant plantains on the exact same land where I am growing my new cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is a great practice. The plantains grow fast to provide essential shade for the young cocoa while providing you with food and quick income before the cocoa yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Plantains lɛ daa oya koni ekɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa aha kookoo bibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii ni amɛnáa shika oya dani kookoo lɛ jeɔ shishi etsuɔ ​​nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage turn into pods due to limited soil nutrients, water stress, or a lack of small pollinating insects called midges.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii yɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi bibii ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ ni bɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick my coffee berries from the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kɔfe kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Coffee berries should be harvested only when they turn bright red or deep yellow. Picking green berries results in bitter beans, while leaving them too long makes them rot or attract pests.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa kɔfe yibii lɛ pɛ kɛji amɛtsɔ tsuru ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Berry eŋɔli ni oookpa lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛ́ oshi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi loo ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with huge leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into leafy top growth rather than storing energy in root tubers. Balanced soil nutrients are needed for good tuber development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ he miihia koni tuber kpakpa aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant maize on the same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil strips away specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛ mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can covering the soil with dry leaves help my food crops survive during hot dry spells?
ga: Te baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miniyenii tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plant roots with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—holds moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents the sun from drying out root systems.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ. (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa hulu la akagbi shishifãi lɛ

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid weather. Pruning dense branches and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and reduces moisture where the fungus thrives.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebaaha hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ hei ni ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Weeds compete aggressively with crops for nutrients, root space, and light. Even with plenty of rain, weeds steal the vital soil minerals your food crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii, shishifãi kɛ la, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Jwɛi hu juɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa oniyenii tsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I trim or prune old branches from my coffee trees when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji momoi ni jɛ mi-kɔfi tso lɛ mli lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa?

english: Pruning removes old, non-producing branches so the tree can direct its water and nutrients into growing fresh branches that produce more and larger coffee berries.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛya niji ni miida ehee lɛ amli, ni no baaha kɔfe babaoo aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build healthy leaves, or that heavy rain has flooded the ground and choked the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they feed the soil with natural nutrients that nearby maize needs to grow.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ dalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas to keep the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni eha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain leaves curl up to reduce the area exposed to direct heat, which stops the plant from losing too much water into the air during the dry afternoon.
ga: Akɛ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni he ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akajie nu babaoo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ shwane ni nu bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Extreme sun heat or unpredictable rainfall stresses tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than using nutrients to make fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do weeds in my garden cause my pepper plants to grow so small?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, root space, soil food, and water, effectively stealing the nourishment your peppers need to grow large.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, shishifãi, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ nu, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa o-peppers lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see chewed holes in my maize leaves early in the morning, but I cannot find the insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ ŋmãa baai amli leebi maŋkpa shi minaaa kooloi bibii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many leaf-eating pests, like fall armyworms, hide deep inside the plant stem or under the soil during the hot day to stay cool and only come out at night to feed.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ baai babaoo, tamɔ fall flukes lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei akui amli shɔŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ pɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specialized crop pests and diseases build up permanently in the dirt.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli daa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil too long after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Once soil dries up and bakes in the heat after heavy rains, buried cassava tubers get trapped in high temperatures and hard ground, which invites soil rot and bacteria.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ni la etswa lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Cassava shishifãi ni afu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ baa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I stored from last season fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds stored in warm or moist rooms lose their internal energy over time, or they may rot quickly in the ground if buried too deep where air cannot reach them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baafite amɛmli hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Aloo ebaanyɛ egbo oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: I saw strange spots on my crop leaves this morning, how do I know if it is a disease attacking my farm?
ga: Ŋmɛnɛ leebi nɛɛ mina he ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ko miigba miŋmɔ lɛ naa?

english: Look closely at the leaves: if the spots are spreading quickly, turning yellow or dark brown, or causing the leaves to dry up and fall, it is likely a fungal or bacterial disease. You should show a sample leaf to an agricultural extension officer to get the right treatment.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ: kɛji ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo eha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi Ekolɛ eji hela ko ni ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii kɛbaa. Esa akɛ ajie nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ atsɔɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What steps should I take immediately when I hear a warning that a crop disease is spreading in my district?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ minu kɔkɔbɔɔ ko akɛ tso hela ko miigbɛ eshwa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Inspect your farm daily for early signs of sick plants, clear out weeds that can host pests, and avoid sharing uncleaned farm tools or moving soil from affected farms to your clean land until you receive specific guidelines.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi kɛha tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe okadi mra. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ji shihilɛhe kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee ni okɛaaha lɛ he. aloo shikpɔŋ ni oootsi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni ena naagba lɛ mli kɛya he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he ni he tse lɛ kɛyashi onine baashɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so that it does not spoil on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ekafite yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and husks turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels become hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops yield very little food during harvest even when I plant them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii fioo pɛ ni miŋmɔ lɛ náa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Low yields usually happen because the soil lacks essential nutrients, plants are planted too close together, or weeds and pests are stealing water and sunlight from your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa ejaakɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni ooodu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ juɔ nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: I just harvested my cassava, how can I prevent it from rotting quickly?
ga: Mifolɔ ŋmei kɛkɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa koni ekafite oya?

english: Freshly dug cassava rots within a few days. To keep it from spoiling, leave it in the soil until you are ready to consume or sell it, or process it immediately into gari, flour, or dried cassava chips.
ga: Cassava ni atsa ehee lɛ Egbo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli koni ekafite Shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaaye loo obaahɔ̃ɔ. loo afee lɛ gari, ashikishaŋ loo ŋmei ni egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to dry and store my harvested grains so insects do not destroy them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ? Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii akafite nakai dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Dry your grains in the sun until they are completely hard and crack when bitten. Store them in clean, airtight storage bags (such as PICS bags) off the floor in a cool, dry room.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli aahu kɛyashi ebaawa ni ebaakumɔ kɛji mɔ ko ŋmɔ lɛ. Kɛto vacuum kotoku ni mli tse mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though there has been plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that your crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water is trapped around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa tso lɛ muɔ.

english: What causes my seeds to fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haaa midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if they are planted too deep in the soil, if insects eat them underground, or if the seeds were old and damaged.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Kɛji kooloi yeɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni efite.

english: How does clearing weeds early help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Te ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the food and space they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it important for me to rotate the types of crops I plant on my farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting different crops each season stops pests and diseases from building up in the soil and helps maintain soil fertility by balancing how nutrients are used.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ bɔ ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your trees are lacking nutrients like nitrogen or are being attacked by pests like mirids. Applying the right fertilizer and controlling pests helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ mirids miitutua lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. You can prevent it by clearing weeds, pruning thick branches to let in sunlight, and spraying recommended fungicides.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Fɔlɔmɔ tsei niji ni mli tse. koni eha hulu la lɛ akpɛ ni ekɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo mli.

english: Why are insects constantly damaging the flowers on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like mirids feed on tender shoots and flower buds, causing them to dry up before pods can form. Spraying recommended insecticides at the right time protects flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids yeɔ tsei bibii kɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi. Gbimɔ amɛ dani ŋmɔtɔi lɛ afee. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ be naa lɛ baabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots that cannot reach underground water during dry periods. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects seedlings from strong winds and direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he.

english: Why are my aging cocoa trees producing fewer pods than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni egbɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 20 years, soil nutrients wear out and the trees lose strength. Pruning old branches, applying fertilizer, or gradually replanting with high-yielding varieties helps restore harvest levels.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye fe afii 20 lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ, ni tso lɛ he waaa. Niji ni egbɔ ni aaafolɔ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, loo ni akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo baadu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to prune the branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overgrown branches, letting sunlight and air flow through the farm. This reduces disease spread and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ haa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do large shade trees help my cocoa farm over time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ eye ebua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees protect cocoa from harsh sunlight, reduce water loss from the soil, and drop leaves that decompose into natural plant food, helping cocoa trees live and produce longer.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni oshɛrɛ baai ni egboi lɛ oshwie akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds around my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Kakao ni ayeɔ daa?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your cocoa trees. Keeping the farm clean prevents this competition and stops dangerous pests from breeding near your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akaŋshii akafee nɔ ko, ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely, usually from green to yellow or red to orange. Harvesting at this point ensures the beans are fully developed and ready for good fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su tsake kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru kɛyaa akutu mli. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans after harvesting instead of drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli beni akpaa nii lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation removes the natural bitter taste in fresh beans and creates the rich flavor that cocoa buyers demand. Skipping fermentation results in low-quality beans that sell for a lower price.
ga: Fermentation jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii heei amli lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ aba. Kɛ́ afoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ, no haa ahɔ̃ɔ kɔfi yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: What is pollination, and how does it help my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa?

english: Pollination is when pollen is transferred from one flower to another so a pod can form. Without pollination, cocoa flowers simply dry up and drop off, leaving you with no cocoa beans to harvest.
ga: Pollination ji be mli ni ajieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli koni efee pod. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi. Enɛ haa obɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni obaakpa.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off because they were not pollinated. Cocoa trees rely on tiny insects like midges—or hand pollination—to move pollen, and unpollinated flowers are shed naturally by the tree.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Cacao tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ midges loo nine nɔ ŋmeii anɔ. koni ejie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi amli Ni fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does hand pollination actually work on a cocoa farm?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Hand pollination involves carefully taking pollen from a flower on a healthy cocoa tree and placing it onto the flower of another tree, ensuring that the flower gets fertilized and turns into a pod.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni ajie fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛkɛ ni ekɛma tso kroko fɔfɔi nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are tiny insects like midges important for my cocoa crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii he hiaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ?

english: Midges are natural pollinators that carry pollen from flower to flower while feeding. Keeping decaying plant matter on your farm gives them a place to breed, which helps pollinate your cocoa naturally.
ga: Midgees ji adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni kɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Tsei ni egboi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ haa amɛ hegbɛ ni amɛfɔ bii. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo kookoo lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Will doing hand pollination on my farm really increase my cocoa harvest?
ga: Ani nine ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha kookoo ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, hand pollination ensures that far more flowers develop into full cocoa pods than relying on natural insects alone, which directly increases the total weight of beans you harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii fe ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii pɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni okpaa lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens to my crop if I pollinate the cocoa flowers incorrectly or carelessly?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ tsuuu nii?

english: Cocoa flowers are very delicate. If you handle them roughly or apply pollen improperly, the flower will be damaged and die, wasting the potential pod and reducing your final yield.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa. Kɛji akɛ okɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo okɛ pollen tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baafite ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ haa pods lɛ laajeɔ ni naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: How does taking extra care during the flowering stage lead to more money for my family?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni akwɛɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua weku lɛ ni ená shika babaoo?

english: Proper flower care and pollination maximize the number of healthy pods each tree carries. More pods mean a larger harvest, which translates to more sacks of cocoa to sell at market for income.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ pollination baaye abua ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Pods babaoo tsɔɔ ŋmaa babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, abaahɔ̃ɔ kookoo kotokui babaoo yɛ jara nɔ koni ana shika.

english: Why does my cocoa tree blossom with hundreds of flowers, but only produce a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei yɛ fɔfɔi ohai abɔ shi aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: A single cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but in nature, less than 5 percent get pollinated. The tree drops all unpollinated flowers to save energy for the few pods that were successfully fertilized.
ga: Kookoo tso kome woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, nɔ ni shɛɛɛ amɛteŋ oha mlijaa 5 ji nɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe. Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi fɛɛ ni shwieee fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato fɔfɔi fioo ni awo mli momo lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for cocoa flowers to receive pollen?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ aná pollen?

english: Early morning is the best time because cocoa flowers open fresh at night, and pollen is most active and effective before the heat of the afternoon sun dries out the flowers.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ gbɛkɛ. Ni pollen tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ dani shwane hulu lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ egbiɔ.

english: Why do some of my tiny, newly formed cocoa pods turn shriveled and black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi ni afee ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. It happens when pods are poorly pollinated or when the tree does not have enough nutrients and water to support all the growing pods, causing it to drop the weaker ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Ebaa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni miida lɛ aye abua. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: When maize turns yellow from the bottom up in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen. The plant is taking food from its older leaves at the bottom and sending it to feed the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Tso lɛ miiye niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ni ekɛmiitsu nii koni eyaye baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central funnel or 'whorl' of the maize plant because it is soft, moist, and protected from the sun while they feed on the young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms, amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi loo ‘rings’ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he beni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off if the weather is too dry, if the soil lacks key nutrients, or if there are no tiny midge insects around to pollinate them. The tree naturally sheds flowers it cannot afford to feed to save energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Niyenii nibii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ, tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtao niyenii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots like oak trees; their roots stay close to the surface. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, the top becomes heavier than the shallow roots can hold, especially if tiny worms or rot have damaged the roots underground.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ oak tsei. Eshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ Yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsii fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii, titri lɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii. loo fitemɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains come late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the soil stays soaked with excess water, it squeezes out all the air, suffocating the roots and letting soft-rot bacteria attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu ni fa fe nine ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baami kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food, which is then sent down underground to build a large tuber. Staking lifts the vines into the sun and keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my maize rows steal nutrients away from the maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, legumes like cowpeas actually help your maize. Their roots work with special soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the soil instead of taking away food.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai krɛdɛɛi tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ niyenii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why does my soil feel hard and dry faster after planting the same crop on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni egbiɔ oya beni midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly wears out the soil's structure and drains the same specific nutrients. Rotating crops or adding organic matter keeps the soil sponge-like, helping it hold moisture and air.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ afite ni niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baafite. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hiɔ shi

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by tiny whiteflies that spread a virus, or by the plant trying to protect itself from extreme heat and drought by reducing the surface area exposed to the hot sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa loo tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do new hybrid maize seeds need more fertilizer than the traditional seeds I usually save from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa ŋmãa babaoo fe blema dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are bred to grow faster and yield much more grain than traditional seeds. Because they produce so much more, they act like heavy eaters and require extra nutrients from fertilizer to reach their full potential.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo fe blema dumɔwui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛwoɔ babaoo fe nakai. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii ni tsii ni amɛbiɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct, harsh sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil before their roots are strong enough to drink enough water. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains next to them protects them until they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point the cassava stick when I push it into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ŋmei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ mɛɛ gbɛ?

english: Yes, planting a cassava stem upside down slows down growth significantly or causes the plant to fail. You should always ensure the small buds or nodes on the stem are pointing upward toward the sky before planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, yucca tsei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ waa loo ebaaha tso lɛ afee shoo. Esa akɛ okwɛ koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ loo ŋmeii lɛ akafite. yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani adu

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main food plants need to stay green and grow. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting my maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away heavy nutrients from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Rotating your crops keeps the soil fertile naturally and stops crop diseases from building up.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaaa tsei ahe helai abua amɛhe naa.

english: Is it good to spread fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rain storm comes?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy rains will wash your expensive fertilizer away down the slope or into streams before your crop roots have time to soak it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist after rain, or when only light rain is expected.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ kɛjɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ loo kɛya faai amli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. aloo be mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant to feed. Spraying approved control products directly into the funnel early in the morning or late in the evening helps control them.
