ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni eye niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: This rot on the bottom of tomatoes is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots carry calcium steadily into the growing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato shishigbɛ fitemɔ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ calcium be fɛɛ be.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they could easily rot or catch diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking baaha baai lɛ akaya hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya loo hela aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my pepper plants even if I give the crop plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi-pepper tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food, root space, and sunlight away from your pepper plants. Clearing weeds regularly ensures all the nutrients in the soil go directly into making your pepper plants grow strong and produce good fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tso niyenii ni he hia, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eyaa tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa o-pepper tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn powdery and grow whitish mold inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ ebatsɔ powder ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize molds in storage because the grains were packed while they still had too much moisture inside them. Drying your shelled maize thoroughly under the sun on clean tarpaulins until the grains are very hard prevents mold and insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ toɔ ejaakɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni ajie lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gĩ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa kɛ kooloi bibii akafite onibii lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani maná nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room to form large, healthy tubers instead of many tiny roots.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni mli wa. Yɛ shishifãi bibii babaoo najiaŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and cannot survive harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from heat and keeps the soil moist until the trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I put a huge amount of chemical fertilizer on my crops all at once, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be kome mli. Ani ebaada oya fe nakai shii enyɔ?

english: No, giving crops too much fertilizer at once can burn their roots and ruin the crop. Crops take in nutrients gradually, so it is better to feed them in small, correct doses at different stages of growth.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo oŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Fiofio lɛ, tso lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aha niyenii bibii ni ja yɛ shweremɔ fã fɛɛ fã mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients without giving it time to recover. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the ears are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani toi lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which it needs to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the crop regain its color and strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to shed flowers to save water and energy. Supplying steady water at the root level and providing light shade helps them retain their blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into tight cups during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to reduce water loss under intense heat, but it can also mean tiny pests like thrips or mites are sucking the sap from under the leaves. Checking under the leaves helps identify if pest control is needed.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ la ni naa wa shishi lɛ aba shi. Shi ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji ehe miihia ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deeply tilled soil to expand downward easily. If the soil is too hard or stony, the tuber struggles to push through, resulting in small, twisted tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ wa akɛ aaatsɔ mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms destroy my entire maize field so quickly if I don't catch them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ kpata mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ oya nɛkɛ kɛji mimɔɔɔ amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworms hide deep inside the growing funnel of the maize plant where they eat continuously and multiply fast. Checking your field weekly allows you to spot and treat them before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyeɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni amɛshwereɔ oya lɛ. Otsi fɛɛ otsi ni oooyakwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa amɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do small whiteflies crawling on my cassava leaves cause the leaves to turn twisted and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mikɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ anɔ shwieɔ shi Haa baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Whiteflies carry the Cassava Mosaic Virus and pass it to the plant while feeding on sap. The virus damages the leaves so the plant cannot produce enough energy to grow large cassava roots.
ga: Whiteflies ji mɛi ni hiɛɔ ŋmei hela lɛ ni amɛkɛhaa tsei be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmei lɛ mli nu lɛ. Virus ni fiteɔ baai lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth and strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in dry weather as a survival mechanism to conserve water. Retaining shade trees and spreading dry leaves or straw as mulch around the tree base helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei ni akɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers heat stress or irregular watering. Providing shade during the hottest parts of the day and watering consistently keeps the soil moist so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Shade yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed, grow strong, and produce full yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii. amɛdara waa ni amɛha yibiiwoo ni fa

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking spreads the vine leaves out to capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight powers the leaves to make food, which the plant sends underground to grow large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ eshwaa koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. ni tsei lɛ tsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in flooded soil because water blocks oxygen from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does covering my soil with dry grass help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mulching baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass—known as mulching—acts like a blanket. It shields the ground from hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, keeps weeds away, and eventually turns into rich natural food for the soil.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya, ehaaa jwɛi akabote mli, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo jɛɛhe.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil. Beans and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring field fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest produce weaker crops than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strong traits in the next generation. Certified seeds are specially produced in controlled conditions to guarantee high yield and resistance to diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔ mli lɛ amli krɛdɛɛ koni eha yibii babaoo aba ni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves early in the farming season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Tiny holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by early pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Inspecting crops early allows you to handpick caterpillars or apply recommended pest controls before damage spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much sun on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni hulu la babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that dry out quickly under direct, hot sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa creates a cool environment that protects the young cocoa until its roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ waa.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shady, and overly wet conditions. Pruning extra branches from your trees lets sunlight and air dry out the farm, which stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. Tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop even produces ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ woɔ toi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow green and healthy. Applying poultry manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's life will restore its green color and improve yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa ni he hiaa ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the major rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until rains fall consistently for at least two weeks so the soil stays deep wet. Planting after just one early rain often causes seeds to germinate and then dry up if a short drought follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa kɛ hoo lɛ otsii enyɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hɔmɔ kuku ko ba.

english: What is causing holes in the leaves and growing tips of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛdalɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baa?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the center leaves of the maize plant. Checking your field weekly and applying organic neem seed extracts or recommended sprays early can protect your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa otsi ni okɛ neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ awo mli mra. Ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Which part of a cassava stem should I cut and plant to get a high yield of roots?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ená shishifãi ni kɛlɛ?

english: Use the firm middle section of a healthy cassava stem with 3 to 7 visible nodes or buds. Avoid using the soft green top or the dry bottom stem, as the middle section sprouts fastest and produces the strongest roots.
ga: Kɛ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ 3 kɛyashi 7 yɔɔ mli lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shishigbɛ tsei ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ, ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds before I plant my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ŋmɔ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil so the tubers can expand easily downwards without restriction. High mounds also keep the roots well-drained, preventing seed yams from rotting during heavy downpours.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, yitso lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi oya ni nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Pile ni nɔ kwɔ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering regularly and mulching around the plant base keeps the root zone cool and stops flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that carry plant viruses. Spraying your pepper plants with mild soapy water or neem oil controls these insects so new leaves grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni ekɛfee baai heei lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun. It also keeps weeds from growing and breaks down over time to enrich your soil naturally.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa oya kɛ́ hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee nɔ ni woɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my chickens produce pale egg yolks, and which crops can I grow to make the yolks bright yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikooloi lɛ miifee ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ? Ni mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ koni mi-egg yolks lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse?

english: Chickens get the deep yellow color in their egg yolks from natural pigments found in certain yellow feed crops. Growing and feeding them yellow maize, orange-fleshed sweet potatoes, or yellow cassava provides these nutrients, which transfer into the egg yolks to make them bright yellow and attractive to buyers.
ga: Kooloi naa su ni mli kwɔ yɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli su ko ni anaa yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ ekomɛi amli lɛ mli. Abɛi ŋmɔŋ ni aduɔ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa Orange fleshed sweet potato loo yellow cassava Ha niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ Enɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ ni egbala mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged from excess rain. Nitrogen gives plants their green color to produce food, so applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eha eshishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ náa su eŋɔli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛye niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare upper stem. You can also carefully scrape away topsoil around one plant to check if the tubers have grown to a thick, marketable size.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ ŋwɛi tso lɛ efolo. Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu ajie. Ajie tso kome kɛjɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ana kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abaanyɛ ahé yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot hours is a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water loss. As temperatures drop in the evening, the leaves usually flatten back out.
ga: Baai ni akɛwoɔ tomato nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he ni haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi, ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a shortage of plant nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my next maize crop grow much stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mi-ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays behind to feed the following maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my farm crops even when rain is small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems adapted to survive harsh conditions. They absorb available soil water and nutrients much faster than farm crops, allowing them to overpower cultivated crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei ni ato ama shi lɛ anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: What causes my sweet potato tubers to split and crack open in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛgbalaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Tubers crack open when a long dry period is followed by sudden, heavy rainfall or heavy watering. The roots take up water too quickly and swell faster than their outer skin can stretch, causing the tubers to burst open.
ga: Bulb lɛ mli gbalaa kɛji egbi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni mli wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. ha yitso lɛ atswa

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout out of the soil even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli moŋ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep in the soil, if the ground was pressed down too hard for shoots to push through, or if soil organisms rotted the seed before it could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ anyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa tsɔ ni ŋmeii nyɛŋ atsɔ mli, Aloo kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow very tall and thin with few pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight. Cocoa trees will stretch upward quickly to reach light rather than spreading wide branches, spending energy on height instead of producing pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Kakao tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya koni la lɛ abote mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eniji lɛ eshwa babaoo lɛ Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii.

english: Why do some farmers plant plantains or cassava together with young cocoa trees on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ plantains loo cassava kɛfataa kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight when they are young. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide necessary shade to protect young cocoa, while also giving the farmer food and income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu cacao tsei bibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How do legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legume crops have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps bring back the green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia otso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight over water and soil nutrients while their leaves fight for sunlight. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough food and light to grow big and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ baawu. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do pests like worms attack my maize plants mostly early in the morning or at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ babaoo leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide in the soil or inside the plant stem during the hot afternoon sun to stay cool. They come out to feed when the weather cools down in the evening, night, and early morning.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ gbɛkɛ, gbɛkɛ, kɛ leebi maŋkpa.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. When weeds take these essential resources away, your crops get weak and cannot produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi jie nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Covering the ground, also known as mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping the sun from drying up water quickly. It also keeps the soil cool and prevents weeds from springing up.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsiɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: You should wait until the ground gets two or three good, deep rains so the soil stays wet enough underneath. Planting in dry or barely wet soil causes seeds to dry up and die before they can sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa aaafee shii 2-3 bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ shishigbɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers from my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: If a plantain tree produces too many suckers, they all compete for the mother plant's food. Keeping only one or two suckers ensures the main tree grows strong and produces a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmeii babaoo Amɛbaatswa niyenii ni jɛ nyɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ to lɛ, ebaawo tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo plantains babaoo.

english: Why is it bad to grow the exact same crop on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests and diseases build up in the ground, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the leaves turn green and stay strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long, especially in heavy soils during heavy rainfall. Planting your cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps rainwater drain away quickly so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ wa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning tiny instead of growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading plant sicknesses. Spraying your crops early with soapy water or natural neem tree liquid keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo adebɔɔ mli neem tso nu tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: What is making small, round holes appear all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji lɛ feɔ bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo? ni shwieɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: Small holes are caused by hungry caterpillars or beetles that feed on the leaves at night. Checking under the leaves regularly and picking them off or applying simple pest sprays will protect the cabbages.
ga: Buji bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ feɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi be fɛɛ be ni ojie amɛ loo okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kaaba lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any tomatoes during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme hot and dry weather stresses the tomato plant, causing the flowers to dry up and fall off before fruit can form. Watering deeply at the base of the plant during hot days helps keep the blossoms alive.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil stays damp at least hand-deep for a few days after heavy rain. Planting after just one small shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry period follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ hoo lɛ, bɔ ni ooonyɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin with small yields when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food from the soil. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough light and nutrients to produce big fruits instead of just tall stems.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji moŋ fe ni eeewo tsei kakadaji kɛkɛ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, beans and cowpeas pull good nitrogen food from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow bigger while giving you two different food harvests from the same plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ nitrogen kpakpa. kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, afeɔ niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce fewer pods when the trees get very bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Thick, unpruned branches block sunlight and trap wet air inside the tree, creating diseases and preventing new flowers from forming. Cutting away extra branches lets light in and encourages new cocoa pods to grow.
ga: Niji ni mli tse ni afolɔko lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli. Ekɛ helai baa ni ehaaa fɔfɔi heei aba. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe lɛ, ebaaha la abote mli ni ewo kookoo tsei heei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit after I move them to a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need time to build a new root system before they can support heavy fruit. Trimming the old leaves when transplanting and adding rich compost around the root hole helps them establish quickly and produce fruit faster.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia be ni amɛkɛma shishifã hee dani amɛye amɛbua yibiiwoo ni tsii. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai momoi lɛ kɛji ootsake ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Shishifãi lɛ amli buji lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai momo lɛ ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow if I accidentally strip off or damage their outer layer before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ oshara shwie kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ loo mifite dani midu lɛ?

english: The outer layer of a seed protects the tiny plant inside and stores its essential food; removing or damaging too much of it leaves the seed vulnerable to rot and deprives it of the strength needed to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he. ni yɔɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa toɔ Kɛ́ ajieɔ babaoo loo akpataa he babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo oya ni hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ baaje mli.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I remove too many leaves or pods from the plant while it is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji mijie baai loo ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli be mli ni edaa lolo lɛ?

english: Leaves produce the food that feeds the entire plant. If you remove too many leaves, the plant cannot make enough energy to nourish its seeds and fruit, leading to weak crops and lower yields.
ga: Baai woɔ niyenii ni haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji ojie baai babaoo lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaha amɛdumɔwui kɛ amɛyibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: What is the correct way for me to store my harvested seeds so they do not spoil before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato koni amɛkafite dani shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Seeds should be dried properly until they are firm, then kept in airtight containers or cool, dry places to protect them from dampness, mold, and insect damage.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, too yɛ tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi koni ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi akafite.

english: Why do my stored grains turn to dust after a few months, and how can I stop this from happening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enɛ naa koni ekaba?

english: Storage pests like weevils eat the inside of stored seeds. You can prevent this by ensuring seeds are thoroughly dried before storage and keeping them in sealed sacks or treated storage bins.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii amli tamɔ ŋmeii baaye dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oooha amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto lɛ nɔ. ni okɛto kotokui ni atsĩ naa loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ amli.

english: How can I test if the seeds I stored from last year are still good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ hi lolo bɔ ni sa akɛ madu?

english: You can do a simple germination test by putting ten seeds in a moist cloth for a few days; if seven or more sprout, your stored seed batch is still healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛha gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji fɔfɔii kpawo loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ Odumɔwui akuu ni okɛto lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo ni efee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: How can I be sure that the seeds I am buying come from a genuine source and will give me good yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ jɛ he ko diɛŋtsɛ, ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Always purchase seeds from certified agricultural dealers or extension officers, as genuine certified seeds are tested for high germination rates and resistance to common diseases.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ loo sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akaa dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: What standards do my seeds or crops need to meet if I want to sell them to foreign markets outside Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai esa akɛ midumɔwui loo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ he kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei ni bɛ Ghana?

english: Foreign buyers require seeds and crops to be pure, uniform in quality, free from pests or chemical contamination, and traceable back to a certified, well-managed farm.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisumɔ ni dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe atse. Nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsofai fɔji bɛ mli. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔji ni awo he odaseyeli ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and die before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ baa shi ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb the oxygen and nutrients needed to keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ eŋɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the hottest parts of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat as a natural defense to trap moisture inside and reduce water loss caused by the hot sun and wind.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛba nu ni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I just pour all my fertilizer on my crops at once when the season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Pouring all your fertilizer on the soil at once can burn your crop roots, waste money when rains wash it away, and damage your soil. Dividing your application into smaller portions feeds the crops right when they need it.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Shika ni afiteɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ baa Ogbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mlijaa bibii Ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ hiamɔ bei amli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend dividing my fertilizer application into three stages?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ aja ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli awo gbɛi etɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Splitting your fertilizer into three applications gives your crops steady feeding at planting, growth, and flowering stages while preventing high chemical concentrations that ruin your soil balance.
ga: Kɛ́ aja ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli awo nitsumɔi etɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. shweremɔ kɛ fɔfɔii ni baa yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni fa babaoo ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it bad to apply fertilizer on my farm without testing or making a plan first?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo ŋmɔ mli ni akaaa loo atooo he gbɛjianɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yes, applying fertilizer without a plan can lead to using the wrong amount or type, which wastes money and can permanently destroy your soil's natural fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo henɔ ni ejaaa atsu nii. Enɛ heɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa lɛ kwraa.

english: Is pouring fertilizer directly near the stem of my plant safe for my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, dumping fertilizer directly on or near crop stems can burn the plant tissue and cause chemical buildup that damages both the plant and the surrounding soil.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo ebɛŋkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli fãji ni ekɛ tsofai ni fiteɔ tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: What does it mean when an officer says my farmland has become 'acidic'?
ga: Beni onukpa lɛ kɛɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ Mɛni ji ‘acidic’ shishi?

english: Acidic soil means the natural balance of your land has been disrupted by chemicals or over-use, making it hard for crop roots to absorb nutrients and leading to poor harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni acid yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ efite adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Can using chemical fertilizer actually ruin my soil instead of helping my crops grow?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy or careless use of chemical fertilizers without proper soil management can turn your soil acidic and kill the good soil organisms needed for crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo loo akɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee acidic ni efite shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ.

english: How do the chemicals inside commercial fertilizer affect my soil over time?
ga: Te tsofai ni yɔɔ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ saa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Over time, chemical fertilizers leave behind mineral salts that can increase soil acidity and harden the earth if not balanced with proper application timing and organic care.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shiɔ mineral salts ni baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ mli acid aya hiɛ ni eha sũ lɛ mli awa. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ be ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofafeemɔ mli kwɛmɔ lɛ kpaaa gbee

english: Why are my crops still weak and yellow even after I bought and applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli moŋ?

english: If your soil has already become too acidic from improper fertilizer use, plants cannot absorb the nutrients you put down, causing them to stay yellow and weak.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo acid tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: What happens to the fertilizer on my land if heavy rains come right after I apply it?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛwo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash unabsorbed fertilizer off your field or push concentrated chemicals deep into the ground, wasting your money and polluting the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔji lɛ shɛɛɛ mli lɛ ahe loo ekɛ tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Efiteɔ shika ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my farmland so it stays fertile for my children in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he koni efee nɔ ni baa nii kɛha miwɔsɛɛ bii lɛ?

english: Protecting your land requires careful fertilizer planning, avoiding chemical overload, and splitting applications so the soil stays rich and balanced season after season.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ooobu lɛ biɔ ni oto ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mligbalamɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ be mli.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has left to the fresh top leaves to survive, leaving the old bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the weather becomes extremely hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Extreme heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii. Ha tsei ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings upside down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmei niji miikwɛ ŋwɛi?

english: Look closely at the tiny bumps or nodes on the cassava stem where leaves used to grow. These buds should point upward toward the sky like small arrows; if they point downward into the ground, the stem is upside down and will struggle to grow.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔi bibii kɛji akɛ amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee ŋwɛi ni ebaawa akɛ ebaada.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni abua naa yɛ bu kome mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, the young roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This competition makes all the plants thin, weak, and unable to produce big yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, shishifãi bibii baawuu kɛha nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put tall wood sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent rot and helps the plant trap light to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ he. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni amɛkafite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ kane ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my farm when the crop seedlings are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and easily bullied by weeds. If weeds grow faster than your crops in the first few weeks, they steal the water and nutrients, permanently stunting the crop's growth even if you clear the weeds later.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi tutuaa amɛ oya. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe otsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa kɛya naanɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ jwɛi shwie nɔ sɛɛ mli po.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize eats up a lot of food from the soil, leaving it tired. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that pull natural fertilizer from the air and return it to the dirt, making the soil rich again for the next crop.
ga: Abele yeɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa enuɔ he akɛ etɔ lɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes and dark powdery dirt inside the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli.

english: That dark dirt is waste left behind by caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm. The worm hides inside the tight, young leaves at the center of the plant to eat the softest parts where it feels safe from heat and predators.
ga: Muji ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji jwɛi ni ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii ni akɛwo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ, he ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: A heavy downpour will wash the fertilizer right off the top of your field or flush it deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ loo etswaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Eheɔ shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient it needs to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves water sitting around the roots, making it hard for the plant to absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha gbɔmɔtso lɛ dalɛ kpakpa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo eshiɔ nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss when the weather is very hot and dry. However, if the leaves remain tightly curled even in the cool morning, it may be a sign of a leaf-curl virus transmitted by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso po lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee leaf curl virus, ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why do my maize crops produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to one another, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb what it needs to develop full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ atsu nii koni ekɛfee tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my pepper plants even if the pepper plants are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? mi pepper tso lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ pepper tso lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Even short weeds have aggressive roots under the soil that steal water and fertilizer meant for your pepper plants. Weeds also act as hiding places for harmful pests that can easily transfer to your crop and spread diseases.
ga: Jwɛi kukuji po yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-pepper tsei lɛ. Jwɛi hu tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe, ni baanyɛ atswa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya ni amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny beneficial insects called midges to pollinate them. If the soil lacks moisture, if there is not enough shade, or if chemical sprays have killed the beneficial midges, the cocoa tree drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ lɛ Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Aloo kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young mangoes drop off the tree long before they grow big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop young fruit when they suffer from water stress during the early fruit development stage. It can also be caused by fruit flies laying eggs inside the tiny fruits, causing them to spoil and drop early.
ga: Mango tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishijee be mli. Ebaanyɛ ejɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ wɔji yɛ aduawai bibii amli lɛ hu mli aba. Enɛ haa amɛgboɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my cabbage plants grow very large leaves but fail to form solid heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages often fail to form heads if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus all its energy on leaf growth rather than head formation. High temperatures during the head-forming stage can also prevent heading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kaabii nyɛɛɛ afee yitsei kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe tuber feemɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ yitso lɛ feemɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ yitso lɛ naa koni ekaya.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting and turning soft under the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot in the ground when soil retains too much water without proper drainage, allowing fungal rot diseases to attack the roots. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps water drain away and keeps tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fungal rot hela baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small ragged holes and fine dust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etse ni eyɛ sũ bibii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides deep inside the central funnel of the plant during the hot part of the day to eat tender leaves, leaving behind holes and waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛye baai bibii. Eshiɔ bu kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and drying up from the edges even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a leaf fungal disease such as Black Sigatoka or root rot. The fungus damages the leaves and stem vessels, preventing the plant from transporting water properly, which makes the leaves dry out as if there were a drought.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fuŋ lɛ fiteɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ nu aya jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ eba.

english: Why is planting my crops in May or the fifth month so important for their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ adumɔ yɛ May loo nyɔŋ ni ji enumɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa amɛdalɛ lɛ?

english: May marks the main rainy season in many regions of Ghana. Planting at this time ensures your seeds get reliable soil moisture to grow strong roots before the dry period sets in.
ga: Abuɔ May akɛ eji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri yɛ Ghana kpokpai babaoo anɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa aba dani amɛbote hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my crops take up to a full year before they are ready to be harvested and sold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ akpaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Certain crops naturally need a full seasonal cycle to mature. They grow during the rainy months and require the dry months to dry out, cure, or build up food in their roots before they can be sold.
ga: Tsei komɛi biɔ be mli tsakemɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛshɛ shweremɔ he. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli ni ehe hiaa be yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli koni amɛgbi, amɛtsa loo amɛkɛ niyenii ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english: How do my crops react when the rains suddenly stop late in the season?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: When the rains stop, crops slow down their growth, shed leaves to save moisture, and begin to mature early. They rely on stored food in their stems or roots to survive the dry period.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ baa shi. Shĩ baai lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. ni ebɔi dalɛ oya Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ amɛtsei loo amɛshishifãi amli lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: What happens to root crops like cassava or yam if I leave them in the ground after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ hu?

english: Root crops can stay underground safely for months as a form of natural storage, but if left too long in dry soil, they can become tough, woody, or vulnerable to pests.
ga: Shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee nɔ ni wa, amɛfee tsei, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye amɛ.

english: Why should I process and dry my crops immediately after harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii ni magbi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Processing and drying reduces water content in crops, which prevents mold, rot, and spoilage, allowing you to safely keep them for many months without losing your harvest.
ga: Nitsumɔ kɛ egbimɔ haa nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. ni tsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ amɛfitemɔ naa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo ni onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: If I keep my processed crops in storage for seven months, will they lose their quality?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsei ni atsu he nii lɛ to nyɔji kpawo Ani nakai tsei lɛ ahe baajɔ amɛ?

english: If crops are thoroughly dried and kept in a clean, dry room, they hold their quality for months. However, any trapped moisture or pest invasion will cause them to spoil or lose weight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsu ko ni mli tse ni mli egbi mli. Tsei lɛ baaya nɔ ahi amɛhe nyɔji babaoo, shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi ni emɔ amɛ lɛ baaha amɛfite loo amɛhe afee shoo.

english: What is the best way to protect my stored crops from rotting when the weather gets dry?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛto lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Drying your crops completely under the sun before storing them in well-ventilated, sealed sacks or structures keeps moisture away, preventing rot throughout the dry season.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi dani okɛwo kotokui loo tsɔnei ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli, ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it often better to hold onto my dried crops for months instead of selling them right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ ato nyɔji babaoo moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Right after harvest, the market is flooded with crops, so prices are low. Holding your non-perishable produce until off-season periods allows you to sell when supply is low and prices are much higher.
ga: kpamɔ sɛɛ Jarayeli lɛ baayi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jara lɛ baa shi. Nibii ni fiteee lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa hiɛ waa lɛ.

english: How does the dry season affect crop prices in the local market?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara he yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During the dry season, fresh produce becomes scarce because fewer farmers are harvesting, which drives market demand up and allows you to command better prices for your stored goods.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nibii heei ni anáa lɛ baafee nɔ ni faaa ejaakɛ okwaafoi fioo ko pɛ kpaɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii ni okɛto lɛ jara woɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can agricultural officers like PPRS help me protect my crops during long storage?
ga: Te okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ PPRS lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Officers from the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRS) provide advice on safe post-harvest treatments, proper pest control, and storage standards so your produce remains safe for sale.
ga: Amralofoi ni jɛ Tsei Ahe Bulɛ kɛ Nitsumɔhe ni Kwɛɔ Tsei Anɔ lɛ (PPRS) lɛ haa ŋaawoo yɛ tsofafeemɔi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ he. Pest Control kɛ nitoo he mlai ni sa Enɛ haa onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why does the soil in my field dry out so fast even after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po lɛ?

english: Soil loses moisture quickly when it lacks organic matter like compost or decayed leaves. Adding manure or mulching with straw helps the soil hold onto water like a sponge so your crops can stay hydrated longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jwɛi wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves produce more food through photosynthesis, which is then sent down into the ground to build bigger tubers.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start producing heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not dig very deep into the earth. When a heavy cluster of plantains develops, the plant becomes top-heavy, which is why propping the trunk with a strong bamboo or wooden pole prevents it from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni efooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji plantains lɛ dara ni amɛfee kui wuji Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni mli wa fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with green bushy leaves but fail to produce any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen makes plants focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth, leaving little energy for flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant is hungry, so it pulls stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tsei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my cocoa trees before turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is under stress from drought, poor nutrition, or lack of pollination by tiny insects like midges. During hot dry periods, the tree sheds flowers to conserve water and survive.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. niyenii ni ehiii Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges lɛ bɛ pollination. Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ nu ato ni amɛhi shi.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies. The plant curls its leaves as a natural reaction to damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni amɛfeɔ kɛji amɛfite.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the roots to absorb and transport calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ calcium lɛ ni amɛkɛyaa he fɛɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots get hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant. As the cassava plant gets older, it begins converting soft, edible starch into tough woody fiber to support its own structural survival.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii kɛtoɔ starch kɛhaa tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ da lɛ Ebaabɔi ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ayeɔ lɛ tsakemɔ ewo tso mli ŋmei ni wa mli koni eye ebua lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ wala.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster in my farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh local conditions with very little food or water. Domesticated crops need extra care and protection because they put their energy into producing food rather than fighting off tough wild competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni niyenii loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Shia tsei biɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ hebuu krɛdɛɛ ko. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawu koo mli akaŋshii ni naa wa lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Retaining tall trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates a protective canopy that shelters the seedlings from harsh heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to build strong leaves and green pigment. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni afee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and choke my crops even when I do not give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛtsiɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ anaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough conditions. Their aggressive roots suck up water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops can, allowing them to rapidly steal light and food from your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground when heavy rains stay on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water collects on the field without draining, it fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil. Without air underground, the roots and tubers cannot breathe and will begin to decay.
ga: Beni nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings compete against each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stalks and big cobs, they stretch upwards to fight for light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe baatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Mohu ɔ, a kplɛɛ a he konɛ a hwu kɛ ha la a.

english: Why does my land produce fewer ears of corn every season when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa toi fioo daa be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize consumes specific soil nutrients heavily every growing season. Repeatedly planting it in the same spot exhausts those specific nutrients faster than the soil can naturally replenish them.
