ga: Abɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi tsuɔ nii daa be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ amɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any tomatoes during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme afternoon heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit formation. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve its water and energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni eha etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make the soil richer for the next crop I plant on the same plot?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special organisms in its roots that draw nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku ni yɔɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ eshishifãi amli lɛ he. ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshiɔ kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers plant beans together with maize in the same row instead of planting them separately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa kome mli moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Beans and maize support each other when planted together. Maize stalks provide a climbing structure for the beans, while the bean plants feed nitrogen into the soil to nourish the maize.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he kome. Abɛi tsei haa anáa gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha ŋmeii ni akwɔɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl up during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava plants intentionally droop and curl their leaves during peak afternoon sun to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, preventing moisture from evaporating through the leaves.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ. Koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to maximum sunlight so they can make enough food. That extra energy is stored underground, creating bigger and healthier tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the benefit of planting beans alongside my main crop of cassava?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ he?

english: Beans naturally add nitrogen back into the soil while covering the ground to trap moisture, which helps the cassava grow stronger without using up all the soil nutrients.
ga: Beans lɛ kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni ekɛ mulching woɔ mli koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa waa ni efiteee niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to grow if I plant them too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too deep cuts off air from the young roots. The plant has to spend extra energy fighting to reach the surface instead of growing strong leaves and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii jogbaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shishifãi bibii amli lɛ mli. Esa akɛ tsei lɛ afite hewalɛ kroko ni amɛkɛwu amɛshi amɛ gbɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ baa nɛ he wa kɛ yiblii tsuo.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push its flowers down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally bury their fertilized blossoms underground so the seeds can safely grow into pods away from heat, sun, and surface pests.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii futuɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni awo amɛ fɔ lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo, hulu la, kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Extreme heat or lack of regular watering causes stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to save water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa daa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tomatoi shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl and stop growing when the weather stays very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to reduce moisture loss in hot weather. If the dry soil makes water scarce, the plant temporarily stops growing to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ, nu he baahia. Tsei kpaɔ dalɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during heavy rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain washes away nitrogen from the soil and waterlogs the root zone. Without air in the soil, roots cannot absorb nutrients, making the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shaded farms where air cannot flow freely between the trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ

english: Why do fall armyworms prefer feeding on young maize leaves instead of older leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall flukes sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa baai bibii moŋ fe baai momo lɛ?

english: Young maize leaves are tender, soft, and full of moisture, making them much easier and more nutritious for young caterpillars to chew.
ga: Baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ŋmɔmɔ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhaa amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai babaoo.

english: Why are light green patches and wrinkles showing up on my cassava leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies as they feed on the sap.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ beni amɛyeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Lower leaves turn yellow when the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Applying compost or the right fertilizer around the base of the plant feeds it the nitrogen it needs to recover.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: During hot afternoons, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can pull water out of the soil, so they wilt to protect themselves. Covering the soil around the plant with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei abu amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my vegetable plants growing big, bushy leaves but no fruits or flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi aduawai loo fɔfɔi ko bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Plants need balanced soil nutrients, including phosphorus, to encourage flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei. ni phosphorus fata he Koni eha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. This makes the stalks thin and weak, resulting in small corn cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii baa loo ŋmãa ko bɛ kwraa.

english: How do I know it is the right time to sow my seeds after the rain starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy rains so the ground is soaked deep below the surface. Sowing seeds after just one light rain can cause them to germinate and then dry up if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cassava and maize together on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast above ground and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly underground over a full year. Planting them together allows you to harvest maize early without stopping the cassava from using the space later.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo Shikpɔŋ shishi afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Companion dumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa mra ni okpaaa ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akatsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high, when water supply is irregular, or when insects fail to visit and pollinate them. Keeping water supply steady and encouraging helpful insects helps fruits set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi nyɛɛɛ ayasara ni amɛfee pollination Nu jɛɛhe ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni awoɔ amɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around the roots for too long without proper soil drainage, or when tiny microscopic soil organisms enter the roots through wounded stems or infected planting cuttings.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Aloo beni wala yibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ bibioo ko mli lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni epila loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster in my farm than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive harsh soil conditions, so they quickly drink up water and fertilizer intended for your crops. Removing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and sunlight from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize or cocoa turn moldy while stored in the room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa loo kookoo ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi beni akɛtoɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mold grows when crops are bagged before they are completely dry or when they are stored in a dark room with bad airflow. Sun-drying your harvest thoroughly and keeping storage bags off the floor in a airy space prevents mold.
ga: Muji baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa loo kɛ́ akɛto tsuji ni mli ewo duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Gbimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ kotokui ato shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer right before a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainstorms wash fertilizer away from the topsoil before the crop roots have time to absorb it. This wastes your money and leaves the plant hungry, so it is best to fertilize when the soil is already moist after a light rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and delicate leaves that lose water very quickly in hot, dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cooler environment and protects young cocoa from direct sunlight.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa. ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining properly. Soggy soil starves the roots of air and allows soil fungus to attack and soften the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛha amɛfee blɛoo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juice from the underside of leaves and spreading plant viruses. Removing affected leaves early or spraying with mild neem water helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni ena hela lɛ mra Loo akɛ neem nu ni mli ejɔ baashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I leave space between my crops instead of planting them tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin plants with low yields. Proper spacing allows plants to spread their roots and lets fresh air flow to prevent diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the food crops I intentionally planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that adapt quickly to local conditions and greedily steal water, fertilizer, and light from your crop. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the space and resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli, ni amɛkɛ hiɛjoomɔ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: How does spreading dry leaves or grass on top of the soil around my crops help them grow?
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (called mulching) acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from drying out the soil, keeps roots cool, stops weeds from sprouting, and turns into organic manure as it decays.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛji efite

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too stressed, often caused by extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving tomatoes steady water and light shade during scorching heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo kɛ hulutsoo ha o-tomato lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my plantain tree stop producing big bunches when many small shoots grow around its stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Edaa yɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Extra shoots (suckers) growing around the main plantain stem steal food and water from the main mother plant. Cutting away weaker suckers and leaving only one or two lets all the plant's energy go into growing a large bunch.
ga: Extra shoots (shoots) ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Plantain tso titri lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ni aaafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli ni ashi 1-2 pɛ koni tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why do my maize plants have tall flowers at the top and silk coming out of the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kakadaji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ siliki ni jɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The tassel at the top is the male part that sheds pollen, while the silk on the cob is the female part that catches it. Every single strand of silk needs to catch pollen for a full grain of corn to form on the cob.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni baajie pollen lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ ji yoo gbɔmɔtso ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Esa akɛ siliki tsɔne fɛɛ tsɔne amɔmɔ pollen koni ená ŋmãa ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my watermelon vines fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants grow separate male and female flowers. The male flowers produce pollen to fertilize the female ones, and once they release their pollen, they drop off naturally without growing into fruit.
ga: Aduɔ watermelon tsei kɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi hii feɔ pollen koni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi yei abɔ. Ni kɛ́ ajie pollen lɛ, ebaagbee shi yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ ni ekwɛɛɛ ni ewooo yibii.

english: Why are some of my pawpaw trees producing many flowers every season but never bearing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo daa afi shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants can be male, female, or both. Male pawpaw trees only produce pollen to fertilize female flowers nearby; because they lack female parts, male trees will never produce fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo amɛ fɛɛ. Pawpaw tsei hii woɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi pɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi yei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ. yɛ yoo gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ hii tsei wooo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures are too high, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries out or becomes sticky, preventing fertilization. If the flower is not fertilized, the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ egbi loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔɔ lɛ Awoɔ tsei lɛ nu koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: If I save seeds from this year's harvest of hybrid maize, will they produce the same high yield next year?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui komɛi ni jɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ to lɛ, Ani yibiiwoo lɛ baafee babaoo tamɔ tsutsu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing two specific parent plants for maximum yield. Seeds harvested from a hybrid crop lose that special combination, so planting them will result in mixed, lower-yielding plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛná yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ baaha tsei ni efutu ni yibiiwoo faaa.

english: How does a flower on a bean plant turn into a long pod full of seeds?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: When pollen touches the inside of the bean flower, it fertilizes small eggs at the base of the bloom. These fertilized eggs grow into individual beans, while the surrounding flower wall stretches out to become the pod.
ga: Kɛji pollen lɛ ta bean fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ekome. Nɛkɛ wuji ni awo amɛ fɔ nɛɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui aŋkroaŋkroi. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi gbogbo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can I manually transfer pollen from flower to flower on my farm if insects are scarce?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi nine ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi amli kɛya fɔfɔi krokomɛi amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ewa akɛ aaana kooloi bibii?

english: Yes, you can gently brush or shake flowers to transfer pollen from male parts to female parts. This is called hand pollination, and it helps plants form fruits when natural insects are not present.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ blɛoo loo okɛwo mli. Koni ajie pollen kɛjɛ nuu lɛ fã lɛ mli kɛya yoo lɛ fã lɛ mli. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bɛ.

english: How do tiny flowers on a cocoa trunk actually turn into big cocoa pods?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji?

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from one cocoa flower to another. Once a flower receives this pollen and gets fertilized, it stays attached to the tree and gradually swells into a cocoa pod.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ muji kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛ́ fɔfɔi ko nine shɛ pollen nɛɛ nɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi wo mli lɛ, Ebaakpɛtɛ tsei ahe ni ebaada fiofio. Efuɔ ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do we plant cassava by cutting and burying stems instead of planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔduɔ ŋmei kɛtsɔ ŋmei lɛ ni wɔfoɔ ni wɔfuɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni wɔduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Stem cuttings give you an exact copy of a high-yielding mother plant with guaranteed root growth. Cassava grown from true seeds takes longer to grow and produces unpredictable, smaller roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ eko ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni ebaaha oná shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ akɛ ebaada. Cassava ni adu kɛjɛ anɔkwa dumɔwui amli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ shishifãi bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba.

english: Why does joining a branch from a sweet mango tree onto a young seedling make it bear sweet fruit faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango nine ni ŋɔɔ ni akɛwo tso bibioo ko he lɛ haa ewoɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ oya lɛ?

english: This process, called grafting, joins a mature branch that already knows how to flower with a young root system. Because the branch is already adult, the new tree produces sweet fruit in just a few years instead of waiting many years.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ grafting. Nɔ ni fata he ji tsei niji ni eda ni le bɔ ni shishifãi bibii fɔɔ fɔfɔi momo lɛ. Ejaakɛ tsei niji lɛ edara kwraa momo. No hewɔ lɛ tsei heei woɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ yɛ afii fioo pɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni amɛmɛ afii babaoo lɛ

english: When maize leaves turn yellow, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant build strong, healthy green leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their vegetable plants with dry palm leaves or dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmei tsei ni egbi loo jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkɛbɔleɔ amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. The dry leaves act like a blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil too quickly, holds in moisture, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This competition leaves all the plants weak and thin, leading to a smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: How do I identify the best plantain sucker to dig up and plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse plantain suckers ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafo ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. They grow much faster and produce stronger, healthier plantain trees than suckers that already have wide leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword bud’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes to give me big tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves catch sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines on stakes helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight, allowing the plant to make more food and feed growing tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii bulbs ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when they are not pollinated by tiny insects, or when the tree is stressed by hot sun, lack of water, or pest attacks. Providing good shade trees helps the cocoa tree keep its flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ tso lɛ nɔ, nu bɛ mli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ebote tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ha kookoo tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my planted crop right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up water and nutrients instantly. Plotted crops take longer to germinate and build roots, so weeds get a head start unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsei ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ ja ojie amɛ mra.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early stops the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the soil when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When heavy rain causes water to sit in the soil without draining away, the roots drown and succumb to fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehooo. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaafite kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium, usually caused by irregular watering that prevents the roots from carrying nutrients steadily up into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be ni haaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aba aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow strong and green, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Can manure from my goats replace the chemical fertilizer I buy from the store?
ga: Ani too ŋmei baanyɛ aye tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, goat manure is a great natural fertilizer that adds nutrients and improves soil quality over time, but it works slower than chemical fertilizer. It should be left to dry and decompose before putting it on your crops so it does not burn the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, too ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo yɛ be ni sa mli. Shi amɛtsuɔ nii blɛoo fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi ni egbo dani adu koni shishifãi lɛ akashã.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to long wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce food for the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the tubers underground grow much larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the leaves and branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso lɛ baai kɛ eniji lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight and air can flow through the tree canopy. This keeps the farm dry enough to prevent black pod disease and helps the tree focus its energy on producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi black pod hela naa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa black pods wuji ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow together, they fight each other for nutrients, light, and water in the soil. Leaving only two or three strong shoots allows the main plant to grow larger, healthier bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ebɔ he lɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso titri lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juice from young leaves, or by a plant virus. Spraying organic solutions like neem leaf water or using insect soaps can help protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai amli Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem baa nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet repeatedly. Giving your plants consistent water and shade during extremely hot days helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Most cassava varieties are ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and cracks will begin to appear in the soil around the base of the plant where the tubers are expanding.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. Ni ŋmeii baabɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã yɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable farm in the early morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha obɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ nu leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Early morning is the best time to water because the plant roots absorb the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Evening watering can leave leaves wet overnight, which creates a warm, damp home for fungal diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ nu ejaakɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shia lɛ mli adɔ ni edɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up dry soil too quickly and then drains away fast, leaving seeds soaked without enough oxygen. It is safer to wait until the rainy season becomes steady so the ground stays evenly moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ oya tsɔ. ni etsɔɔ mli oya Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow with brown spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with brown spots on maize often mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or is being attacked by pests like armyworms. Applying fertilizer like NPK or using organic neem spray early can help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ armyworms etutua lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ni akɛ organic neem spray baatsu nii mra. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect its root tubers below the ground. Once the rainy season starts again, the plant will sprout new, healthy green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, water is irregular, or the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Watering regularly at the base of the plant during early mornings and adding compost helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi daa leebi maŋkpa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, giving young cocoa plants the protection they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko.

english: How do I know if my soil is rich enough to grow vegetables like pepper and garden eggs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rich soil is usually dark in color, feels soft, holds moisture well, and has earthworms in it. If your soil is dry, sandy, or pale, mixing in compost or dried animal manure will enrich it for growing vegetables.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ su tsuɔ, enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, ŋã yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee nɔ ni he hiaa waa kɛha aduawai adumɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally tough and stay hidden in the soil waiting for moisture. When the rains start, weeds sprout immediately and absorb soil nutrients quickly, which is why clearing them early is essential for your crop's growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa kɛjɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready 3 to 4 months after planting when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and die off. You can also gently dig up one plant to inspect the tubers before harvesting the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tso kome hu atsu nii blɛoo. Koni akwɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli dani akpa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested cowpea seeds from insects eating them in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cowpea ni akpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ ahe?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive in moist conditions. Drying your harvested cowpeas thoroughly under the sun and storing them in clean, airtight containers or specialized hermetic bags prevents insects from getting inside and destroying the grain.
ga: Store kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ mli. Kɛ́ agbi tsina ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛto tsɛnsii ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote mli ni amɛfite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei nine lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The buds or nodes on the stem must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow upward, leading to weak plants or dead cuttings.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ oookwɛ tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo tsei niji ni gboi.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and prevents moisture from evaporating, helping your plants survive hot spells without drying out.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers drop down and push themselves into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is a natural process called pegging. Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the plant grows stalk-like pegs that drive into the dirt where the actual peanuts form underground.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fixation. Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ pollin wo mli Tso lɛ yɛ tso ko ni tamɔ peg ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as soon as leaves appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi kɛji baai lɛ je kpo pɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to produce large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tso ji tso ko ni kwɔɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves available nitrogen to newer growth, causing older leaves to fade. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer corrects this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa shweremɔ hee mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai momoi ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the roots to absorb calcium steadily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or thrips, which damage leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with yellow sawdust-like powder in the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf shoot. The sawdust-like material is their waste. Applying recommended control methods early prevents total leaf loss.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ji jwɛi. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ hela lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ fɛɛ akafite.

english: Why do I need to peel off the outer root skin of plantain suckers before planting them in a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ asɛɛ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ?

english: Peeling or paring plantain suckers removes hidden pests like stem borers and microscopic root worms (nematodes), preventing you from introducing pests into your clean soil.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni ajieɔ loo ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ stem borers kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. (Nematodes) koni akɛtsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants keep turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs heavily to grow green and strong. Adding urea fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps replenish nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ babaoo koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ urea loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from neighboring plants. Giving crops proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce a full yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo eŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops rot when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Excess standing water deprives crop roots of air, causing them to suffocate and rot. Planting on raised soil beds and digging drainage channels helps excess water flow away from the root area.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as temporary living umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli shĩai. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing inside the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Holes in the leaf funnel are typical signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating your crop. Applying recommended control methods or neem extracts early prevents them from destroying the growing center of the plant.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiye onibii. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaatsi tso lɛ dalɛ he ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures all soil nutrients go straight into feeding your crops instead of wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe koo mli tsei.

english: Why should I remove the tiny side shoots growing out of my tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato nine lɛ mli lɛ

english: Extra side shoots, called suckers, consume energy that the plant should be using to form big fruits. Removing them allows the main stem to focus its nutrients on producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Side shoots ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ tso lɛ kɛtsu nii ni ekɛfee aduawai wuji tsuɔ nii. Tomatoi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning twisted with yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted yellow-patterned leaves indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Uprooting infected plants and planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties protects your yield.
ga: Baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Etsɔɔ ŋmei mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni odu ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do insects destroy my dried maize grains so quickly inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni yɔɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Storage pests like grain weevils multiply quickly if maize isn't dried completely or stored properly. Drying grain thoroughly and using airtight, hermetic storage bags starves these insects of oxygen and protects your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii lɛ baafa oya kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmaa lɛ kwraa loo akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ, ni ebaabu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa plants from heat and drying out during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants move nitrogen from older lower leaves up to support new top growth when soil nutrients are low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ faaa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots do not drown.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. So the roots don't drown.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when tiny pests feed on the blossoms. Consistent watering helps protect the flowers so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ye fɔfɔi lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why should I space my crops according to measurements instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato bɔ ni amɛdara ha lɛ naa moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong roots and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing leaf rot diseases and maximizing sunlight exposure.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Prevent leaf rot and maximize sunlight.

english: Why is it bad to save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ mi-hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds are specially bred for a single high-yielding harvest. Seeds saved from a hybrid crop will grow unevenly and produce plants with much smaller, weaker cobs.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ nɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing. Applying fertilizer right before heavy downpours will wash the plant food away before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii mli nibii lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital water, sunlight, and nutrients directly from the soil that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food required to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni egbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early stops the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when they are growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi amli be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cutting off unnecessary branches, known as pruning, allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the tree. This prevents diseases from spreading in damp shade and helps the tree direct its food and energy into producing big cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ niji ni afoɔ, ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the right time of year to prune my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo mi-kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Pruning is best done right before the major rainy season starts or after you finish harvesting. Doing it at this time ensures you do not accidentally cut off fresh flowers or young pods that would have turned into crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpa tsei lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi loo beni kpamɔ lɛ egbe naa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ofee nakai yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha okɛ fɔfɔi heei loo ŋmeii bibii ni baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akafolɔ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do extra small shoots grow from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ So special lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: These shoots are called chupons or water shoots. They waste the tree's water and nutrients without producing useful pods, so you should carefully remove them so the main tree stays strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ chupons loo nu ŋmeii. Amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛhaaa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ojie amɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny flowers grow directly on the trunk and thick branches of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni ekwɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow their flowers on the main trunk and old wood so that the heavy cocoa pods have strong support to hang from as they grow bigger.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ tsei momo lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji koni akɛfi kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛfo be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do many of the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated—meaning pollen from one flower is moved to another—by tiny insects. If a flower does not get pollinated within a day or two, it dies and falls to the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ afee cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ mli muji lɛ eshɛɛɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ fɔfɔi kome mli muji lɛ yaa ekroko mli. Fɔfɔ lɛ baagbo ni ebaagbee shikpɔŋ.

english: What happens inside a cocoa flower to make it start growing into a cocoa pod?
ga: Mɛni baa mli yɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebɔi dalɛ ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: When beneficial insects transfer tiny grains called pollen onto the center of the flower, pollination happens. This causes the bottom part of the flower to swell up over several months and form a cocoa pod.
ga: Beni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ŋɔ dumɔwui bibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Polination baaba. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ fuɔ nyɔji babaoo ni efeɔ kookoo tso.

english: What should I avoid doing on my farm when my cocoa trees start bringing out flowers?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: You should avoid spraying strong insect chemicals directly onto open flowers because those chemicals kill the friendly insects that visit flowers to help them turn into pods.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni okɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai nɛɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: What are midges and why do people say they matter for my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji dwarf? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ amɛhe hiaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Midges are extremely tiny flying insects that live on damp ground. They are crucial for cocoa farms because they crawl into tiny cocoa flowers to carry pollen, which is the only way pods can form.
ga: Midge ji kooloo bibioo ko ni foɔ ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Amɛhe hiaa waa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji ejaakɛ amɛshwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii amli. koni ekɛ pollen aya Enɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni pod baanyɛ atsɔ nɔ afee.

english: How can I make my cocoa farm a good home for midges to grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ afee shia kpakpa kɛha mi-dwarf lɛ ni amɛkwɛ nɔ?

english: Midges love damp, shady places. Leaving rotting plantain trunks, cocoa husk piles, and leaf litter on the soil creates the moist environment midges need to breed and increase pollination on your farm.
ga: Midge sumɔɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Eshiɔ plantain tsei ni egboi, kookoo ŋmɔji, kɛ baai ni efite lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni kooloi ni darako lɛ he hiaa koni amɛfɔ bii lɛ baa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me get a better harvest from my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná ŋmaa kpakpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers are trained farm advisors who visit your farm to teach you correct techniques for pruning, flower care, soil management, and pest control so your trees produce more cocoa.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmɔ mli ŋaawolɔi ni atsɔse amɛ ni baaba oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛtsɔɔ bo gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ awo kookoo babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly like straws during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is very hot. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture so it does not dry out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts on my farmland before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛdu ŋmeii yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the bean family, which takes nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, making it richer for the maize crop that comes after.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die if I plant them in an open field without plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains next to them provides essential shade and keeps the surrounding air moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow tall and thin with very small ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii waa lɛ, beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough food to grow strong stalks and big ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves in a V-shape means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important food for growth. The plant pulls remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ V-shape, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant does not get consistent water. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee

english: Why am I finding small holes and broad damage inside the central funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? kɛ fitemɔ ni gbɛ eshwa babaoo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli.

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm that crawl into the center funnel of young corn to hide from the sun and feed on the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he ni amɛye baai bibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than regular crops and steal the plant food (nutrients) directly from the soil before your crops' roots can reach them, leaving your crops hungry despite the rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn tough and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are meant to store starch, but if left in the ground past their maturity, the plant converts that soft starch into hard plant fibers, making the tubers tough and difficult to cook.
ga: Akɛ cassava shishifãi toɔ starch. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛteke be ni ato lɛ Tso lɛ baatsake ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ewo tso mli ŋmɔtɔ ni wa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling within just two days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react quickly with oxygen in the air because they lose their protective connection to the living plant. This causes rapid internal spoiling unless they are processed into items like gari or flour quickly.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛ oxygen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi kɛ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ bɛ tsakpaa ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fitemɔ baa oya. Ja afee lɛ oya ni efee nɔ ko tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why do my food crops grow very fast and yield well in the first two years after clearing a forest area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ oya ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni mijie koo lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Forest soil contains years of accumulated decaying leaves and organic matter, giving your crops a rich boost of natural plant food that naturally wears off after continuous cropping.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ ji baai kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ ni abua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Ehaa otsei lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii babaoo. ni baafite yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast now that all the big trees on my farm land have been cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho oya aahu akɛ afo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Without big trees to shade the ground and block hot winds, the sun evaporates moisture from the soil much faster, causing your crops to wilt quickly.
ga: Kɛji tsei wuji komɛi bɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa lɛ Hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya kwraa. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: How does heavy rainfall damage my crops more easily on clear land compared to forest land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni kooi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: On clear land, heavy raindrops hit the bare soil directly, washing away the fertile topsoil and hardening the ground, whereas tree leaves normally break the force of falling rain.
ga: yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ahe baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛfo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: If I plant forest trees and food crops together on the same land, won't the trees steal all the nutrients from my crops?
ga: Kɛ midu koo mli tsei kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ he kome lɛ Ani tsei lɛ ejuŋ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: If you leave proper space between them, young trees and crops can share land well; crops feed on nutrients near the surface while tree roots pull food from deep underground.
ga: Kɛji oshi he ko ni sa yɛ tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ateŋ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛja he lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei shishifãi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when I plant them too close to young tree seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your crops are competing for nitrogen and water with the tree roots, which are aggressively taking up the soil nutrients first.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ miitswa nitrogen kɛ nu he akaŋ. ni kɛ ehe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ klɛŋklɛŋ

english: Why is it best to plant short-season crops like vegetables while newly planted timber trees are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ odu tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni tsei heei ni adu lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Short-season crops need full sunlight to produce, which they can get while tree seedlings are low, but once the trees grow big and cast dark shade, food crops will no longer yield.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo dani amɛwo yibii. ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni eha hulutsoo be ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ, Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii wooo yibii dɔŋŋ.

english: Can I grow my cassava under heavy tree shade, or does it need open sunlight?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ tso agbo ko shishi? Aloo oosumɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to build up root tubers, so growing it under dense tree shade makes the plant produce mostly tall stems and leaves instead of big roots.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee shishifãi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo shishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ babaoo yɛ shishifãi wuji najiaŋ.

english: How do shade trees help protect crops like cocoa from dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo he koni amɛkagbo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees lower the air temperature around the crop, preserve soil moisture, and protect sensitive leaves and pods from being scorched by direct sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. ni ebuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ akashã amɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing smaller every season on this cleared forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ bibii daa be yɛ koo ni mli tse nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Repeated planting without tree cover drains the soil's natural organic matter and nutrients, leaving less plant food available for yams to form large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ ni tso ko bɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaajie nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei aniyenii ni sweet potato lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji lɛ faaa.

english: Will planting cover crops help fix dry, hard soil after forest trees are removed?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa lɛ sɛɛ beni ajie tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, cover crops spread over the soil surface to block burning sunlight, hold moisture, and decompose into rich organic matter that softens the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry out and die. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and cool air they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. and may easily dry out and die. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water to the dry air. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize every year when I plant on the exact same field without resting it?
