ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients out of the soil every season to grow. If you plant the same crop on the same piece of land over and over without giving the land a rest or adding nutrients back, the soil becomes tired and empty, leading to poor harvests.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli bɔni afee ni amɛdara. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ ni ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni efeɔ efolo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts between the rows of my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap natural nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This enriches the earth naturally and provides free food for nearby crops like maize, helping them grow greener and stronger.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, very dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and ensuring good space between plants helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden sticks to support my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ? koni akɛfi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking holds the yam leaves high up into the air where they can catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to feed and expand the tubers underground. Raising the vines also prevents moist ground diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni tsei kɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ helai anaa koni ekafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before the fruit can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually because of irregular watering. Watering your tomatoes consistently keeps calcium moving smoothly into the fruits.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are mature and ready for me to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, leaving a bare stem, and when cracks begin to appear on the soil surface around the base of the plant from the swollen tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshi tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Ni beni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal essential soil nutrients, space, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with enough rain, your crops will starve if weeds are drinking up all the plant food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baaye hɔmɔ kɛji jwɛi ye tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I not apply chemical fertilizer to my farm right before a big rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wooo ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ wulu lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains will quickly wash the fertilizer off your field before the plant roots have time to soak it up. This wastes your money and washes the nutrients away into nearby streams instead of feeding your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hoɔ oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight can scorch their leaves and dry them out. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that protect young cocoa trees from intense sun while providing extra food and income for your farm.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika kroko aha oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet and humid conditions. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight, weeding regularly, and removing infected pods helps keep the farm dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ afolɔ koni hulu la atsɔ mli Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. ni ojie pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ekpaa ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves. You can fix this by applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or mixing decomposed animal manure into the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Obaanyɛ osaa enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni okɛaafutu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is burning dried weeds on my farm bad for the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and helpful soil insects that keep the earth fertile. Leaving cleared weeds to rot naturally into the soil acts as compost, keeping the ground rich and moisture-retentive.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars inside the leaves of my young maize plants eating holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks young corn plants. Spraying appropriate insecticides into the funnel of the plant early in the morning or late in the evening can destroy them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes turning yellow with twisted patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies. The best solution is to plant improved, disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural extension officers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ atsu he nii ji ni okwaayeli mli nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures they grow thick stalks and produce larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear and heap soft soil into mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli ni mabua naa dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep and thick under the ground, so they need loose, soft soil to expand easily. High mounds also catch rainwater without letting it pool, which prevents the yam tubers from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu mɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛhaaa eho. Enɛ baaye abua ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plants experience severe heat stress, dry soil, or lack of pollination by bees. Watering regularly around the base of the plant and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ, loo ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo mli. Kɛ́ afɔ nu awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ he daa, ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water during hot hours. If the leaves recover by evening, the plant is fine; if they stay wilted in the morning, your farm needs watering.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ he wa amɛ gbɛkɛ Tso lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji amɛgboi lolo leebi lɛ Nu he miihia Oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow weak and yield small fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry leaves or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi loo tsei ahe tsei aha he ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, also called mulching, keeps moisture in the soil during dry days, stops weeds from growing, and cools the roots of your crops.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa cacao tso bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ baashɛ enɔ.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate food that grows large tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii beni amɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks water, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer added to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a vital plant food, or that the soil is too soaked with water, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa loo nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What is eating the young leaves inside the heart of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, destructive caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves (whorl) of maize and chew through them before the leaves open up.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai (rings) ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ dani baai lɛ gbeleɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 8 to 12 months old, lower leaves begin to yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base starts cracking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛji tso lɛ eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds rot in the dirt when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the seeds and allowing water-loving fungi to attack and rot them before they sprout.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ he bibioo ko baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni amɛha ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ atutua amɛ ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What happens to my maize crops if heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots, causing the leaves to turn yellow, growth to stop, and the plant to eventually drown and die.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the rainfall is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots prefer dry to moderately moist soil. Excess water in the soil creates a perfect environment for fungi and bacteria to grow, which attacks the roots and turns the healthy tubers into mush.
ga: Cassava shishifãi sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛyashi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fioo. Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adalɛ baa. Enɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away my topsoil and planted seeds on sloped land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ni edu dumɔwui yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Creating raised ridges or planting across the slope of the land slows down flowing water. You can also plant cover crops or build simple dirt barriers to trap the water and keep your seeds and rich soil in place.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkei loo dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa he lɛ hu loo oma shikpɔŋ gbogbo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Koni akɛ nu ato ni aha dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ ahi he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I plant them in a wide open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They require partial shade from larger plants like plantains or shade trees to keep them cool and preserve soil moisture while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin under big leafy trees but fail to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ tsei wuji ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Plants need direct sunlight to make the energy required for producing food and fruit. When trapped in deep shade, the crop stretches upward searching for light, spending all its energy on height rather than yield.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo niyenii kɛ aduawai. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi moŋ fe nibii ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: This is a defensive reaction. On very hot days, the plant loses water faster than its roots can pull it from the ground, so it curls its leaves to reduce water loss. It usually recovers once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Enɛ ji hebuu hetoo. Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni efiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do dark black spots spread all over my cocoa pods when the weather stays damp and rainy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ diŋŋ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ ahe lɛ? Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, overly wet, and humid conditions. High humidity allows the fungal spores to multiply rapidly and spread across the farm through rain splashes.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fung ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ faa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where short roots cannot reach it, leaving the plant hungry.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ahe baai adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, heavy root systems and hold a lot of water in their trunks. When heavy rains soften the soil, the ground loses its firm grip on the roots, allowing strong winds to easily push the heavy plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni tsii ni amɛtoɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ tswaa tsei ni tsii amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die even when the soil around them is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ miida moŋ? Ani efɔ lolo?

english: This often happens when microscopic worms in the soil attack the roots, or when soil fungi block the plant's internal water pipes. Even if water is present, the damaged roots cannot pump it up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsi tsei amli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ moŋ Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋwɛi kɛbote baai lɛ amli.

english: Can I grow food crops on land that was previously used for galamsey mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ galamsey tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Galamsey destroys the topsoil and leaves behind harmful chemicals like mercury and heavy metals. These toxic substances stay in the ground, preventing crops from growing properly and making any food harvested from that land unsafe to eat without special land treatment.
ga: Galamsey fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni eshiɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mercury kɛ dade ni tsii. These toxins are found in the ground. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Ni enɛ haa niyenii ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai he lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he lɛ he nii krɛdɛɛ ko.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and dying on land near an old mining pit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shika tsuru bu momo ko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil that holds essential nutrients and washes bad chemicals into the ground. Without good soil and clean water, crop roots cannot absorb the food they need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni akuɔ mli lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nibii ni he hiaa lɛ toɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ tsofai gbohii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nu ni mli tse bɛ Tse shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops near the river die whenever the water turns brown and muddy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ faai lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nu lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔ muji lɛ?

english: Muddy brown river water is filled with heavy silt washed down from destroyed upstream lands. This thick silt coats the soil, suffocates the crop roots, and prevents clean water and oxygen from reaching the plant.
ga: Faa lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ eyi kɛ sũ ni mli wa ni jɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni akpata hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ. This thick sediment will cover the soil. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa nu ni he tse kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yashɛɔ tsei ahe lɛ naa

english: Is it good practice to burn all the trash and weeds on my farm before I plant?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ashã jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani adu nii?

english: Burning destroys the good nutrients in the soil and kills earthworms and insects that help your plants grow. Instead of burning, leaving cleared plants to rot on the farm feeds the soil and helps it hold water.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaashã amɛ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does my land become very hard like rock after I burn the bush on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛ beni mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The heat from burning bakes the bare ground and destroys the natural organic layer that keeps soil soft. Without that cover, heavy rain and hot sun turn the top layer into a hard crust that seeds cannot easily break through.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shãa mli lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛji nɔ ko bɛ ni haa nɔ ko nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ŋwɛi fã lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni wa ni dumɔwui nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops produce more food when I leave some big trees standing in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛ́ mishi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big trees act as natural shields against harsh sunlight and strong winds that dry out your crops. Their deep roots also pull up water and nutrients from deep in the ground, keeping the surrounding soil cool and fertile.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ lɛ he. Amɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Make the surrounding soil cool and fertile.

english: What will happen to my cocoa farm if all the big forest trees around it are cut down?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji koo ni ebɔle he lɛ da? Afo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ amli?

english: Without forest trees to provide shade and trap moisture, your cocoa trees get direct sunlight and intense heat. This causes the soil to dry out rapidly, stressing the cocoa plants and drastically reducing your harvest.
ga: Kɛji koo mli tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ahi shi lɛ, O-cacao tsei lɛ baaná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why should I clear blocked gutters and channels near my vegetable field before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ojie nu ŋshɔi ni etsi kɛ nu ŋshɔi ni hoɔ yɛ o-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Blocked channels cause dirty water to overflow into your crop field during heavy rains. Clearing them allows excess water to flow away safely so your crops do not drown or rot from sitting in stagnant water.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni atsĩ naa lɛ haa nu ni mli ewo muji hoɔ kɛboteɔ oŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe. Enɛ baaha onibii akagbo loo amɛkagbo kɛjɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ni oootara lɛ mli.

english: How does dirty wastewater from town gutters affect my crops if it floods my field?
ga: Te nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli nu ŋshɔi lɛ amli lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nu shwie miŋmɔji amli?

english: Town wastewater contains soap, oil, and trash that can poison the soil and block plant roots from taking up nutrients. Clean rainwater helps crops grow, but dirty waste water spreads plant diseases and damages yields.
ga: Samla, fɔ, kɛ jwɛi yɛ maŋtiasei amli nu ni fiteɔ nii amli ni baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha tsei shishifãi akaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nugbɔ nu ni mli tse yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Shi nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does the dark top soil on my farm wash away every time it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: When land is completely cleared of trees and grass, there are no plant roots to grip the dirt when rain falls. Adding grass cover or leaving plant residues traps the soil and stops the rich top layer from washing away.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ tsei kɛ jwɛi lɛ Tso shishifãi ko bɛ ni baakpɛtɛ muji he kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaatsi ŋwɛi ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ anaa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Can I take a tree that grows naturally in the forest and plant it on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ ni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, many wild trees can be successfully grown on farms. However, you need to recreate their natural growing conditions, such as providing proper shade, good soil preparation, and regular watering during their early growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu koo mli tsei babaoo yɛ omanyeyeli mli yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛi ni haa mɔ daa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ, tamɔ hulutsoo ni sa. shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa yɛ shishijee be mli ni shwereɔ lɛ

english: Is it better to plant wild trees using seeds or by digging up young seedlings from the bush?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ dumɔwui baatsu nii kɛdu koo mli tsei loo akɛ dumɔwui bibii ni jɛ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ atsa?

english: While digging up wild seedlings can work if you keep the roots protected, starting from seeds or properly nursed saplings usually produces stronger roots and helps the plant adapt better to your farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni akumɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii kɛji obu shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ oje dumɔwui loo dumɔwui bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli wa baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will a tree that grows well in the Ashanti region also grow if I plant it in Accra?
ga: Ani tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ hu baakwɛ̃ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ Accra?

english: It can grow, but success depends on how you manage local conditions. Accra is drier than the Ashanti region, so you will need to plan for extra watering and soil conditioning during dry spells.
ga: Ebaanyɛ eda Shi omanyeyeli damɔ bɔ ni okwɛɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ anɔ ohaa lɛ nɔ. Accra kpokpaa lɛ mli egbi fe Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe baahia ni oto gbɛjianɔ koni okɛ nu krokomɛi awo mli ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do some trees grow easily in certain parts of Ghana but struggle in other regions?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e yee kaa a maa du tso komɛ ngɛ Ghana ma a he komɛ ɔ? Shi nɔmɔ yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ?

english: Different regions in Ghana have varying soil types, temperatures, and rainfall patterns. Trees adapt to their native environments, so growing a plant in a new region requires adjusting your farm practices to match its climate needs.
ga: Ghana kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi, dɔlɛ, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi. Tso lɛ baatsake ehe kɛya shihilɛ ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu yɛ kpokpaa hee nɔ lɛ biɔ ni otsake oŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi amli koni ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he hiamɔ nii aba mli.

english: What preparations do I need to make before introducing a new tree species to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ hesaamɔi esa akɛ mafee dani mikɛ tso henɔ hee aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Before planting, you must clear the land, enrich the soil with compost or manure, secure a reliable water supply, and set up temporary shade if the young plant is sensitive to hot sunlight.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie he ni odu lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ. Ha nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ofee hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa.

english: Where is the best spot on my farm to plant a tree species I brought from the wild?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni manyɛ madu tsei ni mikɛba kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Choose a spot with rich, well-draining soil that gets suitable sunlight, ideally mimicking the sheltered environment where forest trees naturally sprout.
ga: Halamɔ he ko ni sũ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ nɔ. Ekaseɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How can I help a wild tree establish and grow quickly after transplanting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi koo mli tsei lɛ ni amɛma shi ni amɛdara oya beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Adding compost to the planting hole, keeping the soil moist with mulch, and clearing competing weeds give the young tree the nutrients and space it needs to grow quickly.
ga: Kompost ni akɛwoɔ dumɔ bu lɛ mli Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I observe a few test plants before planting a new crop across my whole land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei fioo komɛi ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ dani madu tsei heei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Testing a few plants first allows you to watch how they respond to your soil, weather, and local pests, saving you time and money before committing to large-scale planting.
ga: Tsei fioo komɛi ni oooka okwɛ lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona bɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa okɛ be kɛ shika tsuuu nii dani okpɛɔ oyiŋ akɛ obaadu tso agbo ko.

english: How do I know if a wild plant is adapting well to my farm's soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: A plant that is adapting well will produce fresh green leaves, sprout firm new shoots, and hold strong in the soil without yellowing, wilting, or dropping leaves.
ga: Tsei ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Tsofai heei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhaaa baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbee shi

english: What care does a newly planted wild tree need during its first dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ he hiaa koo mli tso ni adu ehee lɛ yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Young wild trees need regular watering, a thick layer of grass mulch around the base to keep the soil moist, and protection from farm animals during their first dry season.
ga: Koo mli tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa. Mulch ni mli edɔ waa yɛ jɛmɛ. ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain trees close to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that create shade, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to grow. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives them the nutrient boost needed to turn green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the same nutrients from the soil and lets pests and diseases build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo aba. Abɛi ni atsakeɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii fata he lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and thin when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space ensures it gets all the resources it needs to grow strong and yield big fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my corn plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Small caterpillars, often called fall armyworms, hide in the center of young corn leaves and feed on them. Inspecting your farm early, picking them off, or spraying recommended organic or chemical remedies early will stop them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ fall caterpillars lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra, tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ afee lɛ mra loo shwiemɔ. Obaanyɛ okpa amɛ dani ŋmɔ lɛ akumɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to put my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the rains have settled and the ground stays damp for a few days before planting cassava cuttings. If you plant in dry or poorly watered soil, the cuttings will dry out and fail to sprout roots.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani okɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ adu. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo nu ni ehiii nɔ lɛ Nibii ni afo lɛ baagbi ni shishifãi lɛ ekwɛŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop in high heat to conserve water and protect themselves from burning. Covering the soil around the plant roots with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the soil cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle loo egbee shi yɛ la ni mli wa mli koni nu lɛ ahi mli ni ekɛtsi shãa naa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) shwie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to buy certified seeds or just plant the seeds I saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ loo madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected to resist common diseases, survive tough weather, and yield more harvest. Saved seeds often become weaker over generations and lead to smaller, less reliable yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Hiɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli ni owo yibii babaoo Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ ni ehaa yibii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra branches and leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming excess lower leaves and non-fruiting branches helps the tomato plant focus its food and energy into producing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so the rain doesn't just wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not during heavy downpours. Placing the fertilizer in small holes near the roots and covering it lightly with soil ensures the plant absorbs it before rain can wash it off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ bu bibii amli ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishigbɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo baafata he lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aŋɔ mli dani nugbɔ ashwie lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years under good care, while traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Hybrid cocoa henɔi lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔtɔi feemɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ he lɛ.

english: If my cocoa farm gets heavily damaged by a storm or fire, can the damaged trees recover on their own?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ ahum loo la fite mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ waa hu? Ani tsei ni efite lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa trees are quite resilient. If the main stem or stump is still alive, you can cut back damaged stems (coppicing) and nurture the new shoots (chupons) that grow from the base to restore the tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji tso lɛ shishi loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo Obaanyɛ ofo tso lɛ shishifãi ni efite lɛ. (Pruning) kɛ ŋmeii heei (chupon) ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ akwɛmɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest cocoa pods from my trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ mitso lɛ mli?

english: Pods are ready for harvest when their colour changes completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange. Harvesting too early or too late reduces the bean quality.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su tsake kwraa lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ mra loo sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of the green cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons and in heavy shade. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Is it safe for me to harvest and ferment cocoa pods from branches that have broken off the tree?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni jɛ tso lɛ niji ni ekumɔ lɛ amli lɛ ni mafee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yes, as long as the pods themselves are fully mature and undamaged. If a pod has cracked open on the ground, dirt and mold can ruin the beans inside, so those should be discarded.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eda kwraa ni efiteee. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ fã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ afite kɔfe yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ oshɛrɛ nakai nibii lɛ oshwie.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to shed excess flowers, but heavy flower drop usually means the tree lacks water, fertilizer nutrients, or tiny insects called midges to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi fe nine. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli. ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi bibii Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli.

english: What causes small, dark patches and holes to appear on my young cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa? Yɛ mi kookoo pod bibioo lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by cocoa insects known as mirids or capsids, which suck sap from young pods and leaves. Spraying with approved pest controls during their peak season protects the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kookoo ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under strong sunlight. Shade crops like plantains protect young plants from harsh sun and dry winds until their canopy is large enough to handle full light.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Kɛyashi ŋwɛitsu lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená la fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen or potassium, or poor soil drainage around the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Titri lɛ, nitrogen loo potasium. loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ mli Bad root area

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans after breaking the pods open instead of drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mifo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation is what creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color inside the beans. Unfermented cocoa beans remain bitter, stay purple inside, and fetch a lower market price.
ga: Nɔ ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔ. Cocoa ŋmeii ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ lolo. Mli lɛ baafee purple. ni eyɛ jara ni baa shi

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves dry out and burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantain or shade trees creates a cool, humid environment that protects young cocoa seedlings until their stems become strong and mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etso lɛ mli waa ni edaa.

english: The first rain is often a 'false start' followed by a dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds will germinate but quickly dry up and die in the hot soil before the steady rains actually begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale shishijee’ ni nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium or phosphorus, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of sending nutrients down to swell the tubers under the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo ni potassium loo fɔsfɔs bɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ nɛ a hwɔɔ.

english: Why should I avoid placing solid fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw moisture out of plant tissues. Placing it directly against the stem burns the plant's delicate bark and roots, which can stunt growth or kill the crop.
ga: Nuŋtɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei akpa dalɛ loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same land with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decay, this nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer in the soil that nearby maize plants can feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards, shrinking, and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe, amɛmiigbɔjɔ, ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids, or viruses spread by these insects. They suck out essential plant juices, causing leaves to distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ. tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes with small caterpillar droppings inside the leaf whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is characteristic damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and feeds on young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɛkɛ ji bɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ nii lɛ yɔɔ. Nɔ ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ teeɔ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my cut yam setts rot in the ground before they even start sprouting vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mifo lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛjeɔ wain tsei po shishi lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in waterlogged soil or when fungi enter through unprotected open cuts on the seed yam. Dusting cut setts with fresh wood ash before planting seals the wounds and prevents fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ bote sweet potato dumɔwui ni abuuu he lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ hee shwie he ni afo lɛ nɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi pilamɔ lɛ naa ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is poor pollination. Consistent watering and mulching help keep the plant cool and retain moisture.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni pollination lɛ ehiii Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops stay pale and stunted when I delay weeding my farm by a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ toɔ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your crops need. Early weeding removes this competition so your crops get all the food required for fast, healthy growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Koni oha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong sunlight and dry out easily. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping the maize grow strong without using up all the ground's nutrients.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess moisture, the cassava plant sends all its energy upward to build big stems and leaves instead of storing energy underground in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ tsuɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee tsei agboi kɛ baai. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize ears have missing grains and empty spaces on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli ŋmãa ni bɛ kɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize needs pollen from the top tassels to land on every silk thread of the cob. If hot weather or drought happens during flowering, the pollen dies before completing this job, leaving empty spots on the cob.
ga: Abɛi he miihia pollen kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli koni eshɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Pollen lɛ baagbo dani agbe nitsumɔ nɛɛ naa. Ashi he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many cocoa flowers drop off the tree before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they feel stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Shedding flowers allows the tree to save energy to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hɔmɔ ha amɛhao. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tutuaa amɛ Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava bushes turn yellow and curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by small insects like whiteflies spreading the cassava mosaic virus. Dry, hot weather weakens the plant, making the insect damage and virus symptoms much more noticeable.
ga: Kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sinava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa koolooi kɛ helai ahe okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do black spots spread over my cocoa pods when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and high humidity create the right conditions for a fungus called Black Pod disease to thrive. Raindrops splash the fungus spores from diseased pods and soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod hela lɛ ni ekwɛ̃. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the ground; they spread near the surface. When heavy rains soften the soil, these shallow roots cannot hold up the heavy weight of the plant and fruit stem against strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ajara amɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsei kɛ aduawai ahe tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does my soil become hard like concrete after the rain stops, making it hard for my crops to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ? Ni ehaa ewaa ahaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Soil turns hard when it lacks organic matter such as dry leaves, compost, or decayed plants. Organic matter acts like a sponge that keeps soil loose, soft, and able to hold water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ni egboi bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efeɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Why should I pinch off the top main shoot of my pepper plant when it is young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ pepper tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Removing the top shoot stops the pepper plant from growing into a single tall stem. It forces the plant to send out side branches, creating a bushier plant that produces more flowers and peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ehaa pepper tso lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso kome ni kɛlɛ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ eniji fãa kɛyaa afã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ko ni woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same plot where I am starting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mije kookoo bibii ashishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create natural shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees to harvest extra food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni makpa niyenii krokomɛi?

english: It is better to avoid cassava near young cocoa because cassava roots spread aggressively and absorb a lot of soil nutrients and water, which starves the young cocoa plants. Plantains or cocoyams are safer food crop choices for shade.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie tapioka kɛjɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii lɛ. Plantain loo cocoa ji niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha hulutsoo.

english: What is the best time of year for me to put my new cocoa seedlings into the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei baawo shikpɔŋ?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings is at the start of the major rainy season (around April or May). This gives the roots enough water and time to grow deep into the soil before the harsh dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Dumɔ ni aduɔ mra (aaafee April loo May mli) lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nu kɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa.

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off if the tree lacks sufficient water or nutrients, or if there are not enough tiny insects (midges) around to pollinate them. Extreme heat can also stress the tree into shedding its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ he. Aloo kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu baanyɛ aha tsei ahao ni eha amɛ fɔfɔi.

english: Why are some of the small green cocoa pods on my tree turning black and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi tsei lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease—a fungal infection that spreads in wet, overly shaded conditions—or 'Cherelle Wilt,' which happens naturally when the tree cannot supply enough nutrients to feed every pod it starts.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli, loo ‘Cherelle wilt’, ni baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tso ko nyɛɛɛ aha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua pod fɛɛ pod ni ekɛjeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my young cocoa trees when planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsi kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anaa kɛji midu?

english: Cocoa trees should generally be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures the mature trees have enough room to spread their branches and roots without competing with each other for sunlight and soil food.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3 nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ.

english: Why do so many small plantain shoots keep coming up around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mɛi babaoo jie amɛhe kpo yɛ he fɛɛ he. Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ?

english: Plantains multiply naturally by growing underground shoots called 'suckers.' If you leave all of them to grow, they will steal water and food from the main stem, leading to smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ 'ŋmeii' lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni amɛwɔ kwraa lɛ, amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli, ni amɛbaawo aduawai bibii akui.

english: How can I encourage my plantain trees to produce bigger bunches of fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi plantain tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: To get larger bunches, prune away extra suckers so that only two or three stems (the mother, daughter, and granddaughter) remain on one spot, and apply compost or manure around the base to keep the soil rich.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná kuu agbo lɛ, Kpãa ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ (nyɛ, biyoo, kɛ nabi yoo) ahi he kome. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and folding down during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees lose a massive amount of water through their broad leaves. Yellowing and drooping are signs of thirst; covering the soil around the base with dry leaves or grass (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui laajeɔ nu babaoo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ. Hiŋmɛii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hiŋmɛii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kumai he okadi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How long does a plantain stem take from planting until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain tsei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: A plantain stem typically takes between 11 to 14 months to produce a full bunch ready for harvesting, provided it receives sufficient water, sunshine, and soil nutrients throughout its growth cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ heɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 14 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ akpa. Esa akɛ amɛ na nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ dalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees get damaged easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure can help turn the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When water sits in the soil without draining, it drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Beni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out, or if the plant lacks water during flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps flowers stay attached so tomatoes can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi, loo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni tomatoi lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: How does planting beans alongside my main crops make my soil richer?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni shwereɔ?

english: Beans and cowpeas can take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally adds food to the soil that neighboring crops can feed on.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii fataa shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the hot ground, preventing disease and helping the plant catch more sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide in the center of my young maize plants and eat the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which prefer the tender young leaves inside the leaf funnel. Spraying early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf funnel using recommended organic or chemical controls stops them before they destroy the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ baai ŋmeii amli lɛ. Okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛshwie baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. baatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying plants with neem leaf extract or soapy water kills these tiny insects and protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii. Enɛɛmɛi kɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Young crops are not strong enough to compete with weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early gives young plants a strong start before weeds overtake them.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ baabɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná yitso kpakpa dani jwɛi lɛ abaye nɔ.

english: Why do some of my saved maize seeds fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds lose their ability to grow if they were stored in a damp place, attacked by insects, or harvested too early. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers in a cool, dark place keeps them alive for the next season.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛhiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kooloi bibii tutua amɛ, loo akpa amɛ mra tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil food. Adding compost or well-rotted manure into the soil gives the plant the energy it needs to stay green and produce heavy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo toi ni tsii.

english: Healthy soil is dark, smells like fresh earth, holds moisture well, and has earthworms living in it. If your soil is pale, hard like brick, or washes away easily in rain, it needs organic matter like dry grass and leaves mixed in to rebuild its strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hiɔ jɛmɛ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse Ewa tamɔ brikii loo eshɛɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ Esa akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛma ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny insects gathering under my cassava leaves and making them curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: These are pests like mealybugs or aphids that suck the sap out of your crop, causing leaves to twist and stunt growth. Spraying a mixture of water and mild soap or neem leaf solution directly under the leaves can clear them away without harming the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛdaraaa. Nu ni akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ efutu mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Loo abaanyɛ afɔ neem baa lɛ mli tsofa ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ni eyeee tso lɛ awui.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Cutting away excessive tree branches to let sunlight and fresh air reach the pods helps keep them dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niji lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, their roots fight over the same soil food and water, and their leaves block each other from getting sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to yield a full harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the neighboring maize plant so you do not have to rely only on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ naa niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. Placing dry grass or straw around the base of the stems keeps the ground cool and traps moisture where roots can reach it.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hei ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist—never completely dry or waterlogged—helps the plant retain its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Egbiŋ kwraa loo nu ehiɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to trim off the lower leaves and small branches of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai kɛ niji bibii lɛ?

english: Removing lower, unproductive branches stops the plant from wasting food on unnecessary leaves. It forces the plant to send all its energy upward to produce larger, healthier peppers.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni wooo yibii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ baa niyenii ni he ehiaaa lɛ afite. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ aya ŋwɛi koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When yam vines climb high on stakes, their leaves catch more direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Vines resting on the ground are also more likely to pick up fungal diseases from wet soil.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tso lɛ kwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso ko nɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo he koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tsei ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do people call crop chemicals 'medicine' for plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi tsɛɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ akɛ ‘tsofa’ kɛha tsei lɛ?

english: Just like medicine heals a sick person, farm chemicals treat plant diseases, kill pests that destroy crops, and help struggling plants regain their health so they can yield well.
ga: Taakɛ tsofa tsaa helatsɛmɛi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsaa tsei ahelai Egbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eye ebua tsei ni miitao ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What is fertilizer and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer is like food for the soil. It provides essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that plants need to build strong roots, green leaves, and big fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. akɛ ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ aduawai wuji

english: How quickly should I see my crops recover after applying chemical medicine?
ga: Te esa akɛ mana ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya beni mikɛ tsofai ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Most farm chemicals begin working within hours, but noticeable crop recovery like fresh green leaves or pest reduction usually shows within three to seven days.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ nitsumɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli. Shi tsei ahe nibii ni kadiɔ mɔ, tamɔ baai eŋɔli heei loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shi lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ gbii etɛ kɛyashi kpawo mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even after I sprayed them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Pest medicine only kills insects; yellow leaves are often caused by poor soil nutrients or water problems. Your plants may need fertilizer or better drainage instead of pest spray.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo nu mli naagbai ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ŋmɔŋ baa. Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ he baahia otsei lɛ fe ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How does using a spray drum or knapsack help my crops compared to pouring chemical by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ loo sɛɛ kotoku ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: A sprayer turns liquid chemical into fine droplets so you can evenly cover all leaves and stems without wasting expensive chemical or burning the plants with localized excess.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai anɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ feɔ nu bibii bibii. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa akafite loo okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ashãaa tso lɛ.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together in one spray drum to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: You should only mix chemicals if the product label specifically allows it. Combining wrong chemicals can destroy their effectiveness or create a mixture that burns your crop leaves.
