ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai afutu pɛ kɛji akɛ tsofai lɛ ahe wolo lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ loo efee nɔ ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni shãa otso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I spray too much chemical medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai babaoo shwie nɔ?

english: Applying too much chemical can scorch plant leaves, stunt root growth, damage the soil micro-organisms, and leave unsafe chemical levels on your harvest.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã. tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa Efiteɔ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ tsofai ni bɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid spraying my farm chemicals during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes liquid chemicals to evaporate before plants absorb them, and intense heat combined with chemicals can easily burn soft leaves.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii lɛ ashã oya.

english: How long must I wait after spraying medicine before I can harvest my crops to sell or eat?
ga: Kɛ́ awo mi tsofa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni mahɔ̃ɔ loo maye?

english: Every chemical has a safe waiting period (pre-harvest interval) listed on its label, usually between 3 to 14 days, which allows the medicine to break down naturally so food is safe for consumption.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. (dani ŋmaakpamɔ be) ni atsɔɔ yɛ wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni no haa tsofa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii.

english: How can I be sure that the crop medicine I buy from the local market is safe and genuine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni eji anɔkwale?

english: Buy chemicals only from registered agro-dealers, inspect the container to ensure the safety seal is unbroken, and verify that the label shows approved government registration details.
ga: Hemɔ tsofai kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ pɛ adɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he naatsii lɛ ekumɔko. ni okwɛ akɛ nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ nɔyeli lɛ woloŋmaa he saji ni ekpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantain trees on the same farm with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow faster and have wide leaves that create living shade to protect the young cocoa plants while keeping moisture in the soil during their early years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã baa koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava sticks into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: You must plant cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots and roots struggle to emerge properly, leading to weak plants and poor yield.
ga: Ehe miihia ni okɛ yucca nine lɛ adu ni eshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Tsoi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná naagba ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do we need to build high soil mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and deep underground. High, loose soil mounds give the tubers soft space to expand easily without hitting hard ground, resulting in bigger, healthier yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni etse ehe lɛ haa bulb lɛ he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with my main crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that help the neighboring crop grow.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when daytime temperatures get too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Haa tsei woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that hide inside the central funnel of maize plants and eat the tender new leaves before they open.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (known as mulching) stops heat from baking the roots, traps moisture in the ground so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Ehaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crops very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce smaller total yields than well-spaced crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fɛɛ lɛ faaa fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when rain sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When standing water covers your field for too long, it suffocates the crop roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why does my harvested corn get moldy when I stack it in piles outside before selling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji beni mikɛtoɔ kpo nɔ dani mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested grain still contains moisture. When trapped in tight piles outdoors, heat builds up and creates a warm, damp environment where mold grows very quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Kɛji akɛ akpɛtɛ ŋtayaa ni mli wa mli yɛ kpo nɔ Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli edɔ baa. Fuji lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under direct Ghanaian sunlight. Big trees provide vital shade and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot in the ground during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Excessive water trapped in heavy soil allows soil-borne fungus to attack wet cassava roots, causing them to decay before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa nikpamɔ.

english: Why do armyworms attack my crop leaves more during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mitsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather speeds up insect breeding, while water-stressed crops become weaker and less able to fight off pest feeding.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi afɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni nu haa amɛhe feɔ shoo lɛ baa shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry conditions stress pepper plants, causing them to shed their flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it bad to leave freshly dug yams sitting in the sun on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsa ehee lɛ ashwie? No hewɔ lɛ, ani hulutsoo be mli ni oooha ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ?

english: Direct hot sun burns the delicate skin of harvested yam tubers, making them dry out rapidly, crack, and rot in storage.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ, ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã sweet potato tsei ni akpa lɛ ahewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. egbi oya Egbɛɔ ni egboɔ kɛ akɛto.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, tomato leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than roots can drink it, causing temporary wilt until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why should I dry my harvested paddy rice on raised tarpaulins instead of direct soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ tarpaulin nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Drying rice straight on the ground pulls up dampness from the earth and collects dirt and fungal spores that spoil the grain's quality.
ga: Omɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuaa muji kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow giant leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer pushes the crop to build leafy green stems on top instead of sending nutrients down to expand the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsirɛɔ tso lɛ koni ená ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen, which is a major plant food. As the plant grows, it moves available nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii titri lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve the soil for my next crops?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around crop stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, retains moisture, keeps the soil cool during hot weather, prevents weed growth, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛji egbo.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted instead of growing flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It prevents the leaves from making food, resulting in smaller tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkahoo, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it wrong to spray pest chemicals on my vegetables during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, spraying chemicals under hot direct sunlight causes the liquid to evaporate before it can work properly, and the combination of heat and chemicals can burn crop leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ la dani enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes or peppers in the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, reducing harvests over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers without them turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers they cannot support, but excessive flower drop happens when the farm lacks adequate shade, soil moisture, or tiny pollinating insects like midges.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua. Shi fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji ŋmɔji lɛ bɛ hulutsoo. shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollen tamɔ midges.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain stem for water and soil nutrients. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem grows thick and yields a large bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, is caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium, which prevents the fruit from developing strong outer walls.
ga: Rot diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ. Enɛ haaa tso yibii lɛ aná kponɔgbɛ gbogbo ni wa.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines up tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises yam leaves toward the sun so they can make maximum food to feed the tuber below, while keeping leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ fɛɛ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baa lɛ he helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees need to be sprayed with chemicals before they produce good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ tsofai afɔ mango tsei anɔ dani amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Mango trees attract many tiny pests like fruit flies and diseases like anthracnose. Chemical or natural sprays protect the flowers and young fruits from being ruined or falling off before harvest time.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii babaoo tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ helai tamɔ anthracnose. Tsofai loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite loo amɛkagbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do my mangoes look good on the outside but have white worms inside when I cut them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ hiɛ yɔɔ fɛo yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi eyɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ yɛ emli kɛ́ ofo lɛ?

english: Fruit flies lay tiny eggs under the skin of ripening fruit, which hatch into maggots inside. Using pheromone traps, clearing fallen fruits, and early spraying stop fruit flies from laying eggs.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ ahewolo shishi Pheromone tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ajieɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Koni aduawai amli ŋmeii akawo ŋmeii

english: If I cannot afford chemical sprays for my farm, how else can I protect my mangoes from pests?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hu? Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-mango lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: You can clean the farm floor regularly, set up cheap fruit fly traps, prune old branches to let in sunlight, and use natural neem leaf water sprays to reduce pest attacks without buying expensive chemicals.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsumɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Okɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni jara waaa awo mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji momo lɛ koni hulu la lɛ abote mli. Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ neem baa nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛba tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa aheee.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my mangoes while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mango nɔ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black spots are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose that thrives in wet or humid weather. It attacks flowers and fruit stems, causing fruits to spoil early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etutuaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai akui, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why are my fruit trees dropping most of their young fruits before they reach harvest size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii bibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ dalɛ he lɛ?

english: Trees shed young fruit when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect damage. The tree drops fruits it cannot support to save its own strength.
ga: Tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ hɔmɔ hao lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii lɛ fiteɔ Tso lɛ baafɔ̃ aduawai ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why did my mango tree produce plenty of flowers this year but gave me very few full fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi babaoo miifɔ yɛ afi nɛɛ mli shi aduawai fioo pɛ?

english: Flowers fail to turn into fruit if pests suck out their sap, if heavy rain washes away pollen, or if dry weather starves the plant right after flowering.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ nu amɛmli nu lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha pollen lɛ laaje, Aloo kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ha hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller and fewer fruits every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground every season. Without adding organic manure or fertilizer back into the soil, the land becomes tired and cannot feed large fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ organic fertilizer loo fertilizer fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ aduawai wuji anɔ.

english: Why is it important to cut off top branches from my fruit trees after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree canopy. This kills disease-causing fungi, encourages new flowering branches, and keeps the tree at an easy height for spraying and picking.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ baagbe ŋmeii ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ. Ekanyaa tsei niji heei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahiɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni anyɛɔ ashwieɔ nɔ ni akɛtoɔ.

english: How do weeds growing under my fruit trees reduce the amount of crop I harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ashishi lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients from the tree's roots, and tall bushes act as safe hiding spots for harmful bugs and rodents that damage young fruits.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli. Ni tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ aduawai bibii lɛ.

english: Does a mature fruit tree still need extra water during the dry season when it is fruiting?
ga: Ani nu kroko he miihia tsei ni eda lɛ lolo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Yes, water is needed to pump sap into growing fruits. Without enough water during the dry season, fruits stay small, crack open, or drop off before ripening.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu he miihia koni akɛpompi nu awo aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Yibii lɛ baafee bibioo, ebaagbala loo ebaagbee shi dani ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tip down to the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food the plant needs to stay green and grow tall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛfeɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why does my land produce less crop if I plant maize on the exact same farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of specific nutrients like nitrogen out of the soil every season, so planting it continuously drains the soil completely unless you rotate with legumes like groundnuts or beans to restore soil nutrients.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ kwraa. Ja okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake. Koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ

english: Covering the soil with dry organic leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, holds water in the soil longer so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young corn leaves with brown dust inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide deep inside the growing tip of the corn plant during the day and feed on the fresh leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oye baai heei lɛ dani amɛgbele.

english: Twisted or curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap out of new leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their young roots can pull from the ground. Providing shade plants like plantains protects them until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baa mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet, causing the plant stress so it sheds flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Excess water staying around cassava roots starves them of air, creating a moist environment where soil fungi can quickly rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cassava shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo oya dani akpa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil soaks up the water before the hot sun can evaporate it, giving the plant leaves full moisture to handle the daytime heat.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce food that grows the underground tuber, so staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, keeping them healthy and free from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni helai bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn brown and dry up when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight and extreme heat. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantains protects the delicate leaves from burning, keeps the soil cool and moist, and helps the young plants grow strong roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛ́ oshi loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black and rotting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting mature pods quickly helps keep air moving through the farm and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni akpaa oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves during intense heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun. This is a natural protective reaction to conserve moisture and survive temporary heat stress.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehi shi yɛ be kukuoo mli dɔlɛ mli.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to feed on the tender young leaves hidden inside the center of the plant. Applying recommended biological treatments or a dry sand/ash mixture directly into the central whorl early in the morning destroys them before they kill the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni akɛtee tsei ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo ŋã/sũ ni egbi ni akɛfutu mli lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋta lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛgbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose almost all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves in severe dry weather to stop water from evaporating through the foliage. The plant goes into a resting state to survive, and it will sprout fresh green leaves naturally as soon as the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Tsei boteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Ni ebaakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why do I need to prop up my yam vines with tall wooden stakes instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madamɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the air so they can absorb maximum sunlight to produce energy. It also keeps the leaves dry and off the hot ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛŋɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ haa egbiɔ ni ejɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Etsiɔ fungal leaf helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients, which prevents successful pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing balanced fertilizer helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa. ni nyɛŋ atsĩ pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa aha lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turning pale yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores the deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil for future crops without over-relying on synthetic fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ nɔ tsɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily when it starts carrying a big bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi aduawai wuji womɔ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep woody root systems to support heavy weights above ground. Supporting the main stem with a double bamboo fork or strong wooden prop prevents strong winds from uprooting the plant before the fruit matures.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua tsɔne ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei ŋtayaai enyɔ loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ agbɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow starting from the tips during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves, so when it runs out, the plant pulls it from the older bottom leaves to feed new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ ni oduɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or fallen leaves around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plants (mulching) acts like a blanket that shades the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa saplings burn and drop off during the sunniest months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their root systems are still small. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains to protect them while their roots grow deep enough to survive heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains mli kɛha hebuu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots that sprout around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete directly with the main plantain stem for water and plant food from the soil. Removing them allows the main stem to grow a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the sunlight to make energy. When the vine climbs up a stake, the leaves capture maximum light, sending more nutrients down to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la babaoo ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ahe koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ naa la fe fɛɛ. ni ebaatsu niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates in the soil for too long. Poorly drained soil suffocates the roots and promotes fungal diseases that spoil the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat away the green leaves inside the middle funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest where moths lay eggs inside the central leaf funnel, and the hatched caterpillars eat the soft new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward tightly and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by extreme hot and dry weather stressing the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa, ni egbi ni haa baai lɛ haoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees drop most of their small flowers before any pods develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani pod lɛ baa?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but drop over 90% of them because the tree can only support a limited number of pods based on available soil nutrients, moisture, and insect pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, shi enɛ baa shi fe 90% ejaakɛ cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ nɔ. Edamɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to start my crop seeds in small nursery bags instead of planting them straight into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ kotokui bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Starting seeds in small polybags protects young, fragile seedlings from heavy rains, harsh sunlight, and field pests while they are weak, giving them a safe environment to build strong early roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi awoɔ poly kotokui bibii amli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni shishifãi ni mli wa baa yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: How long should my young seedlings stay in the nursery before I move them to the main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Most tree and bush crop seedlings usually spend about 3 to 4 months in the nursery, which gives them enough time to grow sturdy stems and healthy leaves before facing field conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi kpeɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I leave them in the small nursery bags for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ grow bag bibioo lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If seedlings stay in bags for too long, their roots get cramped and wound tightly together. This damages the roots, stunts the plant's future growth, and lowers yield even after you plant them in the ground.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ hi kotoku lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa wɔsɛɛ. ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛji odu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ po.

english: How do I know when my crop seedlings are fully ready to be transplanted into the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready for transplanting when they have reached 3 to 4 months of age, have a firm main stem, several strong green leaves, and roots that hold the nursery soil together without being root-bound.
ga: Dumɔwui efee klalo kɛha dumɔ kɛji amɛye nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4, kɛ tso titri ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Baai eŋɔlii ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi babaoo ni haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I protect my seedlings from dying when I transfer them from nursery bags into the main ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi midumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛɔ grow bag lɛ mli kɛyaa he titri lɛ?

english: To avoid root shock, transplant during cooler parts of the day like early morning or late evening, keep the soil ball around the roots intact, and water the plants immediately after placing them in the farm soil.
ga: Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Akɛ tso lɛ awoɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli, tamɔ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Ha muji lɛ ahi he fɛɛ he. Ha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young crops seem to grow much faster once they are moved out of the bags into the open land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: In the open field, roots are no longer limited by the small bag. They can spread wide and deep to absorb more water and natural soil nutrients, powering faster stem and leaf growth.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ bɛ husu kɛtsɔ kotokui bibii anɔ dɔŋŋ: amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shɔŋŋ ni amɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: What basic care do my crops need right after I transplant them into the main field?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ mihe hiaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly transplanted crops need reliable soil moisture, clearing of surrounding weeds that compete for sunlight, and temporary shade if the sun is very intense during their first few weeks.
ga: Tsei ni adu ehee lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe ni kɛ hulu la he akaŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mli. kɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛji hulu lɛ naa wa waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How many months does a crop typically spend in the main field before it reaches full maturity?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii aheɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: After being moved from the nursery, many semi-perennial and medium-term crops need about 8 months of continuous growth in the main field before they begin producing or reaching full harvest maturity.
ga: Beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yeɔ afii fã kɛ afii teŋ lɛ biɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli dani amɛjeɔ nibii afeemɔ shishi loo amɛshɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he.

english: How is a crop's growth time split between the nursery stage and the main field stage?
ga: Te ajaa tsei lɛ adalɛ be lɛ mli ahaa tɛŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ateŋ?

english: A crop's early life is split into a short nursery phase of 3 to 4 months for delicate early development, followed by a longer main field phase of around 8 months for final vegetative growth and fruiting.
ga: Ajara tso lɛ shishijee wala mli awo tsɔsemɔ be kuku ni ji nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛha eshishijee shishijee ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni feɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛha naagbee tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why does it take up to 8 months in the main field for some crops to yield fruit after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji 8 dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Once in the main field, the plant must establish deep root networks, grow thick branches, and store sufficient food energy before it can support flowering and produce healthy crop yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ eshɛ he titri lɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. dumɔ tsei niji ni mli tse ni okɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato dani enyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔii ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my newly planted seedling has successfully taken root in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: When a seedling takes root, you will notice new green shoots or leaves starting to grow, and the stem will feel firm and sturdy in the soil when gently touched, showing it is absorbing water and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ Obaana ŋmeii loo baai ni jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ata he fioo, ni no tsɔɔ akɛ eeŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Is natural rain water enough for my young crop trees, or do I need to water them myself?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nu lɛ fa kɛha mi dumɔwui lɛ loo esa akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mawo nɔ nu?

english: Good seasonal rainfall is usually sufficient because it penetrates deep into the soil, but during dry spells or very hot days after planting, you should manually water young trees so their delicate roots do not dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli lɛ fa ejaakɛ efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo gbii ni mli edɔ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Esa akɛ Oha tsei bibii lɛ nu. kɛ enine tsuɔ nii koni eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akagbi.

english: What basic routine should I follow to take good care of my farm trees after planting them?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee gbɛjianɔtoo esa akɛ mafee daa koni makwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: To care for young trees, clear weeds around their bases so they do not steal nutrients, ensure they get adequate water, trim weak branches, and check leaves regularly for any signs of insects or disease.
ga: Yɛ tsei bibii akwɛmɔ mli Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishi koni ekaju niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, ŋmɔ tsei lɛ aniji bibii lɛ, ni okwɛ baai lɛ amli daa kɛji kooloi loo helai komɛi yɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do some pest chemicals I buy at the market work well, while others fail to work on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ekomɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi bɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Different chemicals are designed for specific pests or diseases. A chemical will fail if it is the wrong type for your specific pest, if it was mixed with too much water, or if the product is fake or expired.
ga: Afee tsofai srɔtoi kɛha kooloi loo helai komɛi. Tsofai lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ o-pests lɛ kɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Akɛ nu babaoo efutu mli loo kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛfee lɛ ji amale loo be eho

english: How can I safely choose the right chemical treatment for my farm without damaging my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofa ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Always consult an agriculture extension officer or a certified dealer with samples or photos of your sick crop so they can prescribe the exact registered chemical and explain the correct mixing dosage.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, bi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo nihɔɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ekɛ onibii ni hela mɔ lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii loo mfonirii baaha bo. Enɛ ji koni amɛtsɔɔ tsofai ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛtsɔɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii babaoo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is tree pruning, and why is it important for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tso nɔ ŋmɔmɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Pruning means carefully cutting away dead, extra, or overgrown branches. It allows the tree to direct its food and energy into growing strong main stems and producing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ tsɔɔ niji ni egboi, ni fa fe nine, loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa tso titri ni mli wa lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does cutting off branches help protect my tree crops from insects and pests?
ga: Te tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baanyɛ abu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Trimming extra branches opens up the tree canopy, allowing sunlight and air to pass through freely. Insects love damp, dark, crowded leaves, so opening the tree drives pests away naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ahe lɛ, ebaagbele tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli oya. Koolooi sumɔɔ baai ni mli efɔ, ediŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ tsei ni agbeleɔ lɛ shwieɔ kooloi awuiyelɔi.

english: What should I do if I notice pests starting to eat the leaves of my young trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ ŋmeii miibɔi mitsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ yeli?

english: Do not panic. First, inspect the plant to see how severe the damage is, pick off and destroy heavily infested leaves by hand, and seek advice on whether a mild targeted spray is necessary.
ga: Kaashe gbeyei. Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ tso lɛ mli koni ona bɔ ni efite lɛ mli wa ha. Nine shwiemɔ ni okpãtã tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ahiɛ. Ni obi ŋaawoo yɛ kɛji ehe miihia ni akɛ soft target spray atsu nii loo ehe ehiaaa.

english: What does fertilizer do for my tree crops, and how do I know if my soil needs it?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kɛhaa mi tsei lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for your crops, giving them strength to grow fast and yield well. If your crops grow slowly or their leaves start turning pale or yellow, your soil is likely low on essential nutrients.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai. Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo loo baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Where and how should I properly place fertilizer around my tree so the roots can feed on it?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe koni shishifãi lɛ aye amɛ?

english: Do not pour fertilizer directly against the trunk. Instead, apply it in a circle around the tree underneath the outer edge of its leaf canopy, and lightly mix it into the topsoil so rain can carry the nutrients to the roots.
ga: Kaaha ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai najiaŋ lɛ, Kɛtsu nii yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛbɔle he. Dumɔ yɛ baai lɛ asɛɛgbɛ ni okɛfutu mli blɛoo kɛya ŋwɛi sũ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ lɛ anyɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen or is receiving too much water around the roots. Nitrogen is the main plant food that keeps leaves green and active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ko ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme afternoon heat, when the soil gets too dry, or when tiny pests damage the flowers before pollination can take place.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ wo shwane dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Fiteɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a viral disease carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. Tall canopy trees provide essential shade that protects young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to make energy that feeds the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, improving sunlight capture and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: La tɛ̃ɛ he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni mɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ tso helai anaa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the soil surface. When the heavy fruit bunch develops, wet soil weakens the root hold, or stem borers attack the base, making the plant easily uprooted by wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi. Aloo ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tsei oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in the soil without proper drainage. Wet soil deprives roots of air and allows fungal diseases to attack and decay the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ jieɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii helai tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil season after season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: How can I keep my farm soil from drying out too fast when the rains become irregular?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya tsɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or cut leaves creates a protective blanket that shades the soil, slows down evaporation, and preserves moisture.
ga: Kɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai ni afolɔ aha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko ni ebɔle Rooting plants lɛ he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo, ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller yields even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal nutrients, water, and root space away from your crops, while their tall leaves block sunlight from reaching your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛbaai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. The plant is forced to move its remaining nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Anyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛjie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge stems, but yield very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing stems and lush leaves above ground instead of storing food in their root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa yucca tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Okɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and burn up when planted in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that scorch easily in strong tropical heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ umbrella Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and look limp during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are a crop's natural defense against extreme sun. By curling, the plant reduces its leaf surface area to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Kɛtsɔ curling nɔ lɛ, tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves chewed up with a dark powder hiding deep inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni tsuɔ waa shwieɔ mi-abele baai lɛ anɔ ni akɛteeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The powder is their waste, and they hide deep inside the central growing point of the leaf whorl to protect themselves from rain and chemical sprays.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Pauda lɛ ji nɔ ko ni fiteɔ nii ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ he ni tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ahe.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that multiplies in cold, wet, and shady conditions. High humidity and rainwater splashes allow the fungal spores to jump quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fungal spores lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds come up out of the dirt after I buried them deep to hide them from birds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mifu amɛ shɔŋŋ koni mikɛtee okpoi ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds planted too deep run out of stored energy before their shoots can reach sunlight, causing them to suffocate and die under heavy soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ shishi.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, light, and fertilizer faster than your main crops can reach them, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ baanyɛ aná. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and provide shade, acting like living umbrellas that keep the cocoa seedlings cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help make the soil better for next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots with the help of friendly soil bacteria, leaving natural food in the soil for the next crop you plant.
ga: Akpɔlɔi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛtsɔ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ helai lɛ aye abuaa amɛ nɔ. Shi adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why does my crop yield reduce every year if I plant maize on the exact same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests to build up in the dirt. Switching crops every season allows the soil to recover.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water fills all the air gaps in the dirt, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal diseases to grow and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii helai daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when there is too much fertilizer causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ baa yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight with their leaves. Spreading leaves out in the light allows the plant to create more energy to build large yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ amɛbaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbɛ baai lɛ ashwã la mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I trim off some of the healthy branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning lets light and fresh air pass through the tree canopy, which prevents pod diseases from spreading and encourages the tree to produce more pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo loo afo lɛ, ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa helai ni jɛɔ pod mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo podi babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabi ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi afata he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure will help the plants turn green and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural nitrogen, giving you a better yield without relying entirely on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa onine shɛɔ yibii kpakpai anɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo ni mli tse lɛ hulutsoo. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away, usually during heavy rains. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni ejeee kpo. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from the plant and spread a virus. Controlling these insects early with natural sprays like organic neem oil keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tamɔ organic neem fɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wilt and die suddenly in the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting is caused by soil-borne bacterial or fungal diseases that block the plant's internal tubes from transporting water. Rotating your crops so garden eggs are not grown in the same soil every season prevents these bacteria from building up.
ga: Muawai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa trukaa. Enɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakɛ nu aya. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii koni akadu abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ akabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why is it necessary to stake my yam vines with wood or bamboo poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii awo o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are climbing plants, and lifting their leaves off the ground allows them to capture more sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. It also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing rot and fungal attacks.
ga: Sweet potato ni kwɔɔ tso nɔ Ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat during the day or irregular watering. Providing consistent water at the roots during dry spells helps the plant hold onto its blossoms and form fruit.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ ko kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough food and light to develop full, heavy cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tsei fɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to grow slowly even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than young crops, so they steal the fertilizer and water meant for your crops before the plants can use it. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks ensures your crop gets all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei bibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ dani amɛkɛtsu nii. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my maize when the first rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ lɛ?

english: Waiting for just the very first rain can trick you because the ground is still dry underneath. You should wait until the soil is moist at least hand-deep and rains become steady so your seeds do not dry up and die after sprouting.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ni ooomɛ kɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ alaka bo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo yɛ shishi. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baawo wu bɔ ni abaanyɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to my crops, and why shouldn't I just put a huge amount at once?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ mli shikome?

english: Fertilizer gives crops essential food to grow strong and yield well. Applying too much at once can burn the plant roots and waste your money, as heavy rains will wash the excess food away before the crops can absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ afite dani ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant cowpea or groundnuts in the same field where I planted maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miidu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmã yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally restores nutrients to the soil so your next crop can grow healthier without relying entirely on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa kwraa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves when water is scarce to save moisture and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ baajɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwie shi kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo ahi shi ni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin but produce very small fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They waste all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of using energy to make strong stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ peeɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nguahi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper and tomato plants without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme hot weather, long dry spells, or irregular watering stress the plants, causing them to drop flowers to survive. Keeping the soil evenly moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and form fruits.
ga: kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ Aloo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the tubers underneath. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground and spreads them out to catch solar energy, which helps the underground yams grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni emɔ hulu lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?
