english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally tough and quick to absorb available water and food. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital sunlight and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Ragged holes are usually caused by tiny pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the leaves. Damage to leaves reduces the plant's ability to catch sunlight and feed itself, which reduces your final harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Baai lɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la ni enaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous maize harvest give me smaller yields than certified seeds bought from an input dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mlijaa lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred for high yield and disease resistance in their first planting generation. Saving and replanting those seeds causes them to lose those special traits, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni eha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai sui lɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food crops need to grow green and strong. This often happens when the soil is poor or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Why are the small pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during damp and rainy weather. It happens when there is too much shade or stagnant water sitting around your trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Ebaa kɛji hulutsoo loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong rain wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil. When the soil becomes soft from heavy rain and the stem grows heavy with fruit, the shallow roots cannot support the weight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ wo yibii babaoo lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atere muji lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the maize seeds I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to survive in your soil, so they grab water and light very fast. Farm crops are cultivated and need more time to build strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ la oya waa. Aduɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebiɔ be babaoo dani anyɛ ato shishifãi ni mli wa ama shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil if heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When flooded soil stays soaked for days, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing rot-causing fungi to attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehiɔ shi gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua.

english: How can I tell that my yams under the ground are ready for harvesting without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ akpa ni mikɛfooo amɛ?

english: Yams show they are mature when the green vines and leaves above ground begin to turn brown and dry up. This sign means the plant has stopped feeding the tuber underground.
ga: Abuɔ sweet potato akɛ edara kɛji wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa eshishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly when the afternoon sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a protection mechanism. The tomato plant curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun so it does not lose too much water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi bɔni afee ni nu babaoo akaje mli.

english: Why do people recommend that I plant cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This acts as natural food for the maize growing beside or after it.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why does my orange tree give me plenty of fruit this year, but almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akutu tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ afi nɛɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, eko kwraa bɛ?

english: Citrus trees use up a massive amount of stored energy during a heavy harvest year. If the tree is not properly fed with nutrients afterward, it rests the following year to rebuild its energy.
ga: Citrus tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ kpamɔɔ afii ni mli wa lɛ amli. Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ jɔɔ ehe yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛma ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and burn when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves dry out easily. Leaving larger shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains creates a cool shelter that protects young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ haa anáa he ko ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow fast. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help your maize regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the dirt. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally and helps your maize grow larger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa abɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to multiply. Rotating with different crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ babaoo. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth ridges or mounds helps extra rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I spread dry grass on the soil around my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mi lɛ nɔ lɛ? Mi aduawai lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass is called mulching, which works like a blanket to block the hot sun. It keeps the dirt damp so you do not have to water as often, and it stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa Ehaa muji lɛ mli fũuɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients away from the main stalk. By removing all but one or two strong shoots, the main plant gets all the energy it needs to produce bigger bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso titri lɛ nine shɛɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee plantains akui wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, long dry spells, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist during flowering helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛgbiɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing holes inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni mafo bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys young maize leaves. Checking your fields early and spraying neem leaf water or approved chemicals will save your crop before the damage spreads.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani nɔ ni efite lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and soft while growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo beni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the soil. Watering your tomatoes regularly and adding wood ash or lime to the soil prevents this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi enɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain plants turning yellow before the fruit even comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plantains are missing important nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the ground has too much water which is choking the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-plantains lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miimɔ.

english: Why do some of my plantain stalks fall over by themselves before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain stalks fall over easily when pests like stem borers or nematodes damage the roots and stem, or when the heavy fruit bunch lacks strong root support during windy weather.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. aloo be mli ni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni wa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my plantain leaves and dry them up?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa plantain baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ?

english: Dark spots that dry out the leaves are caused by fungal leaf diseases like Sigatoka, which grow quickly during hot, humid weather and spread from leaf to leaf.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni haa baa lɛ mli egbi lɛ baa ji fungal baa helai tamɔ Sigatoka, ni daa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ

english: How can I know that my plantain bunch is ready to be cut for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ ni akɛya jara nɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits plump up and their sharp corners become rounded, even while the skin is still green.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔjɔ ni eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo po.

english: How do I know if my crop is sick from a disease or just thirsty because of the dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo kumai miiye amɛ kɛkɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ?

english: A thirsty crop droops during the hot afternoon sun but perks back up in the cool evening, while a diseased plant stays wilting, gets spots, or rots regardless of the time of day.
ga: Nibii ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛgboɔ ekɔɔɔ gbi lɛ mli be he.

english: What makes my cassava roots stay small and thin even after leaving them in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ po?

english: Cassava roots stay thin when the soil is packed too hard for the roots to expand, when weeds steal early nutrients, or when the soil lacks enough potassium.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Beni jwɛi juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ shishijee mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn purple or reddish during the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ purple loo etsuru yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually show that the plant cannot absorb phosphorus from the soil, often because the ground is too wet or cold for the young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ kɛha shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do agriculture officers advise us to stop planting the same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkpa tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the dirt.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do crop medicines actually work to help my plants grow better?
ga: Te tsei ahe tsofai tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ koni eye ebua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crop protection medicines work by killing destructive insects, harmful fungi, or competing weeds, allowing the plant to use all its food and water for healthy growth.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ agbemɔ nɔ. Fung ni yɔɔ oshara loo jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei kɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, poor watering, or giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes it grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Tender cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy that traps soil moisture and shields the delicate leaves from harsh heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaabu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, the maize uses that trapped nitrogen to grow stronger leaves and produce larger cobs.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni haa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow with holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms or nitrogen deficiency. The worms eat the tender leaves, which weakens the plant's ability to absorb sunlight and nutrients needed to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo nitrogen ni faaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai yeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand into thick tubers. Planting them too close forces the plants to fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin, small roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ená nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii, ni no haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is better to buy fresh seed each season. Saved hybrid seeds lose their vigor, producing uneven crops with lower yields and weaker resistance to local pests and dry spells.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa shi, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hu nyɛŋ ashi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. The plant drops the flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the plant leaves begin to turn yellow and drop. You can also test a few pods; if the inner shell has dark brown or black markings, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts shɛɔ dalɛ he beni tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka pods komɛi hu okwɛ. Kɛji mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why are the roots of my cassava rotting underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when soil stays too wet and waterlogged during heavy rains. The stagnant water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to break down and rot the tubers.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akumɔ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why should I avoid placing chemical fertilizer right next to the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizer placed too close to the main stem can burn the tender plant tissue and roots. It should be applied in a ring a few inches away where the feeder roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ fãji kɛ shishifãi. Esa akɛ akɛwo ring ko mli ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi yɛ he ni shishifãi ni haa niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tough and hold dormant seeds in the soil that germinate instantly with moisture. They quickly steal the first flush of water and soil nutrients before planted crops can fully establish their roots.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehiɛɔ dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni baakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant mean it is suffering from a lack of nitrogen, which is a crucial food for plant growth. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen to the newer top leaves to stay alive, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea can fix this problem.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen fioo ko kɛmiiya baai heei amli koni ehi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every time I plant it on the same piece of land back-to-back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land repeatedly exhausts specific nutrients in the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles, leading to better harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaanyɛ ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efite ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainstorm falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ wulu ko baanɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the top of the soil before the crop roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist—rather than right before a downpour—ensures the crop actually drinks the nutrients instead of losing them to runoff.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ baafite lɛ

english: Why do young cocoa trees dry up and die if I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Leaving or planting shade plants like plantain or shade trees creates a cool microclimate that keeps the soil moist and protects young cocoa until its root system is strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni ajieɔ loo aduɔ Ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli waa.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, and they target the tender inner leaves (the whorl) where they are protected from heat, rain, and predators while they eat. Spraying appropriate biopesticides or neem extract directly into the center funnel early in the morning or late evening reaches them effectively.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni amɛtutuaa mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo (rings) lɛ he he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ shwie tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early using neem oil or recommended insecticides stops the curling and restores leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ baa lɛ daalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when rain falls continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but flooded soil starves the roots of oxygen, allowing water-loving fungi and bacteria to attack and rot them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat stress, extreme dry soil, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist through mulching and regular watering helps the plant retain flowers and turn them into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to clear away the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ ahe lɛ etee.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main stem for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving only one primary stem and one or two young suckers allows the main plant to put all its energy into growing a thick stem and heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, kɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni miidara lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight to manufacture food, which is then stored underground as tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the air so they get maximum sunlight and stay off damp ground where fungal rot spreads easily.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops lose weight when I dry them in the sun after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ migbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain a lot of natural water. Sun drying removes this excess moisture, which reduces the weight of the crop but prevents mold from growing, allowing you to store the harvest for a long time without it spoiling.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ amli. Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tsiimɔ baa shi shi ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ toɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee.

english: Why do my stored grains rot quickly if I pack them while they still feel heavy with moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli be mli ni amɛhe wa lolo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: High moisture inside harvested crops creates a warm, damp environment that mold and insects thrive in. Drying your grains thoroughly until they are light makes it impossible for these spoilage organisms to survive.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ la lɛ haa nɛkɛ nibii ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi.

english: Why should I sort my harvested crops into different sizes before taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli awo dalɛi srɔtoi amli lɛ? dani ajie lɛ kpo kɛya jara nɔ

english: Buyers pay different prices based on crop quality and size. When you separate your large, clean produce from damaged or smaller ones, buyers will pay a higher premium price for the top quality, helping you earn more money overall.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛdara ha lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ogbala aduawai kɛ aduawai agboi ni he tse kɛjɛ tsei ni efite loo bibii amli lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baawo nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ kɛha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná shika babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do crop buyers weigh my produce in bags using scales instead of just counting the total number of bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ susuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ sɛkɛl nɔ yɛ sɛkɛl nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakane kotokui lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ lɛ?

english: Weighing measures the exact physical quantity of crop material you have, regardless of bag size. It protects you from getting paid less if your bags are packed tightly and ensures fair pricing based on actual weight in kilograms.
ga: Nibii ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ susuɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni kotoku lɛ da ha Ebuɔ ohe koni onine ashɛ shika fioo nɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ kotoku lɛ ewo mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eha jara ni sa ni damɔ tsiimɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ kilogram mli lɛ nɔ mi

english: What is the best way to make money from the smaller leftover crops that main market buyers refuse to buy?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa shika kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko ni jarayelɔi wuji lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaahe lɛ mli?

english: Smaller or irregular produce can still be sold locally at a discounted rate, processed into dried products, or used as nutritious feed for farm animals. This ensures no part of your harvest is wasted.
ga: Abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ nibii bibii loo nɔ ni afɔɔɔɔ feemɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lolo yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. Afee lɛ nibii ni egbi Aloo akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛhaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi. Enɛ haaa afite okpamɔ lɛ fã ko kwraa.

english: Why does a market buyer offer me less money if my harvested grains have spots or insect damage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ miiha mi shika fioo lɛ? Kɛji midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi ni efite

english: Buyers reduce their price for damaged crops because insects and spots lower the taste, appearance, and shelf life of the final food. Clean, undamaged crops guarantee higher quality products, so buyers pay full price for them.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii efite lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ nɔ, ni no haa naagbee niyenii lɛ ŋɔɔ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ be ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ baa shi. Nibii ni aduɔ ni he tse, ni efiteee lɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ fɛɛ.

english: How do my crops use the water and food inside the soil to grow big fruits?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ koni amɛwo aduawai wuji?

english: Crops use their roots like straws to draw up water and mineral nutrients from the soil. The plant uses sunlight to combine this water and food in its leaves, creating the energy it needs to build big, heavy produce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni tamɔ jwɛi tsuɔ nii kɛgbalaa nu kɛ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ hulu la futuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛ amɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee nibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops droop and look lifeless during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot, plants lose water quickly through their leaves. Drooping is the crop's natural survival mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun and save its internal moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Defoliation ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa baai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa emli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my farmland produce lighter and smaller harvests now compared to when I first cleared the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii ni waaa ni eyɛ bibioo kɛ akɛto be mli ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest, crops remove essential food and nutrients from the soil. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted, so adding organic manure or fertilizer is necessary to replace those lost nutrients and restore your yield weight.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he koni ekɛto niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ ni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tsiimɔ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my crops so they have the best weight and quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops reach their peak weight and nutrition when fully mature, which is usually signaled by dry stalks, firm texture, or changes in skin color. Harvesting too early results in watery, small produce, while waiting too long causes rot and pest damage.
ga: Tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ he kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni egbi, amɛhe ni etsilɛ, loo hewolonɔ su tsakemɔ ni kadiɔ enɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii mra tsɔ lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu kɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agboi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite.

english: If I collect wild oil palm seeds from an old farm, will they grow into productive trees?
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua koo mli mu tso dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ, ani amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii?

english: Wild palm seeds usually produce trees with very thick shells, thin fruit flesh, and low oil yields. Buying improved nursery seedlings ensures your trees grow shorter, mature faster, and produce far more oil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ palm dumɔwui lɛ woɔ tsei ni amɛhewolo lɛ mli edɔ waa, amɛyibii lɛ amli tsei, ni amɛwoɔ mu fioo. Kɛ́ ohe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ afee kuku, amɛbaadara oya, ni amɛbaawo fɔ babaoo.

english: Why is acquiring proper planting knowledge more important than just buying cheap palm seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ aaaná dumɔwui ahe nilee ni sa fe ni ooohe ŋmei dumɔwui ni jara waaa lɛ?

english: Even high-quality seedlings will fail if planted incorrectly, spaced poorly, or neglected. Proper technical knowledge ensures you manage soil, water, and fertilizer correctly so your trees reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ po baanyɛ afite kɛji adu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛji akɛ akafee nɔ ko jogbaŋŋ loo aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ŋaa nilee ni sa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ aná ŋmaakpamɔ hegbɛ ni fa.

english: How can I tell if my district's weather and soil are suitable for growing oil palm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ sa kɛha mu tso ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm thrives best in regions with deep, rich soil and heavy, well-distributed rainfall throughout the year. Areas with very long dry seasons or shallow, rocky soil will cause palm trees to produce fewer and smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ. Hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmei tsei lɛ awo yibii bibii fioo ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: How does a severe dry season affect the way my oil palm trees produce fruit?
ga: Te hɔmɔ ni naa wa ko saa oil palm tsei lɛ ayibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During long dry spells, palm trees conserve water by slowing down leaf production and delaying flower development, which results in fewer fruit bunches being harvested several months later.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Palm tsei buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai akui fioo pɛ akpaa yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ.

english: What is the best way to plant a young oil palm seedling so it does not die after transplanting?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ adu oil palm dumɔwui koni dumɔwui lɛ akagboi yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dig a hole twice as wide as the seedling bag, mix rich topsoil into the hole, plant the seedling at the exact depth it grew in the bag, and transplant at the beginning of the rainy season so roots can establish easily.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ fe dumɔwui kotoku lɛ shii 2. Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ afutu bu lɛ mli. Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni adu amɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to leave so much space between oil palm trees when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ mu tsei ateŋ beni miduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm fronds spread wide to catch sunlight, and their roots reach far for nutrients. Spacing them properly prevents the trees from shading each other out and competing for water, which maximizes fruit production.
ga: Mu tso baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he koni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Ni eshishifãi lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe ni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ nu he. Enɛ baaye abua ni nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Can I grow crops like cassava or food crops between my young oil palm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can plant short-term food crops between young palm trees during the first two years, provided you keep them a few feet away from the palm stems so they don't compete for sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛkɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo pɛ bɔni afee ni amɛkaye hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: How long will it take for my newly planted oil palm tree to produce its first harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-oil palm tso ni midu ehee lɛ baawo eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Improved oil palm varieties typically begin flowering and bearing their first harvestable fruit bunches about three to four years after being transplanted into the main field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akui ni abaakpa aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young oil palm tree turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the tree is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or that the ground is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why is it important for me to clear a weed-free ring around the base of each palm tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie ŋtayaa ni jwɛi bɛ mli ni bɔle ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei tso shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Clearing a circle around the trunk prevents weeds from stealing fertilizer and moisture, stops climbing vines from smothering the tree, and makes it easier to spot pests or apply fertilizer.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli ni ajieɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ekpaa wain tsei akwɔɔ koni ekaye tso lɛ. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana tsɛŋemɔ helai loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. When nitrogen runs low, the plant moves what remains to the newer top leaves, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my cassava cuttings when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmei niji ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing gives each cassava plant its own room to spread roots under the ground and leaves above the ground. If planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, small tubers.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋ lɛ haa yucca tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsu ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eshwaa. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: What causes small round holes in the leaves of my pepper plants, and how does it affect them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te enáa amɛnɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Small holes are usually made by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating the leaves. When leaves are damaged, the plant cannot gather enough sunlight to feed itself properly, which leads to fewer and smaller peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii baa. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ efite lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ abua hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii bibii.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during intense heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun and conserve moisture. As long as they uncurl in the cooler evening, it is a normal way the plant protects itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Shii abɔ ni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he koni amɛkagbi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When they die, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground, nourishing the maize crop that follows.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I remove all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Large shade trees act like natural canopy umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from scorching heat and keeping the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them buried in the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava grows past its prime age, the root converts soft, edible starch into tough woody fibers to support the aging plant above ground. Harvesting on time ensures the tubers stay soft, starchy, and good for eating.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei eda kɛho eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ayeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli ŋmeii ni wa koni ekɛye ebua tsei ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni esa akɛ aye.

english: Why should I not save and replant seeds harvested from high-yielding hybrid maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are carefully created by crossing specific parent plants to produce high yields in the first year. Seeds collected from that harvest lose those special combined traits in the next generation, producing weaker plants with lower yields.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ feɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when there is plenty of rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most farm crops, meaning they steal nutrients and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crops can drink them up, leaving your main crop starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nuɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop seeds after just one short rainfall at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ be kukuoo pɛ sɛɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ osharai yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: The first short rain only wet the top of the soil and is often followed by dry days. If seeds germinate in shallow moisture without follow-up rain, the young sprouts will dry up and die before their roots reach deeper water.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi kukuji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ pɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does millet grow better than other crops when there is very little rain in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei krokomɛi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Millet has deep roots and small leaves that prevent water loss, allowing it to survive long dry spells and poor soils where crops like maize would dry up and die.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai bibii. ni tsiɔ nu ni sɛɛ efoɔ lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ shikpɔji ni ehiii lɛ amli. ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: What makes millet and sorghum good crop choices if rainy seasons are becoming shorter?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛji akɛ ajie nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kuku?

english: Millet and sorghum mature faster and require much less water throughout their life cycle, making them reliable options when rains start late or end early.
ga: Sorghum kɛ sorghum daa oya ni amɛhe ehiaaa nu babaoo yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi sɛɛ loo egbe naa mra.

english: Why do my crops start producing flowers very early when the weather becomes too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi mra be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When crops experience heat or drought stress, they feel threatened and try to reproduce quickly by flowering early so they can leave seeds before dying.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo hɔmɔ Amɛnuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfɔ oya kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ mra lɛ nɔ koni amɛshi dumɔwui yɛ amɛsɛɛ dani amɛgboi.

english: Why do people say that planting beans helps improve my soil for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii adumɔ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that feed on air through their roots and trap natural nitrogen in the soil, which acts like free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What type of soil conditions do bean plants need so their roots do not rot?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ he hiaa ŋmeii tsei koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akafite?

english: Beans prefer loose, well-drained soil because standing water chokes their roots, rots their seeds, and stops them from making soil nutrients.
ga: Beans sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ, efiteɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ, ni ehaaa amɛtswa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that feed on maize to build up.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abele taoɔ lɛ baajɛ mli. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because tall maize grows upward toward the sun while low-growing beans cover the ground to suppress weeds and add nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, nanemɛi adumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ daa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ fioo lɛ anɔ koni akɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni akɛ nitrogen awo sũ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is lacking nitrogen nutrient in the soil or that heavy rains have flooded the roots and stopped them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shishifãi lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni haa amɛmuɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crop seedlings much more than my mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ awui waa fe mi tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak root systems and small leaves, so fast-growing weeds easily steal all their water, fertilizer, and sunlight before the crop can establish itself.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la fɛɛ dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ emaa shi.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the stem roots swell up and the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off naturally, typically 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛji shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ efuu. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the seeds I want to plant are good quality or bad ones that will give me problems?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ hi loo ehiii ni baaha naagbai aba?

english: Good seeds are usually whole, clean, heavy, and free from insect holes or mould. Bad seeds feel light, look cracked or discoloured, and often fail to sprout or produce weak crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ emuu, amɛhe tse, amɛtsii, ni kooloi bu loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Dumɔwui gbohii lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe waaa. Etamɔ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa loo ehiɛ su ni bei pii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ loo ekɛ yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baaa

english: Why are my crop seeds taking so long to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady moisture and good soil contact to wake up and sprout. If the soil is too dry, if the seeds were planted too deep, or if the seeds were old or bad, sprouting will be delayed or fail entirely.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ loo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo ehiii Ekwɛ̃mɔ baahe sɛɛ loo ebaafite kwraa.

english: What should I do about the unwanted weeds popping up from the ground that are bothering my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ jwɛi ni ataooo ni miijɛ shikpɔŋ ni miigba miŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ he?

english: Unwanted plants and weeds steal water, sunlight, and food from your main crop. Clear them early by hoeing or weeding by hand so your crops do not have to fight for survival.
ga: Tsei kɛ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Kɛ ŋmei atsu nii loo okɛ onine ajie jwɛi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Does clearing the spaces between my crop rows really help my small plants sprout better?
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛdaraa. Ani minɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, keeping the space between planting rows clean allows more sunlight, fresh air, and rainwater to reach your young plants directly without weeds stealing those resources.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ aha he ni kã dumɔwui akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa Kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shɛɔ odumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni ehaaa jwɛi aju nakai nibii lɛ

english: Why is it important to leave space between the rows when planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ beni aduɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Leaving proper space between rows ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and root room to sprout and grow into a healthy, strong crop.
ga: Shi gbɛ ni sa yɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ teŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni yeɔ emuu.

english: What will happen to my young crops if I plant them too close to each other without enough inter-row space?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they crowd each other out and stay small and weak because they are competing for the same limited water, light, and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baabua amɛhe naa ni amɛbaafee bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: How often do my newly planted crops need water in order to sprout well?
ga: Shii enyiɛ mi tsei ni midu ehee lɛ he hiaa nu koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Newly planted crops and young sprouts need frequent watering to keep the top layer of soil damp. Drought or dry soil during the early sprouting phase can easily kill young seedlings.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ tsei ni adu ehee kɛ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu shii abɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli egbi loo egbi yɛ shishijee be mli ni tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are not getting enough water from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Young crops that lack water will look limp, their leaves will start wilting or turning yellow, and their growth will slow down or stop completely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni nu efo mli lɛ baafee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Baai lɛ baabɔi gboimɔ loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni dalɛ baa shi loo ebaakpa kwraa.

english: Why are my young crop sprouts staying small instead of growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ hiɔ shi bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara lɛ?

english: Small sprouts stay stunted if they lack regular water, if they are crowded together without enough row space, or if bad weeds are stealing nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bean tsei bibii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ nu bɛ amɛhe daa. aloo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ he kome ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Aloo kɛji jwɛi gbohii miiju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is the best way to help small seedlings grow strong right after they come out of the soil?
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ abuaa dumɔwui bibii ni amɛdaraa Te eji kɛji akɛ amɛdara waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Give young seedlings frequent water, remove surrounding weeds immediately, and make sure they have enough room and light to expand their roots and leaves.
ga: Okɛ nu awo dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli shii abɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okwɛ koni amɛná he ko kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates living umbrellas that protect the seedlings until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Cassava is not recommended near young cocoa trees because its aggressive root system steals water and soil nutrients from the cocoa, and its bushy growth blocks too much light.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ akɛ ŋmei atsu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsei bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi ni boteɔ mli lɛ juɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ. ni kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ baatsi la babaoo naa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, damp conditions. When tree canopies are too dense, rainwater stays trapped on the pods, allowing the fungus to grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli eyi tsɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nu baakpɛtɛ ŋta lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmeii daa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa branches curling up and showing tiny dry brown holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Brown ni egbi?

english: This damage is caused by small insects called capsids or mirids that bite into young shoots and leaves to suck out sap, injected poison that causes the surrounding plant tissue to die.
ga: Kooloi bibii kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ kapsid loo myrid. ni ŋmɔɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai koni ekɛnu nu lɛ Okɛ poison ni gbeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support with water and nutrients. The tree drops excess flowers on purpose so it has enough energy to grow a few healthy pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aye abua amɛ. Tso lɛ shĩɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fioo komɛi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off some of the healthy branches from my adult cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ tso niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ komɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded or unproductive branches so sunlight and air can reach the main trunk where pods grow, which lowers humidity and prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni mli eyi obɔ loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Enɛ ji koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ tso titri lɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm's soil is running out of food for the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛha tsei lɛ?

english: When soil nutrients are low, crops show warning signs like yellowish leaves, slow growth, small pod sizes, or trees taking much longer to produce flowers.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Aloo tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do weeds in my farm make my cocoa trees produce fewer pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in the soil by stealing water and fertilizer intended for your cocoa trees. They also create damp hiding places for harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛhaa o-cacao tsei lɛ nɔ. Amɛfeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ hu.

english: Why do I need to heap my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation under plantain leaves uses natural heat to kill the seed inside the bean and bring out the sweet chocolate flavor and smell that buyers look for.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ plantain baai ashishi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. ni ejie tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ kpo

english: How does a long dry season affect the way my cocoa trees behave?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ ajeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During dry spells, cocoa trees shed leaves and drop small pods to save water. Covering the soil around the tree roots with dried leaves helps keep moisture in the ground longer.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ baai ni efoɔ ŋmeii bibii. Bɔni afee ni eye ebua ni akɛ nu akafite Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I plant them in full sunlight without any plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn under direct heat and intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella of shade and keeps the soil moist, protecting the young trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbaashã yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can pass through easily. This prevents excess humidity that causes black pod disease, while directing the tree's energy into developing bigger and healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to lift and stake my yam vines on tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awó sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni adu yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up to capture maximum sunlight for energy while keeping them off damp ground where fungal diseases and rot can easily spread. Better sun exposure directly results in larger underground tubers.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni emɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ akabɔ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency, often caused when heavy rains wash topsoil nitrogen deeper into the ground beyond the reach of young roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps restore green growth and boosting plant energy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsi nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahewalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn yellow and drop even though I am watering the farm every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering floods the soil pores and prevents oxygen from reaching the plant roots, effectively suffocating them and washing away soluble nutrients. Crops prefer soil that is consistently moist but well-drained.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli woɔ nu, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ hoɔ. Tso lɛ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ shi nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some maize plants in my field grow large cobs while plants right next to them produce small, weak cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Uneven cob size usually happens when seeds are planted at unequal depths or spaced too closely together, causing neighboring plants to fight over sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every stalk gets equal resources.
ga: Cob dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee loo amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why do tomato prices fall drastically during peak harvest times in Ghana, and how can I plan around this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato jara baa shi waa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mato gbɛjianɔ yɛ enɛ he?

english: When most farmers harvest at the exact same time, the market gets flooded with perishable tomatoes, driving prices down. Adjusting your planting calendar to harvest slightly earlier or later in the season lets you sell when market supply is low and prices peak.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli Jarayelihe lɛ eyi kɛ tomatoi ni fiteɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji nibii ajara ni baa shi. Kɛ́ otsake odumɔ kalanda lɛ koni okpa nii mra fioo loo sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni jara lɛ hu yaa hiɛ waa lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, signaled when lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a tuft of leaves at the top. You can carefully dig around one outer root to inspect its size and starch firmness before harvesting the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni etsɔɔ be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Shi baai akuu ko yɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni ona kɛji amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe wa dani okpa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep dropping off before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when pepper plants experience stress from irregular watering, high heat, or a lack of essential soil minerals like phosphorus. Consistent soil moisture and balanced soil nutrients help flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji pepper tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus ni bɛ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove the small extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers draw water and nutrients away from the main plantain stem. Removing all but one strong replacement sucker ensures that the main tree receives full nutrition to yield a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tsei wuji lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie sucker ni mli wa lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo plantains ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tseee ni ebɛ hewalɛ waa beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow thick stalks and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding compost helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he ko ni dɔɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a natural way to conserve water and survive drought. Adding mulch around the base of the plant helps keep the soil moist so the plant stays green longer.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Mulch ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants curl up tightly on very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which prevents them from losing too much moisture through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ baa shi lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does adding animal manure to my farm help me get more bags of grain at harvest?
ga: Te miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Animal manure enriches the soil with essential nutrients and improves its ability to hold water. Healthy, well-fed soil feeds your crops continuously, leading to stronger plants and a much higher harvest yield.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha onibii lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ waa, ni amɛnáa yibii babaoo babaoo.

english: Why do I need to heap soft soil into mounds around the base of my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ naa lɛ miwoɔ gɔji ni bɔleɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Creating loose soil mounds gives yam tubers room to expand easily underground without hitting hard dirt, which allows the roots to grow much larger and smoother.
ga: Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same farm field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: What causes small holes to appear all over the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by pests like caterpillars or beetles eating the plant. Checking under the leaves early in the morning allows you to catch and manage these insects before they damage the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu yɛ baai amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni omɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be plucked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ egbɔ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the beans inside have fully developed sweet pulp necessary for good fermentation.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Nɛkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fã nɛɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ŋɔɔ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.
