english: Why must I dry my harvested maize completely before putting it into sacks for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛwo kotokui amli koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Wet or damp maize stored in sacks rapidly develops mold and dangerous toxins that spoil the grain. Thoroughly drying the maize ensures it stays safe to eat and holds its market value longer.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ loo ni edɔ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ oya. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ayeɔ, ni ehiɔ shi yɛ jara nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and roll up during the dry season even when I water them once a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli moŋ?

english: Crops like maize need consistent moisture at their roots during hot periods. Watering only once a week in high heat causes severe heat stress and shallow root drying, forcing the leaves to curl inward to prevent water loss.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa he miihia ni nu ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ kɛ latsaa he haomɔ ni naa wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ baa. Ha baai lɛ atsɔ mli koni nu akaje mli.

english: How do I know if I am giving my pepper plants too much water on my irrigated plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu miiwo mi-pepper tsei ni yɔɔ he ni mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ fe nine?

english: When pepper plants receive too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow, drop off, and the roots turn soft and dark. Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe, and overwatering suffocates them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni akɛhaa fe nine lɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ.

english: What will happen to my tomato crop if my regular water source stops unexpectedly for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni mikɛhaa daa lɛ kpa trukaa otsii enyɔ?

english: Tomatoes have shallow roots and high water demands during flowering and fruiting. A sudden two-week drop in water causes flowers to drop, stems to wilt, and fruits to develop rot at the bottom.
ga: Tomato shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ehe hiaa nu babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Nu ni baa shi trukaa otsii enyɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. tso ni egbo kɛ aduawai ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ

english: Why does water sit on top of my soil for days instead of sinking in to feed my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo nu mli koni ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Hard or compacted soil prevents water from reaching crop roots. When water sits on top, it starves the plant roots of oxygen and can cause root rot instead of nourishing the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ tsei shishifãi ahe. Kɛ nu lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi Ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my main crops as soon as I start watering my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛji mibɔi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu shwiemɔ pɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally hardier and have deeper roots adapted to grab water and soil nutrients instantly, allowing them to overpower young crops unless cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei bibii anɔ kunim ja ajie amɛ oya.

english: Why did my crop leaves burn and dry up after I put fertilizer on the soil during a dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil creates a high salt concentration that pulls water out of crop roots, causing the leaves to scorch and dry up.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo baa, ni no gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are my commercial hybrid crop seeds producing low yields when I grow them using only rainfall and no extra chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo beni mikɛ nu ni nugbɔ nɛɔ pɛ tsuɔ nii ni mikɛ tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he lɛ duɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Commercial high-yield crop varieties are specially bred to require high amounts of water, fertilizer, and pest control. Without these continuous inputs, they often perform worse than native local varieties.
ga: Atsɔ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ebi nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ saji ni yaa nɔ nɛɛ bɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ amɛtsuɔ nii ni ehiii fe maŋ lɛ mli kooloi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes plants to grow tall and weak instead of spending energy producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of the dry season if I do not have a reliable water supply?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛji mibɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need ground moisture during their first few weeks to sprout roots. Planting in dry soil without water causes the cuttings to dry out and die before roots can develop.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ lɛ he miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ajɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Which crops perform best when I have access to year-round water supply on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miná nu jɛɛhe ni mikɛtsuɔ nii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: High-value, short-cycle vegetables like tomatoes, onions, sweet peppers, and cabbage thrive under continuous year-round water supply because they need constant moisture to produce heavy yields.
ga: Aduawai ni jara wa waa, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ tomato, sabolai, bell peppers kɛ cabbage shwereɔ yɛ nu jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbiɔ ni hulutsoo be ahi shi be fɛɛ be koni amɛná nibii babaoo.

english: Why are my oil palm trees growing tall but giving me very little fruit to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ kɛlɛ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need regular fertilizer, proper pruning, and sufficient water to produce heavy fruit bunches. Without proper nutrients and clearing of dead fronds, the tree spends its energy growing tall instead of forming palm fruit.
ga: Oil palm tsei lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha amɛ daa. proper pruning Ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha yibii ni tsii aba. Kɛ́ niyenii ni sa kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ ajiemɔ bɛ lɛ, Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ baawo ŋmei yibii lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛdaraa.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce fruit bunches that yield very little oil when pressed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔ fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛmimɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Low oil yield often happens if the trees lack potassium during fruit development, if bad seed varieties were planted, or if the flowers were not properly pollinated during the flowering period.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ potassium yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui gbohii loo kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: How can I tell if the oil palm seedlings I want to buy will actually give a good harvest years later?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mu tsei ni misumɔɔ ni mahe lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: High-yielding varieties, like certified Tenera seedlings, come from approved nurseries and have thick fruit flesh with thin shells. Planting uncertified seeds from local markets often leads to trees with thick shells and very little oil flesh.
ga: Nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ Tenera dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli. Ejɛɔ hei ni afɔɔ yɛ ni awo he odase akɛ eyɛ aduawai loo ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ haa tsei ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it a problem if I plant my oil palm trees too close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji naagba kɛji midu mu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When oil palms are planted too close, their big fronds overlap and block sunlight from reaching each other. This competition for light and soil food causes the trees to produce fewer and smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ adu mu tso ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai wuji lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Akaŋshii ni akɛwoɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii he lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ aduawai akui fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Can I grow crops like cassava or maize between my young oil palm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first two to three years while the palm trees are small, you can grow short-season food crops between the rows, provided you keep them a safe distance from the palm trunks so they do not steal nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii kukuji yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ateŋ. Esa akɛ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the fronds on my oil palm trees turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing fronds usually mean the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium, or that the ground is flooded and waterlogged, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What kind of soil is best for growing oil palm trees so they produce well?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ ni sa kɛha mu tso ni aduɔ koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Oil palms perform best in deep, well-drained loamy soil that retains moisture well but does not hold stagnant water, as soggy roots easily rot and stunt the tree's growth.
ga: Oil palm tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ shi ehiɛɛɛ nu mli Shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear a ring of weeds around the base of each oil palm tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ ni bɔle mu tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds around the trunk steal water and nutrients meant for the tree, and they also hide pests. Clearing a wide circle around the base ensures the palm gets all the fertilizer and moisture you apply.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu teeɔ. Kɛ́ oshi kooloo ni mli kwɔ ni obɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower fronds on my oil palm trees drooping and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: While older lower fronds naturally die as the tree grows, widespread drooping often indicates that the tree is suffering from drought stress or needs to be pruned to help fresh fronds grow properly.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni tso lɛ daa lɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, Extensive defoliation tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo ehe miihia ni afolɔ tso lɛ koni eye ebua baai heei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many years after planting will it take before my oil palm trees start producing fruit bunches?
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-oil palm tso lɛ aje yibii akui awomɔ shishi?

english: With good care, proper weed control, and fertilizer, a young oil palm tree will usually start producing its first harvestable fruit bunches about three to four years after being transplanted into the field.
ga: kɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa Jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ shishi aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant three maize seeds in one hole instead of just planting one by one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ yɛ bu kome mli moŋ fe ni madu eko shikome lɛ?

english: Planting three seeds per hole acts as insurance. If insects eat one seed or another fails to sprout, you will still have healthy plants growing without leaving empty, wasted spaces on your farm.
ga: Dumɔwui etɛ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ ji inshuɔrans. Kɛji kooloo ko ye dumɔwui lɛ eko lɛ ekwɛɛɛ. Obaaná tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lolo ni oshiŋ he ko ni efite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does the size of the cassava stem or yam seed I plant affect how big my tubers will grow?
ga: Ani bɔ ni cassava tso loo sweet potato dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ da ha lɛ saa bɔ ni mi-tubers lɛ baadara aha lɛ he?

english: Yes, larger planting materials contain more stored energy, which gives the young crop a stronger start to build deep roots and produce bigger tubers during harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, adafitswaa woji wuji ni miiya hiɛ lɛ baaná hewalɛ babaoo ni ato. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Should I cut off the small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Ani ajie plantain shishifã titri lɛ?

english: Yes, you should remove extra suckers so they do not steal water and nutrients from the mother tree. Leaving just one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ baawo plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot tolerate strong direct heat. They need shade crops like plantains grown beside them to block intense sunlight until they grow older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni ekɛha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara

english: Why is my cassava growing plenty of tall green leaves but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen. The plant spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, sucking out the sap and spreading plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa.

english: What happens if I plant my tomato seedlings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight for sunlight, air, and soil food. Crowded plants stay weak and create a humid environment where fungal diseases spread quickly.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and quickly steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your main plants need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otso titri lɛ koni enyɛ eda oya lɛ.

english: How will I know that my maize is completely dry and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husk leaves turn completely brown and dry, and a dark black spot appears at the base of the grain kernel when you peel it off.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa kwraa ni egbi. Ni ŋmeii diji ni tsuɔ waa jeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi kɛji ojie amɛ.

english: Why do my yams start to rot quickly after I harvest them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they get cut or bruised during digging, or if they are stored in hot, unventilated rooms where moisture builds up and attracts decay fungi.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Enɛ buaa ŋmɔtɔ naa ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my farmland?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts like a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for your crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha onibii.

english: Spreading dry grass or dry leaves around your crops is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and suppresses weeds.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni ooogbɛ oshwã Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni etsiɔ jwɛi anaa

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when insects attack the flowers. Regular watering during dry spells helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central shoot of the plant during the day, and applying targeted pest control early in the morning or evening helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies are attacking the plant. Controlling these insects early prevents further leaf damage and disease spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, miitutua tso lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite baai lɛ ni helai akagbɛ ashwã babaoo.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged ground because they cannot breathe in standing water. Planting cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak stems and a much smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa baa.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛfi mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground on wooden stakes lets the leaves catch maximum sunlight to produce food, which directly results in larger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Enɛ saa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds away from my young cocoa trees during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young cocoa trees for limited soil water during dry periods. Keeping the base of young trees clear helps them survive the dry season without drying out.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tsei bibii lɛ ashishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore the green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my yam crop produce huge leafy vines but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ wain tso baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the yam plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and vines above ground instead of expanding its tubers below. Using balanced nutrients ensures the plant feeds the tuber.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ wain tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbala yitso lɛ mli yɛ shishi lɛ Niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shaded farms during the rainy season. Pruning heavy branches to let in sunlight and applying recommended fungicides helps keep the pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni amɛyɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ amli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants roll up and curl tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Spraying with organic neem oil or appropriate insecticides helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops on soil mounds or on flat land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔŋ nɔ loo he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Planting on raised mounds or ridges is ideal for root crops like yams and cassava because it softens the soil for roots to expand easily and prevents waterlogging, while flat ground works fine for grains like maize in light, well-drained soils.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya, ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I spend time clearing weeds around my young crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛjie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ ji daa.

english: Weeds steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops, and they also host harmful insects. Regular weeding ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast and give a big harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli Eji he ko hu ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they can produce any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when the soil dries out completely between waterings, or when there is poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ loo be mli ni pollination bɛ jogbaŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my plantain suckers take so long to yield fruit after planting?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if too many young shoots are allowed to crowd around one parent plant. Pruning extra suckers so only 2 or 3 strong stems remain per stand gives the main stem enough nutrients to fruit quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he. single mother tree Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he koni ashi ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii oya.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't spoil in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha nikpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce plenty of leaves in the heavy rains but very few seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain during flowering damages cowpea blossoms and prevents proper seed formation. Cowpeas yield better grain when planted towards the end of the rainy season so they flower in dry weather.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ fiteɔ jwɛi lɛ ni ehaaa dumɔwui lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas woɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee, no hewɔ lɛ ewoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests after I plant crops on it continuously for five years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni midu lɛ be fɛɛ be afii enumɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without giving the soil a break removes vital nutrients every season, causing the land to become depleted and less productive over time.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee shi lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: My farm used to grow thick and green like a forest, but now my plants look thin and weak. What happened to my land?
ga: Kulɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔji tamɔ koo. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ mitsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Mɛni ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Over time, heavy farming drains the natural plant food (nutrients) stored in the ground. When these nutrients run out, the land loses its ability to support lush growth.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli ni tsii lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ ba naagbee lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has run out of nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Tired or depleted soil usually shows in your crops—they stay small, grow very slowly, have weak leaves, and yield far less harvest than they used to.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite loo efite lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo yɛ onibii amli. Akɛni sũ lɛ daraaa hewɔ lɛ, edaa blɛoo kwraa, eyɛ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why is wild bush vegetation no longer growing back as thick on my land after I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei bibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild plants need fertile soil to grow densely. When farming depletes the soil's nutrients, even natural weeds and bushes struggle to grow back strongly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ he miihia koo mli tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo. Beni okwaayeli haa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii po bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops remaining small and refusing to grow bigger after they germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ji bibioo ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaada agbo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When plants remain stunted and 'just sit there,' it is a sign that the soil lacks the basic food (nutrients) the crops need to build big stems and broad leaves.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi ni egbɔjɔ ni ‘Eta jɛmɛ’ lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa (nutrients) bɛ. Ehe miihia ni tsei akwɛ̃ tsei agboi kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops look healthy right after sprouting but stop growing shortly after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ shi amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds use their own stored energy to sprout, but once that energy is used up, they rely on the soil. If the soil is depleted, the plant's growth immediately stalls.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ tee lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ sũ lɛ nɔ egbɔ lɛ, tso lɛ dalɛ baakpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops dry, underdeveloped, and blowing away easily in the wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ egbi, edarako jogbaŋŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Leaves need nutrients like nitrogen from the soil to grow strong and leafy. Without enough nutrients, plant leaves develop poorly, stay weak, and break off easily.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia baai lɛ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfee baai. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛkuɔ oya.

english: What can I do to bring life and strength back to my exhausted farm land?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛ wala kɛ hewalɛ aba miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore depleted soil by adding animal manure or compost, planting legumes like beans that rebuild soil fertility, or letting the land rest for a period.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. loo amɛŋmɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe kɛyashi be ko

english: Will leaving my land without planting anything on it for a season help it recover?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mishi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni miduuu nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, leaving land to rest (fallowing) gives nature time to break down organic matter and refill the soil with essential nutrients naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ) lɛ haa adebɔɔ be ni ekɛgbalaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why did my parents get big crops from this same land years ago, but my crops today grow poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifɔlɔi ná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɛkɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ? Shi ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Every harvest takes nutrients out of the soil. Decades of farming without putting nutrients back through manure or fallowing slowly drains the soil's natural strength over generations.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛbaatsu okwaayeli he nii ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo ŋmeii ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuuu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ lɛ afite fiofio yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a canopy that protects seedlings from harsh heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning dense branches to let sunlight and air circulate through the canopy helps keep the pods dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: This yellowing pattern is a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure early in the growing season corrects this deficiency.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa lɛ afee baai eŋɔli Ni akɛ ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa nɛɛ.

english: Why does swamp rice survive in standing water while my maize crop rots when the field floods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have internal air passages in their stems that carry oxygen down to roots underwater. Maize roots do not have these passages, so stagnant water prevents them from breathing and causes root rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa amɛmu, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using certified disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting stops the virus from damaging your yield.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ okɛ ŋmei ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ tsu nii beni oduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf surface area to sunlight for energy. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, which prevents fungal rot and helps the plant send energy downward to produce bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ahiɛ afee babaoo koni amɛná hulu la kɛha hewalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off during periods of sudden heat stress or severe drought. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering regularly and mulching around the base keeps root temperatures stable.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are my hot pepper plants staying short and dropping their leaves before producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: This often happens when water collects at the roots due to poor soil drainage. Pepper plants require loose, well-draining soil so their root systems can absorb oxygen and nutrients freely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Pepper tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above the soil if the nuts mature under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After pollination, groundnut flowers produce small stalks called 'pegs' that bend downward and grow into the dirt where the nuts develop. Keeping the soil loose around the base allows these pegs to enter easily.
ga: after pollination Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Shishitoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do some plantain shoots produce big bunches while others stay small and weak on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain komɛi shwereɔ kui wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers with broad leaves early on take energy away from the main stem. Selecting narrow-leaved 'sword suckers' for planting ensures strong growth and larger plantain bunches.
ga: Mra mli lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ shishi. ‘Sword suckers’ ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ahala kɛha dumɔ haa plantain tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are sick with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Sick cocoa trees often show clear signs such as swollen branches, yellowing or patterned leaves, deformed pods, or sudden leaf loss. If you notice these changes, your tree likely has an infection like the Swollen Shoot virus or Black Pod disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ tsei niji ni efuu, baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ mfoniri, ŋmeii ni efite, loo baai ni elaaje trukaa. Kɛji oyɔse tsakemɔi nɛɛ Ekolɛ otso lɛ yɛ hela ko tamɔ Swollen Shoot virus loo Black Pod hela.

english: What actually causes cocoa trees to catch diseases in the farm?
ga: Mɛni diɛŋtsɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ yeɔ hela yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Crop diseases are caused by tiny organisms like viruses and fungi. Insects like mealybugs can carry viruses from tree to tree, while wet weather and dirty pruning tools help fungal diseases spread.
ga: Tse helai jɛɔ nibii bibii tamɔ muawai kɛ ŋmei kɛbaa. Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs baanyɛ aŋɔ helai kɛjɛ tso mli kɛya tso kroko mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni he tseee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your young plants are getting too much direct sunlight, lack essential soil nutrients, or are suffering from water stress or early pest attacks. Providing shade and keeping the soil moist helps them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo amɛmiina naagbai ni jɛɔ nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Are the new hybrid cocoa seedlings better at resisting sickness than my old trees?
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid Ani helai nyɛɔ eshiɔ fe mi kookoo tso momo lɛ?

english: Yes, modern hybrid cocoa varieties developed by agricultural institutes are specially bred to grow faster, bear more pods, and resist common diseases better than older cocoa varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhei fee lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Ha pods babaoo ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ jogbaŋŋ fe kookoo henɔi momoi lɛ

english: Why do extension officers advise me to cut down old cocoa trees that still give me a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ jɛmɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei momo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lolo lɛ?

english: Old, diseased cocoa trees yield very little cocoa and act as hidden homes for pests and viruses. Cutting them down completely stops disease from spreading to healthy areas and makes room for high-yielding new trees.
ga: Kakao tsei ni egbɔ ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ koko fioo ko pɛ, ni amɛhiɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Amɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã hei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni oha gbɛ aha tsei heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cocoa farm has become too old to produce a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa trees produce best between 10 and 25 years of age. When trees grow very tall, develop frequent infections, and produce fewer pods despite good rains and fertilizer, they have reached the end of their productive life.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25, beni tsei lɛ daraa waa lɛ. Na helai ni baa mɔ nɔ shii abɔ ni ekɛ pods fioo pɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai fɛɛ sɛɛ. Nakai tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛsɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ lɛ naagbee.

english: How long should I wait to plant new seedlings after removing old, diseased cocoa trees?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu dumɔwui heei beni mijie kookoo tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to clear the old roots and wait a few months before replanting. This break allows pests and disease organisms in the soil to die off so your new seedlings enter a safe environment.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ shishifãi momoi lɛ ahe ni omɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi dani odu eheei. Nɛkɛ mligbalamɔ nɛɛ gbeɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui heei lɛ bote shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe mli.

english: What happens to my soil after I completely cut down an old cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mifo kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When large trees are cut, the bare soil gets direct hot sun and heavy rain, which can wash away rich topsoil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or food crops helps keep the soil moist and protected for your new cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo tsei wuji Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baaná hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ. ni baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ adumɔ, tamɔ plantains loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ o-cacao tso hee lɛ he.

english: Can diseases on my neighbor's cocoa farm spread to my own land?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa diseases do not respect farm borders. Insects, wind, flowing rainwater, and shared harvesting tools can easily carry infections from a neighbor's sick farm right onto your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo hela lɛ ebuuu ŋmɔ mli husui. Kplukai, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ ajie helai kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Should I inform neighboring farmers if I discover a serious disease on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ adafi kɛji mikɛ hela ko ni naa wa kpe yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, talking with neighboring farmers allows everyone to inspect their trees early and control the sickness together. Managing crop diseases requires teamwork across farms to protect the whole community's harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ni akɛaawie lɛ haa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kwɛɔ amɛtsei lɛ amli mra. kɛ helai akudɔmɔ ekomefeemɔ Tsei ahe helai akwɛmɔ biɔ kuu nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ koni abu akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods early and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm to stop the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I see dark, oozing sores forming on the bark of my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Dark sores on tree trunks are usually caused by stem borers or fungal infections that enter through open wounds. Trimming dead branches and painting protective coating on the open spots keeps pests and diseases out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pilamɔi diji ni yɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ jɛɔ tso lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɔɔ pilamɔi ni agbele mli lɛ amli kɛboteɔ mli lɛ mli. Niji ni egboi lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni akɛ penti ni buɔ mɔ he awo he fɛɛ he ni agbele lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai anaa.

english: Why are the veins in my cassava leaves turning yellow while the rest of the leaf stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ amli fãji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf veins are a common sign of cassava mosaic virus or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil. Planting clean, disease-free stem cuttings prevents this virus from showing up on your farm.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cassava mosaic virus loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Niji ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akaje kpo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the base stems of my tomato plants turning soft and dark near the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe feɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ amɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Soft, dark stems at the soil line are caused by root rot or damping-off fungus, which happens when the soil stays too wet. Improving soil drainage and not overwatering helps keep the stems firm and healthy.
ga: Shishifãi ni egbo loo ŋmeii ni mli efɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ nu shwieee nɔ fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it recommended to spray my crops early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ tsofa lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: In the early morning, plants open leaf pores to take in air and moisture without liquid evaporating quickly. In afternoon heat, liquid sprays dry up before the crop can absorb them properly.
ga: Yɛ leebi lɛ, dumɔ tso lɛ, ni ogbele eshishifãi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba mli ni ohaaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baagbi dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If a branch breaks off my cocoa tree, do I need to cover the open wound?
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo nine ko fã lɛ, ani esa akɛ maha pilamɔ ni egbele lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, open wounds on trees attract insects and fungal spores just like open cuts on human skin. Cutting the broken branch cleanly and applying protective tree paint stops disease from penetrating inside.
ga: Hɛɛ, pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ gbɔmɔ hewolo nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ niji ni ekumɔ lɛ ni okɛ mfoniri awo tso lɛ he koni helai akabote mli.

english: How does a crop disease spread from one sick plant to healthy ones next to it?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛyaa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Diseases spread through wind, rain splashes carrying fungal spores, or dirty farm tools like cutlasses. Cleaning your pruning tools with soap or sanitizer between trees prevents spreading disease.
ga: Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee tamɔ dadei. Kɛ́ akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai tsuɔ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe nii yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the tips of my maize leaves turn dark brown and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Dry, dark leaf tips are usually caused by extreme heat stress or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer keeps the leaves green and growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni egbi ni eyɛ ediŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young plantain leaves look pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves mean the plant is hungry for nutrients or is not getting enough sunlight. Adding compost or animal manure around the root zone helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia tso lɛ loo enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my vegetable leaves curling up with dark spots along the veins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fãji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with dark spots are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids that spread viruses as they feed. Spraying organic solutions like neem oil controls these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids, ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe, ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: My cassava leaves look twisted and small, but my neighbor says it is not a disease—how can a plant look sick if it doesn't have a disease?
ga: Mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ bibioo. Shi akutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ hela mɔɔɔ lɛ. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso ko afee tamɔ helatsɛ kɛji hela bɛ ehe?

english: Plants can show unusual growth because of poor soil conditions, extreme weather, or lack of water rather than a viral or bacterial infection. These are called growth abnormalities, meaning the plant is simply struggling to grow properly due to environmental stress.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ ajie dalɛ ni ejaaa kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli loo hela ko ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ dalɛi ni ejaaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi ahewɔ.

english: Why are my maize stalks staying very short this season even though I don't see any insects eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ efee kuku yɛ be nɛɛ mli be mli ni minako kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: When plants fail to grow tall despite having no visible pests or diseases, it is usually a growth abnormality caused by missing soil nutrients like nitrogen or poor root access to water.
ga: Be mli ni tsei nyɛɛɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni anaaa lɛ bɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛbaa ji dalɛ ni ejaaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are struggling because of a disease or just bad growing conditions?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ hela loo shihilɛ ni ehiii ni eyɔɔ mli kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Diseases usually cause spots, rotting, or spreading infections on leaves and stems. General growth abnormalities—like stunted stems or poor overall growth—happen when the plant lacks water, shade, or soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Nɔ ni haa tsei lɛ daraa ni ejaaa tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egbɔjɔ loo amɛdalɛ fɛɛ ni ehiii Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my tomatoes grow in strange bent shapes instead of normal round fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee nɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Yɛ tso yibii ni yɔɔ kokroo ni yɔɔ daa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Deformed or strange fruit shapes are often non-disease growth abnormalities caused by irregular watering or harsh heat while the flowers were developing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni efite loo amɛhe yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ ji dalɛ ni ejaaa ni jeee hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ amɛ be fɛɛ be loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: If my yam vines remain thin and green but refuse to grow long, does that mean my crop has a sickness?
ga: Kɛji mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɔ shi mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi eŋmɛɛɛ wala sɛɛ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hela?

english: Not necessarily. Growth problems can happen when the soil is too hard for root expansion or lacks essential nutrients, causing stunted growth without an actual disease being present.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Naagbai ni kɔɔ dalɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni hela diɛŋtsɛ baaa.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer cause my crops to grow strangely?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ?

english: Yes, excessive or unbalanced fertilizer can cause physiological growth abnormalities, making plants develop weak stems or heavy leaves without producing proper fruits, even though no disease is involved.
ga: Hɛɛ, fɔmɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli fe nine loo ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha gbɔmɔtso lɛ dalɛ afee nɔ ni ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo baai ni tsii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii ni sa. Kɛji akɛ obɛ hela ko po.

english: Why are my cocoa seedlings struggling to grow bigger even though their leaves look completely healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbaai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Hard or compacted soil around the roots can prevent young plants from absorbing food and water, leading to poor growth performance rather than a plant disease.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso bibioo lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni ehiii yɛ tsei ahela najiaŋ

english: My garden egg plants are dropping their flowers before fruiting—is this a disease spreading through my field?
ga: Eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite efɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii. Ani hela ko ni miigbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ nɛ?

english: Flower drop is typically a growth response triggered by severe heat, dry spells, or nutrient imbalance rather than a contagious plant disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni naa wa, hulutsoo be, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hetoo. moŋ fe hela ko ni tsei kɛbaa

english: My plantain leaves are curling up and stopping growth in the hot sun—is there a chemical spray I should buy to cure this?
ga: Mi plantain baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛkpa shweremɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ani esa akɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛtsa enɛ?

english: Leaf curling from high heat is a natural reaction to sun stress, not a disease. Chemical disease sprays will not fix it; the crop simply needs adequate water and shade.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni jɛɔ hulutsoo mli haomɔ mli baa, shi jeee hela. Tsofai ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he lɛ nyɛŋ asaa. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia tsei.

english: Why are crops in one section of my farm growing very tall while those right next to them remain very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ daa babaoo yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daraaa lɛ? Eyɛ bibioo kwraa lolo

english: Uneven growth across the same field is usually caused by differences in soil fertility or moisture retention across the land, resulting in localized growth abnormalities rather than a spreading plant disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa nibii ni ejaaa baa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dalɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, e gbɛɔ tsehi a he hiɔ.

english: Why should I spend money to buy improved seed varieties instead of just saving seeds from the tomatoes I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe? Mohu ɔ, i ngɔ dumɔwuhi kɛ je tomato nɛ i kpa ngɛ jeha nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ mi.

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops lose their strength over generations and get sick easily. Improved seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests and diseases, withstand dry spells, and yield bigger, uniform fruits that buyers pay more for.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli, ni hela mɔɔ amɛ oya. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo jɛmɛ kooloi bibii kɛ helai. Ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ kpeɔ ni ekɛ nibii ni da ni yaa nɔ daa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow big green leaves. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant pulls what little food it has from its old bottom leaves to feed the new leaves on top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa baai agboi ni eŋɔli. Beni nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii fioo fɛɛ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce so many bright flowers, but then the flowers drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni kpɛɔ babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or lacks nutrients like calcium. When the plant feels stressed by bad weather or poor feeding, it drops its flowers to conserve energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni faaa. Beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo niyenii ni ehiii haa tso lɛ haoɔ lɛ. Ebaafɔ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni eha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that suck invisible plant food out of the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the legumes, that food stays behind in the earth to help your next maize crop grow strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ shwieɔ tsei aniyenii ni anaaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua o-ŋmei tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my tomato plants in the middle of the day under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi nu ni mikɛhaa mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering in the hot sun causes water to evaporate into the air before roots can drink it. Additionally, water droplets left on hot leaves act like small burning glasses and create a warm, moist home for leaf diseases to grow.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni ashiɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni eshã ni ehaa shia ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ kɛhaa baai ahe helai ni baa lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together on the same land, won't I harvest twice as much cassava?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa yɛ he kome lɛ, Ani manyɛ mafee ŋmei ni mikpaa lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and food. Instead of getting many big, heavy tubers, you will end up with thin plants and tiny, woody roots that carry little market value.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ, ni no najiaŋ lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo. Ebatsɔ tso bibioo ko ni shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli. kɛ jarayeli jara bibioo ko

english: Why do my maize stems easily bend over and fall flat on the ground after a short rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are weak or shallow, or when it lacks potassium to build strong, woody stems. Putting soil around the base of the stems (heaping) and feeding the soil properly gives the plant strong anchor roots to stand against wind.
ga: Abɛi baashwie eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ. aloo be mli ni potassium ni akɛbaafee tsei ni wa ni tamɔ tsei lɛ faaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ bɔle tso lɛ shishi (pile) lɛ he, ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa ni ehi shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do black spots start spreading quickly on my tomato leaves as soon as the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash dirt onto the lower leaves, carrying tiny disease germs that live in the soil. Combined with wet leaves and moist air, these germs multiply rapidly and turn into black spots, so trimming lower leaves helps prevent the sickness.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji eshwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ baai ni efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fata he lɛ Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ faa oya ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii diji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela baa mɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly in the barn if I dig them up while the soil is still very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mifo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Yams dug out of wet soil absorb too much moisture and often suffer tiny skin cuts during harvest where wet soil bacteria enter. Storing wet, damaged yams traps moisture, creating the perfect condition for rot fungi to eat the tubers.
ga: Atomɔ ni atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni bei pii lɛ, ehewolo nɔ pilamɔi fioo komɛi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli he ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni efɔ ni efite lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni rot fungus lɛ aye ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow so fast and tall on my field even when I didn't water or fertilize them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli po.

english: Weeds are wild local plants that have spent hundreds of years adapting to survive bad weather and poor soil. Farm crops are cultivated and delicate, so weeds will quickly steal water and plant food away from your crops if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni ehe afii ohai abɔ dani amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ ni amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ baaju nu oya ni ebaakwɛ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli kɛji ojieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need taller plants grown around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Taller crops like plantain or shade trees act as a protective cover, keeping the ground cool and moist while the young cocoa gets established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo shia tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant coconut trees and cocoa trees on the same plot?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, tall coconut trees provide a high canopy that filters sunlight for shade-loving cocoa trees underneath, allowing you to maximize land use and harvest two different yields from the same space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei feɔ ŋmei kakadaŋŋ agboi ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ shishi ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ anɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: Why is it helpful for me to grow more than one type of crop on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe ekome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Growing different crops protects your income if one crop fails, improves soil health by using nutrients differently, and helps slow down the spread of crop-specific pests and diseases.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshika he kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofai fɔji kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excess moisture and humidity. Pruning overgrown branches helps air move freely through your farm and reduces wetness on the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes the leaves on my coconut palm to turn yellow and droop early?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya?

english: Yellowing coconut leaves often point to a lack of key soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, prolonged dry weather, or damage to the roots from soil insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi amli lɛ

english: Why do the flowers on my crops drop to the ground without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience stress from extreme dry heat, sudden lack of water, pest attacks, or poor pollination due to a lack of insects like bees in the area.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbimɔ mli. Nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ Atutuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. aloo pollination ni ehiii yɛ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my coconut seedlings when I plant them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miidu?

english: Coconut palms need to be spaced about 7 to 9 meters apart so their wide roots and giant leaves do not fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food as they mature.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 9 bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ akatswa nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my food crops turning yellow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When water and soil nutrients are scarce, plants naturally sacrifice their older bottom leaves to feed their newer top growth and stay alive.
ga: Beni nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii ni ehi shi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree give me a huge harvest one year and a small harvest the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome mli, ni afi kroko lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Trees use up a massive amount of stored energy and nutrients during a heavy harvest year, so they often need a recovery period the following year to rebuild their reserves.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛkpamɔ afii ni mli wa lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli koni amɛsaa amɛhe ni amɛto lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is suitable for growing coconut palms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Coconut trees grow best in deep, well-draining soil where water doesn't sit logged around the roots for too long, and in warm regions with plenty of sunlight.
ga: Kokoo tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni nu lɛ kɛ ehe kpaaa shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ kɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop in the exact same field every season drains the specific nutrients that crop needs. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted unless you rotate crops or put nutrients back using manure or compost.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafo ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fata he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a widespread pest that burrows into the center of young maize plants to feed on new leaves, which weakens the plant's growth if not treated early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli koni eye baai heei. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to dry up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miigbi miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that drink up water and steal soil nutrients faster than your crops can, leaving your plants starving even during periods of rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli po.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin with very little fruit when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and weak instead of growing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ waa ni amɛhe waaa. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nɛ tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in direct sunlight to capture energy, which the plant then sends down underground to expand the size of the tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Abaamaje tsei lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there is strong sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and short roots that dry out easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains grown nearby to shield them from intense heat until they grow larger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Plantain roots grow sideways near the surface instead of deep into the earth, making the top-heavy plant easy for strong winds to uproot when the soil is wet.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ afãgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baajie amɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when it rains too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, the roots suffocate and rot from excess dampness.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out suddenly, causing stress that makes the plant drop its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi trukaa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he lɛ baa.

english: If I want to start crop farming to support my family, what is a simple crop I can plant that matures quickly?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni mije ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ shishi koni mikɛkwɛ miweku lɛ. Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ ni makwɛ oya?

english: Crops like maize, okra, and sweet potato are great choices because they mature within 2 to 3 months, require basic management, and have strong local market demand throughout Ghana.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, okra, kɛ ŋmãa ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli ni ebiɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli he nibii ni ataoɔ waa yɛ Ghana fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa's first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ Cocoa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of growing into tomatoes?
