ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when they lack water, or when tiny insects prevent proper flower pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, kɛ́ nu bɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ba amɛhe. Hewalɛ ni bɛ ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli pollen jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves twist into small cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Twisted or curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which transmit viruses that cripple leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ eshwaa

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest since they grow under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground spreads the leaves out to catch full sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow larger tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my soil dry out and turn hard like rock after just a few hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ni ewa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil turns hard when it lacks organic matter like dry leaves or compost, which normally acts like a sponge to hold water and keep the soil soft for crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my corn help my soil without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa ni aaadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the surrounding soil and nearby corn crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ kɛ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my corn leaves with brown waste that looks like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central whorl of the corn plant and eats the tender young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni darako lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and survive heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I put dried chicken manure in my farm soil before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbi afata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Chicken manure feeds the soil with essential nutrients like nitrogen, which helps maize stalks grow strong, turn deep green, and produce larger cobs.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa. Eji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my yam plants grow very big green leaves but only produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai ni dara waa lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ afee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the yam plant spends all its energy growing leafy vines above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches lets in sunlight and air to help pods stay dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop expanding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmli eshwaaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the leaves, which stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛdara

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that clogs the internal tubes of the stem so water cannot reach the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ trukaa lɛ ji bacteria shwiemɔ. Enɛ ji hela ko ni sũ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa, ni no haaa nu ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around my young crops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi dumɔwui kɛjɛ shishijee No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops, while also hiding insect pests that can spread diseases to young plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ agbala helai kɛba tsei bibii anɔ lɛ teeɔ.

english: Flowers drop off when plants experience heat stress or lack enough water during the flowering stage, preventing the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ehe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a wo yiblii.

english: Why are there ragged holes and white lines on my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ line yɛŋ lɛ?

english: Holes on young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaf whorl, which reduces the crop's ability to feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa lɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct heat and lose water quickly through their leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava gives young cocoa trees living umbrellas to protect them from scorching heat until their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantain loo cassava lɛ, ebaaha cacao tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to reach upward to catch maximum sunlight. Using stakes keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and allows the leaves to trap solar energy, which helps the plant build bigger yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛyashɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Tsoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ekɛ hulu hewalɛ toɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil does not have enough nitrogen, which corn needs to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK will feed the plants and help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans together with maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and trap it in the dirt. When these plants grow alongside maize or decay after harvest, they release this trapped nitrogen, feeding the maize naturally without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ dara yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo amɛgboi yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ kpo. Ha ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long, suffocating the tubers. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off quickly so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until your land receives two or three heavy, steady rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout too early and dry up if the sun comes back out for a week.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya tsɔ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ hulu lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ ekoŋŋ otsi kome.

english: What causes small worms to eat the leaves in the center of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye baa ni yɔɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These worms are usually Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by night-flying moths. Spraying recommended organic biopesticides or soapy water early in the morning gets deep into the plant funnel to clear the worms before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ wo mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔse nɔ leebi lɛ, eyaa tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ amli koni egbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Watering regularly at the roots rather than on the leaves and keeping the soil cool helps the flowers set into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa moŋ fe baai lɛ, ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds steal vital food, sunlight, and water directly from the crop roots. Clearing weeds around your crops early in their growth leaves all the soil nutrients and moisture free for your planted crops to feed on.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hia, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ mra Yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ, ebaaha otso lɛ mli niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fɛɛ akaje mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant too many seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper plant spacing ensures every crop gets enough room to spread its roots and produce full, heavy harvests.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawuu kɛha niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwã ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni tsii aba.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help my crops grow better than in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: A greenhouse is a structure covered with transparent plastic or glass that protects crops from extreme heat, heavy rains, and destructive pests. Inside, the environment is controlled, allowing crops like tomatoes and peppers to grow faster, stay healthier, and yield far more produce than outside.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsu ko ni akɛ plastic loo glase ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Yɛ mli lɛ, shihilɛ ko ni akudɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ. shwere oya Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni ekɛ nibii babaoo aba fe kponɔgbɛ

english: Why does setting up a greenhouse cost so much money compared to normal farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ heɔ shika babaoo kɛ akɛto okwaayeli ni afeɔ daa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Greenhouse setups require special materials like UV-protected plastic, strong metal or wooden framing, and drip irrigation systems. Although the starting cost is high, it protects your crops from weather damage and pests, allowing you to harvest high-quality produce year-round to earn back your investment.
ga: Nibii krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ plastic ni tsiɔ UV naa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo biɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi. Dade loo tso ni mli wa kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛshwieɔ shi Eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee nyɔmɔwoo lɛ fa moŋ Shi ebuɔ onibii ahe hu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do vegetables grown inside plastic structures produce more yield than those grown in my normal garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ plastic tsɔji amli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ mibɔɔ ni mifeɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Inside a protective plastic structure, plants are safe from harsh weather that causes stress, and pests cannot easily reach them. Because the plants do not waste energy fighting off severe wind, rain, or insects, they use all their strength to produce bigger and more abundant fruits.
ga: Plastic ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ mli Abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni kɛ haomɔ baa lɛ ahe. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe mlɛo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei efiteee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, nugbɔ, loo kooloi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves dry up and burn when the dry season sun gets too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When sunlight is too intense and heat rises, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. This extreme heat stress damages the leaves, causing them to scorch and dry up.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa ni latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. Charred ni egbi

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into peppers when it gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani etsɔɔ pepper kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, pepper plants experience heat stress and conserve water to survive. To save energy, the plant drops its flowers because it senses it cannot support growing fruit under such extreme conditions.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Pepper tsei kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛhi shi. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa tamɔ nɛkɛ mli.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the wet season destroy sensitive crops like sweet peppers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmeii?

english: Heavy rain physically damages soft stem tissues, washes essential plant nutrients out of the topsoil, and creates standing water around roots. Excess water smothers roots so they cannot breathe, leading to root rot and plant death.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ baa tso lɛ mli fãji bibii lɛ anɔ. Efɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baa. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tsei lɛ gboiɔ.

english: How do I know if buying modern drip irrigation will actually increase my income when I harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ hemɔ baaha shika ni mináa lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mikpa nii?

english: Drip irrigation delivers water and liquid plant nutrients straight to the roots in precise amounts with minimal waste. Because crops receive steady moisture without weeds stealing it, your harvest will be larger, cleaner, and ready for market earlier when prices are high.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu kɛ tso mli niyenii ni ji nu lɛ falɛ pɔtɛɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni fiteee nɔ ko kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be ni jwɛi juuu amɛ. Okpamɔ lɛ baafee agbo, ehe baatse ni efee klalo akɛ abaawo jara nɔ oya kɛji jara wa.

english: Is it better for me to start with open-field farming before trying higher-cost methods like greenhouse farming?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ shishi dani maka gbɛ ni jara wa tamɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ makwɛ?

english: Yes, starting with open-field farming allows you to master basic plant care, soil management, and local market sales with lower financial risk. Once you build experience and save money, upgrading to covered farming can help you grow off-season crops for maximum profits.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli ni agbele naa lɛ shishijee lɛ haa onyɛɔ oleɔ tsei akwɛmɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ, kɛ jarayeli yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni shika he oshara baa shi. Kɛji otswa oniiashikpamɔ lɛ oma shi ni okɛ shika to lɛ, Okwaayeli ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli koni onine ashɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do crops grown under shade net covers suffer fewer insect attacks than open-field crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ nyɛŋ atutua amɛ tamɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Shade nets act as a physical barrier that prevents flying insects, moths, and beetles from reaching your plants to feed or lay eggs. In an open field, insects have direct access to attack the leaves and fruits.
ga: Shade net lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ ahe. atsĩɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaba tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbatao niyenii loo amɛwo ŋmeii. Yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, kooloi baanyɛ ashɛ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do plants kept inside enclosed plastic shelters sometimes get leaf mold or rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni akɛtoɔ plastic tsũi ni afo mli lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: When an enclosed shelter lacks proper ventilation, air cannot circulate, causing heat and moisture to build up on leaves like sweat. This trapped wetness creates the perfect environment for plant fungi and molds to multiply.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shĩai ni agbe naa lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ tamɔ latsaa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ adalɛ baa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to move my tomato seedlings from the nursery bed into the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie tomato dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya saatso wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are generally ready for transplanting about 3 to 4 weeks after planting, or when they have grown 4 to 6 strong leaves. Moving them at this stage ensures their root system is developed enough to survive the move into the open field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ. aloo kɛ́ amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 4 kɛyashi 6 lɛ, amɛ ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants look weak and wilting right after I transplant them into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo beni midu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This reaction is known as transplant shock. Moving the seedling disturbs its delicate root system, making it hard for the plant to absorb water for a day or two until the roots settle into the new soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baashɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to transplant my crops in the late afternoon instead of early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mitsei lɛ awo he kroko yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Yɛ leebi maŋkpa najiaŋ?

english: Transplanting in the cool late afternoon gives the young seedlings the whole night to recover and drink water without facing the hot daytime sun, which can dry out roots before they catch in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli He ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ he waaa ni amɛnuɔ nu gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa amɛkpe yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛ ya shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen if I leave my vegetable seedlings in the nursery for too long before moving them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikɛwo he kroko?

english: Leaving seedlings in the nursery bed too long makes their stems thin, weak, and leggy as they fight for light. Their roots also become tangled, which severely stunts their growth after you finally put them in the field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ naji be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná la lɛ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo. Enɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ waa koni amɛkakwɛ beni okɛ amɛ ewo ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to pull out and separate some of my young maize plants when they grow too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala ni magbala ŋmeii bibii komɛi amli beni amɛdaraa ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete for the same soil food, water, and sunlight. Thinning them out gives each remaining plant enough space to produce strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso lɛ shishifã ni wa kɛ ŋmei agbo.

english: What is the proper way to separate delicate seedlings growing together without breaking their roots?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbalaa dumɔwui ni waaa ni edara yɛ he kome ni akuuu amɛshishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Water the soil deeply a few hours before separating so the earth becomes soft and loose. Lift the soil gently around the roots with a stick or small spade rather than pulling the stems by hand.
ga: Okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi dani ogbala mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, okɛ tso loo shɔvel bibioo ko awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ blɛoo, moŋ fe ni okɛ oniji baagbala shishifã lɛ.

english: Why should I remove the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers feed on the nutrients and water that the main plantain tree needs. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest sucker, which allows the parent tree to grow heavy, healthy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa dumɔwu titri lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, eshwɛɔ tsɔne ni akɛmuɔ nii ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ shwereɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cowpea plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: As the crop grows larger, top leaves shade the lower ones from the sun. The plant naturally sheds these shaded lower leaves because they are no longer capturing light to make food for the crop.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da lɛ Ŋwɛi baai lɛ baaha shishigbɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ hulu la lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ nɛkɛ shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ shade nɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii dɔŋŋ.

english: How often do I need to water my crops during their first week after moving them into the field?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Newly transplanted crops need light watering every day, preferably early morning or evening, for the first week until their roots establish in the field soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo tsei heei ni adu lɛ nu fioo daa gbi. Titri lɛ, leebi loo gbɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need to be planted at an angle rather than flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aduɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a sloped angle helps roots sprout deeper and spread widely, giving the plant strong support against wind and resulting in larger, better-formed tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ gbalaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die shortly after I move them from the nursery bag into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotoku lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when their delicate roots are damaged or exposed to intense sun during moving. Transplanting during cool hours like late afternoon and watering immediately helps roots recover and settle safely.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ loo hulu la ni naa wa shɛɔ amɛnɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ bei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli tamɔ shwane mli ni awo mli nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How deep should I put my crop seedlings into the soil when planting on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miidu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings should be planted at the exact same depth they grew in their nursery container. Planting too deep causes the stem to rot under the wet soil, while planting too shallow leaves roots exposed to scorching sun.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ni amɛdu yɛ dumɔwui atoohe lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni adu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a seedling is strong enough to survive on my farm before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu amɛ?

english: A strong, healthy seedling has a thick, firm stem, at least four to six fully formed green leaves, and a dense root system that holds the soil ball together without crumbling.
ga: Dumɔwui ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baaná tsei ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ baai 4-6 ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni efoŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and curling up at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves are a sign that the plant is stressed, usually caused by small pests like aphids sucking sap from under the leaves or a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen

english: Why does my maize stay short and thin with pale leaves even though I weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa?

english: Weeding stops competition, but pale and stunted maize means the soil lacks nutrients. Maize needs nitrogen to build strong green leaves and thick stems, which comes from fertile soil or added organic manure.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii kpaɔ Shi ŋmãa ni mli tse ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa aba. Enɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cowpea leaves develop small holes just a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea gbekɛ lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tender new sprouts attract leaf-chewing insects like beetles and caterpillars. Inspecting under the leaves early in the morning helps catch these insects before they eat enough leaf area to weaken the plant.
ga: Nibii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ladybugs kɛ caterpillars. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛhe baai lɛ ahe gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are naturally shade-loving plants whose leaves burn under harsh direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them while their root systems develop during their first two years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii ji tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo. Baai lɛ shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to my cassava crop if I plant the stem cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava is planted too closely, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This causes the plant to grow tall and slender, leaving very little energy to form large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they turn into actual fruits during dry hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause tomato plants to drop their blossoms as a survival instinct to save energy and protect the main plant from drying out completely.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ wala yibiiwoo su ko koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking much longer to produce fruit bunches than my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ aduawai akui fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain fruiting speed depends heavily on soil moisture and soil richness. If the soil lacks organic matter or holds too little water, the sucker takes longer to build up the energy needed to push out a flower bunch.
ga: Plantain yibiiwoo oyaiyeli lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ waa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ Sucker lɛ baahe be babaoo dani ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛtsi bouquet lɛ kpo lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight and heat. Providing shade crops like plantains helps retain soil moisture and shields young plants from scorching sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: What causes the flowers on my cocoa tree to drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Flower drop occurs mainly due to a lack of insect pollinators like midges, extreme dry weather stress, or a lack of soil nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ babaoo baa ji pollinators tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ amli baa. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the wet season affect my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While water helps the trees grow, constant heavy rain combined with cold, humid conditions creates an ideal environment for fungal infections like black pod disease to spread rapidly.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa moŋ, shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ mli oya.

english: Why are some of the small cocoa pods on my tree turning black and shriveling up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection fueled by high humidity, or natural cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fungal helai ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa loo shwiemɔ ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli baa Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do mistletoe plants growing on my cocoa tree branches harm my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mistletoe ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi kokoo niji anɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Mistletoe is a parasite that sinks roots into cocoa branches to steal water and nutrients directly from the tree, weakening the branches and lowering pod yields.
ga: Mistletoe ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kookoo niji amli koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa niji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Does moss growing on my cocoa tree trunk harm the tree?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ awui?

english: Moss itself does not directly feed on the tree, but thick growth indicates too much shade and humidity, which can trap excess moisture and hide harmful pests or bark diseases.
ga: Moss yeee tsei tɛ̃ɛ. Shi shweremɔ ni mli wa lɛ tsɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni amɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmɔtɔ helai ato.

english: Why is it important to prune the branches of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and airflow, which reduces humidity, prevents fungal diseases, and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava and maize together on the same land as my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa tsei?

english: You can plant temporary shade crops like plantain or cocoyam with young cocoa, but heavy feeders like cassava compete aggressively for soil nutrients and water, which can stunt young cocoa growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cocoa kɛ cocoa ŋmeii bibii adu. Shi niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo bibii lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Cocoa pods change color when ripe; pods that start green usually turn bright yellow, while pods that start red or purple turn an orange-yellow color.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, pods ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ etsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ orange-yellow.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce fewer pods than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their root systems become less efficient at absorbing nutrients and water, making them weaker, more susceptible to diseases, and less productive.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. helai baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo

english: Why are my cocoa leaves turning yellow after I irrigate them with river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ faa mli nu fɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If river water carries harmful chemical residues or heavy mud from upstream ground disturbances, it damages delicate root hairs, preventing the plant from taking up vital nutrients and causing the leaves to yellow.
ga: Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ loo muji ni tsii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mligbalamɔ mli lɛ. Ebaakpata shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my maize growing so poorly even after applying fertilizer on land that was recently dug up by heavy machinery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsɔnei ni tsii ewo shikpɔŋ ni atsa ehee lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery strips away the topsoil that holds essential natural organic matter and severely compacts the ground, making it difficult for maize roots to spread and take up nutrients from fertilizer.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ toɔ lɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ waa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight; they need shade from larger plants like plantains to retain moisture and keep their tender leaves from burning during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji, tamɔ plantains, amli koni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛtsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why did my vegetable leaves turn brown and drop off after chemical spraying was done on a nearby farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbee shi beni mikɛ tsofai shwie ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays can drift through the air on windy days as an invisible fine mist, landing on non-target crop leaves and burning their growth tissues.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ gbii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ amli tamɔ afua bibioo ko ni anaaa. Eshɛɔ tso lɛ baai ni jeee nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ anɔ ni eshãa efãji ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and rotted inside when I pull them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛmiifite yɛ mli kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays overly waterlogged or polluted, suffocating root tissues so the plant cannot process food or expand into full tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ loo eyɛ muji. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsu niyenii he nii loo eda ni etsɔ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is my cassava crop taking much longer to mature on land that I have farmed continuously without resting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi-cassava lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni miduɔ be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Repeated farming on the same plot without resting the land depletes crucial soil minerals like potassium, which slows down the plant's overall growth and tuber formation.
ga: repetitive farming Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ, jɛmɛ baafite shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, ni baaha tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms under severe environmental stress—such as excessive heat, poor water quality, or soil nutrient shortages—to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi ni naa wa shishi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha shishijee wala

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt every afternoon even when the soil around them still feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi daa gbɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli egbi moŋ lɛ? Enuɔ he akɛ edɔ lolo.

english: During hot afternoon hours, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly attack my green maize leaves so rapidly after a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni amɛhe be ni amɛgbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Short dry spells during the rainy season accelerate the armyworm lifecycle, encouraging moths to lay massive clusters of eggs on tender, fast-growing maize leaves.
ga: be kuku ni akɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ashihilɛ yaa oya. Wo ŋmeii hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii baai ni miida oya lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does cocoa swollen shoot disease spread so quickly from one infected tree to nearby healthy trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cocoa bud hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen shoot disease is a virus carried by tiny mealybug insects, which easily crawl across interconnected branches and leaves from one cocoa tree to the next.
ga: Bud swollen hela ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji mealybugs lɛ woɔ. Efoɔ tsei niji ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ amli oya ni eshiɔ cacao tso kome kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: Why do my cashew trees lose almost all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the dry Harmattan season is a natural survival strategy. By shedding its leaves, the tree prevents water from evaporating into the hot, dusty air, keeping enough moisture inside its trunk to survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ato tso lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cashew trees drop so many flowers before any fruit or nuts start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees produce many more flowers than they can support as full nuts. Strong dry winds, sudden weather changes, or tiny pests can cause extra flowers to fall early, though proper watering and pest management help the tree hold onto enough flowers for a good harvest.
ga: Cashew tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua tamɔ ŋmeii muu. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo ko yɛ ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo oya tsɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua ni ebua fɔfɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa kpakpa moŋ, shi.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I plant my cashew trees too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii kɛji midu cashew tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their upper branches overlap and block sunlight from each other. Their roots also fight over the same water and nutrients in the soil, which leads to weak growth and far fewer fruits than well-spaced trees.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ŋwɛi niji lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛhaa hulu la lɛ he tsɔi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa waa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ waa lɛ.

english: What happens to my young crops when a heavy rainstorm floods the farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Heavy rain sitting on the soil cuts off the oxygen supply to the roots, essentially suffocating them. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing food from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the plant growth to stall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔlɔ Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ebaakpa niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my neighbor farmers plant groundnuts or beans in the same soil around their main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ duɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ebɔle mi lɛ nɔ lɛ? amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil as natural plant food. This enriches the soil around main crops, acting as a free, natural fertilizer that helps neighboring plants grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ he lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How many years does it usually take for a newly planted cashew tree to start producing nuts?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cashew tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: A cashew tree grown from a seed typically starts producing its first small harvest of nuts in three to four years. With good weeding, pruning, and protection from fires, it reaches its full production capacity around its seventh year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛɔ lɛ jeɔ ŋmei bibioo ko shishi klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni afoɔ kɛ la he buu kpakpa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔhe lɛ ni enáa nibii ni etsuɔ ​​lɛ fɛɛ yɛ afi ni ji kpawo lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off the low branches near the bottom of my young cashew trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-cashew tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches opens up space for sunlight and fresh air to pass under the tree, preventing humid conditions where diseases thrive. It also directs the tree's energy upward to build a strong main trunk and a wide upper branch canopy.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa, ni no ji he ni hela baanyɛ aba. Etsuɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee tso lɛ shishitso titri ni mli wa kɛ tsei niji ni mli kwɔ.

english: What causes black sticky spots to form on top of my cashew leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mi-cashew baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: The sticky substance is honeydew left behind by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mealybugs. A black fungus called sooty mold then grows on this sweet liquid, which blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves and weakens the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni ŋmɛɔ lɛ ji wuo ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs lɛ shĩɔ yɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei diŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ sooty mold lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ nɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why did my cassava plants grow tall with huge green leaves, but the roots under the ground stayed very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of food roots underneath. Tuber crops need balanced soil rich in potassium to expand their underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha shishifãi lɛ niyenii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia Tubers koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops curl inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the direct sun, keeping itself from losing too much internal moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ abɔle tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ naa kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Tomatoes spoil fast because of high heat and bruised skins during harvest. Storing them in cool, shaded places and transporting them in ventilated wooden crates instead of overfilled sacks prevents damage and extends their shelf life.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ, ni ehewolo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni akɛwo tso adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli mli yɛ kotokui ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafite ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes my stored maize to get eaten by small insects in my barn?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ?

english: Weevils attack stored maize when the grains are not completely dried before storage. Sun-drying your maize until the grains are very hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags prevents insect attacks and food waste.
ga: Weevils tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli baawa waa Ni akɛwo vacuum bag ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ akabote mli.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea when the crops are young helps them stay green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji nitrogen, tamɔ urea wo tsei lɛ amli beni amɛdara lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ hu ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores soil fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer right when I plant the seed or wait until it sprouts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu loo mamɛ kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait until seeds sprout and form roots so the plant can absorb the food. Applying fertilizer to un-germinated seeds can waste the fertilizer or burn the tender seedling.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite loo eshã dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop large roots and reach its full yield potential.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji baa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my crops if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo? Ni kɛji akɛ mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra hu?

english: Weeds act like extra mouths to feed; they steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops while hiding pests. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabui krɛdɛɛi ni ayeɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai teeɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids feeding on the leaf sap or spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with safe sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy for fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛha aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the trees without forming pods during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers to save water and protect themselves from heat stress during dry spells. Planting shade trees and leaving organic mulch around the roots retains soil moisture so flowers can set pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know when my underground yams are fully grown and ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are fully mature when the leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn yellow or brown. Digging them up at this stage ensures the tubers have reached their full size and weight.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ atsa shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ fɛɛ he.

english: Which oil-producing crops can I grow in Ghana that local factories will buy from me?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mu baa lɛ manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhei lɛ baahe kɛjɛ midɛŋ?

english: Oil palm and soybeans are in high demand by Ghanaian processing factories for cooking oil and animal feed, making them reliable choices for earning a consistent income.
ga: Ghana nitsumɔhei ni feɔ mu kɛ kooloi aniyenii lɛ taoɔ mu tso kɛ soybean waa. Enɛ haa nitsumɔhei nɛɛ feɔ gbɛ kroko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛnáa shika daa.

english: How do I know if a new crop will make a good profit before I spend money planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji sɛɛnamɔ baaba ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko nɔ dani mafite shika yɛ eŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ mli?

english: Check local market prices, confirm that buyers or processing companies exist in your district, and ask your extension officer if your soil and weather support high yields for that crop.
ga: Kwɛmɔ jara yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Ma nɔ mi akɛ hɔlɔlɔ loo nitsumɔhe ko yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Ni obi o-extension agent lɛ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ fiɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛha nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I make more profit from my harvested crops instead of selling them raw right away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Processing your crops—such as pressing groundnuts into oil or drying and shelling soybeans—adds value, lets you store them longer, and allows you to sell when market prices are higher.
ga: Onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni ooofee fɔ loo soybeans ni ooogbi ni okɛwo mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee ŋwɛi.

english: Why do crops like groundnuts and soybeans give us so much energy when we eat them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ soybeans haa wɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛji wɔye amɛ lɛ?

english: These seeds store natural fats, oils, and proteins as reserves for the growing seed, which translates into rich nutrition and long-lasting energy when humans consume them.
ga: Nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ toɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔji, fɔji, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa akɛ nɔ ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ni miida lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛ hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ kɛ́ adesai ye amɛ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce small fruit bunches with very little oil inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Ni mu fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli?

english: Oil production requires a lot of water and key nutrients like potassium; if the tree lacks water during fruit development or grows in poor soil, the fruits will dry out and yield less oil.
ga: Mu ni afeɔ lɛ biɔ nu babaoo kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium. Kɛji tso lɛ mli nu fite beni ewoɔ yibii loo edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ, Yibii lɛ baagbi ni fɔ fioo pɛ ebaajɛ mli aba.

english: Why do my crops grow green leaves but fail to produce heavy seeds or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli shi enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui loo aduawai ni tsii lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer makes crops grow big leaves, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to develop strong flowers, heavy seeds, and oil-rich fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ baa agboi. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛná fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ amli tsii. kɛ aduawai ni fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Which crops with high market value grow best in warm areas with moderate rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo yɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and sunflowers thrive in warm climates with moderate rain because their roots can tolerate dry spells better than water-loving crops like rice or sugarcane.
ga: Abɛi kɛ hulu fɔfɔi yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do the seed pods on my leguminous crops dry up and turn brown before the seeds fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-legumes lɛ anɔ lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat during pod filling or attacks by sap-sucking insects can starve the seed pods of nutrients, causing them to dry up early.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ be mli ni awoɔ pod mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuamɔ baanyɛ aha niyenii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ oya.

english: How do I keep my harvested groundnuts and oilseeds from going bad before I sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-peanuts kɛ oilseeds ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Dry seeds thoroughly in the sun until they are completely hard, then store them in breathable bags raised off the damp floor in a dry, dark room to prevent mold growth.
ga: Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni mumɔ baanyɛ ashɛ mli ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli egbi ni mli ewo duŋ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why does my oil palm fruit spoil so quickly if I wait a few days before pressing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mimɛ gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛmiimii lɛ?

english: Once harvested, natural chemical changes inside palm fruits rapidly break down the oil, turning it sour and reducing its quality unless processed within 48 hours.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Adebɔɔ mli tsofa tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ fɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ haa fɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni ehaa ehilɛ baa shi. ja atsu he nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves are very tender. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tip towards the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to stay green and healthy. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil and water sits on the farm for too long, the roots suffocate and rot-causing organisms quickly attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni bɔɔ nii ni miifite lɛ baatutua ŋmɔ lɛ oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. High heat damages the pollen inside the blossom, so the plant drops the flower instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking their sap, or by a virus carried by insects. Treating the crop early protects the new growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ amɛmli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaye abua ni abu baai heei ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my main plantain tree produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain titri lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: The young shoots share the same root system and food with the main tree. When too many shoots grow together, they steal the water and nutrients needed by the main tree to form a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ niyenii ni tamɔ tso titri lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fee ekome tsɔ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the barn even when I haven't planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduko amɛ moŋ?

english: Yam tubers are alive and naturally rest after harvest, but after a few months, their internal clock wakes them up to grow into new plants, especially if they sense warm air or humidity.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Amɛmli ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ teɔ amɛ shi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei heei. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground but form their pods under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi efeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is fertilized, it grows a long peg that bends down and pushes itself into the soil. The soil provides the dark, protected environment the plant needs to grow the actual nuts.
ga: Beni ashɛre ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ agbe naa lɛ Ebaada ni etsɔ ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ni baakoto shi ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ji he ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni abuɔ he ni he hiaa tsei diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛdu ŋmeii.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce fewer and smaller fruit bunches during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ aduawai fioo ni efeɔ bibii yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms require steady water to form big fruit bunches. During the dry season, the tree slows down its fruit production to save water and keep itself alive until the rains return.
ga: Nu he miihia mu tsei lɛ daa koni amɛwo aduawai wuji. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ amɛwoɔ yibii koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea plants flower very early while still tiny if I plant them in certain months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ oya shi ehiɔ shi bibioo kɛji midu yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas react to the length of daylight. When planted during months with shorter daylight hours, the plant gets a signal to stop growing leaves and start making flowers early.
ga: Cowpea feɔ enii yɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ha lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ amli Tsei lɛ baaná okadi ko ni baaha amɛkpa baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛje fɔfɔii ashishi mra.

english: How do I know which part of the cassava stem is best to cut and plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The middle portion of a mature, healthy cassava stem is best for planting because it contains strong buds and enough stored nutrients to sprout roots and shoots quickly, compared to the woody base or tender top.
ga: Kasava tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha dumɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyɛ fɔfɔii ni mli wa, ni eyɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato koni eha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ akɛto tso shishitoo loo tso bibioo ko he.

english: Does it make a difference if I plant my cassava cuttings slanted or straight into the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ du shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, planting cassava stem cuttings at a 45-degree angle or horizontally encourages tubers to grow closer to the soil surface, making them easier to harvest than cuttings planted straight down.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ 45-degree angle loo horizontal lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa ekpamɔ feɔ mlɛo fe ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow and curled leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease or severe nutrient deficiency, which weakens the crop and prevents the roots from growing large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa waa lɛ he okadi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: What is causing white powdery spots on the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ powder yɛŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baa lɛ baa?

english: White powdery spots are typically caused by fungal infections or sap-sucking pests like mealybugs, which feed on plant nutrients and reduce overall crop yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mealybugs, ni yeɔ tsei amli niyenii ni haa yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ baa shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ powdery yɛŋ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small underground roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli ni eyɛ baai shi ehaa mi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes plants to direct all energy into lush leaf growth rather than root development, which requires phosphorus and potassium to swell.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ adalɛ nɔ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shishifãi Enɛ biɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium koni ekɛfutu.

english: Can my cassava crops survive through the long dry season without irrigation?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tso lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛji nu bɛ mli?

english: Cassava is naturally drought-tolerant because its deep root system allows it to drop leaves during dry spells to save water and reactivate growth when rains return.
ga: Cassava ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Koni akɛ nu ato he ni ekanya dalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Is it safe for me to plant maize and cassava together on the same field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava continuously on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ he?

english: Repeatedly planting cassava on the same plot depletes specific soil nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava is typically ready 8 to 12 months after planting, which you can confirm by checking if lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging up one stand to check tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni obaanyɛ oma nɔ mi kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni aaafo mli jogbaŋŋ koni ana bɔ ni eyitso lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava start spoiling and turning dark just two days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni efee duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot quickly after harvest because exposure to air causes rapid oxidation and fungal entry through harvest wounds, meaning they must be processed or eaten within 48 hours.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ, oksideshin oya kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ kpamɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ atsu he nii loo aye yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant my crops on mounds of soil rather than on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Creating mounds loosens the soil so roots can spread easily, improves water drainage to prevent roots from rotting during heavy rains, and makes it easier for crops like plantain and root vegetables to establish firmly.
ga: Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Does planting crops on raised soil heaps help prevent water from drowning the stems after heavy rain?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ sũi ni abua naa lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ?

english: Yes, raised heaps allow excess rainwater to drain away from the stem and roots, protecting young crops from waterlogging and fungal rots during the rainy season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋtayaai ni awó nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Can I plant plantain suckers on mounds alongside other food crops without them competing for nutrients?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ kɛ niyenii tsei krokomɛi? Ni amɛmiitswa akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he?

english: Yes, as long as you give proper spacing. Interplanting on mounds maximizes land use, provides ground shade to control weeds, and helps optimize soil moisture for all crops involved.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he bɔ ni sa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ha hulutsoo koni akɛkudɔ jwɛi lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni kɔɔ he lɛ.

english: What is a plantain sucker and how do I choose a good one to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji plantain ŋmɔtɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui kpakpai ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A plantain sucker is a small shoot growing from the base of a mature plantain tree. Look for vigorous 'sword suckers' with narrow leaves coming from healthy, high-yielding parent plants with clean roots.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ji tsei bibii. Kɛ́ oda kɛjɛ dumɔwu ni eda lɛ shishi lɛ, taomɔ ‘klante suckers’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai bibii ni jɛ nyɛ tso ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni shishifãi ni he tse lɛ mli.

english: Can I dig up plantain suckers and plant them directly into the ground on the very same day?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo dumɔwui ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant them immediately after digging, but it is best to inspect the base, peel off any damaged outer layers, and trim dead roots to prevent pests and diseases from transferring to the new hole.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu beni otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okwɛ shishitoo lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ni efite lɛ. Ni ofolɔ shishifãi ni egboi lɛ amli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai akaya bu hee lɛ mli.

english: How deep should I dig the ground when planting a plantain sucker?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: You should dig a hole deep enough so that the main bulb of the sucker is completely covered with soil, usually about 30 to 45 centimeters deep. This anchors the plant against strong winds and encourages deep root growth.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni okɛ sũ aha suction yitso titri lɛ nɔ kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ mli kwɔ fe sɛntimita 30 kɛyashi 45. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daa ni mli kwɔ.

english: What should I do to the soil after I dig out a sucker from a mother plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ beni mifo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Refill the hole around the mother plant with fertile topsoil or compost. This stabilizes the main tree so it does not fall over and keeps its remaining roots covered and healthy.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu ni bɔle fɔlɔ tso lɛ he lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni ekagbee shi ni eye ebua ni shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe awa.
