english: Why do experienced farmers prefer to plant early in the morning at daybreak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛdu nii leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Planting early in the morning protects young plants from extreme afternoon heat stress. The soil is cooler and moister, which gives the transplants a better chance to recover and settle in.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii leebi lɛ, ebaabu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shwane mli lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baajɔ ni edɔ. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ kpakpa ni okɛbaatsu nii ni okɛ ohe awo mli.

english: How does morning moisture in the soil help freshly planted suckers stay strong?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ leebi shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cool morning moisture keeps the stems and leaves hydrated so the plant loses less water through evaporation before its roots start taking up water from the fresh soil.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni baa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ baai lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei laajeɔ nu fioo kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Dani shishifãi lɛ baaje nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi

english: Why does working with extra hands help me finish planting faster and get better crop results?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔ kroko ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni magbe midumɔ nii lɛ naa oya ni maná yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Working with a team allows tasks like digging holes, moving suckers, and planting to happen simultaneously, reducing the time plant roots are exposed to drying air and ensuring fresh planting.
ga: Kuu ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ nitsumɔi tamɔ bu ni atsaa kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛjieɔ muji kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mli. Ni dumɔ baa yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa be ni tso shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli lɛ baa shi. ni oha nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baafee ehee

english: How can I tell if my soil is fertile enough to support a healthy harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa?

english: Fertile soil usually has a dark, rich color, feels crumbly in your hands, and stays moist without holding water like a puddle. You can also tell by how plants grow on it; rich soil naturally grows healthy, dark green vegetation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Oniji nuɔ he akɛ amɛmiigbɔjɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli tamɔ nubu Obaanyɛ ole bɔ ni tsei daa lɛ hu. Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops feed on nutrients in the ground every season. If you do not add nutrients back using manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted, leaving future crops starved and weak.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo, ni no baaha hɔmɔ aye wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does water sit in puddles on my farm after heavy rains, and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ nubu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water puddles happen when soil is tightly packed or low-lying. Standing water suffocates plant roots by cutting off their air supply, which causes root rot and stops the crop from growing properly.
ga: Puddles baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eba shi. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I keep moisture in my soil during the dry season so my plants do not die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni mitsei lɛ akagboi?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the dirt from the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ muji ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: My neighbor gets double my harvest on similar land; what farming habits make that happen?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa yibiiwoo lɛ toi enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ. Mɛɛ okwaayeli sui haa ebaa lɛ nakai?

english: High crop yields rely on good field practices rather than luck. Proper seed spacing, weeding early so crops do not fight for food, and applying fertilizer at the right time make a huge difference in harvest size.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi kpakpai anɔ fe shweremɔ. He ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ateŋ Jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Koni tsei lɛ akawu yɛ niyenii he. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaha srɔtofeemɔ kpele aba ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ mli.

english: Is it bad practice to plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo?

english: Yes, because planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that like that crop to multiply. Rotating different crops, like planting beans after maize, restores soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛkɛ lɛ ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain and no sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo ni hulu la bɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant cannot make energy. Too much water drowns the roots so they cannot drink nutrients, and a lack of sunlight stops leaves from producing the green chlorophyll needed for growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee hewalɛ. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ni hulu la ni bɛ lɛ haaa baa lɛ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die immediately after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving young plants causes root shock. If you transplant them during the hot afternoon, the strong sun dries them out before their roots can grab water from the new soil. Transplanting late in the afternoon or on cloudy days helps them survive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsake amɛ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How does adding manure or fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Manure and fertilizers act like concentrated food for plants. They deliver essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus directly to the roots, which the plant uses to build green leaves, strong stems, and heavy seeds.
ga: Manure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni mli wa kɛha tsei. Amɛhaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. kɛyaa shishifãi ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli tsotso ni wa kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii

english: Why do insects and pests suddenly attack my crops during specific times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pest populations explode when weather conditions, like high humidity or sudden warm rains, create ideal breeding environments. Keeping your farm clean of weeds helps reduce hiding places for pests before they multiply.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfɔɔ bii baa. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ aba shi dani amɛshwere.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch and lose moisture under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them creates a canopy that protects the young trees until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer into the soil will help green up the leaves and boost growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni yɔɔ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔji amli ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does mixing dried poultry manure into my soil help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Te kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil, holding onto moisture for longer periods while slowly releasing essential nutrients that feed your crops continuously.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Yaa nɔ ojieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Which direction should the nodes point when I push cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ nodes lɛ atsɔɔ beni amɛtsiɔ ŋmei nine kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The small leaf buds or nodes on the cassava stem cutting must always point upwards toward the sky so that new shoots can grow properly above ground while roots develop underneath.
ga: fɔfɔi bibii loo nodes Esa akɛ cassava nine lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi.

english: Lifting yam vines on poles allows their leaves to capture maximum sunlight for food production while preventing leaves from touching damp soil, which reduces fungal infections and leads to larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛbaa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why is it beneficial for my soil if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for nearby corn crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, which causes deformation; spraying neem seed extract or soapy water can help suppress them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni kɛ tsɔne lɛ fiteɔ Neem dumɔwui amli nu loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa enɛɛmɛi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops rot faster if I plant them too close together during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops too tightly prevents fresh air from circulating between them, trapping high moisture around stems and leaves, which creates an ideal environment for fungi and rot to spread.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekabɔle amɛteŋ. Amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahe, ni no haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when air temperatures become excessively hot or when soil water levels fluctuate sharply between dry and overly wet conditions.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ ateŋ.

english: What is the best way to apply fertilizer so the heavy rains do not wash it away from my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie kɛjɛ mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer a few centimeters away from the base of the plant when the soil is moist, and lightly cover it with soil so rain buries the nutrients near the roots instead of washing them away across the surface.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Ni okɛ nɔ ko aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo bɔni afee ni nugbɔ afu niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni eeefɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant naturally moves the available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why does my land produce weaker maize crops if I plant maize on the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize-focused pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni ŋmãa yɔɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the next crop grow much stronger leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ naa baai ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with good soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil, naturally adding fertilizer for the crops that follow.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fataa tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects that feed on the flower stems.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ adɛŋ

english: Why do my yam vines give smaller yams if I do not provide wooden stakes for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiwo sweet potato bibii lɛ? Akɛni mibɛ tso ni amɛbaakwɔ nɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the sunlight on stakes to make enough food. Without stakes, leaves shade each other, reducing the food energy sent down to grow big tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni efee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii hewalɛ ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right on the stem end before they get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ tso lɛ naagbee dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when dry soil suddenly gets a heavy dose of water. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to burst.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nu babaoo trukaa. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get scorched easily in direct sun. They need nurse plants like plantain to provide shade and cool moisture while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the soil when the heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil fills all air spaces, drowning the roots and encouraging rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ekɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily once the heavy bunch of plantains appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ plantains babaoo je kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems spread near the surface rather than deep taproots. When the heavy fruit bunch grows, the stem becomes top-heavy and easily pulls out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa nu lɛ hiɛ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ Ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why do my young oil palm seedlings look burnt when I move them straight from the nursery into full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings grown in shaded nurseries develop tender leaves. Shifting them directly to full open sunlight causes leaf shock, scorching the green tissues before the plant can adapt.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baaná baai bibii. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akpokpo. ni ehaa fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shãa dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe.

english: Why are the young fruits on my coconut tree dropping off before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Early coconut drop often happens because of water stress during dry spells, a shortage of nutrients like potassium in the soil, or poor pollination. Giving the palm adequate water and feeding the soil helps the tree retain its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo pollination ni ehiii Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii amli.

english: Why must I leave so much space between coconut palms when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ lɛ?

english: Coconut palms grow wide root systems and large leafy fronds. Proper spacing ensures that each palm receives enough direct sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors.
ga: Kokoo tsei daa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why are the lower fronds on my coconut tree turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: While old fronds naturally die off, widespread yellowing can indicate a nutrient deficiency (like magnesium or nitrogen) or diseases such as Cape St. Paul Wilt, which block the movement of water inside the tree.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ baai momo lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe moŋ. Shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ (tamɔ magnesium loo nitrogen) faaa loo hela ko tamɔ Cape St. Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing companion crops like plantains to keep the soil moist and leaves cool until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is short of nitrogen, which it needs to produce green leaves and grow sturdy stems. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the field and drown the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ nu ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick leaves but giving me tiny underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi tuber bibioo ko yɛ kɛha mi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely hot conditions, it spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mashɛreɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal water and food from the main plant. Cutting away weak suckers leaves only the strongest ones, resulting in bigger, healthier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi suckers babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. This results in bigger and healthier plantains.

english: Why do flowers on my pepper plants drop to the ground without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants drop their flowers when they get heat-stressed or when the moisture in the soil swings too quickly between very dry and very wet. The plant sheds blossoms to protect itself.
ga: Aduawai tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ hao amɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya tsɔ yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Plants bloom to protect themselves.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply liquid crop treatments or sprays?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni mikɛ nu mli tsei ahe tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: The best time to spray is early morning or late afternoon when the sun is low. Heat during midday causes liquid treatments to evaporate quickly before the leaves can absorb them, and can even scorch the foliage.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli Gbi teŋ latsaa lɛ haa nu ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya dani baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ hu ashã.

english: Why do my crop roots stay weak even after I feed the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo niyenii po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If the soil is packed too tightly or is too acidic, crop roots cannot spread out or draw up nutrients properly. Loosening hard soil and adding organic compost helps roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ acid tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe waa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight because heat dries out their foliage and root zone. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the air cool and humid, protecting the young plants.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ baaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni eha hulutsoo ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ emasɛi? No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao bibioo lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ.

english: Cassava plants are aggressive feeders with long roots that steal water and nutrients from the soil. They also grow wide leaves very quickly, which can block necessary light and stunt the growth of young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Kasava tso ji tso ni yeɔ nii oya ni shishifãi kakadaji ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, baai lɛ daa oya waa. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ la ni he hiaa lɛ naa ni etsĩ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an important food element in the soil. Nitrogen gets washed away easily by heavy rains, so the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ Nitrogen lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden heavy rains. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant stay calm and retain its flowers to form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kpoo ni ehaa efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I get small, twisted leaves on my tomato plants instead of healthy full leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei yɛ baai bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Yɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ?

english: Curled and twisted leaves on tomatoes are often a sign of a plant virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Protecting young plants with nets or using neem-based organic sprays helps keep these insects from infecting your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso mli helai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋshɔŋlooi bu tsei bibii ahe loo okɛ organic neem spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote oŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air to spread their leaves and capture sunlight, which supplies energy to swell the tuber underground. If left on the ground, the leaves crowd together, rot from soil moisture, and produce small tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baabua amɛhe naa. Nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hewɔ lɛ kɛ yitso bibioo ko fɔ

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow fast while others stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daraaa ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers with thin, spear-like leaves get strong food support from the main stem's corm. Suckers that develop broad leaves too early grow weak because they try to feed themselves before their root system is properly formed.
ga: Plantain tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Tsoi ni feɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ oya lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ejaakɛ amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye nii dani shishifãi lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot strips away specific soil nutrients and lets maize pests and diseases build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like beans or peanuts restores nitrogen to the soil and starves maize pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmãa helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmei mli kooloi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain saturates flat soil for long periods, water displaces the air, causing the roots to suffocate and rot. Building high mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ tɛtrɛɛ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ nu be kplaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that keeps sunlight from drying out the earth. It traps moisture in the root zone, keeps the soil cool, and slowly decays into natural plant fertilizer.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when I plant them in an open clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a living canopy that shields young cocoa trees from intense heat and retains soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to stay green and grow strong ears, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same field exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your field with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii ni odu lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very thin even though the stems and leaves grow very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa beni eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely together or have too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in heavy tuber roots below ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ woɔ tuber shishifãi ni tsii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Staking keeps the vines lifted off the hot soil, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant maximum sunlight to produce large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ehe nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha hulu la ni fa babaoo aha tsei lɛ koni amɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery droppings inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli kɛ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ powda yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf funnel to eat young shoots. Early detection and applying recommended neem extracts or insecticides inside the funnels protects the growing crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ mra ni akɛtsu nii. Yɛ funnel lɛ mli lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain stem for water, nutrients, and space. Trimming off extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main tree to form large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo (tso lɛ yibii) kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ he ko. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push thin stem-like pegs down into the ground after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi etsitsi bibii ni tamɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛmiiya fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts develop their fruit underground. After flowers above ground get pollinated, the plant grows downward stalks called 'pegs' that burrow into the soil, where the actual groundnut pods form and mature.
ga: Peanuts woɔ amɛyibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni ajie fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni eba shi ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘peg’ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, severe dry spells, or poor soil fertility. Regular watering and applying organic mulch keeps the root zone cool enough for flowers to set fruit successfully.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on top of the soil around my tomato plants help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-tomato tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, covering the dirt like a protective blanket. It blocks the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture, keeps roots cool, and prevents dry crusting on top of the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ehaa muji nɔ tamɔ atade ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa ŋmeii ni egbi aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná su ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping soil evenly moist and mulched helps plants retain flowers and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni awo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess standing water fills up the soil's air pockets, suffocating the roots and creating conditions for fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii baanyɛ afite lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller, weaker plants.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why are there ragged holes and powdery waste in the center whorls of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ amli buji ni etse kɛ ashikishaŋ bibii yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing whorl of young maize plants. Early detection allows you to treat the center leaves before the growing tip is destroyed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni anaa mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe dani ŋmeii ni miida lɛ afiteɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my pepper plants stop them from wilting in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ebɔle he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, atsĩ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, covering the topsoil to shade it from direct sun heat, which slows down water evaporation and keeps plant roots cool and hydrated.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ awo mli koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and becoming twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the virus from stunting the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekaha tsei lɛ afee shoo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb the applied fertilizer and water faster than your crops can. Clearing weeds ensures your plants get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni akɛwo mli lɛ oya fe otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves to save water when the weather gets very hot and dry. It is a natural self-defense habit, and the roots underground will stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Eji adebɔɔ su ni haa mɔ he fãa. Ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the middle and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which the crop needs for healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plants green up again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ hia baai ni mli wa, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground turn yellow and completely wither. This signal shows that the plant has stopped growing leaves and transferred all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kwraa lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Removing heavily affected plants and controlling whiteflies prevents the rest of your garden from getting infected.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni ena naagbai waa lɛ kɛjɛ mli, ni akudɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsi hei krokomɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. yɛ obɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela lɛ emɔ

english: Why does my bean crop grow plenty of green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Beans naturally pull nitrogen into the ground, so giving them too much additional nitrogen fertilizer makes them grow leaves instead of flowers. Focus on using balanced fertilizers with phosphorus to encourage pods.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Maa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛ fɔsfɔs yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ nɔ mi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to plant vegetables like garden eggs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, and holds moisture well after rain without forming standing pools of water. Adding rotted leaves or animal manure improves poor soil before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni ekɛ nubu ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ baaa Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbo loo kooloi aŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ dani adu.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines spreading everywhere on top of the soil without making large tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If sweet potatoes get too much water or excess nitrogen, they spend all their energy growing long vines above ground instead of food roots below. Avoiding heavy fertilizers encourages better tuber growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato lɛ ná nu babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛdu wain tsei kakadaji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, full sunlight. They need partial shade from food crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their tender leaves from burning while their roots establish in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa crop if I plant the seedlings very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting trees too close makes them fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The trees will grow tall and thin with sparse branches, resulting in fewer cocoa pods per tree.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛ niji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haa cocoa ŋmɔtɔi fioo pɛ baa tso kome nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by lack of water, missing soil nutrients, or when tiny midges (pollinating insects) are absent. Maintaining organic shade and moist soil helps keep these pollinators active and pods forming.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollen lɛ bɛ Organic shade kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pollinators nɛɛ ni amɛtsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod on the tree is ripe enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color completely from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting only fully yellow pods ensures the beans inside are mature and properly filled.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ashwere kwraa ni amɛyi obɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I cut off weak or extra branches from my cocoa tree, won't that reduce my crop yield?
ga: Kɛ mifolɔ niji bibii loo niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso ko nɔ lɛ, Ani no haŋ minitsumɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Pruning actually increases yield. Removing extra and low-hanging branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the stem, reducing fungal diseases and helping the tree direct its strength into producing larger pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji krokomɛi ni shwieɔ shi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Why do weeds around the base of my trees slow down cocoa pod growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ miiha mikokoo ŋmɔji lɛ daraa fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive neighbors that steal fertilizer, soil nutrients, and moisture directly from the shallow root system of your cocoa trees, leaving the cocoa starved and unable to grow pods efficiently.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo lɛ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the pods on my tree turning dark black and going soft during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions. Clearing overgrown branches and improving water drainage around your farm helps keep the air dry and stops the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he nitsumɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akagbi ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my mature cocoa trees turn pale and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during prolonged drought to save water and keep the main trunk alive. Spreading dry grass or crop leaves around the base of the tree as mulch keeps the soil cool and retains water longer.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu tso titri lɛ he. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai aha he lɛ. Tsei ashishitoo haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to heap fresh cocoa beans and cover them with plantain leaves for a few days before drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato kookoo yibii heei ahe gbɛjianɔ ni akɛ plantain baai aha nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani dumɔwui lɛ agbi lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans triggers fermentation, a natural heating process that kills the seed germ, turns the inside of the bean rich brown, and creates the sweet chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ gbɛ ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni ekɛ tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my cocoa beans directly on bare mud or dirt ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ muji ni nɔ bɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans on the bare ground allows soil fungi, goat droppings, and dirt to contaminate them. Drying beans on raised wooden or bamboo mats keeps them clean, uniform, and free from bad molds.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, too ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ muji. Kɛ́ ogbi o-beans lɛ yɛ tso loo ŋmei ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe tseɔ, ni ŋmei gbonyo hu bɛ mli.

english: Why is it so important for me to dry my harvested grains and cocoa beans completely before selling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã mi-cocoa dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: High moisture content inside stored crops causes mold and rot to grow quickly. Removing excess moisture keeps the crop fresh for long-distance transport and prevents spoilage in storage.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa oya. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ehee kɛha gbɛfaa ni yaa shɔŋŋ ni ehaaa efite yɛ nitoohe lɛ.

english: If heavier crops bring more money by weight, why shouldn't I leave extra moisture in my crops when selling?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ haa shika babaoo baa yɛ amɛmlitsiimɔ naa Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ mihɔ̃ɔ?

english: Buyers test moisture levels because wet crops spoil during transport and storage. Damp crops are usually rejected or discounted heavily because excess water ruins the quality of the final product.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi kaa bɔ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ ha ejaakɛ tsei ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ majemɔ kɛ nitoo be mli. Bei pii lɛ, akpooɔ tsei ni efɔ lɛ loo ajieɔ amɛjara waa ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ naagbee nibii ni afee lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested crops are dry enough for storage without using expensive testing equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto ni kaa nibii ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: Well-dried grains or cocoa beans make a sharp cracking sound when bitten or squeezed hard, and they will feel hard and brittle rather than soft or spongy in your hands.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ akɔmɔ loo amɔ mli waa. Ni ebaanu he akɛ ewa ni egbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee blɛoo loo efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ onine mli.

english: Why do my bags of stored grain feel warm when I put my hand inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã kotoku ni ato lɛ mli dɔɔ kɛ mikɛ minine wo mli lɛ?

english: Warmth inside storage bags means there is trapped moisture. The moisture causes the seeds and tiny fungi to breathe rapidly, generating heat that can quickly spoil your entire bag.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ emɔ mli. Fɛ̃i haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ ŋmeii muɔ oya, ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa ni baanyɛ afite obaagi lɛ oya.

english: Why does my dried maize become damp again after I store it inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ beni mikɛto tsu lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dried grains act like sponges and will absorb moisture back out of the damp air or off concrete floors if stored without proper ventilation or plastic sheeting underneath.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni akɛ kɔnkrit fee lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli loo akɛ plastic wo shishi.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruits are ripe enough to produce the highest amount of oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha mu babaoo aba?

english: Oil palm fruits reach peak oil content when the fruit skin turns bright orange-red and a few loose fruits start falling naturally to the ground from the bunch.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛ mu ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ he kɛ́ amɛhiɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse. Ni ŋmei yibii komɛi bɔi shikpɔŋ nɔ gbee kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my groundnuts spoil so quickly if I harvest them when the soil is still very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa amɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Wet soil leaves excess moisture inside the nut shell, which encourages dangerous fungi like aflatoxin to grow, making the groundnuts toxic and unsellable.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine yɛ nut lɛ mli. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce less oil than others planted on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔ fioo fe tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different varieties of palm trees yield different amounts of oil. For example, the Tenera variety has a thinner shell and more oily pulp compared to older wild varieties.
ga: Palm tsei srɔtoi lɛ haa mu falɛi srɔtoi baa. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, Tenera henɔi lɛ ahe tsitsii ni mli tseee kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo kɛ akɛto koo mli henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce fewer fruits with lower oil during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ wooo yibii fioo ni fɔ hu faaa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Oil production requires a lot of water. During prolonged dry spells, the tree saves its energy to survive, leading to smaller fruit bunches with much less oil content.
ga: Mu ni afeɔ lɛ biɔ nu babaoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ Tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibioo, ni fɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why is it wrong for me to dry my harvested cashew nuts directly on bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaagbi cashew ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying nuts on bare ground allows dampness and bacteria from the dirt to soak back into the nuts, reducing their kernel quality and market price.
ga: Beans ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ muji mli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛboteɔ beans lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe sɛɛnamɔ kɛ jarayeli jara baa shi.

english: Why do some farmers plant their crop seeds in small plastic bags first instead of directly into the farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ plastic kotokui bibii amli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaadu yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Nursery bags allow you to give young, delicate seedlings extra protection from harsh direct sunlight, heavy rain, and insects until they grow strong enough to survive in the open farm field.
ga: Grow bags yeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ odumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: How do I know if my seedlings in the nursery are ready to be transplanted onto my main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are generally ready when they have developed three to four strong true leaves and a firm stem, which usually shows they have a healthy root system capable of settling into the farm soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛji amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 3-4 kɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ atswa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when there is no shade above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni hulutsoo bɛ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat; strong sunlight damages their soft leaves and dries out their roots before they can establish deep underground.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ ebaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ egbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋtayaa.

english: Why do I need to plant fast-growing crops like plantain next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ emasɛi? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for young cocoa plants during their early stages.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ amɛshishijee bei amli.

english: What causes the green leaves of my young maize plants to turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is not getting enough nitrogen nutrients from the soil, or that too much standing water around the roots is preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa nitrogen niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ lolo ni ebɔle he Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the base of the plant instead of scattering it everywhere on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the base puts the nutrients directly where the roots can feed on them, while reducing the amount wasted on weeds or washed away by rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ yaa he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni laajeɔ loo nugbɔ shwieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to leave proper space between my crops instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Why is it important to properly space my crops? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, which helps the crops grow larger and yield more harvest.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ ewuuuu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Is it better for me to transplant my nursery seedlings into the field in the morning or late afternoon?
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ amli leebi loo shwane mli.

english: Transplanting in the late afternoon is best because the cooler evening temperatures allow the young plant to recover from the move without the hot sun drying it out.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ mli ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly if I leave weeds around them during their first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop seedlings and steal the essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your young crops need to build strong roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui ni amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season, and will the crop die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a natural way to save water and stay alive; once the rainy season begins, fresh leaves will grow back and root growth will continue.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ ni ahiɔ wala mli. Kɛji akɛ abote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. ni shishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ̃

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to build strong stems and stay deep green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves when there is no rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of saving water during dry periods; by shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss and protects its underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji ŋmei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛbuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines yield bigger tubers underground when I train them to climb tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ koni amɛkwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on sticks allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture more energy to send down into the growing tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when too many suckers grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Extra suckers steal water and food from the soil that the main plant needs; removing excess suckers leaves all the nutrients for one trunk to grow big fruit bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ haa tso kome koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and fail to make good cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmeii kpakpai beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving no single plant with enough strength to form large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and stunting the whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiiha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading a virus that distorts normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu kɛ helai ni fiteɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli.

english: Why do my ripe cowpea pods spoil and turn black when heavy rains fall right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Dry cowpea pods soak up rainwater easily, creating a wet environment on the pod that causes fungi to quickly grow and rot the seeds inside.
ga: Cowpea ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ oya. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa pod lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa oya ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ emli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does putting dry grass on the soil around my garden crops keep them from drying out so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya nɛkɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass creates a protective layer that blocks direct sun heat, keeping the soil cool and trapping ground moisture so plant roots can keep drinking.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ baa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are flooded with water and cannot breathe. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or using well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo mli loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge top leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stem branches and lush leaves above ground rather than storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo tsei niji kakadaji kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide quick canopy shade and hold moisture in the soil, protecting young cocoa plants during their first few fragile years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ oya ni amɛhiɛɔ sũ lɛ mli nu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the same ground where I just harvested eggplants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he ni mikpa eggplant lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and eggplants belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Replanting them in the same spot allows pests and fungal spores hiding in the soil to immediately infect the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ eggplant yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava stems to curl up and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Curled and yellowish foliage on cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the most effective way to prevent this infection.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does striga weed always attach itself around my maize roots and stunt my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe be fɛɛ be ni ehaa mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that taps directly into maize roots to steal water and food. Rotating your farm plot with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts starves the striga seeds in the soil and prevents them from attacking future maize crops.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ. It will starve the striga seeds in the soil. ni amɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatutua ŋmãa tsei wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into powder and get full of tiny holes in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ feɔ powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Small holes and powdery grain in storage are caused by grain weevil insects feeding inside the seeds. Properly drying maize to below 13% moisture and storing it in airtight hermetic bags suffocates the insects and protects your yield.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ starch ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɛɛ 13% ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when extreme heat occurs or when the soil swings from very dry to sudden heavy soaking, causing stress that interrupts the plant's fruit-setting process.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ yibiiwoo naa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their leaves right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baa fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plant roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil for long. Flooded soil starves roots of oxygen, causing the plant to drop its leaves as a panic response to prevent excessive water loss.
ga: Pepper tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbeyeishemɔ hetoohamɔ mli koni nu akafite fe nine.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up completely before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kwraa dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally dry up at the end of the season when the plant finishes transferring all nutrient reserves from the foliage down into the underground tuber, signaling that the yam is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee beni tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli kɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kokoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it better to plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni aaatsɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each plant enough space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm to remove weeds and apply fertilizers without stepping on your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo hu akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oyajie jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ onaji efɔɔɔ onibii anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential plant food found in healthy soil or fertilizers. It can also happen when the soil stays flooded with water for too long, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the soil so you water less, keeps the soil cool during hot afternoons, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
