ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves rolled up with tiny worms inside?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ kɛ baai ni abɔle lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the central leaves of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments can save your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni etsa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off unnecessary branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air to flow and sunlight to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces excess dampness, which helps prevent fungal infections like black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni eha hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants adequate care helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ be fɛɛ be ni akwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: When is the right time for me to apply the first round of fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time for the first fertilizer application is at planting or within two weeks after the seedling sprouts. This early boost gives the young roots the strength to grow deep and build a solid foundation.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ ji be mli ni aduɔ loo yɛ otsii enyɔ mli beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛfee shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the plant starting to crack as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaayɔse akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are common signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from producing food efficiently, which reduces the growth and size of the roots below ground.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cassava mosaic hela he. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Yam rot in the soil is usually caused by fungal infections or tiny worms called nematodes, especially when water stays pooled around the tubers due to poor soil drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ he fɛɛ he. Tubers yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi abifao ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft center leaves of young maize. If left unchecked, they can destroy the main growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite tsei lɛ ashishifãi titri ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do field mice keep digging up my farm after I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli beni midu dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Field mice are attracted to newly planted grain seeds like maize or groundnuts because they are an easy food source. Treating seeds properly before planting or using clean field management reduces their access to the seed beds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu ehee, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii. Ejaakɛ eji niyenii ni anáa oya Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tse tsuɔ nii lɛ baaha gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Extreme heat, insufficient water, or a lack of specific soil nutrients can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to protect themselves instead of investing energy into growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomatoi lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ atsu aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ he nii lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants stay pale green and stunted even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Even with plenty of rainwater, plants need balanced nutrients from manure or fertilizer to build strong green leaves and stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Tsei hu he miihia ni amɛná niyenii ni sa ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛná baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain suckers next to newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantain dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and humidity they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to put my maize seeds in the soil at the start of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to plant after the first two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the ground, ensuring the topsoil stays moist long enough for seeds to sprout without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ bei 2-3 ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time, leading to lower yields.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How does keeping a written record of my harvests help my farm business?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miŋmala mikpamɔ lɛ he saji awo wolo nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Writing down what you harvest and sell helps you track which crops give you good profits, notice if diseases are reducing your yields over time, and plan accurately for buying seeds next season.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmala nɔ ni okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ oshwie shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Kadimɔ akɛ helai srɔtoi Ekɛ onitsumɔ lɛ miiba shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. ni ato dumɔwui ahemɔ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer upper leaves to survive, leaving the old lower leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I know which direction to place my cassava stem cuttings when planting them?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni obaadu o-cassava lɛ yɛ?

english: Always plant cassava stems with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems will struggle to sprout, resulting in poor root growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii bibii hu baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight like a cup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking the sap underneath the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to put bamboo sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in the sun to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they could rot and helps them get maximum sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. If temperatures are too high or the soil goes from very dry to very wet, the plant drops flowers to protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he.

english: Too many shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Leaving only one strong follower shoot ensures the main tree grows a large, healthy bunch of fruit.
ga: Suckers (tsoji) babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie sɛɛnyiɛlɔ tso kome pɛ ni he wa lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ aduawai akuu agbo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my garden eggs turning black and rotting while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually brought on by irregular watering that prevents the roots from taking up calcium steadily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ ni haaa amɛná calcium be fɛɛ be lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and cooling moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Is it best to put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer away into streams or deep underground before the plant roots can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or before light rain.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko baanɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even if I am watering the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with enough water, your crops will starve if weeds consume the food in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii po kɛji jwɛi ye shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my saved maize seeds stop sprouting if I keep them in storage for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ kpaɔ kwɛ̃mɔ kɛji mikɛto be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds are living things that slowly lose their strength over time. If they sit in storage too long without being planted, they dry out or lose their energy, which prevents them from sprouting into healthy crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni fiofio lɛ, amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ amɛtara nitoohe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni aduko Ebaagbi loo ehewalɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haaa amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I test if my stored seeds are still alive before planting them on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo dani madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can place ten seeds on a damp cloth or in a small pot of moist soil for a few days. If seven or eight sprout, your seeds are healthy; if very few sprout, the seed lot has aged and will give a poor field yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ. aloo yɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko ni sũ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ mli mli gbii 2-3, kɛji dumɔwui kpawo loo kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ shweremɔ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ Dumɔwui lɛ hu daa ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: What does it mean when an agricultural officer talks about seed regeneration?
ga: Mɛni amɛtsɔɔ kɛ́ okwaayeli he onukpai wie dumɔwui ni anáa lɛ he?

english: Seed regeneration means taking a small batch of old or stored seeds, planting them in the ground, and harvesting the new, fresh seeds so that specific crop variety stays alive and available for future planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔ tsɔɔ dumɔwui momo loo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ fioo ko, ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ, ni akpaa dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahi shi ni amɛhi shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do traditional crop varieties disappear from our community if we stop growing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ blema tsei srɔtoi lɛ baaje wɔ akutsei lɛ amli kɛji wɔkpa amɛdumɔ?

english: Farm crops depend on farmers to plant and harvest them every year. If farmers stop planting a specific variety, the remaining seeds slowly decay and die, causing that plant variety to vanish completely.
ga: Okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛdu ni amɛkpa daa afi. Kɛji okwaafoi kpa tso pɔtɛɛ ko dumɔ Dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ baafite fiofio ni amɛbaagboi ni no baaha tso henɔi lɛ baaje mli kwraa.

english: How do extension officers keep track of different seed varieties so I get the right one for my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ anɔ koni amɛná dumɔwui ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Officers record crop details on identity records often called passport data. This includes information on plant height, how long it takes to mature, disease resistance, and yield, ensuring you get the exact seed suited for your soil.
ga: Amralofoi ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli fitsofitso yɛ woji ni akɛyooɔ mɔ lɛ amli, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ passport data. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji saji ni kɔɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ he. Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani edaa? helai ahe hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo koni ona dumɔwui ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to buy fresh certified seeds every few years instead of always saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase daa afii fioo komɛi, moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Over time, crop seeds saved on the farm can mix with weaker plants or collect hidden diseases. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures you get clean genetics that produce strong plants and high yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ato yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ afutu tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛhiɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ haa onáa fɔmɔ nii ni he tse ni haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce fewer tubers when I use stem cuttings from the same old field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava stems can accumulate hidden viruses and diseases over many planting seasons without dying. Using old stems repeatedly spreads these diseases, causing the plant to produce smaller and fewer tubers over time.
ga: Cassava tsei baanyɛ ahiɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ bei babaoo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli ni amɛgbooo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei momo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha helai nɛɛ agbɛ ashwã shii abɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ bulbs bibii ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce smaller fruits today compared to the seeds I planted years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiwo yibii bibii kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni midu afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: When you repeatedly save seeds without selecting only the strongest and biggest fruits, the crop gradually loses its best traits across generations, leading to smaller tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji obua dumɔwui anaa shii abɔ Kɛtsɔ yibii ni mli wa ni dara fe fɛɛ pɛ ni ohalaaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ amɛsu ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ fiofio kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do cocoa trees produce fewer cocoa pods as the trees grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their branches become overcrowded, shaded, and prone to diseases. Pruning old wood and renewing the farm with young trees or grafts helps restore heavy pod production.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, eniji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ, ehaa hulutsoo baa, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Niji momoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmɔji heei ni akɛ tsei bibii loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ afee pod ni tsii.

english: What causes my seeds to rot in the soil instead of sprouting after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If seeds are weak, old, or damaged by pests before planting, they cannot wake up fast enough in wet soil. Heavy rain then causes fungus and bacteria to break down the weak seed before it can shoot leaves.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛdara, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ dani adu Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ oya bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ dani amɛwoɔ baai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them out in the open sun without any surrounding shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn and dry out easily under direct heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: When a plantain tree has too many sucker shoots, they all compete for the same nutrients and water in the soil. Pruning away excess suckers and leaving only two or three strong stems per stand allows the main plant to produce larger, healthier bunches.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ ná ŋmeii babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei agboi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is necessary for healthy green leaf growth, so applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure can help restore green growth.
ga: Abele baai lɛ ashishi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni baa eŋɔli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight to feed their underground tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage off damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and results in larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ koni hulu lɛ ajie ehe kpo koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa ni ebaaha bulbs lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants curl up and drop off without producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbee shi ni amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or attacks from sucking insects like thrips and whiteflies. Keeping the soil moist through mulching and spraying for tiny insects prevents flower drop.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips kɛ whiteflies tutua amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛhaa kooloi bibii lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Upward leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by leaf curl viruses spread by whiteflies or by severe water stress. Controlling whiteflies with neem-based sprays and keeping irrigation steady protects the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee lɛ akudɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni abu tsei ahe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help improve the next crop I plant there?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts absorb nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a natural fertilizer stored in their root nodules. When the plant roots decay, this free nitrogen remains in the soil to nourish future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai gboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, vegetable leaves lose water faster than the roots can take it up, causing temporary wilting. Placing dry leaves or straw as mulch around the plant base keeps the root zone cool and slows soil moisture evaporation.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma baa lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crops use to build green, healthy leaves, so when it is lacking, the plant moves what little it has to the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ elaaje lɛ, tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act like large umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from direct sun and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease. It is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread sickness from field to field.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni shwieɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: When temperatures get too hot or water is irregular, tomato plants get stressed. The heat causes the flower pollen to dry out so it cannot form fruit, making the plant drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa Tomato tsei lɛ baahao. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ni aduawai nyɛɛɛ afee. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Planting maize too close forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. As a result, the stalks grow thin and weak, producing tiny cobs with missing kernels.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmei bibioo ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli baa

english: Why are my yam tubers growing crooked and bumpy instead of smooth and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked when the soil is packed too hard or contains many stones. It can also be caused by microscopic worms in the dirt called nematodes that attack the growing tips of the tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni miida lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves inward during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat. This natural reaction stops water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Cowpea shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo lɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why does my avocado tree drop most of its small fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi avocado tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, beni fɔfɔi lɛ ewo sɛɛ?

english: Avocado trees naturally drop excess young fruit because they produce far more flowers than the tree can nourish to full maturity. However, poor watering or bad soil nutrients make the tree drop far more fruit than normal.
ga: Avocado tsei lɛ shwieɔ yibii bibii ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kɛyashi eda. Shi kɛlɛ, nu ni esaaa loo sũ mli niyenii ni esaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ awo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop making new peppers if I delay picking the ripe ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ kɛji mikpa pepper ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: When ripe peppers are left on the plant, the crop receives a signal that its job of making seeds is finished. Picking mature peppers regularly encourages the plant to keep producing new flowers and fresh fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni adu lɛ nine shɛɔ okadi nɔ akɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ nitsumɔ lɛ egbe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eda lɛ tsu nii daa lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi heei kɛ aduawai heei.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest grow into weak plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different parent plants to give maximum strength in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities in the second generation, leading to mixed and low yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni futuɔ kɛ nɔ ni baa shi baa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer will feed the soil and turn the plants green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my piece of land harvest less food each year even though I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaa niyenii fioo daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every season. If you keep planting the same crop without resting the land or rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, the soil becomes exhausted and produces smaller harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ he loo okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more plants in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build thick stalks and full, heavy ears of maize.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa toi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Should I leave all the small shoots growing around my plantain tree or cut some of them away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashwie? Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mifo midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi?

english: You should trim away extra shoots and keep only two or three of different ages. Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal food from the main stalk, resulting in small, thin plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ afii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow instead of spreading wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat and drought stress. Controlling the insects early and watering consistently helps protect the plants from getting stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Mra Be mli Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers falling off the branches before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by excessive heat, lack of water, or attacks from insects like mirids. Shade trees and pest management help the tree keep its flowers so they can develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ hao tso lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which fuels the plant to grow big tubers under the ground while protecting the foliage from dirt-borne rot.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. ni haa tsei lɛ náa tsofa koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni muji kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: Covering the ground with dry mulch keeps the sun from drying out the soil, keeps roots cool during hot days, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly rots into rich soil food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite fiofio koni amɛtsɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster and drink water and soil nutrients much more aggressively than crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the water and nourishment goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ waa fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop, the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack open, and the crop reaches its typical maturity age of 9 to 12 months.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli bei pii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the food that builds large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and ensures maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo baa.

english: Maize draws a lot of nitrogen out of the ground, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally refreshing the land for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so root systems can absorb the nutrients. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can scorch the roots and cause the nutrients to waste away under the hot sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛfite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and turning yellowish-white underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋwɛi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ-yɛŋ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by tiny whitefly pests transmitting cassava mosaic virus. The insects suck plant sap and spread the disease, which stunts the plant and reduces tuber growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii bibii ni gbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ. Kplukai nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are feeding on my young maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall armyworms miiye mibi lɛ ŋmãa?

english: Check the central funnel of the young maize plants for ragged holes in the leaves and small piles of dark green or brown waste (frass) left behind by the caterpillars.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ kɛji buji ni ekumɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ loo ŋmãa ni mli edɔ (ŋmãa) ni ŋmeii eshi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my green tomatoes develop dark, sunken black spots at the bottom before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium into the growing tomatoes.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa tomato ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme dry heat, lack of soil water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and balanced fertilization prevent flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my mango tree flowers keep falling off without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers when they don't get enough moisture during the dry flowering period, or if small insect pests damage the blossoms. Ensuring steady soil moisture and protecting blossoms helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the fruits inside the middle of my tree stay small and green while the outside ones grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Outer branches block sunlight from reaching the inner parts of the tree. Trimming weak inner branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach all parts, helping all fruits grow and ripen evenly.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ he fɛɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under direct heat from the sun. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that shade young cocoa trees, giving them the moisture and protection they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa nu kɛ hebuu ni he hiaa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why are the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree turning black and drying up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: This is often caused by cherelle wilt, where the tree drops extra young pods it cannot afford to feed, or by sap-sucking pests like capsids. Giving the tree enough water and food helps it carry more pods to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cherelle lɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni eshwɛ ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛha nikpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛgboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips on lower leaves means your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen in the soil to keep its leaves green and grow big cobs.
ga: Yellow ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni wa kɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ baa.

english: Why does my cassava have huge green leafy bushes on top but very thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ jwɛi agbo ko ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into leaf growth instead of building tubers. Cassava needs potassium in the soil to transfer food down into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii. Cassava he miihia potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo eshishifãi wuji ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sun exposure to make food for the tubers buried in the mound. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground so leaves catch sunlight instead of rotting in damp shade.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni afu yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni amɛaafite yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium to the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture balanced helps the plant feed calcium to the developing fruits.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium haa aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn pale when heavy rain leaves standing water in my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits for days, it smothers the roots, stopping them from taking up food and causing the leaves to turn pale and stall growth.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi shi gbii babaoo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haaa amɛye nii. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to grow. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish. It also allows soil pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in that spot, weakening future harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni sũ mli kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ. Enɛ baaha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil receives steady, heavy rain for two or three consecutive days rather than planting after the very first light shower. Seeds need continuous moisture in the topsoil to germinate and establish strong roots without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui hia nu ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but yielding tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are given too much fertilizer early on, the cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing food in its roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fe nine mra. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and high temperatures. Large trees act as protective umbrellas that keep the air cool and moist around young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand full heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebɔleɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why are there tiny caterpillars eating holes in the central funnel leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the moist central leaf funnel of maize plants to feed on soft new leaves, which damages the plant before it can grow stalks and ears.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tsei ahe baai ni mli efɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ gbeɔ tso lɛ dani enyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ toi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft, black, and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ, ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit or irregular watering. When watering is uneven, the plant cannot transport calcium from the soil up to the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest of hybrid maize yield much less than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi tsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants to produce high yields in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special genetics, leading to unpredictable, weaker plants with smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai fɔmɔ nii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, allowing them to steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crop's root zone.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do plantain crops seem to grow so tall and yield so much fruit in areas like Agogo compared to my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ he ko tamɔ Agogo kɛ akɛto mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains thrive best in deep, rich, well-draining soil with plenty of organic matter and steady moisture, which allows the root system to expand fully and support heavy bunch sizes.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ.

english: What causes a plantain tree to produce a large, full bunch of fruit instead of a small one?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains woɔ yibii wuji ni eyi obɔ yɛ bibii najiaŋ?

english: A plantain tree produces large bunches when it gets enough sunlight, consistent soil moisture, nutrients like potassium, and when excess suckers are cut away so the mother plant gets all the energy.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baawo niji babaoo kɛji amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu yɛ be fɛɛ mli, niyenii tamɔ potassium, kɛ be mli ni afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. koni tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ

english: How can I keep my harvested plantains from spoiling quickly when sending them on long journeys to distant markets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya kɛ́ akɛmiiya gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ kɛmiiya jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvesting plantains while they are still full but completely green, keeping them in cool shade, and packing them carefully with dry leaves prevents bruising and delays premature ripening during transport.
ga: Plantains ni akpaa yɛ be mli ni amɛyi obɔ lolo ni amɛfee ŋmɔji kwraa lɛ. Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔlɔ naa ni ebaaha amɛshwere oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: How do new plantain plants grow out of the ground, and when should I separate them from the main tree?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui heei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ magbala kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ he?

english: Plantains grow new shoots called suckers from their underground root base; you should let one or two strong suckers remain for the next crop and dig up the extra ones to plant elsewhere when they reach about knee-height.
ga: Plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii heei ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli. Esa akɛ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi atsu nii ni okɛdu yɛ he kroko beni amɛshɛ aaafee amɛnaji ahe lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or that the soil is holding too much water and choking the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my harvested plantains start ripening all at the same time after I cut them off the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ fɛɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ yɛ be kome mli beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cut, plantains naturally release a ripening gas called ethylene; keeping harvested bunches in a well-ventilated, cool place away from ripe fruit helps slow down this process.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo plantains lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: How does dry weather affect the way my plantain crops grow and fruit?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa mi plantain tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose a lot of water daily, so dry weather without sufficient soil moisture causes the leaves to dry up, delays flowering, and leads to thin, light bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu babaoo fiteɔ daa gbi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when the fruit bunch becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees lack a deep taproot, so heavy fruit bunches or damage to the underground corm from soil pests like weevils can cause the entire tree to uproot unless supported with strong wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso yibii lɛ ni shwieɔ shi loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ajie. ja tso ni mli wa fiɔ sɛɛ

english: How can I tell the exact right time to cut down my plantain bunch for selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain ŋmɔji ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to cut when the individual fingers become plump and lose their sharp outer ridges, even while the skin remains deep green.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ ebaafo beni nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔjɔ ni esɛɛgbɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efo mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo moŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting plantains too close forces them to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil food, making the trees grow thin and weak while producing small, poor-quality fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: How many bags of corn should I expect to harvest from one acre of land if I adopt modern farming methods?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi tsu nii lɛ, esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa ŋmãa kotokui enyiɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: When you use improved seed varieties, proper plant spacing, and the correct fertilizer regimen, a single acre of land can produce around 30 to 40 bags of corn, compared to older methods that yield far less.
ga: Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni asaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii Gbɛ ni sa ni ka tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja lɛ teŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ acre kome baanyɛ ajie ŋmãa kotokui aaafee 30 kɛyashi 40, kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni baa shi kwraa kɛjɛɔ blema gbɛi amli lɛ he.

english: Why do my corn crops yield so few bags while my neighbor gets a heavy harvest from the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotoku bibioo ko yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Differences in yield usually come down to soil nutrition, seed quality, and timing. Using certified hybrid seeds instead of saved grains, along with timely weed control and fertilizer, drastically increases crop productivity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibii sɔrɔtoi ni anáa lɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ahe su kɛ be. Hybrid dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ najiaŋ. kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ be naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: What specific farming habits do I need to change to boost my crop yield this season?
ga: Mɛɛ okwaayeli su pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ matsake koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Key habits to change include switching from saved seeds to certified high-yielding varieties, planting in neat rows with exact spacing rather than random scattering, and applying fertilizer at the right stage of plant growth.
ga: Sui titrii ni esa akɛ atsake lɛ ekomɛi ji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli tsakemɔ kɛmiiya dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli lɛ anɔ. Dumɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli fɛfɛo kɛ gbɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaagbɛ ashwã ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ

english: Why perform better when I buy new hybrid seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mihe dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to grow uniformly, resist pests, and produce larger cobs. Saved seeds lose their vigor over time, resulting in weaker plants and far fewer bags at harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbɛ kotokui babaoo kɛji akpa amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young corn plants turn yellow and stop growing fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are starving for nitrogen in the soil or are competing with weeds for food. Applying the right crop fertilizer early in the season restores their green color and keeps them growing fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ jwɛi miitswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ su lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Is taking a bank loan to buy fertilizer and improved seeds worth the risk for my farm?
ga: Ani shika ni mifaa kɛjɛɔ shikatoohe koni mikɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ sa oshara ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Taking a loan for farm inputs can be a smart move if used directly for quality seeds and fertilizer, because the resulting increase in yield (such as reaching up to 40 bags per acre) provides enough income to pay off the debt and leave substantial profit.
ga: Shika ni akɛfaa koni akɛhe nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nilee gbɛ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛha dumɔwui ni hi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Akɛni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ etee hiɛ waa hewɔ lɛ (akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, ashɛɔ kotokui 40 yɛ acre kome mli) hewɔ lɛ, shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaawo nyɔmɔ ni ashi sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ.

english: Why does delaying my investment in fertilizer lower my crop harvest even if I buy it later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi kɛji mihe yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Crops need critical nutrients early in their lifecycle to build strong root systems and stems. Delaying fertilizer starves the crop during its main growth spurt, causing permanent reduction in cob size that later fertilizing cannot fix.
ga: Niyenii ni he hiaa waa he miihia tsei yɛ amɛshihilɛ shishijee mli koni amɛma shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ fɔmɔ nii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ yɛ be titri ni edaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ dalɛ baa shi daa. Anyɛɛɛ ajaje enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting my corn seeds too close together affect how the crop grows?
ga: Te ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When corn plants are crowded, they compete aggressively with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress leads to tall, thin stalks that break easily and cobs with very few kernels.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni fãa oya kɛ tsei bibii ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my corn ears come out half-empty with missing grains at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ fã bɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when the crop suffers from heat stress, drought, or nutrient shortages during the flowering stage, which prevents complete pollination of the cob.
ga: Nibii ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kwraa lɛ naa.

english: How can I protect my crops from failing completely during unexpected dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite kwraa yɛ hɔmɔ ni mikpaaa gbɛ lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your farm by planting drought-tolerant corn varieties, applying organic mulch to retain soil moisture, and planting early with the very first reliable rains of the season.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Kɛ organic mulch atsu nii ni okɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. ni adu kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: Which crops will grow best if my farmland has a lot of sand in it?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ ŋã babaoo?

english: Sandy soil drains water very quickly and loses nutrients easily. Crops like cassava, groundnuts, and cowpeas do well in sandy soil because they handle dry conditions better than crops that need constant moisture like rice.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ oya waa ni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ oya. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛtsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei ni biɔ ŋmei be fɛɛ be tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do the roots of my vegetable crops rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When water sits on the land for too long without draining, it fills up all the air pockets, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct, intense sunlight. They require shade from trees or plantains to shield them and keep the soil cool while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo tsei bibii amli koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants roll their leaves tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from escaping during peak heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ baa shi yɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje kpo yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and crooked when the ground is very hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers grow by expanding underground. If the soil is too hard or compacted, the roots struggle to push through the dirt, resulting in short, thin, deformed tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo ebɔle ehe Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ yɛ kuku ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants fall over easily whenever strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. Mounding up dirt around the stem gives the roots extra support and keeps the plant standing upright.
ga: Pepper tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ babaoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I put too many seeds in one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo dumɔ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes all of them grow tall, thin, and weak with very low harvests.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛ fɛɛ amɛkwɛɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa ni yibiiwoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive thieves on your farm. They grow faster than crops and steal the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to produce healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is a key nutrient that helps plants stay green, and when the soil lacks it, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the newer growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant on the exact same plot without a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every crop harvest removes nutrients from the ground. If you continuously farm the same plot without adding manure or fertilizer, or without letting the land rest, the soil becomes depleted and cannot support heavy yields.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. aloo ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji anɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very tall stems with lots of leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishitso lɛ kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in heavy shade, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo edaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right moisture level in the soil before I start sowing my seeds at the beginning of the rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until the rains are steady enough to wet the top level of soil deeply for two to three consecutive days. Sowing in dry or barely damp soil causes seeds to rot or fail to sprout.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no beneficial insects around to shake the flowers and spread pollen.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaakpokpo fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize removes a lot of food from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly and turn wrinkle-like?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the sap underneath the leaves and spread leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot on the branches before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shaded environments. Pruning excess tree branches allows sun and air to dry out the farm and protect the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, edɔ, kɛ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the mound before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects in the soil without draining away properly, creating soaked conditions that favor fungi and water-logging rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni haa ŋmeii kɛ nu mli ŋmeii ahe naagbai baa.

english: Yam vines climb tall supports to expose more leaves to sunlight, which enables the plant to produce more energy and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that heavy rains have washed away nitrogen from the soil or that waterlogged roots cannot breathe to absorb essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu koni amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, over-fertilization, or irregular soil moisture causes stress to pepper plants, making them drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Ha amɛshwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather, especially if cocoa trees are too crowded and lack good air circulation.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ cacao lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon sun even if the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In hot afternoon sunshine, tomato leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the wet soil, so the plant wilts temporarily to conserve moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the fertilizer I put around my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain can wash fertilizers away from the roots into deeper soil or nearby streams (leaching), preventing crops from absorbing the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ loo faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli (leaching), ni no haaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are adapted to germinate immediately with the first drop of water, whereas domestic crops take longer to break seed dormancy and establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu klɛŋklɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shia tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi.

english: Why do I need to leave specific distances between cassava stems when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?
