english: Proper spacing ensures each cassava plant receives enough sunlight, air, and soil space to develop big, healthy tubers without competing against surrounding roots.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa ŋmei agbo ni mli wa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, the stem thickens, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ, ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ́ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What does it mean when other farmers talk about 'condemned' weed chemicals, and is it safe to use on my farm?
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafoi krokomɛi wie tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ‘abu fɔ’ lɛ ahe lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ? Ni ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Condemned' is a common local term for non-selective weedkillers that destroy every green plant they touch. They are useful for clearing raw bush land before planting, but they will kill your crops if sprayed directly on them.
ga: Afolɔ enaa’ ji maŋ lɛ mli wiemɔ ko ni akɛtsɔɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa mɔ ni kpataaa tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ hiɛ. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ aaajie hei ni tsei bibii ni kwɛɔ daa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ dani adu. Shi ebaagbe oŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ afɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and wither if the spray from my weedkiller touches their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ ebaai lɛ kpe lɛ?

english: Most weedkillers burn plant tissues on contact or stop the plant from making food. Even small droplets drifting in the wind onto crop leaves will disrupt their growth, causing them to turn yellow and die.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shãa tso lɛ fãji kɛji amɛshɛ he loo amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafee niyenii. Nu bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ po tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do some weeds dry up within a few hours of spraying while others take almost a week to die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi gbɛ́ɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ otsi dani amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Fast-acting chemicals are contact weedkillers that burn only the top leaves quickly. Slow-acting chemicals are systemic weedkillers that travel inside the plant down to the roots to kill the whole weed completely over several days.
ga: Tsofai ni tsuɔ nii oya ji tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni shãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi pɛ oya. Tsofai ni tsuɔ nii blɛoo lɛ ji tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yaa tso lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni egbe jwɛi fɛɛ yɛ gbii babaoo mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I spray strong chemicals on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa eshwie ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spraying destroys the growing weeds on top of the soil, but thousands of weed seeds remain hidden inside the soil. Once rain falls and sunlight hits the ground, those hidden seeds germinate and grow into new weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakpata jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Shi jwɛi dumɔwui akpei abɔ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni hulu lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ jwɛi heei.

english: How do I know the right measurement of weedkiller chemical to mix with water in my spraying tank?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ susumɔ ni ja ni akɛfutuɔ nu ni yɔɔ spray tanki lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Always use the measuring cap provided on the chemical bottle and follow the recommended dose on the label. Using too much chemical wastes money and damages the soil, while using too little allows weeds to survive and become resistant.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ susumɔ tsɔne ni akɛha yɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni onyiɛ tsofa lɛ falɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ heɔ shika ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofa fioo ko pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛfee nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela lɛ.

english: Can I mix two different types of weed chemicals together in my spraying machine at the same time to work faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai enyɔ ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afata he yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ mli koni amɛtsu nii oya?

english: No, mixing different chemicals without guidance can cause them to react badly together. This can reduce their strength, create toxic fumes, or damage your crops and sprayer machine.
ga: Dabi Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Kɛ́ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ bɛ lɛ, ekolɛ tsofai nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hewalɛ aba shi, ekɛ lasu ni yɔɔ gbeyei aba, loo efite onibii kɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ.

english: How many days should I wait after spraying weedkiller on my land before it is safe to plant my seeds?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait 7 to 14 days after spraying before planting your seeds. This gives the chemical enough time to break down in the soil so it does not burn or kill your newly germinating crop seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, mɛ aaafee gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 ni okɛdu dumɔwui. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbala yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, eshãŋ loo egbeŋ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I clear weeds with a cutlass or use chemical sprays before planting?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsɔne shwie jwɛi loo mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ dani midu?

english: Clearing with a cutlass protects the soil organisms and leaves organic matter to feed your crops, but takes a lot of time. Chemical sprays save labor on large fields, but using them continuously without break can damage beneficial soil microbes.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe ni eshiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii. Shi eheɔ be babaoo. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nitsumɔ baa shi yɛ hei wuji. Shi kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii ni etseee lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly in places where heavy weedkiller was sprayed during the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi babaoo shwie nɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Over-spraying can leave harsh chemical residues in the dirt that damage delicate crop roots and kill beneficial earthworms and microbes that help plants feed on soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai fɔ̃ɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are some weed chemicals sold very cheap at the market while others cost a lot more money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahɔ̃ɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ekomɛi yɛ jara nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu jara wa kwraa lɛ?

english: Cheaper chemicals may be diluted, expired, or harsh non-selective types that carry higher risks to your soil. More expensive options are often refined, crop-safe, or systemic formulas from approved manufacturers that protect your crops long-term.
ga: Tsofai ni jara waaa lɛ baanyɛ afee tsofai ni mli ewo nu, ni efite, loo tsofai ni mli wa ni halaaa mɔ. ni yɔɔ oshara babaoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, atsakeɔ gbɛi ni jara wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Fomula ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii loo gbɛjianɔtoo ni jɛ nifeelɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni buɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my mango tree falling off without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers often drop due to fungal infections during damp weather, attacks by tiny insects like thrips, or water stress. Ensuring good airflow by pruning dead branches and protecting the flowers early helps them set into healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fungal helai ahewɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo nu mli haomɔ ni baa lɛ Kwɛmɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni ooofo kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni ooobu mra lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa niji lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce a heavy crop one year, but almost no fruit the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewooo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: This is known as alternate bearing. When a tree uses up almost all its stored energy and nutrients to produce a bumper crop in one season, it needs the next season to rest and rebuild its strength before it can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei kɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli. Esa akɛ tso lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni ená hewalɛ kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dani ewo yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is short of nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow thin, weak, and pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal light, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. When weeds grow close, your crop plants spend all their energy fighting for survival instead of building strong stems and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwuɔ koni amɛhi shi. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the stem before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, shaded conditions. The fungus spreads through rain splashes, turning healthy green cocoa pods black and ruining the beans inside.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Fungus gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ. ni efite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Once infected, the plant cannot process sunlight efficiently, causing leaf twisting and reducing the number of tomatoes produced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tomato ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete with the mother plant for food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, resulting in bigger and heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛkɛ nyɛ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to grow large, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eyakwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off when the afternoon heat becomes very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to shed flowers to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out. Providing light shade or adequate watering during dry spells helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ mli tseɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akashwie shi.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully ready for harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the swelling tubers push upward against the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the key nutrient that keeps crop leaves green and helps them produce big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa toi wuji ni wa baa.

english: How do I know when my maize is ready to harvest for market or processing into food like kenkey?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa koni ahɔ̃ɔ loo afee niyenii tamɔ kenkey?

english: Maize is ready for dry grain harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, and the kernels are hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ akpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa akɛ otsitsii lɛ nyɛŋ atswa amɛ mlɛo.

english: Can I put fresh droppings from my chicken farm directly onto my crop beds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni jɛ mi-kooloo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afata ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh poultry droppings are very strong and can burn your crop roots. You should dry or compost the manure with soil for a few weeks before spreading it around your plants.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ eshã otsei lɛ ashishifãi. Esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi loo okɛ sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛshwã otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my crops produce better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients and helps the dirt hold water longer, which keeps your plants strong and healthy even during dry weather.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa muji ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ po.

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's way of saving water during heat. As long as the stem remains green inside, the root tubers will survive underground and sprout fresh leaves when the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmei tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo yɛ emli lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms instead of forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients can stress tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy instead of producing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni ehiii Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tomato.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to full sun so the plant can feed itself and build large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛaaha amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ana niyenii ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my young crops flowering when the plants are still very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: When a plant lacks water or nutrients, it gets stressed and tries to make seeds early before dying. Proper watering and fertilizer help the plant grow large before it flowers.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ Ehaoɔ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ dumɔwui ato mra dani egbo. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why does my fresh farm produce rot so quickly after I harvest it for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii heei lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikpa koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting in the hot afternoon heat traps warm air inside your bags, causing produce to spoil quickly. Harvest early in the morning and keep your crops in a shaded area.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kpamɔ mra ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shĩa mli.

english: What fast-growing vegetable crops can I plant to earn quick money between major farming seasons?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya yɛ okwaayeli be titri lɛ mli?

english: Short-cycle crops like garden eggs, okra, and pepper mature in a few months, allowing you to harvest and sell quickly to earn income while waiting for longer season crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, okra kɛ ŋmeii baakwɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is good enough for planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ?

english: Good soil for maize is usually dark in color, breaks apart easily in your hands, and holds moisture without becoming a thick mud swamp. Dark soil usually means it has plenty of decayed leaves and organic material that feed young plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ yɛ enine mli oya ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ diŋ tsɔɔ akɛ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa tsei bibii lɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from agricultural officers instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛtsu nii lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛ heɔ wuhi nɛ a je nyagbe ní kpami be ɔ mi ɔ yi wami.

english: Certified seeds are specifically tested and treated to grow fast, produce higher yields, and resist local pests and dry spells. Seeds saved from past harvests often lose their vigor over time, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ pɔtɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Ha yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do you recommend planting my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every single plant gets enough space, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much faster and easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing tiny holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by insects like the Fall Armyworm. They feed on tender leaves, but catching them early and applying the right pest control early in the morning or late evening saves the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Shi kɛji akɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow with strange green spots and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or spread through infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural extension services prevents this problem.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsumɔhei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ duɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my farm after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when given in stages: a first portion near the roots around planting or two weeks after sprouting, and a second portion when the crop is growing fast, just before it starts flowering.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli: nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Dumɔ loo otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ, beni tso lɛ daa oya dani ebɔi fɔmɔ.

english: When crops get too much water, their roots cannot breathe in the soggy ground, causing the leaves to turn pale yellow and droop, even though the soil is wet.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly and aggressively even after I clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa waa yɛ be mli ni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions. Their seeds lie hidden in the soil and sprout rapidly with the first rains to steal water, light, and nutrients before your planted crops get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli koni amɛju nu, la kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani onibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know when my maize is completely dry and ready to be harvested for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Maize is ready for storage when the outer husks turn dry and papery brown, and the grains become hard enough that you cannot dent them with your thumbnail. Drying them thoroughly prevents mold and webbed insects from ruining stored grain.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo kɛha nitoo kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, egbi ni efee tamɔ wolo. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nine bibioo ko. Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmaa ni ato lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce wide leaves that shade young cocoa plants, keeping the soil moist and protecting them during their critical first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed away plant nutrients. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer early helps plants regain green leaves and produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ efo tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. NPK loo urea ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa baai eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and look wrinkled during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl under intense heat to reduce water loss, but persistent curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites. Inspecting the underside of leaves and using neem water spray helps keep pests away.
ga: Shi oyitsɔi lɛ ni ebɔle ehe yɛ la ni naa wa shishi koni nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ neem tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during midday even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ aaafee shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil. As long as the soil remains damp, plants naturally recover as temperatures drop in the late afternoon.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi yɛ shwane mli.

english: Why is it wrong for me to plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, leading to thin stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and space to grow big and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ehiɛ wa.

english: Why should I prune the lower branches and suckers off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji kɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches removes useless growth that steals nutrients from pod development. It also allows sunlight and air to move freely through the farm, reducing the moisture that causes black pod disease.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ shweremɔ ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ aba shi.

english: How does covering my garden beds with dry grass help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mibɔɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sun rays. It keeps soil cool, reduces how often you need to water, prevents weeds from taking over, and turns into organic compost over time.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop black rot at the bottom of the fruit before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Bottom rot on tomatoes is caused by irregular watering and low calcium levels in the soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent throughout flowering and fruit growth prevents this damage.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato shishi fitemɔ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ be fɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up for market?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a cluster of leaves at the top, and cracks appear on the soil surface near the root as tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ shwereɔ kwraa kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shi baai akuu ko yɛ nɔ. ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I dig up my yam tubers immediately after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ajieɔ sweet potato ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Harvesting yams in wet, soggy soil makes tubers dirty and prone to scratches during digging. Scratched, damp yams rot quickly in storage before you can sell them at market.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee muji ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Sweet potatoes ni mli edɔ ni efolɔ mli lɛ baafite oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong sunlight and hot winds. They need plantains or shade trees above them to protect their tender leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist until their roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná plantain loo tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo wu ni amɛhe wa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early helps leaves open up and grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year when I plant it on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the same specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it in the same spot continuously drains the land and allows soil pests to build up, whereas alternating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu be fɛɛ be, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abɔle amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do yams need large soil mounds to grow well instead of being planted in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ wuji ahe hiaa sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand under the ground and need loose, soft soil to develop long, smooth roots without pressure. High mounds create deep, light soil and prevent rain from pooling around the yam and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛná shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔnyɛɛ ko bɛ he. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tseee. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ Sweet potatoes kɛ rotten he

english: Why should I push cassava stem cuttings into the soil at a slant instead of laying them flat on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant buries several growing nodes underground where roots can form safely, while keeping the top buds facing upward so shoots can quickly grow into leafy stems.
ga: Yucca tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ futuɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni shishifãi baanyɛ afee shweshweeshwe lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋta lɛ anyɛ ada oya ni etsɔ ŋta ni yɔɔ baai.

english: Why do my crops give me a smaller total harvest when I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and plant food, and their leaves block light from one another. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow full and produce larger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without turning into fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up their pollen, preventing the flowers from fertilizing. When a flower cannot form a seed, the plant drops it to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Beni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ Tsei shwieɔ dumɔwui koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and thin even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight meant for your plants. Even with heavy rain, weeds consume the essential plant food before your crop roots can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ Jwɛi hu yeɔ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest produce smaller yields than fresh seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give a high yield in their very first planting. Seeds harvested from that crop lose those special high-yielding traits in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii krokomɛi lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing good pods if I let them grow too many thick, wild branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii kpakpai kɛji miha amɛniji ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extra branches steal nutrients and block sunlight from reaching the main trunk where cocoa pods grow. Pruning unnecessary branches directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso titri lɛ he ni kookoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Niji ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ mli lɛ kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does cutting off dead or diseased branches from my cocoa tree prevent the whole farm from getting sick?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafo lɛ baatsi ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ naa koni hela akamɔ amɛ?

english: Yes, plant diseases can easily spread from branch to branch and from tree to tree. Removing damaged branches early stops the sickness from spreading and keeps the rest of your farm healthy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tso nine nɔ kɛya tso nine nɔ kɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ oya. Niji ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa hela gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni oye obua ni oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does clearing the grass and bushes under my cocoa trees help the crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ ahe saamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds and tall grass steal water and soil nutrients from your cocoa trees. Clearing the ground underneath removes this competition, allowing your crop to get all the food and moisture it needs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ ajuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli. Shishigbɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii náa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce fewer pods when the trees are overcrowded and untrimmed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowded trees block sunlight and trap heavy, damp air around the crops. Cocoa trees need both sunlight and good airflow to flower properly and set healthy pods without rotting.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa fɛɛ he miihia kookoo tsei koni amɛfɔ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ waa ni amɛgbooo

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves lose moisture quickly in intense sunshine. When the soil lacks water, the tree sheds leaves to save its remaining moisture and prevent itself from drying out completely.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ amli fɛ̃i lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ he ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Excessive wetness allows fungal diseases like Black Pod to grow on the pods. Protecting the trees and applying proper water-based spray treatments prevents the rain from ruining your pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ obu otsei lɛ ahe ni okɛ nu ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akafite o-pods lɛ.

english: Why is it important to loosen and dig hard soil before planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli ni atsa dani adu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Hard soil makes it very difficult for tender young roots to spread out and find food. Digging loosens the soil so roots can grow deep and absorb water easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna niyenii. Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe nu oya.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees start producing smaller pods than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni edara lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii beni amɛdarako lɛ?

english: As crops grow over many years, they suck nutrients out of the earth. Without feeding the soil through compost or fertilizers, the tree lacks the strength to make large pods.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da afii babaoo Amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are ready to harvest without picking them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛkpaaa amɛ mra tsɔ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color, usually turning bright yellow or orange. Harvesting at full ripeness ensures the beans inside have reached maximum weight and quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe Bei pii lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ beni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii.

english: Why is it bad to leave harvested cocoa pods lying on the wet ground for many days before carrying them home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ gbii babaoo dani akɛya shia lɛ?

english: Pods left on wet farm ground attract pests and fungus that rot the outer shell and spoil the beans inside, reducing the quality and value of your harvest.
ga: Pods ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ mli nibii ni hi kɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure around the base will help the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Konii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ni eda waa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and retains soil moisture during hot days. It also prevents weeds from growing and breaks down into natural fertilizer over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know when it is safe for me to plant my seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best not to plant immediately after the very first rain because the deep soil underneath is still dry and young sprouts can burn. Wait until you get two or three steady rains so the ground stays moist enough for the seeds to survive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo, ni tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashã. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide quick umbrella-like shade that cools the soil and protects the young cocoa trees during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni tamɔ ambrela oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward the sun to capture light and build large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal leaves diseases and rotting.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la ni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ eshwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akatsi fungal leaf hela kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, intercropping cowpeas with maize is very helpful. Cowpeas fix nitrogen into the soil to feed the maize, while their broad leaves cover the ground to prevent soil drying and stop weeds from taking over.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas haa nitrogen lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi ni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during the Harmattan to save water and survive the heat. Maintaining shade trees on your farm and putting mulch around the roots helps the soil keep moisture through the dry period.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ Harmattan beaŋ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni okɛ sũ wo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme heat stresses the plant or when watering is irregular. Giving your crops consistent water and light protection during the hottest hours helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu kɛ la ha onibii lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with dark sticky dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's central growing point. Checking your crops early and applying approved biopesticides or neem extract into the shoot funnel can control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my neighbor's cocoa trees turning yellow and spreading to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees can catch contagious viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is carried by tiny insects called mealybugs from infected farms to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei baanyɛ aná helai ni jɛɔ muawai amli tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni koolooi bibii kɛbaa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can cocoa trees recover on their own if they catch swollen shoot disease?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ kɛji amɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ miipiŋ amɛ?

english: No, once a cocoa tree is infected with swollen shoot virus, it cannot heal itself and will eventually die, so infected trees must be cut down to stop the spread to healthy trees.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ hela ni efuu lɛ emɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli pɛ lɛ, Enyɛŋ etsa ehe ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods sometimes turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Bei komɛi lɛ amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and heavy shade, destroying young pods before they can mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kpatamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛdara.

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees are too old and need to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni atsake amɛ?

english: When cocoa trees reach 25 to 30 years of age, their yield drops significantly and they become more vulnerable to diseases, meaning they have reached the end of their productive life.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ eshɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee.

english: What happens to the soil when I cut down old cocoa trees to plant new ones?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mifo kookoo tso momo ko koni mikɛdu ehee?

english: Removing old trees exposes the soil to direct sunlight and rain, which washes away nutrients and dries out the land, making soil treatment necessary before planting new seedlings.
ga: Tsei momoi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ. Ehe miihia ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings take several years before they start bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need 3 to 5 years to build strong root systems and sturdy trunks before they have enough strength and nutrients to support growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa. dani ená hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ

english: Why is it important to measure and map the exact size of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ he ni mafee he mfoniri lɛ?

english: Mapping your farm tells you the exact land area, which helps you buy the right amount of fertilizer, plant the correct number of seedlings, and accurately predict your yield.
ga: Okwaafoi ahe mfonirifeemɔ baatsɔɔ bo he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa. Dumɔ dumɔwui ayibɔ ni sa. ni etsɔɔ nibii ni abaafee lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: What happens to cocoa crop growth if I plant the trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Trees planted too close together fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak trees that produce fewer cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a defense mechanism that helps cocoa trees conserve water during dry weather so they can survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do cocoa trees need shade trees growing above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kookoo tsei aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees evolved as forest undergrowth, so larger shade trees protect their leaves from sun damage and keep the soil moist and cool.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ kooi. No hewɔ lɛ tsei wuji buɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe koni hulu akafite amɛ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stay green. Adding animal manure or compost supplies this missing food so the maize can grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa nɛɛ he nii, ni ebaaha ŋmei lɛ adara waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms during the hot dry season without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause pepper plants stress, so they drop their flowers to conserve water and survive. Giving the plants shade and watering them regularly helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi haoɔ pepper tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha otsei lɛ ni oha amɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving them enough space allows each plant to form thick, heavy underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine ni miida yɛ Midumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: The main plantain stem shares its water and food with every small sucker around it. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the main tree to produce a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm help my maize grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, these roots decompose and leave free plant food in the soil for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when rain falls continuously for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be kakadaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. Continuous heavy rain floods the soil and suffocates the roots, allowing water molds and rot to attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ muji tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers, and the tree needs enough water. If there are few insects or water is scarce, unpollinated flowers dry up and fall off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa tsei. Kɛji kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ Fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollination lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ ni eda lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to look weak and produce smaller food for my household?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhaa niyenii fioo pɛ amɛhaa mishiabii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early leaves all the available nutrients for your crops to produce a large harvest.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni amɛ juɔ hulu la ni he hia, nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the soil so they get full sun and remain safe from ground pests and rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves toward sunlight to produce food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant grow larger tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and grow. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts on the same field where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil. This enriches the ground with free nutrients that help nearby maize plants grow better.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does covering the ground around my crops with dry grass help during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa he ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground and shields plant roots from hot sunlight. It keeps the soil cool, reduces water loss, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants wrinkle up tightly like a fist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ tamɔ fiji lɛ?

english: Wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insect pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Applying neem oil solution or an appropriate crop spray clears these pests so leaves can grow flat again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators like bees. Providing consistent water at the root level and light shade helps flowers stay on the vine to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaving too many small shoots causes them to fight with the mother plant for food, water, and sunlight. Removing excess shoots leaves one or two strong stems, ensuring your plantain tree produces larger, heavier bunches.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ efee babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ kɛ tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Enɛ baaha plantain lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to plant for my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Choose hard, healthy stems from mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old, avoiding soft green tops or stem parts damaged by insects. Stem cuttings taken from the middle of a healthy main stalk produce the strongest roots.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ ŋmei tsei ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tso lɛ fãi ni kooloi efite lɛ ahe. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni wa fe fɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for me to plant maize after the first rainy day?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Scoop up a handful of topsoil from your field and squeeze it: if it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping water or crumbling instantly, the soil has ideal moisture for your seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fioo ko ni okɛmimɔ mli: kɛji akɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ efee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo efooo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ koni odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I use sticks to lift my tomato plants off the ground instead of letting them spread on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei niji woɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants lie flat on the ground, damp soil and dirt pests cause the leaves and fruits to rot easily. Tying them to sticks lifts the plant upwards, keeping the harvest clean and allowing sunlight to reach every part of the crop.
ga: Beni tomato tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛfi tso nine he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo tso lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ lɛ mli tseɔ, ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ nikpamɔ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he.

english: How does helping my yam vines climb wooden poles help them make bigger tubers underground?
ga: Te mi-sweet potato lɛ ni miyeɔ mibuaa amɛ koni amɛkwɔ tso ko nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves like solar panels to make energy for growing heavy tubers beneath the soil. When you stake them so they grow tall, the leaves get maximum sunlight instead of shading each other on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei ni amɛkɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Beni okɛ amɛ fɔ̃ɔ tso nɔ koni amɛdara babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baaná hulu la babaoo moŋ fe ni amɛaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to train cucumber vines to climb ropes or frames?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔtsɔse kukumba wain tsei koni amɛkwɔ kpãi loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ?

english: Training cucumber vines to grow upwards keeps the cucumbers straight, unblemished, and free from ground rot. It also makes harvesting much faster because you can pick the fruits while standing up instead of searching through muddy leaves.
ga: Kukumba wain tsei ni atsɔseɔ amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi ja, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, ni amɛkafite. Ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ hu yaa oya kwraa ejaakɛ obaanyɛ okpa aduawai lɛ beni odamɔ shi moŋ fe ni oookwɛ baai ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli.

english: I have a very small farm plot; how can I harvest more vegetables without buying extra land?
ga: Miyɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko kwraa. Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa aduawai babaoo ni miheee shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: You can maximize a small plot by growing climbing crops vertically on stakes, trellises, or ropes. Utilizing vertical space allows you to plant crops closer together on the ground without them overcrowding each other.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he bibioo ko aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni kwɔɔ ni oookwɛ shi yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ nɔ. Trellis, loo boxwood, ni akɛ he ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ tsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni okɛ tsei lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: What happens to my farm yield if I let my vine crops crawl messily all over the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji miha wain tsei lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ?

english: When vines crawl everywhere in an unorganized way, they take up too much land surface and choke out other plants. You end up wasting space that could have been used to plant extra crops, which reduces your total harvest and profit.
ga: Kɛ wain tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ Ebaahe he babaoo tsɔ ni ejie tsei krokomɛi. Obaafite he ko ni obaanyɛ okɛdu tsei krokomɛi. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi.

english: How does guiding my crops to grow upwards increase the money I make from my land?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni akudɔɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ aha shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Upward growth allows you to fit more plants onto the same piece of land while protecting the fruits from spoilage and soil diseases. More healthy, high-quality plants in a smaller space direct more crop sales straight into your pocket.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei babaoo yɛ he kome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ he ko bibioo lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahɔ̃ɔmɔ awo okotoku mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and vegetable leaves turn yellow and rot when they stay close to the wet dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Soil contains fungi and bacteria that thrive in moisture. When leaves sit directly on wet ground, these microbes easily transfer onto the plant, causing fungal spots, rot, and disease.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria ni shwereɔ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ tsɔɔ tsei amli oya. Enɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai baa.

english: How does training my crops to stand tall protect them from strong heat and humidity?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔsemɔ ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa he?

english: Lifting plants upward allows air to flow freely underneath and through the foliage. This breeze dries off wet leaves quickly after rain and cools the plant down during hot weather, preventing diseases from building up.
ga: Tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ oya yɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛtsɔɔ amɛmli. Kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai ni efɔ lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Tsĩ helai anaa koni amɛkafee

english: Why is it easier to weed and spray chemical treatments when crops grow straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa akɛ abaajie jwɛi ni ashwie nɔ kɛji tsei lɛ dara yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops grow vertically in orderly lines, the paths between rows stay clear. You can walk through easily to weed or apply treatments without stepping on vines or accidentally spraying leaves that are buried under a tangle.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ shi shiŋŋ yɛ linei ni yɔɔ fɛo mli lɛ Gbɛ ni yɔɔ linei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baakã he ahi shi faŋŋ. Obaanyɛ otsɔ jɛmɛ oya ni ojie jwɛi lɛ. Aloo okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ onaji akashɛ wein tsei anɔ yɛ oshara mli loo okɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akashwie nɔ.

english: Will my climbing bean plants produce more pods if I give them bamboo poles to climb?
ga: Ani mi-climbing bean tsei lɛ baawo pods babaoo kɛji miha amɛ ŋmei tso ni amɛkwɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, climbing beans naturally reach for height. Providing poles allows them to branch out freely in the air and blossom fully, producing far more healthy pods than if they were left tangled on the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akwɔɔ lɛ shɛɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tso ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ niji yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa hewalɛ fe ni ashiɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to clear and plough my land before planting crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsu he nii dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Ploughing loosens the soil, allowing crop roots to spread easily, breathe, and absorb water. It also buries weeds, making it easier for seeds to sprout and grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo, amɛmuɔ ni amɛmuɔ nu. Efuɔ jwɛi hu. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow bigger and produce more yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadara ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: What is the benefit of using a seed planting machine instead of planting by hand?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui adumɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni akɛ niji aduɔ lɛ he?

english: A planting machine drops seeds at the exact depth and distance automatically. This helps seeds sprout evenly across the field, avoids wasting seeds, and saves you a lot of manual labor.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ bɔ ni amɛmli kwɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni afiteɔ lɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitsumɔ babaoo baa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly whenever weeds take over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni jwɛi yeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, which makes your crops weak and slows down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: How does spraying chemical pesticides help keep my crops healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Spraying protects your crops by destroying harmful insects that eat leaves and stalks, and by stopping fungal diseases from spreading across your field.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yeɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ni oootsi naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen. Applying fertilizer or manure feeds the crop so it can turn green and continue growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. During dry spells, plants lose water through heat faster than their roots can take it up, causing them to wilt.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ dɔlɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars and insects attack my crops more when the plants are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛdarako lɛ?

english: Young plants have soft, tender leaves that are easy for insects to chew and digest. As crops mature, their leaves often become tougher and harder for pests to eat.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kooloi yeɔ amɛ oya ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ewaa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my crops from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show signs of maturity, such as leaves turning yellow, stalks drying out, or fruits changing color. Harvesting at the right time stops crops from rotting or being destroyed by field pests.
ga: Tso lɛ jieɔ dalɛ okadii kpo, tamɔ baai ni tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ agbi, loo aduawai lɛ su tsake. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haaa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akafite loo akafite amɛ.

english: How can using a tractor help me grow a bigger farm than using a cutlass and hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni edara fe tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: A tractor can clear, plough, and prepare large areas of land in a few hours, whereas doing it by hand takes weeks. This allows you to cultivate much more land with less physical strain.
ga: Trakta baanyɛ ajie, atsu nii ni asaa hei wuji yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni nitsumɔi ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ heɔ otsii babaoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo nɔ, ni ohaoɔ tsɔ.

english: How do I know if the oil palm nuts I collected are good enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mu tso dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ?

english: Not every palm nut will grow into a strong tree. Viable seeds feel heavy and solid, while bad ones may be dried out, insect-damaged, or rotting on the inside.
ga: Jeee ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei tso baada ni etsɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui gbohii baanyɛ agbi. Afiteɔ kooloi bibii. loo ni fiteɔ yɛ mli

english: Why do some of my seeds rot from the inside before I even plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ mli dani midu amɛ po lɛ?

english: Internal seed rot is usually caused by excessive moisture during storage or fungal infections entering small cracks. Sorting out these spoiled seeds early saves time and space.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli fitemɔ baa ji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni boteɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii amli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni efite nɛɛ ni ooohala mra lɛ Haa be kɛ he ko baa shi.

english: Is there a simple way to test if my seeds are rotten inside without cracking them open?
