ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ nɔ aka kɛji midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ mli ni amɛmli etseee?

english: You can place seeds in water; seeds that float are often hollow, damaged, or rotten inside, while solid, healthy seeds sink to the bottom and are good for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo nu mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji, amɛfite, loo amɛgboi yɛ mli. Beni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ni amɛhi kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why should I remove weak seedlings from my nursery instead of planting them all on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sorting out weak or unhealthy seedlings in the nursery ensures you only spend money, labor, and fertilizer on trees that will grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni oootsi kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ haa onáa nɔmimaa akɛ obaafite shika, nitsumɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ yɛ tsei ni baakwɛ̃ waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ ahe.

english: What causes palm seeds to spoil while waiting to sprout in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds spoil when kept in overly damp conditions without proper air flow, allowing mold and rot to destroy the seed nut before it can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Can I just pick any seeds from my harvest to plant a new crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahala dumɔwui kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli koni mikɛdu tsei heei?

english: Not all harvested seeds are suitable for replanting. Many may carry diseases or internal rot, so you must carefully inspect and select only the healthiest seeds.
ga: Jeee dumɔwui fɛɛ ni akpa lɛ ji nɔ ni sa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ. Ekolɛ kooloi srɔtoi babaoo yɛ mligbɛ hela loo ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ohala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on some of my young palm seedlings staying curled up instead of spreading out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Curled leaves in young seedlings often point to genetic weakness, pest attacks, or poor root development. These plants usually stay sickly and rarely yield well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔmɔ nii baanyɛ aha hela aba. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ loo amɛshishifãi lɛ eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ, hela mɔɔ tsei nɛɛ ni amɛwooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some seedlings stay small and weak like young children while others grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi daraaa ni amɛhe waaa tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi daraa lɛ

english: Seedlings remain stunted if they have internal seed defects, root damage, or poor nourishment. It is best not to transplant these weaklings to your main land.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi kɛji amɛyɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɔmɔi, shishifãi ni efite, loo niyenii ni esaaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsiŋ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛya oshikpɔŋkuku titri lɛ mli.

english: Will a seedling with twisted or deformed leaves recover if I plant it in good soil?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni baai ekpɔtɔ loo efite lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ?

english: Seedlings with early leaf deformities rarely recover. Even with good soil and fertilizer, they tend to remain low-yielding, so it is better to replace them with healthy ones.
ga: Dumɔwui ni baa lɛ efite mra lɛ efɔɔɔ hewalɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ moŋ Shi esumɔɔ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ato najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if a young seedling in my nursery is strong enough to take to the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A healthy seedling develops dark green, fully open leaves and a thick stem base. If the leaves remain tightly curled, pale, or stunted, the seedling should be rejected.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli diŋŋ, egbele kwraa, kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa. Kɛji baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akpoo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from direct sunlight when they are young. Without larger shade trees or plantains nearby, the hot sun burns their tender leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he hulutsoo be mli ni amɛji bibii. Kɛji tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ.

english: If plants grow on their own in the bush, why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops regularly?
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eda yɛ jwɛi lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight your crops need. Regular weeding ensures your plants get all the nourishment required to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Pruning removes excess branches that waste the plant's energy and block airflow. Cutting them allows sunlight to reach lower branches, improves air movement to prevent diseases, and directs energy into growing bigger pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa lɛ. Niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje pod ko ni da fe no

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and turn pale green?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why can't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other so I can get more food on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ? bɔni afee ni aná niyenii babaoo yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This results in thin, weak stalks and small corn cobs rather than a healthy harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ

english: When maize lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip. Yellowing leaves early in growth are a clear signal that the soil needs food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience high heat and lack water. Giving your plants enough water during dry spells keeps the flowers intact so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly wears out specific nutrients in the soil and allows pests to settle permanently. Rotating with beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he daa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot and turn black while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet conditions. Removing infected pods early and pruning trees to let light in stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni efɔ tsɔ. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ni ŋmɔ tsei lɛ koni la abote mli koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings fall over and rot at the stem right after coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ beni amɛje kpo etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This issue, called damping-off, is caused by soil fungi that thrive when nursery beds are overwatered or poorly drained. Using fresh soil and avoiding excess water protects fragile stems.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ nu wo ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei lɛ amli fe nine loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing strong stems and big cobs, they stretch upwards to reach sunlight, resulting in tall, weak plants with small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, du tso tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso nguanguahi. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the air moist around the young cocoa while it establishes roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli fũuɔ. Kakao tso lɛ ji gbekɛ beni efeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of young maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away, preventing the plant from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh animal manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Pepper leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by insects that stops healthy plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants attract so many insects as soon as they start bringing out flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ gbalaa kooloi babaoo kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft young pods that naturally attract sap-sucking bugs and caterpillars searching for easy food right as the plant transitions to fruiting.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu mli nu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo beni tso lɛ tsakeɔ kɛyaa yibiiwoo mli lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when the plant experiences extreme stress, which prevents the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a wo yiblii.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right when they look ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ mli gbalaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ eshɛ nikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split open when there is a sudden heavy rain or overwatering after a dry period. The inside of the head absorbs water rapidly and expands faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaabeji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo kɛji nu ho yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push the soil upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ daa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting underground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikɛ amɛ po shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water stays trapped in the soil without draining away properly, which suffocates the tuber roots and allows harmful soil fungus and tiny worms to attack.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni eha sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ atutua.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the tips downward in a V-shape, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛba shi yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the soil, and because the plant carries heavy bunches of fruit at the top, strong winds easily pull the roots out of the soft ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni akɛni tso lɛ yɛ yibii babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli oya. ja akɛ tsɔne ko ni akɛ tsei fee tsu nii

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses to the plant, or by extreme heat and lack of water causing the plant to curl its leaves to save moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛto nu he.

english: Why do small insects swarm my cowpea plants as soon as they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft petals that attract pests like thrips and pods borers, which feed on the flowers and prevent the beans from forming.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni ehaaa ŋmeii afee.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe; when water stays trapped around the roots for too long without draining, it suffocates them and causes fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu ejeee mli Enɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ agbo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young crops with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents the hot sun from drying out moisture, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekagbi ŋmɔtɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before small pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed, so the tree drops surplus flowers if it lacks water, nutrients, or proper shade to support all of them.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ ashwie shi kɛji amɛbɛ nu, niyenii, loo hulutsoo ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small green fruits right after they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ebɔi damɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruits when they experience stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients needed to hold the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛkpa aduawai lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds away from my young yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji kɛjɛ sweet potato tsei bibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from young yam vines, and they also trap excess moisture which encourages leaf diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ sweet potato wain tsei bibii amli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni woɔ tsei ahelai ahe hewalɛ lɛ hu.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of the specific food maize needs and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha abɛi lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long can I store harvested seed nuts before planting them in my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato dani madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Most tree nuts, like coconuts or oil palm seeds, stay good for planting for a few months if kept in a cool, shady place, but planting them fresh gives you the fastest and strongest growth.
ga: Nuts ni wa babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii loo oil palm ŋmeii Abaanyɛ akwɛ amɛ nyɔji fioo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Shi shweremɔ hee Ebaaha oda oya fe fɛɛ ni ohe wa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do many small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a few turn into pods because they need tiny midges (insects) to pollinate them, and dry conditions can cause unpollinated flowers to drop off naturally.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ejaakɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná kooloi bibii ni amɛwo amɛmli, ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: What causes mature shea nuts to fall from the tree before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni haa shea ŋmeii momoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ ajie amɛ?

english: Shea nuts drop naturally from the branches once they reach full maturity, but heavy rain and strong winds can also shake them off early.
ga: Shea ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akpokpo lɛ mra.

english: Can I save seeds from this year's maize harvest to plant next year to save money?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu afi ni baa lɛ koni mikɛ shika ato?

english: If you planted hybrid maize, saving those seeds will lead to a smaller yield next season because hybrid vigor only lasts for one generation; buying fresh certified seeds gives you a higher harvest.
ga: Kɛji odu hybrid corn Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni okɛto lɛ baaha yibiiwoo bibioo aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Yɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hybrid lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ebaahi shi yinɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha oná kpamɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants die after one season while my neighbor's cocoa tree keeps bearing fruit for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ be kome sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tso lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper is an annual crop designed by nature to grow, produce fruit, and die in one season, whereas cocoa is a perennial tree built with deep roots to live and bear fruit for decades if properly cared for.
ga: Peppers ji tsei ni yeɔ daa afi ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛwo yibii ni amɛgboi yɛ be kome mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ maa koni ehi shi ni ewo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves fold up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants close their leaves during the hottest hours of the afternoon to protect themselves from intense heat and stop water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ he, ni amɛtsi nu ni jɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water, and it will sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Ebaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when water sits on my field after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil gets flooded, crop roots cannot breathe or take up nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, which causes the leaves to turn yellow from lack of food.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I identify a good plantain sucker that will produce a heavy bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse plantain suckers kpakpai ni baaha ŋmeii ni tsii?

english: Choose sword suckers that have thin, narrow leaves and a large, heavy bulb at the bottom, as they have the strength to grow fast and bear large bunches.
ga: Halamɔ klante tsei ni baai lɛ mli tse ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb agbo ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛdaa oya ni efeɔ kui wuji.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting buds inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go to sleep after harvest, but after a few months, their natural internal clock wakes them up to start growing a new vine for the next season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yaa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akpa amɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ teɔ amɛ shi koni amɛje wain tsei heei adumɔ shishi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to build green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it yet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge stems and green leaves but end up with very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ tso agbo kɛ baai eŋɔli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the cassava plant gets confused and puts all its energy into growing big leaves up top instead of storing food in the tubers under the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ futuɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have special roots that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the ground, leaving natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do tiny cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before they ever grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani mitsei lɛ baatsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi dani amɛdara?

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree realizes it has more pods than it can feed and sheds the extra ones, though it can also be triggered by fungal diseases like black pod during wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Tso lɛ yɔse akɛ eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. ni ejie wala yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ hu baanyɛ aha ená he miishɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot afternoon temperatures or uneven watering, which causes the plant to protect itself by stopping fruit production until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ he. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛtsɔ aduawai ni ekpaa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and fruit only once in its lifetime; after the bunch matures, that stem naturally dies so it can pass its energy to the young sucker shoots growing at its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Beni ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the tuber under the ground, and climbing up tall stakes keeps the leaves exposed to the sun and off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Ni tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni akwɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ hulu lɛ nɔ, ni amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants roll up into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the tomato plant's defense mechanism against high heat; by curling its leaves, it reduces the amount of surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto its internal water.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ tomato tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ahi mli.

english: Why does my rice crop survive in standing water while my maize crop rots and dies in the same wet ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow spaces inside their stems that act like air tubes to carry oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots do not have these tubes and drown without air in wet soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsũi ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ ni amɛshwieɔ nu mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look droopy and wilted in the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, water evaporates from leaf surfaces faster than roots can draw fresh water from the soil, causing temporary wilting that usually corrects itself once the sun sets and temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ baa lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kukuoo ko mli ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and losing leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants dry out easily under intense sunlight because their root systems are still small. Providing shade crops like plantains or cassava around them protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching and helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo. Ha tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava abɔle ohe. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants show they are mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top, and the ground around the stem base starts to crack due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Cassava tso tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a shape like a V from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tips and moves down the central vein of lower maize leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant regain its dark green color and produce good ears.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛ nitrogen fee tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni amɛwo toi kpakpai.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally enriches the land with free nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize need to grow well.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ niyenii ni he ehiaaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray or insecticidal soap helps new leaves grow back healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do dark black patches appear on my cocoa pods when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rains and cool conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight reach the trunk and removing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ mli koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oya kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination. Mulching around the base of the plant to keep the soil cool and maintaining regular watering helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni akɛ nu awo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down so easily when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden props creates extra balance to prevent the tree from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛfi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akuu ko ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekakumɔ loo eshishifãi.

english: Why is it better for me to make soil ridges across a slope instead of up and down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafee ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Making ridges across a slope creates small barriers that trap rainwater and slow it down, preventing heavy storms from washing away your rich topsoil and fertilizer while allowing water to sink deep to the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa gbɛtsii nii bibioo ko baa. No mɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Enɛ ji koni ahum ni naa wa akafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu lɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why did the leaves of my crops dry up and look burnt after I applied granular fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛshã beni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji granular fertilizer ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer draws water away from plant roots if placed too close to the stem or applied on dry soil. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in moist soil, then lightly covered with dirt to avoid burning the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he tsɔ loo akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ fioo ashwie nɔ koni ekashã tso lɛ.

english: Why is it important to break up hard soil lumps before I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akumɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ mli dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Breaking up hard soil creates small air pockets in the ground. Crop roots need air just like humans do, so loose soil helps roots breathe easily and spread deep to absorb water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akuɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni adesai taoɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shɔŋŋ koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do we raise soil into mounds when planting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔji kɛ́ wɔmiidu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam mounds create a loose, airy layer of soil. This gives the yam tuber a soft environment to grow big without fighting hard dirt, while also letting excess rainwater drain away to stop root rot.
ga: Atomɔ ni abua naa lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli koni ekpa shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop beds if people walk over them and pack the dirt down tight?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔ saatso lɛ nɔ kɛji mɔ ko nyiɛ jɛmɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi?

english: Packing the soil down squashes out the air spaces inside it. Without air circulating around the roots, plants get choked, grow poorly, and struggle to take in plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooowo mli lɛ baajie kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, tso lɛ baatsi, ni edaŋ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ naagbai ni yɔɔ niyenii ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ yeli he

english: Why do I need to turn over the soil before the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Turning the soil mixes fresh air into the ground and opens up hard layers. This creates a comfortable habitat for helpful soil organisms that break down organic matter into food for your crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ futuɔ ni egbeleɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbálaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa onibii lɛ feɔ shihilɛhe ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I arrange dry leaves and green grass in layers when making compost manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi eŋɔli lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli kɛ́ mifee ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Layering different materials keeps the heap loose so air can flow through it. Good air circulation gives tiny beneficial organisms the environment they need to quickly turn plant waste into rich fertilizer.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋtayaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ naa shihilɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsake tsei amli jwɛi oya amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo.

english: How does putting dry grass on top of my crop bed help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool and moist while allowing air to pass through, creating a great living environment for crop roots to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Bɔɔ shihilɛhe kpakpa ni tso shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How does leaving old crop roots to rot in the soil help my new crops?
ga: Te tso shishifãi momo ni mishiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei heei lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: As old roots break down in layers, they leave behind tiny natural tunnels. These tunnels act like air pipes, allowing fresh air and rainwater to reach deep into the ground for your next crop.
ga: Beni shishifãi momo lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ fãi Amɛshi adebɔɔ mli gbɛ bibioo ko. behind Nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔ nu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaving space allows air to move freely around each plant. Proper airflow prevents trapped moisture on leaves, which protects your crops from catching fungal diseases.
ga: He ko ni ashiɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔleɔ he fɛɛ he. each factory independently Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akamɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How soft and loose should the soil be when I set up a nursery bed for my pepper seeds?
ga: Te esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ mi-pepper dumɔwui saatso lɛ toɔ lɛ?

english: Nursery soil should be very fine and light with plenty of tiny air gaps. Young pepper sprouts have delicate roots that need gentle, well-aerated soil so they can spread without struggle.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Pepper bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa ni naagba ko bɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I tightly pack my harvested crop into bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ woɔ kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ beni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops need air circulating around them to stay cool. If packed tightly without airflow, heat and moisture get trapped inside, causing your crop to rot and spoil quickly.
ga: Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni fɛ̃i ahi mli Kɛji akɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsiɔ emli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their tender leaves from sunburn and to keep moisture in the soil. Plantain plants or shade trees are usually grown alongside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yɛ amɛhe koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa ni enáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants turning yellow starting from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on corn usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant food in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls whatever nutrients it has left out of its bottom leaves to feed the upper growing leaves, causing the lower ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to be dug up without pulling up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ni ajieee shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava lets you know it is getting ready when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push outward underground.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ eesaa ehe beni eshishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When a plant gets too thirsty or hot, it sacrifices its flowers to save energy and protect its own survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ kumai ye tso lɛ loo edɔ tsɔ Ekɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ebu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: If I plant beans together in the same field with my maize, will the beans steal food from the corn?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani ŋmeii lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: No, planting beans with maize actually helps the corn. Beans extract nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, which helps fertilize the corn while spreading leaves that shade out weeds.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Beans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ awo ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni egbɛɔ baai ni haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden poles to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni enyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for building large tubers. Climbing high up on stakes exposes all their leaves to maximum light, keeps the foliage safe from soil-borne diseases, and prevents leaves from rotting on wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná la babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the top leaves on my pepper plants crinkling up and rolling inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices. This damage makes the leaves grow twisted and stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛnuɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my plantain stool produce smaller and smaller bunches of fruit over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: When a main plantain stem grows too many shoots or 'suckers' around its base, they all compete for the same food, light, and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, allowing the plant to concentrate its energy on producing big bunches.
ga: Beni plantain tso titri lɛ yɛ ŋmeii loo ‘ŋmeii’ babaoo tsɔ ni ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, la, kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water vapor into the air much faster than their roots can suck up from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to close their pores and preserve water, usually standing back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ nu mli lasu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛŋa ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛha nu ahi mli. Bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ enyɔ shi.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the hidden middle funnel of my young maize plants instead of eating the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: The central funnel or 'whorl' of a maize plant is where the newest, softest leaves are forming. Pests like the armyworm hide deep inside this funnel because it offers tender, nutrient-rich leaf tissue while protecting them from rain, direct sun, and predators.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel loo ‘ring’ lɛ ji he ni baai bibii fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ yɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛjegbɛi nɛɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their delicate leaves burn and dry out quickly. They need shade crops, like plantains, planted nearby to act as umbrellas and keep the soil cool while the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential plant food. Adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer brings nitrogen back to the soil so the plants can green up and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow big leaves on top but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yɔɔ baai wuji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of underground roots. Loosening the soil and balancing soil nutrients helps the plant send food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ mlɛo tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars are attacking my maize before I actually see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmei lɛ dani mana amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Look closely at the young leaves right in the center top of the maize stalk. If you see small ragged holes or white, sawdust-like droppings inside the leaf whorl, caterpillars are inside feeding on the plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ona buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miiye tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do plantain trees easily fall over during heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, weak roots that stay near the surface of the soil. When heavy rain softens the ground and heavy fruits grow on top, strong winds easily pull the roots out of the mud, causing the plant to tip over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni aduawai ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli oya. gbee tsei ashwie shi

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Spacing them out gives each stalk enough room to get what it needs to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do leaves drop off my crop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick crops use to save water during dry weather. Leaves lose moisture into the air, so dropping some leaves helps the plant keep water inside its main stem and roots until rain returns.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi baai komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu ato etsitsi kɛ eshishifãi titrii lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden changes in water. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps keep the root temperature steady so flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu tsakemɔi trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the wet ground where they can get maximum sun and avoid rotting from wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Staking haa tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛ hei ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe fe fɛɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ he.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops slow down my harvest?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your main crops like a thief. When weeds take those nutrients first, your crops grow slower and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Taakɛ julɔi ji lɛ, jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ jwɛi kɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ tsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture to help young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow better when I plant cassava on a different part of the field instead of mixing them tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko mli moŋ fe ni mikɛbaafutu mli lɛ?

english: Maize and cassava both feed heavily from the soil. When planted too close together, their roots fight over the same nutrients and water, causing both crops to produce smaller yields.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ shikpɔŋ waa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kome lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow and staying short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and stunted growth usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them grow tall and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing lots of thick leaves but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai ni mli tse waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, the sweet potato plant puts all its energy into growing leaves on top instead of sending food down to swell the tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛba shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ŋmeii tsei lɛ kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally when water is scarce to conserve moisture and protect its roots underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Yucca baajɛ ebaai lɛ ashwie shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism against hot weather. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, stopping water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves. Sprinkling the plants with neem leaf extract or organic pesticide can help clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do tiny holes appear all over my cabbage leaves within just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ebaaje kpo yɛ kaabii lɛ ahe fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli?

english: Small moths lay eggs under the cabbage leaves that hatch into hungry caterpillars. These caterpillars eat the leaves quickly, so checking under the leaves early helps catch them before they do major damage.
ga: Kplukai bibii fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabeji baai ashishi ni amɛfɔɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ baai oya. No hewɔ lɛ kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ amɛ dani amɛfite nii wuji.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing bent and small instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to push downward as they grow. If the soil mound is hard, rocky, or compacted, the tuber cannot expand easily and becomes twisted or stunted.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, bulb lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã oya ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop their flowers before producing any seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ená dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Cowpeas drop flowers when they get too hot without enough water, or when tiny insects attack the flower buds. Keeping the soil moist and protecting buds from pests ensures pods develop properly.
ga: Cowpeas baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji edɔ tsɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua ŋmeii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves during hot hours to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve moisture and prevent water loss through evaporation during extreme heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaaa nu lɛ afite kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crop field early in the morning or in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashwie ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Early morning watering is best because it gives the crops moisture to survive the afternoon heat, and excess water on leaves dries quickly. Evening watering leaves foliage wet overnight, which can cause fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli. Ni nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbi oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ kome, ni baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall with deep green leaves but failing to yield good tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi ebɛ bulbs kpakpai lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Nitrogen encourages fast leaf and stem growth, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to grow thick, healthy roots and tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛ bulb lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my cowpea crops make the soil better for the maize I plant after them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family. Their roots partner with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ ŋmãa weku lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or viruses transmitted by them. These insects damage the young leaves as they feed, causing abnormal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fiteɔ baai bibii beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. ni kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning dark black and drying up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, overly shaded environments. Proper pruning to let in sunlight and good field drainage help prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu kpakpa atsɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves during drought to conserve water and survive long dry periods. However, if leaf drop is severe early in the season, it could indicate soil nutrient poverty or pest damage.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gbee shi waa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite.

english: Blossom drop in tomatoes happens when temperatures are too high, water supply is irregular, or there is poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and allowing good airflow helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. aloo pollination ni ehiii bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible for food production. Lifting the foliage off the wet ground also protects the leaves from rotting and airborne soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli helai ni fiteɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli helai ahe.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds in a circle around the base of my young plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi plantain bibioo lɛ shishitoo

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing a ring around the trunk gives the plant root space to grow without being starved by faster-growing weeds.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ adaa ni jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ yeee lɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do people say my harvested maize can make my family sick even if it looks normal on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ baanyɛ aha miweku lɛ aná hela lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ

english: Certain crop fungi produce invisible poisons called aflatoxins in grains like maize and groundnuts. Even when crops look clean on the surface, these hidden toxins can stay inside and cause severe long-term health problems like liver disease.
ga: Fungi komɛi feɔ tsofai fɔji ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins yɛ ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse yɛ hiɛ po lɛ, Shi nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ hu baanyɛ ahi mli ni ekɛ helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni mli wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, tamɔ mlɛbo hela aba.

english: Why can eating infected crops cause sickness years later even if I feel completely fine today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ aná hela yɛ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihe miijɔ mi ŋmɛnɛ moŋ.

english: Toxins produced by crop molds do not always cause immediate stomach ache. Instead, small amounts build up silently in the human body over many years until they cause serious organ failure or liver cancer later in life.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be tsofai fɔji ni tsei amli ŋmeii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ kɛ musu mli piŋmɔ baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi fioo komɛi buaa amɛhe naa dioo yɛ adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli afii babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛkɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni fiteɔ waa loo mlɛbo mli kansa baa sɛɛ mli yɛ shihilɛ mli.

english: Can I destroy the poison in damaged grains by cooking or boiling them for a long time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpata poison ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni efite lɛ amli lɛ hiɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhoomɔ loo shãmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nɔ?

english: High cooking temperatures cannot destroy fungal toxins once they are produced in your crop. Boiling or roasting moldy grain will not make it safe to eat.
ga: Nihoomɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nyɛŋ akpata mycotoxins lɛ ahiɛ kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kpo yɛ onibii amli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji ni ashãa loo ashãa lɛ haŋ amɛfee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to dry my harvested maize directly on the bare dirt ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Soil naturally carries microscopic fungal spores and moisture. Placing harvested crops directly on bare dirt allows these invisible fungi to crawl into the grain and produce silent poisons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa nɛɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ tsofai fɔji ni bɛ dioo.

english: What happens to my harvested crops if I pick them during the rainy season and cannot dry them quickly?
ga: Mɛni baaba minikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni minyɛɛɛ maha egbi oya?

english: Trapped moisture allows mold fungi to grow rapidly inside the crop. This produces invisible toxins inside the grain long before you notice any visible spoilage or bad smell.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii daa oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsofai fɔji ni anaaa lɛ baa dumɔwui lɛ amli dani oyɔseɔ nɔ ko ni efite loo ŋmɔlɔ ko ni anaa.

english: How can I tell if my stored groundnuts have hidden fungus if I cannot see mold on the outside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ? Kɛji onyɛɛɛ ona ŋmei lɛ yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ

english: Fungal poisons can exist inside groundnuts without showing obvious white fluff. Shelling a few sample nuts to check for dark inner rot and ensuring thorough drying right after harvest is the best way to prevent hidden contamination.
ga: Mycotoxins baanyɛ ahi ŋmeii amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ko ni anaaa bɛ mli. Nuts nɔkwɛmɔnii komɛi ni ajieɔ koni ana kɛji mligbɛ egbo. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ mujiwoo ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I remove broken or insect-bitten seeds before putting my harvest into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni ekumɔ loo ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ dani mikɛ minibii lɛ awo nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects and physical cracks break the seed's protective outer skin, creating an open entrance for air and mold fungi to invade and poison the rest of your stored harvest.
ga: Kplukai kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ ŋmeii fiteɔ dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Enɛ haa gbɛ ni agbeleɔ naa kɛhaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ababote onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli ni amɛwo amɛ tsofa.

english: Is it safe for me to feed spoiled or moldy groundnuts to my goats and chickens?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha mitooi kɛ mikooloi lɛ ŋmei ni efite loo ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Fungal toxins in spoiled crops harm livestock organs and can pass directly into the animal's meat, milk, and eggs, which will still pose a health risk to your family.
ga: Mycotoxins ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite mli lɛ yeɔ kooloi ahe nibii awui ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ kooloi loo, mliki kɛ amɛwui amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ oweku lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ awui lolo.

english: Why does eating grain with hidden crop mold cause serious organ problems instead of just a simple stomach ache?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ahe naagbai ni mli wa baa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona musu mli hela ni yaa nɔ daa kɛkɛ

english: Fungal toxins are powerful chemical poisons rather than simple germs. They target internal organs like the liver silently over time, damaging tissue without triggering immediate symptoms like vomiting.
ga: Mycotoxins ji tsofai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Amɛtutuaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii, tamɔ mlɛbo lɛ, dioo yɛ be ni sa mli. Efiteɔ fãji ni ekɛ trukaa okadii tamɔ shwiemɔ baaa.

english: What is the proper way to store my dried grains to keep invisible mold from growing on them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ midumɔwui ni egbi lɛ toɔ koni ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ?

english: Store thoroughly dried grains off the floor using wooden pallets, inside clean, sealed, airtight bags in a cool, well-ventilated room to stop moisture and fungal spores from multiplying.
ga: Okɛ ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ ato shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ vacuum kotoku ko ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee babaoo.

english: How many 50kg bags of maize can I expect to harvest from one acre of land?
ga: Abele kotokui enyiɛ ni tsiimɔ ji 50 kg manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ acre kome nɔ?

english: On average in Ghana, with good rainfall and basic management, one acre of land yields between 8 to 15 standard 50kg bags of dry maize grain. Using improved seeds and proper fertilizer can help you reach the higher end of that range.
ga: Average yɛ Ghana He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shishijee nɔkwɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ acre 1 woɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni tsiimɔ ji 50kg ni ji ŋmãa ni egbi ni ji kotokui 8 kɛyashi 15. Dumɔwui ni asaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oshɛ nakai ŋshɔ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ.

english: If I want to produce over one thousand bags of maize a year, how big does my farm need to be?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee ŋmãa ni fa fe kotokui akpe kome daa afi. Te esa akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ adara aha tɛŋŋ?

english: To produce 1,000 bags of 50kg maize in a year, you would need around 70 to 100 acres of land if you harvest once a year, or about 40 to 50 acres if you manage to plant and harvest twice during the major and minor rainy seasons.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná ŋmãa kotokui 1,000 ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 50 yɛ afi mli lɛ, ehe baahia ni oná shikpɔŋ aaafee acre 70 kɛyashi 100 kɛji okpa shikome yɛ afi mli, loo aaafee acre 40 kɛyashi 50 kɛji obaanyɛ odu ni okpa shii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri kɛ nɔ ni baa shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do buyers and officers measure our maize harvest in 50-kilogram bags instead of counting cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ onukpai lɛ susuɔ wɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ he yɛ 50kg kotokui amli moŋ fe ni amɛaakane ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize cobs come in different sizes and contain different amounts of grain. Weighing shelled maize into standard 50kg bags provides an accurate measurement of actual food produced, making pricing fair and transport calculations easy.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ dalɛi srɔtoi yɛ mli, ni ŋmeii srɔtoi yɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmãa ni ajie lɛ awo kotokui ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 50 mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ asusuɔ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ ni afee lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehaa jara ni ja kɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ he akɔntaabuu feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why can't I harvest fresh maize every single month from the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makpa ŋmãa hee daa nyɔŋ nɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes about three to four months to complete its growth cycle from planting to dry harvest. Once a maize plant produces cobs, it finishes its lifecycle and dies, so a single field can only produce a harvest once per growing season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ edalɛ mli kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa nii ni egbi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fee ŋmeii Egbeɔ ewala be lɛ naa ni egboɔ, no hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔ kome baanyɛ awo ŋmãa kome pɛ yɛ ŋmãa be fɛɛ mli.

english: Is it possible for me to grow and harvest maize during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa ni makpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, it is possible, but only if you have an artificial irrigation system like pumps or sprinklers. Maize needs steady moisture to form grains, so relying only on nature during the dry season will cause the plants to dry up without producing cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ebaanyɛ eba mli, shi kɛji oyɛ nu ni akɛfee tamɔ pɔmp loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ pɛ. Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni enyɛ efee dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ he fɔ adebɔɔ nɔ pɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: If you plant seeds too close, the maize plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no grains at all.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of maize when I plant on the same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize takes up a lot of nutrients from the soil to grow grains. Planting it continuously on the same plot without resting the land, rotating with crops like beans, or adding fertilizer empties the soil of food, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha edumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ efɔɔɔ shi. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he, ni no haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: How do I know the exact time my maize is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ ni esa akɛ akpa?
