english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the entire plant turns yellow-brown, the outer husks dry out, the silks on the cob turn dark brown, and the kernels are hard enough that you cannot dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli egbi. Siliki tsɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ otsitsii lɛ eko eko eko eko.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil and get full of insects when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ kɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize holds trapped water. If you put grain into bags before drying it thoroughly in the sun, that moisture creates mold and attracts insect pests like weevils, which rapidly destroy the bagged harvest.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ toɔ nu. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku lɛ mli dani ogbi amɛ yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni fiteɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ oya.

english: Why do extension officers recommend hybrid maize seeds over seeds I save from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ wo ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ he ŋaa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to produce larger cobs, resist local pests, and give a higher number of 50kg bags per acre. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose these strong traits and yield much less grain.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa kotokui ni fa fe 50 kg yɛ acre kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite nɛkɛ sui ni wa nɛɛ ni amɛbaawo dumɔwui fioo kwraa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea when planting helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops in straight lines or just scatter the seeds across my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ loo magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes it easier to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest. It also prevents plants from crowding each other out, ensuring every crop gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa. Ehaa tsei hu shwieɔ amɛhe shi. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves but only producing small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava puts its energy into leaf growth instead of big tubers when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are too shaded. Planting cassava in full sunlight and avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers encourages the plant to build thick roots.
ga: Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ mli ewo hulutsoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ajie nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, heavy drought, or a lack of moisture in the soil during flowering. Mulching around the plants and keeping the soil damp helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap under the leaves, or a virus they spread. Spraying the leaves with a mixture of natural neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap gets rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do my bean seedlings start wilting and dying right after they sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This happens when soil fungi attack young stems in overly wet ground, a condition called damping-off. Planting seeds in well-drained soil and avoiding overwatering protects fragile young seedlings.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tutua tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe.

english: How often do I need to water my vegetable garden during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Vegetables should be watered deep near their roots early in the morning or late in the evening every 1 to 2 days. Mulching with dried grass around the base of plants keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe leebi loo gbɛkɛ daa gbi 1 kɛyashi 2, ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he. Tsei ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown early before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry prematurely due to fungal leaf spot disease or a lack of moisture in the root zone late in the growing season. Staking the vines off the ground helps keep leaves dry and reduces fungal attacks.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fungal leaf spot hela loo nu ni bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ wein tsei lɛ je shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same field without harming the maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miyeŋ ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very good because cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which helps feed the maize plant while giving you a second crop from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Ejaakɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ebaaha ŋmãa ni ji enyɔ hu aba kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why should I clear away extra small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi plantain tsei titrii lɛ etee.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main mother plant for food and water, leading to small bunches. Keeping only 2 or 3 healthy suckers at different ages ensures the mother plant yields big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. ni kɛ kuu bibioo ko baa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohiɛ ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ afii fɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and dry during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade trees like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that protect the cocoa leaves from getting scorched.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni baabu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the rains become heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much rain and dense foliage trap moisture on the pods, creating the perfect conditions for a fungal disease called Black Pod to grow and spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ aya hiɛ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Is it better to water my crops in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the roots to absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot, whereas afternoon water evaporates quickly in the heat before the soil can soak it up.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant shrinks its leaf surface area to prevent water from evaporating too quickly in extreme heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant automatically shifts its limited nitrogen up to the younger top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛyaa ŋwɛi, baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why is my cassava growing lots of tall stems and leaves, but the tubers in the ground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa?

english: When there is too much nitrogen or excess moisture in the soil, cassava puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Beni nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo baai eŋɔli ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale even when weeds are growing green around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal fertilizers and water from the soil before your main crops can reach them, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants drop their flowers before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor pollination by insects.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ehiii

english: Why do crops grow much slower when planted directly under dense forest canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa blɛoo kwraa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight as energy to manufacture their own food. Dense shade starves the plant of the light needed for fast, healthy growth.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Shade ni mli ewo wu lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ana la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya, ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunches start getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and weak stems. When heavy fruit bunches form, the top weight easily pulls the shallow root system out of wet soil during strong winds.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akui babaoo fee lɛ, Muji ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli oya.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth, or the roots are sitting in too much water. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Controlling these pests early stops the curling and keeps the plant growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ anɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up in high heat to protect themselves from losing too much water to the sun. It is a natural way for the plant to save moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite hulu lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct harsh sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a cool shelter until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli gĩɔ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui ebɔle he. Ebaaha he ko ni mli ejɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out small and thin when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, their underground roots compete with each other for space, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant enough distance allows the roots to expand into large, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend when the soil is hard, compact, or rocky, forcing the root to fight its way down. Planting yams in tall, soft soil mounds makes it easy for the tubers to grow downward smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi, ni no baaha shishifãi lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛya shi. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if insects attack the blooms. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot spells helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow many thick leaves but produces very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baai ni mli tse waa shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves instead of pods when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much water. Cowpeas flower better when the soil is not overly rich in nitrogen.
ga: Cowpea woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ babaoo loo nu babaoo. Cowpeas fɔɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen tsɔ.

english: Why does my oil palm seedling stop growing for weeks after I move it to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ otsii komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This pause is called transplant shock, which happens when the plant's roots are disturbed or damaged during moving. Keeping a lump of original soil around the roots and watering well helps it recover faster.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ hejɔɔmɔ nɛɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbala loo amɛfite yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shishijee muji lɛ to Roots lɛ he kɛ nu kpakpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop shoots after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are very tough and can rest in the soil for a long time waiting for water. Because wild weeds are adapted to local soil conditions, they jump into action faster than planted crops after rains begin.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛmɛ nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi tsuɔ nii oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: What is the best month for me to start maintaining my cocoa farm, and why?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔ mlikwɛmɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ?

english: February is the ideal month to start cocoa maintenance in Ghana because it falls right before the main rainy season. Pruning, clearing, and weeding in February prepares the cocoa trees to absorb nutrients and catch the early rains for a better harvest.
ga: February ji nyɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ aje kookoo nɔkwɛmɔ shishi yɛ Ghana. Ejaakɛ eji dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli, ajie amɛ, ni ajie amɛ yɛ February mli lɛ, ehaa cacao tsei lɛ saa amɛhe koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the right time of the year for me to plant rice on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: March is generally the best time to plant rice in Ghana as the major rainy season begins. Planting in March ensures the seeds get the soil moisture they need to germinate and grow quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, March ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ Ghana ejaakɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ March mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛdara.

english: Why does rice need to be planted in March instead of during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ March mli moŋ fe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rice requires a constant supply of water to sprout and establish strong roots. Planting in March coincides with the start of the rainfall, giving the crops natural water so they do not dry up.
ga: Nu he miihia omɔ daa bɔni afee ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔ yɛ March mli ji be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Ha tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli nu koni amɛkagbi.

english: How do the seasons in Ghana dictate when I should work on different crops?
ga: Te be ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ tsɔɔ be ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi atsu nii ahaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Ghana's seasonal weather guides farm labor: dry-weather tasks like cleaning and maintaining tree crops happen around February, while water-dependent crops like rice are planted when the rain starts in March.
ga: Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ shihilɛ saa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi nitsumɔ, tamɔ tsei ahe saamɔ kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ yaa nɔ yɛ February aaafee. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi yɛ March mli.

english: Can I manage both a cocoa farm and a rice field in the same season without running out of time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli ni be sɛɛ efooo?

english: Yes, you can manage both by spacing out your heavy labor. By finishing your cocoa maintenance in February, your hands are free to focus entirely on planting rice when March arrives.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ gbɛ ko ni oooha ohe yɛ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ teŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni agbeɔ Cocoa he saamɔ naa yɛ February mli lɛ. Oniji baafee heyeli ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ ama ŋmãa dumɔ nɔ kɛ́ March bashɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if I delay their maintenance until after I plant my rice?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛkwɛmɔ lɛ to sɛɛ kɛyashi be mli ni midu ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If you put off cocoa maintenance, overgrown weeds and dead branches will choke the cocoa trees, causing them to miss out on the early rains and reducing your overall pod yield.
ga: Kɛji okɛ kookoo nɔkwɛmɔ shwie sɛɛ Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ baaha kookoo tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, cacao tsei lɛ naaa nugbɔshiimɔ bei ni ehaa pod yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why is it helpful to finish cocoa maintenance before starting food crop work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaagbe kookoo he saamɔ naa dani aje niyenii he nitsumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that requires heavy clearing before its growth cycle begins. Finishing it early prevents labor overload when the busy planting window for food crops like rice opens.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni biɔ ni ajie lɛ babaoo dani edalɛ be lɛ aje shishi. Ni agbeɔ naa mra Ebaaye ebua ni nitsulɔi akatsu nii fe nine beni samflɛ ni akɛduɔ niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbeleɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I weed and prune my cocoa trees right before the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe jwɛi ni mafolɔ amɛhe dani nugbɔ ni naa wa anɛ?

english: Weeding and pruning before the rains ensures that weeds do not steal water and soil nutrients from your cocoa trees once the wet season starts.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi ni okɛkpa jwɛi lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ akaju nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: When should I clear my land if I want to plant rice in March?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni madu ŋmãa yɛ March mli?

english: Land for rice should be cleared in February. Clearing ahead of time gives you space to prepare the soil beds so they are ready to receive rice seeds as soon as the March rains begin.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmãa yɛ February mli. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná hegbɛ ni okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ bɔni afee ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi yɛ March mli pɛ.

english: Does working on cocoa maintenance affect how nearby food crops grow?
ga: Ani kookoo nɔkwɛmɔ saa niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Proper maintenance opens up the farm canopy and clears heavy brush, which improves sunlight and airflow across your land, benefiting surrounding food crops like rice.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbeleɔ ŋmɔ mli tsũi lɛ amli ni ejieɔ brɔshi ni mli tse. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh sunlight and dry winds because their roots are small and their leaves are tender. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields the cocoa from scorching sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi bibii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight to make food. Lifting the leaves off the hot ground prevents disease and directs more energy downwards into making bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛfee amɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa hewalɛ ni haa bulb lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and build leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer at the right stage restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: What is eating small holes in my young corn leaves and leaving dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the funnel of the maize plant during the hot part of the day while chewing on tender inner leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli, be mli ni amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or spreading a plant virus that distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the soil when heavy rains last for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves water standing in the soil for too long, air is blocked, causing the underground roots to drown and decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Abaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular, which prevents the pollen inside the flower from fertilizing and turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ afee fɔfɔi ni etsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small yields even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the added fertilizer, water, and sunlight from the soil before your main crop gets a chance to drink it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la krokomɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ nu.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my plantains before they spoil on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains dani amɛgboi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Plantains are ripe for harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp, flat edges and become full and round, even while the skin is still dark green.
ga: Plantains lɛ eshɛ shi kɛha nikpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ efo ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo moŋ.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛwooo ŋmeii kwraa.

english: When is the best time for me to plant rain-fed maize during the major season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: The best time to plant is immediately after the first continuous rains begin, usually around March or April depending on your region, so the seeds get enough soil moisture to germinate and grow strong.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee March loo April. Edamɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and damage the plant. It is best to place fertilizer in a small ring or side pocket a few inches away from the stem where the roots can safely reach it.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tso lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo sɛɛ kotoku Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tsɔne lɛ mli. ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Cassava root rot is often caused by water standing around the roots in poorly drained soil during heavy rains, which allows fungal diseases to attack. Planting on raised ridges or mounds helps water drain away safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni damɔ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal lɛ tutuaa mɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni eegbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus they transmit. Spraying with neem leaf extract or an approved insecticide can help protect the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering and light shade can reduce flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds early while my crop plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal soil food, water, and light from young crops. Clearing them early gives your crops a strong start before the weeds can choke them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ anyɛ agbe amɛ.

english: How do I stop insects from destroying my stored dry maize after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni ato yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ naa?

english: Insects thrive on moisture and exposed grain. Dry your maize completely under the sun, clean your storage room, and store the grain in airtight bags (like PICS bags) or treat it with recommended grain storage powder.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo fɛ̃i kɛ hulu la mli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Tsumɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ahe Ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo okɛ dumɔwui atomɔ powda ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure will help the plant regain its dark green color and continue growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ni tsei ahe baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo kooloi aŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains start again, the plant will quickly grow new green leaves and continue feeding the roots underneath.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei eŋɔli oya ni ebaaya nɔ eye shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when afternoon heat gets too extreme or when the soil gets too dry. Watering your crops regularly and providing light shade during very hot afternoons will help the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei lɛ anɔ daa ni oha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔmɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings stop growing for two weeks after I move them to the farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ otsii enyɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seedlings go through transplant shock when moved to the field because their tiny roots get disturbed. They pause top leaf growth for a week or two while they focus on building strong roots in the new soil.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ naa shoofeemɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ mli yɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Amɛnibii lɛ egba amɛnaa. Amɛkpaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛaama yɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much rich manure or if cassava is planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy making tall branches and big leaves instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo loo adu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei niji kakadaji kɛ baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn dark brown and shrivel up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning extra branches on your cocoa trees to let in sunlight and airflow helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kookoo tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl inward during hot sunny afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which keeps water from escaping through the leaves.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haaa nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out in the air and catch maximum sunlight. When leaves get full sunlight, the plant creates more energy to grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ tso lɛ baafee hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea crops flower very early when planted in poor, dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni egbi ni ohiafoi yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas quickly produce flowers when stressed by heat or bad soil as a survival natural behavior, trying to create seeds quickly before the plant dries up completely.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ fɔfɔi oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ kɛha wala yiwalaheremɔ. Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee dumɔwui oya dani tsei lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits develop soft dark spots and fall off when rain falls heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes wet soil carrying fungal spores onto low-hanging garden eggs, causing the fruit to rot quickly and fall off before it fully ripens.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ eshwieɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛbaa kwraa.

english: When I am planting cassava stem cuttings, should I stick them upright into the soil or bury them flat?
ga: Be ni akɛduɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ Ani esa akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ loo afu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Sticking cassava cuttings upright or at a slant into the soil helps them produce deep roots and compact tuber bundles, whereas burying them flat works best in very dry soils to protect the stems from drying out.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ loo ekɛ ehe shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ be mli ni amɛfumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do some crops grow straight upright while others spread low across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops have natural growth behaviors; upright plants focus energy on reaching sunlight quickly, while spreading plants cover the ground to shade out weeds and keep the soil moist.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ su. Tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa hulu la ni amɛaana oya lɛ nɔ. Beni tso lɛ gbɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I raise my seeds in a seedling bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ dumɔwui atsu lɛ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery bed allows you to protect tender young plants from harsh weather, heavy rain, and pests while giving them special care so that only the healthiest seedlings get moved to your main field.
ga: Nursery beds yeɔ ebua bo ni obuɔ odumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko bɔni afee ni adu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ awo oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die right after I transplant them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock when delicate roots are damaged or exposed to heat. Transplanting in the cool late afternoon and watering the soil immediately helps seedlings survive the move.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli shoofeemɔ beni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fite loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli Hei ni mli ejɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Is it helpful to assign someone on my farm to focus only on seedling care instead of general farm work?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba he akɛ mawo mɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nitsumɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama dumɔwui akwɛmɔ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, young seedlings are very delicate and require constant, precise care like gentle watering and shading that can easily be neglected if labor is split across heavy field work.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni ebiɔ kwɛmɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ daa, tamɔ nu kɛ shade blɛoo. Abaanyɛ aku hiɛ ashwie enɛ nɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ aja nitsumɔ ni wa lɛ mli awo shikpɔŋkuku mli nitsumɔ mli.

english: How can I expand my farm size without losing the quality of my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akafite?

english: Expanding gradually section by section allows you to scale up production while keeping control over labor, water, and soil fertility so your crop yields remain high.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ nitsumɔ, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi babaoo.

english: What basic steps do I need to take if I want my farm to supply major markets in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee kɛji miisumɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ aha jarayelihe titri ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nibii?

english: To supply bigger markets, you must use high-quality planting materials, stick to structured planting schedules, and expand your field size steadily so you can harvest crops consistently.
ga: Bɔni afee ni okɛ jarayeli ni da aba lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ dumɔ nii ni hi jogbaŋŋ atsu nii. Nyiɛmɔ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni oya nɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli alɛɛ bɔni afee ni onyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii daa.

english: Why are my crop plants stretching tall with thin stems instead of growing thick and sturdy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Plants stretch and become thin when they are planted too close together and forced to fight for sunlight. Giving them proper spacing ensures they get enough light to build strong stems.
ga: Tsei lɛ baagbala ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni anyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. He ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baaha amɛná la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná tsei ni wa.

english: Why do the top leaves of my crops turn pale yellow while the bottom leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing top leaves often mean the plant is short on immobile nutrients like iron or sulfur, or that the upper part of the plant is stressed by intense heat and sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni tsiimɔ, tamɔ dade loo sulfur. aloo dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ haoɔ.

english: What happens to the crop's behavior if I trim off the top growing point?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ subaŋ nɔ kɛji mijie he ni ŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting off the top tip stops the plant from growing taller and forces it to send out side branches, which can create a bushier plant with more locations for flowers and fruits to form.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ yitsei lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwereɔ ni enyɛɔ niji anɔ kɛyaa esɛɛgbɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha jwɛi ko ni hei babaoo yɔɔ kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their foliage scorches easily. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields the young trees from heat and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to wooden stakes stuck in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ni akɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight to make food. When vines lie on the wet soil, they get diseases easily and produce smaller tubers.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha baai lɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛhoo nii. Kɛ akɛ wain tso lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, helai baa amɛnɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves and stalks of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on maize foliage. Applying proper pest control into the central funnel of the maize plant early in its growth stops them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai. Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn soft and black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, which usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates wildly or calcium in the soil is low. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying proper manure prevents the fruit bottoms from spoiling.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ calcium lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize in the exact same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within 3 to 4 months, leaving room for the slower-growing cassava to expand and produce tubers over the remaining months.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa gbɛ haa ŋmãa ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ŋmãa aba yɛ nyɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I remove the extra young shoots sprouting around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and soil nutrients from the parent plantain tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong suckers helps the main tree produce larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Tsobii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ niji ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my maize field if the soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmãa momo?

english: Even rich soil gets emptied of key nutrients like nitrogen after continuous planting. Crops like maize need high amounts of fast-acting nutrients at key growing stages to build full, heavy cobs.
ga: Shikpɔji ni baa nii lɛ po naa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii daa lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa biɔ niyenii babaoo ni tsuɔ nii oya yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting lets young crop roots grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, noticeable when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop. Harvesting one plant as a trial confirms if the tubers are full and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Anaa enɛ kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso kome ni akpaa akɛ kaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amaa nɔ mi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain in the season is often followed by weeks of scorching dry heat before the real rainy season starts. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up without regular moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu oya tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli daa.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and failing to grow on land that was previously damaged by illegal mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ efite lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil and leaves behind compacted subsoil mixed with heavy metals or chemicals. Without topsoil and organic matter, crops cannot absorb nutrients or water, causing leaves to turn yellow and growth to stop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ, ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni mli edɔ ni akɛ dade ni tsii loo tsofai efutu mli lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii loo nu. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava straight away on land where heavy machines cleared the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu instant cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni tsii ni akɛjieɔ sũ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Heavy machinery compacts soil very tightly, making it hard for roots to spread. Cassava needs loose soil to expand its tubers underground, so you must first till or loosen the land and add compost before planting.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ Cassava he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse koni ekɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli dani odu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under intense sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to protect themselves from water loss during severe heat or drought. It reduces the surface area exposed to the sun so the plant can save moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko koni nu akafite yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ be mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall when microscopic worms (nematodes) or banana weevil pests destroy their root system under the ground. Without strong roots to anchor the heavy stem, the plant easily topples over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ. (Nematodes) loo banana tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ tso ni tsii lɛ Tsei lɛ hu gbeeɔ shi mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot before I am able to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, or overgrown farms with dense shade. Pruning overhead branches and letting air flow through your farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, efɔɔ loo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni hulutsoo mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my yam vines turning dark brown and dropping off during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which thrives in wet and humid weather. Water splashes spread the fungal spores from leaf to leaf, causing them to rot and drop off early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose kɛ enɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ fungal spores lɛ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall green leaves but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kakadaji waa shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its energy on growing leafy stem foliage above ground instead of storing starch in its roots. Balancing soil nutrients helps cassava direct energy into bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cassava ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot spells, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Without calm conditions and key nutrients, the flowers cannot set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao, tamɔ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji shihilɛ ni yɔɔ kpoo kɛ niyenii titrii bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do my maize ears have missing grains or empty gaps on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni bɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize relies on wind to blow pollen from the top tassels onto the silks of the cob. If extreme dry weather or heat hits during the flowering stage, the pollen dies, resulting in incomplete pollination and empty spots on the cob.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ pollen ni jɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Pollen baagbo. Enɛ haa pollination ni eshɛɛɛ he kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ yɛ cob lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects the seedlings from heat stress until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu la lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree yield very small bunches if I allow all the shoots to grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji miha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? mi plantain lɛ

english: When too many young suckers grow around the main plantain stem, they steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the mother plant. Pruning away extra suckers and keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to grow large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahiɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the leaves of maize plants is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires plenty of nitrogen to produce green, healthy leaves, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help restore their green color and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yes, intercropping maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or beans is beneficial because these legumes take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. The maize uses this extra soil nourishment to grow bigger, while the bean plants cover the ground and suppress weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ ŋmãa nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni fata he nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli

english: Cassava stems must be planted with the small leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow upwards, resulting in weak plants and reduced tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ Tsobii lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around my young crops as early as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ oya bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to these nutrients so they can establish strong roots and grow healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛná niyenii nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Koni shishifãi lɛ awa ni amɛdara waa

english: Why do we make high mounds of soil when planting yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔfeɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ beni wɔduɔ sweet potatoes lɛ moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, soft soil so their tubers can expand and grow deep underground without hitting hard earth. High soil mounds also help drain excess rainwater away, keeping the yam roots from rotting during heavy rain seasons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni wa etswaaa amɛ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ fiteee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot sunlight and retains soil moisture longer. It also prevents weeds from growing easily and decomposes over time to feed the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding in the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani akɛtee gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on the inner growing leaves of maize. Controlling them early using recommended biopesticides or neem extract spraying helps protect the plant before the central growing shoot is destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ahe dani ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ afite.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without developing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off, known as blossom drop, when the plants face stress such as sudden high heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. Keeping the root area consistently moist with regular watering helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Ale tomato fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ tsei kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ oha shishifã lɛ mli edɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce healthy green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛfeɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa, ni eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my farmland make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, working like a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees curl up tight during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up during dry, hot weather to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant trap moisture inside and survive with less water.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛmli ni amɛkɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients, as the plant feels too weak to support growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii.

english: What is making ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Tiny caterpillars called Fall Armyworms hide inside the deep center whorl of young maize plants, chewing on the tender leaves as they open up.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni oooye beni amɛgbeleɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up all the air spaces in heavy soils, depriving the cassava roots of oxygen and allowing rot fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. ni oha rot fungus lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my tomato seedlings very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces seedlings to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak stems and higher disease spread.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need their leaves lifted high into the sunlight so they can manufacture enough energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when exposed to full direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn quickly in hot sunlight, requiring temporary shade trees like plantains to protect them while their stems mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni akɛbu he yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when I do not add any fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko fataaa he?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients from harsh soils faster than cultivated farm crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔji ni nɔ wa nɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up when there is intense sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight because intense heat dries out their tender leaves and stops them from making food. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby keeps the soil moist and protects the young cocoa from sun damage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ agbi ni eha niyenii afee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small ragged holes in them and look like something is eating them at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii, ni egbɛ eshwã ni etamɔ nɔ ko eye nii gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant during the day and feed on young maize leaves at night. Catching them early with proper control methods protects your crop before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei amli yɛ gbi mli, ni eyeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua ni obu onibii ahe dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi no mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lolo beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground instead of swelling its roots into big tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo ni potassium loo fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛfeɔ bulb agbo ko yɛ shishi.

english: What will happen to my yam crop if I do not put tall wooden stakes for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko emaaa shi koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their leaves can capture sunlight easily. Without stakes, the vines trail on the hot ground, get attacked by soil fungal diseases, and produce much smaller yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he mlɛo. Wein tsei lɛ baatsɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bɛ nɔ. Fungal helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and die during the day even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ efɔ lɛ?

english: This sudden drooping is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, where harmful germs in the soil block the plant's water-carrying tubes, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves regardless of how wet the soil is.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ gbee ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. he ni helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ nu ni akɛyaa paipii lɛ anaa lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu ashɛ baai lɛ anɔ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoot suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ajie lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plantain tree, they compete with it for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only 2 or 3 strong shoots, which allows the plant to produce much bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ baashi, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the air becomes too hot and dry, or when the plant lacks essential nutrients during the flowering stage, causing the plant to shed flowers to save its energy.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell what nutrients my crops are missing just by looking at the color of their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni he hiaa mitso lɛ kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ ahe su ni makwɛ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pale green or yellow leaves on older growth usually show a shortage of nitrogen, while leaves turning reddish-purple indicate a lack of phosphorus, helping you know which fertilizer or manure your soil needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot under the ground if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often heats up the hot, dry soil, creating a steaming effect that rots the seed before it can sprout. Waiting for a few steady rains ensures the soil stays cool and moist enough for germination.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ haa lasu baa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Nugbɔ ko ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops hurt my harvest even if I add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ miiná mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo, ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before crop roots can reach them, starving your crops and reducing your final harvest yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani amɛshɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ahe. Hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni oha onaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting a coconut seedling before it starts giving me fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: It depends on the variety you plant. Hybrid or dwarf coconut trees usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties can take 6 to 8 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni ji hybrid loo dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii.

english: Why do young coconut fruits fall off my tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoobii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshɛɔ he ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Young fruits often drop because the tree is stressed, usually from a lack of water during dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or sudden changes in weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ miihao. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa

english: Why must I leave wide spaces between my coconut trees when planting them?
