ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmeii tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees grow large leaves and wide root systems. Giving them enough space prevents them from fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients as they grow bigger.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Can I plant maize or cassava between my young coconut trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping with short-term crops like maize, legumes, or cassava is a great way to earn income and food while your young coconut trees are still small and not yet bearing fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ kɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa. Aloo ŋmei ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa shika kɛ niyenii. Yɛ be mli ni o-coconut tso bibioo lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ewooo yibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young crop turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the roots are sitting in too much water due to poor drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted in the afternoon heat even when there is some moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko po.

english: During intense heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the ground, so the plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Why is my seedling growing very tall and thin instead of developing a strong, thick stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛhe wa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Plants grow tall and thin when they are trying to reach for sunlight because they are shaded by bigger trees or planted too close to weeds.
ga: Tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ shwiili kɛji amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu la he ejaakɛ tsei wuji haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jwɛi tsɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds around the base of my young trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei bibii ashishi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your young tree, which severely slows down its growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer immediately on the day I plant my new seedling?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbi ni miduɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to wait a few weeks after planting so the seedling can settle and recover from transplant shock before adding fertilizer to avoid burning its delicate roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ mli. dani awo mli koni akashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Should I trim off green leaves from my tree to help it focus energy on growing fruits?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ koni eye ebua lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni miida lɛ nɔ?

english: No, green leaves are the factory of the plant that makes food using sunlight. Cutting off healthy green leaves weakens the tree and actually slows down fruit production.
ga: Dabi, baai eŋɔli ji tsei anitsumɔhei ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tso yibii lɛ woɔ fioo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow. Water alone isn't enough; applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients required to produce green, strong leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni abele akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Leaving taller shade trees like plantains or forest trees creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa from burning and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and leaves dark dirt inside the center stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) during the day and chew the leaves, but applying recommended pest control measures early in the morning or late evening reaches and stops them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Shi gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baashɛ ni ebaakpa amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers very thin and watery when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ nu kɛji mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers stay thin if harvested too early or planted in hard, unploughed soil. Giving cassava 9 to 12 months to mature in loose soil allows the roots to absorb enough sunlight and store the starch needed to grow big and firm.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ mra tsɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ekɛ ŋmei ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ lɛ toɔ koni efee agbo ni ehi shi shiŋŋ

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during dry weather to reduce the surface area exposed to hot air, preventing water loss. Covering the soil around the plant base with dried grass (mulching) keeps the soil moist and reduces heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni eha he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashɛ amɛhe lɛ aba shi. ni etsi nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close causes crops to crowd each other and fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tiny tubers. Proper spacing (about 1 meter apart) gives each plant enough space to build large, healthy roots.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni haa tsei bibii a-bulbs lɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ (aaafee mita kome) lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni wa baakwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from the hybrid maize I bought and harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid ni mihe ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength, disease resistance, and high yield capacity in the next generation. Buying fresh certified hybrid seed every season ensures uniform growth and maximum harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Helai ni nyɛɔ mɔ nɔ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaa yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli Dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Cowpeas and beans have natural bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently damp and using balanced fertilizers helps flowers turn into full peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly after I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when stored in hot, enclosed spaces with little airflow or when damaged during digging. Storing intact yams off the ground on raised, shaded wooden racks lets fresh air circulate, keeping them cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ boteɔ mli. aloo kɛ́ efite yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Too sweet potatoes ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso shĩa ko ni awo nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Ha edɔ ni egbi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize stalks turning yellow in a V-shape, even though the top leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V-shape mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: This happens because your farm is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen is a key nutrient plants need, and when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant pulls it out of its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with bushy leaves, but produce almost no tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani tomato ko kwraa bɛ?

english: Your plants are getting too much nitrogen from manure or fertilizer. Excess nitrogen tells the plant to spend all its energy growing stems and green leaves instead of making flowers and fruits.
ga: Otsei lɛ miiná nitrogen babaoo kɛmiijɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛɔ tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ eshishifãi ni miida kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is the plant's way of protecting itself from thirst. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant hides its surface area from the hot sun so it loses less water into the dry air.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kumai he. Tsei kɛ amɛhiɛ he lɛ teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms, even when the stems are thick and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ mli etse ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots right under the topsoil. Heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy, so strong winds easily pull their shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi kuɔ we ngɛ zugba a hiɔwe ɔ mi. Yibii ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ baaha amɛhe afee shoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why do groundnut crops help my corn grow greener when I plant them on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei lɛ ni efeɔ eŋɔli kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut roots work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut crop leaves decay, that trapped nitrogen acts as free food for the corn.
ga: Peanut shishifãi kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmei baai lɛ miifite lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around my young cassava instead of letting them cover the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Baby cassava yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds act like thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crop. If left alone, their roots choke the young cassava and prevent it from expanding big underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ pɛ Eshishifãi lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do many tiny, young cocoa pods dry up and turn black before they get big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ Mɛi babaoo gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: This is a natural reaction called cherelle wilt. When a cocoa tree does not have enough water or food to feed all its young pods at once, it deliberately lets some dry up so the remaining ones can survive.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherel wilting. Beni cacao tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaahã ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ. Ebaajɛ etsui mli eha fãi komɛi agbi koni fã ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers dry up and fall off without ever growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when weather gets too hot and dry, or if insects aren't visiting to move pollen around inside the flowers. Without proper pollination or under heavy heat stress, the plant drops flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbajie pollen lɛ kɛbɔle fɔfɔi lɛ ahe, kɛji akɛ afeee pollen lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo kɛji akɛ eyɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa shishi. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does planting pepper on the exact same patch of land for three years in a row make the plants wilt and die fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Diseases and pests that feed specifically on pepper roots build up and multiply in the soil over time. Changing to a different crop like maize or cassava starves those pests and cleans the soil.
ga: Helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ni aaatsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli atse.

english: Why do I need to put long bamboo stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Keeping the leaves off the wet soil also stops fungal diseases from rotting the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Shade trees or shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the air moist and soil cool until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ni hiɛ ka. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants rolling up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to hide their broad surfaces from the sun, which reduces the amount of water they lose through evaporation during the heat of the day.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei wuji kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he, ni no haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves to save water and survive drought. The plant goes to sleep above ground while keeping its root tubers safe under the soil, sprouting fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tso lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa eshishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe. Baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their blossoms without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they are stressed by excessive heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil like potassium, which the plant needs to hold and nourish fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkɛto amɛyibii lɛ ahe ni amɛha amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Will trimming off the lower side shoots on my garden egg plants help them produce bigger fruits?
ga: Ani eggplant tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ shishi lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji?

english: Yes, pruning weak side branches and lower leaves prevents the plant from wasting food energy on useless leaves, directing extra water and nutrients straight into growing bigger, healthier eggplants.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ afã kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni eggplant lɛ adara ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow long, bushy leaves but give me very small tubers underground at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If yams receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure without enough sunlight and proper staking, the plant puts all its energy into growing leafy vines instead of storing starch in the root tuber.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha sweet potato nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmei ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ he nii moŋ fe ni eeekɛ starch ato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my groundnut seeds are rotting in the ground or just taking time to sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛheɔ be kɛkɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Groundnuts need damp but loose soil to germinate. If planted too deep in heavy, waterlogged soil, the seeds suffocate and rot from lack of air rather than pushing green shoots above the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ shi eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Mohu ɔ, a tsiɔ tso ɔmɛ nɛ a ngɛ ŋmɔ ɔmɛ ɔ kɛ yaa hɛ mi.

english: What causes black spots to spread from the bottom leaves of my tomato plants all the way to the top?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛigbɛ?

english: Black spots on tomatoes are caused by fungal diseases that live in the soil. When rain splashes water onto the lower leaves, the fungi jump onto the plant and spread upward in humid weather.
ga: Hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Fuji lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli.

english: How do I know my groundnuts are mature underground without digging up the whole farm too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ oya tsɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer foliage starts turning yellow and dry. You can check a few sample pods: if the inner skin of the shell has turned dark brown instead of white, the crop is ready.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ pod nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko mli: kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why are some of my newly planted plantain suckers shooting up quickly while others take months to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei komɛi ni adu ehee lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Maiden suckers with broad leaves grow slower because they spend energy supporting old foliage, while sword suckers with thin, pointed leaves have stronger food reserves in their corm for rapid stem growth.
ga: Broad leaf suckers lɛ daa blɛoo ejaakɛ amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ baai momoi lɛ asɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, klante suckers ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni ato yɛ amɛ bulbs lɛ amli koni eha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ada oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow even when it rains continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow when maize lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil. Heavy rain can wash these nutrients deeper into the ground away from the roots, so applying the right fertilizer helps feed the plant and restore its green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ ahe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn brown and dry up after I put chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and acts like salt. If placed directly touching the plant stem or leaves, it pulls moisture out of the plant cells and burns them. Fertilizer should always be buried a short distance away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he wa waa ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi loo baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, fumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller yields every year even when I plant the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ po

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every season drains specific nutrients faster than the soil can replenish them. Rotating your land with crops like beans or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii baatsake Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and tall without making big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for the same limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the stalks weak and thin, leaving them without enough energy to form large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout out of the ground completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of soil moisture, warmth, and depth to germinate. If buried too deep in the soil or planted in dry earth, the seed will run out of energy before reaching the surface or rot in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ, dɔlɛ kɛ mlibotemɔ teŋ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon but look fresh again in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can absorb it from the soil, causing temporary drooping to conserve moisture. Overnight, when temperatures drop, the roots catch up and fill the leaves with water again.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛkɛ nu baawo baai lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Heat stress prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large shade trees from my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot withstand direct scorching sunlight and dry winds. Large trees provide natural shade and keep the air humid, protecting the young plants until their stems grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsei wuji haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are growing large under the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mafo amɛ?

english: As cassava roots swell under the ground, they push the surrounding soil upward, creating visible cracks around the base of the plant stem. Additionally, the bottom leaves of the plant naturally turn yellow and drop off as energy shifts to the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi Ebaatsi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baa. Kɛfata he lɛ, tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni hewalɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants with strong roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the food and light they need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cowpeas focus all their energy on growing big green leaves rather than flowers and pods. Cowpeas actually make their own nitrogen in the ground, so they need very little added fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cowpeas lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ, tsina ŋmeii feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ he miihia amɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the soil without draining away, it suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi to attack and decay them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing any fruit during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛduɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is extremely hot or the plant lacks water, it gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy so the main plant can survive instead of feeding new fruit.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa loo tsei lɛ bɛ nu. Ebaafee nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii baashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii heei.

english: How does covering my soil with dry grass keep my crops from drying out?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mulching aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass—called mulching—acts like a shield against the hot sun, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why should I clear away fallen, rotten cocoa pods from under my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie kookoo ŋmeii ni efite kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Rotten pods carry spores of the black pod disease. Leaving them on the ground allows rain drops to splash those disease spores back onto healthy pods and infect the whole farm.
ga: Pods ni egbo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nɛ ni ekɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai aku sɛɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli. ni egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than the crop seeds I deliberately plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe dumɔwui ni mito akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, naturally tough plants that are better adapted to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. ni atsake koni ekɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ aye akaŋ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees close to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade to cool the young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Akɛ hulutsoo haa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ koni eha kookoo bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants suddenly full of small holes and look like they were chewed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm that eat tender leaves. Catching them early and spraying recommended organic mixtures or approved insecticides onto the leaves can stop them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Mɔ amɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains around them provides temporary shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know which side of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I am planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small raised bumps or buds on the stem where old leaves grew. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so the stems can grow out easily above the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ baai momoi lɛ ashishifã nɔ Ehe miihia ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow even though I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water fills up air gaps in the soil and smothers the roots. Water deeply only when the top layer of soil feels dry, rather than adding heavy water every day.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efiteɔ. Nu lɛ mli kwɔ pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nu he akɛ egbi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ muji afata he daa gbi lɛ

english: What is the main difference between chemical fertilizer like NPK and natural animal manure?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: NPK fertilizer gives your crops a quick shot of nutrients for rapid growth, while animal manure releases nutrients slowly and improves the soil's structure so it holds water better in future seasons.
ga: NPK Fertilizer haa otsei lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya koni amɛdara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii fiofio. ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ aya hiɛ koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔsɛɛ bei amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting with proper distance gives each plant enough food to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants before any fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Mulching the soil with dry grass helps keep root temperatures cool and moist.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the soil for years. When you clear the top layer, you expose hidden seeds to sunlight and rain, which triggers them to germinate instantly alongside your crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo Kɛ́ ojie ŋwɛi fã lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛfata onibii ahe.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the damp ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and stay free from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. He ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo yɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ amɛhe yɛ.

english: How can I prevent insects and weevils from ruining my harvested maize in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Ensure the maize is dried thoroughly until hard before storing, keep the storage area completely dry and clean, and use sealed hermetic storage bags (like PICS bags) that suffocate insects.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛto. Ha he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ mli agbi kwraa ni ehe atse. Ni okɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ naa (tamɔ PICS kotokui) ni baaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting at the tip and moving down the middle, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for keeping leaves green and strong, so applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ ni amɛyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from high heat, uneven watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving them shade during extreme sun and maintaining consistent moisture in the soil helps the flowers set into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni akɛhaa hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving shade trees provides a cool environment that prevents heat stress and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo hulutsoo tsei ni ashiɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is eating holes in the leaf centers of my young corn plants and leaving dark droppings behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the funnel of young maize plants during the day. Early detection and applying targeted organic or chemical treatments directly into the leaf whorl protects the growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater collects around them and starves the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away quickly, keeping the tubers safe from decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Ha yitso lɛ akafite

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and hard when the wet weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi efee fɛ̃i lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, humid shade. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the canopy, drying out the moisture that the fungus needs to grow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches when I leave many stems growing around one mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii kome he lɛ?

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain mat, they all compete for the same soil food and water. Removing excess suckers and leaving only two or three main stems focuses energy into producing larger bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii titrii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ ahi ŋmeii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato stems break and lie on the ground when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛkãa shikpɔŋ beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants produce heavy branches and fruit that pull the vine downward toward damp soil, making them vulnerable to rot. Tying the plants to wood stakes lifts the stems into the air where leaves stay dry and fruit stays safe.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ niji ni tsii kɛ aduawai ni gbalaa wain tso lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ fĩ tso tso ko he lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ shishi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. he ni baai lɛ baagbi ni aduawai lɛ baahi shi shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural nodes on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Intercropping provides your maize with free natural nutrients while protecting the ground from drying out.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ haa o-corn lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the root underground. Staking holds the vines up off the damp ground so leaves gather full sunlight, resulting in bigger tuber sizes.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Okɛ wain tso lɛ awo ŋwɛi kɛjɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ etso lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why is it better for me to use an irrigation scheme to farm rice instead of depending only on rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants need a steady and controlled supply of water throughout their growth. Relying only on rain can be risky because rain can stop unexpectedly, but irrigation allows you to give your crops the right amount of water at the right time to guarantee a good harvest.
ga: Nu ni akudɔ daa lɛ he miihia omɔ tsei yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Nugbɔ pɛ nɔ ni akɛaafɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa trukaa. Shi nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu ni sa haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli koni eha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ abakpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How deep should the water be in my rice field while the plants are growing?
ga: Te esa akɛ nu lɛ mli akwɔ tɛŋŋ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ?

english: For most of the growing stage, keep a shallow water level of about 2 to 5 centimeters. This keeps the soil soft for root growth and prevents weeds from growing, but you should drain the water completely about two weeks before harvest so the land dries for easy cutting.
ga: Kɛha dalɛ fãi babaoo lɛ Ha nu lɛ mli akafee shɔŋŋ, aaafee sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 5. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃. Shi esa akɛ ojie nu lɛ kwraa aaafee otsii enyɔ dani okpa. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi koni anyɛ afo lɛ mlɛo.

english: What basic steps do I need to take to prepare my land properly before planting rice?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: You need to clear all bushes and weeds, plow the soil to make it soft, and level the ground so water distributes evenly. Building small mud borders around the field, called bunds, helps keep the water inside your farm plot.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni efee bɔdɔɔ. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome bɔni afee ni nu lɛ aja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ Atsɛɔ muji husu bibioo ko ni akɛbɔleɔ ŋmɔ ko he lɛ akɛ bund. Ebaaye ebua ni nu ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to sow rice seeds directly into the soil or raise seedlings in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo makwɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Raising seedlings in a nursery and transplanting them into flooded fields gives young plants a stronger start and makes it easier to manage weeds. Direct seeding is faster and uses less labor, but weeds can easily choke the young crops if you do not control them early.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo Dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ yaa oya ni ekɛ nitsumɔ babaoo tsuuu nii. Shi jwɛi baanyɛ afite tsei bibii oya kɛji okuuu amɛ mra.

english: How do I estimate the amount of rice seed and money I need to start planting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ŋmaa kɛ shika ni he hiaa koni akɛje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You calculate your seed needs based on land size, usually needing about 20 to 25 kilograms of quality seed per acre. For budgeting, add the costs of land preparation, fertilizer, seed purchasing, and labor for weeding and harvesting so you know your total cost beforehand.
ga: Okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni he hiaa bo lɛ he akɔntaa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ aaafee kilogram 20 kɛyashi 25 he hiaa yɛ acre kome mli. kɛha shika he gbɛjianɔtoo Okɛ shika ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ dumɔwui ahemɔ afata he. kɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛha jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ Enɛ ji koni ole nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my rice field to inspect my crop, and what should I look for?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛyakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ matao?

english: You should walk through your field at least twice every week. Check for yellowing leaves, missing plants, insect pests like stem borers, weed growth, and check whether your water levels are too high or too low.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oyale mli shii enyɔ daa otsi. Kwɛmɔ baai ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni elaaje, kɛ kooloi tamɔ stem borers. jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ Ni okwɛ kɛji onu lɛ fa tsɔ loo eba shi tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the water level in the field is wrong. Applying a balanced nitrogen fertilizer like Urea and regulating your water will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli, loo akɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni ja, tamɔ urea tsu nii, ni akudɔ nu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast in my irrigated rice plot, and how can I control them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aaatsɔ akudɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds thrive because the water and fertilizer meant for your rice also feed weed seeds in the soil. Maintaining a proper water depth smothers many weeds, and pulling out remaining weeds by hand when the plants are young prevents them from stealing plant nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ onu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. Nu lɛ mlibotemɔ ni sa lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ baagbe jwɛi babaoo. Ni kɛ́ okɛ onine jieɔ jwɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ.

english: What is paddy rice, and how is it different from the rice we buy in the market?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmãa? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni wɔheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ he?

english: Paddy rice is the raw, freshly harvested grain still inside its hard protective outer husk. The white or brown rice you buy in the market has been milled to remove that outer husk so it can be cooked.
ga: Paddy ji ŋmaa ni akpa ehee ni yɔɔ esɛɛ ŋmei ni buɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lolo. Akɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ loo ŋmãa ni tsuɔ ni oheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ efolɔ mli koni ajie kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ koni anyɛ ahoo.

english: How can I tell that my rice is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Your rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn from green to a bright golden-yellow color and the heads of the plants bend downward under the weight of the grain.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmaa lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli lɛ. ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ tsiimɔ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why will my crops burn if I put chemical fertilizer directly touching their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water out of tender roots and stems, causing severe chemical burns. Applying fertilizer in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to absorb the food safely through the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Ekɛ tsofa shãa ni naa wa baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ ŋwɛibɔfoi bibii amli Loo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater collects and sits in the soil without proper drainage, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy until harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: The season's first rain often wets only the surface soil, which dries out quickly under hot sun and causes newly germinated seeds to dry up and die. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures deep soil moisture so seeds can sprout and establish roots safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ. ni gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni ehaa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Kɛkɛ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtswa shishifãi shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by long dry spells, excessive sun heat, or attacks from pests like mirid insects. Providing overhead shade trees and controlling pests helps the flowers stay attached and develop into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli. hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ tutuamɔ. Shade ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole forces the growing seedlings to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Planting seeds at recommended distances gives each crop enough room to build thick stems and yield bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni miida lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce fewer and smaller fruits if I leave them in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, light, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds during the early growing weeks ensures your main crops get all the food they need to produce large, healthy fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, kane, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ otsi ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa otso titri lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy forked wooden pole prevents the tree from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eye ebua aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akutsei ni tsii lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant, often due to irregular soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and adding lime or organic matter helps tomatoes form solid, rot-free fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ lime loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tomato ni ewo yibii ni wa ni fiteŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is a major food source for crops. Heavy rain often washes this nutrient deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season, and will this kill them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani ebaaha baai lɛ agbo loo amɛgbooo?

english: Cassava intentionally drops its leaves when dry weather sets in to prevent water from evaporating through the leaves. The plant is not dead; its roots remain alive underground, and fresh leaves will sprout as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ ŋmei baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather becomes extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy until growing conditions become cooler and more stable.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli baajɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water into the air faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground. Curling their leaves reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, helping the plant save moisture until the evening cool down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: The first rain of the season can trick seeds into sprouting, but it is often followed by a long dry spell. Without follow-up rain, the soil dries out quickly and burns the young, delicate seedlings before the true rainy season established itself.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni eshãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning instead of during midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai lɛ amli leebi moŋ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Watering under the hot afternoon sun causes a lot of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots. Morning watering allows the soil to absorb moisture and gives the plants fuel to survive the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eŋɔɔ nu ni ehaa tsei lɛ tsofa ni amɛkɛyeɔ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize ears turn out small and weak when I plant several seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete fiercely for the same limited food, water, and sunlight in that spot. Spacing seeds out properly gives each plant enough space and food to produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la fioo ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui amli gbalamɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain shishitoo lɛ he lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main stem. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures that the main plantain tree gets enough food to grow a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa plantain titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulch, acts like a blanket over the soil. It shades the soil from direct heat, keeping it cool and stopping soil moisture from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the funnel of my young maize plants instead of eating the outside leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant contains the tenderest, sweetest new leaves. Caterpillars hide deep inside this area because it shelters them from direct hot sunlight and hides them from birds while they feed.
ga: Abɛi tso bibioo ko teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ ji baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ, ni ŋɔɔ fe fɛɛ. Kplukai kɛ amɛhe teeɔ amɛhe yɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ mli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ekɛ amɛhe teeɔ okpoi ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from direct sunlight during their early years. Without shade plants like plantains to protect them, intense sunlight burns their leaves and slows down their growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with lots of green leaves, but giving very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing stem and leaf leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme hot weather or long periods without water. The plant sheds its blossoms to save water and stay alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo nu bɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when water supply is uneven, preventing the plant from delivering nutrients to the bottom of the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tso yibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ekɛ ehe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the central leaves of young maize plants to feed, which can destroy the growing point if not caught early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite he ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over whenever strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot support the heavy weight of the fruit bunch during strong winds. Supporting the main trunk with bamboo poles prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso fi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why do I need to build soft soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ŋmɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil so they can expand downward without resistance. Raising mounds also prevents excess rainwater from sitting around the roots and rotting the seed yam.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents soil moisture from evaporating under the sun, and suppresses weeds.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu la shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for nutrient-hungry crops like maize in the following season.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni he hiaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seeds rot under the soil when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by severe hot days. If the soil gets wet and then bakes in dry heat, the seeds dry out and decay before they can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, egbiɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from direct harsh sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantain or leaving selected tall trees keeps the soil moist and cools the cocoa plants while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo ashi tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha cacao tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, cool shade. Pruning dark branches to let sunlight through and clearing weeds helps air flow and reduces the moisture the disease needs to spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni edɔ. Niji ni tsuɔ diŋŋ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la atsɔ mli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli ni ebaaha hulutsoo ni hela lɛ he hiaa koni egbɛ eshwa lɛ aba shi.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny waste inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Eboteɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli ni eshiɔ jwɛi fioo ko yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the center leaves of the maize plant, and applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel leaf early in the crop's growth controls them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo cone baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli koni eye nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings for planting is the most effective way to prevent this disease.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmei ni helai nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi eshi lɛ ni tomato ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing the plant to focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Ha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which improves the land for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha jɛmɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper crops in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the plants absorb moisture before heat builds up, and it stops leaves from staying wet overnight which can cause plant diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ baa. ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome, ni baanyɛ ekɛ helai aba tsei anɔ.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing sprouts and soft spots even when they are kept indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ shĩa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from resting after a few months and prepare to grow again. Keeping them in a dry, well-ventilated traditional yam barn off the ground slows down sprouting and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛdara ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ blema sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants wrinkling and shrinking into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites underneath the leaves. Spraying with neem oil extract or appropriate insecticides helps control these insects and protects new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebu tsei ahe tsei heei ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings shade and holding moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my old farm getting smaller every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi lɛ?

english: When a plantain plant grows, it shoots out many small baby plants called suckers around its base. If you do not trim these suckers away, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil, which makes the main plant produce small bunches.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara Ewoɔ tsei bibii. Mɛi babaoo, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, jeɔ kpo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛji ofolɔɔɔ enɛɛmɛi ahe. Amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: How do I know if my land is good for planting plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii?
