english: Plantains grow best in deep, soft soil rich in decaying leaves or dark earth where rainwater drains easily. If water stays trapped on top of your land for days like a pond, the roots will rot and the plants will die.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baai egbo loo shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ni nugbɔ nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu ŋmɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo tamɔ nubu. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni tso lɛ baagbo.

english: What month is best for me to put my plantain suckers into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui baawo shikpɔŋ?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the major rainy season, around April or May. This gives the young plants plenty of water to establish strong roots before any dry weather sets in.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Aaafee April loo May Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu babaoo koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or small worms in the soil are attacking the roots. Adding animal manure or organic compost around the base can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miitutua shishifãi lɛ. Koolooi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛku esɛɛ aba eŋɔli.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close makes the crops fight among themselves for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, making them produce very small yields and easily fall over in high winds.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, etswaa shi oya.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my main crops so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ adalɛ miiba shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they quickly drink up the water and take away the fertilizer and soil food intended for your crops, leaving your plants hungry and slow to grow.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ. Ha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ ni amɛdara fiofio.

english: How do I pick the best plantain suckers from an old farm to start a new one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for young suckers that have narrow, spear-like leaves and strong, bulb-like bases—these are called 'sword suckers'. Avoid suckers with broad, flat leaves or those growing on diseased plants, as they carry sickness to your new field.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ bulb, ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘klante tsei.’ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe, ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ hela aba osɛɛ hee lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is ready to be cut down?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaafolɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready when the individual fingers lose their sharp, angled corners and become full and round. The dry flower tips at the bottom of the fruits should also rub off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo beni nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fiteɔ eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni eyiɔ obɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ. Esa akɛ fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ hu atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and hang down during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmatta gbimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl and droop during hot, dry spells as a natural way to save water and stop themselves from drying out. Covering the ground around the stem with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and conserves soil moisture.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ ni atsĩɔ nu ni egbiɔ lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa he ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Sandy soil has large particles with wide spaces between them, acting like a sieve that lets water drain away rapidly instead of holding moisture near your crop's roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii wuji ni gbɛ babaoo yɔɔ amɛteŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa nu hoɔ oya. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ nu nɛ ngɛ o tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a he ɔ.

english: Why should I take my soil for testing before buying fertilizer for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ dani mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Soil testing acts like a health checkup; it reveals exactly which nutrients your land is missing so you don't waste money buying the wrong fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ mlikwɛmɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kpo. Bɔni afee ni okafite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa.

english: How does mixing animal manure into sandy land help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Manure acts like a sponge inside sandy soil, helping the ground trap water and essential plant food so the roots have time to drink and feed.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa kɛ tsei aniyenii hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nii ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Is it better to pour liquid fertilizer directly into the soil or spray it onto the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Spraying liquid fertilizer on leaves gives crops a fast emergency boost, while putting it directly into the soil allows the roots to feed steadily over a longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli.

english: How do I know if I am giving my plants too much water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mitsei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: When crops get too much water, their roots drown from a lack of air, causing the leaves to turn yellow, feel soft, and wilt even though the dirt is soaking wet.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nu babaoo Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks steady water, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmeii

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains all the specific nutrients from that soil and encourages pests and soil diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ nakai sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ. ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sunlight, keeps water from evaporating, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni otsi jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ naa

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and stronger than the crop seeds I sow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive harsh conditions, so they quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: How long do common insect pests usually live on a farm, and why does their age matter to me?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ hiɔ ŋmɔji amli? Ni mɛni hewɔ afii ni amɛye lɛ he hiaa mi lɛ?

english: Many crop pests have a life cycle of around 90 to 95 days, moving from eggs to destructive caterpillars and then adults. Knowing their lifespan helps you identify which stage they are in so you can stop them before they reproduce.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 95, ni amɛjɛɔ amɛwui amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli. kɛ onukpai Kɛ́ ole amɛwala be lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ole he ni amɛyɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa amɛ dani amɛfɔ bii.

english: How can I tell if an insect on my crop is a harmful pest or a friendly bug?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo amɛji naanyobɔɔ?

english: Harmful pests leave visible signs like chewed leaves, small holes, or discolored spots, especially on young plants. Observing where insects gather on your crop and checking for leaf damage helps you identify true pests.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shiɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre, bu bibii, loo hei ni amɛhe su etsake. titri lɛ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ onibii anɔ lɛ, ni okwɛ bɔ ni baai lɛ efite amɛha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oyoo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Is there a specific stage in a pest's life when it is easiest to kill?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko wala mli ni egbemɔ waaa fe fɛɛ?

english: Yes, pests are easiest to destroy when they are young larvae or eggs early in their life cycle. Once they mature into adults, they become harder to control and do the most damage to your yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ewaaa akɛ abaakpãtã kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahiɛ kɛ́ amɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ onukpai Ebaawa akɛ oookudɔ ni ekɛ nɔ ni fiteɔ nii fe fɛɛ baaba onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to return to my farm every three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa nyɔji etɛ lɛ?

english: Many farm pests complete a full generation cycle in about 90 days. If the eggs or young bugs from the previous group were not completely eliminated, a fresh batch hatches to start a new attack three months later.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo gbeɔ amɛ nifeemɔi lɛ anaa yɛ aaafee gbii 90 mli kɛji ajieee ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni jɛ kuu ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ kwraa. Kuu hee ko baaje kpo koni amɛje tutuamɔ hee shishi yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I regularly walk through my field to inspect my small crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ mli koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni adu lɛ? mi lɛ daa?

english: Walking your field regularly lets you spot pest attacks early while plants are small. Early detection makes pest control much cheaper and prevents full-scale destruction of your plot.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji bibioo lɛ Mra be mli ni anaa Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ feɔ nɔ ni jara waaa kwraa ni etsĩɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ kwraa naa.

english: Why do pests attack my young seedling crops more aggressively than mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ waa fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young plants have soft, tender leaves that are easy for young pests to bite and digest. Because small plants are weak, pest damage at this stage can kill the crop completely before it produces fruit.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Ejaakɛ tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa dani ewo yibii po.

english: What basic signs should I look for when checking my crops for pest damage?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee okadii esa akɛ matao beni mikwɛɔ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai efite ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Check underneath leaves, inside young shoots, and around the stem for tiny eggs, caterpillars, leaf holes, or sticky residue. These are early indicators that pests are active on your plot.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi, tsei bibii lɛ amli, kɛ tsei lɛ ahe kɛha ŋmeii bibii, ŋmeii, baai lɛ amli bu, loo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ mra akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some sections of my farm have heavy insect damage while other plots remain healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii waa lɛ miifite miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi lɛ? be mli ni shikpɔji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo?

english: Pests often start in one specific plot where conditions favor them, such as areas with younger or shaded plants. Inspecting plot by plot allows you to treat only the affected spots before the insects spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai jeɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni shihilɛi lɛ hi yɛ nɔ, tamɔ hei ni tsei bibii yɔɔ loo hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔji lɛ amli ekomekomei lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ otsaa hei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know if the number of insects on my plants is serious enough to treat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: You need to monitor the pest levels across your crops. If only one or two leaves show minor nibbles, natural predators may control them; but if pest levels grow across many plants, immediate action is needed.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ fa ha. Kɛji akɛ baa kome loo enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ he okadii bibii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tee hiɛ yɛ tsei babaoo amli hu? Ehe miihia ni atsu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent pests from moving from one side of my farm to the rest of my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkajɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ amli?

english: By catching pests early through regular field checks, you can isolate and treat infected plots immediately. Removing heavily infested young plants prevents the pests from completing their life cycle and spreading.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Amɔmɔ Mra Pass daa ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔi. Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsi ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe ni otsa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akagbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new top growth, causing the bottom leaves to starve if there is not enough fertilizer or manure in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume crop dies, it leaves this natural fertilizer behind, feeding the hungry maize crop that follows.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji legume tsei gboi Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ esɛɛ. ni ekɛ niyenii ha ŋmãa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of thick green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo baai ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ?

english: Giving your pepper plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers. To get plenty of peppers, the soil needs phosphorus and potassium, which encourage flowering and fruit growth.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha o-pepper tso lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo aba. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural way of protecting itself. By rolling its leaves inward, the tomato plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing it from losing too much moisture when the air is dry.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie mli lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their blossoms without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, harsh dry winds, or attacks from tiny insects like mirids. It can also happen if there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni tswaa lɛ tutuaa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ faaa.

english: The first rain usually wets only the top layer of soil, leaving the deeper ground hot and dry. If a dry spell follows, your seeds will sprout and quickly dry up; it is safer to wait until the ground gets a deep, thorough soaking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbi. Kɛji hulutsoo be nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi oya. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baawo mli jogbaŋŋ ni ebaatsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide and eat right inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the central leaf funnel because the young leaves inside are tender to eat, and the funnel protects them from rain, direct sun, and predators like birds.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ayeɔ. Ni gbɛjegbɛi lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ tamɔ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the ground stays wet for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, the roots drown, die, and become food for fungi that cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once the fruit bunches start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can easily be weakened by pests like nematodes or stem borers. Without strong roots anchored in the ground, the heavy weight of the fruit bunch pulls the whole plant down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ aná amɛ oya. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɛ lɛ Tso yibii ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around the base of my young cassava plants regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your cassava needs to build strong leaves and underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa o-cassava lɛ koni ekwɛ baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Is it good to give my plants as much fertilizer as possible so they grow bigger quickly?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ makɛ tsofa awo mitsei lɛ amli bɔ ni manyɛ koni amɛdara oya?

english: No, giving plants too much fertilizer is like forcing a person to overeat. Excessive fertilizer burns the plant's delicate roots, turns the water or soil toxic, and will eventually kill your crops instead of helping them grow.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli fe nine lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ mɛi anɔ koni amɛye nii fe nine. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ha nu loo shikpɔŋ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua ni ekwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if I am overfeeding my crops with fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine?

english: When crops get too much fertilizer, their leaves may suddenly turn dark green or show burnt brown tips. You may also notice the standing water around them turning green quickly, followed by the plants wilting and dying.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ trukaa loo amɛyitsei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shã. Ekolɛ obaana nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle he. oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Tso ni gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plant leaves start turning brown and drying up even after I gave them plenty of food and water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ miha lɛ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: When you put too much fertilizer in the soil or water, it creates an environment with too many dissolved salts. This prevents the roots from taking up clean water properly, causing the leaves to dry out and burn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ loo nu lɛ mli Enɛ baaha shihilɛ ko ni ŋmei ni egbɛ eshwa babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ aba. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu ni mli tse lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why do my young seedlings rot and die shortly after I apply liquid fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ewo mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have fragile roots that cannot tolerate strong amounts of nutrients. Applying too much liquid fertilizer creates unsafe water conditions that chemically burn the tender roots, causing the seedlings to collapse.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ niyenii babaoo nɔ. Nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa nu mli shihilɛi ni bɛ shweshweeshwe ni kɛ tsofai shãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why has the standing water in my crop field turned dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ?

english: Water turns green quickly when there is too much fertilizer or organic waste in it. The extra plant food causes tiny water plants called algae to multiply rapidly under the sun, which spoils the water quality.
ga: Nu lɛ tsɔɔ eŋɔli oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ fa babaoo. Tsei aniyenii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa nu mli tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ algae lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya yɛ hulu la shishi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ mli afee fɛo.

english: Should I drain out stagnant green water from around my plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie nu ni ji eŋɔli ni ekã shi lɛ kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ amli?

english: Yes, you should drain green stagnant water immediately. Green water contains excessive nutrients and algae that destroy water quality, smother plant roots, and will eventually cause your crops to die.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ajie amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nu ni mli tse lɛ yɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ baafite nu lɛ mlihilɛ, ebaafite tsei shishifãi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my flooded crops dying even though there is plenty of water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu shwie nɔ lɛ gboi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ He ni nu babaoo yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Having plenty of water is not enough if the water quality is bad. If the water contains too much dissolved fertilizer or rotting waste, it loses air and turns harmful, choking your plants from the root up.
ga: Nu babaoo ni mɔ ko yɔɔ lɛ faaa kɛji nu lɛ mli ehiii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji loo muji ni fiteɔ babaoo yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ, Nu lɛ laajeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebafeɔ oshara. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: What should I do if I accidentally pour too much chemical fertilizer into my small irrigation pond?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo wo mi-nu ŋshɔ bibioo lɛ mli yɛ oshara mli?

english: You should drain or flush out the pond water as soon as possible and replace it with fresh water. Leaving the excess fertilizer in the pond will spoil the water and harm any crops you water with it.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni yɔɔ nubu lɛ mli lɛ ajie loo okɛjie nu lɛ oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ ni okɛ nu kpakpa awo najiaŋ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine yɛ o-pond lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafite nu lɛ ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ nu woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does water turn dirty and smelly so fast after I add animal manure to my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ mli woɔ muji ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya beni mikɛ ŋmeii ewo mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Animal manure is rich in nutrients, but adding too much causes it to break down rapidly in standing water. This overload of nutrients ruins the water quality and makes it bad for plant roots.
ga: Koolooi aŋmɔ mli nibii babaoo yɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite oya yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ babaoo fiteɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ehiii.

english: How often should I change or flush the water in my flooded farm plots?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsake loo mafo nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: You should flush or change the water whenever it starts looking thick, green, or dirty. Replacing bad water with fresh water clears out built-up fertilizers and provides healthy air to the crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu lɛ afɔ loo otsake be fɛɛ be ni ebaaje shishi etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, etsɔ eŋɔli, loo etsɔ muji. Nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛ nu kpakpa baatsake lɛ baaye abua ni ejie ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebua shi lɛ, ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow when the sun gets too bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ tsoɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade from taller crops, like plantains, to shield them and keep the soil moist until they grow strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu tso lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Ani abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii kɛfata kookoo tso hee lɛ he?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantains alongside new cocoa trees provides vital shade for young cocoa while giving you food and income before the cocoa trees start producing fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ baaha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely causes them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak trees and lower pod yields. It also traps air moisture, which makes trees more likely to catch fungal diseases.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni pod ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi. Emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ hu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baanyɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ.

english: Why do so many cocoa flowers fall off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support into full pods. However, excessive flower drop can happen if the tree is stressed by drought, lacks nutrients, or if tiny insects called midges are not available to pollinate them.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhiɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni baa shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kɛji kooloi bibii ba tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haoɔ lɛ. Anyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa pod to mature after the tree flowers?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ?

english: Once a cocoa flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about five to six months for the pod to grow to full size and ripen into its harvest color, usually yellow or orange.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Ebaahe aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani ŋmɔtɔi lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he ni amɛshwere kɛyashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: Dropping leaves during the dry season is a survival reaction. The tree sheds leaves to reduce water loss so it can keep its trunk and root system alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ he nifeemɔ. Tsei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pods turn black and rot due to Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather when rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmei mli ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa stems curling up and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and browning is often caused by sap-sucking insects like mirids (capsids) that bite tender shoots, or by severe water stress during heatwaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni ŋmɔɔ tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off small shoots growing out from the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Removing extra shoots, called chupons, prevents them from stealing water and nutrients away from the main stem, ensuring the tree directs its energy toward growing healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my land has good soil for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, soft, and deep enough for roots to grow without hitting hard rock. It should hold moisture during dry periods without staying waterlogged when it rains heavily.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ blɛoo, ni eyɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni enaaa tɛi ni wa lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. Esa akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli ni nu akabote mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my maize help my soil and crops?
ga: Te ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the maize plants growing nearby and improves soil fertility without extra cost.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aye niyenii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Crop roots cannot absorb dry fertilizer. Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve into a form plants can drink up; putting it in dry soil can actually burn and damage the roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni tsei baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long or when soil diseases attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ta shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes through the middle leaves of my maize, and how do I protect my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides inside the central leaves of maize plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended insecticides or neem oil into the center shoot early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye amɛnɔ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that spread a virus to the plant. Controlling these insects early prevents the virus from spreading and damaging your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave tall shade trees on my farm when planting young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei kakadaji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally prefer shade because direct, harsh sunlight stresses them, dries out the soil, and attracts damaging pests. Tall trees keep the farm cool and humid so young cocoa can thrive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo be ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ, ni egbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa koni kookoo bibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, so why are the flowers falling off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi shi jeee tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plants do not get enough water, or if bees are not visiting to pollinate them. Regular watering during dry spells helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the hot ground and puts them up into the sunlight. When leaves get full sunlight, they make more food for the plant, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potatoes lɛ kɛjɛ he ni edɔ lɛ ni ekɛ amɛ awo hulu lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebaafee niyenii babaoo aha tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing around my main plantain shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ etee.

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches. Leaving only one main plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot ensures large, healthy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tso titri kome pɛ, tso bibioo kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to protect them from harsh heat and retain soil moisture while they establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to grow green leaves and strong stalks. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi biɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Cassava mosaic hela lɛ kɛbaa Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or soil lacks proper nutrients. Regular watering and spreading mulch around the base keeps the roots cool and helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ. Kɔnii lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for roots to spread and leaves to catch light for bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛ baai lɛ koni amɛná la kɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce better corn when I plant groundnuts on it the season before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil. This enriches the ground with natural food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my pepper fruits turn dark brown and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark rot at the blossom end of peppers is usually caused by uneven watering, which prevents the plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for the plant. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground so leaves catch maximum light, sending energy down to make the underground tubers grow large.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba tso lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aná la babaoo. ni etsuɔ ​​hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adara

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas between my rows of corn, and how does it help?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas between corn rows helps cover the bare soil to suppress weeds, retain moisture, and feed natural nitrogen into the soil to support the corn crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko kɛmiitsɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the growing tip of maize plants. Checking crops early and spraying appropriate botanical or recommended controls prevents them from destroying the crop center.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nɔkwɛmɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afeɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and dark green on one side of my farm, but remain short and yellowish on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi fã kroko lɛ yɛ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo?

english: Plants turn yellow and stay short when the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. The dark green area likely has richer soil from past organic material, while the yellowish area needs fertilizer or compost to replenish missing nutrients.
ga: Tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi kuku kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Ekolɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo kɛjɛ tsutsu nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Shi hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni elaaje lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the large trees and shade around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ ni mikɛ amɛhe woɔ amɛhe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and strong heat. Keeping larger shade trees or planting broad-leaf crops like plantain next to them provides a cool umbrella that retains soil moisture and protects the young plants until they are strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. Watering the plants regularly at the base during dry periods helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped water sits around them in low or heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots firm and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni emɔ amɛ lɛ bɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with natural or approved sprays protects the leaves from damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ yellowfeemɔ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: It is best to wait until two or three heavy, steady rains have thoroughly soaked the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting in fully moist soil ensures seeds germinate fast without drying out in the heat.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ehaaa dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Why is it helpful to cut off small unwanted branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni sumɔɔɔ ni eshiɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Trimming extra or dead branches opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can circulate freely. Good airflow reduces humidity around the pods, preventing diseases like black pod rot from spreading.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine loo egboi lɛ, ebaagbele tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa. koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni no haa helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: If I add double the recommended amount of fertilizer to my farm, will my crops yield twice as much food?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ fata he lɛ, Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa fe nakai toi enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer can burn the roots and scorch the leaves, which harms or kills the plant. Using only the recommended amount gives the plant exact nutrients without causing chemical damage.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eshã baai lɛ. ni baanyɛ aye tsei awui loo efite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ falɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ, ni tsofai efiteee amɛ.

english: Why do tiny beetles appear and turn my harvested dried maize into powder inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii je kpo ni amɛtsake mi-abele ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ amɛfee powda yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Those insects are grain weevils that lay eggs in grain stored with too much moisture or left unsealed. Properly drying your maize to a low moisture level and storing it in airtight bags starves the insects of air and stops them from spoiling your harvest.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji ŋmaa ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa ni akɛto ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ni ashi ni akatsi mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni okɛto vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller harvests even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential plant food, root space, and sunlight from your crops. Even with abundant rain, crops growing alongside weeds cannot get enough nutrients to build big tubers, pods, or grain heads.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tso niyenii ni he hia, shishifãi gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ jwɛi ahe lɛ hu nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee bulbs agboi, pods, loo dumɔwui ayitsei.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight and dry out fast. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a living umbrella that shields the young cocoa leaves from harsh sun and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are typically caused by leaf-eating pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Catching this early allows you to spray appropriate organic or recommended controls into the whorl before the pests destroy the central growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ baa, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures are too high or moisture is lacking because the extreme heat prevents proper pollination. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo hulutsoo be ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa haa fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ esaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt during the hot afternoon but stand up straight again by evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ ni ja ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: Pepper plants temporarily drop their leaves during high afternoon heat to cut down on water loss through transpiration. As long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will bounce back once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni faaa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba be mli ni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with many leaves but produce small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to focus their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of root development. Reducing nitrogen and ensuring balanced soil nutrients encourages the cassava to send food down into growing big roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ama baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni ekɛ ehe akpã gbee Ebaatsirɛ ŋmei lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii amaje shishifãi wuji ni miida lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to build chlorophyll, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores leaf greenness and crop strength.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V-shape mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee klorofil. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni eha tso lɛ hu aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the next season's crop yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into plant food in the soil. When their roots decay, they leave behind natural nitrogen fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji eshishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot in the ground instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot when planted upside down or in waterlogged soil with poor drainage. Sticking the stems firmly into well-drained soil with the bud nodes pointing upward allows roots and leaves to sprout easily without trapping excess water.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ fĩ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daa oya ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain forces them to fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in smaller bunches. Pruning the extra shoots so that only two or three strong stems remain allows the main plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain kome he Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni eshi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which fuels tuber growth underneath the soil. Keeping vines upright on stakes also keeps the foliage away from damp soil where fungal rot and diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi ja lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ akashɛ he.

english: Officer, why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off whenever the rain falls too heavily?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can physically wash away the small flowers from cocoa trees and discourage pollinating insects like midges from visiting them. Excess moisture also creates a high humidity environment where fungal diseases, such as Black Pod, quickly infect and destroy young flowers and tiny pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo fɔfɔi bibii. kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ni etsi kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii tamɔ midges lɛ anaa koni amɛkasara amɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ hu haa shihilɛ mli fɛ̃i babaoo baa. Fungal helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. oya oyai

english: Does heavy rainfall mean my cocoa farm will yield more crop, or can too much rain actually hurt my harvest?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo. Aloo ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: While crops need water to survive, too much rain can harm your harvest. Continuous heavy downpours leach nutrients out of the soil beyond the reach of roots, cause waterlogging, and create damp conditions that spread diseases like Black Pod across your cocoa farm.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ. ekɛ nu baa ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni gbɛɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji eshwaa o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water sits on my farm field for many days after a big rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water pools on the soil for too long without draining, it starves the roots of oxygen, preventing them from feeding the plant and causing the leaves to turn yellow and weaken.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Hɔmɔ miiye shishifãi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he. Enɛ haaa amɛha tsei lɛ niyenii. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni efee blɛoo.

english: If the rain suddenly stops for a few weeks in the middle of the rainy season, will my young cocoa trees die?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ otsii fioo komɛi. Ani mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ baagbo?

english: Young cocoa trees have short, delicate roots that dry out easily during sudden dry spells. However, you can save them by spreading dry grass or fallen leaves around their base to trap moisture in the soil until the rains resume.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa trukaa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua amɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi ni oookɛshwie amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Konii ni akɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my soil wet for my crops when the rains become light or stop earlier than usual?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ faaa loo ekpaa mra fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: You can practice mulching, which means covering the bare soil around your crop stems with dry grass, crop residue, or cocoa husks. This layer acts as a shield against the sun, stopping soil water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. tso shishifã ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli tso mli fãi loo kookoo shishifãi Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: What simple thing can I construct on my land to store rainwater in the ground so my crops don't suffer during short dry spells?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ nugbɔ nu baato shikpɔŋ? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii akapiŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: You can dig small, shallow retention trenches or pits along the gentle slopes of your farm. When heavy rain falls, these trenches catch the running water and slow it down, allowing it to soak deep into the soil where crop roots can reach it later.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu loo bu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ dalɛ bibioo atsu nii yɛ gɔji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa Nɛkɛ ŋshɔkei nɛɛ buaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo. Ha ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni sɛɛ mli lɛ tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers leave large permanent trees standing inside their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shiɔ tsei wuji ni hiɔ shi daa yɛ amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Large shade trees shield delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight during dry periods, reduce temperature stress, and drop leaves that decompose into rich organic manure, helping the soil retain water better during dry periods.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Ha hulutsoo be mli haomɔ aba shi ni eha baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do you recommend pruning off extra branches from my cocoa trees before the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to flow through the farm. This helps wet leaves and cocoa pods dry faster after rain, making it much harder for destructive fungi to grow and spread.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tsei lɛ ashishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai ni efɔ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akɛ amɛbaada ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my crop when the early rains are very light and unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu tsei? Be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ waaa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba?

english: It is safest to wait until the ground gets thoroughly soaked by a few continuous days of rain rather than planting after the very first short rain. Planting in dry or barely moist soil can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if the rain stops for several days.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kuku lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Is it a good idea to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rainstorm arrives?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, putting fertilizer down right before a heavy storm is wasteful. The strong surface runoff from heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away into streams before your crop roots have a chance to absorb it.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani ahum wulu ko baa lɛ ji shikafitemɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ.

english: When soil gets flooded with excessive water, the roots cannot breathe and lose the ability to take up nitrogen from the ground. This lack of nitrogen causes the lower leaves of the maize plant to turn yellow.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni faaa nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: If your crops from the previous season grew very slowly, produced small yields, or had pale light-green leaves, your soil is likely low in nutrients and needs organic manure or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwo nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Ehaaa yibii fioo loo eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ awo mli.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This extra nitrogen feeds the maize crop, helping it grow stronger without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni etee hiɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Ye obua ni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin and fall over when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the plants stretch tall and develop weak stems that easily break in strong winds.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fãa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop broad leaves that provide natural shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Curled and patterned yellow leaves on cassava are caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this infection.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kasava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Weeds have deep and aggressive root systems that quickly absorb surface moisture and nutrients faster than young crop seedlings, allowing them to sprout and spread rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the officer instead of using saved seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases and yield higher harvests. Saved seeds lose these strong traits over time, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too hot or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant drops the flower before a fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and rot inside the barn after a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji ni efite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛkɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage when it is put away before being fully dried. High internal moisture allows fungi and insects to multiply quickly inside the grains.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji ajie dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo oya yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will do better on my farm than the traditional seeds I usually save?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ daa lɛ?

english: New high-yielding or hybrid seeds are specially bred by agricultural researchers to withstand local pests, resist common diseases, or grow faster. However, they may require specific planting distances, adequate soil fertility, or proper water to reach their full potential compared to older local varieties.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi etsɔ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, akɛni helai ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ loo amɛdaraa oya hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ ebaabi ni amɛdu he ko pɔtɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nu ni sa koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which it needs to grow green leaves and strong stems. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the roots waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ baai eŋɔli ni miida kɛ tsei ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or too much water. It can also mean the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus, which the plant needs to turn flowers into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. prolonged drought or there is too much water It could also mean the soil is lacking nutrients like phosphorus, which plants need to turn flowers into peppers.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl inward during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural defense behavior. Plants curl their leaves to hide their surface area from the hot sun, which helps them hold onto water and prevent drying out until the heat cools down.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛtee hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa amɛgbi kɛyashi la ni tsoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant the seeds close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them correctly gives each plant enough space and resources to grow full, healthy produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtaoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will growing groundnuts together with my cassava help or hurt my crop yield?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ duɔ lɛ baaye abua loo ebaana miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts alongside cassava is beneficial because groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which feeds nearby plants. Meanwhile, cassava takes longer to grow tall, allowing groundnuts to mature without being shaded out.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmei mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni no haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, Cassava heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛɔ. Ha ŋmeii lɛ adara kwraa ni ŋmeii akawo amɛmli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ he ni mibua mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot year after year allows these pests and diseases to build up in the soil and attack your new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii kɛ helai nɛɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua onibii heei lɛ.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking branches on my cocoa or cashew trees help them bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cocoa loo cashew tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that suck water and food away from the rest of the tree. Clearing these extra branches allows more sunlight and air into the tree center, encouraging the plant to put its energy into flowering and fruiting.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Niji ni fata he nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell if tiny holes in my crop leaves are caused by insects or by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ bu lɛ ji bibioo? yɛ mitso lɛ baai ni kooloi loo tsei ahe helai kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Insects typically bite or chew physical holes with clear edges out of the leaves. Diseases usually cause discolored spots—like brown, yellow, or black patches—that dry out and crumble into holes over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ŋmɔɔ loo amɛyeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni tsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ediŋŋ baa, ni egbiɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even if they are not directly shading them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe po lɛ?

english: Even if weeds are shorter than your crops, their roots grow fast and steal large amounts of water and fertilizer directly from the soil, leaving your main crop starved of the nutrients it needs.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ yɛ kuku fe otsei lɛ moŋ, shi amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa yɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why is raw cassava juice harmful if it spills into a nearby stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei fɔ ni ahoko lɛ yɔɔ oshara kɛji eho kɛtee faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally contains compounds that turn into cyanide when the roots are crushed. When raw cassava liquid enters small streams, this natural toxin reduces oxygen in the water and can quickly kill fish and other living water creatures.
ga: Nɔ ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni tsɔɔ cyanide kɛji akɛ atswa shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmei mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔ ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ho kɛtee faa bibioo ko mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa nɛɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa nu lɛ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ebaanyɛ egbe loo kɛ nu mli nibii krokomɛi. oya oyai

english: Why does some cassava from my farm taste bitter while other tubers taste sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmei krokomɛi ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants produce a defense chemical to protect themselves from pests. Varieties with high levels of this chemical taste bitter and require careful processing, while sweet varieties produce very little of it and are safe with simple cooking.
ga: Cassava tsei feɔ tsofai ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Tsofai srɔtoi ni tsofa nɛɛ fa babaoo yɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ, ni kɛ́ ahoo amɛ mlɛo lɛ, amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it good practice to plant my cassava right on the bank of a stream?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ faai ahe lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa?

english: No, cassava tubers need well-drained soil. Planting too close to a stream causes waterlogging, which starves the roots of air and leads to root rot before the tubers can mature.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko tsɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when the soil near the stream stays soaked in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ he lɛ mli ewo nu lolo lɛ?

english: When soil is constantly flooded, plant roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly. The yellowing of the leaves is the plant's way of showing it is suffocating from lack of soil air.
ga: Beni nu eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ. Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhe niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji gbɛ kome ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ etsɔɔ akɛ eefo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.
