english: Why does cassava manage to stay alive during the dry season when maize dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni ŋmei egbi lɛ?

english: Cassava is a naturally drought-tolerant crop. During dry periods, it stores water and nutrients deep in its underground tubers, allowing it to survive long hot spells that kill shallower-rooted crops.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plant drop off when hot dry weather starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism. By shedding older leaves, the cassava plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preserving precious moisture in its main stem and roots.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Cassava tso lɛ haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ baai momoi ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa hiɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ amli.

english: Can I pour leftover liquid from processing raw cassava onto my garden soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafɔ nu ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to avoid pouring raw cassava processing liquid directly onto crop soil. The acidic and toxic nature of the raw juice can burn plant roots and kill beneficial soil microbes.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛfeɔ ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni oooshwie shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nu ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ acid kɛ poison lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni egbe sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: How does water contaminated with chemicals from upstream affect my farm downstream?
ga: Te nu ni tsofai ni jɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ewo mli lɛ saa faa lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water carrying toxic substances from upstream can soak into your soil, harming the helpful insects and microorganisms that keep your soil rich and potentially contaminating your food crops.
ga: Nu ni hiɛ tsofai fɔji ni jɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ kooloi kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui, ni ebaanyɛ efite niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do cassava tubers rot quickly in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil encourages fungi and bacteria to grow. These organisms attack the soft, water-filled tubers underground, causing them to decay before you can harvest them.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Nɛkɛ bɔɔ nii nɛɛ tutuaa ŋmeii bibii ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Ha amɛgboi dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why should I wait a few days after heavy rains before harvesting my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ dani makpa ŋmei?

english: Right after heavy rains, cassava tubers soak up extra water, making them watery, low in starch, and quick to spoil. Waiting allows the tubers to stabilize so you harvest dry, high-quality roots.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ, ni no haa efeɔ nu, ŋmei fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni efiteɔ oya. Mɛmɔ baaha yitso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni egbi.

english: Can I safely use water from a nearby muddy river to water my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ni mli ewo muji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe koni mikɛha aduawai?

english: If river water is heavily polluted or muddy from activities like mining, it carries harmful chemicals and heavy silt that can coat plant leaves, block root intake, and make crops unsafe for people to eat. Clean water sources are essential for growing healthy, safe crops.
ga: Kɛji faa lɛ mli nu lɛ mli ewo muji waa loo etsɔ muji kɛjɛ nitsumɔi tamɔ shika tsuru tsaa mli lɛ, tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ sũ ni tsii ni baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ baanyɛ ahi mli. tsiɔ shishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ naa Ni enɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ. Nu ni mli tse jɛɛhe he miihia kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up even after I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi ni amɛgbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: If the water you use contains harmful chemicals or high salt levels, or if the soil is too compacted to hold water properly, plant roots become damaged and cannot absorb the moisture, causing the leaves to wilt despite watering.
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ nu ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli loo ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Tso shishifãi efite ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu po.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and protecting the cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eshɛɔ hulu lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use to protect themselves from excessive heat or water loss, but it can also be a sign of sap-sucking insects like aphids or a plant virus weakening the crop.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine loo nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Shi ebaanyɛ efee kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo tso mli helai ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ hu he okadi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking important nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become damaged or waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why does my maize grow tall stalks but produce small, incomplete cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abele yɛ tsei kakadaji shi eyɛ tsei bibii ni yeee emuu lɛ?

english: Maize needs extra phosphorus and good soil nutrition when forming ears; if the soil is poor or plants are planted too close together, the plant spends energy on height rather than building full cobs.
ga: Abele he miihia phosphorus kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai krokomɛi kɛji eefee toi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo adu tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaama ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant cassava in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to multiply in the ground over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsake amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures are too high or water is inconsistent, as a survival mechanism to preserve energy when conditions are tough.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Eji gbɛ ni wala tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ hewalɛ he yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are the bases of my yam stems turning black and soft near the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shishitoo lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Soft, black stems usually indicate root or stem rot caused by excessive wetness or fungal infection in the soil, which cuts off the flow of nutrients between roots and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji ediŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi loo tsei lɛ amli fitemɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ kpaɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves get large black spots and dry up from the bottom moving upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji wuji ni amɛgbi kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Black Sigatoka, a common fungal leaf disease that spreads quickly in humid weather, destroying leaf area and reducing the size and weight of the plantain bunches.
ga: Enɛ ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji ŋmeii ahe hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ he okadi. Efiteɔ baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa plantain ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi.

english: Strong sunlight causes heat stress and burns young crop leaves when plants lack shade or adequate water, which slows down their growth and damages the plant.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do some crops survive the harsh afternoon sun easily while my cocoa trees suffer so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi joɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa foi oya yɛ be mli ni mi cacao tsei lɛ naa amanehulu waa lɛ?

english: Different crops have varying natural heat tolerances; while some plants have thick leaves or deep roots built for full sun, cocoa trees need shade and extra care to survive heavy heat.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ he tsuishitoo srɔtoi. Shi kɛlɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ baai ni mli tse loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ama koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Shi hulutsoo kɛ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ he miihia kookoo tsei koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Can putting dried grass around the bottom of my plants help protect them from the harsh sun?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: Yes, this practice is called mulching; it acts as a blanket over the root area, keeping the soil cool and stopping the sun from evaporating water away from the crop's base.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How does pouring water directly at the base of my crops help them during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Watering at the base places moisture right where the roots can absorb it, reducing water loss from evaporation caused by the hot weather.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it good to water my crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane mli. Ani hulu ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ hi?

english: It is better to water early in the morning or late evening because strong afternoon heat evaporates water before roots can absorb it, and hot surface water can stress the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ejaakɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii.

english: Why does the soil around my cocoa trees dry out so quickly even after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mikookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight on exposed soil bakes the surface and rapidly pulls moisture out through evaporation if there are no shade trees or soil covers to protect the ground.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ ni akɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ bɛ lɛ,.

english: Is it better to plant only cocoa on my land or mix it with other crops like plantains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikome too makwɛ cocoa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛ tsei krokomɛi tamɔ plantain afutu mli?

english: Mixing cocoa with fast-growing food crops like plantain creates a healthier farm environment because the taller crops provide temporary shade and extra moisture while giving you extra food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo futu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii krokomɛi hu.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from water stress before they completely wither?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ he dani amɛgbi kwraa?

english: Crops show early signs of heat stress by curling their leaves, drooping stems, or losing their bright green color long before they dry up completely.
ga: Tsei jieɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he okadii mra kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. tso ni egbee shi loo ehiɛ su ni mli tse lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani egbiɔ kwraa.

english: What steps should I take on my farm when I hear a warning about an coming severe dry spell?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ minu kɔkɔbɔɔi ni kɔɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni miiba lɛ he?

english: Early warnings allow you to prepare by clearing weeds that compete for water, applying mulch around crop bases, and setting up shade or irrigation before the dry heat hits.
ga: Kɔkɔbɔɔ ni akɛhaa mra lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni osaa ohe kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni kɛ nu he akaŋ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani hɔmɔ latsaa lɛ baashɛ.

english: Can a cocoa tree bring back new leaves after losing them all to a severe dry season?
ga: Ani cacao tsei baanyɛ akwɛ baai heei ekoŋŋ beni amɛfite yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ko mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If the root system survives by getting minimal water at the base, cocoa trees can sprout new leaves once rain or irrigation returns, though prolonged dryness will reduce fruit yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishifã lɛ hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni enine shɛɔ nɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Cacao tsei baanyɛ akwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi moŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to produce food that grows the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch more sun and stay away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow green leaves, or that the soil is overly waterlogged and roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔlii ni yaa hiɛ Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the ground around the base of the stem will start cracking as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi fãmɔ be mli ni yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers dry up and drop off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures become too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium and boron needed for fruit setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant's sap and transmitting plant viruses, or by severe heat and dry conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli

english: Leaving too many shoots (suckers) forces the mother plant to share its nutrients with all of them, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures bigger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ agba niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha plantains lɛ afee wuji ni amɛhe afee mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to yield much smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds take those resources, your crops do not get enough food to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni jwɛi yeɔ nakai nibii lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed on the tender young leaves inside the plant's central funnel (whorl), which slows down the crop's growth if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli (whorl), ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves up to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the legumes die, that trapped nitrogen stays behind in the soil as free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei gboi Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes all the plants grow thin, weak, and tall, resulting in small cobs or no yield at all.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ shwiili, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii loo amɛwoɔ yibii kwraa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and off the hot, damp ground, which also protects them from leaf diseases and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ mli kɛjɛ hei ni edɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai kɛ fitemɔ hu naa.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my pepper plants help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that shields the ground from the hot sun. It keeps the moisture in the soil, keeps the root area cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, protecting young cocoa trees from heat and preserving soil moisture during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up their pollen, making pollination impossible. When a flower cannot be pollinated, the plant drops it to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haaa pollination aba mli. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Cassava root rot happens when water gathers around the roots for too long, especially in heavy soils during heavy rains. The waterlogged soil starves the roots of air and allows destructive fungi to infect and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: These caterpillars, often Fall Armyworms, target the central funnel of the plant because it is soft, nutritious, and moist, while also shielding them from direct sunlight, rain, and predators while they feed.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛji Fall Armyworms lɛ, kwɛɔ tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo. Amɛhe wa ni amɛhaa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe hu beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can reach them, leaving your crops starving even with sufficient water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Ha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ kɛji amɛyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea to the soil will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛdu tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the exact same nutrients every season. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Cassava stems should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space ensures the roots under the ground have room to expand into big, thick tubers without competing for water and food.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mita kome. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ aná tsu lɛ mli ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Koni eha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni efee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my corn plants and leaving dark dirt behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by a pest called Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the central leaf whorl during the hot sun; spraying recommended organic neem extracts or approved insecticides early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji neem ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye enɛɛmɛi anɔ.

english: Should I burn all the dry weeds and bushes after clearing my farm land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egbi lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie he ni adu nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning kills beneficial soil organisms and burns away natural organic matter that feeds your soil. It is better to clear the weeds and leave them to rot naturally into mulching material that traps moisture and enriches the earth.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie jwɛi lɛ ni oha amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does water disappear so quickly when I water my tomato plants in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has loose, large particles, so water drains right through it before plants can drink. Mixing organic compost or decomposed animal droppings into the soil helps it act like a sponge to hold water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic compost loo kooloi aŋmei ni egbo futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsu nii tamɔ sponji, ni eha nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Wait until two or three heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil, usually at the start of the rainy season. Planting in dry soil causes the seeds to dry out and rot, while waiting too long wastes critical growing time.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi. Mɛɛmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ be babaoo ni akɛduɔ nii.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from extreme sun heat, lack of water, or soil lacking nutrients like potassium. Watering regularly during hot dry spells and applying compost stops the flowers from dropping.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ mli. Nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni fɔfɔi akagbee shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn ears are fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani abele toi lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This usually happens because the soil is running out of nitrogen, or heavy rain has washed the plant food deeper into the ground where the young roots cannot reach it. Adding compost or fertilizer supplies the nitrogen needed to keep the leaves green and growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa tsei aniyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop big leaves that shade the young cocoa plants from the harsh sun and help retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai agboi ni haa hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shɛɛɛ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yams produce food for their underground tubers through their leaves. When the vines climb high on stakes, the leaves spread out to catch more sunlight, producing more energy to swell the tuber beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ niyenii haa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ babaoo.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into pepper fruits when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee ŋmɔtɔ yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the air is very dry, pepper plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy and water. Providing shade or watering them during dry spells helps protect the flowers so they turn into fruits.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the land for too long, the roots drown because there is no air, allowing bacteria and fungi in the damp soil to cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baafo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa muawai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops whenever the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local soil and rainfall. They quickly drink up water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops, which is why early weeding gives your crops the space and food they need to catch up.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni ekɛ ehe ewo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni aduɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛhi shi.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the central leaves of my young corn and eating holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. The adult moths lay eggs inside the folded center leaf of the maize because it is tender and protected, and the hatching caterpillars feed on those soft leaves as the plant grows.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii ji enɛɛmɛi. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana Ŋmeii ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni abuɔ he Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ nakai baai bibii lɛ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: If I only have a small land plot of about 120 square meters, can I still harvest enough vegetables to sell?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko, ni dalɛ aaafee mitai 120 lɛ, ani manyɛ makɛ aduawai ato lolo koni mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yes, small farm spaces can yield plenty of food if you plant with proper spacing, use vertical supports for climbing crops, and feed the soil with manure so every single meter produces healthy, high-yielding plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ bibioo ko baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɛ ni sa du. Kɛ nibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ atsu nii kɛkwɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni mita fɛɛ mita awo tsei ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do tomato plants planted too close together grow tall and thin but produce very few small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ tomatoi fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When tomatoes are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into growing big fruits, the plants stretch tall to reach light, leaving little food left for fruit growth.
ga: Beni tomatoi lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tomatoi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai wuji lɛ, Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛha la abote mli. Niyenii fioo ko pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding organic manure helps the plant regain its green color and grow stronger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller crop harvests every year even though I plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its nutrients when the same crop is planted year after year without a break. Rotating your main crop with leguminous plants like groundnuts or cowpeas restores vital nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ he ehiaaa lɛ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my crop plants growing very tall with many leaves but yielding very little grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo shi amɛwoɔ dumɔwui fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Plants grow excessive leaves instead of grain when there is too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium in the soil. Using a balanced fertilizer encourages the crop to spend its energy producing fruits and seeds rather than just foliage.
ga: Tsei woɔ baai babaoo yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ awo yibii kɛ dumɔwui. Jeee baa kɛkɛ

english: Excessive water trapped in heavy soil cuts off air to cassava roots, causing them to drown and rot. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ atsɔ jɛmɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turn dark and squishy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent allows the tomato plant to absorb calcium properly from the soil.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my plantain crop falling over even when there are no strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miigbee shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or banana root weevils eat away the root system underground. Using clean planting suckers and treating the planting hole prevents these pests from destroying the roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana shishifãi lɛ ye shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ sucker ni he tse tsu nii ni okwɛ dumɔ bu lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap underneath the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil or mild soapy water keeps these sucking pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie tsei anɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaŋɔ enɛɛmɛi kɛya.

english: Why do caterpillars quickly devour my young maize leaves as soon as the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, known as fall armyworms, multiply rapidly in warm, moist weather when fresh green shoots appear. Checking your fields early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides while the caterpillars are still tiny prevents severe leaf loss.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii ni kpɛɔ lɛ je kpo lɛ Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ afɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree flowers keep dropping off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from heat, direct sunlight, or lack of soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the delicate flowers and gives the young cocoa trees time to establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha cacao tsei bibii lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛdara.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and dying long before it is time to harvest the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani be ni akɛkpaa ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up prematurely mainly due to fungal diseases that thrive when wet leaves touch the moist soil. Staking your yam vines onto tall wooden poles keeps the foliage off the ground and improves air flow to prevent fungal rot.
ga: Nɔ titri ni haa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa kɛji baai ni efɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: How can I know if a chemical I buy for my cocoa farm is safe and approved to use?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni miheɔ kɛhaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii?

english: You should check if the chemical is tested and approved by the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana (CRIG). Only chemicals passed by CRIG are guaranteed to be safe for cocoa trees and will not ruin your crop quality.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji akɛ Cocoa Nibii Amlipɛimɔ Nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ Ghana (CRIG) lɛ eka tsofai lɛ ekwɛ ni ekpɛlɛ nɔ. Tsofai ni CRIG ekpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha kookoo tsei. Ni efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is CRIG, and why must my cocoa chemicals be tested by them?
ga: Mɛni ji CRIG ni mɛni hewɔ mikaa mi-cocoa tsofai lɛ mikwɛɔ?

english: CRIG stands for the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana. They test cocoa fertilizers and pesticides scientifically to ensure they effectively control pests without killing your cocoa trees or leaving bad chemical residues.
ga: CRIG ji gbɛi kuku ni akɛtsɔɔ Cocoa Nibii Amli Taomɔ Nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ. Amɛkaa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ amɛkwɛɔ yɛ jeŋ nilee mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛyeɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee kookoo tsei lɛ loo amɛshiŋ tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: What should I check when a trader brings farm chemicals directly to my farm to sell?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ mli kɛ́ jarayelɔ ko kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ebahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Always look for official CRIG approval seals and labels on the package. Never buy unlabelled or hand-mixed chemicals from travelling traders, as unverified mixtures can destroy your cocoa crop.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ CRIG naatsii kɛ odaseyeli wolo ni yɔɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kaahɔɔ tsofai ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo ni akɛ niji futu mli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni fãa gbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite o-cacao tsei lɛ.

english: Why is it difficult for a farmer like me to tell if a farm chemical is good quality just by looking at it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa okwaafoi tamɔ mi akɛ amɛaale kɛji tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ amɛkwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical liquids and powders look similar on the outside regardless of how they were made. Because you cannot see the active ingredients or hidden toxins with your eyes, relying on official scientific approval is the only way to confirm quality.
ga: Yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ, nu kɛ powda tamɔ nɔ kome ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni afee amɛ aha lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, onyɛɛɛ okɛ ohiŋmɛii ana nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Jeŋ nilee mli hegbɛ ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni akɛaafɔ lɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ amaa nɔ mi akɛ nɔ ni hi ji nɔ ni hi.

english: Can I mix different farm chemicals together on my own to save time when spraying my cocoa?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni jɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ afutu. okɛ ohe afee ekome koni okɛ be akafite ni okɛshwieɔ kookoo nɔ?

english: No, mixing chemicals on your own is risky because combining wrong ingredients can cause dangerous chemical reactions. This can weaken the medicine or create harmful compounds that damage your cocoa trees.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni okɛfutuɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko ni yɔɔ oshara aba. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ekɛ nibii ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ afite o-cacao lɛ aba.

english: Why do some chemicals sold in the local market work well while others ruin my cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fiteɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Chemicals vary widely in how they are made and mixed. Approved formulas are carefully balanced to fight diseases, while fake or untested chemical mixtures often contain harmful ingredients that destroy cocoa leaves and pods.
ga: Tsofai lɛ yɛ srɔtoi babaoo yɛ bɔ ni afee amɛ kɛ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ amɛ ahaa lɛ mli. Akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ toɔ he jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ helai srɔtoi awuu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ji amalei loo ni akako amɛ akwɛ lɛ mli nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ kookoo baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: People say some farm chemicals contain poison that can ruin my cocoa. Is this true?
ga: Akɛɛ mi akɛ tsofai komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji tsofai fɔji ni baanyɛ afite mi-kookoo lɛ. Ani enɛ ji anɔkwale?

english: Yes, using uncertified or wrong chemical mixtures can introduce harsh toxins to your farm that poison cocoa trees, cause leaves to burn, and render your harvested beans unusable.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni naa wa aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tsofa fɔŋ kɛha cacao tso lɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni okpa lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees dry up after I spray them with new chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ beni mikɛ tsofai heei eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Trees dry up when sprayed with unapproved chemicals or harsh mixtures that contain toxic substances. Using chemicals certified for cocoa ensures the spray kills pests without burning or drying out the tree.
ga: Tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni mli wa ni tsofai fɔji yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛfee kookoo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ni eshãaa tsei lɛ loo ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Why can't I just buy any general pest spray from the store for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji generic lɛ kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli kɛha mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are sensitive to specific chemicals. General pest sprays designed for other crops may contain strong toxins that harm cocoa pods or contaminate the beans, which is why cocoa requires specially approved formulas.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ nuɔ tsofai komɛi ahe waa. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni afee aha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsofai fɔji ni naa wa ni yeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ awui loo efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ kookoo lɛ aná fɔmula krɛdɛɛ ko ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: How do safe chemical sprays protect my cocoa pods without hurting the tree itself?
ga: Te tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ni eyeee tso lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Approved cocoa chemicals are specifically formulated to target only crop pests and diseases. When properly tested, they destroy pests while remaining completely safe for the tree's leaves, trunk, and pods.
ga: Afee kookoo tsofai ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛtutua kooloi kɛ tsei ahe helai pɛ. Kɛji aka lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaakpãtã kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha tso lɛ baai, eshishifãi, kɛ eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do strong winds keep snapping my crops in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fiteɔ midumɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Strong winds put heavy pressure on tall or thin crop stems, especially when rainfall makes the soil loose. If plants do not have deep root support or strong stems, the force of the wind breaks them at their weakest point.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa baa tsei ashishifãi ni kɛlɛ loo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo shishifã ni mli wa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baakumɔ tsei yɛ hei ni amɛgbɔjɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my tall crops from breaking when heavy winds blow across my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛkakumɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can plant tall trees or hedges around the edges of your farm as windbreaks to block strong gusts, or mound soil around the base of your crops to give their roots stronger anchor support.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei kakadaji loo gbogboi obɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he koni etsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔnei ni buɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa lɛ he. loo muji ni abua naa ni bɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe koni amɛshishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why are my crops breaking off during storms while my neighbor's crops stay standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite yɛ ahum ko mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kã shi lɛ?

english: Crops usually break if they are planted too close together, lack key soil nutrients like potassium that strengthen stems, or belong to varieties that are not bred to withstand strong local winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei fãa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nibii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ hewalɛ. aloo amɛfata tso srɔtoi ni atsɔko amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: How do I know the best time of year to plant my seeds so the weather does not ruin them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Timing depends on local rain patterns; planting right after the rainy season fully establishes gives crops enough water to build deep roots before strong seasonal winds or dry spells begin.
ga: Be ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eshɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani be mli kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too early in the season?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ mra tsɔ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Planting too early can cause seeds to dry up in hot soil if rains pause, or leave young seedlings vulnerable to early seasonal winds before their root systems are strong enough to hold them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akpa nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ko. Aloo shi tsei bibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ amɛ.

english: Do I really need to buy expensive agrochemicals before I can start planting on my land?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni mahe agrochemicals ni jara wa dani mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: While chemical weedkillers quickly clear land, you can also use cleared weed mulch, animal manure, or compost to prepare healthy soil and lower your initial planting costs.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii hu atsu nii ni okɛwaje shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛba shishijee dumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ shi.

english: Why do my crops seem to struggle to grow unless I apply chemical fertilizers right at the start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ja mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ?

english: Overworked soil often lacks essential nutrients needed for early growth. Initial fertilizers provide a fast dose of nitrogen and phosphorus that seeds need to build strong roots and green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sũ ni atsuɔ he nii fe nine lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii haa nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ oya koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Is there a way to clear my land for planting without spending so much money on weedkillers?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ajie shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔwui ni afiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, manual clearing, growing cover crops that suppress weeds naturally, or practicing crop rotation helps control weed growth over time without depending entirely on chemical spray.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii ni aduɔ nibii ni akɛhaa nibii ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Aloo, nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why is it so hard for me to make a good profit after spending money to plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa yɛ be mli ni mifite shika kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: High upfront costs for seeds and chemicals, combined with crop damage from wind or pests, reduce your total harvest yield and leave less crop volume to sell for profit at the market.
ga: Shika ni fa babaoo kɛha dumɔwui kɛ tsofai ni akɛfataa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he. Ehaa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi. kɛ gbɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni ana sɛɛnamɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: What causes tall crops like maize or cassava to bend over completely before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa? Ani ebɔle ehe kwraa dani ekpa?

english: This is known as crop lodging, which happens when plants grow too fast and weak due to excess nitrogen, poor root anchoring, or exposure to heavy wind and rain late in their growth cycle.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɛɔ shi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei dara oya tsɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ tsɔ yɛ nitrogen babaoo hewɔ. Shishifãi ni ekpɛtɛɛɛ he jogbaŋŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ dalɛ be lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and scorching in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava to shield their leaves and retain moisture until their roots are deep enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Enɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baa mli bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Maize leaves curl inwards during hot, dry hours as a defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, which helps the plant trap moisture and prevent excessive water loss.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni edɔ, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ baa lɛ hiɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa.

english: Does it matter which way up I insert cassava stems into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, te ehe hiaa ha tɛŋŋ akɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the buds to grow downwards before turning up, which wastes the plant's energy and results in weak stems and very small tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yitsei bibii waa.

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the damp soil where fungal diseases thrive and exposes maximum leaf area to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce larger subterranean tubers.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa yɛ ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper plants often shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering, as the stress prevents proper pollination and forces the plant to conserve resources.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔnyɛɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nibii ni eyɔɔ lɛ ato he.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack open on the sides right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when plants receive a sudden surge of water after a dry spell, causing the inside of the tomato to swell faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ ná nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ mli lɛ fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: How does planting groundnuts in my field help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and grow so slowly even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal essential nutrients and fertilizer from the soil before your main crop can absorb them, leaving your plants starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ hɔmɔ aye tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Excess suckers drain energy and nutrients away from the main plantain tree, resulting in smaller bunches of fruit if they are not thinned out.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji akɛ afeee lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them stay green during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective blanket that keeps the ground cool and stops soil water from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Mulch (mulch) ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an important food crop plants need to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or leaves the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii tso ko ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ adara waa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. If the plant gets too hot or dry, it sheds its flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto nu he ni ehi shi.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven—such as letting the soil dry out completely and then heavy watering later.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, ashwieɔ nu babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle full, harsh sun and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them creates a cool environment and protects them until they grow older.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ nakai tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that grow near the surface instead of deep into the earth. When heavy fruit bunches grow on top, the tree becomes top-heavy and needs support stakes so strong winds do not pull the roots out of the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ko ni mli wa kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo ni ehe baahia ni aye abua lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer that helps your maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: It is best to water early in the morning while the sun is low. Morning watering lets the soil absorb moisture before heat causes evaporation, and it prevents hot water from scalding delicate roots.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni hulu la lɛ faaa lolo lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani dɔlɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni otsi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack because the expanding tubers are pushing upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso ni mli elɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The virus weakens the plant's ability to make food, resulting in smaller root yields.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and bent instead of straight and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend and twist when they hit hard ground, stones, or thick roots underneath the soil. Making high, soft soil mounds or ridges allows the tubers to stretch and grow straight easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli tse. Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbalaa amɛhe oya ni amɛdaraa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it true that oil palm trees grow better in southern Ghana than in the northern regions?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ mu tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ fe kooyigbɛ?

english: Oil palm trees require heavy and continuous rainfall throughout the year, which is abundant in southern Ghana. Northern Ghana has a longer dry season, making it difficult for oil palm to produce good yields without heavy artificial irrigation.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni eyaa nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ayɛ babaoo yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ. Ghana kooyigbɛ hei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa mu tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaawo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni akɛfee nibii ni tsii shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Which crops naturally do better in the drier northern parts of Ghana compared to the forest zones?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ kpokpai ni mli egbi lɛ anɔ kɛ akɛto kooi amli kpokpai lɛ ahe?

english: Crops like millet, sorghum, cowpeas, and groundnuts thrive in northern Ghana because they have deep root systems and short life cycles, making them adapted to survive in areas with lower rainfall and high temperatures.
ga: Nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni ewala be kukuoo pɛ. Enɛ haa amɛ nyɛɔ amɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛ hi shi yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo.

english: What crops can I plant during the dry season in Ghana so I do not stay idle for months after my main harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni mahi shi diŋŋ. nyɔji babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ

english: You can plant short-duration vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, okra, or leafy greens near riverbanks or valley bottoms using bucket irrigation, as these crops mature quickly and fetch high market prices during the dry season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, okra, loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa loo ŋshɔkei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nɛɛ daa oya, ni amɛjara wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: If my farmland is resting for a few months after harvest, should I leave the soil empty or plant a green crop?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he jɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ani esa akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo madu tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli?

english: It is better to plant cover crops like leguminous beans or mucuna rather than leaving the soil bare. These plants protect the soil from burning in the sun, prevent soil erosion from winds, and add nitrogen back into the dirt for your next main crop.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo mucilagina. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. ni okɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha onibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize seedlings turn yellow and grow tall but weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa shi amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The young plants stretch upward rapidly to get light, making them thin, while the lack of nutrients turns their leaves yellow.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ tsɛɔ oya koni amɛha la lɛ abote mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ bibii, yɛ be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wither and die right after I move them from the nursery bed to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplanting shock if moved during hot sunshine or if their young roots are broken. It is best to transplant them in the late afternoon when the sun is cool and water them immediately so they settle gently.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ baaná he sɛɛ kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ fã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei yɛ shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la ni mli ejɔ kɛ nu yɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eha ehi shi blɛoo.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted oil palm tree to start producing palm fruit bunches?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ mu tso yibii akui?

english: Improved hybrid oil palm varieties usually take between three to four years after being transplanted into the main field to produce their first harvestable fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni ji hybrid oil palm henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛtee shishijee ŋmɔji amli lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛná amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa farmers plant plantain suckers on the same field with their newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi komɛi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛdu kookoo tsei heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool environment young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural self-defense action. The plant curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss and prevents the plant from drying out completely.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo, ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as intense heat, lack of soil water, or poor nutrients like phosphorus. Ensuring regular watering and good fertilizer application helps the flowers stay and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esaaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Applying well-rotted manure or an appropriate fertilizer like NPK gives the crop the nutrients it needs to regain its rich green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa tamɔ NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow big and healthy on one part of my land but stay small and weak on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miidara ni amɛhe wa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? shi eji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli

english: Soil depth and quality vary across a field. Cocoa trees need deep, soft soil that retains moisture; areas with hard, rocky, or waterlogged ground restrict root growth, preventing the tree from absorbing enough food and water.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Cocoa tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa, tɛi loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the stems compete for sunlight, ground space, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper distance allows the roots enough space under the ground to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting plantains next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu kookoo tsei yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tsei ni adu ehee

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and conserving soil moisture while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hɔɔŋ ni he hia ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or a sudden lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist during dry spells and using mulch around the base helps the plant retain its flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning brittle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by hot dry winds or tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies. Protecting the plants with regular watering and applying organic neem oil spray controls insects and keeps leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Buu tsei ahe kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha amɛ daa kɛ organic neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni akɛkudɔ kooloi bibii ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I am buying in the local market are good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ hi akɛ adu?

english: Healthy seeds look clean, whole, and uniform without insect holes or dark spots. You can test a small batch in water; seeds that sink are usually healthy and ready to germinate, while seeds that float are dry or damaged inside.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse, amɛye emuu, ni amɛhe tse po, ni kooloi abu loo he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka kuu bibioo ko okwɛ yɛ nu mli - bei pii lɛ dumɔwui ni ebote nu mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ baagbi loo amɛbaafite.

english: Where can I get certified improved seeds that yield better than the ones I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maná dumɔwui ni asaa he ni awo he odaseyeli ni woɔ yibii kpakpai fe nɔ ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ?

english: Certified seeds are available from registered agricultural input dealers or local extension officers. These seeds are specially selected and tested to resist diseases, handle climate changes, and produce higher harvests than saved grains.
ga: Ayɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli shweremɔ nitsulɔi adɛŋ. Ahalaa nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he nitsumɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe ŋmaa ni ato

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow small and crooked while other farmers get long, heavy yams?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi naa sweet potato kakadaji ni tsii?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to push down easily as they develop. Building high, loose mounds mixed with organic manure allows the tubers to expand straight and reach a heavy, full size.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsi amɛhe oya be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dalɛ fa ni tsii.

english: Why does my cassava crop take much longer to mature during a dry year compared to a rainy year?
