ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli kɛ akɛto afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava plants slow down their growth process during drought to save energy and survive the dry heat. Once steady rains return, the roots resume absorbing nutrients and building up starch normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ daa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ ekoŋŋ ni amɛbaafee starch bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and soil moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds once the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain, as the soil underneath is still dry and hot. Wait until you receive two or three steady rains so the soil is deep-moistened, ensuring your seeds germinate without drying out.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure around the base will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei ahe baai lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo kooloi amli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni bɔleɔ he lɛ baatsu nii Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. You can control them by regularly checking your field early and applying recommended insecticides or neem leaf extractions directly into the funnel (center leaves) of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni odu lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ daa kɛ mra nɔ. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo tso lɛ funnel (teŋgbɛ baa) lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are white powdery spots spreading on my pepper plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miigbɛ eshwa mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are a sign of powdery mildew, a fungal disease common during humid periods. You can manage it by trimming overcrowded leaves to improve airflow and applying a suitable organic or copper-based fungicide.
ga: Powder ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji powder mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fɔɔ baa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ baai ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ooofo mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni ji organic loo copper fungicide ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain leaves lose water quickly in hot, dry winds. Covering the soil around the base of the plant with dry leaves or straw (mulching) helps hold moisture in the soil and prevents the plant from drying out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi mli. Mulching around the base of the plant with dry leaves or straw (mulching) helps retain moisture in the soil and prevents the plant from drying out.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick leaves but producing very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded too closely together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of expanding tubers underground. Proper plant spacing helps tubers grow large.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your crops properly gives every plant enough space to build strong stems and produce good yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tso ni mli wa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: It is best not to save hybrid seeds for replanting because hybrid varieties are bred for one-time performance. Replanting saved hybrid seeds will result in uneven growth and a much lower harvest yield.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ hybrid dumɔwui lɛ akato koni akɛdu ekoŋŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, afɔɔ hybrids kɛha nitsumɔ shikome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛhe saji awo mli ni aduɔ lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ afee ekome ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How do I know when my yams are fully mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. This shows that the plant has finished growing and transferred all its nourishment into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eda ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yams grow small and twisted when I plant them in hard, stony soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo ni efiteɔ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are root tubers that need soft, deep soil to expand easily. When planted in hard or rocky ground, the growing tuber struggles to push through the soil, causing it to become stunted, crooked, or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato ji shishifãi ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji adu yɛ hei ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ lɛ Bulbs ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ, ebɔleɔ ehe, loo egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young yam vines early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally aggressive and will quickly steal sunlight, water, and nutrients from your young yam plants. Early weeding gives the yam leaves enough light to feed the growing tuber under the ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli basabasafeemɔ ni ebaaju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛ o-sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl as a self-protection mechanism against heat stress. Rolling up reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant hold onto its water so it doesn't dry out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why does cassava manage to survive long dry spells while my other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava has very deep, tough root systems that reach moisture stored deep underground. It can also shed its leaves to save energy during dry periods and sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ hu koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ baai heei hu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines on tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight to feed the tuber below. It also prevents leaves from rotting on the damp soil and protects the plant from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ hu fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat destroys tomato pollen, which stops flowers from getting fertilized. When flowers cannot form seeds, the plant drops them to conserve water and energy until cooler weather arrives.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Kɛ fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ Tsei baaha amɛ nu koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help the crops I plant there next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with beneficial soil microbes to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This leaves the soil naturally rich in plant food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni tsei niyenii yɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen or is receiving too much water. The plant moves essential nutrients to its new top leaves, causing older bottom leaves to weaken and drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo miiná tso lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain often doesn't soak deep enough into the dry soil. If seeds germinate and the rains stop for a few days, the young sprouts will dry up and die before the real rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ eboteee shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly when I store them in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still living organisms that produce heat and moisture. In a closed room without air movement, heat builds up and fungus grows quickly; storing them off the ground in a shade barn with good airflow keeps them dry and safe.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ ji bɔɔ nii ni hiɛ ka lolo ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Yɛ tsu ko ni aŋã ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa ni ŋmɔtɔ daa oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing harmful rot-causing fungi in the soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects that feed on the plant sap. It can also happen when the weather gets extremely hot and dry, forcing the plant to curl its leaves to reduce water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers around one plantain stem creates heavy competition for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. This weakens the main stem and leads to very small plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ plantain tso lɛ he lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ plantain tsei bibii waa baa.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by tiny midges (insects), or when the tree suffers from heat and water stress. Spraying harsh chemical insecticides while the trees are flowering can also kill off the beneficial insects needed for pollination.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa kɛha pollination lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea plants focus their energy on leaf growth instead of flowers. Tiny pests called thrips might also be attacking and feeding on the young flower buds before pods can form.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ thrips lɛ baanyɛ atutua ni eye fɔfɔi bibii bibii lɛ dani pods lɛ afee.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their small fruits before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Dani ebaashɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their young fruits when soil moisture changes drastically—such as going from very dry conditions to sudden flooding—or when afternoon heat becomes too intense for the plant to sustain the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa, tamɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa mli kɛyashi nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ yibii amli.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that builds large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off damp soil, which prevents leaf diseases and produces bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ foliar helai anaa ni eha sweet potatoes wuji aba.

english: Why is it better for me to water my garden vegetables early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ obɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi fe shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Watering in the cool morning gives roots plenty of time to absorb water before the heat of the day. In the hot afternoon, much of the water evaporates before roots can take it in, and hot wet leaves become easy targets for diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be babaoo ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ lɛ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ bafeɔ helai ni helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that give young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ehaa baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them off wet soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow and thin before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow big, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni eha toi lɛ adara ni ehe wa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year when I plant the same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time to recover or replenish itself.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land before planting other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather and on farms where trees are planted too closely together with poor air movement.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. kɛ ŋmɔji ni adu tsei yɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil with good drainage. When heavy water sits in the soil for too long, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji muji lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients needed during flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why does my oil palm take several years before it starts producing any fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi aduawai akui feemɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees spend their first three to four years developing deep roots and a strong trunk so they are sturdy enough to support heavy fruit bunches later in life.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa baa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua aduawai akui ni tsii sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no big trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and soft root systems. Direct, harsh sunlight burns their foliage and dries out topsoil rapidly, so they require shade trees or plantains to shield them and trap moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa ebaai lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe ni eha amɛhe ajɔ amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged and cannot feed. Nitrogen is the main leaf-building food for plants, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye nii. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni akɛfeɔ tsei ahe baai. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which feeds the hungry maize plants naturally and improves soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot underground when heavy rain falls for too many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the field for too long, the soil becomes waterlogged and starves the roots of oxygen, allowing soft-rot fungi to invade and spoil the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise us to cover the soil around crops with dry grass or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops solar heat from drying out the soil, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wood sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high off the damp ground toward the sun, allowing the leaves to catch sunlight evenly to make food for growing big tubers while protecting them from soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ baai helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu naa.

english: Why is my plantain sucker taking so long to produce a bunch compared to my neighbor's field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekɛ ŋmeii baa kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain growth slows down if the sucker is planted too deep, lacks sufficient water, competes with weeds, or grows in poor soil. Proper spacing and adding manure around the base speed up leaf development and fruiting.
ga: Plantain dalɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ adu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ Gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into small shapes and refusing to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe bibii bibii ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites hiding underneath. As they suck the plant juice, they deform the leaves and can spread viruses that stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo amɛshishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. beni ekɛ tso nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Ebaatsake baai lɛ ahe mfoniri ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni tsiɔ dalɛ fɛɛ naa lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the stem before turning into small green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators to fertilize the blooms before they wither.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Aloo pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii dani amɛgboi lɛ bɛ.

english: How do simple weeds in my farm actually reduce the final harvest of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds act as silent thieves in your field. They aggressively drink the ground water, consume applied fertilizers, and block sunlight from reaching your crops, causing your main plants to stay small and yield less.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo yɛ oyale mli. Amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hiɛdɔɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ atsu nii. ni etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or water. When maize doesn't get enough nitrogen, it cannot make green chlorophyll, causing older leaves to turn yellow starting from the tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu. Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ náaa nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, enyɛŋ ekɛ klorofil eŋɔli aba. Enɛ haa baai momoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ naagbee.

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for your maize plants while giving you an extra harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn tsei lɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: If I harvest seeds from my best maize plants this year, will they grow into equally strong plants next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli afi nɛɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ tsei ni he wa tamɔ nɛkɛ. Kɛfata he yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli loo daabi?

english: Not always. Many improved or hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in the first generation. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation often grows unevenly, produces smaller cobs, and loses the strong traits of the parent plant.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛto ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmeii bibii aba ni eha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ sui ni mli wa lɛ afite

english: What makes the improved cassava varieties from extension officers different from my traditional local varieties?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei henɔ ni atsake lɛ ni jɛ extension officer lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ shishijee maŋ lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ he?

english: Improved cassava varieties are bred by scientists to resist common diseases like Cassava Mosaic Virus and produce bigger roots faster, allowing you to harvest early and get higher yields compared to older local varieties.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ ŋmeii mosaic virus lɛ anɔ kunim. ni ehaa shishifãi wuji oya Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa oya ni onáa yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are some of my papaya trees producing plenty of flowers but never growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees have sexes. Male papaya trees only produce flowers with pollen to fertilize other trees, but they cannot form fruit themselves. You need female or bisexual trees in your field to get papayas.
ga: Papaya tsei kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii Papaya tsei hii woɔ fɔfɔi pɛ ni pollen yɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei krokomɛi amli. shi enyɛŋ ewo yibii kɛjɛ ehe Esa akɛ oná tsei ni ji yei loo tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni onyɛ okwɛ papaya.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the branches without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If the flowers drop, it usually means there were no midges around to pollinate them, or the tree is suffering from severe water stress.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ gbɔmɛi komɛi bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination, loo tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ ni naa wa.

english: Leaf curling is a natural self-defense trick tomatoes use to shrink their surface area and save water during extreme heat. If the leaves uncurl when the evening cools down, the plant is behaving normally.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ ehe ni tomato kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni ekɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi kɛji edɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifee enii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms right when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikome beni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dried-out soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha amɛhao. shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition makes them stretch high for sunlight instead of growing thick stalks and large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛmɔ hulu lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit when planted under thick shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains need direct sunlight to make energy for fast growth. Under heavy shade, the plant grows slowly and delays producing a fruit bunch because it lacks enough light energy.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio ni amɛbaaha aduawai awomɔ asɛɛ afo yɛ la hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen fertilizer out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This feeds the soil naturally and helps your maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-ŋmã lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cassava plants turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots because of poor drainage. Adding well-decayed manure around the plants helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Obaanyɛ oná tsei lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need partial shade because direct, harsh tropical sunlight damages their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Keeping larger shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain creates a cooler mini-climate that protects young cocoa during its early growth.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize turn light yellow and dry up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow, and when there is not enough in the soil, the plant pulls whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to keep its new upper leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my pepper plant flowers falling off instead of turning into pepper fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is a sudden dry spell. The plant does this as a survival response to preserve water and energy until weather conditions become favorable again for bearing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba trukaa. Tsei feɔ enɛ akɛ wala yibiiwoo hetoo koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha yibiiwoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and soft if I leave them in the ground after the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains begin after a dry spell, the cassava plant rapidly absorbs water and draws stored starch out of its roots to grow fresh green leaves. This process reduces the starch content in the roots, making them watery and prone to rotting.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli koni ebaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ nu ni esumɔɔ ni egbo.

english: Why does spear grass make my maize grow tall and thin without developing strong cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ebɔko lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep, aggressive roots that steal water, nitrogen, and nutrients from the soil before your maize can reach them. Because the grass also blocks light, the maize stretches upward to find sunlight instead of spending energy on thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, nitrogen, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmãa baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ hu tsiɔ kane lɛ naa. Abɛi lɛ shwie shi koni ena hulu la lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji baatsu nii lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl tightly upward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves inward during peak heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface directly exposed to the sun. This natural defense helps the plant conserve water and prevent moisture loss through evaporation.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni latsaa waa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ajie baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up completely when it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The yellowing and drying of yam leaves is a natural sign that the plant has reached full maturity. It means the vine has finished transferring all its food energy down into the underground tuber and has completed its growth cycle.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ egbi ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eda. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ egbe eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa, ni egbe edalɛ be lɛ naa.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help my soil grow better maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmei kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with friendly microbes in the soil to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni feɔ naanyo lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot much faster during the continuous rain than in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, wet conditions. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores from the damp ground onto low-hanging pods, allowing the rot to spread quickly across the farm.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep inside wet clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen as well as moisture to sprout. Heavy wet clay holds a lot of water and very little air; if seeds are planted too deeply, they suffocate and rot before their shoots can reach the soil surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: This yellowing usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize refreshes the soil fertility naturally so your next crops grow much better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kwraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide in the central funnel of the maize plant. Applying neem oil spray or carefully dropping clean wood ash into the leaf funnels can help kill or drive away these caterpillars.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse shwie baai lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni egbe loo eshwie nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled tomato leaves are often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a leaf curl virus while feeding on the leaves. Controlling these insects using soapy water sprays or neem oil helps keep the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ loo neem fɔ tsu nii kɛye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from high heat, dry soil, or pests. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and adding mulch around the stems helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ amli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Tsoi ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make food for big tubers to grow underground. Staking lifts the vine off the ground to catch light and keeps the leaves away from wet soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ la nɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akanáa helai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Too many young shoots compete directly with the main plantain stem for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Leaving just one main stem, one medium shoot, and one small sucker ensures large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. Shi tso wulu kome pɛ, tsei ashishi 1 ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ tsei ashishi bibii 1 kɛha tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crop with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass—called mulching—keeps the soil cool under hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and burn in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily damaged by direct sun. Planting quick-growing shade crops like plantain or banana next to young cocoa creates a umbrella that protects the seedlings until they mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantain loo banana, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the base stem becomes thick and woody, and the ground around the plant begins to crack open, which typically happens 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tso. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn even forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: When bottom leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, your maize is hungry for nitrogen. The plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top, showing that the soil needs nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or urea.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers without them turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can nourish. Many drop off due to stress like dry spells, lack of shade, or lack of tiny pollinating midges that need moist leaf litter under the trees to survive.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha amɛ niyenii. Mɛi babaoo shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ bei, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii bibii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. ni biɔ baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ koni ehi shi

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water stays around the roots for too long in soaked ground, rot-causing organisms thrive and suffocate the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain excess water.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaahã shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller even though the mother plant looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: A plantain plant shares its food and water with all the small shoots (suckers) growing around its base. If you do not cut back extra suckers to leave just one strong shoot, the mother plant gets exhausted and produces smaller bunches.
ga: Plantains kɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashwɛ bo. Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni ebaagbala ewo kui bibii amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes tomato pollen dry up, so the flowers cannot form fruit properly. When pollination fails because of high temperatures, the plant drops the unfertilized flowers to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on young shoots, or a virus they spread. As they suck the juices, the leaves grow unevenly and curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Beni enuɔ nu lɛ Baai lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over so easily when a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over if their roots are weak from shallow planting, poor soil nutrition, or stem borer insects eating the inside of the stalk. Heap soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) to give them stronger support.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔ kɛjɛ dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ mli. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii Aloo kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli. Okɛ sũ ato tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) koni ekɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni mli wa aba.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce the food that builds big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo naa tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the tiny green cocoa pods on my tree turning black and shrinking before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree realizes it has more pods than its water and nutrients can support. It can also be caused by black pod disease during wet weather.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ eji hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ le akɛ eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe nu kɛ niyenii ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua lɛ. Black pod hela hu baanyɛ aha eba yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of bushy green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Giving cowpeas too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally create their own nitrogen, so they need phosphorus instead to make flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ekɛ fɔsfɔs afee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii moŋ.

english: How do I know if the maize seeds I buy at the market are certified and safe to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ nɔ ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni ehi akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for official certification tags or seals from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA) on the bag. Certified seeds are officially inspected and treated to guarantee high germination rates and protect young plants from early pests and diseases.
ga: Taomɔ tag loo stamp ni tsɔɔ akɛ odaseyeli ni jɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MOFA) lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ nɔ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant seeds brought in from outside Ghana, or will they fail in our local weather?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ aba lɛ? Aloo ebaaye omanye yɛ wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds brought from outside Ghana may not tolerate local heat, rainfall patterns, or native pests unless they have been officially tested and approved for Ghanaian soil. It is always safer to use varieties inspected and certified by local agricultural authorities.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ maŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. ja aka lɛ akwɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni aha he odase akɛ eji Ghana shikpɔŋ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ekwɛ mli ni amɛha he odase lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do my plantain plants grow well next to my young cocoa trees, but my cocoa dies when I clear all the tall plants away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ? Shi mikoo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunlight and heat when they are small. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide living shade that protects young cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any fruit during the dry heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers as a natural survival reaction when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes abruptly from dry to wet. Providing steady watering and light shade during extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala shihilɛ mli nifeemɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green and build strong stems, which can be restored by adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa. Abaanyɛ aku sɛɛ afee enɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnut puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni efo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when we get heavy rains for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing around the roots for too long, the soil becomes waterlogged, cutting off oxygen and causing fungal rot to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and weak with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows stems to grow thick and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars suddenly eating the central leaves of my young maize plants right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ trukaa beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that multiplies rapidly when warm weather meets new rainy season growth. They target the tender central leaves, so applying approved control measures early prevents them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be hee lɛ mli dalɛ kpe. Amɛtutuaa teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaatsi he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if a chemical spray for farm pests is safe to use on crops that my family will eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Check the chemical container for an official approval label from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) or Ministry of Agriculture. Safe, certified agrochemicals will list exact dosage instructions and specify a safety waiting period between spraying and harvesting.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli koni ona woji ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛ Shihilɛ He Buu Nitsumɔhe (EPA) loo Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ. Agrochemicals ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni awo he odase lɛ baaha gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ atsu he nii aha lɛ he, ni ebaatsɔɔ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food they need to build green leaves. It can also happen if the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of leaf movement from wind and insects that assist in pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the base helps stabilize the plant so it can hold its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa hao tso lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa Aloo baai lɛ tsiii amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ebuaa kɛ pollination lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ muji awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ fɔfɔii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight little cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the undersides of new leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. Spraying the leaves early with soapy water or neem oil helps clear these pests before they damage the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Amli ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during damp, rainy weather. You can protect your cocoa by pruning extra leaves to let sunlight and air reach the trunk, and by removing infected pods immediately so the fungus does not spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Obaanyɛ obu kookoo he kɛtsɔ baai krokomɛi ni ooofo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine yɛ bu ni akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing center of the plant. Applying recommended biological treatments, neem extract, or targeted pesticides directly into the center funnel early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ hei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli, neem mli nu, loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ mli lɛ wo tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown from the edges before the plant even yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ dani tso lɛ woɔ yibii po lɛ?

english: Early leaf drying in plantains often points to leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka or a lack of water during dry spells. Cutting off infected leaves and burying them, along with piling mulch around the base of the plant, keeps moisture in the soil and slows the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni gbɛ́ɔ mra yɛ plantains mli lɛ tsɔɔ baa he helai tamɔ Sigatoka loo nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛ muji afu amɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha helai aje shishi.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests that love maize to build up in the field. Swapping maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil and starves maize pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa mli kooloi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my cassava when cassava is already a tough plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle ŋmei lɛ he lɛ, be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ?

english: Even though cassava is hardy, weeds compete for the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that the cassava roots need during their early months. Clearing weeds early allows the roots to swell into large, heavy tubers instead of thin, woody ones.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei mli wa moŋ Shi jwɛi lɛ hu kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei shishifãi taoɔ yɛ shishijee nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ he akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Mohu ɔ, yi ɔ ngɛ tsɔe nɛ e ngɛ kaa tso.

english: Why should I wait for the major rainy season to settle before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds need reliable, steady soil moisture to germinate and grow strong root systems. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die in dry soil if the rains take a break for several days.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ adalɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo.

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is too hard and compact for the root to push downward easily, or when tiny pests in the soil attack the tubers. Planting yams in high, soft mounds of loose soil allows the tubers to expand smoothly without resistance.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi mlɛo. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua yitso lɛ Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa.

english: Why are the rains not coming at the usual times I have always planted my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ ebaaa yɛ be ni sa mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsei edu be nɛɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Climate change is causing weather patterns to shift unpredictably, making traditional planting months unreliable. Farmers now need to rely on local weather updates and wait until soil moisture is consistent before sowing seeds.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ kusum naa nyɔji ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Amrɔ nɛɛ ehe miihia ni okwaafoi lɛ kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji anɔ ni amɛmɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa dani amɛdu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my crop seeds die in the ground even when I plant them right after the first heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ miigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Unpredictable weather often creates 'false starts' where a single rainstorm is followed by weeks of intense heat. Young roots dry out and die because the soil loses moisture before the real rainy season establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ kɛ ‘amale shishijee’ baa he ni nugbɔshiimɔ kome ni nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa.

english: How can I protect my crop soil from drying out too fast when the rain stops unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ he koni ekagbi oya tsɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves, palm fronds, or grass—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the ground and shields crop roots during unexpected dry spells.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ baai ni egboi, ŋmei tsei, loo jwɛi aha onibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa beans if rain falls on them while I am drying them outside?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni migbiɔ amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Unexpected rain on drying cocoa beans introduces moisture that causes mold to grow and rot the beans inside. Moldy beans lose quality and fetch much lower prices at buying centers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ gĩɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ ni egboɔ yɛ kookoo yibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nuts ni mli ewo muji lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛheɔ jara ni baa shi kwraa kɛjɛɔ jarayeli hei.

english: Is it harmful to harvest my cocoa pods during a week when rain falls continuously?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ abaakpa kookoo ŋmeii yɛ otsi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ mli?

english: Harvesting in heavy rain keeps the pods wet, making them spoil faster and spreading fungal spores across your farm. It is best to wait for brief dry periods or move harvested pods under shelter right away.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa egboɔ oya ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni omɛ be kuku ni nu bɛ. Aloo tsimɔ pods ni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ shishi.

english: How can I keep my harvested crops dry during months when it rains without warning?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mikpamɔ lɛ agbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli ni kɔkɔbɔɔ ko bɛ he?

english: Building raised drying racks covered with clear plastic sheets allows air to flow beneath your crops to dry them while keeping sudden rainfall from wetting them.
ga: Kɛ́ ooofee tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii ni awo nɔ ni akɛ plastic ni mli tse ehà nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi koni egbi amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when there is sudden, heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa lɛ?

english: Excess rain and cool moisture create the ideal environment for Black Pod disease fungus to spread rapidly. Pruning excess branches lets wind and sunlight into the farm to dry out the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod hela lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before they turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Sudden shifts between hot dry weather and sudden rain cause weather shock. When stressed by unpredictable climate changes, cocoa trees drop flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ teŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa baa. Yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my fertilizer before my crops can use it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mi-ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Sudden, heavy rain creates surface runoff that carries away loose fertilizer sitting on top of the soil. Burying fertilizer in small ring trenches around plant roots stops it from washing away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo bu bibioo ko ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekaho.

english: Why should I grow crops like plantain alongside my cocoa when the weather is hard to predict?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ? Be mli ni ewa akɛ aaatsɔɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee aha

english: Mixing crops gives you a safety net; if unpredictable rainfall ruins the harvest of one crop, resilient food crops like plantain or cassava can still provide food and income.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa onáa shweshweeshwe shihilɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ Niyenii ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii kɛ shika aha lolo.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their yellow flowers back into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are unique because after the flower is pollinated above ground, the plant grows a stem called a peg that buries itself into the soil, where the actual groundnut pod develops underground in the dark.
ga: Peanuts yɛ srɔto ejaakɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe sɛɛ. Tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean pods lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ duŋ mli.

english: Why do groundnut plants struggle to yield well in heavy clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil gets too hard when dry, making it difficult for the groundnut pegs to push into the ground to form nuts, and harder to pull out without breaking the pods during harvest.
ga: Shikpɔji ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee ni tsii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa tsɔ kɛji egbi. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmeii. ni ewa akɛ abaajie ni akuuu ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: What will happen if I plant my groundnuts too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When groundnuts are crowded, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to leafy growth with smaller, fewer pods underground.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii ni faaa lɛ daa.

english: Can I grow groundnuts under tall crops like mature cassava or heavy shade?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ yucca ni eda loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ashishi?

english: Groundnuts require full, direct sunlight to convert energy into healthy pods; planting them in heavy shade causes weak stems and very low yield.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmeii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛtsake hewalɛ amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi waa.

english: Why do crops like maize grow better when I plant them on a field where groundnuts grew last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil, making the land richer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are dark brown spots appearing on my groundnut leaves and making them drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miije kpo yɛ mi-peanut baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: This is a common fungal disease called leaf spot, which spreads in wet weather and reduces the plant's leaf area, stopping pods from filling out completely.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf spot. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ baa shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli baai eyiɔ obɔ kɛ baai.
