english: Why do some of my groundnut pods turn out completely empty without seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean pods lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty pods, often called 'pops,' usually occur when there is a lack of calcium or moisture in the soil during the time the subterranean pods are filling up.
ga: Pods ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ fɔɔ baa kɛji calcium loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ bei ni shikpɔŋ shishi pods lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time that my groundnuts are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the lower leaves begin turning yellow and shedding, and when you open a sample pod, the inside of the shell shows dark brownish-black veins.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele sample pod lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli jieɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ-diŋŋ kpo.

english: Why do many groundnut pods break off and stay in the dirt when I pull the plant up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo fãa ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ́ migbala amɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: If the ground is too dry at harvest time or if you wait too long after maturity, the stalks attaching the pods to the main root become weak and snap easily underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo omɛ be kakadaŋŋ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ tso ni kɛ pod lɛ kpãa shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni efoɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts develop mold and smell bad when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ mli tsɔi ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts rot or spoil in storage if they are bagged before being fully sun-dried, creating a damp environment where damaging mold and toxins thrive.
ga: Peanuts baafite loo ebaafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani hulu lɛ mli egbi kwraa. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ tsofai fɔji baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli lɛ baa

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up during dry spells, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsĩ naa?

english: Maize leaves roll up to prevent water from evaporating off their surfaces during extreme heat. Applying mulch, such as dry leaves or grass, around the base of the plants keeps the soil cool and retains soil moisture much longer.
ga: Abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akajɛ ŋwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni edɔ waa lɛ. Mulch tamɔ baai ni egboi loo jwɛi ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farmland make my crops stay green longer than using chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔji be kakadaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure builds up organic matter in the soil, which helps it hold onto water and release nutrients slowly over time, while chemical fertilizers provide a fast boost but easily wash away during heavy rains.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii buaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he oya shi efɔseɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpea or beans alongside my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them with cassava acts as a natural fertilizer, feeding the soil and improving overall crop yields while reducing weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cassava ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yams get smaller and weaker every year when I plant them on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating yams with legumes or letting the land rest allows soil nutrients to naturally recover.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsake loo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni ehaa ehe baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cover crops like mucuna help suppress stubborn weeds on my field?
ga: Te mucilaginous cover crop ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni egbe jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cover crops grow rapidly and form a thick leafy canopy over the ground, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds underneath so they cannot germinate or grow.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Koni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekakwɛ̃ loo eda

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings get scorched and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ mi-shade tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need soft, filtered light because intense, direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture they depend on during their early growth stages.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia kane ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli tse. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ. ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ ni damɔ enɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms without forming fruit when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants and stops proper pollination, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy. Providing light shade and watering during cooler hours helps plants hold their blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ekpaa pollination. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. La kɛ nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they can even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering that prevents the plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil. Keeping soil moisture steady helps prevent this issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be ni haaa amɛná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do crops on demonstration farms look so much healthier and yield more than crops on my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Demonstration farms combine multiple best practices—such as certified seeds, precise spacing, timely weeding, integrated soil care, and proper water management—which work together to maximize crop productivity.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ babaoo fata he, tamɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni afee ekome kɛ nu he nitsumɔ ni sa Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow with tiny holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Holes and yellow leaves on maize are usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves, or because the soil lacks nitrogen. Early spraying with recommended insecticides or adding nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baa. aloo akɛni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie nɔ mra Aloo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot or when the plant experiences water stress. Irregular watering and excessive nitrogen fertilizer can also cause the plant to shed flowers instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my pepper leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity during the rainy season create ideal conditions for fungal and bacterial diseases to spread on foliage. Proper spacing between plants helps air circulate and keeps the leaves dry.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni baa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ anɔ. He ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when it rains heavily for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot absorb oxygen in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is my farm soil becoming hard like concrete after growing maize on the same spot for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome afii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same heavy-feeding crop continuously removes nutrients and organic matter that keep soil soft. Rotating crops with beans or groundnuts and adding animal manure restores soil softness and fertility.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ kooloi aŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up quickly if the rains stop for just one week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize has shallow root systems that stay near the surface, so when topsoil dries out during rain breaks, the plant quickly runs out of water, especially while flowering.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nu sɛɛ foɔ tsei amli oya. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and hot winds, which dry them out. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baaha kookoo tso lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I get very small tubers even when I make big mounds for my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ yitso bibioo nɛkɛ? Ni mifee ŋmɔtɔ agbo ko?

english: Large mounds alone do not guarantee big yams if the seed yam is diseased, planted too close to other crops, or if the soil lacks potassium and phosphorus needed for tuber development.
ga: Pile agbo pɛ haaa aná nɔmimaa akɛ sweet potato agbo ko baaba kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ emɔ hela. Aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning them allows the main stem to produce larger, healthier bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Foomɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ tsei wuji, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do small insects destroy my harvested maize inside my storage room after just two months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kpata mi ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils multiply quickly if maize is stored while still moist or in a room that is warm and damp. Thoroughly drying maize in the sun until it is hard before storing reduces insect damage.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo loo yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛto lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade trees or plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects the young plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Shade tsei loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, dark, and humid conditions. Pruning dense tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods regularly prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hela ni ji black pod hela baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli koni hulu lɛ aba mli, ni akpaa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if the small caterpillars in my maize farm are Fall Armyworm, and what damage will they do?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm kɛ mɛɛ fitemɔ amɛmiiba?

english: Fall Armyworms hide inside the center funnel of the maize plant, leaving ragged holes on the leaves and producing sawdust-like waste. If untreated, they destroy the main growing point of the maize plant and drastically reduce your harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ teɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Eshiɔ bu ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Efiteɔ hei titri ni ŋmãa tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants look twisted, crumpled, and yellowish instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite, ni egbɔjɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Twisted yellow leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or passed through infected stem cuttings. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties for planting keeps your crop healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii loo kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ Kɛ okɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I build high soil mounds before I plant my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, well-aerated soil to expand and grow long and thick. High mounds protect the tubers from rotting by keeping excess rainfall water from pooling around the roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. Koni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ buɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni etsiɔ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Which plantain suckers should I cut from an old plant to start a strong new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ tso momo ko mli koni maje ŋmɔ hee ni mli wa shishi?

english: You should choose 'sword suckers', which have broad bases and narrow, spear-like leaves. They grow faster, establish stronger roots, and produce larger bunches than 'maiden suckers' with broad leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘Sword Bud’ ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Amɛ daa oya. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ofee kui wuji fe ‘tsofai bibii’ ni baa lɛ mli kwɔlɔ

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn dark and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called Blossom End Rot, which happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent throughout the growing period prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni baa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: What damage happens to my land if I clear my bush by burning it every year before planting?
ga: Mɛni fitemɔ baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie mi-hedgerow lɛ kɛtsɔ la ni mishãa daa afi dani miduɔ nii lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning bush kills important soil organisms, destroys organic plant matter, and exposes nutrients to rain wash. Over time, annual burning turns your soil hard, dry, and poor for crops.
ga: Bush ni ashãa lɛ gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa waa. efiteɔ tsei amli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa nugbɔ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa ni ashãa daa afi lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni egbiɔ, ni ehiii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnut help improve the soil for my next crop season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, leaving these root residues in the ground naturally fertilizes the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Shishifãi ni eshwɛ nɛɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak if I do not weed the field during the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwieee amɛnɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the first four weeks, young crop roots are small and easily overwhelmed by fast-growing weeds competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Early weeding gives your crops the best chance to build strong roots and foliage.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ ji bibii ni jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade plants like plantains or cassava around them to block the harsh heat, keep the leaves cool, and retain moisture in the soil while their roots develop.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni ebɔle amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the food it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soaked, waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on high soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same field with my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the ground through their roots. This feeds the soil and helps the nearby maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ waa ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines with wood instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for growing large tubers underground. Tying the vines to stakes lifts the leaves into the air and sun while keeping them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ fĩ tso ko he lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know when the soil is wet enough to sow my seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until after two or three good rains have soaked deep into the ground. Planting too early after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die when the ground dries out again.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and causing the plants to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mild soapy water solution or neem leaf oil stops the pests and allows fresh leaves to unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem baa mli fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa ni eye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛje kpo.

english: Why should I remove the extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stem fight each other for food, light, and water. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only the strongest main stem, which results in larger and heavier bunches of fruit.
ga: ŋmeii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Plantain kome yɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii, la, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ daraa ni amɛtsiiɔ.

english: Why do farmers recommend covering the soil around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ awo mli lɛ? Mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi ŋmɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot sun so it stays wet longer. It also stops weeds from growing and turns into rich plant food as it breaks down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the land I have in Ghana is good enough to plant mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ mango tso nɔ?

english: Mango trees need deep soil that lets water drain easily so the roots do not rot. You can test your land by digging a small hole and pouring water into it; if the water disappears within a few hours without standing like a pond, the soil is generally good for mangoes.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni haa nu hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo. Obaanyɛ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni oootse lɛ nɔ. no sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ nu mli Kɛji nu lɛ laaje yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli ni efeee tamɔ ŋshɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha mango.

english: Why is it better for me to buy grafted mango saplings instead of planting seeds directly from a sweet mango I ate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miheɔ mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ? Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛjɛ mango ni ŋɔɔ ni miyeɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Trees grown directly from seeds can take up to ten years to produce fruit, and the fruit might not taste like the original one. Grafted saplings act like shortcut plants that produce sweet, high-quality fruit in just two to three years.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii nyɔŋma dani amɛwo yibii. Ni ekolɛ aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔŋ tamɔ shishijee tso lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso ni tsɔɔ gbɛ kuku, ni ewoɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I space my young crop trees when planting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miidu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Crops like mango trees grow very large leaves and wide roots over time. Giving them at least eight to ten meters of space between each tree ensures they do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food.
ga: Tsei tamɔ mango tsei lɛ woɔ baai wuji waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, shi mitai kpaanyɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋma yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How often do I need to water my young fruit trees during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei bibii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young saplings need to be watered about two times a week during the dry harmattan season until their roots grow deep enough. After one or two years, their deep roots can reach underground water and survive on rain alone.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Yɛ afi kome loo afii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ pɛ nɛ.

english: Will cutting off some of the branches hurt my growing tree, or does it help it grow better?
ga: Ani niji lɛ ekomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye mitso ni miida lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning or cutting away dead, low-hanging, or overcrowded branches actually helps the tree. It allows fresh air and sunlight to reach the inner parts of the plant, which keeps diseases away and helps the tree focus its strength on making big fruits.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni shwieɔ shi, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ loo ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibii wuji ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes young mango fruits to turn black and drop off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni haa mango bibii lɛ feɔ diŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa?

english: Early fruit drop and black spots are usually caused by tiny fungal diseases or fruit flies. Cleaning up fallen fruits from the ground and applying safe spray treatments before the tree flowers helps protect the fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ mra kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. loo aduawai amli ŋmeii Tsumɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe afɔ nɔ dani ewo fɔfɔi koni eye ebua ni ebu aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad to let tall weeds grow around the base of my young crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves that steal water and fertilizer away from your young plants. They also hide pests like grasshoppers and bush rodents that chew on the soft bark and leaves of your trees.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ otsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ baai lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Why does my tree produce a lot of flowers, but very few of them turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Flowers need visits from friendly insects like bees to turn into fruit. Heavy rain, strong winds, or spraying chemicals while the tree is flowering can drive bees away or wash the pollen off, preventing fruits from forming.
ga: Fɔfɔi he miihia ni kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ amɛ koni amɛtsɔ aduawai. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ ashwie ŋmeii lɛ loo efɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Can I put fresh animal manure directly around my young plant roots to make them grow faster?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei abɔle he. Ani manyɛ mafolɔ midumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara oya?

english: Fresh animal manure is too strong and hot, which can burn and kill young roots. You should dry the manure and let it rot into dark compost for a few weeks before mixing it gently into the soil around your plant.
ga: Nibii ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi bibii Esa akɛ ogbi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni oha egbo ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii fiofio. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that a fruit on the tree is ready to pick without waiting for it to fall on the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ tso lɛ nɔ yibii lɛ eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ni omɛɛɛ ni egbee shikpɔŋ?

english: Look at the top part of the fruit near the stem; when it becomes full and rounded instead of flat, and the skin changes slightly from dull green to a lighter shade, it is mature enough to pick and ripen safely indoors.
ga: Kwɛmɔ aduawai lɛ yiteŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Beni eyi obɔ ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hewolo lɛ tsake fioo kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli. Ebaafee agbo bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto ni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shia.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or manure can replenish the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ mli awo ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is eating the center of my young maize leaves and leaving broad holes?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni eshi bu ni mli kwɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant's growing center. Early spraying with approved biopesticides or neem extract helps protect the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni abu nibii ni adu lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat stress. Keeping pests away with field hygiene and proper watering helps reduce leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ashishifã aba shi.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves toward sunlight to make food. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, which prevents leaf rot and allows tubers to grow bigger underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni efee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ akafite, ni ebaaye ebua bulb lɛ ni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight for the same sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awuu koni ená hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava cuttings standing upright or laying flat?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu mi-cassava niji lɛ ja loo mafee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting stem cuttings at a slanted or upright angle encourages deep root growth, helping the cassava resist drought and strong winds better than stems buried flat.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ koŋ loo he ni ja lɛ, ebaawo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni enyɛɔ edamɔɔ hɔmɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa jogbaŋŋ fe kɛji akɛ adu lɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off before developing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from dry soil, high temperatures, or insect damage. Shading the trees and keeping soil moist helps blossoms develop into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii amli lɛ kpeɔ. Kɛ́ afee tso lɛ he ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot weather, crop leaves lose water faster than roots can suck it up from the soil. Placing dead grass or mulch around the base of the crop helps trap moisture in the root zone.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi gbohii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he. Tso lɛ shishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper fruits getting black rotten patches on the bottom before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ yɔɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Dark soft spots at the bottom of peppers are caused by blossom end rot, which happens when plants don't get steady water to absorb calcium properly during fruit growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ he ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa koni amɛkɛjie calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in intense sunlight. Providing shade plants like plantains protects them from extreme heat, retains soil moisture, and helps the seedlings establish strong roots during their early growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa yɛ amɛdalɛ mra be mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay dark green so the plant can make big, heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii jɛɛhe titri kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔji wuji ni tsii.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crops receive all the food and water they need to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and shady environments. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunshine and fresh air to dry out the leaves and pods, which stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod rot baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil. This provides free nutrients for your maize plants and improves soil fertility for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa o-ŋmei tsei lɛ yeɔ yaka ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why do small worms hide and eat inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii teɔ shi amɛwoɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer hiding inside the soft, moist center of the plant where they are protected from predators. Identifying them early allows you to apply safe remedies into the whorl before they destroy the main growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ ateŋ he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ he titri ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil moist around the roots with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli fũu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can drink them up. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and waste your money because the plant cannot absorb dry chemicals.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã, ni eji shika fitemɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ tsofai ni egbi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the tiny extra shoots growing on the sides of my mature cocoa trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso ni eda kwraa lɛ masɛi

english: Those extra shoots, often called water shoots or chupons, waste the tree's food and water without growing fruit. Removing them directs all energy into developing larger, healthier cocoa pods on the main branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii loo chupon ŋmeii. Ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ aya yaka ni ewoŋ yibii. Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nine wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots get tough and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are meant to store food for the plant, but as the plant gets older, it converts that stored starch into hard fibers for its own survival. Harvesting at the recommended mature time ensures the tubers remain soft and rich in starch.
ga: Akɛ cassava shishifãi toɔ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ eda lɛ Etsakeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa mli koni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehi shi. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them provides the cool shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ebaaha shade kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wala yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baaha.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers underneath the soil. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, helping the underground yams grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: If too many shoots grow together, they fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil. Removing extra suckers leaves the main stem strong enough to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ plantains akui wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni abele akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and look tired during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ amɛ ni amɛfolɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally closes or droops its leaves during peak afternoon heat to reduce water loss. It is a normal survival behavior, and the leaves will stand up straight again when the evening cool returns.
ga: Cassava baakpa loo ebaagbee shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji wala yiwalaheremɔ mli subaŋ ni sa. Ni baai lɛ baadamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the young leaves. Controlling these pests early stops the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when they lack enough water. Maintaining regular watering and mulching the soil keeps the plant stress-free enough to hold its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ bɛ haomɔ bɔ ni sa koni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my garden egg plants growing lots of tall green leaves but refusing to produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes garden egg plants build leafy stems instead of fruits. Balancing the nutrients helps the plant switch from leaf growth to flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa abɔɔ mli eggplants lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ baa dalɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why is it better to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ooodamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting stem cuttings at a slight slant puts more root nodes below the soil surface, encouraging the plant to form more tuberous roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Can I save the seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give maximum yield only in the first generation. Replanting saved hybrid seeds usually results in weak plants and much smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the key food it needs to grow strong green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients away or left the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my maize stems grow tall and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight. They stretch upward as fast as possible to reach the light, which makes their stems thin and weak, causing them to fall over easily in strong winds.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooogbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet conditions. When tree branches are too thick and shade is too heavy, moisture stays trapped on the pods, allowing the fungus to grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ tso niji lɛ ebɔle tsɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i baakpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. It can also happen when the plant is extremely stressed by heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ tsei amli lɛ haoɔ amɛ waa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and twisted instead of straight and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛtsi amɛhe shi moŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yams expand underground, so if the soil is hard, stony, or not dug deep enough, the tuber struggles to push through and becomes misshapen. Creating high, soft mounds or ridges gives the roots loose soil to grow big and smooth.
ga: Atomɔ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ tɛi, loo atsako lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛbaafite. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ koni amɛfee agbo ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce large green leaves but very small tubers inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above the ground instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells or when the soil lacks enough plant food. The tree intentionally sheds flowers to save its strength and survive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ kɛ wala mli.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures become too hot or when there is a sudden change between dry soil and heavy watering. Extremely dry air prevents the flowers from pollinating properly.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsakemɔ ko ba trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight all day. Planting companion crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the air cool and humid, protecting the young cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Hefatalɔi tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi cacao lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain suckers turn yellow and dry up prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: While plantains naturally lose old leaves as new ones appear, rapid yellowing of lower leaves usually means the roots are suffering from prolonged dry soil or are being damaged underground by microscopic worms or stem borers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains lɛ baai momo lɛ laajeɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni eheei jeɔ kpo lɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miipiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ loo ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ efite amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and cannot handle intense heat. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantain or cassava to keep the soil moist and cool while their canopy develops.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ adɛŋ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ be mli ni ŋshɔŋloo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen, so adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth will restore leaf health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil because excess water cuts off oxygen to the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my maize leaves and sticky material inside the young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ nibii ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing point of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts early in the morning or late evening controls them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni okɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize improves soil fertility naturally and provides an extra harvest from the same piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni amɛha nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why does my land yield less crop when I plant maize on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up. Alternating maize with legumes or root crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi aba. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and hard before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ewaa dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot and is caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding agricultural lime or compost helps plants absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy that feeds the growing tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during dry periods?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It slows down water evaporation, keeps root temperatures low, and prevents weeds from taking light and water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Ha shishifãi lɛ amli dɔlɛ aba shi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or insecticidal soap protects the leaves and fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ he.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting at the tips and moving down the middle, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and starves maize pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to use as planting cuttings for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good cassava cuttings should come from a healthy, mature plant that is 8 to 12 months old, with no visible insect damage or spots. Choose the thick middle section of the stem rather than the green top or woody base, and cut pieces with at least 4 to 6 clear buds.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpa ni afo lɛ ajɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni anaaa bɛ mli lɛ amli. Halamɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni mli tse lɛ. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ yi mi tomi loo tso sisi. ni afo mli bibii Kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni mli tse.

english: Why will my crops produce less food if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants are forced to compete for the same sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Spacing crops correctly gives each plant enough space and resources to grow strong roots and yield a big harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shishifãi ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant, making the main plantain bunch smaller. Cutting away weaker suckers so only one or two strong ones remain ensures the main plant gets full energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha plantains akuu titri lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli koni ashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and small roots that easily burn and dry out under intense direct sunlight. Leaving large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain creates a cooler environment and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni baanyɛ ashã ni amɛgbi oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground with stakes gets them more sunlight and protects them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo ni ebaatsi helai anaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How do my groundnut plants manage to grow their nuts underground after flowering above ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-peanut tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛduɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated on the stem, it forms a small stem-like shoot called a 'peg'. This peg grows downward, bends toward the earth, and pushes itself into the soil, where the tip swells up to form the actual groundnut pod.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ wo pollination sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baaje kpo. Etamɔ tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ 'peg'. Nɛkɛ peg nɛɛ daa yɛ shishigbɛ. Ekoto shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Naa lɛ baafu aahu kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei ŋmei diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, prolonged drought, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies, thrips, or mites sucking the juice out of young leaves, or transmitting a plant virus. Controlling these small insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ eshwaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa wo mli lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up when the sun gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot hours as a defense mechanism to reduce their surface area and trap moisture, preventing the plant from drying out too fast in heavy sunshine.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be mli akɛ hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look lifeless in the afternoon sun but wake up again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon, leaves lose water faster through heat than roots can draw from the soil. Overnight, the plant recovers water balance because transpiration stops, making leaves firm again by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛkɛ kome mli lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ekoŋŋ ejaakɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ kpaa. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi

english: How does strong sunshine right after planting affect my new crops?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa beni adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Intense heat heats up the top layer of soil and dries out moisture quickly, which can burn young shoots or cause seeds to die before their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gĩɔ oya. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii loo egbe dumɔwui dani shishifãi lɛ mli alɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu baakpe.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when heavy rains fall immediately after I sow them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can compact the soil, wash seeds away, or cover them too deeply with mud, preventing air from reaching the seeds and causing them to rot instead of germinating.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ afɔ, loo efu dumɔwui lɛ tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: How do I tell if my crops are suffering from too much rain in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miina nugbɔ fe nine yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli?

english: When crops receive too much water, their roots suffocate from lack of air, causing leaves to turn pale or yellow, growth to stunt, and root rot to set in.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Edaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and stunted when the rains are unpredictable and stop early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ trukaa kɛ mra lɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of moisture to build stems and leaves; if rains cut off early, the soil dries out before plants can form strong roots or mature properly.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛfee amɛshishifãi kɛ baai. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmɔ oya Shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa loo amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava and plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains and cassava have broad leaves and shallow root systems, making them top-heavy. When heavy winds hit soft, wet soil, the roots lose their grip and the stems snap or uproot.
ga: Plantains kɛ cassava yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baakumɔ loo abaajie lɛ.

english: Can strong wind dry out my crops even when the weather is not very hot?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha midumɔ nii lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔɔ tsɔ po?

english: Yes, strong winds carry away the layer of humid air around crop leaves, forcing the plant to lose internal moisture rapidly even on cooler days.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔle tso lɛ baai ahe lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crops before the main farming season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ mli dani okwaayeli be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Planting too early before steady rains arrive leaves seeds in dry soil where heat can kill them, or creates weak early sprouts that die during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ, dani nugbɔ anɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ he ni latsaa baanyɛ agbe amɛ yɛ lɛ. aloo eha tsei bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How does knowing the length of the rainy season help me decide which crop variety to plant?
ga: Kɛ́ mile bɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi ni mikpɛɔ miyiŋ yɛ tsei ni esa akɛ madu lɛ ahe?

english: Different crops take different amounts of time to mature; if a short rainy season is expected, planting long-duration crops means they will dry up before yielding, so fast-maturing crops are better.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi lɛ heɔ be srɔtoi dani amɛshwereɔ. Kɛji akɛ akpaa nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku gbɛ Be kakadaŋŋ mli dumɔ baaha tsei lɛ agbi dani amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii, no hewɔ lɛ tsei ni daa oya lɛ hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential food they need from the soil. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in their growth helps restore their deep green color and encourages healthy development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer baafata he mra Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha shweremɔ kpakpa aya hiɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field make the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil. When the cowpea plants die, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsina tso lɛ gbo Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my maize plants staying very short and failing to grow big leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ baai wuji lɛ?

english: Maize stunting happens when roots cannot reach enough nutrients in hard, poor soil, or when tiny insects like fall armyworms attack the growing center of the plant early in its life.
ga: Abɛi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ehiii nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutua he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ yɛ egbekɛbiiashi.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa baa lɛ shãaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat or lack of water. The plant sheds its blossoms to preserve water and energy so it can stay alive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ. Koni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes crack open on the sides before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani manyɛ majie amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when dry weather is suddenly followed by heavy rain. The roots take up water too quickly, causing the inside of the fruit to swell faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli lɛ fuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects in heavy soil and cannot drain away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges keeps excess water away from the tubers and allows air to reach the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋmei ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akabote ŋmeii lɛ amli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong rain and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay close to the surface and do not anchor deeply into the soil. When rain softens the ground and the fruit bunch grows heavy, wind can easily pull the shallow roots out unless the tree is supported with wooden stakes.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni aduawai aniji lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ mlɛo, ja akɛ tsei ni akɛfee tso lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my stored dry maize grains turn into fine white powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ kpakpa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils lay eggs on the maize. When the eggs hatch, the tiny pests eat the insides of the dried grains, leaving behind hollow shells and dusty powder.
ga: Kooloo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ seed moth lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii Baaye dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli. Kpoji ni mli ewo muji kɛ sũ pɛ eshwɛ.

english: How do my seed yams know when it is the right time to start sprouting in the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato dumɔwui leɔ be ni sa ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seed yams undergo a natural resting period after harvest called dormancy. They wake up and sprout when they sense the increased soil temperature and moisture that comes with the arrival of rainy season.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Amɛteɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ kpo kɛ́ amɛnu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa kɛ latsaa ni kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops sometimes fail to produce a good yield even after I plant them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Crop harvests can fail due to unpredictable rainfall, nutrient-depleted soil, pests, or poor-quality seeds. Even with timely planting, crops need consistent moisture, rich soil nutrients, and protection from diseases throughout their growth cycle to yield well.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo dumɔwui ni ehiii bɛ nɔ Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ be ni sa mli po lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli daa. Niyenii ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ helai atsimɔ yɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ koni yibiiwoo kpakpa aba.
