english: Why are my crops producing smaller food items than they used to in the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land continuously drains essential nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with legumes like beans or adding compost restores soil health, helping your crops grow larger and healthier.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Should I change how I harvest my crops if market prices suddenly become very high?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsake bɔ ni mikpaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mihaa lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ jara lɛ tee hiɛ babaoo trukaa lɛ hu?

english: When market prices rise, harvesting in careful stages rather than all at once allows you to sell top-grade produce immediately while letting the rest mature fully, preventing wastage and maximizing your profits.
ga: Kɛ jarayeli jara lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ Nikpamɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ohaa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ shwereɔ kwraa. Tsi nibii ni elaaje lɛ anaa ni oha sɛɛnamɔi ni oná lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest so my crops don't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa nii? Koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Each crop shows clear maturity signs, such as leaves turning yellow, stems drying out, or fruit changing color. Harvesting at peak maturity prevents field rot, bird damage, and loss of crop weight.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baajie dalɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miigbi, loo aduawai lɛ ahe su ni miitsake. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hei ni fiteɔ, okpoi afitemɔ, kɛ tsei lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ naa.

english: Why does gentle handling during harvesting matter if I am just selling the crop anyway?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni blɛoo ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ he hiaa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihɔɔ kɛkɛ bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ?

english: Rough handling causes hidden bruises and cuts on harvested produce. These injuries allow bacteria and fungi to enter, causing rapid rotting before your crops reach the buyer, which lowers their market value.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ. Nɛkɛ pilamɔi nɛɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ fiteɔ oya dani onibii lɛ shɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Enɛ baaha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do people in the town say food is hard to come by during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ niyenii namɔ wa yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Food becomes scarce when most farmers experience harvest gaps between seasons or face widespread crop failures due to bad weather. High demand with low market supply makes food scarce and expensive.
ga: Niyenii bafeɔ nɔ ni anaaa beni okwaafoi babaoo kɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli yɛ bei lɛ ateŋ loo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he kpeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii hewɔ lɛ. Niyenii ni ataoɔ babaoo shi jara ni anáa lɛ faaa lɛ haa niyenii he waaa ni ejara hu wa.

english: How can I plan my farm work so that I have crops to sell when food prices are very high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni mahɔ̃ɔ be mli ni niyenii jara wa waa lɛ?

english: By practicing staggered planting—planting small plots a few weeks apart—or using basic dry-season irrigation, you can produce crops when others cannot, allowing you to sell during periods of high prices.
ga: Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ he nitsumɔ nɔ—shikpɔji bibii ni aduɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ateŋ lɛ nɔ—loo shishijee nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ odu nii yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi nyɛŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni jara wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up or spoil quickly after I bring them home from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo egboɔ oya beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba shia lɛ?

english: Crops spoil quickly if harvested while wet from dew/rain or stored in warm, unventilated spaces. Thoroughly drying grains and storing produce in cool, dry, elevated areas keeps them safe for longer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ/nugbɔ lɛ edɔ. Aloo okɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Nibii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects attack my crops most aggressively right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshinii lɛ waa fe fɛɛ dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: As crops ripen, their sugar content increases and scent grows stronger, attracting insect pests. Regular field monitoring and harvesting as soon as crops mature prevents these late-stage pest attacks.
ga: Beni tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eŋɔli lɛ mli waa. ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Gbɛjianɔtoo mli kwɛmɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara pɛ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ni baa sɛɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: How does a sudden dry spell right before harvest affect the quality of my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa trukaa dani kpamɔ baa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A dry spell close to harvest causes crops to dry prematurely, resulting in shriveled grains or small tubers. Applying mulch around crop roots helps retain soil moisture during short droughts.
ga: Hɔmɔ be ni bɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ bulb bibii. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight, which scorches their young leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving some tall canopy trees or planting plantains provides essential shade and keeps the air humid, allowing the young cocoa plants to establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land before planting my new cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dani madu kookoo tsei heei lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create an instant shade umbrella. This shelter protects tender young cocoa trees from intense sun and heat during their first two years until the cocoa canopy is mature enough to handle full exposure.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɛkɛ shĩa nɛɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to grow healthy leaves. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Eji tso ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni wa lɛ adalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with food that neighboring maize plants can use to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛdara waa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the center funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets the tender, growing centers of maize leaves. Catching them early and applying proper control directly into the funnel prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yam tubers require soft, loose soil to expand easily as they grow underground. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the growing tuber struggles to push through, resulting in stunted, misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛji amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni miida lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings with the buds pointing upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems with the leaf buds pointing up ensures the main shoot grows straight up toward sunlight while root systems form down below. If planted upside down, the plant wastes vital energy twisting itself upright, leading to poor tuber development.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa ŋmeii titrii lɛ daraa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ hiɛ shi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa yɛ amɛtsimɔ ni ja lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get extremely high or when plants experience water stress from sudden dry spells. Regular watering around the base and providing slight shade during midday heat helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Aloo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛjɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does spreading dry grass or palm fronds around my crop stems help them survive hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around plants with organic material, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, lowers soil temperature, and suppresses weed growth during hot, sunny weeks.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ aba shi ni etsĩ jwɛi adalɛ naa yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it bad to plant hot peppers on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the exact same spot year after year depletes specific soil nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target peppers to build up in large numbers. Rotating crops breaks this disease cycle and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are stressed by severe heat, lack of soil nutrients, or pest attacks like mirids. Providing adequate shade, organic fertilizer, and proper pest control helps the flowers convert into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nugbɔ, hulutsoo be ni sa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Shade trees protect delicate cocoa trees from harsh sunlight, prevent the soil from drying out quickly, and act as windbreaks. They create a cool environment that reduces stress on the cocoa plants.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne Amɛhaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa cacao tsei lɛ anɔ haomɔ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the ground is waterlogged, which prevents roots from taking up nutrients. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn my farm field before planting new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã miŋmɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial living organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops. It also leaves the soil bare, making it dry out faster and wash away easily when heavy rains fall.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa egbiɔ oya, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, efoɔ oya.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Managing these insects early using neem oil spray or recommended treatments helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa kroko ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot disease present in the soil. Overwatering starves roots of air, while soil bacteria block water transport inside the stem. Rotating your crop location helps prevent disease build-up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni awoɔ fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ aye hɔmɔ. yɛ be mli ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ nu ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. He ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabua amɛhe naa.

english: How can I know that my cassava crops are fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack. You can carefully dig around one plant to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Kwɛmɔ tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji eyitso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers come out small and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep, and loose soil in high mounds or ridges to expand easily. Compacted soil, stones, or shallow planting physically stop the tubers from growing straight and large.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gɔŋji loo ŋmeii amli koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ, tɛi, loo dumɔwui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ Enɛ baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni efee agbo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains need constant moisture and rich soil nutrients to grow quickly. If planted in poor soil without compost, or if weeds are allowed to compete with them for water, maturity and fruiting will be delayed.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli Aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛye nu he akaŋ. Akɛ shweremɔ kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall during flowering harm my cowpea crop?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ saa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain can physically knock delicate flowers off the plant before pods form. High humidity and heavy moisture also foster fungal infections that cause flowers and young pods to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ afee. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni naa wa hu kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunshine because their leaves burn easily. Planting tall trees or plantains nearby provides living shade and keeps the air cool, protecting the young cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei kakadaji loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Yellow leaves on corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my vegetables stay small and weak when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii lolo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni ekpɛtɛ he yɛ he kome?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight over the same water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing seeds properly gives each plant enough room to feed and grow large.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni eda.

english: Why do you recommend covering the ground around my crop stems with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei ahe baai aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, blocks the sun from drying out the dirt. It keeps the soil moist for longer so plants do not wilt quickly during dry days.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ gbooo oya yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes pull specific nutrients from the soil and attract specific pests. Planting them in the same spot repeatedly drains those nutrients and allows pests to build up in the dirt, causing smaller harvests over time.
ga: Tomato jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi. Amɛdumɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsɔ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do weeds on my farm make my crops produce less food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal light, rain, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to yield plenty of food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nugbɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua onibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertilizer before the plant roots have time to soak it in. Applying fertilizer when the ground is already damp or during light rain ensures the food sinks into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛwoɔ nu mli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii lɛ abote shishifã lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava under the ground is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem. You can also carefully dig up one test plant to see if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni amɛshi shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa kaa tso kome hu koni ona kɛji bulb lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden sticks to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes helps the leaves capture maximum sunlight to make food for big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off wet ground, reducing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa helai hu baa shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from heat, lack of water, or poor soil food. Keeping the soil evenly moist and well-fed helps the flowers stay on and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the soil waterlogged so roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why does my cowpea farm produce plenty of heavy green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen in the soil. If you add extra nitrogen fertilizer or plant in very rich soil, the crop spends all its energy growing big leaves instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars eat holes inside the funnel leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai ni tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central growing tip of maize plants. They feed on fresh leaves before they unfold, which can stunt or kill the crop if not treated early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛgboi kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni eegbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water around the plants, the roots drown and soil fungi rapidly attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain suckers split into strips after strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ fãi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their veins during high winds as a survival method. This lets the wind pass through easily so the entire plant does not get snapped or uprooted.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fãji lɛ ahe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, akuuu tso muu lɛ fɛɛ loo ajieee lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shishifãi amli.

english: Why do my oil palm fronds turn yellow with brown spots during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry harmattan, dry air and lack of rain cause moisture stress. Combined with a lack of potassium in the soil, the older palm leaves turn yellow and develop dry brown spots.
ga: Yɛ harmattan ni egbi lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he haomɔ baa. Kɛ akɛ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, tsei ahe tsei ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower dropping happens when the tree experiences dry stress, attack by mirid insects, or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi ni anyɛɛɛ afee amɛ shia. Shi fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Kpluka fɔŋ ko tutua lɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How can I tell under the ground that my yam tubers are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines on top of the soil naturally turn yellow and completely dry up, showing that the plant has stopped feeding the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa bulb lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering where the soil goes from very dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Is it possible for me to plant plantains at any time of the year, or do I still need to wait for a specific season?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu plantains yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be? Aloo ani ehe miihia ni omɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko lolo?

english: Plantains require steady moisture to establish strong roots. While traditional farming relies on the start of the rainy season, you can plant at any time if you have a reliable source of water or irrigation to keep the soil moist.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni nu ahi shi daa koni enyɛ efee shishifãi ni wa. Eyɛ mli akɛ blema okwaayeli damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee nɔ moŋ, shi obaanyɛ odu be fɛɛ be kɛji oyɛ nu loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I start planting my basic food crops today, or do I have to wait for the main rains to fall?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabɔi niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ dumɔ ŋmɛnɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ titri lɛ anɛ?

english: Most food crops depend on regular water during their early growth stage. Unless you have access to artificial watering or irrigation, planting today without wet soil can cause your seeds or suckers to dry up and die.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ daa yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ mli. Ja oyɛ hegbɛ ni okɛ nu loo nu ni akɛfee lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ odu ŋmɛnɛ ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha odumɔwui loo oshishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Has the changing weather in our area altered the best months for me to put my crops in the ground?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ etsake nyɔji ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, changing weather patterns have made rainfall less predictable in Ghana. Rather than sticking strictly to old calendar months, it is best to plant when local rains show a clear, consistent pattern of returning.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi eha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ efee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe akpɛtɛ kalanda nyɔji momo lɛ ahe lɛ. strictly Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ jieɔ sɛɛkuu ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ kpo.

english: Do my food crops always need heavy rainfall right after planting, or is regular light moisture enough?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni naa wa he hiaa mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ aloo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ fa?

english: Young crops need steady, moderate soil moisture rather than heavy flooding. Light, frequent rain or careful hand-watering is ideal to help new plants establish roots without washing away the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo kɛ po. Yɛ nu afua ni naa wa najiaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ loo ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baaye abua tsei heei ni amɛto shishifãi ni amɛshwieee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best way to apply fertilizer to my plantains so the plant gets all the nutrients?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-plantains lɛ amli koni eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer in a ring around the base of the plantain stem, keeping it a few inches away from the trunk itself. This places the nutrients directly where the feeder roots can absorb them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo plantain lɛ shishi yɛ kooyigbɛ, ni oha ekɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ yaa he ko ni niyenii halɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Should I spread my fertilizer broadly over the soil or place it close to the base of my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛma he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone of individual plants is better than scattering it broadly, as broad spreading allows weeds to steal nutrients and increases the risk of rain washing the fertilizer away.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso fɛɛ tso shishifã he lɛ, ehi fe ni ooogbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he. Akɛni jwɛi lɛ gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry for fertilizer or if they just need more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo?

english: Plants needing water will usually wilt or curl their leaves during the heat of the day, while plants needing nutrients often show pale green or yellow leaves even when the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni he hiaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni niyenii he hiaa amɛ lɛ jieɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo bei pii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: What are the common signs of plantain diseases that I should look out for on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji plantain hela he okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look out for leaves turning yellow prematurely, dark spots or streaks on leaves, wilting central shoots, or soft rotting stems. Catching these signs early helps stop diseases from spreading to healthy suckers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Hei ni tsuɔ loo okadii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. ŋmeii ni egbo yɛ teŋgbɛ loo tso ni egbo Okadii nɛɛ ni amɔmɔɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I protect my plantain plants from getting sick in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi plantains anaa koni hela akaye amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Protect your farm by planting disease-free suckers, keeping weeds down, removing dead or infected leaves, and ensuring water does not sit around the base of the plants for too long.
ga: Buu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu, jwɛi ni ooojie, kɛ baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oha nu lɛ akahi tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves sometimes turn yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during wet periods can be caused by plant diseases, poor soil drainage drowning root systems, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Tse helai baanyɛ aha baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ aba. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, shishifãi ni ebote nu shishi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: If I collect fresh goat droppings from my backyard pen and put them straight onto my pepper plants, will it make them grow faster?
ga: Kɛji mibua too ŋmɔtɔ hee naa kɛjɛ sɛɛtsu lɛ mli ni mikɛwo ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ani ebaaha amɛdara oya?

english: Fresh animal waste carries high levels of heat and raw nitrogen that can easily burn tender plant roots and kill the crop. Animal droppings need to be left to rot and cool down for several weeks before they become safe food for your crops.
ga: Koolooi ahe jwɛi ni afee ehee lɛ mli dɔlɛ babaoo kɛ nitrogen ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ oya ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo ni edɔ otsii babaoo dani ebatsɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I safely turn the manure piling up in my goat pen into good fertilizer for my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mitooi atsu lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmei kpakpa kɛha ŋmei shweshweeshwe?

english: You can pile the droppings in a shady spot, mix them with dry leaves and a little water, and turn the pile every few weeks. After about two to three months, it turns into dark, rich compost that feeds crops safely without burning them.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Okɛ baai ni egbi kɛ nu fioo afutu mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ku sɛɛ okɛ pile fɛɛ pile aba. otsii enyɔ komɛi Aaafee nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ Etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe ni shãaa.

english: Why do so many weeds suddenly sprout around my crops after I spread fresh goat manure on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ trukaa kɛbɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii beni midu too ŋmei hee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Goats eat wild grasses and seeds, and many of those seeds pass right through their stomach without being destroyed. When you apply raw droppings, those seeds end up in your field and germinate right next to your crops.
ga: Tooi yeɔ jwɛi kɛ koo mli dumɔwui. ni nakai dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo tsɔ emusuŋ ni amɛfiteee. Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ tsu nii lɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baaya ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How does well-rotted animal manure help my crop soil stay moist during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mitsei lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When manure breaks down completely, it acts like a natural sponge inside the soil. It binds dirt particles together so the land holds onto rainwater much longer, helping crop roots stay hydrated during hot days.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ fite kwraa lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ muji bibii lɛ feɔ ekome bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants get sickly and rot when I plant them in the exact spot where my livestock sleep every night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ he yeɔ ni amɛgboɔ beni miduɔ yɛ he ni mitooi akuu lɛ wɔɔ daa gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Soil where animals sleep and drop waste continuously becomes heavily contaminated with bad bacteria and concentrated salts. This unhealthy ground causes crop roots to rot and easily contract soil-borne diseases.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni kooloi wɔɔ nɔ ni amɛshwieɔ muji daa lɛ mli eyi kɛ muji fɔji kɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo. Nɛkɛ he ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Can I use the dirty wash water from my animal pen to irrigate my kontomire and vegetable garden?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ kooloi atsu lɛ mli lɛ afɔ mi-cone kɛ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: Dirty water contaminated with fresh waste carries harmful parasites and bacteria that stick to crop leaves, making the harvested food unsafe to eat and damaging the crop leaves with excessive salts.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni jwɛi heei ewo mli lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe. Enɛ haa niyenii ni akpaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ. ni efiteɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ ŋmei babaoo

english: Does keeping open animal waste near my crop garden bring harmful insects to my plants?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii abɔɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, piles of unmanaged animal droppings attract pest insects like flies and beetles. Once these insects gather around the waste, they easily move onto nearby crops and spread plant diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni abuuu ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji kooloi nɛɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ jwɛi ahe lɛ, amɛfãa kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my garden crops look yellow and stunted when planted in soil that stays soaked in animal pen runoff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ewo mli lolo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil soaked continuously in waste runoff loses fresh air and becomes suffocating for roots. Without oxygen in the dirt, crop roots cannot breathe or drink water, turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ faaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ amu loo amɛnu nu. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: What happens to my maize crops if I plant the seeds too close together in one small patch of land?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he bibioo kome?

english: Just like animals confined in a tight space struggle for food, crops planted too closely fight over the same sunlight, water, and nutrients. As a result, the plants grow weak, thin, and produce very small yields.
ga: Taakɛ kooloo ni awo lɛ tsuŋ yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ ji lɛ, esa akɛ ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ena niyenii. Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa, amɛhe feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do the lower stems of my crops turn soft and black when planted in messy, poorly drained soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays muddy and contaminated with decaying organic dirt without proper drainage, fungal diseases thrive near the ground level and attack the base of crop stems, causing the plants to fall over and die.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ kã he efee muji ni muji ni fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ewo mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Fungal hela lɛ daa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni etutuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. haa tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ

english: Why are my fruit trees producing small and sour fruits instead of big, sweet ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni mli edɔ yɛ yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Fruits need specific plant food like potassium to develop size, sweetness, and weight. When soil lacks potassium, crops produce small, weak, or poor-tasting fruits even if the trees look healthy.
ga: Tso yibii lɛ he miihia tso niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium, koni amɛná dalɛ, ŋmɔlɔ kɛ shwiili be mli ni potassium faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni adu lɛ baawo yibii bibii, ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni ehiii kwraa. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Why does my orange tree drop its green fruits before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ miifite eyibii ni eŋɔli lɛ dani eda bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Trees shed immature fruits when they do not have enough nutrient strength or water to carry them to maturity. Adding potassium to the soil strengthens the stems and helps the tree hold its fruit until harvest.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ aduawai ni eshɛko kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he lɛ bɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaawaje tso lɛ shishi, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ eyibii lɛ amli kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: What causes the flowers on my pepper plants to dry up and fall off without producing any pepper?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee pepper ko kwraa?

english: Flower dropping happens when plants are stressed by extreme heat or lack key nutrients needed for fruit formation. Proper feeding and steady watering help plants hold onto flowers so they turn into crops.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tsei anaa loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ. Niyenii ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What can I do to make sure my harvested fruits do not rot quickly on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mikpamɔ lɛ akafite oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Feeding your plants balanced nutrients, especially potassium, builds thicker fruit skins and firmer flesh. This helps the harvest stay fresh much longer during transport and storage.
ga: Niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei kɛ niyenii ni ja titri lɛ potassium Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni loo lɛ hu afee shiŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ehee be babaoo yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though rain is falling regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water helps plants drink, but yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of essential plant food like nitrogen or potassium. Rain alone cannot feed a hungry crop.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Nugbɔ pɛ nyɛŋ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know which kind of plant food or fertilizer my farmland needs before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tso niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani madu?

english: You can judge by how previous crops performed; small fruits and weak stems point to a lack of potassium, while pale green leaves suggest a lack of nitrogen. An extension officer can also test your soil to give exact advice.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo enɛ kɛtsɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ tsuɔ nii eha lɛ nɔ. Yibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa. yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛha ŋaawoi ni ja.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during early morning or evening when crops are actively growing or flowering, allowing roots to absorb the nutrients before sun or rain carries them away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Enɛ ji be ni tsei miida loo amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai dani hulu la loo nugbɔ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my maize seedlings remaining short and stunted while my neighbor's farm is growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe ejɔko yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Crop growth depends heavily on the nutrients available in the soil. If your land has been farmed continuously without replacing nutrients, seedlings will remain weak and stunted.
ga: Tsei adalɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ atsuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii be fɛɛ be ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plant is sick from insects or just lacking soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ mitso lɛ kɛjɛ kooloi amli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Insect attack leaves visible bite marks, holes, or curled edges on leaves. Nutrient shortage usually changes the color of the whole leaf—turning it pale yellow, purple, or brown at the edges—without any physical holes.
ga: Koolooi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ shiɔ ŋmeii ni anaa, bu loo ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa baa muu lɛ fɛɛ su tsakeɔ—ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eshishigbɛ—ni ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers in my village plant plantains close to their young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛ kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young crops like cocoa cannot handle harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and cooling the soil so the young crops can thrive.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to grow green and stay healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize turn green again and produce larger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha toi lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans on the same land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you grow them after maize, they naturally feed and restore the soil so your next crop can yield better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eha ehe awa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha yibii kpakpai aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by hungry pests like caterpillars or moth larvae feeding on the crop. Checking under the leaves early and applying neem oil mixture or recommended spray will protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Ni oookwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ni okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu loo spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn sticky during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes often happens when tiny insects called whiteflies suck the sap from under the leaves and leave sticky honeydew behind. Watering regularly and managing these small pests keeps the plant leaves flat and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ nu nu ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ ni amɛshi wuo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ Enɛɛmɛi baaha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When heavy rain leaves water sitting around the roots for too long, oxygen gets trapped out, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen lɛ efo mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off before turning into fruits during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they feel heat stress or lack enough moisture in the ground. Mulching around the base with dry grass and watering regularly keeps the flowers attached so they turn into full peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akakwɛ̃ kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How can I tell exactly when my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Cocoa pods show they are mature by changing color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange. Harvesting them at this color change ensures the beans inside have fully developed sweet mucilage for fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛdara kɛtsɔ amɛhe su ni amɛtsakeɔ kwraa lɛ nɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems near the surface and become top-heavy when carrying a full bunch of fruit. Using strong wooden props to support the stem under the heavy bunch keeps the tree upright during storms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ, ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ kɛji amɛwo aduawai ni eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa tsu nii koni akɛfi tso lɛ shishi yɛ tsei ni tsii amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight measured lines instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every single plant has enough space, air, and sunlight to grow properly without fighting its neighbors for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ tso fɛɛ tso da yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ awui kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around my yam mounds when the vines are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ato be mli ni wain tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your yam crop. Clearing them early allows the young yam vine to build enough food energy to produce large tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛhaa o-sweet potato tsei lɛ. Clearing up early Enɛ haa sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ feɔ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the young leaves on my new cocoa trees turn brown and dry up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso hee lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot store enough water to handle direct heat. Direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries them out, which is why they need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them while they are growing.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ko be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat to protect themselves from losing water. By curling, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, keeping moisture inside until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni nu akafite. Kɛtsɔ curling nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Ha fɛ̃i ahi mli kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Yellowing that starts from the leaf tip and moves down the central vein is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow tall with many green leaves, but the tubers in the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive moisture, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo tsɔ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, providing free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fall over easily when I plant three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole creates competition among the plants for sunlight, water, and soil food. As a result, each plant becomes starved, growing tall and weak instead of thick and sturdy.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa tsei ateŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi. edaa ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings during the first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow broad leaves very quickly, creating a natural canopy that provides moisture and shade to protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight during their delicate early stage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa baa ni mli kwɔlɔ oya waa. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa koni ebu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ amɛshishijee bei ni mli wa lɛ amli.

english: Why does spear grass make my crops turn pale and weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep, aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer nutrients from the soil much faster than your crop roots can, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering, which prevents the flowers from successfully producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa be mli. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does maize produce flowers at the very top of the stalk while the cobs grow lower down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: The flower at the top is the tassel, which creates dust called pollen. This pollen drops down in the wind to catch the sticky silks lower on the stalk, allowing the seeds on the cob to form.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ji tassel, ni jieɔ sũ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen lɛ kpo. Nɛkɛ pollen nɛɛ gbeeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni emɔɔ siliki ni kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ.

english: What is this 'Abedome' cocoa variety that other farmers in Ghana keep talking about?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘Abedome’ kookoo henɔ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ wieɔ he lɛ?

english: Abedome (also known as Akokoora Bedi) is an improved high-yielding hybrid cocoa variety that fruits earlier and can produce significantly more bags of cocoa per acre compared to older traditional cocoa trees when given proper care.
ga: Abedome (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Akokoora Bedi) ji kookoo henɔ ko ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Amɛwoɔ yibii mra ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo kookoo kotokui babaoo yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛto blema kookoo tsei ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many bags of cocoa can I realistically harvest from my farm in a good year?
ga: Cocoa kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko mli diɛŋtsɛ yɛ afi kpakpa mli?

english: While traditional cocoa farms yield around 3 to 5 bags per acre, planting improved hybrid varieties along with proper fertilization, weeding, and pest control can increase your yield to 10 to 15 bags or more per acre.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema ŋmɔji ni akɛ kookoo tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii aaafee kotokui 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ acre kome mli moŋ, shi kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashɛ kotokui 10 kɛyashi 15 loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ acre kome mli.

english: How many years after planting do high-yielding cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu kookoo tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start fruiting, but improved hybrid cocoa varieties can start producing their first cocoa pods within 18 months to 2 years after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ nyɔji 18 kɛyashi afii 2 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Will my cocoa trees keep producing the same high number of bags every single year as they get older?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ baajie kotokui ayibɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. afii beni edaa loo edaaa

english: No, cocoa trees usually reach peak production between 10 and 20 years of age, after which their yields naturally begin to drop unless you prune them, nourish the soil, or gradually replant old trees with new seedlings.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛyibɔ ​​ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 teŋ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, amɛyibiiwoo lɛ baaje shishi eba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ja ofolɔ tsei, oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ, loo okɛ dumɔwui heei edu tsei momoi lɛ amli blɛoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a huge harvest one year and then very few pods the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome, ni afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees often experience yield fluctuation because producing a massive crop exhausts the tree's nutrients, so it needs time, good rainfall, and fertilizer to rebuild its strength for the next major harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ naa tsakemɔi yɛ yibiiwoo mli ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ eheɔ be. nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtswaa hewalɛ hee kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ wulu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do so many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ŋmeii enyiɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmeii?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to shed up to 80% of its flowers because it cannot carry every pod to maturity, but excessive flower drop can be caused by prolonged dry spells, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pests.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli 80% ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo pod fɛɛ pod kɛyashɛ shweremɔ mli. Shi fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ mli aba. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing very tall with plenty of leaves but giving me very few cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ cacao ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees receive too much shade or are left unpruned, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves to reach for sunlight instead of spending that energy on flowering and fruiting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo be babaoo loo afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ, Kookoo tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai kakadaji lɛ amli kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nakai hewalɛ lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo he lɛ.

english: Why do some of my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads in cold, overly wet, or shaded conditions, which can be controlled by pruning branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Efɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ hulutsoo, ni abaanyɛ akudɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni afolɔ koni hulu la abote mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers come to inspect cocoa farms during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Officers visit farms to check for early signs of diseases like Swollen Shoot, help estimate your crop yield, and make sure you are using safe farming methods so your cocoa beans meet market standards.
ga: Nitsulɔi yaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyakwɛ hela he okadii mra, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo. Ni kwɛmɔ ni okɛ okwaayeli gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii bɔni afee ni o-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ jarayeli he mlai lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant my cocoa seedlings closer together, will I harvest more bags of cocoa from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani makpã kookoo kotokui babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting cocoa trees too close together makes them fight for sunlight and soil nutrients, and creates a damp environment where fungal diseases spread quickly, resulting in fewer overall pods.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pods fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When you harvest them and leave the roots to decay, they leave behind natural fertilizer in the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa ni oha shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or food crops like plantain growing beside them to block the intense heat and keep moisture in the air while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni amɛkadɔ fe nine ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce food. If the vines lay flat on the hot ground, the leaves get shaded, overheated, and easily diseased, leading to very small yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛji wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edɔ fe nine ni helai baaye amɛnɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest if I cannot see them under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa kɛji onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava gives signs above the ground when mature: the lower leaves naturally turn dry and drop off, the stem turns woody, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to bulge and crack open as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Yucca jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpo beni edara lɛ: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water, food, and light from the main plantain tree. By cutting them off and leaving only one or two strong suckers, all the plant's energy goes into making one large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsofai krokomɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ efolɔ ni ashiɔ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa plantains akui wuji ni he wa lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small fruits when I sow seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for sunlight, water, and food from the soil. They stretch high and weak trying to reach light, leaving them with no energy to produce big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛmiitao ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haaa amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by high heat or sudden dry spells. When the plant feels it doesn't have enough water to support new fruit, it drops the flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai heei bɛ lɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the soft leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Checking under the leaves early helps you stop insect damage before it stunts the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni okpa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ dani ekɛ otso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long scorching dry spell that bakes the ground. If you plant too early, seeds may sprout but then quickly dry up and die before the regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and scorch when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not have strong foliage to withstand direct sun and lose water rapidly through their leaves. Providing shade trees like plantain shields them from excessive sunlight and keeps the surrounding soil moist while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ baai ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni nu lɛ baaje mli oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni fe nine lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni aduɔ nii lɛ

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots like hardwood trees; their root system spreads shallowly near the topsoil. When the soil becomes too wet and heavy bunches grow, the shallow roots struggle to anchor the plant against strong wind.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei ni wa. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmĩ tso lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks sufficient nitrogen, which is the primary fuel plants use to produce chlorophyll and build healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tsofa titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ klorofil ni amɛfeɔ baai ni wa.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can soak up the nutrients. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots, and if applied right before heavy downpours, the nutrients can be washed away before plants absorb them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. ni kɛ akɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dryness, or nutrient shortages. Without adequate water and moderate temperatures, the flowers fail to pollinate and drop off.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ŋmɔlɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do I need to make loose, high soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the ground. Soft, high soil mounds give the tuber space to expand smoothly without pushing against hard, compacted dirt, allowing large tubers to form.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa yitso he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ muji ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwieee shi. Enɛ haa yitso agbo ko baa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves or spreading a virus, which disrupts normal leaf cell growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni tsiɔ baa mli wala yibii lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why do caterpillars keep eating my crops even after I spray chemical pesticides on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ po lɛ?

english: Chemicals may fail if they are substandard or fake products, if they are diluted incorrectly, or if pests have developed resistance. Using genuine products approved by regulatory agencies like the EPA ensures effective pest control.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ amɛji nibii ni esaaa loo amale nibii. Kɛji akɛ ajie mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ Nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ EPA lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ koni anyɛ akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when rain stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits on the field for too long without draining, the roots drown and harmful fungi in the wet soil attack and rot them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatutua ni amɛbaafite.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts alongside my main crop improve the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts work with beneficial soil microbes to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for surrounding crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛjie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ

english: How do I know if my soil is strong enough to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Soil strength, or fertility, can be checked by taking soil samples for testing to see its nutrient levels, or by observing its color, texture, and how well crops grew there in the past.
ga: Abaanyɛ akwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ loo bɔ ni ewoɔ nii ehaa lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni aŋɔ ni aka lɛ akwɛ koni ana bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai lɛ fa ha. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ahe su, amɛhefɛo, kɛ bɔ ni amɛdara yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I ask an expert to test my farmland before I spend money buying seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ ni eka nibii ni midu lɛ ekwɛ dani mawo dumɔwui ahe nyɔmɔ?
