english: Testing your land tells you which nutrients your soil is missing so you only spend money on the right crops and fertilizers that will actually grow well on your land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteɔ shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ he.

english: How do I choose which crop is best to plant on my piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Different crops need different soil types and moisture levels; matching your crop to your specific soil prevents poor growth and crop failure.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii lɛ anaa.

english: Are there specific crops I should avoid planting on my land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, if your land is too sandy, rocky, or holds too much water, certain crops will root-rot or starve, so you must avoid crops that do not match your land type.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã, tɛi, loo nu babaoo yɛ nɔ. Nibii ni adu lɛ ekomɛi baagboi loo hɔmɔ baaye amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ kpãaa gbee lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil over and over and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he pɔtɛɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for my soil to burn cleared weeds or leave them to rot on the farm?
ga: Ani ehi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ loo maha amɛgbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving cleared weeds to rot on the ground protects the soil from heat, holds moisture, and turns into natural food that makes the land stronger for future crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni he tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛgboi lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa.

english: How can I improve the strength of my land without buying expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can strengthen your soil naturally by adding animal manure, composted leaves, or planting legumes like cowpeas that put nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi ashishifã ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. baai ni edɔ Aloo dumɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli.

english: What is my maize plant trying to tell me when its leaves start turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni mi ŋmãa tso lɛ miitao ekɛɛ mi beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your land lacks nitrogen, which is an important food crops need to build strong green leaves and big ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger when I leave wider space between them when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa beni mishiɔ gbɛ ni da yɛ amɛteŋ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: When plants are given enough space, their roots do not have to fight each other for nutrients and water in the soil, allowing each plant to draw maximum food from the land.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa Ehe ehiaaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu atswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Can poor soil condition cause my crops to get attacked by pests and diseases more easily?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abatutua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya?

english: Yes, crops growing in weak or unsuitable soil become stressed and weak, making it much easier for pests and plant diseases to overcome them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo esaaa nɔ lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai anɔ kunimyeli feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to shield their delicate leaves from intense sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Planting shade trees or temporary food crops like plantains provides a protective umbrella during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo hebuu yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava cuttings at an angle instead of pushing them straight down into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle allows the roots to spread naturally near the surface layer of soil, making it easier for tubers to swell larger and making harvesting much easier.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. While water keeps the plant alive, it needs nutrients like nitrogen from manure or fertilizer to stay green and produce heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu haa tsei hiɔ shi moŋ, shi niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hu he miihia lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: How does burning my farm after clearing the bush affect my crops in the long run?
ga: Te miŋmɔ lɛ ni mishãa beni mijie brɔshi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but intense heat kills beneficial soil organisms and burns away rich organic matter, leaving the soil dry, hard, and less able to hold nutrients for future crops.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewaa ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ato kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the leaves expose less surface area to direct sunlight, helping the plant conserve precious moisture during hot afternoons.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. kɛ curl Baai lɛ baajie he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fioo pɛ kpo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni he hiaa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out their pollen, causing the flowers to fall off unused before tomatoes can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ni okɛtsuuu nii dani tomatoi lɛ afee.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early protects the new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting under the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil happens when fields have poor drainage and excess water gets trapped around the tubers, allowing soft-rot fungi and bacteria to attack.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ sweet potato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji ŋmɔ ko mli nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atutua.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my young corn reduce my harvest so heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oha jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Mi baby corn lɛ miiha mi yibiiwoo lɛ miiba shi waa?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from the roots of your young corn before the crop can use them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil and turn dark within just two or three days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not store well once removed from the moisture of the earth because exposure to air triggers rapid natural decay inside the root tissue.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Certified seeds are specifically tested and bred to resist local pests and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from harvested hybrid crops lose their strong traits over time, resulting in smaller cobs and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni akwɛ amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ sui ni wa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do some cassava varieties resist disease better than the traditional ones I have been planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi nyɛɔ helai anaa fe blema ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Improved cassava varieties have been developed through research to carry natural resistance against widespread local diseases like Cassava Mosaic Virus, allowing the stem and roots to stay healthy.
ga: Afee ŋmei henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ niiamlitaomɔ nɔ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ helai ni gbɛ eshwa maŋ lɛ mli tamɔ ŋmei mosaic virus lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive in direct, scorching sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to keep their leaf temperature cool and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni baa lɛ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against heat. The maize plant curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, trapping moisture inside and stopping the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi.

english: This yellowing is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals it from older bottom leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and displaying yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by small whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from catching sunlight properly, which starves the tubers underground.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela lɛ haaa hulu la lɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of heavy green leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the yam plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. A balanced fertilizer helps build bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni afee bulbs wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a shortage of phosphorus. Phosphorus is the specific nutrient plants need to convert flowers into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa Fosfɔs ji niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛtsɔ fɔfɔi amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to reach light, becoming tall and weak while lacking the energy to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Ebafeɔ mɔ ni kɛlɛ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal essential soil nutrients and fertilizer directly from your crops. Even with sufficient rainfall, your crops starve because weeds are taking their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii po hɔmɔ miiye amɛ ejaakɛ jwɛi miihe niyenii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my healthy cocoa tree when it seems to be growing so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kookoo niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekomɛi amli be mli ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ waa?

english: Pruning removes dead, overcrowded, or weak branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This helps prevent diseases and forces the tree to direct its energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni eyimɔ obɔbɔ, loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni enyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What are those straight green shoots growing out from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai tsei eŋɔli ni ja ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Those shoots are called chupons or water shoots. They drain water and nutrients away from the main trunk without producing good fruits, so you should cut them off early so the main tree stays strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ chupons loo nu ŋmeii. Amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai komɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofo amɛ mra. koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Is it better to clear away all the fallen dry leaves on the ground around my cocoa trees or leave them there?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie baai ni egboi ni egbee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mikoo tso lɛ he lɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: You should leave the leaf litter on the ground. The dry leaves act like a blanket that keeps moisture in the soil during dry heat, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your trees.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ. Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why do older cocoa trees need tall shade trees scattered around the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large shade trees protect cocoa from harsh winds, keep the farm cool, and drop leaves that enrich the soil. They also protect the crop from extreme heat during the hot dry Harmattan season.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni oha baai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ aba shi Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii hu ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ Harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra branches lets light and air into the farm to help dry out the trees and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Ehe miihia ni afolɔ tsei krokomɛi koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: What is this bushy green plant growing directly out of my cocoa tree branches, and is it harming my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kokoo nine lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Ni ani eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite that attaches itself to your tree to steal water and food. If you do not cut it off completely, it will dry out the branches and reduce the amount of cocoa you harvest.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ lɛ kwraa lɛ Niji lɛ baagbi ni ebaaha kookoo ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are many of the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Cocoa tsei enyiɛ ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ cacao ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction become pods. Flowers drop if tiny insects called midges do not pollinate them, or if the tree suffers from dry soil or lack of proper soil nutrients.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ E pɛ ebafeɔ pod. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii mɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ efɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo ebɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing smaller pods and fewer fruits than they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 20 or 25 years, their natural strength decreases, making them produce less fruit and absorb fewer nutrients from the soil. They may need pruning, extra fertilizer, or gradual replanting.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko eye fe afii 20 loo 25 lɛ, ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa aduawai fioo pɛ baa, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni afolɔ amɛhe. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he loo okɛdu ekoŋŋ fiofio

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa plants to turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are sitting in excess water because the soil is not draining properly after heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain on the same land with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei tsei yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: You can plant plantains or cocoyams with young cocoa trees to give them shade and bring you early food, but you should avoid planting heavy feeders like cassava or maize too close to mature cocoa trees, as they steal sunlight and plant food.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu cacao dumɔwui loo tsei ni cacao tsei bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ koni eha oná hulutsoo ni ekɛ niyenii aba bo leebi. Shi esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjuɔ hulu la ni amɛduɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much sunlight on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantain to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shaded environments. Clearing heavy weeds and pruning tall branches allows air and sunlight into the farm to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree lacks enough water or nutrients, or when tiny insects called midges are not present to pollinate them. Proper soil nourishment and keeping surrounding bush light helps insects pollinate the flowers successfully.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo beni kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ baaa koni ebafee pollinate. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akwɛmɔ fioo yeɔ ebuaa pollinators lɛ ni amɛyeɔ omanye.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi?

english: It is not recommended because cassava grows strong, heavy roots that steal water and nutrients away from young cocoa roots. Cassava also casts too much dense shade, which can choke young cocoa plants.
ga: Akɛ enɛ etsɔɔɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛhe wa. ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii amli Yucca hu haa hulutsoo ni mli wa fe nine. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ bibii lolo lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is missing nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crop leaves often turn yellow, growth slows down, and plants produce smaller fruits or fewer pods. Fertilizer or rich organic manure helps replace missing nutrients in old farm soil.
ga: Kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni tsei woɔ yibii bibii loo ŋmeii fioo komɛi Ŋmei babaoo loo humus yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ momo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and stems during the growing season?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baa kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the center of maize plants and eat the young leaves. Identifying them early helps farmers spray safe remedies before the crop is ruined.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni ayɔseɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛshwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems and branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso ni eda lɛ shishifãi kɛ eniji krokomɛi?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy. Removing them directs food and water to the main trunk so the tree can produce more and bigger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu baa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo ni dara.

english: Harmattan winds bring dry, hot air that strips moisture from leaves faster than roots can pull water from the dry ground. Crops drop leaves to save energy and protect themselves from dying of thirst.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and soft if left in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots soak up extra water from soggy soil, which reduces their starch quality and causes tubers to spoil quickly. Harvesting tubers at the right time before soils become waterlogged preserves their starch and taste.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kroko kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha starch lɛ mli afee fɛo, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afite oya. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli, dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why are some insects good for my farm even though other bugs destroy my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii komɛi hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi krokomɛi miifite miŋmɔshi nibii moŋ.

english: Not all insects are pests; useful insects like bees and midges move pollen between flowers so trees can make seeds and fruits. Other good bugs eat harmful pests, helping to protect your crops naturally.
ga: Kplukai komɛi jeee kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsiɔ pollen yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ. koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo dumɔwui kɛ yibii Kooloi kpakpai krokomɛi Ye kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara Koni eye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food they need to build strong leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or organic manure early in their growth helps the leaves turn green again and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year if I keep planting the exact same crop on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows specific soil pests to build up. Rotating your crops—like planting beans or groundnuts after maize—restores plant food naturally and breaks the life cycle of pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi komɛi aba Oŋmɔshi nibii ni otsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii baa ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil richer for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil as natural fertilizer. When you harvest them, that trapped nutrient stays in the ground to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni okpaa amɛ Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater gets trapped in heavy soil around the plant for too long. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away easily, keeping the roots dry enough to remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and fold down so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and lose moisture rapidly through their broad leaves when the air is hot and dry. Covering the soil around the stem with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps water in the root zone.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells cause severe stress that forces tomato plants to shed their flowers to survive. Giving your tomato plants steady, regular water at the root level during hot weeks helps the flowers stay on and form tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa aahu akɛ esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee tomato.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves and stealing plant juices. Spraying the underside of the leaves early with neem oil or recommended treatments stops the pests and allows fresh leaves to grow normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛjuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kpaa ni ehaa baai heei lɛ daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do tiny young pods on my cocoa trees turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Young cocoa pods wither when the tree suffers from fungal infection during wet conditions or when the tree is carrying more pods than it can feed. Pruning excessive shade trees to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Aloo kɛ́ tso ko hiɛ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my seed yams stay buried for weeks in the mound without sprouting after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ efu otsii babaoo ni ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams go through a natural rest period called dormancy right after harvest. Until this internal biological clock finishes resting and senses enough warmth and moisture in the soil, the yam will wait safely underground before sending up a vine.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛyashi nɛkɛ mligbɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ baagbe hejɔɔmɔ naa ni anuɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Yams lɛ baamɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛtsu wain tsei kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to local soil and weather conditions, so they absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the head start they need to capture sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa otsei ni miida lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow very dark green and fast in the exact spot where I dump my household rubbish and yard sweepings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛɔ oya yɛ he ni mikɛ shia jwɛi shwieɔ shi ni mikɛshwieɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Household rubbish and plant sweepings rot down into rich organic matter full of nutrients like nitrogen. Nitrogen acts as a natural plant food that makes leaves grow very fast and turn a deep, healthy green.
ga: Shia mli jwɛi kɛ tsei ni egboi ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use the dirt, ash, and dried leaves I sweep from my compound to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ muji, sũ, kɛ baai ni egboi ni mishwieɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, sweepings and household plant waste contain valuable plant nutrients. When you gather them and let them rot into the soil, they act as natural fertilizer, improving soil health and helping your crops grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, shia mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei amli jwɛi lɛ yɛ tsei amli niyenii ni jara wa. Kɛ́ obua amɛnaa ni oha amɛgboi yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, Amɛbaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ ni oye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does soil turn darker and softer in places where rotting plant waste has been left for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ hei ni ashi tsei ni egboi ni eshwɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: As earthworms and tiny microbes break down decaying plant matter, they turn it into humus. Humus makes the soil dark, soft, and spongy, which helps the ground hold water and nutrients for crops.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ fite tsei amli nibii ni miifite lɛ, Amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ humus. Humus haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it better for my farm soil if I burn dry plant waste or if I let it sit and rot on the field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji mishã ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ loo miha egbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is much better to let plant waste sit and rot on the field. Burning destroys valuable soil nutrients and kills helpful soil organisms, while rotting waste slowly feeds the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ agbo yɛ shia lɛ mli. Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ fiofio Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do strange new weeds suddenly start sprouting in places where I dumped soil sweepings from another part of my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ trukaa yɛ he ni mikɛ sũ ni jɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kroko nɔ lɛ shwie lɛ?

english: Sweepings often contain hidden seeds from mature weeds or wild plants. When you move those sweepings to a new spot, the seeds drop onto the soil and germinate quickly as soon as it rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ jwɛi ni eda loo koo mli tsei amli lɛ yɛ cleanups lɛ amli. Kɛji otsi he ni ashwieɔ nii yɛ lɛ kɛtee he ko hee Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster and stronger than my actual crops after rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitsei diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally hardier than crop plants and have aggressive roots designed to grab water and nutrients first. When soil is rich, weeds take advantage of it very quickly.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni afee koni amɛmɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaná he sɛɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if a patch of land on my farm has rich soil without buying expensive chemical tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛkaa nii lɛ?

english: You can identify rich soil by looking at the natural plants growing on it—if weeds or wild grasses are tall, leafy, and dark green rather than short and yellowish, the soil is full of nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Kɛji jwɛi loo koo mli jwɛi lɛ kɛlɛ, eyɛ baai, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kuku ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops looking pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. It can also mean the soil is too dry or flooded with too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Does leaving a layer of dry grass and leaves over my crop beds help keep the moisture in the soil during dry heat?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi ni mishiɔ yɛ midumɔ saatsoi lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, placing dry grass and leaves over your crop beds acts as mulch. It protects the soil from the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the root zone cool and moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kɛ baai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How can I make my crops grow bright green leaves without spending money on store-bought fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai ni mli tse ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ shwapo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: You can feed your crops by making compost from kitchen waste, animal manure, and rotted farm weeds, which releases natural nutrients into the soil to build strong, healthy green leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha onibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni fiteɔ, kooloi ashishifãi, kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Enɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I avoid burning the weeds and grass on my field after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mikɛshãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the organic food in the topsoil that feeds your crops and helps the soil hold water. Leaving cleared weeds to rot naturally or using them as mulch puts free nutrients back into your soil and protects it from the hot sun.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa sũ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaku sɛɛ ekɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green and yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow well. Applying animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant many seeds together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni miduɔ babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui yɛ be kome mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough room and food to grow thick stalks and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and fall off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind and heat pull moisture out of young cocoa leaves faster than their roots can drink water from the soil. Planting shade crops like plantains near young cocoa protects them from harsh winds and intense sunlight.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ latsaa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil, leaving it weak. Groundnuts and cowpeas are leguminous crops that trap nitrogen from the air and restore soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. make it weak Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing light green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curled cassava leaves are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava varieties helps keep your field healthy and productive.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kasava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni tereɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛ́ odu ŋmei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔji lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of leafy stems but produce very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to waste energy growing leaves instead of fruits. Pruning excess branches and using balanced fertilizers high in phosphorus helps the plants make flowers and produce tomatoes.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi fe nine lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot and die when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water sitting around crop roots stops them from breathing and encourages soil diseases that rot the stems. Planting your peppers on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: nu ni ebɔle Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpaa mumɔ ni ewoɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my stored harvested maize get full of small holes and insects after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni kooloi bibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils multiply quickly if maize is stored while it is still damp or placed in unclean granaries. Drying your maize thoroughly until the grains are hard and storing them in clean, airtight bags keeps insects out.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo loo akɛwo ŋmãa ŋmãa ni he tseee mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni okɛwo vacuum bag ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaje kpo.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than the crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally tough plants that spread fast roots to steal soil food, water, and sunlight before your young crops can get them. Removing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ oya koni amɛju niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli dani otsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ana. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil or are receiving too much standing water, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ená nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their blossoms before any pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Bean plants often shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil without enough water, or when tiny pests feed on the delicate blossom stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛbote la ni naa wa waa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ba Ye fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems that suck up water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: How does growing beans on the same farm help my maize crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby maize plants.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I plant maize and beans in the exact same row together?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa kome mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: It is better to plant them in separate alternating rows so the tall maize gets full sunlight while the lower bean plants cover the soil without being completely smothered.
ga: Esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli bɔni afee ni ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaaa nɔ kwraa.

english: How can I keep my farm soil damp when the hot sun shines for days without rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni hulu lɛ etswa gbii babaoo ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves creates a protective layer that stops water from evaporating quickly and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Planting maize seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to put my maize seeds in the ground at the start of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until two or three heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the topsoil so the seeds have enough deep moisture to germinate without drying out in the heat.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi tsɔ.

english: Why are tiny holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my growing maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii eba trukaa yɛ mi-abele ni miida lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Small holes in maize leaf funnels are usually caused by early caterpillars like Fall Armyworm that hatch and feed on tender leaves, which requires early treatment to protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ shishijee mli. ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi koni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Why should I buy new maize seeds instead of planting the seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested seeds from hybrid maize lose their vigor in the second generation, producing weaker plants with smaller, uneven cobs compared to fresh high-yielding seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: The lower leaves turn yellow when the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. The plant takes the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the newer top leaves to survive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big green leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ wa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or dry, or when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water. This stress prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii.

english: Why do groundnut flowers need loose soil around them after they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Beni fɔfɔi lɛ etse sɛɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they bend down and grow stalks into the ground where the nuts form. Loose soil makes it easy for these stalks to push underground and grow pods.
ga: Beni amɛwo ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ Amɛkotoɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ akɛ amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii.

english: Pepper plants save water and energy during severe heat by stopping new flower growth. Once regular water and cooler weather return, the plant will start flowering again.
ga: Pepper tsei haa nu kɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi heei ni amɛkpaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade from plantain trees when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ adɛŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa and keep the soil moist while the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over in strong wind when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ beni aduawai akuu lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot support the heavy weight of a full fruit bunch during storms. Supporting them with strong wooden sticks prevents the plant from snapping or pulling out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafo loo ekaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my sweet potato leaves have small holes all over them that make them look like a fishing net?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaafee tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo?

english: Small holes in leaves are caused by tiny leaf-eating insects like beetles or caterpillars. If too many leaves are eaten, the plant cannot make enough food to grow healthy tubers.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛji oye baai babaoo Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn black before the harvest season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ egbo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by fungal diseases like anthracnose or when the roots rot from too much standing water. This stops the yam tuber from getting any bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji ŋmeii helai tamɔ anthracnose tutua amɛ loo kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite kɛjɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Enɛ baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee agbo.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my crops when the crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ? He ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the best chance to grow strong root systems without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from strong heat and direct sunlight. Leaving selected shade trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantain around them keeps the soil moist and cools the young cocoa until it is mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shi tsei ni ahala ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ amli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the hot ground and exposes them to sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow much larger tubers underground while protecting leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Staking jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ he ni edɔ lɛ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell the right time to sow my maize seeds once the rain season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until there have been two or three good, consistent rains so that the ground is deeply moist. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if the heat returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ni baa shi daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ awo amɛ la ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper seeds are tiny and delicate. Raising them in a nursery allows you to protect the young sprouts from heavy rain, hot sun, and insects until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei bibii yɛ he ni akwɛɔ tsei yɛ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii srɔtoi lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts on my plot before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɛ mɛi akɛ amɛdu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛdu ŋmeii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes collect nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving maize the free nutrients it needs to grow strong later.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shika babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ ni aheee nɔ ko koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is my soil turning hard like rock, and how does leaving dry grass on top help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa?

english: Soil hardens when exposed to direct sun and rain without cover. Covering the soil with dry grass or crop leaves (mulch) shades the earth, traps moisture, stops weeds, and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai (Mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ehaa jwɛi lɛ kpaa. ni ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛ́ egbo.

english: Why should I avoid burning the dry bushes on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei ni egbi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys beneficial organisms in the ground and burns away organic matter that holds water. Clearing without fire allows the organic material to rot back into the soil, keeping it fertile and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa nibii ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni la bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ni edɔ.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural offices is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ etsɔɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: What is eating holes into the leaves of my maize plants and leaving green dust in the center?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ sũ eŋɔli yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your farm early and putting recommended treatments or neem extracts into the leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi loo neem mli nu lɛ awo baa lɛ mli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers falling off the trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges to carry pollen between them. If there are no midges on your farm, the flowers fail to set fruit and eventually drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛkɛ pollen awo amɛteŋ. Kɛji mɔ ko bɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Are all the bugs I see around my crops dangerous pests that I should kill?
ga: Kplukai fɛɛ ni mina yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: No, many insects are helpful friends. Bees and midges pollinate your crop flowers so they can produce fruit, while insects like ladybugs eat harmful pests that damage your crops.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii babaoo ji nanemɛi ni yeɔ amɛbuaa. Wuobii kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ otsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ladybugs yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ onibii.

english: Why do my cucumber plants have many flowers but only produce a few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumbai lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cucumbers have separate male and female flowers on the same plant. If insects like bees do not carry pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers, the female flowers dry up without making fruit.
ga: Kukumba yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ tso kome nɔ. Kɛji akɛ kooloo ko tamɔ ŋmei kɛ pollen kɛjɛɛɛ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli kɛyaaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Does spraying chemical pesticides on my farm reduce my crop yields?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii baa shi?

english: Yes, if you spray heavily, you can accidentally kill the friendly insects that pollinate your flowers. Without these insects, fewer flowers turn into harvested crops, lowering your yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ waa Obaanyɛ ogbe naanyobɔɔ kooloi ni feɔ ofɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Kɛji kooloi nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi baatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does clearing all the natural bush around my farm affect my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie adebɔɔ mli jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Te miŋmɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing all surrounding wild plants destroys the natural shelters and food sources where beneficial pollinating insects live, leaving fewer insects available to visit your farm crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛɛmɛi fɛɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhei kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ he ni ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hiɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii fioo pɛ baasaraa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What time of day is safest for me to spray pesticides so I do not hurt beneficial insects?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ? koni akaye kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui

english: It is best to spray late in the evening or early in the morning when pollinators like bees are not active. This prevents direct contact between toxic chemicals and useful insects.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa be mli ni ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ akabɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce flowers but never grow any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male trees only produce pollen to help fertilize female trees, so a male tree will bloom with flowers but will never bear any fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Tsei hii feɔ pollen pɛ koni eye ebua ni amɛkɛ tsei yei afee ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ni ji nuu lɛ baawo fɔfɔi shi ewoŋ yibii ko kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Why do my passion fruit vines need large carpenter bees to visit their flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi passion fruit wain tso lɛ he hiaa kapintɛfoi wuji koni amɛyasara fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Passion fruit flowers have heavy pollen that cannot be carried by wind or tiny flies. They need large insects like carpenter bees to move pollen from flower to flower to produce fruit.
ga: Passion fruit fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ pollen ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii bibii nyɛŋ ajie kɛya. Amɛmiitao kooloi wuji, tamɔ kapintɛfoi, koni amɛjie pollen lɛ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya fɔfɔi kroko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What can I do on my land to attract more bees and helpful insects to my farm?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛgbala ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can plant flowering cover crops, leave small patches of wild vegetation at the edges of your field, and avoid over-using strong chemical sprays that drive useful insects away.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi. Shi koo mli tsei ahe fãi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine lɛ he koni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ akabote mli.

english: Can I artificially transfer pollen to my crop flowers myself if insects are missing?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ pollen awo mi diɛŋtsɛ mi tsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ amli? Kɛji akɛ kooloo lɛ laaje?

english: Yes, you can manually use a small brush or cotton swab to transfer pollen between flowers, but this hand pollination takes a lot of time and labor compared to letting natural insects do the work.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ brɔsh bibioo loo odonti swab atsu nii ni okɛ onine ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Shi nɛkɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli nɛɛ heɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nitsumɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving shade trees on the farm protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding poultry manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ekoŋŋ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the soft center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the central growing part of young maize. Catching them early and applying recommended neem extracts or approved sprays prevents them from destroying the growing tips.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni daraa lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away easily, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam leaves need to climb up to get plenty of sunlight to produce food for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the vines off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa wain tsei ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Giving the plants steady water and partial shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juice out of young leaves and passing on plant viruses. Spraying the plants early with soaps or organic sprays stops these insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Emuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli ni ekɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ yaa. Akɛ organic samla loo spray ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow better without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni ooodu yɛ abele masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass, known as mulching, stops hot sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps soil cooler, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly turns into useful plant food as it decomposes.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: The first rain usually leaves the ground hot underneath, and there is often a long dry spell right after. Waiting for two or three reliable rains ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil. The plant is forced to pull food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Anyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni egbala niyenii kɛjɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, drink water and steal nutrients from the main tree. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong shoots, ensuring the mother plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso nyɛ lɛ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their leaves and drop small green pods during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiho baai lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ? Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli

english: During the Harmattan, dry air and lack of rain make the tree lose water fast. Shedding leaves and young pods is the cocoa tree's natural defense mechanism to save water and protect its main branches from dying.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ haa tsei amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ebuɔ niji titrii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out plant sap. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue and can spread viruses that stop the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni haaa tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain in waterlogged soil starves the underground roots of air. Without oxygen, cassava roots rot easily because waterborne fungi invade and break down the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shishi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot or when watering is inconsistent. Extreme heat destroys pollen, preventing the blossom from getting fertilized to form fruit, so the plant sheds it.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ nii ni amɛwo yibii. Tsei lɛ ho kɛje kpo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable stems with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields soil from harsh sunlight. It traps soil moisture so you water less, suppresses weed growth, and keeps plant roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer when the soil is dry or right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moist soil to dissolve safely; in dry soil, concentrated fertilizer chemicals burn root tips. Heavy rain washes fertilizer away down hills and streams before roots can drink it in.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ gɔji kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why do extension officers suggest planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-corn lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?
