english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes with natural root nodes that pull nitrogen gas from air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them alongside corn provides natural plant food that helps the corn grow better.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb high wooden stakes instead of creeping on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to capture energy and manufacture food. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground into sunlight and airflow, boosting tuber development beneath the earth.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛfee niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ mli. Wo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ashweremɔ he hewalɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them provides essential shade and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ebaaha shade ni he hiaa ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Keeping only two or three strong suckers allows the main plant to produce large, heavy fruit stems.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii agboi ni tsii.

english: Yam plants make energy for tuber growth through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and air circulation, which prevents leaf diseases and leads to much bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli babaoo. Enɛ tsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa bulbs ni dara kwraa baa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall with dark green leaves but produce very small fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ aduawai loo bulbs bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium. Nitrogen encourages heavy leaf growth, while phosphorus and potassium are required for strong roots, flowers, and heavy yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ fa babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baa lɛ daa waa. Yɛ be mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium he hiaa kɛha shishifãi, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ,.

english: If I plant beans in my farm after harvesting maize, how does that help my soil?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ Te ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like beans can capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing and restoring the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ekoŋŋ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes in the leaves and centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Checking your field early in the morning allows you to spot them early and apply appropriate controls before they destroy the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona amɛ mra. ni amɛkɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa atsu nii dani amɛfite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early stops the curling and allows healthy new leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the roots absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the base stem thickens. You can carefully dig around one side to check root size before full harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii kɛbɔle fã kome he koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifã lɛ da ha dani okpa lɛ kwraa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that bakes the topsoil and kills tender young sprouts. Waiting until the rainy season settles fully ensures seeds have constant moisture to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba shi koni dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that protect the young cocoa from heat and help the soil stay moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during severe heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve moisture and prevent itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa egbi.

english: How can I tell if my land's soil is healthy enough to support a good maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa kpakpa nɔ?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, feels crumbly and moist, and contains living creatures like earthworms. Pale, hard, or overly sandy soil lacks nutrients and requires compost or manure before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewa, loo eyɛ ŋã babaoo, niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii dani adu.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and protect their root system. The plant is not dead; once the rains return, it will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing its tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and wilt when there is too much rainwater sitting around the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates the plant's roots by preventing them from getting oxygen, causing root rot. When roots rot, the plant cannot absorb food or water, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ haaa amɛná lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii loo nu. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa kɛha mi?

english: Yes, intercropping beans with maize improves soil health. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it to the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger, while the maize stalks offer support for the bean vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Will I harvest more crops if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to weak, thin stalks and tiny ears of maize instead of a large harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni toi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ ŋmãa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to build tall stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to capture maximum sunlight for energy. This sunlight energy is transferred down into the ground, helping the yam roots grow larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha hewalɛ. Akɛ hulu la hewalɛ nɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa bulbs wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of friendly insects like bees to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ kpe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to your local soil. They consume water and nutrients much faster than farm crops, which is why clearing them early is essential so they do not starve your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛfiteɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia. Bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshinii lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on the soil, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny root sacs that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, natural feeding your maize.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa babaoo haa kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi bibii. No mɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-corn lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen. The plant moves whatever little nitrogen it has left to the fresh top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I don't leave it to rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji mihaaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Every crop you harvest takes nutrients out of the earth. If you keep planting without resting the field or adding manure and organic matter, the soil runs out of plant food and gets tired.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oya nɔ odu nii ni okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ejɔɔɔ he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay small even when the leaves on top look very bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji waa moŋ?

english: If there is too much nitrogen in the soil, the yam plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe niyenii ni amɛaatsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni amɛma ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark places. High rainfall and too much shade keep the farm wet, allowing the disease to jump from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baaha ŋmɔji lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny hidden insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices out of young leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the dirt for too long without draining away, the roots drown and soil bacteria cause them to turn soft and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛfee blɛoo ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without ever turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: When the heat is too strong or the air is extremely dry, tomato flowers get stressed and drop to save the plant's life before fruit can form.
ga: Beni latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni haoɔ ni amɛgbee shi koni amɛhere tso lɛ wala dani ewo yibii.

english: Why should I clear weeds when my crop seedlings are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak. If weeds grow next to them, the weeds steal all the sunlight, water, and soil food, smothering your crops before they get a chance to grow tall.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi Jwɛi lɛ baaju hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How do I know if my tree has become too crowded with branches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fa tsɔ?

english: Look closely at the tree's canopy; if it appears too thick and dense with no clear openings for light or air to pass through, the branches are too crowded and need trimming.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni he ko bɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni la loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ amɛ.

english: Can I decide on my own when to prune my trees without waiting for fixed instructions?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpɛ miyiŋ mi diɛŋtsɛ be ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mitso lɛ mli ni mimɛɛɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Yes, you can observe your own farm conditions and tree density to judge when a tree is too thick, rather than strictly following standard pruning advice given by others.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ fa ha lɛ koni okojo be mli ni tsei lɛ fa tsɔ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ blɔ tsɔɔmihi nɛ ni kpahi kɛ ha ngɛ tso ɔ he ɔ a se pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Should I prune my crop trees a fixed number of times every year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ko daa afi?

english: Not necessarily. Pruning should be based on how dense your tree's canopy gets and its specific location on your farm, rather than following a set rule like once or twice a year.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ ayibɔ kɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni eyɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ akpɛ tso lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ mla ko ni ato tamɔ shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I determine which specific branches I should cut from my tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mafolɔ nine pɔtɛɛ ko kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ?

english: Observe how the tree is positioned and look for areas where the foliage is thickest; you have the right to trim away any section that appears too dense to you.
ga: Kadimɔ he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ni otao hei ni tsei ahe tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Oyɛ hegbɛ ni ofoɔ hei ni tamɔ nɔ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my farm feel stuffy without any breeze passing through the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When tree canopies are very thick with no open spaces, they block wind movement down inside the farm, making the area feel sheltered and airless.
ga: Beni tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli edɔ waa ni he ko bɛ ni agbele. Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Ehaa he lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: What does it mean when no wind is moving through my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni tswaa yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shishi?

english: A complete lack of wind down around your crops usually means the tree branches are closed up and too dense, preventing air from circulating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kwraa yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei aniji lɛ efo amɛhe ni amɛmli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he

english: How can I help wind move better around my crop trees?
ga: Maye mabua kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni ebɔle mihe jogbaŋŋ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu mitso lɛ?

english: You can create openings in the canopy by cutting back areas where branches are too dense, allowing the wind to flow down through the farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hei ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ni ooofo mli lɛ nɔ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Why might pruning advice from another farmer not work for my own trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋaawoi ni jɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi adɛŋ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ esaaa mi diɛŋtsɛ mitsei lɛ?

english: Every farm has unique wind levels and tree positions, so what works on someone else's farm may not fit the specific density and needs of your trees.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛ tsei lɛ agbɛhei srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ ekolɛ nɔ ni tsuɔ nii kɛhaa mɔ kroko ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ otsei lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ amɛhiamɔ nii kpãaa gbee.

english: Does the location or position of my tree change how I should trim it?
ga: Ani he ni mitso lɛ yɔɔ loo he ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni mifoɔ lɛ mihaa lɛ?

english: Yes, where a tree is positioned affects its exposure to wind and how dense it grows, which determines how much trimming it requires.
ga: Hɛɛ, he ni tsei yɔɔ lɛ saa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ayibɔ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akpɛ tsei lɛ babaoo aha.

english: What should I do if my tree canopy has no open spaces left at the top?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ko eshwɛɛɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ?

english: If there are no openings for air to enter, inspect the tree and prune the heavy sections to open up space and reduce overcrowding.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ botemɔ bu ko bɛ Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ amli ni ofolɔ fãi ni tsii lɛ amli koni egbele gbɛ ni eha mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up when there are no big trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct, harsh sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, or that too much water is sitting around the roots, preventing the plant from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa.

english: Removing extra shoots ensures that the water and soil nutrients go directly into growing one strong main stem and large fruit bunches, rather than being shared among too many plants.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa ŋmeii titrii ni wa kɛ aduawai tsei wuji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ tsei babaoo baaja lɛ

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which starves the plants and reduces yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye tsei ni ebaaha yibiiwoo aba shi.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry organic matter traps moisture in the ground, shields roots from intense sun heat, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ he. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can get direct sunlight to make energy, which the plant then uses to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Akɛ tso lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off due to high temperatures, uneven watering, or poor pollination, which prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni ehiii ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer off the top of the field or push it too deep into the ground before the crop roots have a chance to absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ loo ekɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut cassava branches into short pieces before planting instead of planting the whole long stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ ŋmei niji amli kukuji dani adu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting cassava stems into smaller pieces focuses the plant's energy on growing roots and fresh shoots from specific nodes, resulting in stronger plants and better root tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ni afoɔ mli bibii bibii Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ maa shishifãi ni miida kɛ ŋmeii heei ni jɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ waa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu feɔ kpakpa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow primarily when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth, or when heavy rain drowns the roots and stops them from feeding. Applying fertilizer like NPK or decomposed animal manure restores their green color and strength.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛkpaa niyenii yeli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck the plant's juices and spread crop diseases. Spraying the plants with neem oil mixture or recommended insect sprays will get rid of these pests and allow healthy leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni ewo baai lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade provided by plantain trees or mature trees to protect them from intense direct sun and preserve soil moisture during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ la he waa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to put tall sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ niji kakadaji awo sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sunlight so they can make enough food to send down into the soil. Staking keeps the vines off the ground, protects them from damp rot, and helps produce larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyashɛ hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Should I start sowing my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. The very first rain is often followed by a hot, dry spell, which will scorch young seedlings in the dry soil before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, ahum ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before they are mature enough for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them in flat, waterlogged ground during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the tubers safe and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that capture natural plant food (nitrogen) from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the dirt to nourish the maize planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa niyenii lɛ Niyenii ni amɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving the plants consistent water and mulching the soil with dried grass keeps the roots cool enough to hold fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during small windstorms before the bunches are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum bibii amli lɛ? Dani jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the ground, and the heavy fruit bunch makes the plant top-heavy. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden or bamboo fork holds the weight and prevents the wind from knocking it over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni aduawai akutsei ni tsii baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehiɛɔ muji lɛ mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ he.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young maize, and how do I protect my farm?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ yeli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Those holes are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant. Applying recommended pest control solutions or wood ash directly into the funnel early in the morning destroys the worms before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tso mli sũ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color and helps them grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make my next maize crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of crops that trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize after them, the maize feeds on that leftover nitrogen without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ŋmãa ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves, or by viruses they spread. Spraying with neem oil or recommended treatments kills the insects and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii lɛ ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and letting fungi attack them. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat, dry winds, or irregular watering, which prevents pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ pollination naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does cutting off small side shoots from my tomato plants help me get bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii wuji

english: Extra stems and leafy shoots steal food and water away from the developing fruits. Trimming those extra shoots forces the plant to send all its energy directly into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe. Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come up out of the dirt if I plant them too deep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ejeŋ kpo kɛjɛŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: A seed only has a small packet of energy inside it to sprout and reach the top of the soil. If buried too deep, it runs out of food and oxygen before it can reach sunlight, causing it to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ paketi bibioo ko pɛ yɛ amɛmli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. ha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my crops grow thin, weak, and tall without producing good yield when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough space, light, and food to grow thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the stem looks big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni ehe wa moŋ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface and are easily damaged by tiny soil pests called nematodes. Propping heavy fruiting trees with wooden poles and using clean planting suckers keeps the root system anchored securely in the ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Yibii tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ duɔ kɛ tsɔne ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place dry fertilizer directly touching the stem of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer placed directly on or next to a tender stem acts like salt on a open cut, burning the plant's skin and roots. Spreading fertilizer a few inches away in a ring allows the roots to reach out and safely drink the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii ahe tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo kɛ́ afo mli yɛ pilamɔ ko mli. Ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant pulls remaining nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the soft growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Does it matter which way I push my cassava stem cutting into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down will slow down growth and cause poor root development. Always make sure the buds or node bumps on the stem point upward toward the sky so shoots can grow straight up easily.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ akafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ. mlɛo

english: Why shouldn't I plant plantain suckers that already have broad, wide leaves like a mature tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo tamɔ tso agbo lɛ?

english: Suckers with broad leaves (called water suckers) have weak roots and produce smaller bunches. You should plant 'sword suckers' with narrow, needle-like leaves because they have strong underground bulbs and yield larger, healthier plantain bunches.
ga: ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ Klante ŋmeii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ nu ŋmeii) lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii. Esa akɛ odu ‘klante tsei’ ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa, ni ewoɔ plantain ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants overnight and leaving dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome ni eshi ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center funnel of the plant during the hot day to protect themselves and come out at night to eat young leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he, ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling tightly upward like a spoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe tamɔ spun lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. These insects suck sap from under the leaf tissue, causing the growing leaf to buckle, twist, and curl upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ nuɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa baai ni miida lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, ni amɛkuɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to get maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the wet soil prevents leaf diseases and ensures the plant catches enough light to feed and expand the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ náa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It often happens when soil water levels fluctuate wildly, preventing the plant roots from taking up calcium consistently.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ aná calcium daa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when a sudden heavy rain falls during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A sudden downpour after dry weather shocks the cocoa tree. The drastic change in temperature and soil moisture causes the tree to shed flower buds to preserve energy until climate conditions stay steady.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ hosoɔ kookoo tsei lɛ. Tsakemɔi ni baa oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ haa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea field producing plenty of flowers but failing to form pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or insect pests like flower thrips can damage flowers right after opening. If pests destroy the flower parts or heat dries them out, the flowers fall off without setting pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips Baanyɛ afite fɔfɔii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji agbele. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ fãi komɛi ahiɛ loo dɔlɛ ha amɛgbi. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can I put fresh poultry manure directly around my young maize plants to help them grow?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ kooloi afɔfɔi heei abɔle he. Ani manyɛ madu mi-baby corn tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Fresh chicken manure is strong and hot because it contains high levels of nitrogen and ammonia. Placing it directly on young plants will burn their roots and leaves, so it must be left to dry or composted with dry grass before applying it to your farm.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ yɛ nitrogen kɛ ammonia ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo tsei bibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi loo ekɛ jwɛi awo mli dani akɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on the same soil where I plan to plant maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally fertilizes the soil and improves crop growth without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Niyenii nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ni aheee tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the plant lacks enough nitrogen in the soil. Maize prioritizes new growth, so it moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to nourish the younger top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi sumɔɔ dalɛ hee. No hewɔ lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso waa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a crop's natural survival mechanism to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Excessive heat causes heat stress in tomatoes, which dries up the pollen inside the blossoms so they cannot form fruits, causing the unpollinated flowers to fall off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ baaha pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ agbi. no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ ekɛ yibii aba Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I harvest more food from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stalks, small fruit sizes, and a lower overall harvest compared to well-spaced crops.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii Yibii lɛ daraaa. ni ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in tough conditions with minimal water and nutrients. Because they grow faster and consume resources quickly, they can easily overpower and choke cultivated crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni nu kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye tsei ni ama shi lɛ anɔ kunim ni amɛfite amɛ oya kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why are holes appearing on my cabbage leaves when I cannot see any pests on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Akɛni minaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ gbi lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, like caterpillars and armyworms, hide under leaves or inside the topsoil during hot daylight hours to avoid the sun, emerging only at night to feed on leaves.
ga: Tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi. Okɛ ohe awo baai ashishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni hulu lɛ akashɛ ohe. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ pɛ koni amɛye baai.

english: Why is it risky to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting crops from the same family in one spot depletes specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and fungal diseases to build up in the soil, making future harvests weaker each year.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli lɛ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ be kome mli lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn to dust or grow mold when stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ sũ loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize harvested before it is thoroughly dried retains moisture inside the grain. Moisture attracts mold and destructive pests like grain weevils, which eat and destroy stored produce from the inside out.
ga: Abele ni akpaa dani egbiɔ kwraa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii, ni yeɔ nibii ni ato lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Applying well-decomposed manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early in the plant's life will help it produce green leaves and grow rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall with many green leaves but very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes pepper plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than fruiting. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop producing excess leaves and start setting heavy flowers and fruit pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni baa lɛ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekpa baai ni fa fe nine lɛ feemɔ. ni ebɔi fɔfɔii ni tsii kɛ aduawai ashishifãi

english: When cassava stems are planted too close to each other, their root systems fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their branches block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing gives every plant enough soil room and sunlight to develop large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛniji lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni tsii aba.

english: Should I save seeds from my current hybrid maize harvest to plant next season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crops usually results in lower yields and weaker plants in the second generation because hybrid traits do not pass on reliably. Buying fresh certified hybrid seeds every planting season ensures uniform growth, disease resistance, and high yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ sui ni ji hybrid lɛ aha yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ haa amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the leaves and centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of young maize. Checking your field frequently and applying recommended control methods as soon as you see the first damaged leaf prevents them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ. He ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ shii abɔ Ni kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ tso lɛ atsu nii kɛji ona klɛŋklɛŋ baai ni efite lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps the plant absorb calcium evenly and prevents black fruit bottoms.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa tso yibii ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming fruits during hot, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: High temperatures combined with dry soil put stress on tomato plants, causing flowers to dry up and drop off unpollinated. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture so flowers can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛnáaa ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds during the first month after my crops sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have weak root systems and cannot compete well against aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Removing weeds early allows your crop seedlings to establish strong roots and grow tall enough to naturally shade out later weeds.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams take up significant nutrients from the soil, leaving it tired. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally renewing soil fertility for the next season's crop without needing expensive synthetic fertilizers.
ga: Sweet potatoes shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha etɔ lɛ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehiaaa.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy and get attacked by insects so fast inside my storage crib?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya ni kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Grain that is stored with too much moisture creates a moist environment where mold grows and storage insects multiply quickly. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly until the kernels are hard before storing them in clean, dry, or airtight bags stops rot and keeps pests away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa. Fuji lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ baafa oya. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛwo kotokui ni mli tse, ni egbi, loo ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. Ehaa fitemɔ kpaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dying during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their foliage is tender. They need shade crops like plantains or leguminous shade trees planted alongside them to protect them from heat stress and retain soil moisture while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo ŋmeii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil still feels slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo lolo moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce its exposed surface area and conserve moisture, usually recovering by late afternoon or evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛgboiɔ koni amɛha he ni amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli.

english: This yellowing is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, and when the soil lacks it, the maize plant draws nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Abele lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very bushy green leaves but produce only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo lɛ? shi eyɛ yitso bibioo Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the cassava plant to focus all its energy on growing stem and leaves instead of roots. Cassava requires balanced soil nutrients, particularly potassium, to swell its root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia Cassava. titri lɛ potassium ni haa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the legumes decay, this natural nitrogen stays in the soil to feed your subsequent maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them with dark sticky droppings inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, chewing on tender new leaves and leaving behind frass (waste material).
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Okɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ atsu nii ni oshi tso mli ŋmɔtɔi (nibii ni fiteɔ nii) lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects such as aphids, thrips, or mites. As these insects feed on the sap underneath the leaf, they distort leaf growth and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ejaakɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over on its own just when the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsiimɔ wa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially in loose soil or strong winds. Weakening by root pests can also cause the plant to uproot, which is why farmers use wooden or bamboo props to support the stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ loo he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ajie ehe. Nɔ ni haa okwaafoi kɛ nibii ni akɛ tso loo ŋmei fee lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, poor pollination, or irregular watering. If temperatures stay too high or the plant is water-stressed during flowering, it sheds the blossoms to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. pollination ni ehiii loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tso lɛ nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to maximum sunlight, allowing the plant to make more food for large tuber formation. It also keeps leaves off the hot soil, preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛha bulbs wuji afeemɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know which side of a cassava stem to stick into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ eta shikpɔŋ he kɛ́ oodu lɛ?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds along the stem where leaves used to grow. Plant the stem with those buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can sprout easily above ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni awó nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sunlight. Staking allows the foliage to capture maximum heat and light, which gives the plant energy to build large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Staking haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Nibii ni baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from intense sun heat, keeps soil moist for longer periods, stops weeds from growing, and rots down into rich food for the plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni fitemɔ bafeɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha tsei.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots decay, they naturally feed the soil with nitrogen, helping neighbor crops like maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fite lɛ Amɛkɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off when the dry Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds pull water out of leaves faster than dry roots can pull water from the soil. Providing shade trees and placing grass mulch around the trunk keeps the soil moist and protects tender cocoa leaves from drying out.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing much smaller fruit bunches than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miiwo aduawai bibii babaoo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Over time, plantain stands produce too many young shoots called suckers that steal nutrients and water from the main stem. Pruning away excess suckers so only two or three stems remain will make your fruit bunches big again.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Perennial dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ eshwɛ lɛ, ebaaha oyibii akuu lɛ afee agbo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food plants need to build strong leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are ragged holes suddenly appearing in the middle leaves of my maize, full of brown powdery dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ teŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ? Te nɔ ni sũ ni akɛfee powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf fold of the plant. Spotting and treating this early prevents the caterpillar from destroying the main growing point of the maize plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni ayɔseɔ mra kɛ tsamɔ Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite hei titri ni ŋmeii tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when soil moisture fluctuates wildly and prevents roots from absorbing calcium. Regular, steady watering keeps the soil evenly moist and stops this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, ni afeɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaaa enɛ aba mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience severe heat stress or lack water. Keeping the soil consistently damp during dry spells helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii anyɛ afee.

english: This usually happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves and big cobs. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots with the help of beneficial soil bacteria. When the plant roots decay, that extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni enyɛɔ emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi amli kɛtsɔ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ayebuamɔ nɔ. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary nurse crops like plantain or cassava beside them provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baawa.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow very tall and thin with small roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhiɛ shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they compete heavily for sunlight and stretch upward to reach light, spending their energy on tall stems instead of swelling their roots into big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Ekɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ ŋwɛi koni emɔ la lɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛyashi amɛbatsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize seeds right after the first major rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Early planting allows seeds to use the sudden release of plant food in the soil caused by early rains, giving the crop a rapid, healthy start before pests accumulate or late-season dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ tsei niyenii ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ kɛbaa trukaa lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tsei jeɔ shishi oya, ni amɛnáa hewalɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baa amɛhe shi loo hɔmɔ he okadii baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaf funnel of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl deep into the central funnel of the corn plant to hide during the day while feeding heavily on the soft young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatee amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning light green with yellow patches and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ mli ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: This symptom is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a plant virus spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings for planting helps prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ okadi nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, which weakens the pollen and prevents flowers from setting fruit, causing the plant to shed the unused blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why does planting cowpea crops help reduce the weeds on my farmlands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ aba shi lɛ?

english: Cowpea grows fast and spreads broad leaves that form a dense mat over the ground, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds and stopping them from growing.
ga: Cowpeas daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mli tse lɛ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni etsĩɔ dalɛ naa.

english: Yams are mature when the green leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely, showing that the plant has finished transferring its growth energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the main tree trunk instead of on the tips of the branches like other fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei niji lɛ anɔ tamɔ aduawai tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees bear fruit directly on the trunk and main branches—a trait called cauliflory—because cocoa pods grow very heavy and need the strong, sturdy support of thick wood so they do not snap fragile outer branches.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ yibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ cauliflower Enɛ ji akɛ, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsii ni ebiɔ tso ni mli wa, ni wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Bɔni afee ni kponɔgbɛ tsei niji ni waaa lɛ akakumɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are extremely sensitive to heat and direct light. Big trees provide shade, acting like protective umbrellas to keep the young cocoa plants cool and preserve moisture in the surrounding soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta, ni ehaa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off the small water shoots that spring up from the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Those small shoots, often called chupons, steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing them forces the tree to direct all its energy into producing leaves, flowers, and healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ chupon. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ biɔ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Excess rain creates high humidity, allowing a mold-like disease called black pod to thrive and spread through water splashes from infected pods or wet soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa hela ko ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni ashwieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I am planting it in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds on the stem cutting. The buds should always point upward toward the sky so the leaves can easily sprout above ground and root properly below.
