ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. yɛ nine lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ada yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwo shishifãi ni sa yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting within just two or three days after I dig them out of the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unlike crops with tough skins like yams, cassava roots continue to breathe rapidly after being harvested and lack a protective bark, causing them to spoil quickly unless processed into gari or flour immediately.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsei ni amɛhe tsitsii wa tamɔ sweet potatoes lɛ ahe. Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛbɛ ŋmei ni buɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya ja afee amɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does cassava manage to survive and yield tubers even when the dry season lasts longer than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei nyɛ ehi shi ni ewo ŋmeii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ moŋ?

english: Cassava has deep, extensive root systems that can reach water far beneath the soil surface, and it drops its leaves during droughts to conserve internal water until rain returns.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Amɛbaajie amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwie shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛto nu yɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the corn plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important food element in the soil that helps plants stay green and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do I get tiny corn cobs with missing grains when I plant my corn seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ? Ni dumɔwui bɛ beni miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting corn seeds too close together causes their roots and leaves to compete for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving the plants without enough energy to fill out full cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo abele ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does every single thread of silk on a corn cob need to catch dust from the flower at the top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ abua sũ naa kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Each individual silk thread connects directly to a single potential seed on the cob. If a silk thread does not catch pollen from the top tassel, that specific grain will never form, leaving a blank spot on the cob.
ga: Akɛ siliki kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsa dumɔwu kome ni baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji siliki lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ pollen kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwu lɛ teŋ shi. Ashi he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged from heavy rains, which stops the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow thick leafy bushes above ground but produce very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jwɛi ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or excessive leafy growth causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of storing food underground to form large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo baai ni shwereɔ babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ niye ní toɔ zugba sisi konɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do experienced farmers always plant plantain suckers alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui kɛ kookoo dumɔwui be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight; fast-growing plantains provide living shade, cool the soil, and prevent the delicate cocoa plants from drying out and dying.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehaaa kookoo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi ni egbo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit mainly because of extreme dry heat, irregular watering, or hot winds drying out the pollen before the flower can be fertilized.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii, titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ awo lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough rain and sunlight on the land?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds steal water and essential soil nutrients directly from your crops' roots, and they also harbor insect pests and diseases that easily spread to your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã otsei titrii lɛ amli oya lɛ hu.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa bɔni afee ni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting crops too close forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems and much smaller, low-quality yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ nibii bibii babaoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which allows the plant to manufacture enough food to feed and swell the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ koni amɛbaji lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and droop during the afternoon heat even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mibɛ eko lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: In intense afternoon sun, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up, causing the plant to temporarily wilt to protect itself until temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some farmers pinch off the growing tips of young pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi miiye teemɔŋ sane ni haa aduɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii lɛ he fɛo lɛ?

english: Pinching the top tip stops the plant from growing only straight up and encourages side branches to form, creating a bushier plant that produces far more flowers and peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa lɛ, etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ, ni ewoɔ esɛɛ niji hewalɛ koni amɛfee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ko ni woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does covering the soil around my plants with dry grass or straw help them survive dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli?

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter acts as a protective blanket that traps soil moisture, blocks weed growth, and keeps root zones cool during dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: What happens to my maize crops when rain does not fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo?

english: When rain stops, maize plants roll up their leaves into tight tubes to prevent water from escaping. If the dry period lasts too long, the plant slows down its growth and the leaves start turning yellow and dry because it cannot take up nutrients without water.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ ebaa lɛ ewoɔ paipii ni mli wa mli koni nu akaje mli. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaagbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji nu bɛ.

english: How can I keep moisture in my soil so my plants do not dry out quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni mitsei lɛ akagbi oya?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or straw. This practice, called mulching, acts as a protective shield that prevents the strong sun from evaporating water directly from the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ jwɛi, baai, loo jwɛi haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can young seedlings survive if I am only able to water them once a week during dry weather?
ga: Ani tsei bibii baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ manyɛ mawo amɛ nu shikome pɛ yɛ otsi mli yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Young plants have very short roots that stay close to the top layer of soil, which dries out fast. Watering once a week is usually not enough for them; they need light, regular watering every few days until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji waa ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ faaa kɛhaaa amɛ. Amɛbiɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu daa, ni fioo pɛ. Gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu.

english: If my crops wilt during a long heat spell, will heavy rain bring them back to life?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: If the leaves are only wilting during the daytime heat but still soft and green, water will restore them within hours. However, if the plant stems have completely dried out, turned brown, and snapped, those parts are dead and cannot recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gboi yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ pɛ mli Shi eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ hu. Shi kɛlɛ, nu lɛ baatsake yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli, kɛji tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ etsɔ blɔfo ni efo lɛ, nakai fãi lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsake.

english: Why do my crops stop thriving and stay small even though they started growing very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ ni ehi shi bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ ebɔi shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops often stall in growth when they use up the initial nutrients in the soil or when hard ground stops their roots from expanding. Adding well-rotted manure or compost gives the roots new food and helps them push deeper into the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛji akɛ shishijee niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ amɛshwã Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii hee ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in strong afternoon heat is a protective trick the plant uses to shrink its surface area so it loses less water. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is okay, but if they stay curled all night, the soil needs water.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ji ŋaa ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba amɛhe nɔ koni nu fioo pɛ afite. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ Nu he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ hu.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crop turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences stress from lack of water or soil nutrients, it sacrifices its older bottom leaves. It moves all available food and water to feed the top young leaves where new growth happens.
ga: Kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baafite ebaa ni egbɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the tips and edges of my crop leaves drying up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi kɛ amɛshishigbɛi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Brown, burnt edges on leaves usually mean the plant is suffering from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much chemical fertilizer. The plant cannot push enough moisture all the way to the edges of its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shã ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miikpe. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛre ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛyashi baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is dying from lack of water or from a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni bɛ loo tsei ahe helai miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: If crops lack water, entire rows will wilt together during the daytime and look better at night. If it is a disease, usually only a few plants get sick first, showing spots, yellow patches, or rotten stems even when the soil is damp.
ga: Kɛji nu efo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta muu lɛ fɛɛ baafee ekome yɛ gbi lɛ mli, ni ebaafee fɛo gbɛkɛ. Kɛji hela mɔ amɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei fioo komɛi pɛ baaye hela klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baaje kpo. Aloo tso lɛ tso lɛ miifite eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ.

english: Is it good to apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is very dry?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ?

english: No, putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn and destroy your crop's roots because chemical fertilizer needs water to dissolve safely. Always wait for a rain or water the soil thoroughly before applying fertilizer.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu dani enyɛ etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ loo okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong and green. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Will putting fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop help it grow faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mitsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya?

english: No, placing fertilizer right against the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots due to high salt content. It is better to place the fertilizer in a small circle or hole about two to three inches away from the stem so the roots can safely reach it.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi yɛ ŋmei babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli. Aloo, bu lɛ kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee 2-3 inch koni eha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ abote mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if the caterpillars eating my corn leaves are fall armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ?

english: Fall armyworms usually hide inside the central funnel of the corn plant, leaving ragged holes and sawdust-like waste. If you look closely at the caterpillar's head, you will see a distinct upside-down white 'Y' pattern.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa. Kɛ okwɛ ŋmei lɛ yitso jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Obaana ‘Y’ ni atsake lɛ yɛŋ ni mli tse.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over easily before the fruit bunches are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that weaken if tiny pests called nematodes or stem weevils attack them underground. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, strong winds easily blow the weakened tree over unless you support it with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem weevils lɛ tutua amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ tswaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi oya. Ja okɛ tso miitsu nii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under forest cover and need light shade to protect them from intense heat and harsh winds. Without shade, the trees become stressed, dry out faster, and are more easily attacked by pests like mirids, leading to fewer pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi ashishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo be ni mli tse koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ, amɛgbiɔ oya ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pods fioo komɛi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without proper drainage, causing root-rot fungi to thrive. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving the plants consistent water and using dry grass to mulch around the roots keeps the soil cool and helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Okɛ nu awo tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: The first rain after a long dry period is often followed by a week or two of harsh heat, which dries out the topsoil and kills newly sprouted seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become frequent and reliable so the soil stays continuously moist.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa ni yeɔ otsi kome loo enyɔ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ shii abɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow much slower and look thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because weeds are tough and fast-growing, they steal these vital resources away from your crops, effectively starving them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ wa ni amɛdaraa oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my hybrid maize harvest give smaller cobs than the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed from two distinct plant parents to produce high yield in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special combined traits, resulting in smaller cobs, varied plant heights, and lower overall yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei afɔlɔi srɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui bibii. tsei lɛ agbɔjɔmɔi srɔtoi kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava grown alongside them to block the harsh sun while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wood and stake my yam plants with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji ni madu sweet potato tsei ni akɛ tsei ebɔ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to catch light and generate energy. Staking keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the tubers below ground to grow larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná la ni amɛfee hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-pattern on lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time helps restore green leaves and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni tamɔ V-shaped ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni egbɔ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni eboteɔ shishi lɛ?

english: This is known as Blossom End Rot, caused by irregular watering which prevents the plant from absorbing enough calcium. Keeping soil moisture consistent stops the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai ashishi akafite.

english: Why do my maize leaves look shredded with small holes inside the growing tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani eyɛ tip ni miida lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves from inside the whorl. Catching them early and spraying recommended neem oil or pest control treatments protects the crop yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are tiny green bugs clustering under my pepper leaves and causing them to curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: These pests are aphids, which suck sap out of the leaves and cause them to distort. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or standard insecticide removes them.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ji aphids, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa amɛ fiteɔ. Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Aloo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why do my healthy plantain trees keep falling over during moderate wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ni mli wa waa mli lɛ?

english: Tiny worms called nematodes or banana weeping beetles may be eating the underground roots and weakening the tree's base. Planting clean, heat-treated suckers and mounding soil around the base prevents root collapse.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana beetles lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni amɛha tso lɛ shishi agbɔjɔ. Nibii ni he tse ni akɛ la etsu nii yɛ mli lɛ adumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves develop yellowish patches and twist out of shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties from certified sources prevents this sickness from spreading in your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛ hei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn brown, then black, and dry up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛkɛ lɛ amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra shade branches and removing infected pods helps keep air flowing and stops the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ amli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle he ni ekpa helai.

english: Why are my garden egg flowers falling off the branches instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when plants suffer from excessive heat, dry soil, or attacks by insect pests like thrips. Ensuring adequate watering and controlling insect pests encourages flowers to set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ni abaakwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Should I get my land tested before I start planting mango trees on it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi mango tso dumɔ?

english: Yes, testing your soil before planting helps you know if the land has the right nutrients and depth for mango roots, saving you time and money before you make a big investment.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa dani aduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛ mlibotemɔ ni sa kɛha mango shishifãi. Enɛ haa okɛ be kɛ shika tsuuu nii dani okɛ shika babaoo woɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is good enough for growing mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ mango tsei?

english: Mangoes need deep, well-drained soil that does not hold excess water after heavy rain. Checking your soil depth and getting a basic land test will tell you if your plot is suitable.
ga: Mango he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehiɛɛɛ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishijee kaa baatsɔɔ bo kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ sa.

english: Is it better to look for naturally good land or can I just fix poor land with fertilizer for my fruit trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oootao adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ kpakpa loo obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii asaa shikpɔŋ gbonyo kɛha tsei ni woɔ yibii?

english: It is much better to choose suitable land from the beginning. While fertilizer adds nutrients, it cannot fix bad soil structure like hard rock layers or land that floods easily.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛjɛ shishijee. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he moŋ Shi enyɛŋ esaa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii tamɔ tɛi ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why is soil testing important for someone starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa he hiaa mɛi ni jeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Soil testing shows you what nutrients are already in the ground and what is missing, so you only buy the specific fertilizers your crops actually need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ pɛ oheɔ.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted mango tree to start producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start bringing fruit little by little after about three years, but they take five to seven years to reach full production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi fiofio yɛ aaafee afii etɛ sɛɛ. Shi ebaahe afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo dani ewo yibii kwraa.

english: My young tree has been in the ground for a few years and is growing very slowly, what can I do to help it?
ga: Mitso bibioo lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ afii fioo komɛi ni eho ni edaa blɛoo waa. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ matsɔ maye mabua?

english: You can help a slow-growing tree by clearing weeds around its base, mulching to keep moisture in the soil, and applying the right fertilizer during the rainy season.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye obua tsei ni daraa blɛoo lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ ni ooojie kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ooowo nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa afata he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why do fruit trees seem to grow so slowly in their first few years after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ daraa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the first few years, the tree spends most of its energy underground developing strong, deep roots. Once the root system is established, the top of the tree begins to grow much faster.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ eba shi pɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yiteŋ baaje shishi eda oya kwraa.

english: Does putting extra fertilizer on a young tree make it produce fruit faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tsei bibii amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛwo yibii oya?

english: No, over-fertilizing a young tree can burn its delicate roots and harm it. Fertilizer should be given in small, balanced amounts to support natural growth, not to force early fruiting.
ga: Dabi, tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eye tso lɛ awui. Esa akɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni sa koni eye ebua adebɔɔ mli dalɛ. Kaaha ewo yibii oya.

english: What basic steps can I take to care for my young fruit trees so they survive their early years?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee koni makwɛ midumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli?

english: Protect young trees from farm animals, keep the base free of weeds, provide water during long dry spells, and watch for early signs of pests on the leaves.
ga: Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe. Ha jwɛi akafee shishitoo lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli ni otao mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the right time to start applying fertilizer to a young crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awomɔ shishi?

english: You should wait until the plant has recovered from transplanting and shows new green leaves—usually a few weeks to a month after planting—before applying light fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ená baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa baafata he

english: If I clear my brush by burning it, does that help my crops grow better in this soil?
ga: Kɛji mijie jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ shãa nɔ Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ?

english: Burning cleared bush gives a quick burst of ash fertilizer, but it burns away the rich organic layer of the soil and kills beneficial soil insects. Over time, burning makes the soil dry out faster and lowers your crop yields.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ baaha sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atswa oya. Mohu ɔ, e shãa zugba a mi níhi nɛ a ngɛ mi ɔ, nɛ e gbeɔ zugba a mi koolohi nɛ a he hia a. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya ni ebaaha onibii ni oduɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I prevent goats from eating my young cassava plants on my newly cleared land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tooi anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Goats love young cassava leaves because they are tender. You can plant living fences using thick, unpalatable hedgerow plants like Jatropha or Gliricidia around your farm boundary to create a natural physical barrier that keeps goats out.
ga: Tooi sumɔɔ ŋmei baai bibii ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei bibii ni mli tse ni esaaa tamɔ jatropha loo glicidia abɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ adu ŋtayaa ni hiɛ ka. Koni afee adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni haaa tooi lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, shallow roots and cannot survive direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat stress until their roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni enyɛŋ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the roots under the ground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of food storage below ground. Balancing the soil nutrients helps the plant focus energy on swelling its tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛ hewalɛ maa bulbs ni efuu lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I plant my maize seeds right after the very first rainfall of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three consistent rains so the soil holds steady moisture. Planting after the very first rain is risky because a long dry spell usually follows, which dries up and kills the sprouting seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ji oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and fail to make big cobs when I put four or five seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ waa ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji beni mikɛ ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed its own space allows the roots to spread and grow strong stalks with heavy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hegbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa ni ŋmeii ni tsii yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants developing ragged holes with small dirt trapped inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ muji bibii lɛ? Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ baa lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides deep inside the leaf funnel during the day and feeds on the young leaves. Catching them early with neem oil or targeted treatments stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to full sunlight, which helps the plant make food efficiently. It also lifts the foliage away from hot, damp soil, protecting the plant from fungal rots and leading to bigger tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits when the hot dry wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato plants to lose moisture faster than their roots can drink water. To save energy and survive the heat stress, the plant sheds its flowers instead of feeding growing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii ni miida.

english: How does leaving dry leaves and cut grass on top of my soil help my crops during hot days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni afo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves creates mulch, which acts like a blanket. It blocks the direct sun from baking the ground, keeps the root area cool, and prevents water from evaporating out of the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ashã. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Does stripping off some leaves from my plants really help them bring out flowers?
ga: Ani baai lɛ amli gbalamɔ kɛjɛɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fɔfɔi?

english: Yes, removing certain leaves reduces the energy the plant spends on maintaining excess green foliage, redirecting essential nutrients toward flower production.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai komɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yaa fɔfɔi afeemɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my crop leaves looking big and healthy, but the plant refuses to produce any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ? Shi tso lɛ kpooɔ akɛ ebaafɔ fɔfɔi kwraa?

english: When a plant puts all its energy into growing thick leaves, it may delay flowering. Carefully trimming select leaves signals to the plant that it is time to transition from growing leaves to blooming.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsu baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe nii lɛ Ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ afo. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni ahala lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ etsake kɛjɛ baai ni miida lɛ mli kɛya fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Is there a safe time during the crop's life to remove leaves without hurting the harvest?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ tso ko wala be mli ni esa akɛ ajie baai ni efiteee ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Leaf removal should typically happen just before the expected flowering period so the plant shifts its main energy to producing buds rather than extra stems.
ga: Yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, esa akɛ ajie baai lɛ dani fɔfɔi be ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ tsakeɔ ehewalɛ titri lɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii amli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: If I try to force my crops to flower early, will it destroy the plant?
ga: Kɛ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni manyɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra Ani ebaakpata tso lɛ hiɛ?

english: If proper techniques like controlled pruning are used, it encourages healthy flowers without damage. However, pulling leaves off roughly or at the wrong time can stress and damage the plant.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋaai ni sa tsu nii, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akudɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee amɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Aloo be ni esaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ahao ni efite nii.

english: What information should I write down or remember when a sudden disease hits my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ saji esa akɛ maŋmala loo makai kɛji hela ko ni ba trukaa lɛ ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: You should note the exact day you first noticed the change, how the damage started, and which parts of the crop showed symptoms first so an expert can diagnose it correctly.
ga: Esa akɛ okadi gbi pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔse tsakemɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ. Te fitemɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ehaa tɛŋŋ? ni tso lɛ fã ni jieɔ okadii lɛ akpo klɛŋklɛŋ? Bɔni afee ni ŋaalɔi lɛ anyɛ ana hela lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does an agricultural officer always ask me when and how a problem started on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛbiɔ mi be kɛ bɔ ni naagbai je shishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Knowing the exact timeline and early symptoms helps officers determine whether the issue is caused by a fast-spreading pest, a soil disease, or weather changes.
ga: Kɛ́ onukpai lɛ le be pɔtɛɛ ni hela lɛ heɔ kɛ shishijee okadii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnaa kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya, hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba lɛ ba.

english: Why do flowers drop off my crop before they can form into full fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers can fall off due to heavy weather stress, lack of nutrients, or because the plant does not have enough strength to carry both excess leaves and new fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa mli baa, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakpɛlɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ aduawai heei fɛɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I correctly learn a new farm technique if I have never done it before?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makase okwaayeli he ŋaai heei jogbaŋŋ? Kɛji mifeee nakai dã

english: The best way is to watch an extension officer or experienced farmer perform the process step-by-step in the field so you can replicate the exact movements on your farm.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okwɛ sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ loo okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni enyiɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okase bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can I get a better harvest simply by watching and copying how experts work on demonstration farms?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa kɛtsɔ bɔ ni ŋaalɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛmɔ kɛ amɛhe mfonirifeemɔ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Yes, watching live demonstrations allows you to learn practical skills like proper trimming, spacing, and application timing that cannot easily be explained by words alone.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni okwɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ trimming kpakpa, gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋ, kɛ be. ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ wiemɔi pɛ atsɔɔ mli mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop is matured enough to start flowering naturally?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Crops usually signal they are ready to flower when stem growth slows down, leaves reach full size, and tiny flower buds start forming where the leaves meet the branch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo fɔfɔi kɛji tso lɛ yitso lɛ dalɛ tee hiɛ fioo. Baai lɛ eyi obɔ. kɛ fɔfɔii bibii Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ yɛ he ni baai lɛ kɛ tsei niji lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the cocoa beans inside my pods are developing properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ mi-pods lɛ amli lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: When cocoa trees receive good care, the cocoa inside fills out the pod completely, producing beautiful, well-developed beans with rich pulp that are ideal for processing.
ga: Kɛ́ akwɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Kookoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eyiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛfɛo ni ehiɛ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to harvest my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: You know it is time to harvest when the cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange, indicating that the cocoa inside is fully mature.
ga: O le kaa be su nɛ e sa nɛ o kpa ní benɛ kookoo ɔmɛ a su tsake kɛ je e ngɔmi loo tsuru nɛ mi kuɔ mi ɔ kɛ ya ngɔmi loo ngmli tso ɔ mi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbɔ kwraa.

english: Is it bad if I harvest my cocoa pods before they are fully mature?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, harvesting too early means the cocoa inside has not had enough time to fully develop, resulting in small, flat beans with poor flavor and lower market value.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ enako be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo yibii lɛ yɛ bibioo, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehiii, ni jarayeli jara eba shi.

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the well-developed beans inside to start germinating or rotting, ruining an otherwise beautiful and healthy pod.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɛo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the proper way to remove a cocoa pod from the tree during harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: The best method is to hold the pod steady with one hand and use a sharp knife to cut cleanly right at the stalk junction where the pod connects to the tree.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ enɛ ji ni akɛ nine kome atsu nii ni akɛfi tsɔne lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tsɔne ni mli wa atsu nii ni Ofo tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he ni pod lɛ kɛ tso lɛ kpaa gbee yɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just pull or twist cocoa pods off the branch with my bare hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ miniji ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ gbalaa loo mikɛtsakeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Twisting or pulling rips off the flower cushion on the tree trunk, which is the delicate spot where future flowers and next season's pods must grow.
ga: Kɛ́ atsɔ mli loo agbala lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi, he ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ehe baahia ni fɔfɔi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ kɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to use a sharp knife when harvesting cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ kakla ni naa wa atsu nii lɛ? Koni akpa kookoo ŋmeii?

english: A sharp knife makes a clean, swift cut at the stem junction without stripping the bark, which prevents fungal infections from entering the tree.
ga: Kakla ni naa wa baafo tso lɛ nine lɛ oya, ni ehe tse ni ejieee tso lɛ yibii lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akabote tso lɛ mli.

english: Where exactly on the stem am I supposed to cut when harvesting a pod?
ga: Mɛɛ tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafo kɛji mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: You should make your cut right at the narrow junction of the stalk, leaving the raised flower cushion on the tree trunk completely intact.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo yɛ he ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ, ni oshi fɔfɔi akushin ni awo nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛ akafite kwraa.

english: Why should I hold the cocoa pod with my hand while cutting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ minine amɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli beni mifoɔ lɛ?

english: Holding the pod keeps it steady so your knife makes a precise cut at the junction without accidentally slipping and wounding the tree trunk or dropping the pod.
ga: Pod ni akɛhiɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɔne lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. koni tsɔne lɛ anyɛ afo pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hei ni gbɛjegbɛi lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ ni ekɛ oshara akatswa ni ekɛ tso ko atswa loo ekɛ pod lɛ akashwie shi.

english: How does my harvesting technique affect the health of my cocoa tree for the next season?
ga: Te gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mikpaa nii lɛ baaná mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahewalɛ nɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Using a knife to cut carefully at the junction protects the tree's cushion nodes, allowing the tree to stay healthy and continuously yield well-developed cocoa pods year after year.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni gbɛjegbɛi lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ kushɛŋ hei lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyaa nɔ ewoɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni edara jogbaŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: My land used to give me many bags of maize, but now the harvests are small. Why is my soil losing its strength?
ga: Kulɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ haa mi ŋmãa kotokui babaoo. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ, nibii fioo pɛ afeɔ. Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its feeding power when crops absorb its nutrients season after season without those nutrients being replaced. Adding poultry manure, compost, or fertilizer helps restore the soil's natural strength so it can feed plants again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ ŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ nakai niyenii lɛ tsakeee. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifãi, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni enyɛ eye ebua tsei ekoŋŋ.

english: I have leftover fertilizer from last year that got a bit hard. Is its strength completely gone, or can I still use it on my cassava?
ga: Miyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ni wa waa. Ani hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ etee loo obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei atsu nii lolo?

english: Even if older fertilizer hardens or loses a bit of its original strength due to damp air, it is still useful. Breaking the lumps and applying it to your soil will still give your crops helpful nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ mli wa loo eshishijee hewalɛ fioo po yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ hewɔ lɛ. Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lolo. Kɛ́ akumɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lolo.

english: Can I plant the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest, or should I buy new certified seeds from the store?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase yɛ shwapo ko mli?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and tend to yield less food. Certified seeds are specially prepared to resist diseases and grow stronger, giving you a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛdara waa. Ehaa okpaa nii babaoo

english: Yellow, curled leaves usually mean the plant is stressed—either tiny insects are sucking its strength from under the leaves, or the plant is hungry because the soil lacks nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Kɛji akɛ eji kooloo bibioo ko ni miihe hewalɛ kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ ashishi Aloo tsei miiye hɔmɔ ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Drooping is their natural way of protecting themselves, and they usually stand back up as the sun cools.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ohiŋmɛii ni oootsi kɛjɛ ohe lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ obuɔ ohe he. Ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛte shi kɛji hulu lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: My pepper plants have plenty of flowers, but why do the flowers keep falling off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mi pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is under stress from high heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save its strength for survival rather than fruit production.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ miihao amɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni esaaa mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the cassava plants I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmei tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and naturally aggressive, meaning they take up water and soil nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early stops them from stealing the food your cassava needs to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni amɛfeɔ basabasa yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Ehe saamɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa bo koni okɛdu o-cassava lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the lower green branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Removing lower extra branches allows the plant to direct its strength and nutrients straight into growing big, healthy fruit instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam plants signal maturity above ground when their leaves and vines naturally stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up. This shows that the plant has finished storing food in the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa dalɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eshishigbɛ tsɔji lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why should I grow orange-fleshed sweet potatoes instead of the traditional white ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ najiaŋ yɛ blema ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes are rich in Vitamin A, which builds strong immunity and improves eyesight, especially for young children and mothers, making them a high-value food crop for family health.
ga: Vitamin A babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli, ni enɛ haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni hiŋmɛii lɛ naa nii jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ kɛha gbekɛbii bibii kɛ amɛnyɛmɛi. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni aduɔ ni he hiaa waa kɛha weku lɛ hewalɛnamɔ.

english: Does growing and eating yellow maize give my family better health benefits than white maize?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni miduɔ ni miyeɔ lɛ haa miweku lɛ náa hewalɛ fe ŋmãa yɛŋ?

english: Yes, yellow maize naturally contains Vitamin A which promotes good health and vision, whereas white maize mostly provides basic energy without those extra essential vitamins.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, vitamin A yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔŋ mli, ni haa mɔ náa hewalɛ kɛ hiŋmɛi kpakpa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yɛŋ babaoo haa shishijee hewalɛ ni vitamini krokomɛi ni he hiaa fataaa he lɛ.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers encouraging us to grow green leafy vegetables like kontomire and amaranth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contomir kɛ spinach lɛ?

english: Green leafy vegetables contain vital nutrients, iron, and vitamins that protect the body against sickness, ensuring your family stays healthy alongside staple starches.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa waa, dade, kɛ vitamini ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe lɛ yɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli amli. Ye obua oweku lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛfata ŋmɔtɔ titri lɛ he.

english: How does harvesting my food crops at the right maturity stage affect their health benefits?
ga: Te mi niyenii tso lɛ ni mikpaa yɛ be ni sa mli ni edaa lɛ saa ehewalɛ he sɛɛnamɔi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harvesting crops at their full maturity ensures they hold the highest concentration of vitamins and good nutrients, whereas overripe crops lose nutritional value and spoil faster.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akpaa beni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa amɛnáa vitamini kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ naaa niyenii kpakpa ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my vegetable plants turn yellow and stop growing well during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that plants are stressed by lack of water and nutrients; without water, roots cannot absorb the essential soil elements required to maintain healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why do my papaya and fruit trees drop their flowers before setting fruit when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya kɛ aduawai tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Trees shed flowers during extreme heat as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water and protect the main stem from drying out.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nu nɔ ni abuɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is missing the essential nutrients my crops need to be healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: If crops grow slowly, have pale or spotted leaves, or produce small fruits, the soil is lacking essential plant food and needs compost or manure to restore its health.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ehaa yibii bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha ehewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I try planting uncommon crops like soybeans on part of my farm instead of only maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi tamɔ soybeans akwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa pɛ

english: Soybeans are packed with protein for good health and also naturally feed nitrogen into the soil, which restores land fertility for your other crops.
ga: Soybeans eyi kɛ protein kɛha hewalɛ kpakpa ni ekɛ nitrogen hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is moringa considered a special health crop to plant around the home garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ moringa akɛ eji hewalɛnamɔ he tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni esa akɛ adu yɛ shia abɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Moringa leaves are loaded with a dense variety of vitamins and minerals that defend the body against illnesses, making it a powerful medicinal food crop.
ga: Vitamin kɛ mineral srɔtoi ni buɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe lɛ eyi Moringa baai lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsofafeemɔ niyenii tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to grow leguminous crops like cowpeas together with cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kome?

english: Cowpeas grow quickly to cover the soil, protecting cassava from drying heat while adding natural nutrients that support overall plant health and yield.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ daa oya ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ ŋmei he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ fataa he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when too much rainwater settles on my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater pools on the land without proper drainage, it starves the roots of air and causes fungi to grow, which rots the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii akwɛ̃. ni haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell if I am giving my pepper plants too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ?

english: If water forms puddles around the stems and the leaves turn yellow and drop off, you are overwatering. Soil should be moist like a wrung-out sponge, not soaked with standing water.
ga: Kɛji nu fee ŋmeii ni bɔle tso lɛ he ni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oowo nu babaoo tsɔ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ sponji ni mli edɔ. Kaawo nu ni mli ejɔ mli.

english: Why do we make high earthen mounds when planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔfeɔ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ́ wɔmiidu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Raised mounds keep the soil loose so yam tubers can grow large, while allowing heavy rain to spill off the sides so water does not gather around the tubers and decay them.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ajɛ sɛɛgbɛ koni nu akabɔle bulb lɛ he ni efite.

english: What happens to my farm soil when heavy rains wash down a sloped field?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni nɛ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ?

english: Unprotected rainwater sweeps away the dark, rich top layer of soil where crops get their food. Planting across the slope slows down the rushing water and keeps your soil in place.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni abuuu he lɛ hoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ duŋ ni woɔ yibii lɛ he ni akɛ niyenii haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to measure exact distances between maize seeds instead of just scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asusu he pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ ŋmãa lɛ ashwã kɛkɛ

english: Giving each maize plant its own space prevents them from fighting over soil nutrients and sunlight. Correct spacing results in bigger cobs and a higher harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ he akaŋshii. Gbɛ ni ja ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of using our traditional random scattering method?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ wɔ kusum gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajaa nibii amli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Planting in straight rows allows equal sunlight and water for every crop, makes weeding much easier, and ensures your farm produces more food overall without extra cost.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nu lɛ yeɔ egbɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow well if I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often tricks the dry ground, leaving hot soil underneath. Waiting for steady rains ensures the soil stays cool and moist enough for seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa egbiɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ shishi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Is there a simple way I can protect my crop soil from drying out without spending money?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mi-pot sũ lɛ he koni ekagbi ni mikɛ shika babaoo efiteee?

english: Yes, you can cover the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching. This free practice shades the dirt and keeps moisture from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha onibii ahe. Nɛkɛ nifeemɔ ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ muji naa ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees actually increase my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa mi yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess leaves and branches so the tree can focus its energy directly into growing cocoa pods, while letting light in to keep pod diseases away.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ ajwɛŋmɔ ahi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa la boteɔ mli koni helai akabote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to remove tiny weeds early when they seem harmless?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ majie jwɛi bibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ, eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni amɛyeee mɔ awui moŋ?

english: Tiny weeds grow fast and secretly steal water and food away from your crops. Clearing them while small takes little effort and prevents your main crop from becoming weak.
ga: Jwɛi bibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ teemɔŋ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ, eheɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo ko pɛ, ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What is a cover crop, and how does it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cover crops are plants grown primarily to protect and nourish the soil rather than for harvest. They act like a carpet over your bare dirt, keeping heavy rains from washing away good topsoil, stopping weeds from taking over, and keeping moisture in the ground.
ga: Cover crops ji tsei ni aduɔ titri koni akɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni akɛha lɛ niyenii moŋ fe ni akɛbaakpa nii. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ kapɛti ni ha oshikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my groundnuts and beans seem to make the soil better for my next crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii kɛ mi ŋmeii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family. They have a natural ability to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds whatever crop you plant after them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he. Amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I plant cover crops between my main food crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ko nɔ lɛ yɛ mi niyenii titrii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting low-growing cover crops between rows of taller crops like maize or millet helps shade the soil and keep weeds down without competing for sunlight with your main harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ fioo ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yeee akaŋ yɛ hulu la he.

english: Why should I plant different crop varieties instead of sticking to just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei srɔtoi babaoo moŋ fe ekome pɛ?

english: Planting different varieties protects you against risk. If one variety gets attacked by pests or suffers during a dry spell, the other varieties may be tougher and still yield a harvest to feed your family and sell.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ Ebaabu ohe kɛjɛ osharai ahe. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua tso ko loo enaa amanehulu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, Ekolɛ tso kroko baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo yibii lolo ni okɛbaahã oweku lɛ niyenii ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: What does crop diversification mean for a smallholder farmer?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha okwaafoi bibii?

english: Crop diversification means growing a mix of different crops—like grains, legumes, and roots—on your farm instead of relying on a single crop. It gives you multiple sources of food and income throughout the year and keeps your soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi tsɔɔ akɛ ooodu nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii, tamɔ ŋmaa, ŋmeii, kɛ shishifãi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii kome nɔ. Ehaa niyenii kɛ shika srɔtoi yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is millet a good crop to plant if my region does not get much rain?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ babaoo yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, millet is a very tough grain that thrives in hot weather and dry soil. It develops deep roots quickly to find water underground, making it a reliable crop during seasons with low rainfall.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ji dumɔwu ko ni wa waa ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ekwɛɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ oya koni ena shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature in three months while others take much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo fe nakai lɛ?

english: Different varieties are bred for different climate conditions. Fast-maturing varieties are designed to yield food quickly before rains stop, while longer-maturing varieties use full seasons to grow bigger roots and produce higher yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ kooloi srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Afee tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛwo niyenii oya dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛná shishifãi wuji kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why do bean plants spread out and cover the ground so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Many bean plants naturally grow low to the ground and spread their leaves wide to catch sunlight. This creeping behavior helps shade the surrounding soil, keeping it cool and moist while choking out competing weeds.
ga: Bean tsei babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa babaoo koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ shwiemɔ su nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni ojieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flowers into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the stems bend down and push into the soil. Groundnut pods actually grow and ripen beneath the surface where they are safe from heat and pests.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee lɛ pollination lɛ, tso lɛ baakoto ni ekɛ ehe baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut pods lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi, he ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: How do I know which crop variety is best suited for my soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Different varieties prefer different soil conditions; for example, groundnuts need loose, sandy soil so their pods can grow underground easily, while millet tolerates drier, harder soil. Observing your soil type helps match the right seed to your land.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi srɔtoi. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋã he miihia ŋmei bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui ni sa lɛ kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that protects young cocoa from sun damage and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key food they need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer when the soil is moist helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Dark spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium and uneven soil watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant absorb the calcium it needs to build healthy fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are at least 8 to 12 months old. Avoid stems with holes, fungal growths, or insect damage so your new crop grows strong roots.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni he wa kɛjɛ tsei ni kɛ hoo lɛ eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bu lɛ ahe. fungal dalɛ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Enɛ baaha onibii heei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large fruits or heavy grains.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadu aduawai wuji loo dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Can I plant beans on the same plot of land with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful because bean plants trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and improves soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii tsei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps moisture in the soil, stops weeds from growing, and prevents the sun from overheating the roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tsɔ

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and tiny worms inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: Holes in maize leaves and shoots are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Catching them early and applying recommended pest treatments or neem oil sprays keeps them from destroying the growing point of the corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ baai kɛ yiteŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Vegetable leaves curl up during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, stopping water from evaporating too fast. If they bounce back in the evening, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Aduawai baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkaho?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not flooded, ideally right after a light rain or during cool morning hours. Applying it on dry soil can burn the roots, while heavy downpours will wash the food away before plants can drink it.
