ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ fioo loo yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii lɛ dani tsei lɛ nuɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or when too much water around the roots stops them from breathing. Giving them proper food through manure or fertilizer helps them turn green again to make food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Shishifãi babaoo kpaɔ mumɔ Kɛ́ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ koni amɛfee niyenii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I harvest more food from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting too close makes your crops fight with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow strong and produce bigger, heavier yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have a special ability to take natural food from the air and fix it into the soil. When you harvest them, that extra food stays behind to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ fɛ̃i yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. beni okpa lɛ Nakai niyenii kroko lɛ baakã sɛɛ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants dropping their bottom leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves to save water when the weather gets hot and dry. The plant rests to protect itself, and once the rain returns, it sprouts new leaves and continues growing underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Tsei lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Ebaakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to catch energy and form big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot soil where they could rot or get diseased.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ lɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by drinking the water and taking the soil nutrients faster than your crops can. Clearing weeds leaves all the food and moisture for your crops to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ onibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛŋɔ oya fe otsei lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shĩɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sɛɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When too many small suckers grow around the main stem, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures your main plantain bunch grows large.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-plantains titri lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade from plantains or larger trees to shelter them from harsh heat and keep the soil moist until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or damage from tiny insects. Keeping the soil evenly moist and covered with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects sucking the sap from underneath the leaves. Protecting the plants with natural sprays like neem water keeps these insects away so leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ tamɔ neem nu lɛ bu tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Koni ebaa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves in an inverted 'V' pattern usually means your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need plenty of nitrogen to stay green and produce full ears, so adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or urea, or well-rotted manure, will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmã tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo toi ni eyi obɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does my extension officer tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani wɔdu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them with maize naturally fertilizes your land, giving the next crop free food to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tso ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ náa niyenii ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—they burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving permanent shade trees protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why is it helpful for me to spread dry grass or leaves around the base of my tomato plants during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ ashishitoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi.

english: Spreading dry organic matter around plants is called mulching. It acts like a blanket over the soil, trapping moisture so you water less often, keeping the ground cool, and preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ nibii ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Locks yɛ moisture mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting, curling upwards, and staying tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe, ebɔle ehe, ni eyɛ bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap, or by a virus these insects transmit. Sprays made from neem leaf extracts or recommended pesticides help control these insects early.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ latex lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ feɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown sawdust-like dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the central stem whorl to feed on soft new leaves. Checking your field early and applying neem powder, wood ash, or recommended insecticides into the center whorl kills the worms before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli mra ni okɛ neem powder, tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ koni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When too many young shoots (suckers) grow around a plantain tree, they compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning back excess suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main plant grows a huge, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛkɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put strong wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ni wa awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight efficiently for food production. Staking keeps leaves dry and healthy, which leads to much larger yam tubers underground compared to unstaked plants.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mostly due to extreme hot weather, dry soil, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil evenly watered and encouraging bees by keeping flower borders around your farm helps tomato flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni owo ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee fɔfɔi husui yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he koni eye ebua tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without spoiling them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 8 and 12 months after planting. You will know they are ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top, showing the energy has moved to swelling the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo baahi shi aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ efã ni eha ŋmeii lɛ efo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is essential plant food, or the soil has too much water around the roots. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark black spots at the bottom before they can even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet, preventing the plant from taking up calcium properly.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Ebaa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea leaves more than the other crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-cowpea baai lɛ fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Cowpeas are naturally attractive to pests because their leaves and flowers are rich in protein and sweet nectar. You can manage pests by planting early in the season or using safe, recommended crop sprays right when flowers start to appear.
ga: Cowpea ji tso ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Ejaakɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛji fɔfɔii je shishi amɛje kpo pɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other on the ridge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This struggle leaves you with weak plants and very thin tubers instead of big, heavy cassava roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ ta nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the ground deeply at least two or three times. Planting after the very first light rain can cause your seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot, dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ be ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ba.

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which is then transferred down to build a large, healthy yam tuber under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, ajieɔ enɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells without water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant focus only on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nu loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baa lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are large and lose water quickly in hot sun. During the dry season, when water in the soil is low, the plant naturally lets its older leaves dry up to save water for its stem and growing center.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara ni kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. yɛ fɛ̃i be mli Beni nu fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei haa baai ni egbɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ he ni edara yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my piece of land produce less harvest every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired and loses its nutrients over time when the same crop is grown repeatedly without a break. Resting the land or rotating crops like groundnuts and beans helps return essential nutrients naturally into the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe loo atsake ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods staying very small with tiny seeds inside this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ daraaa ni dumɔwui bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? hi shi yɛ be nɛɛ mli

english: Cocoa pods remain small if the tree does not get enough water while the pods are developing, or if pests like mirids damage the stems and stop water and nutrients from reaching the growing pods.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids lɛ fiteɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛtsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni miida lɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin stalks with small or empty cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce large, healthy ears of maize.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ feɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can capture direct sunlight to make food. When you stake yams, the leaves spread out better, which feeds the plant and allows larger, heavier tubers to develop underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Beni Okɛ Sweet Potatoes lɛ Woɔ Stake lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava tubers when I plant cassava on the same farm plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that cassava needs from the soil and allows cassava-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmei pɔtɛɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or root damage from waterlogging. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves regain their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi ni efite kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling these pests early using recommended organic or chemical sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to stress from high temperatures, lack of moisture in the soil, or damage by insects like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist through mulching and protecting flowers from pests helps them set fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nibii ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips fiteɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ fɔfɔi ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out quickly under harsh sun and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa shelters the young trees from direct sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Excess rainwater fills up the air spaces in the soil, causing the roots to drown and rot from fungal attacks. Creating high mounds or ridges and ensuring good field drainage prevents water from standing around the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ amli. Gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afee kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekabɔle bulb lɛ he.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes cowpea plants focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers allows the plant to naturally transition into producing flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ fe fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ atsake amɛhe amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the bunch of fruit starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy bunches against strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo or wooden prop takes the weight off the roots until the fruit matures.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua jwɛi ni mli tse ni teɔ shi woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso fi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ aba shi kɛyashi yibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from dying. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing its underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why does my maize grow tall but produce very small ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ shi toi lɛ ji bibioo lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall with small ears when plants are planted too close together or lack nitrogen in the soil. The plants end up competing for sunlight and food instead of directing energy into forming big grains.
ga: Abele daa kɛ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ tsei nɛɛ ashi akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ wu nguanguahi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the air gets too hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet, or when there are no bees and insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii bɛ he fɛɛ he. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Without wooden prop stakes to support the stem, strong winds easily push them down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛji tso ko bɛ ni fiɔ esɛɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsi tso lɛ shi oya.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a viral sickness spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ hela ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather and damp, overcrowded cocoa farms with too much shade.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: White spots are a sign of powdery mildew, a plant fungus that develops when plants are too close together and air cannot flow freely between them in hot, humid weather.
ga: He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji powder mildew he okadi. Enɛ ji tso mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yam tubers become twisted or small when planted in hard, compact soil. Yams need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil so the tubers can expand easily underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii loo bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo.

english: Why must I remove weeds around my crops while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have small, weak roots that easily lose the fight against weeds for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures the young crop gets all the food it needs.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Ehaa onyɛɛɛ ote shi owo hulu la ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ni nu lɛ waaa yɛ jwɛi anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft instead of folding into hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ hiɔ shi blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefolɔ efee bɔɔlu ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form hard heads if they do not get enough water consistently during growth, or if high temperatures force the plant to grow too fast without packing its inner leaves tightly.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ daa oya tsɔ ni ekɛ mligbɛ baai lɛ ebɔko he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade from larger trees or plantains to shield them, the intense sun burns their soft leaves and dries out their shallow roots before they can fully establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni jɛ tsei wuji loo dumɔwui amli ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni eha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ aba. Egbiɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. When crops do not get enough nutrients from the soil, they cannot make green leaf material, causing them to turn yellow and grow weak.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Enyɛŋ efee baai eŋɔli nibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon even when the ground has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ́ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing moisture too quickly in the strong sun. It is their natural way of saving water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli hulutsoo baa.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their underground roots fight each other for soil food, water, and space. Giving them enough breathing room allows the roots to spread out freely and grow big, fat tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu lɛ mli, kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ aha amɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛmu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ loo.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience severe stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of proper plant food. The plant drops its flowers to save energy so it can stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso niyenii ni sa ni bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do tiny holes appear all over my cabbage leaves right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Rain causes young crops to grow tender new leaves, which attract insects like caterpillars and beetles. These pests feed on the fresh green foliage, creating holes that make it harder for the plant to catch sunlight and make food.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ baai heei ni mli tse. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Enɛ haa buji baa ni ehaa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaná hulu la ni amɛhoo niyenii.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there looks like enough room on the farm for both?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji akɛ he ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and aggressively steal sunlight, drinking water, and soil nutrients before your crop roots can reach them. Even if there is physical space, the weeds underground starve your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu ni anuɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Eyɛ mli akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ he ko yɛ moŋ Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hu haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii.

english: Why should I trim off the lower branches and extra shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots draw heavy amounts of food and energy away from the main stem. Cutting them off forces the plant to send all its water and nutrients straight into growing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ afo amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ mli ni ewoɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Maize sucks out the exact same food nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly drains the ground completely empty, making the soil weak unless you rest the field or plant leguminous crops like beans to rebuild the soil.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. gbɔjɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ja okɛ ohe ejɔ ohe loo odu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii koni okɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer right against the stem of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly touching a young stem burns the plant's delicate skin and roots like hot chemical water. Fertilizer must be placed a short distance away in the soil so the roots can drink it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni baa tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Taakɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ji lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo sũ lɛ mli ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ akabɔ fioo koni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I mix different varieties of rice seeds together when planting them in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ futuɔ amɛhe kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties grow at different speeds and mature at different times. If you mix them in one field, some plants will be ready to harvest while others are still green, leading to low yield and poor grain quality that buyers will not want.
ga: Omɔ henɔi srɔtoi daa oya oya, ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Kɛji okɛ amɛ futu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Tsei komɛi efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔɔ.

english: If I get rice seeds brought from another country, will they automatically grow well on my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji miná ŋmãa ni akɛba kɛjɛ maŋ kroko nɔ lɛ Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not always. Seeds from other countries are adapted to their local climate and soil. Without testing them first, they might fail to withstand Ghana's specific rainfall patterns, heat, or local crop diseases.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui ni jɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kaa ko bɛ klɛŋklɛŋ Ekolɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛdamɔ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ, dɔlɛ loo tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: What is the actual difference between brown rice and white rice after harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ teŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Brown rice is the whole grain with only the hard outer hull removed, leaving the nutrient-rich bran layer intact. White rice has had both the outer hull and the nutritious bran layer polished off during milling.
ga: Brown rice ji ŋmaa muu ni ajieɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ pɛ. Bran layer ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Ajieɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my rice grains break into tiny pieces when I take them to the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii lɛ? Beni okɛ penti tsɔnei baa maŋsɛɛ?

english: Grains break during milling if they were harvested when too dry, or if they were dried too quickly under harsh, direct sunlight. Sun-drying your harvested paddy slowly in the shade helps keep the grains whole.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baakumɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛgbi tsɔ. aloo kɛji egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ni aaagbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fiofio Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ akayimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: Does planting my rice or maize too close together make the grains smaller?
ga: Ani ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee bibii?

english: Yes. When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to produce big, full grains.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some plants in my rice field grow very tall while others stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu feɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Uneven growth usually happens because soil nutrients and water are not spread evenly across your field, or because low spots collect too much water while higher spots dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa ejaakɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ ejaraaa he fɛɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. aloo akɛni hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I tell that my rice crop is fully ready for harvest just by looking at it?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni oookwɛ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Your rice is ready when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn from green to a golden-yellow color, and the grains at the bottom of the stalk feel hard when pressed with your fingernail.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo beni o-rice yitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ akɛ nine ŋmei mimɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do birds attack my rice field much more than my neighbor's field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If your rice variety matures earlier or later than your neighbors' crops, birds in the area will gather on your field because it is the only mature food available. Planting around the same time as your neighbors spreads the bird damage across all farms.
ga: Kɛji o-rice henɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya loo ekwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo fe okutsoŋnyo tsei lɛ Kuu lɛ mli okpoi baaba oŋmɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ no pɛ ji niyenii ni ahoo ni yɔɔ. Dumɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni okutsoŋnyo lɛ gbɛɔ okpoi afitemɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce fewer grains if I plant rice on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dumɔwui faaa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Rice draws specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients and allows rice-specific pests and weeds to build up in the soil.
ga: Omɔ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ji ŋmãa pɛ lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my grain crops when there is a long dry spell right when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cereal tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ be kakadaŋŋ ko ba beni amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage for grain crops. A lack of water at this time stops the flowers from forming seeds properly, resulting in empty or lightweight grain heads.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmaa tsei. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni ekawo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ feɔ efolo loo amɛhe waaa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space allows sunlight to reach all leaves and lets the roots gather enough food to build large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛbuaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants spread across the ground while my maize grows straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ miida yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally grow sideways to cover the ground, which keeps the soil cool and prevents weed growth. While doing this, cowpeas also capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps nearby crops like maize grow better.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyaa afã koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃. Beni amɛfeɔ enɛ lɛ, tsina ŋmeii hu mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by intense heat, dry soil, or tiny insects like thrips. Watering regularly during hot periods and checking under leaves for pests helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes dark spots to appear on my cocoa pods and turn the whole pod black?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mikookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads in wet, humid, and overly shady conditions. Trimming excess tree branches lets sunlight and air into the farm to dry off the pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ, ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is the plant's way of protecting itself to reduce water loss in strong sun. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they stay curled, it means the soil needs more water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni nu ni efiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why did my maize seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when planted in soil that stays flooded without good drainage. Seeds need moisture to wake up, but if they sit underwater without air in the soil, they suffocate and decay before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ yɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛtara nu shishi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ lɛ mli hu? Dumɔwui lɛ baafo ni amɛbaafite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the ground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack as the expanding roots push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Eshwɛ tso ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and stay short when the soil beneath the mound is hard, compact, or stony. Making deep, soft mounds with loose soil gives the yam room to expand straight downward easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛhi shi kuku kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni sũ ni mli tse yɔɔ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need shade, especially when young, because intense direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Large shade trees protect cocoa from excessive heat and help retain soil moisture, keeping the plants healthy.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo. Titri lɛ kɛ́ eji gbekɛbii Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in the sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, which catches more light and prevents fungal diseases from infected soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enaa la babaoo ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli lɛ naa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires a lot of nitrogen to build strong leaves; without it, the plant steals nutrients from its lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ebaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally feeds the soil, helping the maize grow taller and yield more harvest.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot strips the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like cowpeas restores soil health and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ abɛi helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to bear a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfi tsei niji wuji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce fewer fruit bunches if I cut off too many lower green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji mifo shishigbɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ?

english: Green fronds are the food factories of the oil palm tree. Removing too many healthy green leaves deprives the palm of the energy it needs to form and mature heavy palm fruit bunches.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii lɛ ji mu tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ni eda ni etsɔ tso lɛ yibii ni tsii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy, standing water after rainy days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu ni damɔ shi waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need oxygen in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, suffocating them and encouraging harmful soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛná hela ni amɛfite.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without ever turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or erratic watering, as heat stress stops pollen from fertilizing the flower. Consistent watering during dry spells helps protect flowers so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni ejaaa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔmɔ nii. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and slowing down plant growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiiha tso lɛ dalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under leaves and transmit viruses. Controlling these pests early stops the curling and allows the pepper plant to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ baa. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ baai ashishi ni ekɛ helai baa lɛ Kudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Enɛ baakpa ŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua o-pepper tsei lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to cut down old cocoa trees even if they are still bearing a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei momoi lɛ? No yɛ aduawai fioo komɛi lolo?

english: Old cocoa trees become weak, yield very little fruit, and easily carry diseases like Swollen Shoot Virus. Cutting them down allows you to replant healthy, fast-growing varieties that will produce far more pods in the long run.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ni amɛheɔ helai tamɔ bud swelling virus lɛ oya. Kɛji okɛ amɛ shwie shi lɛ, obaanyɛ odu tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daa oya. Enɛ baaha pods babaoo aba yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How long will it take for my newly planted cocoa seedlings to start producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ aje shishi amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start flowering and bearing small pods within 2 to 3 years if properly cared for, unlike older varieties that took up to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 5 lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers mainly due to heat stress or dry soil. When temperatures are too high or the plant lacks sufficient water, it cannot pollinate its flowers, causing them to dry up and fall off.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hewɔ titri. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔii lɛ awo mli Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi akɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged from heavy rain. Nitrogen gives leaves their rich green color and helps the plant produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Excessive shade and unpruned branches trap moisture around the trees, allowing the disease to spread quickly.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Shade babaoo kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, ni no haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects that stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ada lɛ nɔ

english: How can I know that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity when its lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why does a plantain sucker grow much faster after I harvest and cut down the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sucker dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kwraa beni mikpa ni mifo tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The main stem consumes most of the plant's water and food. Once cut, all the nutrients absorbed by the underground root system go directly into feeding the young sucker.
ga: Tso lɛ yitso lɛ heɔ tso lɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Kɛ́ afo lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them late when the rainy season is almost ending?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miiba naagbee lɛ?

english: Late-planted crops miss the steady moisture needed during flowering and seed formation. Drought during these critical growth stages leads to stunted plants and poor yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ be mli. Hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nɛkɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do young crop seedlings grow so slowly when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from young crop seedlings, effectively starving them and delaying their development.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii amli Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni ehaa amɛshweremɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. When food is short, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining nutrients to the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ yɛ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my maize grow much better during the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in root nodules. When the groundnut leaves and roots decay in the soil, they release free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmei baai kɛ shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow small and weak when weeds grow close to them, even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ woɔ mli moŋ

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer away from your crops. When weeds grow right next to your crops, they absorb the soil nutrients first before crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers dry up and fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree lacks sufficient water, shade, or soil nutrients, or if insects do not pollinate the flowers, the tree naturally sheds them to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Kookoo tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ Tso lɛ baajie hewalɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my tomato plants look weak and wilted during the hot afternoon but bounce back in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Under intense heat, tomato leaves release water vapor faster than their roots can pull water out of the soil. The plant limps to protect itself from losing too much moisture, then recovers once the sun sets and the air cools down.
ga: yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ Tomato baai lɛ jieɔ nu mli lasu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ lɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ pɛ.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, or a virus spread by them. These pests feed on the leaves' juices, causing new growth to become distorted, curled, and stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa dalɛ hee lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ejaaa, nɔ ni ebɔle ehe, ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Roots need oxygen from tiny air pockets in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves soil waterlogged for days, the air pockets fill completely with water, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii amli lɛ. yɛ sũ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ehi shi Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ sũ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farmland when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ midumɔi lɛ anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so crop roots can absorb it. Applying concentrated fertilizer to dry soil can burn roots and waste your input, as the nutrients sit unused on top of the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they are carrying a heavy bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ mihiɛ aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; they rely on shallow surface roots. When a heavy fruit bunch shifts the tree's balance, rain-softened soil or strong winds can easily pull those shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Beni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Nomɛi jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots inside the barn even without soil or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nugbɔ bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: A yam tuber is a living organ holding stored water and energy. When atmospheric conditions become warm, the tuber naturally breaks its resting period and uses its internal food reserves to sprout shoots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Yitso lɛ baafite adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ. ni okɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃

english: What does potassium fertilizer actually do to help my crops like maize and cassava grow better?
ga: Mɛni potassium ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ afee ni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Potassium acts like a health booster for crops. It strengthens plant stems so they do not fall over in strong winds, helps the crop survive dry weather, and improves the size and weight of tubers and grain heads.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ tsei ashishifãi koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. High nitrogen forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why should I avoid applying fertilizer to my rice field right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater washes the fertilizer away before the plant roots have time to absorb it. This wastes your money and washes valuable nutrients off your field into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni okɛ niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ oyale mli lɛ afɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants make the soil healthier for the next crop I plant in the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei tso ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf area exposed to the hot sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekagbi. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my yellowing rice leaves turn green again after I drain stagnant water off the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ efee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ beni mijie nu ni ekã shi kɛjɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice roots need air to breathe. When water sits continuously without draining, the roots choke and cannot absorb nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow. Draining allows air back into the soil so roots can feed normally.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni nu homɔ bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye nii bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems without forming any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme afternoon heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato blossoms. When pollen is ruined by heat, the flowers cannot turn into fruit, so the plant sheds them to save its strength.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji la ni tsoɔ lɛ kpata pollen ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ lɛ bɔni afee ni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural shields, keeping the seedlings cool and moist until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibii. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I stake them on tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛwoɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air where they can catch maximum sunlight to produce food for the tubers. It also keeps leaves off the hot ground and prevents diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha amɛ bulb lɛ. Ebuɔ tsei ahe tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ hu, ni etsiɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why does planting my rice in neat, straight lines give a better yield than scattering seeds randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ja nɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo kpakpa fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every rice plant gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients without crowding each other. It also makes weeding and fertilizer application much easier and more effective.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei fɛɛ naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiii amɛhe. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather when there is too much shade or poor airflow around the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Be mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree is stressed—either from a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, poor rainfall during the dry season, or damage caused by insect pests like capsids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. kɛji akɛ jɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli Nugbɔ ehiii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. loo nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Why do some of my mature cocoa trees die suddenly while the ones next to them stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ gboiɔ lɛ? Eyɛ eŋɔli lolo.

english: Sudden tree death is often caused by Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus or root diseases like white root rot, which block water and food from traveling up the trunk of the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus loo shishifã hela, tamɔ shishifãi yɛŋ ni fiteɔ, ni haaa nu kɛ niyenii aya tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso gbele trukaa baa.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce many pods one year, but very few pods the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, ani nibii fioo pɛ abaajie lɛ kpo?

english: Cocoa yields depend heavily on weather patterns, rainfall timing, and tree energy. A heavy harvest exhausts the tree's stored nutrients, requiring proper feeding and good weather to recover for the next season.
ga: Cocoa feemɔ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔshiimɔ be, kɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ nɔ waa. Nikpamɔ ni tsii haa niyenii ni tso lɛ eto lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ biɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai koni enyɛ ehiɛ aya nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree experiences water stress, lacks nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) on the farm to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, loo kɛji kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does a young cocoa plant take to start producing pods after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing fruits within 2 to 3 years under good care, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Hybrid cocoa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that dry out under full sun and dry winds; they require temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune extra branches and chupons from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ tsei niji krokomɛi ni jɛ cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary growth that steals food from the pods, and opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and air, which reduces fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nibii ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. ni ogbele tso lɛ shishi koni enine ashɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi lɛ nɔ

english: If your cocoa trees grow slowly, produce small pods, or show pale green leaves even when there is enough rainfall, the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium and nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii, loo amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my crop more during the rainy season than the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rainfall causes trees to sprout tender new leaves and shoots, which attract insect pests like capsids and mealybugs looking for food and wet breeding conditions.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ blɛoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii heei. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ mealybugs ni taoɔ niyenii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are these small caterpillars eating up all the leaves on my maize farm so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ miiye baai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: These pests, often called Fall Armyworms, travel and feed in massive groups like an army. They target the tender leaves and inner funnels of young maize plants, so discovering them early before they hide deep in the plant is essential to saving your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, fãa gbɛ ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii yɛ kui wuji amli tamɔ asraafoi akuu. Amɛtutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai bibii kɛ amɛmli gbɛi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtaomɔ mra Dani amɛbaatee amɛhe amɛwo tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ehe miihia ni ohere okpamɔ lɛ yiwala.

english: Why do insects keep returning to attack my crops even after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa koni amɛbatutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ spray shwie shi moŋ

english: Pests return if the spray did not reach their hiding spots under the leaves, if neighboring farms have untreated pests that migrate over, or if you use the same chemical repeatedly, which allows the pests to build up resistance to that medicine.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ eyashɛɛɛ he ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsako amɛ ni fãa kɛyaa jɛmɛ loo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aná tsofa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do pests cause more damage to my crops during dry and warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures help many insect eggs hatch much faster and allow pests to reproduce rapidly. At the same time, heat stresses your crops and makes them weaker, making it easier for pests to feed on them.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ Heat haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Makes it easier for pests to eat plants

english: How can I protect my crops from pests when farm chemicals are too expensive for me to buy regularly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Akɛni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ mahe daa hewɔ lɛ.

english: You can cut chemical costs by combining low-cost methods like clearing weeds early, rotating your crops each season, hand-picking large pests, and using natural sprays like neem leaf extracts before resorting to commercial agrochemicals.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ahe nyɔmɔwoo aba shi kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni jara waaa, tamɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ ni oookɛfata he lɛ nɔ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa be.
