Kɛ onine ajie kooloi wuji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii Dani okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ jarayeli mli.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop medicines together in one sprayer tank?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baafutu yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kome mli?

english: Mixing different farm chemicals without expert guidance can cause chemical reactions that reduce their power, burn your crop leaves, or create harmful fumes that are dangerous for you to breathe in.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli Kɛji ŋaawoo ni he esa bɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni haa hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baa shi lɛ aba. Shãa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai. loo efee lasu ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ́ omu lɛ, eyeɔ bo awui.

english: Why is it better for me to spray crop medicine early in the morning rather than in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ tsofa lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon, strong sunlight causes farm medicines to evaporate into the air before they can kill the pests, and the heat combined with the chemical can scorch leaf tissue. Morning spraying ensures maximum contact while pests are actively feeding.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ. Ni dɔlɛ ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ashã. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ ehe kpo babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling and yellowing leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids. As they feed on your plants, they spread plant viruses and drain the nutrients your crop needs to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Beni amɛyeɔ otsei lɛ Ebaagbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwa tsei lɛ amli ni ebaajie niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very leafy and tall but dropping all their flowers without fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ baa ni kɛlɛ waa lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer forces tomato plants to focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of fruits. Excessive heat and uneven watering can also cause young flowers to dry up and fall off.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tomato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves develop yellow patchwork patterns and stop growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus carried by whiteflies or spread through infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-free or resistant stem varieties is the best way to keep your cassava healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Hela bɛ mli loo tso yibii ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some parts of my maize farm grow tall and dark green while other spots stay short and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi Edaraa kuku ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Soil nutrition and water drainage vary across a single farm field. Areas where plants stay short and yellow often have poorer drainage, hard soil where roots cannot spread, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi kwraa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Bei pii lɛ, hei ni tsei ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees like plantains on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides shelter to protect tender leaves and preserve soil moisture during the seedling's first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni ebuɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ dumɔwu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Do my fully grown cocoa trees still need big forest trees around them?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tso ni eda lɛ he miihia tsei agbo ko ni ebɔle ehe lɛ lolo?

english: Yes, mature cocoa benefits from light to moderate shade provided by permanent forest trees. These trees shield cocoa from extreme sun heat, block strong destructive winds, keep the soil moist, and help your cocoa trees live longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ni edara lɛ baanyɛ ana hulutsoo fioo kɛyashi hulutsoo ni jɛɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ amli lɛ he sɛɛ. Tsei nɛɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ nii lɛ he Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do so many small cocoa flowers and tiny pods dry up and drop off my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This natural dropping is called cherelle wilt. A cocoa tree usually produces far more flowers and young pods than it can support, so it sheds the extra ones to focus its energy on growing the remaining pods to full size.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ kɛyashɛ he ni amɛdara lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my mature cocoa trees when they seem healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kokoo niji ni eda lɛ ekomɛi? Etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa.

english: Pruning removes excess branches so sunlight and air can flow freely through the farm. Good airflow reduces dampness that causes diseases and directs the tree's food and energy straight into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and humid conditions. Weeding regularly, pruning branches, and removing infected pods helps keep the farm dry and prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa. tsei ahe ŋmɔshi Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on some of my cocoa trees turning yellow and the branches swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eniji lɛ miifu lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is carried from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees gradually produce fewer pods and die, so removing infected trees is necessary to stop it from infecting your whole farm.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli hela ni efuu lɛ. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ woɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baafee fiofio Ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni egboɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods grow into strange, hard shapes and fail to develop beans inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo dumɔwui yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Deformed or hardened pods are usually caused by fungal infections or severe insect damage during early pod growth. Cutting away affected pods as soon as you notice them keeps the problem from spreading to healthy pods on the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii waa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni efite loo ni wa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni ena hela lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni oyɔse lɛ, ebaaha naagba lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes small dark burn marks and dry patches on my young cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ shãa he okadii bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa? Kɛ hei ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: These dark marks are caused by mirids (also known as capsids), which are tiny sap-sucking insects. They pierce the bark and pods to feed, causing tissues to dry out, which can be controlled by spraying recommended treatments during peak pest seasons.
ga: Mirids (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔi nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ tso lɛ yibii kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛná niyenii. dry the tissue Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm needs fertilizer to help my cocoa yield better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha kookoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: If your cocoa trees have yellowish leaves, grow slowly, or produce very few pods despite good weather, your soil may be lacking nutrients. Testing your soil or applying recommended cocoa fertilizers restores essential nutrients to boost pod production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni eha pod lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: You can tell a pod is ripe by its color change: green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting pods when fully ripe ensures high bean quality and stops seeds from germinating inside the pod.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ pods lɛ egbɔ kɛtsɔ su tsakemɔ nɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: What fast-growing crops can I plant to earn money when my cocoa trees are out of season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ eshɛɛɛ be mli?

english: Crops like maize, cassava, peppers, and tomatoes mature quickly in a few months, allowing you to harvest and sell them for regular cash during the months when cocoa trees are not producing.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ shika tamɔ bɔ ni afeɔ yɛ nyɔji ni afeee cacao lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees only give harvests during specific months instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli pɛ, shi jeee yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees rely on natural weather cycles, needing a specific balance of rain to form flowers and dry sunshine to ripen the pods, which only happens during certain seasons of the year.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ damɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. Ehe miihia nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi aba, ni hulu la ni egbi lɛ hu baaha ŋmeii lɛ ashwere. Enɛ baa mli yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, and overly wet conditions, especially when trees are overgrown and air cannot circulate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tsei ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How do crop diseases spread so quickly from one farm to another in our village?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ kroko mli yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through tiny fungi spores or insects carried by the wind, rain droplets, shared farming tools, or even on clothing when people walk between farms.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ fungal spores loo kooloi bibii anɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, okwaayeli he nibii ni ajaa loo atadei po nɔ beni gbɔmɛi nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some food crops produce harvest in a few months while cocoa trees take years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpaa niyenii komɛi ni aduɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei heɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Short-season food crops focus all their energy on producing seeds quickly, while perennial tree crops like cocoa must first spend years building strong trunks and deep root systems before they can support heavy fruit production.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ oya lɛ he nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ he miihia afii babaoo koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai babaoo ni anáa lɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantains and cassava on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa provides necessary shade to protect tender cocoa leaves from sun damage while giving you food and income while the cocoa grows.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce lots of small flowers but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo shi anɔkwa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers; if chemical sprays kill these insects or if conditions are too dry, the unpollinated flowers simply drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive extreme heat, keeping the main stems alive until rain returns.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Is it bad for my land if I plant the exact same crop on it year after year?
ga: Ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Yes, planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows pests that feed on it to build up permanently in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for growing cocoa or better for vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ loo ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha aduawai ŋmɔ?

english: Cocoa requires deep, fertile soil that retains moisture without waterlogging, under light shade, whereas vegetables need lighter soil with full sunlight and easy access to water for regular watering.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu bɛ mli yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulu lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he miihia Cocoa. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa he miihia aduawai. kɛ nu ni anáa mlɛo kɛha nu ni akɛhaa daa.

english: If I plant coconut trees on my land today, how many years will I have to wait before I can start harvesting the fruits?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani aje yibii lɛ akpamɔ shishi?

english: Improved dwarf and hybrid coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 7 years. Once mature, a tree can produce fruits continuously for over 60 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Tso lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii fe afii 60 sɔŋŋ.

english: Do coconut trees produce fruits continuously throughout the year or only during specific seasons in Ghana?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei woɔ yibii be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ loo yɛ bei komɛi amli pɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Coconut trees produce a new flower bunch about every month once mature, allowing for year-round harvests as long as the trees receive enough water and nutrients during the dry season.
ga: Kokoo tsei baajie fɔfɔi heei be fɛɛ be. nyɔŋ nɔ beni edara kwraa No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ akpa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ náa nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of leafy green foliage but very few or small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo loo bibii kwraa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages leaf growth over fruit production. Crops require balanced nutrients, particularly potassium and phosphorus, to bloom properly and form large fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa fe aduawai ni anáa lɛ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. titri lɛ potassium kɛ phosphorus kɛha fɔfɔi ni sa kɛ aduawai wuji ni anáa

english: Can I grow short-term food crops like cassava or maize between my young coconut trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping with fast-growing crops provides early income and food while the tree canopy is small. It also helps suppress weeds, provided you leave enough space around the base of the young trees so they do not compete for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni daa oya lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaha aná shika kɛ niyenii yɛ shishijee mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ji bibioo lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛyaa kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshiɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi koni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I space tree crops like coconut on my land during planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need proper spacing, usually about 7 to 9 meters apart, so their leaves get maximum sunlight and their roots can spread without fighting neighboring trees for water and nutrients.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ato ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe gbɛ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 9 bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Is it better to plant crop seeds directly into the field or start them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo aaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery allows you to protect young shoots from heat and pests, ensuring that only the strongest, healthiest seedlings get transplanted into your main farm field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is suitable for long-term tree crops like coconut?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ ŋmeii?

english: Tree crops thrive best in deep, well-drained soils such as sandy loam where water does not sit in puddles for days. Poorly drained, waterlogged soils can rot the tree roots over time.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋã nɔ. Nu lɛ ehiɛɛɛ nubu lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it better for me to clear and plant my entire farmland at once or expand my acreage step by step?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni madu shikome loo magbala okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio?

english: Starting with a smaller acreage allows you to manage maintenance costs, weeding, and watering effectively. As you gain experience and farm income, you can gradually clear and expand into additional acres.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ he bibioo ko je shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. jwɛi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa jogbaŋŋ Beni onine shɛɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛ shika nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Obaanyɛ fiofio Abaanyɛ ajie ni agbɛ ashwã hei krokomɛi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my coconut trees turning yellow and dropping off prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of drought stress, nutrient deficiency, or diseases like Cape St. Paul Wilt Disease. Ensuring proper fertilizer application and inspecting the trunk for pests can help diagnose the cause.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee hɔmɔ he haomɔ he okadi. Niyenii ni esaaa loo helai tamɔ Cape St. Paul’s wilt Kwɛmɔ ni akɛ fɔmɔ nii ni sa kɛ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ana nɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa.

english: How can I help my young crops survive the long dry season in Ghana without dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo?

english: Mulching—placing dried grass or crop residues around the base of young plants—helps trap moisture in the soil, keeps root zone cool, and protects crops from heat stress during dry months.
ga: Mulching—Akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Obalanyo stem base—eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the heavy rains start in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains usually mean the soil is waterlogged, which stops roots from breathing and washes away nitrogen, the primary nutrient plants need to stay green and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ mli. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ waa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: If I make a mistake and apply too much chemical fertilizer to my young crops, why do they dry up and burn?
ga: Ni kɛji mitɔmɔ ni mikɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii hu? Mɛni hewɔ tsei gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa lɛ?

english: Excess fertilizer creates a high concentration of salt in the soil that draws water out of the plant roots, causing the leaves to scorch and dry up even if the ground is moist.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni no gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to leave shade trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔshi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young and mature cocoa plants get stressed under full sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas that reduce heat, retain moisture in the soil, and prolong the productive life of cocoa trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela koni ekɛba dɔlɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ ayibii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and dry out during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are large and lose water rapidly in dry, windy Harmattan weather. The plant allows its outer leaves to drop to save water and protect its core until the rains return.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa yɛ Harmattan lɛ mli. Tso lɛ haa esɛɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishigbɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What happens underground if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots compete aggressively for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in tall thin stems with very small, light tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii waa ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one strong generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their vigor and uniform strength, leading to lower yields and weaker plants in the second season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ ni he wa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize while covering the soil to prevent weeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmãa ni haa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry grass around my vegetables help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ sũ wo mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Mulching with dry grass keeps the soil cool under direct sun, traps water so you irrigate less, suppresses weed growth, and gradually decomposes into natural organic manure.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ekɛ nu toɔ koni onyɛ okɛ nu afɔ nɔ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and dropping their flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often triggered by sap-sucking pests like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or extreme heat. Stressed plants shed flowers to preserve energy rather than feed growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa Tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaaye aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yam crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams indicate maturity when the above-ground vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season, showing that the plant has transferred all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ edara beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo bulb lɛ mli.

english: When corn plants do not get enough nitrogen food from the soil, they automatically move whatever nitrogen they have to the top growing leaves. This starves the older, bottom leaves, causing them to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why does my cassava grow tall with many leafy branches, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or if cassava is planted in overly rich soil, the plant uses all its energy to build leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo aduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm helps my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special natural bacteria in their roots that suck nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in the soil, acts as free natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruits during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the pollen inside tomato flowers gets damaged by the heat and cannot fertilize the bloom. The plant drops the unfertilized flowers to conserve its remaining water and energy.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔmɔ nii amli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look soft in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot afternoons, water evaporates from pepper leaves faster than roots can suck water out of the soil. Rolling their leaves tight helps the plant reduce sunburn and water loss, and they normally recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni hulutsoo kɛ nu ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same plant food and soil water. Removing extra suckers leaves one or two strong stems, which allows the main tree to bear large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ebɔle ehe Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ tsei komekomei lɛ amli kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ plantain jwɛi agbo ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden sticks to climb up instead of growing across the bare soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ tsei tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunshine to manufacture food for the growing tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on tall stakes spreads the leaves open to the sun and keeps them off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do weeds growing near my crop plants make my crops grow thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and root space directly from your crops. Without enough nutrients and space, your crop plants cannot build thick stems or big fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ shishifãi amli lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ he ko bɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ awo ŋmeii ni mli tse loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them with dark dust sitting inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ diŋ ni ekpɛtɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms that crawl deep inside the growing whorl of the corn plant during the day, eating the soft leaves from the inside out and leaving their droppings behind.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's maize crop produce smaller yields than the certified seeds I buy from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for maximum strength, uniform growth, and pest resistance in their first generation. Saved seeds lose these superior traits in the second generation, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo. shweremɔ ni tamɔ ekome kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni nɔ kwɔlɔ nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my neighbor's maize plants grow much faster and taller than mine even though we planted on the exact same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ daa oya ni ekwɛɔ fe mi nɔ lɛ? ni wɔdu yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ

english: Planted crops grow at different speeds based on soil fertility, moisture, and early care. Soil rich in organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives young shoots an immediate energy boost to outshine plants growing in depleted soil.
ga: Tsei ni adu lɛ daa oya yɛ srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulutsoo kɛ mra be mli kwɛmɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni humus loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ, bɔni afee ni tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use the exact same crop fertilizer on my cassava field that I use for my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Different crops need different nutrients. Maize requires high nitrogen to build leafy stalks, while cassava requires higher potassium to develop thick, heavy starch tubers under the ground. Applying maize fertilizer to cassava creates huge green leaves but leaves you with small, thin roots.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei biɔ potassium babaoo koni enyɛ efee ŋmei ni mli tse ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo ŋmãa mli lɛ, ebaa baa agboi eŋɔli shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: Why does rain water sit on top of my farm soil for days after a heavy downpour instead of sinking into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water pools when topsoil is heavily compacted or contains high clay content without air pockets. Mixing dried leaves, compost, or decaying farm waste into the soil loosens it so water and oxygen can reach crop roots easily.
ga: Pond be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni fa babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, ŋmɔ mli jwɛi, loo ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni egbo futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ anyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow and curling up into little tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tomato leaves curl as a defense mechanism against intense heat and drying winds to conserve moisture. However, if they stay yellow and tightly curled, it is a sign of a plant virus spread by tiny whitefly insects feeding on the sap.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he koni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpã amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ, No ji tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi.

english: What causes small green worms to bore inside my maize stalks and destroy the leaves before the cobs form?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid under leaves by moths. They hide deep inside the growing center of the plant to feed, requiring early control before the main stalk gets damaged.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni edaa lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii. It must be controlled from the beginning. before the main stem is damaged

english: Why do my sweet pepper plants stop producing flowers and fruits when I plant them right underneath cassava bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai kɛ midu lɛ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ ko shishi lɛ?

english: Tall, leafy cassava plants block sunlight from reaching low-growing pepper plants. Pepper plants require bright, direct sunlight to convert nutrients into flowers and fruit; without light, they remain stunted.
ga: Cassava baai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ pepper tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ fioo lɛ ahe. Pepper tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛtsake niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai amli. If there is no light They will be stunted.

english: Why do agricultural officers always advise us to plant plantain suckers beside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsei bibii yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Cocoa tsei lɛ ji bibii be fɛɛ be.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantain suckers grow quickly with broad leaves, creating a natural umbrella that shades fragile cocoa trees during their first two years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers under the ground are mature and ready to harvest without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yams indicate maturity above ground when the green vines and leaves turn yellow and naturally dry up at the end of the rains. This signals that the plant has finished sending all its energy into growing the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔ lɛ naagbee. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my mango tree blossoms dry up and drop off the branches when strong Harmattan winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eniji fiteɔ kɛji harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of delicate flower stems, causing flowers to drop before insects can pollinate them into fruit. Planting tall windbreak trees along your farm boundary protects fruit blossoms from harsh wind currents.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani kooloi nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ amɛ yibii. Tsei kakadaji ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ aduawai ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why is it important to clear my farm land step-by-step before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo miŋmɔ lɛ mli fiofio dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing step-by-step allows you to properly map out your field, create drainage paths, and clear weeds so your crops have a clean, stress-free environment to take root.
ga: Nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he mfoniri. Bɔɔ gbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli ni ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ Enɛ haa onibii lɛ feɔ he ko ni he tse, ni haomɔ bɛ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo shishifãi yɛ mli.

english: How does clearing my land properly prevent rainwater from rushing through my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: Proper clearing lets you mark out clear natural channels so heavy rain flows away smoothly instead of building up and washing away your topsoil and crops.
ga: He ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa okadiɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni mli tse. koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Moŋ lɛ, ebua ehe naa ni ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I rush to plant all my land at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ oyaiyeli yaduɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Taking land preparation step-by-step ensures each section is properly cleared, drained, and managed, preventing you from getting overwhelmed by weeds or water problems later.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ ni yaa nɔ fitsofitso lɛ haa akwɛɔ koni ajie fã fɛɛ fã jogbaŋŋ, ajie nu kɛjɛ mli, ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okɛ jwɛi loo nu he naagbai akabɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why does heavy rainwater sweep away my young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mitsei bibii lɛ?

english: When land is not prepared with proper drainage channels, rainwater builds up momentum and rushes across the surface, carrying away topsoil and unrooted plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nu homɔ gbɛi ni sa Nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa hewalɛ naa ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Efoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ tsei ni shishifãi bɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep water from pooling on my field after rain?
ga: Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni nu akadamɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: You can clear simple drainage paths along the natural slope of your land so excess rainwater drains away safely without suffocating crop roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ mlɛo. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. ni ehaaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why is checking the slope of my land necessary before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha dani aje dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Checking the slope shows you where water naturally flows during heavy rains, helping you plan where to put pathways and crop rows to prevent erosion.
ga: Slope monitoring baatsɔɔ bo he ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otoɔ he ni okɛ gbɛjegbɛi kɛ tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ baawo koni ŋshɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do experts place cocoa in a different category from crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi kɛ kookoo woɔ gbɛ kroko nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that takes years to mature and yields for decades, unlike seasonal food crops like maize or cassava that are harvested in a few months.
ga: Cocoa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni heɔ afii babaoo dani edaa ni ewoɔ yibii ni hiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ be mli niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ he.

english: Can I plant cocoa seedlings directly into bush land without clearing it first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ tsei bibii ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛjieee jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: No, young cocoa seedlings need a cleared area with prepared drainage and controlled shade so they do not compete with wild weeds and bush roots for water and nutrients.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná he ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli ni asaa he kɛ hulutsoo ni akudɔ. Bɔni afee ni akafee akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe akaŋshii kɛ koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii shishifãi ahe.

english: How do I know if my land is fully ready for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Your land is ready when it is cleared of heavy bush, water drainage paths are created to avoid root rot, and shade trees are organized to protect the young cocoa.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛji ajie brɔshi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Afee nu ni hoɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite. ni amɛha tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa koni amɛkɛbu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to cocoa seedlings if rain water sits around their stems for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo dumɔwui anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi tso lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Standing water deprives the roots of oxygen, leading to root rot and weak plants that may yellow and die before they can mature.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from intense sunlight. Direct sun burns their tender leaves and dries out the moisture they need, causing the leaves to turn yellow and fall off to conserve water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli.

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas. They protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh sun exposure and wind while keeping the surrounding soil cool and humid.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds close together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks with smaller or missing cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess rainwater fills all the tiny air spaces in the ground, suffocating the roots and creating ideal conditions for rot-causing fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ amli obɔ. fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛi ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is moist before applying fertilizer to my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔ nii lɛ mli?

english: Crop roots can only absorb nutrients when they are dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and wastes the fertilizer since the crop cannot drink it in dry form.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter, or mulch, traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root zone cool during hot days, and stops unwanted weeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ la he koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like extra mouths to feed in your garden. They steal water, sunlight, and vital soil nutrients away from your crops, starving your plants during their most active growing period.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛi ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ obɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: These are likely pests like fall armyworms that target the tender growth center of maize plants. They feed on the fresh leaves before they unfold, which damages the plant's growth point and reduces yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ anɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ. ni fiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why should I trim off extra branch shoots from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and breeze can reach the inner trunk. Good airflow reduces fungal diseases like black pod and allows the tree to send its energy directly into growing larger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛya tso lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pod blackening baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa pods wuji amli.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and return it into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant both maize and oil palm on my land instead of focusing on just one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ mu ŋmãa fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ baama ŋmãa kome pɛ nɔ?

english: Growing different crops spreads your financial risk. If bad weather or pests ruin your maize crop, your oil palm trees can still survive and give you a steady harvest so you do not lose all your income.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Ehaa oshika he oshara lɛ feɔ srɔtoi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kpata o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ O-oil palm tso lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lolo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shika ni onáa lɛ fɛɛ fiteee bo.

english: How do fast-growing crops like corn help me while I wait for my tree crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Fast-growing crops like corn yield produce within a few months, giving you quick food and immediate cash to handle daily living costs while slow-growing tree crops take several years to start bearing fruit.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baawo yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Ehaa oyeɔ nii oya ni eyɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ekɛbaatsu daa gbi shihilɛ mli nyɔmɔwoo he nii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni daa blɛoo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: What happens to my household food supply if a crop disease destroys my main grain field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishia niyenii ni mikɛhaa lɛ nɔ kɛji tso hela ko kpata miŋmaa ŋmɔ titri lɛ hiɛ?

english: If you rely on only one crop, a disease can leave you with nothing to eat or sell. Planting resilient cash and food crops alongside grains ensures you still have food to eat or harvest even during a crop failure.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome pɛ nɔ lɛ Hela baanyɛ aha oná nɔ ko ni oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ. Shikayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli Ŋmãa hebuu haa onáa niyenii lolo ni oyeɔ loo obaakpa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii po.

english: How does oil palm produce fruit compared to seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Te oil palm lɛ woɔ yibii ahaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: Maize produces its harvest all at once in a short season, whereas oil palm produces fresh fruit bunches continuously throughout the year, offering you a regular stream of work and income.
ga: Akpaa ŋmãa fɛɛ shikome yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mu tsei lɛ woɔ aduawai heei babaoo be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa onáa shika kɛ nitsumɔ ni yaa nɔ

english: Is it better to harvest all my palm nuts at once or harvest them bit by bit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakpa ŋmei yibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo fiofio?

english: Oil palm bunches ripen at different times on the tree. Harvesting ripe bunches as they mature every few weeks gives you better quality oil and consistent cash flow throughout the season.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akpamɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ fɛɛ. otsii enyɔ komɛi Enɛ baaha oná fuɛl ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my corn so it does not spoil during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Enɛ ji koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Corn is ready for dry storage when the husks turn brown and dry and the grains become hard. Harvesting too early leaves moisture that causes mold, while waiting too long leaves the crop vulnerable to pests.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛbaato he ko ni egbi beni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kpamɔ mra tsɔ shĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye amɛ awui.

english: Can I grow corn between my young oil palm trees without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ mu tsei ateŋ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, growing short-season crops like corn between young palm trees uses the empty land efficiently before the palm canopy grows wide enough to shade out sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ kɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani ŋmei lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why do tree crops like oil palm continue to produce fruit for many years without replanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mu tsei lɛ woɔ yibii afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Oil palms are perennial plants with strong, deep roots that store energy over many years, allowing them to produce fruit continuously once mature, unlike seasonal crops that die after one harvest.
ga: Mu tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ afii babaoo. Ehaa enyɛɔ ewoɔ yibii be fɛɛ be kɛ́ eda kwraa. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ be mli tsei ni gboiɔ yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does planting crops with different harvest times help me manage farm labor?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ ni kpamɔ bei srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops mature at different times of the year, farm work like harvesting and weeding is spread out, allowing you and your family to manage the workload without having to pay for extra laborers all at once.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii daa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa bo kɛ oweku lɛ nyɛnyɛɔ nyɛtsuɔ nyɛnitsumɔ lɛ he nii ni ehe ehiaaa ni nyɛwo nitsumɔ kroko he nyɔmɔ shikome.

english: How do tree crops like oil palm react when dry weather lasts longer than usual?
ga: Te tsei tamɔ mu tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli?

english: During prolonged dry spells, oil palm trees slow down fruit bunch production to save water, but their deep roots keep them alive until the rains return to restart full growth.
ga: Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Oil palm tsei lɛ haa aduawai akui ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ ahi wala mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba koni eku esɛɛ eda kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. Planting shade trees or plantains around them acts as a shelter, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting the fragile cocoa leaves from burning until the trees are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ ashɛ enɔ.

english: When soil lacks nitrogen, maize plants move whatever nitrogen they have left from the older bottom leaves up to the new top leaves. The yellowing at the bottom is a clear sign that your crop needs nitrogen fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ. Yellow ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ otso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rain stays on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm without draining away, it suffocates the roots, causing waterlogging which leads to fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. kɛ nu ni hoɔ baa Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ baa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight, which produces energy to grow big underground tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage away from damp ground pests and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni haa hewalɛ ni akɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves around the stems of my vegetable plants during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã he lɛ? Aduawai ashishifãi yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass creates a mulch layer. This layer acts as a shield against the hot sun, stopping water in the soil from evaporating quickly and keeping the roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why are tiny worms hiding inside the central leaves of my young corn instead of feeding on the outside leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms burrow into the deep center (whorl) of maize plants to hide from sunlight, heavy rain, and birds while feeding on the softest, most tender new leaves growing inside.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo hulu, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I chop off the small extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing most of them leaves only one or two strong suckers and ensures the main plantain tree has full energy to produce large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ehaa dumɔwu titri lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo niji wuji.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is done, that trapped nitrogen acts as free food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu nii agbe naa Nitrogen ni amɔ lɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why did the fertilizer I applied burn and scorch my crop stems when the ground was dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ shãa ni eshãa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are concentrated salts that require soil moisture to dissolve safely. When applied to bone-dry soil, the fertilizer draws moisture out of the plant's roots and stems instead, causing them to burn.
ga: Fertilizers ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni biɔ ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. ha amɛshã

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off onto the ground before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant experiences stress, it sheds flowers to save water and energy just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔ kpe Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the fruit buyers rejecting my mangoes even though they taste sweet inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ aduawai lɛ kpooɔ mi mangoi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔ moŋ?

english: Buyers and market brokers buy with their eyes first. Minor skin spots, insect damage, or scars make the fruit look spoiled and shorten how long it stays fresh, so buyers refuse them even if the inside tastes good.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi kɛ jarayelɔi kɛ amɛhiŋmɛii hɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ, ŋwɛi ŋmeii bibii, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. Aloo ŋmeii haa aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo, ni ehaa be ni ekɛhiɔ shi ehee lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ nibii nɛɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ po.

english: What does a broker mean when they say my mangoes are not up to export quality?
ga: Mɛni brokers tsɔɔ kɛji amɛkɛɛ mi mango lɛ jeee nɔ ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ?

english: Export quality means the mangoes must have perfect, clean skin without any spots, sap burns, or insect marks. They must also be the exact right size, shape, and harvested at the right maturity so they can survive long sea or air travel without rotting.
ga: Export quality tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mango lɛ hewolo lɛ he atse jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, shãa loo kooloi akadi. Esa akɛ afee amɛ dalɛ. ehi jogbaŋŋ ni akpaa amɛ kɛji amɛdara jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛhi ŋshɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do my mangoes get dark black spots just as they start getting soft and ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ amɛfee blɛoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black spots on ripening mangoes are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose. The fungus hides quietly in the skin while the fruit is green and breaks out into rotting spots as the fruit softens, especially after rain or high humidity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Fuji lɛ teeɔ ehe dioo yɛ hewolo lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni egboi beni aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa sɛɛ.

english: Why do fruit flies like my mango trees so much, and what are they doing to the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii sumɔɔ mi mango tso lɛ waa lɛ? Ni mɛni amɛkɛ aduawai lɛ feɔ?

english: Fruit flies pierce the skin of maturing mangoes to lay their eggs inside the fruit. When the eggs hatch into tiny maggots, they feed on the flesh, causing the inside of the mango to turn watery, brown, and rotten before you can harvest it.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii tsɔɔ mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hewolo mli koni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ wɔɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛbatsɔmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ebaaye loo. Enɛ haa mango lɛ mli feɔ nu, efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa.

english: Why is liquid dripping from the stems of my picked mangoes leaving dark burns on the skin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mango tso ni mifo lɛ mli lɛ shi shãa he okadii diji yɛ mihewolo nɔ lɛ?

english: Mango sap contains natural strong acids that burn the skin of the fruit when it spurts out during harvesting. When sap runs down the fruit, it leaves black streaks called 'sap burn' that ruin the fruit's appearance and lower its selling price.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, acid ni mli wa yɛ mango nu mli ni shãa aduawai lɛ hiɛ kɛji efo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛji nu lɛ ho kɛba shi kɛtee aduawai lɛ anɔ Ebaashi line diŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Milk burning’, ni fiteɔ aduawai lɛ ahe fɛo ni ehaa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest green mangoes so they ripen properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mango ni ahoko lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Green mangoes are ready to harvest when the shoulders around the stem swell up and flatten out, the dip at the stem gets deeper, and the skin color turns from a dull green to a slightly lighter yellowish-green.
ga: Mango eŋɔli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji tsitsii ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ efuu ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dip ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli kwɔ. ni hewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli tseee nɔ kɛtee eŋɔli ni mli tse fioo.

english: Why do my mangoes rot so quickly just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Quick rotting happens when fruits are bruised during picking, dropped on the ground, or packed tightly in hot containers. Small hidden cracks in the skin allow rot fungi to enter and ruin the fruit fast.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ oya baa kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ fã yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ, ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ, loo akɛwo tsɛnsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛjegbɛi bibii ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ aduawai lɛ oya.

english: Why do my mango trees drop almost all their flowers before any small fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ fɔɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers fall off easily due to water stress, dry winds, or attacks by tiny pests like thrips and diseases like powdery mildew. If the flowers are damaged or don't get pollinated, the tree drops them.
ga: Mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nu mli haomɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ helai tamɔ powdery mildew tutuamɔi ahewɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ efite loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Tsei lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why are some of my mangoes growing small and twisted instead of smooth and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ bibii ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Misshapen mangoes usually happen when insect pests bite the tiny fruit right after flowering, or when the flower was not properly pollinated by bees and insects during the blooming stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango ni efite lɛ baa kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ awui lɛ ye aduawai bibii lɛ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ ewo fɔfɔii lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ loo beni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi efɔɔɔ fɔfɔii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee be mli lɛ.

english: Why does the skin on one side of my mango turn hard and yellow-brown while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ko fã kome wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ eyɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is sunburn, which happens when intense direct sun heats up fruit that isn't protected by leaves. The heat damages the skin and the flesh beneath it, making that part of the mango hard and unmarketable.
ga: Enɛ ji hulutsoo. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa aduawai ni baai ebuuu amɛhe lɛ mli dɔɔ. Dɔlɛ lɛ fiteɔ hewolo lɛ kɛ loo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa nakai mango lɛ fã lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: How long should I run my drip irrigation hose every day to keep my vegetables healthy?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ drip hose lɛ atsu nii daa gbi koni mi-vegetables lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Most vegetable crops prefer short, consistent daily watering rather than heavy flooding. Running your drip irrigation for just 8 to 10 minutes every 24 hours keeps the root zone consistently moist without drowning the plant or washing away fertilizer.
ga: Aduawai babaoo sumɔɔ nu kuku ni akɛhaa amɛ daa gbi fe nu afua ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi minitii 8 kɛyashi 10 pɛ daa ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli fũuɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ tso lɛ shwieee shi loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: Is it better to water my crops heavily once a week or give them a little water every day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli loo mawo amɛ nu fioo daa gbi?

english: Crops absorb water best when soil moisture remains steady. Giving them a short daily watering routine keeps the soil around the roots continuously damp, preventing heat stress during dry afternoons.
ga: Tsei nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli edɔ daa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ji daa gbi nifeemɔ kuku. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Akɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be. Tsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa yɛ shwane ni nu bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf wilting in midday heat is the crop's natural way of protecting itself from losing water too fast through evaporation. If the plant bounces back by evening, short daily morning waterings will help it handle the heat better.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ oya tsɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ ku esɛɛ efo gbɛkɛ mli Nu kuku ni akɛhaa lɛ Daa gbi lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aŋɔ dɔlɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I pluck off some small fruits if my plant grows too many at once?
ga: Esa akɛ mafolɔ aduawai bibii komɛi. Ani ehi kɛji mitso lɛ da babaoo shikome?

english: Yes, removing extra young fruits helps the plant focus its energy. Although a branch might set up to 12 tiny fruits, reducing them to an average of 6 or 7 allows the remaining fruits to grow much larger and healthier.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai bibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai bibii ni baanyɛ ashɛ 12 baanyɛ ahi tso lɛ nine kome nɔ moŋ, shi kɛ́ aja mli lɛ, aduawai lɛ ba shi kɛyashɛ 6 loo 7 nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when the crop experiences stress from irregular watering, poor soil nutrients, or high temperatures. The plant deliberately drops flowers to conserve energy for its survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are giving a good harvest count per branch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ miiwo yibii kpakpai ni akɛwo mli lɛ?

english: While a cocoa tree branch can physically hold up to 12 pods, carrying an average of 6 to 7 fully developed, disease-free pods per branch is considered a strong yield for a well-fed tree.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo nine baanyɛ akwɛ tsei 12 nɔ moŋ, shi kɛ aja mli lɛ, tsei 6 kɛyashi 7 ni edara kwraa, shi tsei ni helai bɛ mli lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa kɛha tso ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the fruits on my plant small even though there are many of them on one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyi fa yɛ tso kome nɔ moŋ?

english: When a stem carries too many fruits, they all compete for the same limited food and water coming from the soil. Thinning the extra fruits leaves more food for the remaining ones to swell big.
ga: Beni tso lɛ yibii babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afee tso yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ bibioo lɛ, ehaa niyenii babaoo baa bɔni afee ni tso yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How often should I feed my crops with liquid fertilizer through my watering system?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops thrive when fed in small, regular amounts rather than getting a massive dose at once. Giving your plants light liquid food in short daily intervals ensures roots take in nutrients steadily.
ga: Tsei yeɔ omanye kɛji akɛ aha amɛ niyenii fioo ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona babaoo yɛ be kome mli Niyenii ni ji nu ni akɛaaha tsei yɛ be kukuoo mli Gbi fɛɛ gbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai daa.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer at one time damage my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli shikome lɛ baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Yes, excessive fertilizer creates a buildup of salts in the soil that can burn crop roots and cause leaves to dry out. Light, controlled applications spread out over time are much safer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha baai lɛ agbi. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni akudɔɔ ni ajaa be fɛɛ be lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why are my young crop leaves turning yellow even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating from waterlogging. Balanced daily feeding combined with proper soil drainage will turn the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi lɛ amli nu efo yɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa daa gbi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: If I use a heavy tractor to plow my farm, will it change how my crops grow in the soil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ trakta agbo tsu nii kɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani ebaatsake bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: While a tractor clears and turns land quickly, heavy machinery can compact the lower layers of soil. Very tight soil makes it difficult for young crop roots to push deep, spread out, and absorb nutrients and water.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, traktɔi feɔ oya kɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ. Shi tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli shɔŋŋ, amɛgbɛ amɛshwã, ni amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do my groundnuts make the soil better for planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?
