english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When maize is planted in the same soil next, it feeds on this natural nitrogen fertilizer to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni no gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmãa nɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have massive leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cassava and maize on the same field at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early in the season, while cassava grows slowly over many months. Planting them together uses farm space efficiently, gives you an early food harvest, and keeps the soil covered to stop weeds.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ be lɛ mli mra. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli lɛ, Companion planting kɛ ŋmɔ mli he ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa niyenii oya. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akpa

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow after days of continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the field, excess water displaces air in the soil. Without oxygen, the roots cannot breath or pull up nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to lose green color and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become extremely hot or when water is low. The plant drops the blossoms as a survival tactic to conserve energy and water until weather conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ faaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to local conditions and poor soil. They sprout quickly with the first rain and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before crop seeds can fully establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛ shikpɔji ni ehiii lɛ amli. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over my maize leaves after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on tender, newly grown leaves. Checking crops early helps you catch these insects before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baa bibii ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I avoid watering my vegetable garden in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ he yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering under bright sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before hitting the roots. Hot sun combined with water droplets on leaves can also cause leaf scorching and encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why must I wait until my yam vines turn yellow and dry before digging up the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi dani mafo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yellow and drying leaves show that the yam plant has finished making food and transferring all its energy into the underground tuber. Harvesting before this means smaller yams that rot faster during storage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ egbe ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa mra lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii bibii aba, ni amɛbaafite oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout out of the ground after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need steady moisture and warm soil to wake up. If the soil is too dry or packed hard, the seed delays pushing its shoot through the surface until rainfall softens the ground enough for it to break through.
ga: Abele dumɔwui lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛte shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ebote mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my newly planted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool while cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crops turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves are a signal that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. To survive, the maize plant steals nitrogen from its oldest bottom leaves and moves it up to feed the new top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni amɛhi shi Abɛi tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: If I plant yellow corn right next to my white corn, will the grains mix on the same cob?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa ni ji yellow yɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ masɛi Ani abaafutu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa kome nɔ?

english: Yes, corn relies on wind to carry pollen from the flowers at the top to the silks below. When yellow corn pollen blows onto white corn silks, it fertilizes those seeds, resulting in cobs with a mix of yellow and white kernels.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni jɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli lɛ aya siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmãa ni ji yellow pollen lɛ tswa ŋmãa siliki yɛŋ nɔ Ebaaha nakai dumɔwui lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dumɔwui ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ eyɛŋ efutu mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when daytime heat gets too intense or when there are no bees to shake the pollen inside the flower. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the flower because it cannot form seeds.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji pollination lɛ yeee omanye Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui.

english: Yams signal maturity above ground. When the green leaves and vines naturally yellow, dry up, and die back at the end of the season, it means the plant has finished sending all its food down into the underground tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Kɛji baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii lɛ fɛɛ emaje shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does pinching off the top tip of my pepper plant make it grow more peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mɔ ko tsɔ pepper tso lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa edaa babaoo lɛ?

english: Removing the top growing point breaks the plant's habit of growing straight up. This forces the plant to send its energy sideways into stem branches, creating a bushy plant with more flowering sites for peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛi he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ afã kɛyaa niji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ fɔfɔii babaoo baa kɛha ŋmeii.

english: Why do fall armyworms always hide and feed deep inside the center whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe be fɛɛ be ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The inner whorl of maize offers young worms shelter from heat and predators like birds. The leaves inside are also soft, moist, and easy for young caterpillars to chew compared to the tougher outer leaves.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ tamɔ okpoi ahe. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ejɔ ni ŋmeii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya kɛ akɛto kponɔgbɛ baai ni wa lɛ ahe.

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck water out of leaves faster than roots can pull water from dry soil. The cocoa tree drops its leaves on purpose to reduce water loss and protect its main trunk from drying out completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay small and stop forming big roots during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ekpaa shishifãi wuji lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava enters a protective resting stage when water is scarce. Instead of wasting energy building leaves or growing big root tubers, the plant conserves its stored food just to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava baabote wɔɔhe be mli beni nu faaa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛfee baai loo shishifãi wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ. Tsei kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ toɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start showing fresh flowers right after the first rain following the harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rain triggers cocoa trees to wake up from their dry resting period. The moisture allows the roots to absorb nutrients quickly, which signals the tree to sprout new flowers for the next crop season.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ teɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛwɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does a late rainy season affect when my cocoa trees will yield pods?
ga: Mɛni hewalɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa naagbee lɛ náa yɛ be mli ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ baawo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: When rains arrive late, flowering is delayed. Because pods take about five to six months to mature after flowering, a late rain pushes back your harvest time and can shorten your main crop yield.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ efɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, amɛheɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛdaraa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ baaha kpamɔ be lɛ asɛɛ afo. Ni ebaanyɛ eha o-primary output lɛ afee kuku.

english: Why do cocoa trees take a natural break from producing pods during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ heɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ mli yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need rest to rebuild energy after carrying a heavy harvest. During the dry season, the tree conserves water and nutrient reserves so it can flower strongly when the rains return.
ga: Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni wa sɛɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei toɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efɔ fɔfɔi waa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do so many tiny flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Tsei enyiɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated by microscopic insects called midges. If there are not enough midges or if weather conditions prevent pollination, the unfertilized flowers naturally dry up and fall off.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ afee kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsiɔ pollination naa lɛ, fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: What is hand pollination, and how can it help my cocoa farm yield more pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ ni ekɛ pods babaoo aba?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually transfer pollen from one flower to another using small tools. It ensures flowers get fertilized even when insect pollinators are scarce, drastically increasing the number of pods your trees produce.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ji be mli ni okɛ onine jieɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ kɛji akɛ ewa akɛ aaana fɔfɔii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ baa lɛ po. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni otso lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: How do tiny insects in the soil and leaf litter help my cocoa flowers produce pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ baai amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Tiny insects called midges live and multiply in moist leaf litter on the farm floor. They fly up to cocoa flowers to feed and carry pollen from flower to flower, which is necessary for pods to form.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ baa ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Amɛfoɔ kɛyaa kookoo fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛyatao niyenii ni amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha pods feemɔ

english: What work should I be doing on my cocoa farm during the off-season when there are no pods to harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ esa akɛ matsu yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: The off-season is the time to prune unwanted branches, weed the farm floor, remove diseased pod husks, and prepare shade cover so your trees are healthy and ready to bloom once the rains begin.
ga: Be ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ ji be ni esa akɛ afo tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Jiemɔ pod ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni oha hulutsoo koni otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo fɔfɔi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Does having too many shade trees stop my mature cocoa trees from blooming well?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo ni miyɔɔ lɛ baatsi mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, heavy shade blocks the sunlight cocoa trees need to generate energy. While young cocoa plants need heavy shade, mature trees need plenty of filtered sunlight to produce strong flowers and pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Ehe miihia ni cacao tso lɛ afee hewalɛ. Kokoo tsei bibii po he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa. Shi tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni mli tse ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my elders say traditional timing of farm activities is getting harder to rely on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi onukpai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kusum nifeemɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Jeɔ shishi efeɔ nɔ ni wa waa akɛ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns are changing, making rainy seasons less predictable than in the past. Today, farmers must observe soil moisture and tree signals directly rather than relying only on traditional calendars.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tsakeɔ Enɛ haaa anyɛ atsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli tamɔ tsutsu lɛ. Amrɔ nɛɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ahe okadii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ blema kalanda lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why is it important to prune dead branches before the flowering season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tsei aniji ni egboi lɛ dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so air and light can circulate. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod from destroying new flowers and allows the tree to send food directly to flower development.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi heei lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from mature trees or nurse crops like plantains to survive. Direct hot sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil before their root system is fully established.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi. Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ agbe naa.

english: Is it necessary to use tall sticks to hold up my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei kakadaji atsu nii. Ani ooomɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni oooha ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking holds yam leaves up so they receive maximum sunlight to produce bigger tubers, while also keeping the leaves off hot, damp soil where fungal diseases quickly spread.
ga: Ni akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ baawo ŋtayaai amli koni hulu la ni fa babaoo aba koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha sweet potato baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves and moving upward usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, heavy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ ni eyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ toi ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my maize farm so the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ mli koni nugbɔ akashi lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a gentle rain, burying it in a small hole a few centimeters from the plant stem and covering it with soil so heavy rains do not wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Afu yɛ bu bibioo ko mli Sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land for three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up in the field, reducing your harvest over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars and holes inside the funnel leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ buji? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ cone lɛ mli

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide in the central leaf whorl to chew young growing points. Early detection and applying recommended treatments into the funnel saves the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli koni amɛye hei ni edaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nibii ni ana mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies, which multiply quickly in dry, warm conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli.

english: Why do all the flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat stress or lack of water in the soil, which prevents pollination and fruit setting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. ni tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai set naa

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause waterlogging in flat or poorly drained soils. Cassava roots suffocate in standing water, which is why planting on raised soil mounds or ridges is essential for drainage.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ lɛ he hiaa koni nu atsɔ mli lɛ.

english: Which plantain sucker should I dig up from my old field to start a healthy new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni maje ŋmɔ hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shishi?

english: Choose a 'sword sucker'—a sucker with a broad, solid base and narrow, spear-shaped leaves. These have strong stored food in their root base to grow faster than 'water suckers' that have wide leaves early on.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante sucker’, ni ji sucker ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ, ni wa kɛ baai ni mli tse, ni tamɔ lance. Enɛɛmɛi yɛ niyenii ni wa ni ato yɛ amɛshishigbɛ koni amɛdara oya fe ‘nu mli ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ yɛ shishijee bei lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops curling up and turning yellow when it has not rained for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When maize plants do not get enough rain, they roll up their leaves to protect themselves from losing moisture to the hot sun. The leaves turn yellow because dry soil prevents the plant from drinking up essential nutrients like nitrogen from the earth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ náaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaabɔle ebaai lɛ ahe koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ he. Baai tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekanu niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need room under the soil to expand into large tubers. If you plant them too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, resulting in thin and small cassava roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji odu ni obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to grow heavy crops like tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ tomato?

english: Good soil for tomatoes is dark, crumbly, and stays moist when you squeeze it in your hand without turning into sticky mud. If soil turns into hard clay or drains water immediately like beach sand, crops will struggle to feed and grow properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha tomato lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ okɛmimɔ oniji amli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ batsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo nu hoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ tamɔ ŋshɔnaa ŋã. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaná naagba yɛ niyenii namɔ kɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ jogbaŋŋ mli.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the same farm, and how does it help?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good. Bean plants pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil, acting like a free natural fertilizer that feeds the maize and helps it grow strong.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Bean tsei gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why are there holes in my cabbage leaves, and what is causing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu lɛ? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually made by small green caterpillars feeding on the plant. These insects eat the leaves to grow, which weakens the plant and stops it from forming a firm, healthy cabbage head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii eŋɔli ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa cabbage baai amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛdara. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ekwɛ kaabe yitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with strong, aggressive root systems that swallow up rainwater and soil food much faster than farm crops. When rain falls, weeds quickly spring up and can choke young crops if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛmiɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei bibii kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my farm so it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekafo?

english: Apply fertilizer when the ground is moist after a light rain, but not during heavy downpours. Burying the fertilizer in a small hole near the plant root and covering it with soil keeps heavy rains from washing your investment away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ooofu yɛ bu bibii amli Ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. When the plant gets too stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy so it can stay alive until conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ miihao tsɔ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Koni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get insect holes and rot when I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if it was not completely dried under the sun first, because trapped water encourages mold. Insects like weevils enter loose bags to lay eggs, so dried grains must be stored in airtight bags or sealed containers to stay safe.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Akɛni nu ni amɔmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii baabote kotokui ni etse amɛhe lɛ amli koni amɛwo amɛwui. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ awo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight during their first few years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living umbrella that shields the seedlings and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: When maize seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller cobs with fewer grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ dumɔwui fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why does my soil grow weaker every season if I keep planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize heavily consumes nutrients like nitrogen from the soil every season. Rotating your maize crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen to the soil naturally through their roots.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii waa daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava field needs additional nutrients before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava he lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi dani adu?

english: If your previous harvest produced thin, stunted roots or if the leaves look pale yellow instead of dark green, your soil lacks nutrients and needs compost, manure, or fertilizer added before planting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he dani adu.

english: Why are fall armyworms appearing in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms miije kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay eggs on young maize leaves because the tender growth in the plant center provides easy food for hatching caterpillars. Inspecting leaves early allows you to spot and control them before major damage occurs.
ga: Autumn mli ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baa bibii anɔ. Akɛni tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa blɛoo hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛyeɔ nii. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ onaa baa lɛ ni okudɔɔ amɛ dani nɔ ko ni fiteɔ waa baa.

english: Yellow curling leaves are typically caused by a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Managing whiteflies with yellow sticky traps or recommended sprays helps protect healthy plants from getting infected.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ tsu ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ ahe nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my vegetable crops right after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to thrive aggressively in local soil. They quickly absorb available water and fertilizer, so clearing them early prevents them from stealing food from your vegetables.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, eka shi faŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ o-vegetables lɛ amli.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra side branches growing near the base of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Removing small side shoots allows the plant to send its energy and water straight to flower production and fruit development, producing bigger and healthier peppers.
ga: Afã tsei bibii ni afoɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu yaa fɔfɔii afeemɔ kɛ aduawai amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to rot quickly when left in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ ashi yɛ tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that release moisture and heat after harvest. Trapping them in a hot room with poor airflow causes mold and bacteria to grow fast, whereas a shaded, airy yam barn keeps them dry and cool.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ kpo yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ aŋɔ amɛ awo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, sweet potato tso ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha amɛgbi ni amɛhe ajɔɔ.

english: Why is it important to wait until the rains settle before planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni amɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani adu ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need moist soil to sprout roots properly. Planting them into dry soil during irregular rains causes the stem cuttings to dry out and die before roots can grow.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ afomɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: If I take good care of my tomato plants, can they start producing fruits earlier than the normal time?
ga: Kɛ́ mikwɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii mra fe bɔ ni amɛwoɔ daa lɛ?

english: Yes, when you give tomato plants proper nutrients, water them regularly, and keep pests away early on, the plants grow faster and can start flowering and setting early fruits a week or two ahead of standard timelines.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni okɛ niyenii ni sa haa otomato tsei lɛ. Ha amɛ nu daa. ni ojie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. Tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii mra dani be ni ato lɛ aba.

english: Why are my neighbor's plantains producing fruit faster than mine even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo plantain lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Plantain growth speed depends heavily on soil nutrients, water availability, and weed control; plants that receive better moisture and soil management in their early months mature and flower much faster.
ga: Bɔ ni plantain lɛ daa oya lɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. nu ni yɔɔ kɛ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ ji waa Tsei ni naa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli Ebaada ni ewo fɔfɔi oya kwraa.

english: Will applying fertilizer make my garden eggs mature faster or will it just grow big leaves?
ga: Ani fɔmɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ adara oya loo ebaaha baai wuji kɛkɛ?

english: Using the right balanced fertilizer at the proper stage promotes strong plant growth and early flower formation, leading to faster fruiting rather than just leafy growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi mra. Enɛ haa aduawai baa oya moŋ fe baai ni baakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do some cassava farms harvest at eight months while others wait up to fifteen months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ŋmɔji komɛi heɔ nyɔji kpaanyɔ dani amɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji komɛi mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ enumɔ?

english: Different cassava varieties have different growth cycles; improved early-maturing varieties are ready for harvest in 6 to 9 months, whereas traditional varieties need up to 15 months to fully develop heavy tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni atsake amɛ ni shwereɔ mra lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema nibii srɔtoi lɛ heɔ nyɔji 15 dani amɛyitsei ni tsii lɛ baa kwraa.

english: How many months after planting should I expect my hybrid oil palm trees to produce their first fruit bunches?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-hybrid oil palm tso lɛ baawo eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii akui?

english: With proper weed control and field management, high-yielding hybrid oil palms usually start producing their first small fruit bunches between 24 and 30 months after being transplanted into the field.
ga: Kɛtsɔ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ kɛ he ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, mu tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ nyɔji 24 kɛyashi 30 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact time my maize is mature and ready for harvesting as dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmã lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the leaves turn pale brown and dry, the silks at the tip of the cob turn completely dark brown, and a tiny black layer forms at the base of the seeds.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ kwraa. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishi

english: How do I know if my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready for picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods undergo a distinct color change—pods that were green turn bright yellow, while pods that were reddish or purple turn bright yellow-orange when ready for harvest.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baaná su tsakemɔ ni kadiɔ mɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji akɛ esa akɛ akpa.

english: What happens if I harvest my sweet potatoes earlier than the expected harvest date?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa sweet potatoes dani gbi ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ akpa lɛ shɛ?

english: Harvesting sweet potatoes too early results in small tubers with low starch content, which significantly reduces the total weight and market value of your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa sweet potato mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ kɛ jarayeli jara nɔ aba shi waa.

english: Is it bad if my pepper plants start showing flowers when the plants are still very small?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mi-pepper tso lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ beni eji bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: If pepper plants flower too early before building strong stems, the early fruits will remain small and weaken the plant; removing the very first set of early flowers helps the plant grow bigger so it can yield far more peppers later.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ oya tsɔ dani amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa lɛ, Mra be mli yibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ ojie fɔfɔi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eda. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ chili babaoo aba sɛɛ mli.

english: What causes maize plants in the same field to produce silks at different times?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli?

english: Uneven soil fertility, irregular watering, or planting seeds at unequal depths cause individual maize plants to grow at different speeds, resulting in staggered flowering across your field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso daa oya yɛ srɔtofeemɔ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii ni shwereɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow instead of remaining bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your rice plants are lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the field has either too much or too little water. Giving them the right fertilizer and managing your field water helps them recover their green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-rice tsei lɛ amli yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo nu babaoo loo nu fioo pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, ni amɛkwɛ nu ni yɔɔ amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ekoŋŋ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants curl up tightly like tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss during intense heat. It is the plant's way of saving moisture until the sun goes down and temperatures cool off.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Eji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant feels stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and well-fed helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni eyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together if I want to get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe kɛji miisumɔ ni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce a much larger, healthier yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my planted crops after a rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that adapt very quickly to absorb water and soil food before your planted crops can. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light and nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my young vegetable seedlings growing very tall and thin instead of short and sturdy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ miida waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ kukuji ni amɛhe wa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward and become weak when they do not get enough direct sunlight. Moving them to a sunnier spot encourages them to build thick, strong stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tee he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ, ebaawo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why did many of the seeds I planted in the ground fail to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ waaa lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the soil dries out completely, or if soil bugs eat them. Planting seeds at a shallow depth and keeping the soil moist helps them sprout safely.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: If my farmland soil looks dark, why would my crops still need me to put fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Even rich, dark soil loses specific plant nutrients every time you harvest crops. Fertilizer puts back essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so the soil can keep feeding future crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ediŋ po laajeɔ tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha tsei wɔsɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when my rice crop is fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn a clear golden-yellow color and the grains at the lower part of the head feel hard rather than soft or milky when pressed.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bulb lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo loo amɛfee tamɔ mliki kɛji akɛ amɛmimɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why does my harvested rice break into small pieces when it gets processed at the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akumɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Be ni atsuɔ he nii yɛ ŋtayaa he lɛ?

english: Rice grains break easily during milling if they were harvested too late after drying out too much in the sun on the field, or if they were dried too fast after harvest. Drying your harvested paddy slowly in a shaded area keeps the grains whole and strong.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni akpaa lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ eshɛ ehe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. aloo kɛji egbi oya tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni egbiɔ blɛoo Yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe awa.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in direct sunlight. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantain or shade trees to retain leaf moisture and grow safely during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava plant have plenty of leafy branches but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant directs all its food energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of expanding its underground root storage.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etso kakadaŋŋ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and dark dirt inside the center funnel of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing point of the maize plant, chewing the young leaves and leaving behind dark waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil has become too weak to support a good maize yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmãa kpakpa baawo?

english: Weak or depleted soil often shows signs like stunted crop growth, pale yellow lower leaves on young plants, or the appearance of parasitic weeds like Striga that thrive in low-nutrient land.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ loo efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ni edaaa lɛ kpo. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ loo jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits and lower yields when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough energy to produce full-sized yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash pollen off the tomato blossoms or make pollen wet and sticky so wind and insects cannot transfer it. Without pollination, the unfertilized flowers drop off the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aho ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ he loo eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi nyɛŋ afã. Kɛji pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Removing lower leaves and weak side shoots redirects the plant's food and water away from unnecessary foliage and focuses that energy into forming larger, healthier pepper fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe. ni okɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ ama pepper aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpea alongside my maize crop help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsina ŋmei ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This acts as natural fertilizer that feeds the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot in heavy or waterlogged soil because standing water starves the tuber of air, creating ideal conditions for soil fungi and tiny parasitic worms called nematodes to invade and destroy the skin.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Akɛni nu lɛ yɛ dioo hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ yitso lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ababote hewolo lɛ nɔ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do some of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds may fail to emerge if planted too deep where they exhaust their stored energy before reaching sunlight, if planted too shallow where heat dries them out, or if soil pests eat the germinating seed.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛhewalɛ ni amɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo dani hulu la lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ yɛ he ko ni latsaa ni mli egbi yɔɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Excess water drowns crop roots by filling up all air spaces in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves root crops of oxygen and creates favorable conditions for soil fungi, causing mature tubers to decay quickly before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ehaa shihilɛ kpakpa baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni edara kwraa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akpaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in a cleared open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and wind, so they need temporary shade crops like plantains to shield them until they grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to come up when I plant them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too deep causes them to burn through all their stored energy underground before their shoots can reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛshãa hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy tops but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stalks too close together or putting too much nitrogen in the soil makes the plant focus its growth on leaves rather than expanding roots.
ga: Cassava tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects to conserve their energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo kooloi ni feɔ pollinating lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hewalɛ ahi shi.

english: Soil-borne bacterial or fungal diseases can clog the water-carrying veins inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves despite wet soil.
ga: Helai ni bacteria loo fungi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ lá fãji ni kɛ nu yaa tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛji amɛhe edɔ po.

english: Why should I cut off some of the lower leaves on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves improves air flow to prevent fungal diseases from spreading and channels energy directly into growing larger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã, ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa tsei wuji ni woɔ yibii ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant cowpeas or groundnuts after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally replenishing nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize removed.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ baa ekoŋŋ Biɛ ji he ni ajieɔ tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛɔ.

english: How do weeds reduce my yield even when there is enough physical space in the field for both?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ he ko yɛ ni fa kɛha amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal hidden soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni amɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, fɛ̃i kɛ hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ baaye amɛhe hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when there are no big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get burnt easily by strong direct sunlight. Shade trees shield them from heat stress and help keep the soil moist so the cocoa roots can establish properly.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and light yellow instead of dark green and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ji kukuji ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow, stunted maize usually means the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or the right fertilizer gives the crops the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji yellow dwarf lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing light patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are symptoms of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant my crops very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests and diseases build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems that absorb early rainwater and soil food much faster than young crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing essential nourishment from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous harvest yield less than certified seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength and uniformity over generations, leading to lower yields. Certified seeds are specially bred and tested for high purity, vigor, and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ akɛ amɛhe tse, amɛhe wa, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe waa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Mulching with dry grass around the plant base keeps the soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains get damaged by tiny insects even when I keep them inside sealed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Insects or their eggs often enter the grain while it is drying in the field. Properly drying grains to a low moisture level and treating them with safe storage protectants before bagging stops insect eggs from hatching and multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo ŋmeii boteɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli beni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Nibii ni haa hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛgbiɔ ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ nii ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani awoɔ kotoku mli lɛ haaa kooloi lɛ afɔ ni amɛfɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct hot sunlight burns their fragile leaves and dries out topsoil moisture before their roots can grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni waaa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which often happens when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when the soil has been overworked without added fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ laaje. aloo kɛ́ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii fe nine ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too close causes crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak, thin stems and a smaller total harvest than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛkpaa nii fioo fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to multiply year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsei lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayi fa daa afi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil when the plants break down.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks adequate sunlight, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo bulbs yɛ shishi.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high enough to catch sunlight so the leaves can produce food, which is then sent down into the ground to build bigger tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ akwɛ bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ nɔ koni baai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛbatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants face extreme heat, uneven watering, or a shortage of essential nutrients needed during the flowering phase.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap, or by viral infections spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Removing extra shoots prevents them from stealing food and water from the main mother plant, allowing the main stem to produce a much larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide living shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees the right environment to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, crumbles easily in your hand, and drains water well without turning into swampy mud. If crops like plantains or cocoyams grow strong on the land, cocoa will likely do well too.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ sũ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji tsei tamɔ plantain loo cocoa kwɛ̃ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Cocoa hu sumɔɔ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are sitting in flooded soil. Clearing weeds and applying the right fertilizer helps the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from dry weather or lack food in the soil. It is the tree's natural way of saving energy when it doesn't have enough water or nutrients to grow pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ toɔ be mli ni ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: This is called cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally sacrifices some of its young pods because it has more than it can feed, or because of sudden water stress. Removing stressed pods leaves enough food for the healthy ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Taakɛ eji lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ ekomɛi shaa afɔle ejaakɛ eyɛ babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. aloo yɛ nu he haomɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Pods ni haa mɔ haoɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha mɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do full-sized cocoa pods turn black while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in overly damp, dark, and crowded farms. Pruning thick branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods regularly stops the spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Nibii ni afolɔ mli waa koni hulu la aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa daa lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do insects attack my cocoa trees more right after the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa kookoo tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like mirids thrive when fresh green shoots grow right after the rains, especially where direct sunlight hits gaps in the farm cover. Pruning damaged branches and using safe control methods during this time protects the farm.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ tswa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he ni aha lɛ lɛ. Niji ni efite lɛ ni aaafolɔ mli kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why must I cover cocoa beans with plantain leaves to ferment them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ plantain baai aha kookoo yibii lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fermentation under plantain leaves produces heat that kills the seed sprout and develops the rich chocolate flavor inside the bean. Unfermented beans remain bitter and are rejected by buyers.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ haa dɔlɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. ni ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa baa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Beans ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ lolo ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa harvest dropping even though my trees look very big and old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ni mikpaa lɛ miiba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛgbɔ moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their ability to produce pods naturally declines, and they get sick more easily. Old farms require pruning or gradual replanting with new seedlings to restore good yields.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmeii lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni hela baamɔ lɛ oya Ehe miihia ni afo ŋmɔji ni egbɔ lɛ amli fiofio loo adu dumɔwui heei koni nibii kpakpai aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does heavy rainfall right when my cocoa trees are flowering affect my final yield?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ lɛ baaná minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive heavy rain can knock delicate flowers off the branches and prevent small insects from pollinating them. It also creates damp conditions that cause pod rot, leading to fewer healthy pods at harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ, ni eha kooloi bibii akafee amɛ pollen. Ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ hu baa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ́ akpa amɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small root systems that easily dry out in full sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains around them to shield them from high heat and keep the soil moist while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I dig too close to the trunk of my cocoa trees with heavy metal tools like hoes or cutlasses?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dade ni tsii tamɔ spade loo dagger tsuɔ nii kɛbɛŋkɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees have delicate feeder roots right near the top of the soil that gather water and food. Cutting into the ground too close to the trunk damages these roots, making it hard for the tree to feed itself and leading to lower pod yields.
ga: Cacao tsei yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu kɛ niyenii he. Kɛ́ afo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite shishifãi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaana niyenii. ni eha pod yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree suffers from water stress, lacks nutrients, or if beneficial insects like midges are missing to pollinate them. Proper watering and maintaining leaf litter helps keep these tiny pollinators active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu he haomɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ, loo kɛji kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ baai amli jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Mɛnɛɛmɛi ehiɛ kã shi.

english: What causes the leaves on my cocoa trees to turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yellow leaves during dry months usually mean the tree is losing more water than its roots can pull from the dry earth. Covering the ground around the tree with dead leaves (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efo nu babaoo fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant my crops right at the edge of a river or lake?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsei yɛ faa loo ŋshɔ ko naa?

english: Planting too close to a river can cause waterlogging, which rots plant roots because the soil becomes too wet and lacks air. Leaving a grassy boundary near water bodies prevents heavy rain from washing your good farm soil away.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nu abɔle he. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi fiteɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi bibioo ko yɛ nu jɛɛhe ko he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale after heavy rain, even though crops need rain to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ.

english: When rain falls too heavily, excess water washes away essential plant nutrients deeper into the earth where shallow roots cannot reach them. Creating simple drainage paths helps excess water flow away without ruining the soil nutrient levels.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does rainwater carry away topsoil on my slanted farmlands, and how can plants stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te tsei baanyɛ akpa lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain striking bare, sloping ground washes away the rich topsoil where crops feed. Planting groundcover crops like legumes or cover crops anchors the soil with their roots and stops heavy rain from washing your fertile soil away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ kɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if a new piece of land will be good for cocoa before I clear it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha kookoo dani ajie lɛ?

english: Good cocoa land has deep, rich soil that lets water drain easily while keeping enough moisture for root growth. Lands that flood easily or contain thick rocky layers close to the surface will restrict cocoa root development.
