ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni haa nu hoɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Hei ni nu shwieɔ nɔ oya loo tɛi ni mli tse ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ haaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do crops planted on freshly cleared forest land grow faster than crops on old grassland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ hee ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi shikpɔŋ momo nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest soils are rich in rotten leaves and natural plant food that built up over many years. Grassland soils often have fewer nutrients and hard ground that makes it harder for young crop roots to spread out.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ baai ni egboi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kooloi alɛɛhei lɛ amli lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo, ni ehiɛ hu wa, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete heavily with each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block light from each other, resulting in smaller crops and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ ŋmaa bibii hu baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need extra fertilizer if they are already growing in normal soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa nɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, growing cocoa trees pull nutrients out of the soil to produce pods. Applying fertilizer puts essential plant food back into the ground, helping the trees stay strong and produce bigger yields every season.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo daa be mli.

english: How can I tell if the fertilizer I applied is actually working on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You will notice the leaves changing to a deeper green color, fresh leaf shoots appearing, and the trees flowering more abundantly, which eventually leads to more pods forming.
ga: Obaana akɛ baai lɛ etsɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ waa. Tsofɔi heei jeɔ kpo. ni tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo Enɛ baaha yɛ naagbee lɛ, afee pods babaoo.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops during the heavy rainy season or the dry season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ loo hulutsoo be mli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist at the start of the rainy season. Torrential rains can wash the fertilizer away, while dry soil stops the crop roots from absorbing the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet weather. Spraying approved protective chemicals prevents the fungus from attacking and destroying your pods.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akatutua o-pods lɛ ni efite.

english: Spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool and calm. High midday sun can make the chemicals evaporate too quickly or cause chemical burns on the plant leaves.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eyɛ dioo lɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eha tsofai ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why do insects keep returning to my farm even after I spray my crops once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ shikome moŋ?

english: Spraying often kills adult pests, but their eggs hatch a short time later. You need to follow a regular spraying schedule to destroy new generations and fully break the pest cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni eda lɛ. Shi amɛwuji lɛ fɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ. Esa akɛ onyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ koni okpãtã yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ hiɛ ni okɛfo tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Why should I use recommended officers' chemicals instead of buying cheap ones at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai ni onukpai lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe nɔ ni jara waaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Officially supplied chemicals are tested to ensure they effectively treat crop diseases without damaging your trees, whereas unverified market chemicals might be fake, dangerous, or ruin your crop yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsofai ni maŋ lɛ kɛhaa lɛ mli koni ana akɛ amɛtsaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee otsei lɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ jara nɔ ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale, oshara, loo efite onibii.

english: What does it mean when the leaves on my cocoa tree start turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mi-kookoo baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that your crop is lacking essential soil nutrients, not getting enough water, or suffering from pest damage. Feeding the soil or treating pests helps restore the tree's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni oduɔ lɛ bɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When trees are planted too closely, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight over water and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the trees to produce pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee pods.

english: How does joining a local farmer cooperative actually help me improve my crop yield?
ga: Te maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cooperatives organize farmers into groups so agricultural officers can easily supply genuine fertilizers and spraying chemicals directly to you, while also providing training on proper crop care.
ga: Kuu ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome lɛ toɔ okwaafoi ahe gbɛjianɔ amɛwoɔ kui amli bɔni afee ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ aha bo tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves and grow big. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and becoming small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a viral disease spread by these pests. Removing heavily affected plants helps stop the problem from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Tsei ni ena naagbai waa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni naagba lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by hot, dry weather, when insects like mirids attack the stems, or when the soil lacks the nutrients needed to feed developing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Beni kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui tutuaa tso lɛ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, especially in heavy clay ground during heavy rains. Excess water cuts off air to the roots, allowing harmful fungi to grow and spoil the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ mli wa waa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ ŋmei tso lɛ masɛi koni ŋmei tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. When leaves absorb plenty of sunlight, they make the food needed to grow large, heavy yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbai lɛ aya hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ŋɔ hulu la babaoo lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ baai lɛ bafeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra young shoots coming up around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and soil nutrients from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On very hot days, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, but usually recovers once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔ.

english: What is causing ragged holes to appear in the center of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji ni etse ehe lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Holes inside young corn leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding and feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Checking plants early helps you treat them before the growing point is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ tsũi lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsa amɛ dani he ni amɛdaraa lɛ akpata.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure to my farm help my soil hold water longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil. It binds soil particles together, allowing the ground to retain moisture much longer during dry periods while slowly feeding the plants.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ be babaoo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii fiofio.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant the exact same crop in the same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning and turning brown in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates living shade umbrellas that protect the cocoa roots and leaves while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo shishifãi kɛ baai ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baa.

english: If my maize seedlings get sick or damaged early on, can they still recover and give me a full harvest?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ hela mɔ amɛ loo amɛfite mra Ani ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni yeɔ emuu aba?

english: Early sickness usually causes permanent damage that stays with the crop throughout its life. Even if the plant recovers, the early stress stunts its root growth, resulting in smaller cobs at harvest time.
ga: Hela ni jɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ kɛ fitemɔ ni hiɔ shi daa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ ewala be fɛɛ mli baa. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa po Shi mra be mli haomɔ haa eshishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, cob tsei lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: What is the white coat that looks like flour or fuzz spreading across my pepper leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ atade yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda loo ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛ eshwa mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ nɛɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It forms on leaf surfaces in humid weather, blocking sunlight and weakening the plant's ability to produce fruit.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Efeɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves have tiny white sticky insects gathering underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Abua naa yɛ ŋmei baai ashishi?

english: Those are mealybugs or whiteflies. They suck sap directly from the leaves, causing them to curl and slowing down the growth of the cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Ani amɛji mealybugs loo ŋmeii yɛŋ? Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa amɛkpãa shi ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa fioo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: When crops experience heat or water stress, they drop their blossoms to save energy and survive. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering during flowering keeps the blossoms on the plant.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo loo nu he haomɔ kpe Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baawo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the afternoon heat but look normal again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw it from the dry soil. Covering the soil with grass mulch keeps the ground cool and moist, stopping the leaves from wilting.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the young top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize plants automatically take nitrogen from their old lower leaves and send it up to support new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ amɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and rotting while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which happens when soil moisture fluctuates wildly. Keeping the ground evenly watered helps the plant transport calcium into the growing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings staying small and turning pale even though I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe tseee lɛ? Namɔ nuɔ etsitsi nɔ daa gbi?

english: Overwatering drowns tiny seedling roots by removing air pockets from the soil. Roots need air as well as water to absorb nutrients and grow strong.
ga: Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Okɛ ohe awo nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni ooojie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I clear all the big trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Keeping older shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby provides a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa bushes are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves from the tip downward usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to produce green leaves and grow strong stalks, so adding compost, poultry manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can correct this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do people tell me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ afee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer improves the soil health and helps the neighboring maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them and cannot drain away, suffocating the tubers underground. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋɔ be kɛwo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch sunlight with their leaves. Lifting the leaves off the hot ground allows the plant to produce more energy through sunlight, which leads to bigger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛjɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Spraying the plants early with organic sprays like neem oil or recommended insecticides helps clear the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ejie kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: Why is my tomato plant producing plenty of leaves and height, but dropping all its yellow flowers without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ baai babaoo kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato.

english: When tomato plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing leafy branches instead of setting fruit. Switching to a fertilizer rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to hold its flowers and form fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why should I cut down the small shoot suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, sunlight, and water in the soil. Pruning away the extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce a large, heavy cluster of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cowpea crops look crowded and produce very few pods when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed adequate spacing allows the plant to branch out fully and produce maximum pods.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niji shwieɔ shi kwraa ni ewoɔ pod yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or dry leaves over the bare soil around my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egboi loo baai ni egboi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle mi-aduawai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, prevents the hot sun from drying out the soil, and stops unwanted weeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: How often am I supposed to harvest my cocoa pods once the main season starts?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛji be titri lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: You should not stick to a rigid schedule like waiting a whole month. Cocoa pods ripen at different times, so you need to inspect your farm regularly and harvest ripe pods promptly before they spoil.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ ohe kpɛtɛɔ be he gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni mli wa he, tamɔ nyɔŋ muu fɛɛ mɛmɔ. Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani amɛfite.

english: Why does my cocoa field produce so many ripe pods starting around October?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ aaafee October kɛyaa lɛ?

english: October marks the start of the main cocoa harvest season in Ghana because rain patterns earlier in the year cause trees to flower and develop mature pods around this time.
ga: October ji kookoo kpamɔ be titri lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana. Akɛni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: If I am busy on another farm, can I wait until the end of the month to harvest all my cocoa at once?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ mihe wo ŋmɔ kroko mli Ani manyɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nyɔŋ lɛ naagbee dani makpa mi-kokoo lɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: Waiting a full month is too risky because many pods will become overripe before then. Harvesting regularly protects your beans and keeps your overall yield high.
ga: Nyɔŋ muu fɛɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ yɛ oshara tsɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo baakwɛ̃ tsɔ dani nakai be lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ okpaa nii daa lɛ, ebaabu okɔfi yibii lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What happens to cocoa pods if I leave them on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo ŋmeii anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes them to overripe. The seeds inside can begin to sprout, the flesh rots, and the entire pod becomes damaged and unusable.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere fe nine. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi akwɛ̃, loo lɛ baagbo, ni ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efite ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is ready for harvesting versus one that is already overripe?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ loo amɛshwere tsɔ?

english: A ready pod turns a clear yellow or orange color depending on the variety, while an overripe pod starts turning dark brown or black, feels soft, and may show rot.
ga: Pods ni asaa he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse, ni enɛ damɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ, ebaanu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ egbo.

english: How does leaving pods to overripe affect the price I get for my cocoa beans?
ga: Te ŋmɔtɔ ni mikɛhaa lɛ baaná jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Overripe pods contain germinated or decayed beans that lower the grade of your harvest. Cocoa buyers reject or discount bad quality beans, reducing your profit.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ yɛ ŋmeii loo amɛmiifite, ni no haa okpamɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ kpooɔ loo amɛjieɔ kɔfe yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does it become harder to clear my cocoa pods if I delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛji mikpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Delayed harvesting causes pods to rot and soften on the branch, making them harder to pick cleanly and breaking them open without damaging the good beans inside becomes difficult.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni baa sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahala nibii ni he tse. ni ogbala amɛ ni ofiteee ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ ebafee nɔ ni wa.

english: Does leaving overripe pods on my trees attract diseases to the rest of my farm?
ga: Kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaagbala helai kɛba hei krokomɛi. Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo daabi?

english: Yes, overripe and rotting pods become breeding grounds for fungal diseases like black pod disease, which can quickly spread to healthy young pods on nearby trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni egboi lɛ bafeɔ he ni ŋmeii helai, tamɔ black pod hela, ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛya ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Does harvesting ripe cocoa pods quickly help my tree grow better future pods?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa oya lɛ baaye abua mitso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii kpakpai wɔsɛɛ?

english: Yes, removing mature pods promptly prevents the tree from wasting nutrients on overripe fruit and reduces disease stress, allowing the tree to focus energy on new pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni edara lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hela mli baa lɛ baa shi Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ maa pod hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I mix beans from overripe cocoa pods with fresh beans when I ferment them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ amli lɛ afutu ŋmeii heei beni mikɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: No, mixing germinated or spoiled beans from overripe pods with fresh beans ruins the fermentation process for the whole batch, leading to poor flavor and lower quality cocoa.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo efite ni jɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ futu ŋmeii heei amli lɛ, ebaafite bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haaa kookoo lɛ ŋɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, intense sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly. Keeping selected large trees or interplanting with fast-growing plantains creates a protective canopy until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni eda ni ahala lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni daa oya ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Why should I plant my maize in neat rows with proper spacing instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni gbɛ ni sa nɔ? Yɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each maize plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing heavily with neighboring plants, leading to thicker stems and larger grain ears.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aka akaŋ waa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui lɛ atoi wuji.

english: Yellowing leaves that start from the leaf tip and move down the middle usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which crops need in large amounts to maintain healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa yɛ babaoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai amli

english: Why shouldn't I burn the cleared bush on my field before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and micro-organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops. Allowing cleared weeds to decay naturally returns nutrients to the soil and helps retain moisture.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and distorted yellow leaves are a main sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small flying insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this issue.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ebɔle ehe, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi titri. Kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and dark dropings inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing point of the plant. Regular monitoring and early application of safe bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ daa kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or insufficient water, causing stress that prevents pollination and forces the plant to shed blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ pollination naa baa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take three to four years before I can harvest any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani manyɛ makpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that must build a strong trunk and deep root system before it has accumulated enough stored energy to produce flowers and sustain fruit pods.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni esa akɛ ená shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani ebaanyɛ ebua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni ekɛha aduawai akui lɛ niyenii.

english: If I plant seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest, why is my yield much lower this year?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi kwraa afi nɛɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields for only one generation; saving and replanting those seeds causes the crop to lose its vigor, uniformity, and resistance to pests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe waaa, amɛfeɔ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans get full of tiny holes and turn into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Tiny insects called bruchid beetles lay eggs in the stored beans and eat them from the inside. Storing well-dried beans in airtight containers or triple-layer PICS bags suffocates the insects and protects your grain.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ bruchid beetles lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo PICS kotoku ni yɔɔ ŋmeii etɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu odumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to make green leaves, and when the soil runs out, the plant steals nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed the new growth on top.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I wait to apply my solid fertilizer until after the ground is moist from rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa afata he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha sũ lɛ mli atsɔ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil so crop roots can drink it in. If you put dry fertilizer on dry ground in hot sun, it cannot feed the plant and can actually burn the roots or evaporate into the air.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enyɛŋ eha tso lɛ niyenii ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are weak under direct sunlight and high heat. They need partial shade from plantain trees or tall shade trees during their first two years to keep the soil cool and moist while their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo tsei ni kwɔlɔ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Cassava shows it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the main stem becomes thick and woody, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward from the large tubers expanding beneath the surface.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso titri lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii wuji ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting and getting soft even while sitting in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo be mli ni mita mi-shĩa lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living roots that go to sleep after harvest. When the warm season arrives, the tuber naturally wakes up from dormancy and begins using its stored food and moisture to grow new stems, which softens the yam.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni yaa wɔɔhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ba lɛ Yitso lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ ehiɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni obɔi niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni ekɛwo tsei heei. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing any fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When daytime heat gets too high and air is dry, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries out and fails to fertilize the plant. Unable to make seeds, the plant drops the useless flowers to conserve its energy and water.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ tso lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Bɔni afee ni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward into cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf undersides, or by a virus carried by those insects that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni anyɛ adu shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants tall and weak, resulting in small ears or empty cobs with no grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ kwɔlɔɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa toi bibii loo ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do some plantain suckers grow fast and strong while others remain small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei komɛi daraa oya ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Suckers with narrow, needle-like leaves (sword suckers) have strong underground corms packed with energy to grow quickly. Suckers with broad leaves (water suckers) grew attached too loosely to the mother plant and lack the stored energy needed for fast growth.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmeii (klante tsei) lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni baaha amɛdara oya. Suckers ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ (suckers) lɛ kpɛtɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he waa tsɔ. ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ oya lɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my cowpea harvest even if I clear them late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cowpea ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ amɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds do the most damage during the first three to four weeks of a crop's life by stealing nutrients and water while the crop is young. Once a young plant is stunted early on, clearing weeds later cannot undo the lost growth potential.
ga: Jwɛi fiteɔ nii fe fɛɛ yɛ tso ko wala klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni ejuɔ beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbɔjɔ mra lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ asaa bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its green color and build big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop harvests every year when I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your main crop with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Nibii komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves high off the damp ground so they capture maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne fungal diseases, leading to bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ. ni amɛkwɛ hetsemɔ nɔ kɛjɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ yitso agbo baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: When too many young suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete with the mother plant for soil nutrients, water, and light. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough nourishment to grow large bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛkɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one spot causes the seedlings to fight each other for survival, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room for root growth, water uptake, and leaf sunlight exposure.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo he kome lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ, nu ni amɛheɔ, kɛ baa lɛ hulu la.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and dry up during the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, where invisible organisms in soggy soil block the tubes inside the roots. Improving soil drainage so water does not collect around the stem helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ, ehaaa nu abua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe.

english: Curled and pale leaves are a classic sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies and spread through infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents the virus from stunting crop growth.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii ni ale waa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akatsi tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do small holes appear all over my cabbage leaves shortly after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Amɛje kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars and beetles eating the tender green foliage. Checking under the leaves early in the morning and applying recommended neem oil or pest treatments protects the cabbage before the heads form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa kaabeji baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kaaba lɛ he dani ekɛ eyitso awo mli.

english: Black, sunken spots on the bottom of tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady through regular watering and mulching prevents this condition.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many tiny, shriveled young pods before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni egboi babaoo dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he lɛ?

english: The natural dropping of tiny cocoa pods, called cherelle wilt, happens when the tree has more pods than it can feed with available water and nutrients. Proper shade management, pruning, and soil feeding reduce tree stress so more pods grow to full size.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cherelle wilt lɛ adebɔɔ mli shigbeemɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ aye. Shade management pruning Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Koni eha pods lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for plants, or that the soil has too much standing water, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ekã shi babaoo Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and diseases that love maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does animal manure help my crops differently than buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahemɔ he?

english: Chemical fertilizer provides quick food directly to the plant, while animal manure improves the long-term quality of the soil itself, helping it hold onto water and nutrients much longer.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi aŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular, as extreme heat and water stress cause the plant to drop flowers to save its own strength.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ ahi shi.

english: Staking exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight so the plant can make more food, which leads to much larger yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the ground too fast, keeps weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as it decays.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, dark, and humid conditions; trimming extra branches lets sunlight in and helps keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, duŋ, ni efɔ. Afolɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he koni hulu la abote mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are sucking the juices out of the leaves or spreading a virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ he okadi. Amɛmii nu nu kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ amli loo amɛmiigbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ mli.

english: Should I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is usually safer to wait for the rains to become frequent and steady, because the first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ kɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds early before they grow big on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Dani jwɛi lɛ baadara yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Early weeding stops weeds from stealing food, sunlight, and water from your young crops. If you wait until weeds grow tall and mature, they drop seeds that multiply and make your farming work much harder later.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akaju niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ shwere ni amɛdara lɛ, Amɛbaashi dumɔwui ni baashwere ni baaha okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to weed my farm before the rains start or after rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ aje shishi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to weed when the ground is slightly moist so roots come out easily, but before heavy rains start. If heavy rain falls right after you weed, uprooted weeds with remaining live roots might attach back to the wet soil and start growing again.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie jwɛi lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ajie amɛhe kpo oya. Shi dani nugbɔ baanɛ waa Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Jwɛi ni ajie shi eyɛ shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lolo lɛ baanyɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I leave weeds I have pulled out on top of the soil, will they rot and help my crops?
ga: Kɛ mishi jwɛi ni migbala lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ani ebaagbo ni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, when uprooted weeds are left on the ground and rain falls on them, they decay and rot into organic matter. This natural compost enriches the soil with nutrients that feed your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, Nakai jwɛi lɛ baafite ni amɛbaatsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How do weeds affect the growth and yield of my maize crops?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa mi ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your maize for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. When weeds dominate your farm, your maize plants become thin, yellow, and produce small ears.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-corn lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu. Kɛ jwɛi ye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, O-abele tsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛbaawo toi bibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when there are too many weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your crops are starving for nutrients like nitrogen because the fast-growing weeds around them are taking up all the food and water in the soil.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii tamɔ nitrogen, ejaakɛ jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some weeds grow back on my farm even after I have cut them down with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ dade tswa lɛ po?

english: Slashing only removes the top stems and leaves, leaving the root system alive underground. To completely kill stubborn weeds so they do not return, you must uproot them completely from the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ afo lɛ, ajieɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ani oosumɔ ni ojie jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ koni amɛkaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba? Esa akɛ ojie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Should I completely uproot weeds from the soil or just cut them off at ground level?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa loo mafo amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Uprooting is better for deep-rooted weeds because it removes the entire root system so they cannot sprout again. Cutting at ground level only works temporarily for soft grasses.
ga: Shishifãi ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ejieɔ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni ekakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afoɔ lɛ ji be kukuoo ko pɛ kɛha jwɛi bibii.

english: What happens to weeds I uproot if heavy rain falls on my field immediately after weeding?
ga: Mɛni baa jwɛi ni migbala lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni migbe jwɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: If the uprooted weeds have fully dried out in the sun, rain will make them rot into natural manure. However, if the weeds were pulled out fresh and left on wet soil, the rain can cause them to root themselves back into the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ lɛ gĩ yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Nugbɔ baafite jwɛi lɛ ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi, kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ ehee ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, Nugbɔ baanyɛ aha jwɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ atswa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds multiply so fast on my farm right after the first rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ faa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in dry soil during the dry season. As soon as the first rains fall, the moisture and heat cause these hidden seeds to germinate all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Fɛ̃i kɛ latsaa haa nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shikome.

english: How does clearing weeds in time prevent me from wasting my money on fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ mi gbɛ koni mikafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: When your farm is clean, all the fertilizer you apply goes directly to your crops. If weeds are present, they will absorb most of the expensive nutrients before your crops can even reach them.
ga: Beni oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ lɛ, amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii ni jara wa lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or planting cowpeas and beans before maize helps put this food back into your soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo adu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei dani ŋmãa baa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops get smaller and weaker every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the exact same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients out of the earth until the soil becomes exhausted. Swapping maize with groundnuts or cowpeas every season helps rebuild and refresh the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli aahu kɛyashi sũ lɛ mli baaho. Ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for me to sow my seeds when the early rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Sowing right after the very first light rain is risky because the hot sun can return and scorch the seeds. It is safest to wait until the rains become steady and soak the ground several inches deep so seeds stay moist and grow strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli kɛyashɛ inchii babaoo. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard like concrete a few days after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare, uncovered soil loses its moisture quickly to the hot sun and gets packed hard by heavy rain drops. Covering the bare ground around your crops with dried leaves, grass, or straw keeps the dirt cool, moist, and soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ahako nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Ha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ nii kɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi koni eye ebua ni eha muji afee fɛ̃i, efɔ, ni efee bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are soft like newborn babies and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa creates a leafy canopy that shields them from scorching heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee. ni enyɛŋ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excessive rainwater sits around them without draining away, especially in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps extra water flow away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. ni nu ejeee kpo titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, light bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many young suckers grow around a single plantain tree, they all compete for the same food and water in the dirt. Pruning away the extra shoots and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the main tree to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi niji fioo komɛi pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: What is eating small ragged holes inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended, safe treatments into the center of the plants kills the pests before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baagbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dani ekpata oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the heat becomes too intense or when the plant goes through dry spells without enough water. Mulching the base of the tomato plants and watering them regularly keeps the ground cool so the flowers can form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei tsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ha o-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi ni okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stunted in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Spraying the plants with safe botanical or recommended insect sprays stops these tiny bugs from spreading the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa curl lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii lɛ akabote tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi baanyɛ agbɛ helai ashwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in full sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil, helping young cocoa plants survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo canopy tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shade aba ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to bear fruit when there are many suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same food and water in the soil. Pruning extra shoots so only two or three healthy suckers remain allows the main plant to grow faster and fruit earlier.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛshiɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni edaa oya ni ewoɔ yibii mra.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is missing nitrogen, a main nutrient needed for green growth. Applying manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the plants are young keeps the leaves green and increases crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo tsei lɛ amli beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔji amli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants falling off without forming any vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo aduawai ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, poor watering, or lack of pollination by insects like bees. Regular watering during dry weather and avoiding heavy chemical spraying while plants are blooming helps fruits set properly.
ga: Eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. nu ni ehiii Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ pollination. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo be mli ni tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava yields get smaller every time I replant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing cassava continuously on the same soil drains essential nutrients and allows crop diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and improves future harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ŋmei ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and stopping overall growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Spraying early with neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides clears the insects and allows healthy leaves to grow back.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie kooloi bibii lɛ kɛya ni eye ebua ni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rotten before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven soil moisture and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering tomatoes regularly and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps the plant build firm, healthy fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ tomato nɔ nu daa ni akɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava tubers turn dark and spoil within just two days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ ediŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start to decay quickly once removed from the ground because air enters the harvested root and breaks it down. Harvest cassava only when you are ready to sell or process it immediately into products like gari or flour.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shishifãi ni akpa lɛ amli ni efiteɔ amɛ. Kpãa ŋmãa lɛ pɛ kɛji ofee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo okɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofee nibii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots in the barn long before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be saŋŋ dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their resting phase and sprout when temperatures rise inside storage areas. Keeping yams on raised bamboo racks in a well-ventilated, shady barn slows down sprouting and keeps tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji hulutsoo be tee hiɛ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes to ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my stored dried maize end up full of small holes and fine powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Small holes and powder in stored maize are caused by grain weevils eating the inside of the seeds. Thoroughly drying maize until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags or sealed drums protects the grain from insect infestation.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ewa ni akɛto vacuum kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu ŋmãa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing from the bottom leaves upward is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Giving the maize nitrogen-rich fertilizer at the right time helps the leaves turn deep green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ha ŋmãa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and stops pest buildup.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akpa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a mild rain, but avoid applying it right before or during heavy downpours. Covering the fertilizer lightly with soil near the plant's roots keeps it from washing away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ amɛwomɔ he dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa nɔ fioo Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while preventing leaf rot.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli ni atsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite lɛ nɔ.

english: Multiple suckers compete with the mother plant for nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers directs energy into growing large, heavy fruit.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, eheɔ hewalɛ ni akɛbaawo aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know which cassava stem is best to cut and plant for a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afolɔ ni adu koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Choose strong, mature stems from healthy plants that are 8 to 18 months old. Cuts taken from the middle part of the stem sprout fastest and produce healthier roots than soft green tips or old base wood.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ amli tsei ni wa ni eda. Tsoi ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo basal tso momo.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns out weeds that would otherwise compete with young rice plants, while giving the rice roots the constant moisture needed to draw nutrients from the soil efficiently.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efuɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ abɔ akaŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they grow full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches and cocoa foliage lets in sunlight and airflow, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
