ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine kɛ kookoo baai ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress or lack consistent soil moisture and key nutrients. Regular watering during hot spells helps flowers stay attached and turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds consume nutrients, water, and sunlight much faster than young crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the soil food they need to grow strong and tall.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or planting beans before maize restores the soil's strength.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani ashɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts helps my soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that pull nitrogen food out of the air and store it in small balls on their roots. When the groundnut plant dies, that stored food remains in the ground to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts ji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni gbalaa niyenii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ bɔɔlu bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo lɛ, Niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep dropping off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as too much direct sunlight, strong heat, or lack of water. Providing light shade from taller trees and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yam leaves act like solar panels that catch sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on sticks helps the leaves catch full sunlight and air, resulting in larger yam tubers at harvest.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, ni emɔɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji kɛ́ akpa.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden heavy soaking of water after a long dry period, causing the inside of the fruit to grow faster than the skin. Keeping your watering consistent stops the skin from bursting.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu mli trukaa beni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe hewolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaatsi hewolo lɛ naa koni ekafo.

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the funnel of the plant to feed. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides destroys the worms before they ruin the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ faai lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛtsu nii lɛ baagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛkpãtã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds growing near my cassava reduce the size of my tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cassava lɛ masɛi lɛ miigbɔjɔ mi-tubers lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your cassava. Clearing weeds during the first three months gives your cassava full access to the nutrients it needs to grow big roots.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-cassava lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small ears of corn instead of large, full yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii agbo ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal food and water away from the main plantain mother tree. Removing most of the suckers and leaving only one strong replacement ensures the main tree yields a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ashi nɔ kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛto najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmeii wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in open land without trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni tsei bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight during their first two years. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain or cocoyam provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture, protecting fragile cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cocoa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing jagged holes with brown sawdust-like waste inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaf whorl of the maize plant to feed on fresh, tender tissue, leaving behind chewed leaves and frass (waste).
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ. Ashiɔ baai ni ashɛre kɛ nibii ni efite (nibii ni efite) lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot away quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ duŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in damp, cool, and overly shady conditions. Excessive rainfall sweeps fungal spores across the farm, especially if air cannot flow freely between trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ tsɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: Why are my cassava roots soft and rotting underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soggy and waterlogged for too long. Stagnant water deprives underground tubers of air, encouraging rot fungi to attack and decay the crop beneath the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fite.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark brown and sunken while they are growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efoɔ shi beni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by calcium deficiency in the fruit. It usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly, preventing the plant roots from taking up calcium consistently during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aná calcium daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete directly against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This leaves each plant weak and unable to form large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I cut down extra suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Excess suckers steal water, plant food, and sunlight away from the main mother plant. Removing extra shoots leaves only 2 or 3 healthy suckers of different ages, giving the parent tree enough energy to grow heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, tso niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ baashiɔ, ni enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ panicle ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can trap solar energy to make food. Proper leaf exposure to light directly drives the growth of large, healthy yam tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. koni ená hulu la Enɛ ji koni ebaa lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu hewalɛ ni ekɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ awo la mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my land produce better maize yields after I grow cowpeas or groundnuts on it the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ beni midu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen directly from the air and trap it in their roots. When they complete their life cycle, this trapped nitrogen naturally enriches the soil for nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I cover fertilizer with soil near the root zone instead of scattering it on dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer scattered on top of hot, dry ground evaporates into the air or gets washed away by surface rain runoff. Burying it near the root zone allows the crop to absorb the nutrients straight into its root system.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ afu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep dying even though the leaves look healthy before they suddenly collapse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ yaa nɔ egboɔ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa dani amɛgbee shi po?

english: Some plant diseases live hidden in the ground and attack the roots directly. This prevents the plant from drinking water and taking up food from the soil, causing it to suddenly die even if the top looked fine at first.
ga: Tsei ahe helai komɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtutuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anu nu ni amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ha egbo trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: How can I prevent diseases from staying in my soil from one farming season to the next?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hela naa koni ekahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ be kome mli kɛyashi be kroko mli?

english: You can practice crop rotation by planting a different type of crop in that soil each season. This starves out the soil-borne pests and diseases because the specific plant they feed on is no longer there.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ atsu nii kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ejaakɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know which chemical medicine is right to fix yellow leaves on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ lɛ tsamɔ?

english: Yellow leaves can be caused by missing nutrients in the soil or by pests, so you must identify the exact problem first. Using the wrong chemical medicine can waste your money and damage your plants.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ŋmɔŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni oyɔse naagba lɛ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsofa ni ejaaa ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ afite shika ni efite otsei lɛ.

english: Is it safe to sprinkle pesticide powder directly onto my crops to kill insects?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ powda afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛgbe kooloi bibii?

english: Pesticide powders can kill insects, but using too much or applying it incorrectly can burn the plant leaves, pollute the ground beneath, and make your food unsafe to eat.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi powda baanyɛ agbe kooloi. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine loo akɛtsuuu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai ashã. Ekɛ mujiwoo baa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa oniyenii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical medicine on my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ aduawai anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when the sun is low, because strong heat during midday can cause the medicine to evaporate quickly or burn the leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo leebi maŋkpa. Yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ fioo lɛ yɔɔ Ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa lɛ atsɔ oya loo eha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Can applying too many chemical medicines hurt the ground where I grow my food?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, overusing harsh chemicals can kill the helpful living organisms in the ground, like earthworms, leaving your soil weak, dry, and unable to support healthy crops in the future.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ agbe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egbi, ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to fall off the stems onto the ground before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani eshɛɔ?

english: Tomatoes usually fall early because insects have damaged the stem, the plant lacks steady water, or a disease has weakened the point where the fruit connects to the branch.
ga: Tomato lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya ejaakɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ eshishifãi lɛ. Nu bɛ tsei ahe be fɛɛ be. Aloo hela lɛ haa he ni aduawai lɛ kɛ tso nine lɛ tsaa yɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants turn soft and rot after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil drowns the roots by blocking air, allowing harmful fungi living in the wet ground to multiply and rot the plant roots.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hiɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ tsei shishifãi.

english: How does the quality of my soil affect how fast my cassava roots grow big?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa bɔ ni mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ daa oya lɛ he?

english: Soil is where your crop gets its food and water; if the ground is too hard or lacks essential nutrients, the cassava roots cannot spread easily or grow large.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ji he ni onibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu yɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli lɛ, Cassava shishifãi hu nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo loo amɛfee agbo.

english: Can I use animal manure to improve soil that isn't producing good yields anymore?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ ni wooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, adding well-dried animal manure feeds the soil naturally, helps it hold water better, and brings back friendly organisms that keep the ground healthy for crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloo ŋmei ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from drought. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many big green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɔlɔ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when there is insufficient water, which prevents pollen from properly fertilizing the flowers to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Enɛ haaa pollen lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over easily when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Underground pests like nematodes and root weevils weaken the roots, making it hard for the plant to support the heavy weight of a maturing plantain bunch without extra wooden stakes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes kɛ shishifãi ahe ŋmeii haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tso lɛ akɛ eeekwɛ plantains kuu ko ni eda kwraa lɛ nɔ ni tsii ni tsoi krokomɛi fataaa he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my ginger plants dry up when I plant them in a clear, open field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger tso lɛ mli egbi beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli ni tsei bɛ he lɛ?

english: Ginger naturally thrives under forest canopy shade. Direct, harsh sunlight causes the leaves to scorch and dries out the soil too quickly for the rhizomes to develop.
ga: Ginger kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi ashishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ bɔni afee ni rhizomes lɛ aba.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize help the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmã lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmã lɛ ni ewaa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural food supply that feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why do the improved high-yield maize varieties require different care than my traditional farm seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni atsake lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi blema ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to grow faster and produce larger yields in less time, but they require precise spacing, regular weeding, and adequate nutrients to reach their full potential.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be fioo mli. Shi he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ he miihia amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni anyɛ ashɛ nyɛmɔ fɛɛ he

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and get infested with insects so quickly in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite ni mihe miiwo mi nitoohe lɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Grains stored with high moisture content attract mold and encourage insect eggs to hatch. Drying grain thoroughly in the sun until it is hard prevents pests and rot during storage.
ga: Ŋmãa ni ato he ni fɛ̃i babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa ŋmei ni ewoɔ koolooi awɔlɔi hewalɛ koni amɛ fɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they don't rot after digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? Bɔni afee ni ekagbo kɛji atsa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves naturally turn yellow and die down, signaling that the tuber has fully accumulated its starch and formed a tough outer skin that protects it in storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tuber lɛ ebua starch ni fa bɔ ni sa naa ni efee kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni mli wa ni buɔ ehe koni akɛto.

english: Why do my harvested cabbage heads feel soft and spongy instead of hard and tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei ni akpa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ sponji moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads remain soft if the plant receives irregular watering or experiences nutrient shortages during the stage when the inner leaves are folding tightly together.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baakã he afee blɛoo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nu ni ejaaa nɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa lɛ yɛ be mli ni emli baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I cut down all the tall trees on my land before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani mijeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ shishi?

english: Leaving some tall trees provides natural shade and protects your soil from being washed away by heavy rains. Soil needs organic cover from tree leaves to stay rich and moist for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei kakadaji komɛi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahole lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛ tsei ahe baai amli koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa ni edɔ.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard a few years after I clear the forest to farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mijie koo lɛ mli kɛha okwaayeli lɛ?

english: When forest trees are cleared, the ground loses its protection from direct sunlight and rain. Without leaf mulch and tree roots to hold moisture, the topsoil gets washed away and dries out quickly.
ga: Kɛji ajie tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he dɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tso shishifãi ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Afɔ̃ɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni egbiɔ oya.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing much fewer pods now than they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, the soil around them loses nutrients, and old branches become less productive. Without proper pruning, soil feeding, or replanting, the trees naturally yield fewer pods over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni niji momo lɛ baaná yibii babaoo Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ niyenii loo dumɔ hee ko bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops, like plantain or cassava, to shield them until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. koni amɛtsu nii tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛyashi amɛhe baawa

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and spoil on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is often Black Pod disease, caused by fungi that thrive in cold, wet, and overly shaded environments. Trimming extra branches lets in sunlight and air to keep the pods dry.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ eji black pod hela Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune or trim branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless or diseased branches so the tree can send all its water and food directly to growing healthy, large cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajieɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ enu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya kookoo tsei wuji ni miida waa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I get higher crop yields from my small farm without having to clear a new forest?
ga: Maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee enɛ ni mikɛ koo hee ko efoŋ?

english: You can harvest more from small land by using improved seed varieties, applying the right fertilizer, maintaining correct plant spacing, and keeping the soil healthy rather than simply expanding farm size.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant only one crop on my land or mix cocoa with food crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo makɛ kookoo afutu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Mixing young cocoa with food crops like plantains provides shade for the cocoa, gives you food and income while waiting for cocoa to yield, and keeps the soil covered.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo bibii kɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains futu mli lɛ, ehaa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo. Ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ ajie ehe kpo lɛ. ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How can I protect my crops from dying when the rains stop for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps moisture trapped in the soil and prevents the sun from drying out the plant roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) shwie oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is weak and needs extra nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni maná niyenii krokomɛi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If your crop leaves turn pale or yellow, plants remain small, or flowers fall off without making fruit, your soil is likely missing key nutrients that fertilizer or compost can replace.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei lɛ ji bibii lolo. Aloo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ atsake lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants use to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and getting sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like mealybugs sucking the sap out of your plant. Spraying the leaves with a light mixture of soapy water or neem oil helps wash these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ fioo shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil gets too dry during hot days. Watering the plants consistently at their roots keeps the soil moist so the flowers can stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛtsɔmɔ chili ŋmeii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from dry soil. Keeping the soil moist continuously helps the roots move calcium into the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I plant them under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a living shelter that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa shĩa ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa.

english: Why should I avoid planting my corn seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants end up fighting for the same food, sunlight, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stalks and produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kome he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How many suckers should I leave growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Tsofai enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ he fɛɛ he? Midumɔwu titri lɛ

english: It is best to leave only one or two strong suckers next to the main plantain tree. If you leave too many, they will steal plant food from the main tree and lead to small, light bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ plantain lɛ fã titri lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ eshwɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ, Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni efeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together with my corn make my corn grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmã lɛ, ehaa mi-ŋmã lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When you plant them with corn, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that help the corn grow.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa du lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I test if my soil has the right moisture for planting maize after rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a small ball of topsoil in your hand; if it holds together without water dripping out and crumbles easily when gently pressed, the ground is ready for your seeds.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afee bɔɔlu bibii yɛ onine mli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni efooo ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ onyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to catch sunlight and grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from weeds so they can catch maximum sunlight without rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ kpaa gbee bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛfiteee.

english: I want to start planting rubber trees on my land, but where do I go to get proper training and certified seedlings?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi rɔbɔt tsei dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi nɛgbɛ maya koni mayahe tsɔsemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Before planting rubber, you should visit a local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA) office or contact established rubber companies like Ghana Rubber Estates Limited (GREL). They provide certified seedlings and step-by-step guidance so you do not lose your investment by using wrong planting methods.
ga: Dani obaadu rɔbɔt lɛ, esa akɛ oyasara Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ loo oyatswa rɔbɔt nitsumɔhe ko ni ato ama shi tamɔ Ghana Rubber Estates Limited (GREL) lɛ. Amɛhaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he koni okɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ akafite kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni ejaaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How many years do I need to wait after planting rubber before I can start harvesting the liquid latex?
ga: Kɛ́ odu rɔbɔt lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi latɛs ni mli edɔ lɛ naabuaamɔ?

english: Rubber trees usually take 6 to 7 years to mature before they are ready for tapping. Tapping them too early damages the tree trunk and ruins future yields, so it is important to wait until the trunk reaches the correct thickness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ otswa tso lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite tso lɛ shishi ni ebaafite wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ shishi lɛ baashɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni sa lɛ he.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and small cobs, reducing your overall harvest compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for growing rubber trees instead of cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha rɔbɔt tsei adumɔ yɛ kookoo najiaŋ?

english: Rubber trees grow best in deep, well-drained acidic soils with high rainfall, mostly found in the Western and Central regions of Ghana. You can ask an agricultural extension officer to test your soil depth and drainage to tell you which crop will perform best.
ga: Rɔba tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Anaa amɛ babaoo yɛ Ghana anaigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ hei. Obaanyɛ obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ ni eka shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ekwɛ koni ekɛɛ bo tsei ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava between my young rubber trees while waiting for them to grow big?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-gum tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛdara?

english: You can plant food crops like cassava or plantain between young rubber trees during the first two years to generate income, but you must leave enough space around the tree bases so the cassava does not steal sunlight and nutrients from the rubber.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ rɔba tsei bibii ateŋ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni oshi he ko obɔle he. tso shishitoo ni fa bɔ ni sa Bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ akaju hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli nu lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ miinɛ bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Ensuring consistent watering and applying the right fertilizer during the flowering stage helps fruit set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛmli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does leaving weeds around young tree crops really reduce how fast they grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani tsei bibii baaye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛha amɛdalɛ aba shi oya?

english: Yes, weeds grow faster than young crops and quickly steal water, fertilizer, and light. Clearing weeds regularly around the base of young trees ensures all nutrients go directly into growing your main crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la oya. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ Tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii titri lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees curling up and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curled and brown leaves are often caused by pests like mirids (capsids) attacking the shoots, or direct sun scorch due to lack of shade trees. Extension officers can advise on the right protective shade trees and approved spraying schedules.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋaa yɛ tsei ni sa ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli kɛ be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: How does too much rain during the flowering stage affect my cowpea plants?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ saa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rainfall can knock the flowers off cowpea plants before they can form pods, and it creates high humidity that encourages fungal diseases. Good field drainage helps excess water leave the field quickly to protect the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ dani amɛfee ŋmeii. ni ekɛ hulutsoo ni fa ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ baa. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya koni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tall maize plants keep falling over whenever strong winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants have shallow root systems and heavy tops, making them easy for strong winds to push over. Planting rows of trees or bushy plants along the edges of your farm creates a windbreak that slows down heavy winds and protects your crops from falling.
ga: Abele tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli. Tsei loo jwɛi ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ onibii ahe koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Is it better for me to plant my vegetable farm right next to the dam or higher up on the dry land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ mibɔɔ lɛ yɛ faa ko masɛi loo nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ fe nakai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Planting too close to a dam can cause root rot if the land gets flooded, while planting too high up makes it hard for crops to get water. The best spot is slightly elevated ground near the water source, where the soil drains easily but water is still close enough to fetch.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo kɛji nu shwie jɛmɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha tso lɛ akɛ ebaaná nu. He ni hi fe fɛɛ ji he ko ni nɔ kwɔ fioo ni bɛŋkɛ nu ko. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli oya shi ebɛŋkɛ lolo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ejie nu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa trees from sunlight and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Why does my cassava crop lose all of its leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and prevent themselves from drying out completely. The plant is not dying; it is conserving energy so that the cassava tubers underground can continue to survive.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkagbi kwraa. Tso lɛ gbooo, ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, prevents the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil. It also stops weeds from growing and keeps the soil cool so the tomato plants can take in water smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ bɔni afee ni tomato tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I put three or four seeds into the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo ŋmãa bu kome mli?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This struggle leaves all the stalks thin and weak, resulting in smaller and fewer corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ nɔmɔ nɛɛ haa abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can trap direct sunlight to nourish the tubers below. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an important food for crop growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Giving the soil regular moisture and protecting plants from midday heat helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni ejaaa mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas in my field after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground, leaving the soil tired. Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally restores fertility for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, etɔ sũ lɛ. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rainfall because the soil underneath is still dry and hot. Wait until you get two or three steady downpours so the soil holds enough deep moisture to keep your seeds growing safely.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ be fɛɛ be koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni odumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch full sunlight, which helps the plant direct energy into growing bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore its green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to protect themselves from heat. By curling up, the leaf reduces its surface area exposed to the sun to slow down water loss until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Curling haa baai lɛ baa amɛhe nɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become woody and hard to eat if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso ni ewaa akɛ ayeɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store soft starch when young, but as the plant gets older, it converts that starch into tough wooden fibers to support its stem, making the roots hard and unpalatable.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo mli kɛ́ amɛji gbekɛbii. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ eda Ehaa nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa ni ekɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ŋɔɔɔɔ

english: Why is it better to build mounds or ridges before planting sweet potatoes instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaama gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani adu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen up the soil so the tuber roots can expand easily without resistance, while also protecting the crop from waterlogging during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tuber lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nu afua he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather becomes extremely hot or when water supply is irregular, causing stress that prevents pollination and forces the plant to shed flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ pollination naa baa, ni enyɛɔ tomato tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings in the nursery growing very tall, thin, and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow long and thin when they do not get enough light, causing them to stretch towards the sun. Placing your nursery bed where it gets morning sunlight makes seedlings grow thick and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji amɛnaaa la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ekpãa kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo hei ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ leebi lɛ, ebaawo dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more when I allow weeds to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds create shady, safe hiding spots for harmful insects to breed, allowing them to easily move onto your crops and damage them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha koolooi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛfɔ. Enɛ haa amɛyaa onibii anɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Can I grow rice on the same dry farmland where I usually plant my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mifɔɔ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Traditional rice varieties thrive best in swampy or lowland areas (lowlands/valleys) with lots of water, while maize prefers well-drained dry soil. However, if you want to farm rice on dry land, you must choose special 'upland rice' varieties that can survive on rainfall alone.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa shikpɔji loo shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. (kplanaa/jɔɔ) ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Abele sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji oosumɔ ni odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ohala ‘ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa’ henɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni baanyɛ akpɛlɛ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and break up the soil before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mafo mli dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil allows young seed roots to easily push deep into the earth to find water and nutrients. It also buries weeds and helps rain soak into the ground instead of washing your seeds away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting maize seeds about 25 to 30 centimeters apart in rows gives each plant enough room to spread its roots, soak up sunlight, and feed on soil nutrients without fighting with neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa, ekɛ hulu la lɛ baatsu nii, ni eyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu.

english: At what stage of growth does my maize crop need the most water and attention?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli mi ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa nu kɛ hiɛdɔɔ fe fɛɛ?

english: Maize needs the most water and care when it starts flowering and producing cobs (the tasseling stage). If the plants suffer from drought or poor nutrients during this critical point, the cobs will end up small or empty.
ga: Nu kɛ kwɛmɔ he hiaa ŋmãa fe fɛɛ beni ebɔi fɔfɔii kɛ kpojiemɔ (toi fã). Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ ye hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa yɛ nɛkɛ be ni mli wa nɛɛ mli lɛ, nu kɛ kwɛmɔ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni eshɛɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Kob lɛ baafee bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that gives plants their healthy green color. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Apply the first round of NPK fertilizer about 1 to 2 weeks after the seeds sprout so the young roots get strong. A second application of nitrogen fertilizer should be done when the plants reach knee height.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ Esa akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaneshi lɛ.

english: How many times do I need to clear weeds from my farm after planting rice?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni midu ŋmãa sɛɛ?

english: You should clear weeds at least twice: first within 2 to 3 weeks after planting, and again around 5 to 6 weeks. Early weeding stops wild grass from stealing the sunlight and fertilizer meant for your rice.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii shii enyɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be yɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Ni ekoŋŋ aaafee otsii 5 kɛyashi 6 mra ni ajieɔ jwɛi. Enɛ baaye abua ni koo mli jwɛi akaju hulu la ni ekɛwo o-rice lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is getting too much or too little rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ babaoo loo miinɛ fioo tsɔ?

english: If maize gets too little rain, its leaves will roll up tight like pencils during the day to save moisture. If it gets too much water and the land becomes waterlogged, the roots rot and the plant turns yellow and stops growing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji nu fa babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: How do I know when my rice is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn a golden yellow color and the stalks begin to bend downward under the weight of the grain.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 feɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jeɔ shishi ekotoɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ashishi

english: It is best to buy fresh certified seeds each season, especially if you planted hybrid maize. Seeds saved from your own harvest will produce weaker plants and give you a much smaller yield the following year.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ oduɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baawo tso ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii babaoo kwraa yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitswa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them from the heat until their root system is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Removing extra suckers ensures that soil nutrients go directly to the main stem, which results in larger and heavier plantain bunches when harvest time comes.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and air. This reduces the dampness that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to lift my yam vines onto tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the ground and up into the sunlight so they can make food for the plant, which helps grow larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if the caterpillars eating my maize leaves are Fall Armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji ŋmeii?

english: Fall Armyworms leave large ragged holes in the maize leaves and yellowish waste inside the center stalk. If you look closely at the worm's head, you will see an inverted Y-shaped mark.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ shĩɔ bu agboi yɛ ŋmãa baa mli kɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ okwɛ ŋmei lɛ yitso jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Obaana okadi ko ni tamɔ Y ni etsɔ hiɛ efo shi.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The best way to control it is by planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ ji ni adu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips. Regular watering and using neem oil sprays can help protect the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ kɛjɛ latsaa he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become consistent. The very first rain often dries up quickly, which can scorch your seeds in the hot soil before they take root.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shãa yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apply the first dose of fertilizer about two weeks after planting when seedlings emerge, and the second dose when the maize reaches knee height, ensuring the soil is wet when applying.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ afata he beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ.

english: Is it better to scrape all weeds away or leave some on the ground during dry periods?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaajie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ loo abaashi ekomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli?

english: Leaving clear-cut weeds on top of the soil as mulch protects the ground from direct sun, keeping the soil cool and preserving moisture for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, or heavy rains are washing the nutrients deeper down where the roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miifɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛya shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ?

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year produce smaller harvests each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows soil pests to build up, leaving the land tired and unable to feed new crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ.

english: Why are my yam vines growing so bushy with lots of green leaves, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to swell the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei ahe tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun but stand up straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ ni ja ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: Drooping is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture by reducing leaf exposure to intense heat during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛtsɔ baai ni baa shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ bei amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Extreme afternoon heat or insufficient soil water stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to preserve energy and survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds in my field grow so much faster and stronger than my crops during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems designed to steal water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni afee koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close together so I can get more food from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi bɔni afee ni maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and tiny tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulb bibii baa.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my cereal crops help make my soil better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ kɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Cowpeas gather nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer for nearby plants.
ga: Cowpeas buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why does one sick plant with spots on its leaves quickly infect all the healthy plants around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ ni ebaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ anɔ lɛ? oya oyai

english: Leaf spots are usually caused by fungi or bacteria that spread quickly through splashing rainwater, wind, or hands moving between plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei loo helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo niji ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ he tsɔi baa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings suddenly rot and fall over right at the soil level after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a soil-borne fungal disease that thrives in overly wet conditions, attacking tender young stems near the surface.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Etutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that protect the trees and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa wala hiɔ shi ni buɔ tso lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant stay green and form healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the ground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil loses air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil or appropriate organic pesticides helps control these pests and restores leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the tomato plant draw up calcium evenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium daa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the fruits start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches, making them top-heavy. Propping up the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden forks prevents wind damage and supports the weight of the growing fruit.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛyɛ jwɛi ni mli tse, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ yibii ni miida lɛ muji lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds early around my young yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni bɔle mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mra? No hewɔ lɛ ehe hiaa mi.

english: Young yam sprouts grow slowly at first and cannot compete with aggressive weeds for water, light, and nutrients. Weeding early gives the yam vines room to grow strong and build larger tubers below the ground.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ ashi akaŋ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the crop is harvested, the trapped nitrogen remains in the soil, natural fertilizing the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔ lɛ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my cowpea plants dropping off instead of forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when the plant suffers from severe heat stress, dry spells, or damage from insects like flower thrips. Protecting the crop from thrips and ensuring adequate moisture helps flowers turn into grain pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hulutsoo be, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips lɛ fitemɔ. Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ thrips he kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why does my soil turn dry and hard like brick so quickly after I finish watering my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni ewaa tamɔ brikii beni migbe mitsei lɛ anɔ nu lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly due to direct sun heat and evaporation. Spreading dry grass or crop leaves around the base of your plants, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground and keeps the soil soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni agbɛɔ ashwaa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure will help feed the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mikɛ mihe ewo mi-abele tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ amli

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that eats maize leaves and damages the growing shoot. You can protect your crop by spraying early in the morning when the caterpillars are active or by applying recommended natural treatments like neem oil.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii ji enɛɛmɛi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni efiteɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni oooshwie nɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii tamɔ neem fɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural extension services.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni oootsɔ Agricultural Extension Agency lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin instead of swelling into big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ ni amɛfuu ni amɛdara lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is packed too tightly or if the plants are packed too close together. Digging the soil well to loosen it and leaving enough space between plants allows the roots to expand freely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni egbɔjɔ ni oshi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning dark black and rotting on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in very wet and overly shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight and air into the farm, and removing rotten pods quickly, will help prevent it from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ oya. Ebaaye ebua ni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden sticks to climb on?
