ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that travels down to feed the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyaha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he, ni eha ehe akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why must I clear weeds around my yam mounds if the yam grows safely underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ he kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water that your yam plant needs to grow big. Even though the tuber is underground, the leafy vine above needs all the food it can get from the soil to nourish the tuber.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu ni he hiaa o-sweet potato tsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Eyɛ mli akɛ yitso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ Shi wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ he miihia niyenii fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha amɛ bulbs lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the fruits are not fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai lɛ edako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can easily rot or be damaged by tiny microscopic soil pests called nematodes. Putting mulch around the base and using strong wooden or bamboo poles to prop up the stems keeps them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ agbo oya loo sũ mli kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he ni akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Watering your tomato plants regularly at the base and placing dry grass around the roots keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Okɛ nu awo tomato tsei lɛ amli daa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni okɛ jwɛi awo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my yams turn out small or bent even when I plant healthy seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ji bibii loo ebɔle ehe eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Yams need soft, deep soil mounds or ridges to grow smoothly. Hard or stony soil stops the tuber from expanding freely, which leads to small or crooked yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔji ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ŋmeii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ehe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines on stakes helps leaves get light and keeps them off the wet ground where diseases live.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ náa la, ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, he ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ.

english: Can I grow yams on the exact same spot every year without adding fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli?

english: Yams take a lot of food out of the soil as they grow. Planting them in the same place every year dries out the land's nutrients, causing smaller harvests each season.
ga: Atomɔ baaye niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning yellow and dry before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early yellowing usually means the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen, or it is being attacked by pests or fungal diseases like anthracnose. Leaves should stay green until the tuber finishes maturing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmɔŋ mra lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ anthracnose miitutua lɛ. Esa akɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli kɛyashi bulb lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How does a long dry spell affect my yams while they are developing underground?
ga: Te be kakadaŋŋ ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ saa mi-sweet potatoes lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If yams don't get enough water while expanding, the tubers stop growing and can become hard or woody, leading to a much smaller total harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Tubers lɛ baakpa dalɛ ni ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni wa loo tso. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing shoots before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ dani mifee klalo akɛ madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy when kept in warm, humid conditions. Warm air tricks the tuber into thinking rainy season has arrived, making it sprout early.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛji akɛ amɛto amɛhe dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ lakaa yitso lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ eba, ni no haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time my yams are ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ?

english: Yams are ready when the vines and leaves naturally dry up and turn brown at the end of the season, showing that the plant has finished storing food in the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it bad to use bruised or damaged yam tubers as seeds for my next farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ loo efite lɛ baatsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Damaged seed yams carry rot-causing germs right into your soil. Using sick seeds lowers the chances of sprouting and can spread diseases to healthy plants.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni efite lɛ kɛ helai ni haa sũ baa lɛ baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni hela mɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa hegbɛ ni amɛyɔɔ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting in storage before I sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ nitoohe lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they get hot, wet, or bruised. Keeping them in a cool, shaded, well-ventilated yam barn elevated off the ground prevents moisture buildup and spoilage.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji edɔ, edɔ, loo edɔ. Ha amɛ awo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ owó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa ni efite.

english: Why do yams spoil quickly after being packed tightly into trucks for long market journeys?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya beni akɛwo lɔlei amli shiŋŋ kɛha gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ kɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tight packing causes internal bruising and heat buildup during transport. Even small scratches or pressure damage create entry points for rot fungi, causing the yams to decay before reaching buyers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa mligbɛ fãji kɛ dɔlɛ baa be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ. Nibii bibii ni akpɛ́ Loo nɔ ni nɔnyɛɛ efite lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baagboi dani amɛyashɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or improving drainage in your field helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are salts that need moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink them in. If applied to dry soil, the concentrated fertilizer will burn and damage the roots, causing the crop to wilt and dry up.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni biɔ ni nu atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if heavy rains stay on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the ground for days, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to drown and rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away fast.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. beni nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Yam vines use their leaves like solar panels to catch sunlight and make food, which then grows the heavy tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the wet ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct heat and bright sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to act as umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni etsu nii akɛ umbrella Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow at the edges and droop even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by leaf diseases like Black Sigatoka or root damage from soil pests. Pruning off the affected yellow leaves and using clean planting suckers stops the disease from spreading through your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmeii ni he tse tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when they do not get enough water, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and planting in the right season keeps flowers attached.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stay small instead of spreading wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã babaoo lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves. Controlling these small insects early prevents them from curling the leaves and stunt-growing the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkabɔle baai lɛ ahe ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to grow when I bury them deep inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds have only a small amount of stored energy to sprout and reach the surface. If buried too deep, the young sprout tires out and dies before reaching sunlight, so seeds should only be buried at a depth twice their size.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato koni amɛdara ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani hulu la lɛ baashɛ amɛnɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afu dumɔwui kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ fe amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ pɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny green droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing funnel of the plant to eat fresh leaves, and applying recommended treatments into the center of the plant gets rid of them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei. kɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni akɛjie amɛ.

english: What happens if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long before plucking them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mifolɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree signals to the plant that it does not need to produce new fruit yet, which stops new flowers from forming and reduces your next harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ewo yibii heei lolo. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi heei aba ni ehaa okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does plucking my crops regularly help the tree make more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Regular harvesting frees up the tree's energy and sends a signal to start producing new flowers and pods, keeping yield high throughout the season.
ga: Kɛ́ akpaa tso lɛ daa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ jeɔ kpo ni etsɔɔ lɛ akɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei feemɔ. Koni afee ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Pods are ready when their color changes fully from green or red to a bright yellow or orange; harvesting right at this stage prevents energy waste and protects the beans.
ga: Pod lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ehiɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa, ni ebuɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ ahe.

english: Will plucking my cocoa pods as soon as they are ripe make the next harvest come faster?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii ni aaakpa beni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ lɛ baaha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ oya?

english: Yes, harvesting as soon as pods mature encourages the tree to immediately put its energy into developing the next flush of flowers and young pods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmaa ni akpaa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ eda kwraa lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods feel light and empty inside when I open them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ agbele kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi amli lɛ, enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Light or flat pods usually happen when the tree lacks nutrients, lacks water during pod development, or when flowers were not properly pollinated by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni etse ehe lɛ baa kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nu ni bɛ yɛ be mli ni pod lɛ yaa hiɛ loo be mli ni kooloi esaaa kɛha fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing flowers after a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ wulu ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Trees spend a lot of energy ripening fruit; if old fruit remains on the tree, the plant holds back new flower growth until those mature fruits are removed.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ. Kɛji aduawai momo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ Tso lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi heei adalɛ naa kɛyashi abaajie nakai aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are my crop yields getting smaller even though my trees look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Trees can look healthy while focusing energy on leaves instead of fruit, especially if old pods are left on the branches or if soil nutrients are out of balance.
ga: Tso ko baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ ejwɛŋmɔ ni akɛaama baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii momoi lɛ eshwɛ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa

english: Does leaving overripe fruit on the tree cause diseases to spread on my farm?
ga: Ani aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni ashiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, overripe fruit attracts pests and holds moisture that leads to diseases like black pod rot, which quickly spreads to young green pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni no kɛ helai tamɔ black pod rot, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do some flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Trees drop excess flowers if they are overloaded with old fruit, stressed by dry weather, or if there were not enough midges to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji eyɛ aduawai ni edara babaoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa mɔ haoɔ Aloo kɛji jwɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: How does a cocoa tree know when to start growing new pods?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cacao tso leɔ be ni esa akɛ ebɔi ŋmeii heei akwɛmɔ?

english: The tree reacts to internal chemical signals; when mature pods are plucked, the reduction in load tells the tree that energy is free to grow new pods.
ga: Tsei hereɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ajie ŋmeii ni eda lɛ Jatsu ni eba shi lɛ kɛɛ tso lɛ akɛ hewalɛ yɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii heei baa.

english: Why do some farmers leave big trees on their farms instead of cutting them all down before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ tsei wuji yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafolɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛdu lɛ?

english: Trees provide gentle shade that protects tender crops from the burning sun, keep the ground cool, and drop leaves that rot into free, natural food for your crops.
ga: Tsei lɛ haa hulutsoo be blɛoo koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it better to build shade structures out of dry palm leaves or to plant living shade trees on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ matsɔ ŋmei tsei ni egbi nɔ ama hulutsoo he ko loo madu hulutsoo tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Living shade trees are better because they grow along with your farm, last for many years without needing rebuilding, and feed the soil with their fallen leaves.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ hi fe no ejaakɛ amɛkɛ oŋmɔ lɛ daa. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ama ekoŋŋ. ni okɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Can planting my crops near large forest trees help protect them when heavy winds blow?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koo agbo mli lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu tsei ahe kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa?

english: Yes, large trees act as natural windbreaks that slow down fierce winds, preventing your crops from snapping or being uprooted during heavy storms.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi. Tsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ loo amɛkashi yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli.

english: How do I choose the best seeds from my harvest to save and bury in the ground for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli koni mikɛto ni mafu yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Pick seeds from your healthiest, strongest plants that gave the best fruits. Make sure the seeds are fully dry, undamaged, and free from insect holes before saving them.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni wa fe fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi kwraa, efiteee ni kooloi ahiɛ bɛ mli dani okɛto.

english: How deep into the soil should I bury my seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu midumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: A good rule of thumb is to plant a seed at a depth about two to three times its size so it stays moist but can still easily push through to the surface.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛdalɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ mli lolo.

english: Why do some of my seeds rot in the dirt instead of sprouting into healthy plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ ni amɛbatsɔ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually rot if the soil is too wet, if they are buried too deep where there is no air, or if the seed was already weak or damaged before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ fitemɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛfite dani adu

english: Why are seeds harvested from strong local trees often better than some of the inputs I buy at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni wa amli lɛ hi fe nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Local trees have naturally adapted to your area's weather, soil, and pests over a long time, so seeds taken from the best local trees are already well-suited to thrive on your farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei lɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can rotting leaves from forest trees help my crops grow without relying only on bought chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai ni egboi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tɛŋŋ?

english: Fallen leaves decompose into organic manure that enriches the soil, improves its structure, and feeds crops naturally over time without costing you money.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni okɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni okɛ shika babaoo efiteee.

english: Why does the ground stay damp under big trees even when it hasn't rained in a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo yɛ tso agbo lɛ shishi lɛ? Be kakadaŋŋ nɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Tree leaves block direct sunlight from evaporating moisture from the earth, and the layer of fallen leaves acts like a blanket trapping water in the soil.
ga: Tso baai tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni emɔɔ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Will big tree roots steal all the water and nutrients away from my small crops?
ga: Tsei wuji ashishifãi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Deep-rooted forest trees actually pull water and food from deep underground up to the topsoil, which can benefit smaller crops growing near them if the trees are managed well.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ kooi amli ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. The leaf damage prevents the plant from making enough food, which stops your cassava tubers from growing large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ Baai ni fiteɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baatsi cassava shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms have invaded my maize farm before my crops are destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall armyworm ebatutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite?

english: Check the central funnel (whorl) of young maize plants for ragged holes in the leaves and yellowish droppings that look like saw-dust. Catching armyworms early while they are small makes controlling them much easier.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli kɛji bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ niyenii mli ŋmeii mra, beni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, ebaaha amɛ nɔyeli afee mlɛo kwraa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of developing thick stems and large cobs, they waste all their energy stretching upward to reach light.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi agbohi. Mohu ɔ, a puɛɔ a he wami tsuo kɛ yaa hiɔwe konɛ a ya su la a he.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during extremely hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High heat causes severe stress to tomato plants and destroys the pollen inside the blossoms. Without successful pollination, the flower dies and falls off instead of developing into a tomato.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the large forest trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie koo mli tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because it burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil fast. Leaving taller shade trees creates a cooler microclimate that helps young cocoa survive until it matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a temporary rain followed by days of intense heat. If you plant early, the hot, dry soil can bake or rot your yam tubers underground before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko ni gbi ni mli edɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra Hot, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha sweet potato tubers lɛ ashã loo egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why does my soil produce huge yields in the first year after clearing, but smaller yields in the years after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli beni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ani ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Freshly cleared forest soil contains years of built-up leaf mold and plant food. Every harvest takes those nutrients out of the soil, so without adding fertilizer, compost, or resting the land, the soil becomes depleted.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ mli baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni ebua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ yɔɔ mli. Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite.

english: How does leaving dried weeds on top of my field help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the ground forms a protective layer called mulch. This blanket keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, prevents weed growth, and decays into free organic fertilizer over time.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my harvested hybrid maize yield much less when I plant them the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred from distinct parent plants to produce one single generation of high yields. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in uneven, low-yielding plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni woɔ yibii ni baa shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be pulled from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Sample a few plants across your farm by pulling them up and opening the pods. Groundnuts are ready when the inside lining of the shell turns dark with veins and the kernels completely fill the pod space.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ amli etsɔ duŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and dry up while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green. When soil nutrients are low, the plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and moves it to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ, ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa koni ekɛ ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very big green leaves but produce almost no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eshwɛ fioo ni fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: This happens when plants receive too much nitrogen from manure or fertilizer without enough phosphorus and potassium. Excess nitrogen tricks the plant into spending all its energy building leaves and stems instead of flowering.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii amli moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi.

english: Young cocoa plants act like human babies and burn easily under full sun. High sunlight dries out their small leaves faster than their roots can draw up water, so planting temporary shade crops like plantains keeps them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ adesai abifabii ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee bibii. Egbiɔ oya tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and watery if I leave them in the ground past one year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ fe afi lɛ?

english: Cassava stores energy as soft starch in its roots, but as the plant gets older or goes through dry seasons, it converts that stored starch back into tough wood to keep itself alive, leaving less edible starch for harvest.
ga: Cassava toɔ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo mli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ eda loo amɛtsɔ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ ŋmei ni ato lɛ mli ekoŋŋ efeɔ tso ni wa koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni ayeɔ lɛ faaa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines completely die back and turn brown before the tubers are dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egboi kwraa ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ dani atsaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam leaves turn brown and die at the end of the rainy season because the plant is transferring all its remaining energy down into the underground tuber, signaling that the yam has stopped growing and is ready to harvest.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sweet potato tso lɛ miitsɔ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛmiiya ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekpa shweremɔ ni eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, tight cups and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔpoi bibii amli ni atsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of young leaves. As the insects suck out the leaf sap, the damaged tissue twists and curls upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. be mli ni kooloi bibii nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ Faji ni efite lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off the stalks before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tsei lɛ anɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop mainly when tiny insect pests called thrips attack the blossom buds, or when the soil gets too dry. When stressed or damaged, the plant intentionally sheds its flowers to preserve moisture.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ thrips lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔii ashishifãi. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Be mli ni haomɔ loo nɔ ni efite lɛ ba Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold down and roll inward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up on hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to shade themselves. Rolling reduces the leaf area exposed to direct sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ atsɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the farm right before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when heavy rains come suddenly after a long dry spell. The roots absorb water so fast that the inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer rind can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu oya aahu akɛ tso yibii lɛ loo lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli. ha efo

english: Why do some of my garden egg flowers dry up and drop off without developing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers need bees or wind to move pollen inside the flower so fruit can grow. If there are no pollinators around or if heat stress ruins the pollen, the unfertilized flower drops off naturally.
ga: Egg fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ koni ekɛ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ aya koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ kooloi ni feɔ pollen lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he loo kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my harvested rice look dark and burnt, and how can I keep it clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni eshã lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ehe atse?

english: Rice grains turn dark or burnt-looking when they are harvested too late or left to dry directly on very hot bare soil. To keep your rice bright and good, harvest when most of the field turns golden yellow and dry the grains on a raised tarpaulin or clean mat.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa lɛ feɔ ediŋ loo etamɔ nɔ ni eshã kɛji akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ loo ashi lɛ koni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Bɔni afee ni o-rice lɛ afee nɔ ni kpɛɔ ni ehi Kpamɔ be mli ni kpokpaa lɛ fa ko etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni ogbi ŋmaa lɛ yɛ tarpaulin loo mat ni he tse nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is their main food for growth. Adding a small amount of fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure around the plants will quickly bring back their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko he miihia o-abele tsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi afata he lɛ he. Tsei lɛ baaná amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ekoŋŋ oya.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: Small ragged holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the growing center of the plant. Checking your crops early in the morning and applying recommended organic sprays or pesticides into the plant centers will protect them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi yɛ tsei ahe nitsumɔhei lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and turn soft in the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits around them for too long in heavy or flat soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ebɔle amɛhe. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants keep falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. Covering the soil around your tomatoes with dry grass (mulching) and watering them regularly helps keep the plants cool so fruits can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Mulching around Kɛ akɛ jwɛi ha tomato nɔ (mulching) ni afɔ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small cups during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in the heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. If the leaves open back up in the cool evening, the plant is doing fine, but if they stay curled all day, it could mean tiny insects like aphids are sucking the plant's juice.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ gbele yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ efo gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids miinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops in straight lines rather than scattering the seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop enough room to get light, air, and soil food. It also makes it much easier for you to weed, add fertilizer, and walk through your farm without trampling your crops.
ga: Nibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid maize crop to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially prepared to yield well only for their first planting. If you save and plant seeds harvested from those crops, the second generation will grow unevenly and produce very small, weak cobs.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ. Kɛji obua dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ anaa ni okwɛ nɔ. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and very fast at stealing water, sunlight, and soil food from your crops. Clearing weeds early when they are still small prevents them from taking food away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa oya waa ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Kɛ amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkajie niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs extra food before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii kroko dani madu?

english: If your crops from the previous season grew very short, had thin stems, or gave weak yields despite good rain, your soil is likely tired. Adding compost, livestock manure, or the right fertilizer before planting restores energy to the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ shwere kuku waa, eyɛ tsei bibii, loo ewo yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ baafite. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its healthy green color and grow stronger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. Planting them alongside corn feeds the soil naturally, helping the corn grow better while giving you two crops from the same land.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ he kome lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same spot repeatedly allows pests and soil diseases that target tomatoes to build up in the soil. Rotating your crops with non-related plants like corn or beans starves those pests and keeps your soil healthy.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ji tomato lɛ otii lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni okɛtsakeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ ni eye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave so much space between my cassava cuttings when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmei niji ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava plants need enough room underground for their roots to expand into large tubers, and above ground to catch sunlight. Planting them too close makes them fight for water and soil food, resulting in thin, small roots.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Young crops have weak root systems and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a strong start before the weeds choke them out.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi aha amɛhe.

english: Why should I remove the extra side branches growing from the stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra side branches, often called suckers, steal energy and water from the main stem. Removing them directs the plant's energy away from growing excess leaves and toward producing bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni fata he, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the afternoon heat even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: On very hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. They droop to protect themselves from scorching heat and usually perk back up when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛfo amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ni amɛfɔɔ amɛyitsei anɔ womɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, sudden dry spells, or too much water. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and providing partial shade during extreme sun can prevent blossoms from falling.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Gbimɔ trukaa loo nu babaoo yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young corn leaves with powdery sawdust inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ powder yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in leaves along with powdery waste inside the leaf funnel are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the plant. Inspecting the center of young plants early allows you to treat the infestation before the worms destroy the crop's growing point.
ga: Buu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ fiteɔ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize seeds get full of tiny holes and insects before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ kooloi bibii dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ

english: Stored seeds get damaged by seed-boring insects if the grain is not completely dried before storage or if it is kept in loose bags. Drying seeds thoroughly under the sun and storing them in airtight containers keeps insect pests out.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto kotoku ni mli tse mli Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How do I know when my cassava crops are ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. A common sign is when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. You can also carefully dig around the base of one plant to check if the tubers underneath have grown to a mature size before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ ji be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atswa tso lɛ yitso kome koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ edara kɛyashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How many cassava plants do I need to dig up to feed my family for a meal?
ga: Cassava tsei enyiɛ ehe baahia ni otsa koni okɛha oweku lɛ niyenii?

english: A single healthy cassava plant usually yields between 3 to 6 large tubers. Depending on the size, just one or two well-developed cassava plants can yield enough tubers to prepare a meal of fufu or boiled cassava for a family of three to four people.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni falɛ ji 3 kɛyashi 6. Kasava tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaafee fūfu loo cassava ni ahoo niyenii aha weku ko ni mɛi etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ damɔ bɔ ni edara ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I leave my cassava tubers in the ground after they mature, or will they spoil?
ga: Kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ani obaanyɛ oshi ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Aloo ebaagbo?

english: Cassava can safely remain stored underground in the soil for several months after reaching maturity without spoiling. However, if you leave them in the ground for too long—usually beyond 18 months—the tubers will become tough, fibrous, and woody, making them unsuitable for making smooth fufu.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo beni edara sɛɛ ni efiteee. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite. (bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fe nyɔji 18) Tubers lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tso, ni no haa esaaa akɛ afeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the cassava tubers under my plant very small even though the leaves on top look big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Mɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni eyɛ baai?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or if you use too much leaves-focused fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of growing tubers underground. Good drainage and balanced soil nutrients like potassium are required for the roots to expand into big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ahe tsei babaoo haoɔ lɛ tsu nii. Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja, tamɔ potassium he miihia koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What kind of soil helps cassava form big tubers easily under the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo?

english: Cassava forms the largest tubers in loose, well-drained, sandy-loam soils. Heavy clay soils are too tight and hard, which restricts the tubers from expanding freely underground and can hold water that causes the roots to rot.
ga: Cassava ji tso ni da fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni ewa. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ mli

english: Does cassava need a lot of water to survive during the dry season?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia ŋmei koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is very drought-resistant once its root system is established. During long dry spells, the plant drops its leaves to conserve water and survives on moisture deep in the ground, making it one of the most reliable crops for hot climates.
ga: Cassava nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa waa kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ ebɔi shi pɛ. Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tsei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ fe fɛɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ ateŋ ekome.

english: How do I select the best cassava stem cuttings to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select stem cuttings from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from pests or diseases. Use the middle, woodier part of the main stem, cutting pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long with at least 4 to 6 visible growth buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai bɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ tso ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Afolɔ mli aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: How deep into the soil should I plant my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei ni afo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Plant cassava cuttings about 5 to 10 centimeters deep in raised soil mounds or ridges. Planting them at a 45-degree slant with the growth buds pointing upward helps the plant root firmly while making the underground tubers easier to harvest later.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 5 kɛyashi 10 yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ 45-degree angle mli ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ damɔɔ shi shiŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava turn out hard and difficult to pound into smooth fufu after boiling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ wa ni ewa akɛ aaatswa lɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni ashã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava becomes hard or gummy when pounded if the tubers were harvested too late after becoming old and woody, or if the plant suffered severe dry weather while maturing. Some cassava varieties are also naturally higher in fiber and better suited for making gari rather than soft fufu.
ga: Kassava baafee nɔ ni wa loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa cassava shishifã lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ beni egbɔ ni efee tso lɛ sɛɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ naa shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa beni edara lɛ. Cassava henɔi komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛmli fiber fa babaoo, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kari feemɔ fe fufu ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why does harvested cassava spoil so quickly within two days of digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ?

english: Once cassava is dug out of the soil and separated from its roots, air enters the damaged ends and starts a fast natural process called post-harvest rot. To prevent this, process your harvested cassava into products like gari or flour within 48 hours, or submerge unpeeled tubers in clean water to keep them fresh for a few extra days.
ga: Kɛ́ ootsa ŋmei lɛ, jiemɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni otse kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa ni efite lɛ mli ni ejeɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni yaa oya ni atsɛɔ lɛ post-harvest rot lɛ shishi. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ Gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ naa lɛ, akpaa ŋmãa ni akɛfeɔ nibii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli, loo akɛ ŋmãa ni ajieee lɛ woɔ nu ni mli tse mli koni ehi shi gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why should I try planting new improved cowpea seeds instead of using the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka cowpea dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ akwɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ i he kɛ je nyagbe kpami be ɔ mi ɔ tsu ní.

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, grow faster, and yield more food even during short rainy seasons. Saved seeds lose their vigor over time, leading to smaller harvests and higher risk of disease.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. shwereɔ oya ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli po Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo, ni helai hu baa.

english: How can I tell the difference between traditional climbing beans and the new bush bean varieties?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ blema ŋmeii ni akwɔɔ kɛ tsina ŋmeii heei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Traditional climbing beans need tall sticks to grow upward and take longer to mature, while new bush varieties stay short, do not need support, flower early, and produce pods all at the same time.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmeii ni akwɔɔ lɛ biɔ niji ni kwɔlɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa. yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi heei lɛ yɛ kukuji. Ehe ehiaaa ni aye abua lɛ, ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli.

english: How do I know when my cowpeas are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cowpeas lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cowpeas are ready to harvest when the green pods dry out, harden, and turn light brown or yellow. If you pick them while still green and soft, the seeds will shrivel and rot during storage.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ egbi, ewa, ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji ogbala amɛ be mli ni amɛji eŋɔli lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my bean plants producing plenty of green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excessive water, the bean plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of flowering. Reducing water slightly when the plant matures encourages it to bloom.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo nu babaoo Bean tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ ba shi fioo beni tso lɛ miida lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains knock off fragile blossoms and wash away pollen before the flowers can turn into pods. It is a natural reaction where the plant drops stressed flowers to preserve its overall strength.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ dani fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ ŋmeii. Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni haoɔ amɛ koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: People in my village say cowpeas make the soil good for maize; is this true?
ga: Mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa. Ani enɛ ji anɔkwale?

english: Yes, cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through small nodules on their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer behind for the next crop of maize.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas and maize together on the same land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping cowpeas with maize works well because cowpeas cover the ground to prevent weeds and hold soil moisture, while tall maize grows upward without shading the cowpeas too much if properly spaced.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahi shi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ haŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my neighbor get a much bigger bean harvest than I do, even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Yield differences usually come from using certified seeds, proper spacing between plants, and clearing weeds early. If plants are too crowded or choked by weeds, they compete for sunlight and food, resulting in fewer pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Kɛji tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi tsɔ loo jwɛi ehà nɔ lɛ, Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pods fioo komɛi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cowpea plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is waterlogged from poor drainage, or the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen and sulfur due to poor root development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. aloo tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ sulfur yɛ shishifãi ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ

english: How do I stop small insects from eating holes in my harvested cowpeas while in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye bu ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive in moist, exposed grains. You can protect your cowpeas by sun-drying them completely until they are hard, then storing them in sealed, airtight containers or specialized PICS bags that suffocate pests.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmaa ni mli efɔ, ni agbele mli. Obaanyɛ obu tsina ŋmeii ahe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni oooha amɛgbi waa lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo PICS kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow so much bigger when I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli yaa hiɛ waa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for crops by giving the soil key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that get washed away over time, allowing plants to grow stronger and produce more.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni hoɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I harvest crops every year without putting anything back into it?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii daa afi ni mikɛ nɔ ko fataaa he ekoŋŋ?

english: Every harvest removes natural nutrients from the ground, so continuous farming without adding manure or fertilizer makes the soil weak and leads to smaller yields over time.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aya nɔ atsu okwaayeli he nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is the difference between animal manure and the commercial fertilizer bought in bags from the agro-shop?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kooloi aŋmei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ kotokui amli kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Animal manure improves soil moisture and health over a long time, while commercial fertilizer delivers a fast, concentrated boost of nutrients directly to the crops during critical growth periods.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli wa fataa tsei lɛ ahe oya yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Is it really possible for fertilizer to double or triple the number of bags of groundnuts I harvest?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli diɛŋtsɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ kotokui lɛ ayibɔ afee enyɔ loo etɛ?

english: Yes, when soil lacks food, crops produce tiny yields; giving plants proper nutrients allows every plant to reach its full potential, producing many more pods and heavier seeds.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, beni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ. Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni eshɛɔ ehewalɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Amɛwoɔ pods babaoo kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce plenty of flowers but very few actual nuts in the end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa naagbee lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they do not have enough nutrients or water to support nut development, so feeding the soil gives the tree the strength to turn flowers into fully formed nuts.
ga: Tso lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛtsake efɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni eda.

english: How can I tell if my nut crops are starving for nutrients just by looking at them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hɔmɔ miiye mi-pea tsei lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛkwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Nutrient-starved plants usually have pale or yellow leaves, thin stems, and slow growth, whereas well-fed plants have dark green, broad leaves and heavy flowering.
ga: Tsei ni niyenii faaa lɛ fɔɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni niyenii kpakpa yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, ni mli kwɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii.

english: How does feeding my crops properly help them survive periods of low rain or dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ bei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo loo hɔmɔ baa lɛ amli?

english: Well-nourished crops grow deeper, stronger root systems that can search for water far below the surface, making them tougher during dry periods.
ga: Tsei ni ayeɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa. ni baanyɛ atao nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ Enɛ haa amɛhe waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to apply fertilizer at specific plant ages instead of dumping it all at planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ wala be yeɔ lɛ naa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ fɛɛ oshwie yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Crops need different nutrients at different life stages, so applying fertilizer at key moments ensures the plant uses the food to form leaves, flowers, and fruits without wasting it.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ bei ni he hiaa amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why should I try new fertilizer treatments when my family has farmed the traditional way for generations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii hee aka? Kɛjɛ be mli ni miweku lɛ efee kusum okwaayeli kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Traditional methods worked well on fresh soil, but modern techniques and treatments help restore old, tired soils so you can get much higher yields from the same amount of land.
ga: Kusum gbɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai kɛ tsamɔi yeɔ ebuaa ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ momo ni efite lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Will putting extra fertilizer on my farm harm my crops if I put too much?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ babaoo fata he?

english: Yes, using too much fertilizer can burn the crop roots and damage the plants, so it is important to apply only the exact amount recommended by agricultural experts.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi woɔ he ŋaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants need nitrogen to build green leaves and grow strong, so adding composted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmã tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without producing fruit when the heat gets too high or when the plant lacks consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants adequate shade during extreme heat helps set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ba loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha tso lɛ hulutsoo bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the roots of my cowpea plants have small round balls attached to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔɔlu bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo ni akɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Those small balls are called root nodules, and they are very good for your soil. They store friendly bacteria that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it to your crop naturally.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ bɔɔlu bibii nɛɛ akɛ shishifãi. ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Amɛhiɛɔ naanyobɔɔ helai ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees lose water very fast during the hot, dry Harmattan winds. Planting shade trees nearby and covering the ground around the tree roots with dry grass mulch keeps moisture in the soil and protects the leaves.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo ni okɛ sũ ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading viral diseases that stunt your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do I see tiny holes eaten through my young maize leaves and stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ yeli

english: Tiny holes in young maize are typically made by stem borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths. Checking the plant leaves regularly and applying recommended controls early stops them from destroying the inner stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem borers ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ daa kɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɔne lɛ mligbɛ tsɔne lɛ akafite.

english: Why do I need to clear away extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra plantain suckers steal water and nutrients directly from the parent plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which allows the plant to produce much larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Plantain tsei krɛdɛɛi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ plantains ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to lift my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible, which feeds the growing yam underground. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also protects them from leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni ji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ baai helai ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess rain sits in the ground for too long without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the roots so they stay dry and healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Growing maize on the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally and breaks insect pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my maize farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, which allows them to absorb soil nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops like maize.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and stop growing when wild grass covers my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni koo mli jwɛi ehà miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Wild grasses form dense root mats underground that steal water and fertilizer from pepper roots, while their tall leaves block essential sunlight from reaching the crop.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii shishifãi amli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa lɛ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds manage to sprout all over my land even when I never planted any weed seeds?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ be mli ni miduko jwɛi dumɔwui ko pɛŋ?

english: Weed seeds are easily carried across farms by wind, rainwater, birds, and farm tools, remaining hidden in the soil until rain triggers them to sprout all at once.
ga: Abaanyɛ ajie jwɛi dumɔwui kɛbɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, okpoi kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ oya. Akɛ amɛ teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shikome.

english: Is pulling out weeds by hand better for my cassava crop than cutting them with a cutlass?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni akɛ niji gbalaa lɛ hi fe ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ?

english: Pulling weeds out by hand removes the entire root system so the weed cannot quickly regrow, whereas cutting the tops leaves roots intact to sprout again.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niji jieɔ jwɛi lɛ, ejieɔ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds pop up again almost immediately after I clear my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ baa ekoŋŋ aaafee beni mijie he ni adu nii yɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?
