english: Clearing the top soil exposes millions of dormant weed seeds buried underground to sunlight and fresh rainwater, which signals them to germinate immediately.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ baawo jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui akpekpei abɔ ni afu yɛ hulu kɛ nugbɔ hee shishi. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear all the weeds from my plot before planting seeds instead of waiting until the crops come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu nii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ,.

english: Clearing weeds before planting ensures your crop seeds germinate in clean soil without immediately competing against strong, already-established weed roots for nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi dani odu lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni he tse nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ jwɛi shishifãi ni wa ni ehi shi momo lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out much faster when there are many weeds growing around my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ be mli ni jwɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like extra mouths drinking from the soil; their roots draw up large amounts of groundwater and release it into the air through their leaves, drying out the soil.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii titri tamɔ nu ni amɛmuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛjieɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: How does covering my vegetable beds with dry plant leaves help stop weeds from growing?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi ha mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, jwɛi lɛ kwɛɛɛ?

english: A layer of dry leaf mulch acts as a blanket that blocks sunlight from reaching the soil, preventing hidden weed seeds from getting the light they need to sprout.
ga: Mulch ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do fewer weeds grow under my mature cassava plants than when the cassava plants were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwereɔ fioo yɛ mi yucca tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi fe beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: As cassava grows, its large leaves form a dense ceiling that shades the ground, starving weeds below of the sunlight they need to survive.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei miida Ebaai wuji lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ duŋ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ jwɛi yɛ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ shishi.

english: Why does delaying weeding by just two weeks cause my young cocoa seedlings to get weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ sɛɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ haa mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings grow slowly and have small roots; when weeds surround them early on, the weeds consume the topsoil water and fertilizer before the cocoa roots can reach them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛshishifãi bibii yɔɔ. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he mra lɛ Jwɛi yeɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli dani kookoo shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree is stressed. This can happen when the soil lacks key nutrients, during long dry spells, or when diseases like swollen shoot or pests attack the roots and branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli loo be mli ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu loo ŋmeii tutuaa shishifãi kɛ tsei aniji.

english: How can I tell if a damaged leaf on my farm is sick from a disease or just burnt by hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni efite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela emɔ amɛ loo hulutsoo be ko emɔ amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Weather damage usually causes dry, light brown edges across many plants at once, while a leaf disease creates dark, spreading spots, strange shapes, or powdery growths that spread from leaf to leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ agbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ shikome. yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ mli helai haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ, ni yɔɔ srɔto, loo ŋmeii ni tamɔ powda ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does a plant disease spread so quickly from one cocoa tree to the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Diseases travel fast because wind and rain splashes easily carry small fungal spores from sick leaves to healthy ones, and farm tools or insects can also carry the sickness between trees.
ga: Helai yaa oya ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii. Kɛjɛ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ lɛ mlɛo Ni okwaayeli nibii loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ hela kɛba tsei anɔ hu.

english: Should I cut off sick leaves from my crops or leave them to fall off on their own?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli loo maha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbee shi?

english: It is best to pick off sick leaves and burn or bury them away from your farm, because leaving them allows rain and wind to carry the sickness to healthy leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie helatsɛmɛi ahe baai ni oshã loo ofu amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ, nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ekɛ helai aba baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are some leaves on my cocoa tree perfectly healthy while leaves on another branch look dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ tsei aniji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi.

english: Pests or localized fungal attacks often start on a single branch that has more shade or moisture, before spreading to the rest of the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ tso nine kome ni hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. dani egbɛ eshwa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can heavy rain make the leaves on my crops get sick faster?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii amɔ hela oya?

english: Yes, heavy rain creates wet and cold conditions where fungi thrive, and rain droplets splash disease spores from the soil and old leaves up onto clean leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ sũ kɛ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai ni he tse nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot hours to reduce heat exposure and save water, but if they stay curled even in the evening, it could mean sap-sucking insects are hiding under them.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he. Shi kɛji amɛkoto gbɛkɛ po Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ ni amɛtee amɛshishi.

english: Can hot sunlight burn young cocoa leaves even if there is no disease on my farm?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo baai bibii kɛji akɛ hela lɛ bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli po?

english: Yes, young cocoa trees need shade trees like plantains above them because harsh direct sunlight burns tender leaves, turning them dry and brown.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ kooyigbɛ plantains. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Ha egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I know if my soil is giving my cocoa trees enough food to grow healthy leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiha mi-kookoo tso lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy leaves are large and dark green. Pale, yellow, small, or twisted leaves are strong signals that the soil lacks essential plant nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ dara ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Baai ni tsuɔ, ŋmɔŋ, bibii, loo ni etsilɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on both the leaves and pods of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ kookoo baai kɛ ŋmeii anɔ?

english: Black spots on cocoa leaves and pods are a main sign of Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that grows when the farm is too dark, crowded, or damp.
ga: Nibii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo baai kɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii diji hela lɛ he okadi titri. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa kɛji ŋmɔ ko mli ewo duŋ tsɔ, eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi loo hulutsoo be tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops always perform poorly when I plant them near the water's edge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Soil right at the edge of a water body stays soaked with water for too long. Excess water drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen, causing them to rot and preventing the crop from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ naa lɛ baakã he ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plants look like they are drying up even though the soil near the water is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mitso lɛ miigbi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ he lɛ mli edɔ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil is constantly waterlogged near water edges, the crop's roots rot and die. Once the roots are damaged by bad drainage, the plant can no longer take up water, causing it to wilt as if it is in a drought.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ naa be fɛɛ be lɛ. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagboi. Kɛji nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ tamɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli

english: Can using water from a different source harm my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ hei krokomɛi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, water from different ponds or rivers can vary in temperature, salt content, or cleanliness. Sudden changes in water quality can shock plant roots and slow down their growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui loo faai sɔrɔtoi amli. Srɔtofeemɔi baanyɛ aba yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli, loo bɔ ni ehe tse ha lɛ mli. Nu lɛ mli tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe afee shoo ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt as soon as I move them from the nursery into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ kɛji mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Moving plants to a new environment causes transplant shock. Seedlings go from a shaded, protected space to full sun and different soil temperatures, requiring a few days and extra shade to adjust.
ga: Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛyaa he hee lɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Dumɔwui tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni abuɔ he kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa sɔrɔtoi amli. Ebaahe gbii fioo komɛi kɛ hulutsoo kroko ni akɛfata he dani ekɛ ehe aaawo mli.

english: If I buy crop seeds from a different part of Ghana, will they grow the same way on my farm?
ga: Kɛ mihe dumɔwui kɛjɛ Ghana he kroko Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops adapt to the specific climate of where they are raised. If you bring seeds to a new environment with different temperatures and rainfall pattern, they may behave differently or require extra care.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ he ni aduɔ amɛ yɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui tee he ko ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ srɔtoi yɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui baanyɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ loo ehe baahia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I help my young crops adjust when I plant them in a new farm location?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo ŋmɔ hee mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: You can shade the young plants with palm fronds and water them during the cooler early morning or late afternoon hours to reduce heat stress while they get used to the new environment.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei baai awo tso bibioo lɛ he ni okɛ nu awo mli leebi maŋkpa loo shwane ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni akɛba dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi be mli ni amɛkaseɔ amɛshihilɛhe hee lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow strong on one part of my land but struggle just a short distance away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miida waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi amɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Even on the same farm, environmental conditions like soil moisture, drainage, and heat levels can change within a few meters, directly affecting how well crops grow.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli po lɛ, shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsake yɛ mitai fioo komɛi amli. ni saa tsei adalɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop off during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: High environmental temperatures cause plants to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. To save energy and water under high heat stress, the plant drops older leaves.
ga: Shihilɛ mli latsaa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato he yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa shishi. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ baai ni edara lɛ.

english: Does high temperature affect how much water my crops need to grow well?
ga: Ani hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ saa nu ni he hiaa mi tsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ he?

english: Yes, hot weather warms up both the air and soil, causing water to evaporate rapidly. Crops need significantly more water in hot environments to stay cool and healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli dɔɔ. Ha nu lɛ atsɔ oya Tsei lɛ he miihia nu babaoo yɛ hei ni edɔ lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow slower when the heat in my area becomes too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo be mli ni hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat forces plants to spend their energy staying cool rather than making food for growth. High soil temperatures can also damage delicate feeding roots.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ fɛ̃i mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee niyenii ni amɛdara. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite niyenii shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Should I plant small young seed yams or cut up a big yam to plant on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Using fresh, young seed tubers gives the plant strong natural energy, helping it grow faster and produce bigger, healthier yams than using old or oversized cuts.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ayitsei heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni mli wa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe blema loo ŋmeii wuji ni afolɔ.

english: Can I eat part of my harvested yams and still save enough good tubers for next season's planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ maye sweet potato ni akpa lɛ eko ni mikɛ ŋmeii kpakpai komɛi ato lolo kɛha dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can separate your harvest by setting aside healthy, young tubers specifically for planting next season while keeping the larger mature ones for food or market.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ogbala okpamɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ bulbs bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oookɛto tɛ̃ɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ toɔ niyenii loo ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: What happens if I keep re-using the same old seed yams year after year without adding new ones?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni akɛ dumɔwui ewo mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii ekoŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ dumɔwui heei fataaa he?

english: Re-using old seed stock continuously weakens your crop over time, while introducing fresh young seed tubers rejuvenates the crop and boosts your yield size.
ga: Dumɔwui momo ni okɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ daa lɛ baaha onibii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui bibii ayitsei heei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa onibii lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa onibii lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How many new yams can I expect to get from a single heap if I plant good seed tubers?
ga: Sweet potatoes heei enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maná kɛjɛ ŋtayaa kome mli kɛji midu dumɔwui ayitsei kpakpai?

english: With good soil preparation and healthy seed tubers, a single planting heap can produce over ten new yams within a single growing cycle.
ga: Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni wa nɔ Dumɔwui akuu kome baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii heei ni fa fe 10 yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ be kome mli.

english: Why did my neighbor get much bigger yams than me even though we planted on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa ŋmeii ni da kwraa fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Tuber size often depends on seed quality; adding fresh, young seed tubers to your mounds provides the plant with better energy to build larger yams.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha lɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui heei ni darako lɛ ayitsei fata o-pile lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛkɛwo sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Why do big seed yams sometimes produce many small yams instead of one huge yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmeii ni dumɔwui wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii agbo kome najiaŋ lɛ?

english: A single big yam has multiple growing points that compete with each other for nutrients, causing the plant to divide its energy into many smaller tubers rather than one giant one.
ga: Sweet potato agbo ko yɛ hei babaoo ni edaraa yɛ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jaa ehewalɛ lɛ mli ewoɔ bulb bibii babaoo mli yɛ bulb agbo kome najiaŋ.

english: How many months does it take for a newly planted seed yam to start making new tubers underground?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛɔ ŋmeii heei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam plants begin forming new tubers within the first few months, and with proper care, you can see significant new tuber growth in as little as six months.
ga: O sweet potato tso lɛ baabɔi bulbs heei akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Ni kɛji okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ lɛ Obaana yitso hee ni sa kadimɔ waa yɛ nyɔji enumɔ pɛ mli.

english: Do I have to wait a full year before I can harvest any yams from my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani makpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, you do not always have to wait a full year; certain planting methods and good seed tubers allow you to harvest new yams within six to eight months.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be ehe baahia ni omɛ afi muu fɛɛ. Gbɛi komɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei kpakpai baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okpa ŋmeii heei yɛ nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi kpaanyɔ mli.

english: If I put more than one seed tuber in a mound, will it hurt my yam crop?
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ayitso ni fe ekome wo gɔŋ lɛ mli. Ani ebaana sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Planting a few young seed tubers together in one mound can actually increase your overall yield, giving you a larger cluster of new yams at harvest time.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ayitsei ni aduɔ Bulb fioo komɛi ni akɛaafata he yɛ gɔŋ kome mli lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Is it normal for a yam plant to keep producing extra tubers before the growing year is over?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni sa akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ baaya nɔ amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo dani afi ni amɛdaraa lɛ aba naagbee?

english: Yes, healthy yam plants naturally multiply underground throughout their growing season, continually forming extra tubers before the year ends.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baafɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tubers lɛ baaya nɔ aya hiɛ dani afi lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily in full sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting plantains around them provides protection from heat and retains soil moisture until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Enɛ baabu he kɛjɛ latsaa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds before planting my yam seed tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ naa yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ dani miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Creating high mounds loosens the soil so yam tubers can expand easily downward and grow large, while also preventing excess water from drowning the roots.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi oya ni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to make food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara hewalɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which helps feed the corn plants naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Growing the same crop on the same land continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets soil diseases that attack pepper build up to dangerous levels.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eha helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tutuaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashɛ he ko ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, suffocating them and encouraging soil fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. shwieɔ mɔ mumɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so the heavy rain doesn't wash it all away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie fɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly moist after a light rain, and to cover or bury the fertilizer shallowly near the roots so heavy downpours cannot carry it off.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Ni okɛ nɔ loo ofu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he fioo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Should I remove the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mihe? Nɔ ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ani ajie mi plantain shishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, removing extra shoots—called suckers—ensures that the main plantain tree gets all the soil nutrients and water, resulting in larger, healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui titrii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni yeɔ emuu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, rotten patches on the bottom while the fruit is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ beni edara lɛ?

english: Dark spots on tomato bottoms, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant doesn't get enough calcium, often caused by uneven or irregular watering.
ga: Hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What is making small holes in my young corn leaves and eating the plant from the center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni oye ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Small holes inside young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on new leaves inside the heart of the maize plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees not producing any fruit even though they look fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ wooo yibii ko lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni eda kwraa?

english: Unproductive cocoa trees often suffer from poor pruning, disease, lack of soil nutrients, or old age. Removing unproductive shoots and applying proper fertilizer helps the tree focus its energy on bearing healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ tsei ni afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Hela ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo onukpayeli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni wooo yibii lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmeii ni sa woɔ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni wa ni etswaa lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes cocoa branches to become thin, weak, and stop bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo niji lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii?

english: Thin, unproductive branches (sometimes referred to as 'monkey tails' or water sprouts) happen when a tree isn't pruned properly or lacks sunlight. They drain nutrients away from the main trunk without producing any fruit.
ga: Niji lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii. (Bei komɛi lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘monkey tail’ loo nu mli ŋmeii) baa kɛji akɛ afolɔko tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo hulu la bɛ mli. Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do some branches grow long and fast on my cocoa tree without ever flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji komɛi daa oya ni amɛtsɛɔ yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ shi amɛfɔɔɔ fɔfɔi kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: These fast-growing shoots are called chupons or suckers. They steal essential water and nutrients from the main tree stem, so farmers cut them off early to allow the main branches to flower and yield fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni daa oya nɛɛ akɛ chupon loo ŋmeii. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ tsei wuji lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, okwaafoi lɛ foɔ lɛ mra. bɔni afee ni niji titrii lɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii

english: Why are my cocoa pods staying small and drying up before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Small, shriveled pods usually indicate pest damage, black pod disease, or a lack of nutrients and water. Clearing shade slightly and spraying against pests helps pods grow into healthy, mature fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni egbo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii efite, ŋmeii diji hela, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni faaa. Kɛ́ afee hulutsoo be lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda.

english: Is cheap land always good for starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni jara waaa lɛ hi be fɛɛ be kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Cheap land might have poor soil quality, bad drainage, or hidden crop diseases left from previous farming. It is best to inspect the soil depth and drainage before planting cocoa, as poor land will lead to low harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni jara waaa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sũ lɛ ehiii kwraa. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi ni eho lɛ amli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ dani odu kookoo. Akɛni jɛmɛ ehiii hewɔ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: What should I do if I acquire land with very old cocoa trees that don't produce well?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ onine shɛ shikpɔŋ ni kookoo tsei ni egbɔ waa yɔɔ nɔ shi amɛwoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ hu?

english: Old, non-bearing cocoa trees take up space and resources without giving income. Cutting them down and replanting with fast-yielding hybrid cocoa varieties is often better than trying to revive worn-out trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ekɛ shika haaa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ aafolɔ amɛ ni akɛ kookoo ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii oya lɛ adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ehi fe bɔ ni aaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni aha tso ni efite lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can agricultural officers from the government help me with my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ maŋ lɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni madu kookoo?

english: Government extension officers provide advice on best farming practices, supply high-yield seedling varieties, assist with disease control programs, and train farmers on proper pruning and harvesting methods.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa yɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe. Dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni akɛaaha Ye obua yɛ helai ahe nitsumɔi amli ni otsɔse okwaafoi yɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tsei kɛ nibii ni akpaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the government send special teams to prune and harvest cocoa trees in some communities?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ tsuɔ kui krɛdɛɛi koni amɛyafolɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ akutsei komɛi amli lɛ ni amɛkpa amɛkpamɔ lɛ?

english: Government rehabilitation initiatives send trained teams to help farmers properly prune overgrown trees and manage diseased farms across Ghana, boosting overall yield and protecting nearby healthy crops.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ helatsamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsuɔ kui ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛyaye amɛbua okwaafoi ni amɛfo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔji ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Ha yibiiwoo fɛɛ aya hiɛ ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What is the correct way for me to harvest my cocoa pods without hurting future yields?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni matsɔ nɔ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni enaaa wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni abaawo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cocoa pods should be sliced cleanly at the stalk using a sharp harvesting hook or shears. Pulling or twisting pods off damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk, preventing future pods from growing there.
ga: Esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli bibii bibii. Kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛkpaa nii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii ni okɛgbala tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ogbala loo otsi fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. ni etsĩ wɔsɛɛ be mli pods lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How often should I harvest ripe pods from my cocoa farm during the main season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should harvest every two to three weeks during peak season. Leaving overripe or rotting pods on the tree attracts pests and spreads fungal diseases to healthy, young pods.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛba ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I know whether my land is better for growing cocoa or rubber trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo loo rɔba tsei adumɔ?

english: Cocoa trees prefer rich, well-drained soil with balanced rainfall and partial shade, while rubber trees are hardier and can thrive in wetter, acidic, or poorer soils where cocoa might struggle.
ga: Cocoa tsei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo fioo. Yɛ be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei wa fe tsutsu lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ. Eyɛ acid. loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni kookoo baanyɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I have to wait so many years before I can start harvesting latex from rubber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛmɛ afii babaoo dani amɛje latɛs ni jɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli lɛ shishi?

english: Rubber trees require about 6 to 7 years to develop a trunk thick enough to survive continuous tapping. Tapping too early will stunt the tree's growth and permanently reduce its life span.
ga: Rɔba tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛya nɔ amɛtswa amɛhe. Kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaaha ewala be lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why is it bad if I leave too many full-grown trees standing close together on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji miha tsei ni eda babaoo damɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ midumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are overcrowded, their roots compete heavily for underground nutrients and water, while their thick canopy blocks sunlight, causing all the trees to produce fewer fruits or pods.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii loo ŋmeii fioo.

english: Why should I buy prepared nursery seedlings instead of just planting seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa he yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Nursery seedlings are specially bred from high-performing mother plants to resist diseases and grow faster. Planting random seeds from your harvest often leads to low yields and unpredictable tree strength.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛdara oya. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tso lɛ hewalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young seedlings wither and die right after I plant them out in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is often caused by transplant shock, root damage during planting, or intense sunlight. Planting in the early morning, watering well, and providing temporary shade helps young seedlings adjust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli loo hulu la ni naa wa Dumɔ leebi, nu ni awoɔ jogbaŋŋ, kɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or maize in between my young tree seedlings?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani manyɛ mikɛwo mi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping during the first two years gives you quick food and income. You just need to leave enough space around each seedling stem so the food crops do not shade them out or steal their nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika oya. Esa akɛ oshi he ko kɛkɛ ni obɔle he. Tsoi ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli. Enɛ ji koni niyenii tsei lɛ akatsi niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa loo amɛkaju.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they face heat stress, lack sufficient soil moisture, or suffer from nutrient deficiencies like low potassium. It can also mean there are not enough pollinating insects around.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa tamɔ potassium ni faaa lɛ he piŋmɔ Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ.

english: Why do I need to prune healthy branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kookoo tso mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage to allow air and light to circulate through the canopy. This keeps humidity low to stop fungal diseases like black pod and directs energy into growing cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi koni ekpa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Will making cuts on my rubber tree to harvest latex damage the tree permanently?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt tsei ni aaafo koni akɛbu latɛs naa lɛ baafite tsei lɛ kwraa?

english: If done correctly, tapping only cuts the thin outer layer of bark to collect latex without touching the inner wood. The tree naturally regrows its bark, allowing you to harvest safely for decades.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Tapping lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã bibioo lɛ pɛ. Koni abua latex naa ni ataaa tso ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa nii shweshweeshwe afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer around my tree crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ahe?

english: The best time is at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is damp. The moisture helps roots absorb the fertilizer quickly, but applying it during very heavy rains will wash the nutrients away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is fertile enough for me to plant plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ baa nii bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu plantains?

english: Fertile soil usually has a dark, rich color, holds moisture well, and is soft with plenty of decaying leaves or earthworms. If wild plants on the land grow tall with thick green leaves, the soil is usually fertile enough for plantains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. ni eyɛ blɛoo Ayɛ baai ni fiteɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo. Kɛji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa kɛha plantains.

english: What can I add to my soil to make it fertile before I put new crops in the ground?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii dani madu tsei heei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can mix animal manure, composted food scraps, or decomposed leaves into the planting holes. This feeds the soil naturally and gives young plants the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifãi, niyenii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egbo afutu dumɔ bu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei bibii lɛ adara.

english: How do I know if a specific location on my farm is bad for plantain farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Avoid very stony ground or swampy lowlands where floodwater sits for days. Plantains need loose, deep soil that drains water easily, as waterlogged soil rots their underground roots.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia plantains. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What is the proper way to uproot a young plantain shoot from an old plant to transplant it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ plantain tsei bibii kɛjɛɔ tsei momo amli koni akɛwo tsei krokomɛi amli?

english: Use a sharp cutlass or spade to slice carefully between the mother plant and the shoot base. Make sure you lift the shoot with its underground bulb intact and avoid damaging its delicate young roots.
ga: Kɛ kakla loo shɔvel ni naa wa atsu nii. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋ. Kwɛmɔ ni owó ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ eshishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ afitemɔ he.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when I am ready to plant a young plantain sucker?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu mli aahu tɛŋŋ beni mifee klalo akɛ madu plantain tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Dig a hole about knee-deep and broad enough so the bottom bulb of the shoot fits easily. Cover the bulb completely with topsoil up to the point where the shoot meets the stem, pressing the soil down firmly so it stays upright.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee tsitsi ni elɛɛ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni bulb ni yɔɔ mfoniri lɛ shishi lɛ ashɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Okɛ ŋwɛi sũ aha bulb lɛ nɔ kwraa kɛyashi he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooonyɛ shi shiŋŋ koni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain plants when setting up a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-plantain tsei lɛ ato amɛhe beni mikɛ ŋmɔ hee miito shi lɛ?

english: Space your plantain plants about 3 meters (10 feet) apart in straight rows. This gives their large leaves enough space to catch sunlight and prevents their roots from fighting for food in the soil.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ odumɔwui lɛ ateŋ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ sɛɛkuu ni ja mli. Enɛ haa baai agboi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ awuu yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How do I select the healthiest plantain shoot to dig up for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni mikɛfo mli koni mikɛdu?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a wide, heavy bulb at the bottom. These grow into much healthier, higher-yielding plants than shoots with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ lance kɛ bulbs ni mli kwɔ ni tsii yɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛɛmɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Are there different varieties of plantain I can plant, or should I stick to what everyone else uses?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makwɛ plantain henɔi srɔtoi babaoo. Aloo esa akɛ madu lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi krokomɛi kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: There are several varieties, including early-maturing types, disease-resistant varieties, and tall or dwarf types. Trying improved varieties recommended by agricultural officers can yield bigger bunches than traditional varieties.
ga: Ayɛ henɔi babaoo, tamɔ henɔi ni shwereɔ oya. Helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛ henɔi ni kɛlɛ loo ni yɔɔ bibioo Kɛ́ aka henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ taakɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha yibii babaoo aba fe blema henɔi lɛ.

english: Why do some plantain varieties take longer to yield fruit than others on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain henɔi komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Different varieties have different natural growth lifecycles. Some varieties naturally focus energy on building strong trunks before fruiting, while shorter or improved varieties are bred to produce bunches much faster.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ bei srɔtoi. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsei srɔtoi komɛi kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni wa ni amɛtswaa lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, afee srɔtoi ni yɔɔ kuku loo ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii oya kwraa.

english: What should I do to the soil after uprooting old crops so the land stays healthy?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ beni mijie tsei momoi lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leave leftover leaves and stems on the soil to rot as natural mulch, or plant leguminous crops like beans for a season. This restores lost nutrients and protects the soil from drying out in the heat.
ga: Shi baai kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛgboi tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo dumɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛha be kome. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant moves available nutrients from its older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ baa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ aba.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts before planting my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei dani midu ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land with free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmei wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I build my yam mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ etooo amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When yam mounds are spaced too closely, the vines fight for sunlight above ground while the roots compete for moisture and nutrients below, resulting in smaller yam tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Vines kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why should I remove the extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow from the same mother plant, they compete for nutrients, leading to smaller plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing large fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida kɛjɛ nyɛ tso kome mli lɛ Amɛbaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ yibii ahe lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai wuji ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off during periods of intense heat or drought. The extreme stress causes the plant to abort its flowers to conserve water and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ loo hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Haomɔ ni naa wa haa tsei kpaɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my plantain leaves wilting and turning yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbo ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by underground root damage from soil-borne diseases or pests like nematodes, which destroy the root system so the plant cannot absorb water despite rainy conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes, ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato plants in the morning or in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to water tomatoes early in the morning so that any water splashed on the leaves dries quickly during the day, which helps prevent fungal diseases from growing.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tomato nu leebi bɔni afee ni nu fɛɛ nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akaya hiɛ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly before storing it in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã mi-abele ni akpa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moist maize attracts mold and destructive insects like weevils. Drying the grains until they are hard prevents fungal rot and keeps pests from ruining your stored harvest.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ewa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nibii ni ato lɛ anaa.

english: Plantains need enough room so their broad leaves don't shade each other out and their roots don't fight for soil food. Spacing them about 3 meters (10 feet) apart allows each plant to get full sunlight, grow thick stems, and produce heavy, healthy bunches of fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ plantains lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ akatsi amɛhe naa. ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii yeee akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu ni fa, eyɛ shishifã ni mli tse, ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up during dry spells because the plant is trying to save water. Plantains have shallow roots and need a lot of moisture, so when the soil dries out, the plant naturally drops its older outer leaves to keep its stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ejaakɛ tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he. Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, eshiɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ koni eha shishifã lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize on the same piece of land alongside my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, you can intercrop plantains with fast-growing crops like maize or cassava during the first year. Because young plantains take time to grow wide leaves, early intercrops provide quick food and income while protecting the exposed soil from weeds and hot sunshine.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa awo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ be he miihia plantain bibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ. Shishijee lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ jwɛi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my freshly cleared land than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ni mijie lɛ ehee lɛ fe tsei ni adu lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil for a long time and are adapted to sprout immediately once cleared ground gets open sun and rain. Young crops need extra help through regular early weeding until they grow big enough to shade out competing weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebaatsake ehe koni ekwɛ̃ kɛji he ni ajie lɛ lɛ ná hulu la kɛ nugbɔ pɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ kroko kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ amɛ daa, mra nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do people leave dry leaves and grass around the base of their plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shiɔ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi yɛ plantains shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving dry organic material around the base is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and moist, prevents weeds from growing, and rots over time to feed the shallow roots of the plantain.
ga: Atsɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha plantain lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do so many small stem shoots grow around my main plantain tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso bibioo lɛ ji Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ ehe lɛ. Midumɔwu titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, which naturally sprout from the base to multiply the plant. If you leave all of them, they steal food and water from the main plant, resulting in small fruit; you should trim away the weaker ones so the main plant produces a large bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ koni eha tsei ayibɔ aya hiɛ Kɛji akɛ ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie kwraa lɛ, amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli, ni no baaha aduawai lɛ afee bibii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ koni tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know when a bunch of plantains on the stem is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits become full, round, and lose their sharp corners. You will also notice the bottom flower hanging below the bunch has dried up completely and the lower plant leaves naturally turn yellow.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko eyi, ebɔle ehe ni eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efo mli lɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni fĩɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbi kwraa ni tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is putting animal manure or compost around my plantain stem good for its growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he fɛɛ he? No hewɔ lɛ mi plantains lɛ hi kɛha dalɛ.

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that need a lot of rich soil food to grow tall and produce big bunches. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost improves the soil's ability to hold water and slowly releases key nutrients like potassium directly to the plant.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii, ni eheɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmeii wuji. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni fiofio lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii, tamɔ potassium, kɛyaa tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is my plantain plant falling over even when there is no heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi lɛ? He ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants often fall over without wind because tiny pests called nematodes or weevils have eaten away the roots underground. Without strong root anchors in the soil, the heavy weight of the growing fruit bunch easily pulls the whole plant down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli yɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yibii ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ baanyɛ agbala tsei muu fɛɛ kɛba shi mlɛo.

english: Does plantain grow better in bright sunny land or under big tree shade in the forest?
ga: Ani plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ loo yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Plantains thrive best in bright sunlight with rich soil rather than deep shade. While very young plants benefit from light shade, plantains grown under dense tree shade will grow thin and weak, taking much longer to flower and producing very small bunches.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ moŋ fe he ni hulutsoo be mli kwɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii baaná hulutsoo ni mli tse lɛ he sɛɛ moŋ, shi plantains ni adu yɛ tsei ni mli ewo muji lɛ ashishi lɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ fɔfɔii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my crops get diseased when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa helai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, air cannot move freely between them. Good airflow and breeze help dry wet leaves quickly, which stops fungal diseases from growing and spreading across your farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ aya nakai tsei lɛ ateŋ oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai ni efɔ lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yaa hiɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does trimming or pruning leaves help keep my crops healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes excess leaves so the wind can blow through the field easily. This breeze reduces moisture around the plants, making it hard for crop diseases to take hold.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atswa amɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo. Kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei ahe helai.

english: Does letting more sunlight and breeze into my farm really stop leaves from rotting?
ga: Ani hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mihaa etswaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, sunlight and breeze work together to evaporate dew and rainwater from leaves, preventing damp conditions where leaf-rot and fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha bɔ́ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli lɛ afee lasu. Ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ he ni baai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: What does it mean when officers say a crop seed is a 'hybrid' or cross-bred?
ga: Kɛ́ onukpai kɛɛ akɛ tsei dumɔwui ji ‘hybrid’ loo hybrid lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A hybrid crop is created by intentionally combining two different plant varieties—such as one that resists drought and another that produces big fruit—so the new plant gets the best qualities of both parents.
ga: Afeɔ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛ amɛ feɔ ekome lɛ nɔ, tamɔ eko ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ kɛ ekroko ni woɔ yibii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, tso hee lɛ nine shɛɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from a cross-bred crop, will they grow into the exact same strong plants next season?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni jara waaa kɛjɛ tsei ni cross-pollinated yɔɔ mli lɛ amli Ani nakai dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: No, seeds saved from hybrid crops often lose their strength in the second generation and break down into mixed traits, which is why it is usually best to get fresh hybrid seeds each season.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ni amɛgbala amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona hybrid dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I cross-breed different crop varieties myself on my farm?
ga: Ani mi diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ mafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can cross-breed by manually transferring pollen from the flower of one variety to the flower of another, but it takes practice, clean technique, and multiple growing seasons to get consistent results.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofɔ kɛtsɔ pollen ni okɛ onine baajɛ fɔfɔi srɔtoi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli lɛ nɔ. Shi ebiɔ nifeemɔ. ŋaa ni he tse kɛ shweremɔ bei babaoo koni anyɛ ana nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why do improved crop varieties produce bigger harvests than the local traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved varieties have been carefully selected and cross-bred over many years to combine strong traits like high fruit yield, disease resistance, and faster growth into a single seed.
ga: Ahala srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔse amɛ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli koni akɛ sui ni mli wa tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ awo mli. kɛ oyaiyeli ni yaa hiɛ yɛ dumɔwu kome mli

english: Why do some varieties of the same crop grow very tall while others stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni ji henɔ kome lɛ daraa waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu feɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Height is mainly determined by the plant's breeding, but plants also stretch very tall when they are planted too close together and are competing with each other for sunlight.
ga: Bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ damɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ fɔɔ lɛ nɔ titri. Shi tsei hu baanyɛ adara waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛmiitswa hulu la he akaŋ.

english: How many years does it take to create a reliable new crop variety through cross-breeding?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ afee tsei srɔtoi heei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Developing a stable crop variety usually takes several years of planting, selecting the best individual plants, and breeding them across multiple seasons until the traits stay consistent.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni anáa lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Halamɔ tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ofɔ yɛ bei babaoo mli kɛyashi sui lɛ baahi shi nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does planting my crops in straight rows help control disease better than scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ hi kɛha helai akwɛmɔ fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows creates clear pathways that allow breezes to blow through the field smoothly, lowering the humidity around the plants and stopping disease outbreaks.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ aba shi ni okpa helai ni baa lɛ.

english: How do I know if a specific crop will grow well on my land before I spend money to plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mafite shika kɛdu amɛ?

english: Crops require specific soil types, drainage levels, and weather conditions to thrive. By testing your soil and observing how well water drains on your field, you can choose crops naturally suited to your land instead of planting aimlessly and risking crop failure.
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ he hiaa tsei? drainage level kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ dalɛ he Kɛtsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ kaa kɛ bɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ oyale mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ kpãa gbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii ni yiŋtoo ko bɛ he ni okɛ ohe awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe oshara mli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do some crops grow very healthy in one part of Ghana but fail completely when planted in another region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ waa yɛ Ghana kpokpaa ko nɔ shi amɛfiteɔ kwraa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Ghana has different ecological zones with varying rainfall patterns, temperatures, and soil types. Crops thrive best in climate conditions that match their natural needs, so planting a variety suited to your specific ecological zone guarantees better growth and yield.
ga: Ghana yɛ shihilɛhei srɔtoi. Amɛyɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi. Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni kɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hiamɔ nii kpãa gbee lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni ooodu koni ekɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee lɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some cassava farmers make a good profit while others on the same size of land barely clear their costs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii okwaafoi komɛi náa sɛɛnamɔ waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛshika ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he?

english: Profitability depends on choosing high-yielding and disease-resistant crop varieties, using proper planting techniques, and securing a market buyer before planting, rather than just planting without a clear strategy.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ ni anáa lɛ damɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ahalaa lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋaai ni sa atsu nii kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ jara nɔ dani adumɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aduɔ nii kɛkɛ ni gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli ka shi faŋŋ bɛ mli.

english: Is it more profitable for me to grow cash crops like cocoa or fast-growing food crops like vegetables?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba kɛha mi akɛ madu shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai?

english: It depends on your long-term goals and income needs. Cash crops like cocoa take years to yield but bring steady long-term income, while fast-growing vegetables provide quick cash flow within months but require intensive daily care and reliable water.
ga: Edamɔ otii ni okɛma ohiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛ shika he hiamɔ nii anɔ. Shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii babaoo dani anáa shi ehaa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa shika baa oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi, ni aha lɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: What is the difference between using seeds saved from my previous harvest and buying certified improved seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛ dumɔwui ni asaa he ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ miheɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their vitality over time, resulting in smaller yields and higher disease risk. Certified improved seeds are scientifically selected to resist local pests, tolerate drought better, and produce higher harvest yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni helai hu baa. Ahala dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase yɛ jeŋ nilee gbɛ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and dry up during dry spells while my neighbor's crops remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different root depths and water needs. Deep-rooted or drought-tolerant varieties can pull moisture from deep underground, while crops planted in well-prepared, organic-rich soil retain moisture longer during dry periods.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ nu he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Henɔi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Is it better for me to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year or wait longer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo abaamɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Planting after the very first rain is risky because the rains may stop for weeks, causing young seeds to dry up. Waiting until the rainy season establishes fully ensures your crops get continuous moisture to survive and grow strong.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa otsii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui bibii ni egbi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara waa.

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed, grow strong, and produce a maximum yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii. amɛdara waa ni amɛha yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ

english: Why does planting legumes like beans together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes naturally absorb nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This provides free organic food to nearby plants like maize, helping them grow healthier without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ náa niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni aheee nɔ ko, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and starves out pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather. Clearing weeds and removing infected pods keeps air moving through the farm and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ aya nɔ abɔle ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ebaaha hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cocoa pods with sticky sap coming out?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli buji bibii? kɛ mliki ni mli tse ni miije kpo

english: This damage is caused by mirid insects that suck sap from stems and pods. Their bites leave wounds that damage your harvest, so spraying approved insecticides at the right time helps protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji mirid kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Amɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ kɛ pilamɔi ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ be naa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are some branches on my cocoa tree swelling up and making the leaves look pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi efuu ni eha baai lɛ efee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny mealybug insects. It weakens the tree and reduces yield, so infected trees often need to be cut out to protect the rest of your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji kookoo bud hela ni efuu lɛ he okadi. Virus ko ni mealybugs bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds under my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ mikoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and soil nutrients that your cocoa trees need to produce healthy pods. Keeping the farm clean also stops harmful insects and fungal diseases from breeding near your trees.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baafɔ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so the tree can send energy straight into growing pods. It also allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the tree trunk, keeping the farm dry and healthy.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ majeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them before they can form pods. Dry weather, extreme heat, or lack of midges cause unpollinated flowers to fall off naturally.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni ekɛ amɛ afee pollination dani amɛfee pods. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: During dry periods, cocoa trees drop leaves to save water and survive the heat. Planting temporary shade crops or permanent shade trees keeps the soil cool and reduces this leaf loss.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Cocoa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa daa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi.

english: How do large shade trees help my mature cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Shade trees block direct hot sunlight, reduce wind damage, cool the farm air, and drop leaves that rot and turn into rich, natural fertilizer for your cocoa soil.
ga: Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he hulutsoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli jɔɔ Ni enɛ haa baai ni egboi lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha o-cocoa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Look at the pod color. Unripe pods are green or dark red, but fully mature pods change color to bright yellow or orange-yellow, showing the beans inside are fully formed.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɔɔ ha. Pods ni eshɛko lɛ ji eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ. Shi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛsu kɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ebɔi feemɔ kwraa.

english: Why do I need to wrap my fresh cocoa beans in plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii heei woɔ plantain baai amli gbii 2-3 dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: This process is called fermentation. It removes the sweet white pulp, turns the beans brown inside, and creates the chocolate flavor that buyers require before purchasing.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛtsɔ loo yɛŋ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɔfi yibii lɛ amli tsɔɔ asarasu. ni afee tsokolate ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ dani amɛhe

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ kui bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: The young shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main mother plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves only the strongest stem to receive full nourishment, resulting in larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii, ni atsɛɔ amɛ young shoots lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Ehe miihia ni afolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed most of their small flowers without developing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, eyaaa hiɛ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more blossoms than they can feed. Many flowers drop because they were not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or because dry weather stresses the tree, forcing it to drop flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Aloo akɛni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ hewɔ? Nyɛ fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛgbee shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my yam crop produce much larger tubers when I train the vines to climb wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo beni mitsɔseɔ wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tso tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growth. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so it receives maximum light and fresh air, while keeping leaves away from damp soil diseases that reduce tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba mli babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and produce food; when soil nitrogen is low, the plant draws remaining nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ niyenii aba. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye amɛbua dalɛ yɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm improve the growth of the crops I plant after them?
ga: Te tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen breaks down into the soil, providing free organic fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ fiteɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains fall right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, causing root cells to suffocate and allowing soil fungi to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ abote mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their buds and flowers when the hot dry season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, pepper plants lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it. Dropping flowers is a defense reaction that conserves water and prevents the plant from drying out completely.
