ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni haa nu hiɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even though I watered the ground in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛtsu nii leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose moisture into the dry air faster than the roots can draw water up from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to reduce surface exposure to the sun, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my young oil palm tree produce only male flowers and no fruit bunches during its first flowering year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso bibioo lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ ni ewooo yibii yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young oil palms produce male flowers first to save energy while building strong roots and trunk systems. As the tree matures and stores enough nutrients, it will begin producing female flowers that form oil palm bunches.
ga: Palm tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni ekɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa to lɛ Ebaabɔi fɔfɔi yei ni feɔ oil palm panicles lɛ feemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upwards and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Upward curling and stunted growth in tomatoes are commonly caused by a virus transmitted by tiny whitefly insects. Controlling whiteflies early and removing infected plants prevents the virus from spreading to healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato mli shwiemɔ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. Whitefly Nɔkwɛmɔ Mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important plant food, or it is getting improper water. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the plant's life keeps the leaves green so the corn cobs can grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa, loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the field, it drowns the roots and causes rot. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the middle of the day even when the soil feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: On very hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. As long as the soil has moisture, the plants are usually resting and will recover in the cooler evening once the strong sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves. Spraying early with neem water or safe insect control helps keep these tiny pests away and protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo mra ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ kooloi ahe nii Ebaaye abua ni atsĩ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. Enɛɛmɛi jeɔ kpo ni amɛbuɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the growing centers?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Yɛ ŋmãa dumɔhe lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which loves to eat young maize leaves. Inspecting your farm early and putting recommended treatments or crushed neem seeds directly into the funnel of the plant can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ ni oookɛwo tso lɛ tsɔnei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkpa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. Leaving a few large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains gives the young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji fioo komɛi loo adu tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni daa oya lɛ, ebaaha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get steady water, or when insects damage the flowers. Giving the plants consistent water and light shade during peak heat helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during small windstorms before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry very heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. You can prevent them from falling by propping up the heavy stems using strong bamboo poles or wooden stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ko ni tsii waa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Obaanyɛ otsi enaa koni ekagbee shi kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb up long wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ sweet potato wain tso ko hiɛ koni makwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that needs sunlight on its leaves to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they catch more sunlight and stay safe from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni amɛnaa hulu la babaoo yɛ. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: Why do groundnut plants push their flowers down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but once the flower is pollinated, the stem naturally bends and grows downward into the soil. The actual groundnuts grow and mature safely buried inside the earth.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ atswa fɔfɔi lɛ pollen lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baabɔle ehe ni eda kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akpɔlɔi diɛŋtsɛ daa ni amɛdaraa, ni amɛfuɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the plants turn green again and produce larger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ewo baai wuji.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Look closely at the small raised bumps or 'eyes' along the stem cutting. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so the plant can easily shoot leaves above ground while developing strong roots below.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo, yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when they suffer from sudden heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ trukaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto stakes instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso ko nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã ekplekeshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunshine to manufacture food that feeds the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off the damp soil where fungal diseases can easily infect them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Curled or twisted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. Inspecting under the leaves and using an appropriate organic spray or insecticide will clear the pests and allow fresh, flat leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe loo etsɔ ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and wither before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda?

english: Tiny cocoa pods can turn black due to a fungal disease called black pod or natural tree stress when there is too much shade and moisture. Pruning extra branches lets in sunlight and air movement, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: cocoa ŋmɔtɔi bibii Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ hewɔ. loo adebɔɔ mli nɔnyɛɛ ni baa tsei anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do simple weeds actually reduce the amount of food my crops yield?
ga: Te jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Weeds act like hidden thieves in your farm by competing directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to everything they need to grow strong and produce maximum yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehaa otsei titrii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the hot afternoon or in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning when the sun is gentle. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it, wasting your water and effort.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ leebi be mli ni hulu la lɛ tsoɔ fioo lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Efiteɔ nu kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Why didn't the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest sprout well when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa yɛ naagbee nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to germinate if they were stored with too much moisture or damaged by webworms and weevils. Drying seeds thoroughly until they are hard and storing them in sealed containers keeps them alive and ready for the next planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo wɛbworms kɛ ŋmeii efite amɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee klalo kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because intense sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out their roots quickly. Planting nurse crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides the shade and cool air they need until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ oya. Nurse tsei tamɔ plantains ni akwɛɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and build wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji ni matswa tsei ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up high to catch as much sunlight as possible, which helps the plant make food to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp wet ground, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs agboi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build green leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the maize regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots in the soil. When planted with maize, they share this natural fertilizer, making the soil richer and helping the maize grow bigger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛbaajara adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ adara

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are very strong salts that can burn the stem and roots of your plant if placed directly on them. It is best to place fertilizer a few inches away from the stem so the roots can draw in the nutrients safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ he 2-3 inches koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in soil that stays soaked with water for too long. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy rains so the soil is wet deep down, not just on top. Sowing seeds after just one light rain can cause them to sprout and dry up if the sun returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa. Jeee ŋwɛi pɛ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or a sudden lack of water in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist by covering the soil around the plant with grass or dry leaves helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oookɛwo he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ nɔ. tsei ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli Ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: Those holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central funnel of the plant during the day. Checking your farm early and applying safe bio-pesticides or neem extract into the funnels will kill the caterpillars.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ awo kooloi lɛ amli lɛ baagbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why does leaving wild grass and weeds on my farm reduce the size of my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by taking away water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvest without digging up all the plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava shows clear signals when it is ready above ground: the leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, the main stem turns woody and brown, and the soil around the base begins to crack open as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Yucca jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛ́ efee klalo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time cocoa pods are ripe for harvesting so the beans inside do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteee.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color clearly on the tree, turning from deep green or reddish-purple to a rich golden yellow or orange. Additionally, if you gently tap a ripe pod, it makes a hollow sound because the seeds inside have detached from the outer shell.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ faŋŋ mli. Etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo magenta mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ ota ŋmei bibioo ko he blɛoo lɛ, ebaafee gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji beni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efo kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants producing tassels at the top before I see any corn cobs growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani manyɛ mana ŋmeii lɛ ni miida lɛ?

english: The tassels at the top produce pollen that must dust the silks lower on the plant. This is a normal growth step, as pollen from the top flowers must reach the lower silks before corn cobs can form and fill with grains.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ pollen ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ ji dalɛ gbɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ashɛ siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he dani ŋmei lɛ afee ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in open fields without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out quickly under full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains gives cocoa trees the cover and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ náa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops look revived and stand upright so quickly after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa wala mli ni amɛteɔ shi oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During dry weather, crops conserve water and weaken to survive heat. When the first rain arrives, the dry roots take in water rapidly, raising internal cell pressure which makes leaves uncurl and turn green almost immediately.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli ni egbɔjɔɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba Shishifãi ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ wala yibii lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before turning into green peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of proper nutrients. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save its remaining energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna haomɔi ni baa trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni sa ni haa amɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly into tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is a natural protective reaction to hot weather, lack of water, or attack from small insects like whiteflies. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss and shield itself from heat.
ga: Tomato baa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsiɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ atuatsemɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall with many green leaves after I fertilize, but produce very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛnáa baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ? Shi ani ekɛ yibii fioo ko pɛ haa?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus on growing leaves and stems instead of fruit. Crops need balanced soil food containing phosphorus and potassium to convert healthy leafy growth into strong flowers and big fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ etsɔ fɔfɔi ni he wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food for the tuber below. Lifting the vines on stakes keeps leaves exposed to light, protects them from soil pests, and leads to much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. ni ekɛ yitso ni da kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: Why do small shoots keep growing around the base of my plantain tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ edaa yɛ mi plantain shishitoo lɛ he Ni ani esa akɛ mafo lɛ?

english: Plantains grow new shoots called suckers to multiply. If you leave all of them, they compete with the main tree for soil nutrients and water; cutting back extra suckers leaves only one or two to ensure a heavy, healthy plantain bunch.
ga: Plantains lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii heei ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji oshi amɛ fɛɛ lɛ, amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli, ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ, ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight during their first two to three years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield the cocoa leaves from sun burn and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to reduce water loss and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing its underground roots.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ehi wala mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants rolling up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll up their leaves to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the hot sun. This helps the plant hold onto moisture and prevent drying out during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akabaa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I have to heap the soil into big mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ muji agbo ko ato dani odu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Making deep, soft soil mounds gives yam tubers loose earth to expand downwards easily without hitting hard ground, while also improving drainage so the roots do not rot in standing water.
ga: Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do people tell me to cut off the broad-leaved shoots around my main plantain tree and leave only the narrow ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mifolɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ. Ni gɔŋ bibioo ko pɛ eshwɛ?

english: Thin shoots with spear-like leaves draw energy efficiently from deep roots to grow strong, whereas broad-leaved shoots consume the mother plant's nutrients without producing large, healthy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsofɔi bibii ni baai tamɔ akpɔlɔi lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ yeɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ekɛ tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baaa.

english: Planting maize too close together causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stalks that produce tiny or empty corn cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This leaves natural food in the ground that fertilizes hungry crops like maize when planted next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ́ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of bees for pollination can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, dark conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows air and sunlight to dry out the farm, keeping the pods healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaa pod lɛ mli waa

english: Why do my young maize plants turn pale and stop growing when weeds surround them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ jwɛi bɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients faster than young maize can. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nutrients in the soil go directly into feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmãa bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa otso lɛ niyenii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when water sits around the roots for too long.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hole niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my crop when applying it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa miiwo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains strong salts that can scorch and burn the plant stem and roots if placed directly against them. It is best to place the fertilizer a few inches away in a ring or line so the roots can reach for it safely.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã ni ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta loo line mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my farm yield less harvest each year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the young cocoa plants with the shade and moist soil they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop down during the hot afternoon sun but stand up again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: In the intense afternoon heat, plantain leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun and preserve moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Plantain baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni ekɛba etso lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when the soil remains waterlogged for long periods during heavy rainy seasons. Excessive water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha bulb lɛ agbo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put strong sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ nine ni wa ama shi koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up to catch sunlight, while weeding prevents wild plants from stealing light, water, and soil food.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking fiɔ baai lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ koo mli tsei anaa koni amɛkaju la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and look twisted and small?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ bibioo?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. These pests damage the leaf structure and stop healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ, ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop off unpollinated when temperatures get too high, when air humidity is extremely dry, or when water supply to the soil is irregular. Heat stress weakens the flower stems, causing them to break off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ mli egbi waa loo be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa Heat stress haa fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ fãa.

english: Why is my okra crop growing very tall with huge leaves but producing almost no okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi okra ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow big stems and green leaves instead of making flowers and fruits. Balancing the fertilizer with phosphorus helps trigger flower and fruit production.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai eŋɔlii. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔsfɔs mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Is it profitable for me to grow food crops between my young coconut trees?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ niyenii tsei yɛ mi ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping short-term crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between young coconut trees helps you earn income from the land while waiting for the trees to mature, while also helping control weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei loo ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ haa onáa shika kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni omɛɛɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni eyeɔ jwɛi anɔ.

english: How do I know if my coconut trees are getting enough water and plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-koko tso lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdu niyenii?

english: Healthy coconut trees have deep green leaves and hold large bunches of nuts; if the fronds turn yellow early or green nuts keep falling off, the tree is suffering from water stress or a lack of soil nutrients like potassium.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwie shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he haomɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium lɛ miipiŋ tso lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees like plantains or timber trees protects the seedlings from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains loo boxwood ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: What happens to my yields if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients, which results in tall, weak stems and small fruit yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and curl up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce water loss when the soil is too dry, and yellowing usually means the soil is short on nitrogen or the plant's roots are damaged.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ efite.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting with yellow patches and producing small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ fãi srɔtoi lɛ? Eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies; you can prevent it by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ nɔ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to develop black spots at the bottom and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ?

english: This is blossom end rot, which occurs when plants cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering during hot weather.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy and quick to absorb surface water and nutrients, which is why clearing them early is critical so they do not starve your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia. Bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: How can I improve my soil fertility without spending a lot of money on bag fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni mikɛ shika babaoo akawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ akotokui amli?

english: You can naturally enrich your soil by adding animal manure, well-rotted compost, or by planting leguminous crops like cowpeas, which take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi ashishifã ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ loo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ, ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds when the rainfall keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy rains so the soil is deeply wet, rather than planting after the very first light shower which might dry up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se, nɛ lɔ ɔ ma nyɛ maa gbi.

english: How do I know when my plantains are fully ripe and ready to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the fruit becomes plump, the sharp corners on the skin become rounded, and the tiny dried flowers at the tips fall off easily, usually about three to four months after the flowers first appear.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Ayɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. kɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni egbi lɛ Naagbee lɛ baagbee shi oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ beni fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested plantains from ripening too quickly before I take them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya tsɔ dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: Keep harvested green plantains in a cool, well-ventilated shade away from direct sunlight, and do not store them near already-ripened fruits, which give off natural gases that speed up ripening.
ga: Kɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. He ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ni okɛto he ko ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃. Enɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya lɛ kpo.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when setting up a new field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ beni miduɔ saatso hee lɛ?

english: You should space plantain suckers about 3 meters apart so their broad leaves have enough room to capture sunlight and the roots do not fight each other for nutrients and soil moisture.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 bɔni afee ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe etswaŋ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant plantains on the same land alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is very good because the fast-growing plantain leaves create shade that protects delicate cocoa seedlings from direct sunlight and heat.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ hi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I see so many small plantain shoots growing around one main stem, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa plantain tsei bibii lɛ? Nibii babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso wulu kome he Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Multiple shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the main tree, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. You should prune extra shoots and leave only two or three healthy suckers at different ages.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain jwɛi lɛ feɔ bibioo. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni okɛfata he lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli.

english: Why do heavy winds easily knock down my plantain trees when they carry fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ mi-plantains lɛ shi oya kɛ́ amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems rather than deep taproots. When heavy fruit bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs support from strong wooden or bamboo props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni aduawai akuu ko ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ tsii ni ehe miihia ni tso loo ŋmei ni wa aye abua lɛ.

english: What type of manure or fertilizer works best to make plantain trees yield larger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kui wuji amli?

english: Plantains grow best in dark, rich soil mixed with organic matter like well-decomposed poultry manure or compost, which provides steady nitrogen and potassium for strong stem development.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni edɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi ashishi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ efutu mli. ni haa nitrogen kɛ potassium ni yaa nɔ daa koni tso lɛ adara waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plants turning yellow and dying before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks water during dry periods or lacks potassium in the soil. It can also indicate root damage caused by tiny pests called nematodes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hu.

english: What causes tiny holes and dark rot inside the base of my plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ mli

english: This rot is caused by plantain stem borers or weevils that lay eggs inside the stem. The hatching grubs burrow through the trunk, blocking the flow of water and nutrients to the plant.
ga: Stem borers loo weevils ni woɔ wui yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kpɔŋɔi ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli. Etsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody instead of soft when I harvest them for making fufu?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo beni mikpaa amɛ koni mikɛfee fufu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody if they are left in the ground too long past maturity or experience severe drought, causing the plant to turn its soft starch into tough fiber to survive.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ fe nine loo amɛbaaná hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ haa tsei tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why did you hang those small plastic objects on my mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ plastic nibii bibii fĩɔ shi lɛ? Mɛi ni yɔɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Those are pest traps containing a chemical scent. The scent travels through the air to attract bad insects like fruit flies away from your mangoes and catch them before they can damage your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsofai ni shãa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Ehe ŋmɔlɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni egbala ŋmeii gbohii tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛjɛ mango lɛ he ni emɔmɔ amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Will using smelly chemical traps on my farm make my fruits unsafe to eat?
ga: Ani tsofai ni shãa mɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi aduawai lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ?

english: No, these traps only release a scent into the air to catch insects inside the container. The chemical stays inside the trap and does not touch or harm your fruit at all.
ga: Dabi, nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛmɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ pɛ. Tsofai lɛ hiɔ tsɔne lɛ mli ni etaaa oyibii lɛ ahe loo eyeee amɛ awui kwraa.

english: How do I know when an insect trap on my fruit tree is no longer working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ?

english: The chemical scent inside the trap slowly fades over 4 to 6 weeks as it evaporates in the air. Once the scent is gone or the trap is full of insects, it stops attracting new pests and needs to be replaced.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaho aya fiofio. Efoɔ yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 mli beni efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ laaje loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii Ebaakpa kooloi bibii heei agbalamɔ. ni ehe miihia ni atsake

english: How can small insects smell things on my farm if they don't have noses?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔlɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji amɛbɛ ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Insects use their feelers (antennae) to smell subtle chemicals floating in the air. This allows them to smell ripe fruit, prospective mates, or chemical traps from very far away.
ga: Kplukai kɛ nibii ni nuɔ nii ahe (antennas) tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛnu tsofai bibii ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃, suɔlɔi, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: How far away can pests smell the traps we place in my farm?
ga: Te kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ anu tsɔnei ni wɔkɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe kɛyashi tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects have a very sharp sense of smell and can detect trap scents carried by the wind from hundreds of meters away, pulling them away from your main crops.
ga: Kplukai yɛ henumɔ ni mli wa waa ni amɛnuɔ nii ahe. ni ebaanyɛ ena tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa kɛjɛɔ mitai ohai abɔ kɛyaa he ko lɛ. koni ogbala amɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe

english: Why do certain insects only target my mango trees but leave my cassava alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi komɛi kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ mi mango tsei lɛ anɔ shi amɛshiɔ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Insects are drawn to specific scents and sugars produced by certain plants. Mango fruit flies specifically look for sweet, soft fruits to lay their eggs, which cassava plants do not provide.
ga: Gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛyaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛi kɛ sugar ni tsei komɛi feɔ lɛ anɔ. Mango aduawai amli ŋmeii taoɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo pɔtɛɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛwui lɛ baawo nɔ. ni ŋmei tso lɛ bɛ lɛ

english: Why do my mango flowers drop off before turning into real fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ miigbee shi dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off due to stress from hot weather, lack of water, or tiny pests attacking the blossoms. Protecting the trees from pests early allows the flowers to stay strong and form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ hewɔ. Ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe mra Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhewalɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do fruit flies ruin my mangoes even when the fruit looks healthy on the outside?
ga: Te aduawai amli ŋmeii miifite mi-mango lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ?

english: Fruit flies poke tiny holes in the skin of young mangoes to lay eggs inside. The eggs turn into tiny worms that eat the fruit from the inside out, causing it to rot and fall off early.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii lɛ woɔ bu bibii. yɛ mango ŋmei lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii yɛ mli Wɔji lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni yeɔ aduawai kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ Enɛ haa egboɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do pests attack my fruit trees more heavily during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the dry season, wild plants dry up, so insects travel long distances searching for moisture. Juicier crops like mangoes attract hungry insects looking for food and water.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, koo mli tsei lɛ gbiɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii fãa gbɛ kɛyaa he ko shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao fɛ̃i. Tsei ni mli ewo muji tamɔ mango lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitao niyenii kɛ nu lɛ.

english: Why should I ask an extension officer before trying new pest protection methods on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi mi-extension agent lɛ dani maka gbɛ hee ni akɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ?

english: Extension officers understand how different chemicals and devices work. Asking for guidance ensures you put protection tools in the right place so you don't waste money or accidentally harm your trees.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ nuɔ bɔ ni tsofai kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ shishi. Ŋaawoo ni ooobi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ ohebuu lɛ ewo he ni sa. Enɛ ji koni okafite shika yɛ oshara mli loo okaye otsei lɛ awui.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps keep the leaves green and produces bigger ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ afee ŋmɔji.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it better to put fertilizer on my farm when the soil is moist rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only absorb nutrients when they are dissolved in moisture. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop's roots and waste your money, whereas moist soil helps the roots absorb the fertilizer safely.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshwie ŋmɔtɔ mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under strong sunlight. Shade trees like plantains or forest trees create a cooler environment and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa is mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when it rains continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, but standing water starves the roots of air and encourages harmful soil fungi to grow. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shi nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do farmers spread dry leaves and dead grass around the base of their crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni egboi amɛshwieɔ amɛhe lɛ? Amɛtso lɛ shishitoo lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass around crops is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry or when the soil lacks steady moisture and essential minerals like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently watered and shaded during hot afternoons prevents this problem.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ hulutsoo daa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Weeds are fast growers that aggressively steal sunlight, space, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil that your crops need to thrive. Even with water, crops surrounded by weeds become weak and yield much less harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu po yɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the foliage off my vegetable crops so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiye mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Caterpillars are in a rapid growth phase and need huge amounts of leaf material to survive before turning into moths or butterflies. Regularly inspecting under leaves allows you to pick them off or treat the crop before they destroy the whole foliage.
ga: Kplukai yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya, ni amɛbiɔ baai babaoo koni amɛhi shi dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ofoɔ amɛ loo otsaa tso lɛ dani okpãtãa baai lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do farmers cut off the lower or diseased branches of their crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lower and sick branches lets fresh air and sunlight flow through the plant, which prevents fungal diseases from spreading. It also forces the plant to direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier fruits instead of wasteful leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ hu koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafite baai.

english: Why should I leave space between my pepper plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ pepper tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting peppers too close forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to smaller plants and fewer fruits. Proper spacing lets sunlight reach all parts of the plant and allows air to flow, which helps prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do people say planting beans or groundnuts on my farm will make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant crops like maize after legumes, the maize feeds on that natural fertilizer to grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Abɛi lɛ baaye nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eda ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft roots and cannot handle direct heat and hot winds. They need shade from taller plants like plantains to protect them from burning until their roots grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi yɛ blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ la he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants, and how do I stop it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by armyworms or caterpillars feeding on the soft leaves. Inspecting your farm early and applying the right pest control early in the morning when pests are active will protect your leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaagbe tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii yɛ leebi be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and covered in sticky white spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with white spots are caused by tiny pests like mealybugs or whiteflies that suck the juice out of the plant. Using clean, healthy cassava stems for planting and spraying neem water or recommended treatments keeps them away.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ ni akɛ neem nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my maize so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the plants are growing fast, usually two weeks after planting and again when the maize is knee-high. Avoid putting fertilizer right before heavy rains, and place it a few centimeters away from the stem so it doesn't burn the root.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida oya. Bei pii lɛ, otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ shɛ tsitsi nɔ lɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Ni okɛwo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 koni shishifãi lɛ akashã.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon heat even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Vegetables lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it during the hottest part of the day. As long as the soil remains damp, the leaves will bounce back once the afternoon heat passes.
ga: Nu ni aduawai tsɔɔ amɛbaai amli lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ ho.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially combined in a lab to grow strong only once. If you plant seeds saved from your harvest, the second-generation crops will grow unevenly, give smaller yields, and be easily attacked by diseases.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ feɔ ekome krɛdɛɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli koni amɛdara shikome pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ni helai tutuaa amɛ oya

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster than the maize I planted after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe ŋmãa ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally survive harsh conditions, so their seeds sprout quickly to grab sunlight and soil food before your crops can build strong roots. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛmɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani onibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, or when the plant gets too much or too little water. Extreme stress prevents the flowers from forming fruit, so keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps save the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni tso lɛ náa nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ Haomɔ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water. The maize spends all its energy stretching high up to reach light instead of putting energy into making big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Abɛi kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji

english: Why shouldn't I burn my field after clearing the bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashãa ŋmɔ ko beni ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable natural organic matter that feeds the soil, kills beneficial soil organisms, and leaves the soil exposed to severe heat, which makes it dry out quickly.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni jara wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat becomes too intense, when the soil lacks steady moisture, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing excessive water loss.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Etsiɔ nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy with large leaves but gives me small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing leaves above ground rather than storing food energy in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii hewalɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside their maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil and acts as free fertilizer for nearby maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die if I do not plant plantains beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in full direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaf shade that shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulutsoo muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the hidden center of my maize plants right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm lay their eggs on fresh foliage when rain triggers new growth. The young caterpillars hide inside the central leaves (whorl) where it is moist and safe from predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai heei anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii heei daa. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (rings), ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ amɛye amɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when the soil dry spell lasts too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Plants need water to transport nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. Without water, the plant cannot feed itself properly and loses its green chlorophyll.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛ klorofil eŋɔli lɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ.

english: How can I know that my yam is ready for harvest without digging open the whole mound?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: When yam tubers reach full maturity underground, the green vines above ground naturally stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up, indicating that the leaf growth phase is complete.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Green vines ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakpa amɛdalɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi Etsɔɔ akɛ baa lɛ dalɛ fã lɛ egbe naa.

english: How can I tell if my tree or crop is healthy just by looking at it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso loo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ ekwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: A healthy tree has vibrant green leaves, steady new growth, and strong stems. If the leaves look pale, yellowish, or stunted, the plant is struggling to get enough nutrients or water from the soil.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dalɛ hee ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ. kɛ tsei ni mli wa. Kɛji baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔŋ, loo egbɔjɔ lɛ, tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ená niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What specific signs should I look for when checking my farm's progress?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ matao beni mikwɛɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa lɛ?

english: You should look closely at the color of the leaves, check for signs of pests or disease on the stems, and see if new shoots and branches are growing properly.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ baai lɛ ahe su jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ amli kɛji ŋmeii loo helai komɛi yɛ amɛhe. ni okwɛ kɛji tsei ashishifãi kɛ tsei aniji heei miida jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to inspect my crops regularly instead of waiting until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli daa moŋ fe ni mamɛ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Checking your crops regularly helps you catch problems like poor soil nutrition or pest attacks early, allowing you to treat the plants before permanent damage occurs.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona naagbai tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tsei dani amɛfiteɔ daa.

english: How do I know when my fruit trees need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your tree is growing slowly, has pale yellow leaves, or drops its flowers without producing good fruit, it is showing that the soil lacks essential food and requires fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai ko baaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: How soon should I expect my trees to improve after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Te esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mitsei lɛ baafee oya beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Once fertilizer is applied and receives moisture, you should see noticeable improvements—such as darker green leaves and fresh shoots—within two to four weeks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni onine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ Obaana hiɛyaa ni kadiɔ mɔ tamɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ heei. yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli

english: Can applying fertilizer incorrectly hurt my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni esaaa lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, putting too much fertilizer or placing it too close to the main tree stem can burn the roots and leaves, which can weaken or kill the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli loo akɛma tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ashã. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: How do I choose the right fertilizer for my fruit trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Fruit trees need fertilizers rich in nitrogen early on for strong leaf growth, and higher potassium and phosphorus when they start flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ adara waa ni ebi potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo beni fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my mango trees producing small or poor-quality fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii loo ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Mango trees require full sunlight and nutrient-rich soil to develop healthy, sweet fruit. If the tree lacks nutrients, the fruit will remain small, taste poor, or fall off prematurely.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Yibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo, ebaafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, loo ebaagbee shi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my fruit trees turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ su fɛfɛo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help from the plant, showing that it lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or is receiving improper watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bolɔɔ amɛtsɛɔ tso lɛ koni eye ebua lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ebɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ awo mli nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: What should I do if my young mango tree seems stuck and is not growing?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi mango tso lɛ efo ni ekwɛɛɛ?
