english: Clear away weeds around the base so they don't steal food, ensure the tree gets plenty of sunlight, and apply organic manure or fertilizer to stimulate new root and stem growth.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. cones koni amɛkaju niyenii Kwɛmɔ ni tso lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii ni okɛha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tip down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again and produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When you plant maize on that same land next season, the maize feeds on that trapped nutrient without you needing to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye niyenii ni ekɛkpɛtɛ he lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo.

english: What are these caterpillars eating holes in the leaves and center whorls of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni yeɔ bu yɛ baai kɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ ring lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that destroys maize crops by eating the young leaves from the inside out. Checking your farm early in the morning and spraying recommended crop protection products or applying neem extracts can save your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmãa nibii kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curled up with yellow patterns, and why are the roots so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread through infected stems used for planting. To prevent it, always plant improved, disease-resistant stem varieties provided by agricultural officers.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa lɛ Esa akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ afee tso yibii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle full sunlight and harsh dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside your cocoa creates temporary umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa egbiɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of forming pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get too stressed by heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Providing regular water during hot dry spells and avoiding excessive fertilizer helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotten before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is growing. Irregular watering often causes this, so keeping soil moisture steady and adding agricultural lime or organic compost fixes the problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ okwaayeli mli lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground using the sunlight trapped by their leaves above ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the soil so they catch more sunlight and stay safe from fungal diseases, leading to much bigger yam tubers at harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ, amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: Why is this weed with purple flowers making my maize dry up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni hiɛ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa mi-ŋma lɛ gĩɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛɔ moŋ?

english: That weed is Striga, also known as witchweed, which attaches its roots directly to your maize roots under the soil to steal water and food. Pulling it up before it produces flowers and rotating your crops with leguminous plants helps clear it from your farm.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ abɛi jwɛi. ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ogbala amɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi dani amɛfɔ̃ ni okɛ ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant them on raised soil mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds and ridges loosen the soil so roots can spread easily and prevent rainwater from flooding the roots. Soft, loose soil is especially helpful for root crops like cassava and yams so the tubers can expand without pushing against hard ground.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni nugbɔ nu lɛ akaho shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ titri kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested crops rot so quickly while waiting for buyers to collect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miifite oya nɛkɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Once crops are harvested, they continue to breathe and generate heat. High ambient heat and lack of airflow break down the plant tissues rapidly, causing fungi and bacteria to multiply and cause rot.
ga: Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Amɛyaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa babaoo ni ekɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do my crops spoil much faster when buyers pack them tightly into large sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya waa kɛ́ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ wo kotokui wuji amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tightly packing produce crushes plant cells inside the crop. These crushed areas leak plant juices, creating ideal conditions for decay-causing pathogens to spread rapidly through the whole bag.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ hei ni ekpɔtɔ nɛɛ haa tsei amli nu lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ agbɛ ashwã kotoku lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my leafy crops wilt and lose weight on the long journey to the market in Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛyaa jara nɔ yɛ Accra lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leafy crops lose moisture through tiny pores in their leaves after harvest. Sunlight, wind, and dry air speed up this water loss, causing leaves to shrink, wilt, and lose total weight.
ga: Tso baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Yɛ baai ni akpaa sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ, hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛtsiimɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why does the Adwera plant grow so fast and spread everywhere on my farm even during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Adwera tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa he fɛɛ he yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi po lɛ?

english: Adwera is a succulent plant with thick leaves that store water, allowing it to survive dry periods and quickly absorb soil nutrients and space before other crops can grow.
ga: Advera ji tso ko ni mli edɔ ni baai lɛ mli tse ni haa nu hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya dani tsei krokomɛi baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why did the new crop seeds brought by agricultural officers fail to yield well on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛba lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: New seed varieties often require specific soil nutrients, moisture levels, or planting depths to thrive; if local soil or rainfall conditions do not match these needs, the crop will struggle or fail.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui heei taoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Humidity level loo bɔ ni dumɔ nii lɛ mli kwɔ ha koni ekwɛ̃ Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ shihilɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ eshɛɛɛ taomɔ nii nɛɛ ahe Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ loo amɛbaafite.

english: Why do my produce spoil quickly if I harvest them early to sell to buyers who arrive early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ mra kɛji mikpa mra koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Immature crops have high water content and soft, thin outer skin that punctures easily, making them far more vulnerable to bruising and microbial decay than fully mature crops.
ga: Tsei ni edako lɛ yɛ nu babaoo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni anyɛɔ aboteɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa tsei nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛfiteɔ kɛ helai bibii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ fe tsei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weaker when I plant them on the same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil depth that crop uses, while allowing pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and fall off when the rains dry up for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni amɛgbi otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing and leaf dropping is a defensive mechanism where the plant sheds its leaves to reduce water loss and protect its stem and roots during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up the life cycle and breeding rate of insects, while heat-stressed plants have weaker natural defenses, making them easy targets for pests.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ashihilɛ kɛ amɛfɔmɔ yaa oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni dɔlɛ haa amɛnaa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of bushy green leaves but very few fruits or seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi aduawai loo dumɔwui akui fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages vegetative growth like leaves and stems, but prevents the plant from switching its energy to flower and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa, tamɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi, shi etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkatsake hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to keep its new top leaves growing, showing that it is time to feed your soil with fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the central funnel of the plant where it is cool and moist. They target this spot because the young leaves are tender, but catching them early prevents them from destroying the plant before it forms corn ears.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Amɛtuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ nɔ ejaakɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi ni ooomɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ fitemɔ naa dani efee ŋmãa toi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are too young to absorb water fast enough. Keeping shade trees protects young cocoa from burning up and helps the soil retain moisture during hot periods.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ otso lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaabu kookoo tso lɛ he koni ekashã, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start carrying heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches high up. Leaving too many suckers growing around the main trunk weakens the root support, so trimming extra suckers and using wooden props helps keep the tree upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse ni kɛlɛ. Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔle Tso titri lɛ he lɛ baaha shishifã lɛ sɛɛfimɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo ŋmeii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ, ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stem cuttings too close to each other on the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients underground, resulting in many thin, weak roots instead of thick, heavy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Yɛ ŋmeii shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of creeping on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight to build bigger tubers under the soil. It also keeps the leaves away from damp ground heat, which causes leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baa lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ he. ni ji nɔ ni kɛ baa hela baa lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the afternoon heat but stand up again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi te shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: On hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce water loss, and recovers automatically once temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ yiŋtoo ko shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni ebaatsa ehe kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when soil watering is uneven. High heat makes the pollen inside the flower useless, so keeping soil moist and shaded helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that drink water and steal soil nutrients much faster than your crops can. Even with good rain, weeds consume the crop's food first, leaving your plants starving.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya fe otsei lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi hu yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my dry chemical fertilizer when the farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it. Spreading fertilizer on dry soil under intense heat can actually burn and damage the roots instead of feeding the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni egbe amɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if a chemical or fertilizer sold in the market is genuine and safe for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Approved agrochemicals carry official registration labels and seals from regulatory bodies like the FDA or EPA. Fake products usually lack proper batch numbers, registration details, or clear usage instructions.
ga: Agrochemicals ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ okadi kɛ woloŋmaa he okadi ni jɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ FDA loo EPA dɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni afee lɛ amale lɛ bɛ batch nɔmba ni sa. Woloŋmaa he saji loo gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ he

english: What happens to my crops if I mix two different agrochemicals together before spraying?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ agrochemicals enyɔ futu mli dani mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals can cause a chemical reaction that burns crop leaves or cancels out their effectiveness. Unless product labels specifically state they can be mixed, each chemical should be applied separately.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko ni shãa tsei ahe baai loo ebaaha amɛhewalɛ aba shi. Ja nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ abaanyɛ akɛfutu mli. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofa fɛɛ tsofa atsu nii srɔtoi.

english: Why do my crops grow big green leaves but fail to produce good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni eŋɔli shi etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages lush leaf growth at the expense of fruits. Crops need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to form strong blossoms and heavy fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ daa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. Nɔ ni fata he ji fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii

english: How does burning my field before planting affect the way my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys the natural organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the soil. Over time, this makes the soil dry, hard, and lacking essential crop nutrients.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewa ni niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually signs of insect damage from tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies, or a viral infection spread by these insects while sucking sap from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies efite amɛ. loo helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients can cause tomato plants stress, leading them to drop their flowers to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii amɛshwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily in direct sun. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as temporary shade umbrellas while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from my last harvest produce weaker crops than certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from modern high-yield varieties lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation. Certified seeds are specially produced under strict standards to ensure uniform growth and strong yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ yɛ mlai ni mli wa shishi koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara be fɛɛ be ni amɛwo yibii ni mli wa.

english: Is it safe to harvest my cassava right after spraying weedkiller on the farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ afɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, crops absorb chemicals and need a mandatory waiting period after spraying to break them down. Harvesting too early leaves chemical residues in the food that can make consumers sick.
ga: Dabi, tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsofai amli ni amɛbiɔ be ni amɛmɛ beni afɔse tsofai lɛ amɛshwie shi lɛ sɛɛ koni tsofai lɛ akumɔ. Niyenii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni eshwɛɔ yɛ niyenii mli ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn mouldy even when stored in a dry barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni egbi mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize mould happens when grains are stored before they are fully dried to a safe moisture level. Residual moisture inside the cob creates an environment for fungus and toxins to spread.
ga: Abele mli ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmaa to dani egbi kwraa kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni ŋmei kɛ tsofai fɔji baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. Applying compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ eshishifã ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow better without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes expensive fertilizer off your field and away from root zones before crops can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain, or during light drizzling weather so nutrients sink into the ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. aloo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo koni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large forest trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct, hot sunlight. Keeping mature shade trees or planting plantains alongside new cocoa provides a humid, shaded canopy that protects young plants until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my plantain trees with dried grass instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dried plant leaves or grass—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool and moist during hot weeks, prevents weed growth, and gradually decays into natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ tso baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What causes small ragged holes and insect droppings in the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the leaf funnel during the day and chew tender leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying safe insecticides or neem tree extract into the plant funnel will control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baakudɔ tso lɛ.

english: When weather becomes extremely hot and dry, tomato plants get stressed and drop their blossoms to save moisture. Watering plants at the root early in the morning and providing light shade helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tomato tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni amɛbaafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa ni aha amɛ hulutsoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to cut when preparing to plant a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni mikɛsaa mihe kɛha shikpɔŋ hee ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Choose stems from healthy, high-yielding cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free of pests. Cut pieces from the strong, woody middle section of the main stem, as soft top stems rot easily and very old bottom stems sprout poorly.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ ashishifãi. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli wa ni tso yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋwɛi tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ oya ni shishigbɛ tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker should I dig up from an old farm to plant on my new field?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sucker esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad bulb base. They establish stronger roots and grow faster into high-yielding trees compared to 'water suckers' which have broad leaves and weak bulbs.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai lɛ mli tseee, tamɔ akpɔlɔi, ni amɛshishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ ni tamɔ bulbous. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ akɛto ‘Water Bud’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ yitsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I grow cassava continuously on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmei be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating cassava with legumes or letting the land fallow allows the soil to rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ ŋmãa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eha hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Alternating with crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains nearby creates living canopy protection that shields young seedlings until they grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to generate energy to produce big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to capture more light and prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni emɔ la babaoo ni ekɛtsi fungal hela naa.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow after I stick them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings will not grow if they are planted upside down or taken from dry, diseased stems. Always plant healthy cuttings with the buds pointing upward so roots and shoots can emerge correctly.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ edaŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi loo afo kɛjɛ tsei ni egbi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell, which warms up damp soil and bakes fragile seeds before they can establish roots. Waiting until the rainy season fully settles prevents seeds from drying out or rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ mli adɔ. ni egbiɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba shi kwraa koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi loo amɛkafite.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting during cooler periods helps flowers stay on the vine and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ yibii.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to capture water, sunlight, and soil food faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing the vital food your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: How can I stop insects from eating holes in my leafy vegetables without buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye bu ni yɔɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crushing leaves from neem trees, soaking them in water overnight, and spraying the liquid on your plants acts as a natural pest deterrent. The bitter taste keeps hungry insects away without hurting the plant.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ neem baai lɛ ni okɛwo nu mli nyɔɔŋ kome. No sɛɛ lɛ, nu lɛ ni oooshwie tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Nɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ he ni amɛyeee tso lɛ awui.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves during damp weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: White spots are usually fungal diseases that thrive in warm, humid air with poor air circulation. Spacing your plants further apart helps wind dry out the leaves and slows down the spread of fungus.
ga: White spot ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ mli. Tsei lɛ ni oootsi amɛhe lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: How do I choose which crops will give me good profits at the market instead of just feeding my family?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã miweku lɛ niyenii?

english: To make good money from farming, focus on high-demand cash crops like tomatoes, pepper, maize, or cassava. Look at what buyers in your local market are searching for and plan your planting time so your harvest comes out when supply is low and prices are high.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oná shika kpakpa kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama shika nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo, tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa nɔ. Kwɛmɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ taoɔ. ni oto be ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ Bɔni afee ni okpamɔ lɛ aba be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni jara hu yaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from the agrodealer instead of just saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ dɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i he dumɔwui nɛ ngɛ ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ yi wami.

english: Seeds saved from old harvests lose their strength over time and carry diseases easily. Certified seeds are specially tested to sprout faster, resist common pests, and yield bigger and healthier harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni ekɛ helai baa oya. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ekɛ nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main plant food in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, so adding fertilizer or compost around the roots gives the crop its green color and growth back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ, ni ji tsofa ko ni jɛɔ tso mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Shishifãi lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eda ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my piece of land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant cassava on it continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmei be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. Rotating your cassava with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally and refreshes the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-cassava lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving cassava enough space allows the roots to spread wide underground and grow into thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first. By the time the cassava needs full space, the maize is already harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa he ko ni eyi obɔ lɛ Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa lɛ agbɛnɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds when the rains start in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Do not plant with the very first rain, as the soil might still be too hot and dry underneath. Wait until you get two or three steady rains in a week so the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lolo ni egbi yɛ shishi. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding excess chemical fertilizer helps the plant keep its flowers to form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ajie tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are small caterpillars destroying the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves hiding in the funnel of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract keeps them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa tsei amli ŋmeii amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crop seedlings much faster than they harm older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ oya fe bɔ ni amɛtutuaa tsei ni edara lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have weak, short roots and tiny leaves, making them easy targets for weeds that steal their sunlight, water, and food. Once crops grow tall with large leaves, they shade out weeds naturally.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, kukuji kɛ baai bibii, ni no haa jwɛi ni juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ Amɛbaafee jwɛi lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I do not plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi lɛ? akɛ miduuu plantains yɛ emasɛi

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool and moist for the cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ he ni amɛshãa kwraa. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni kookoo lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build healthy green leaves and strong stalks; without it, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abɛi he miihia nitrogen babaoo koni ekɛfee baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops absorb nutrients from the ground every season. If you continuously plant on the same land without adding manure or fertilizer, or letting the land rest, the soil loses its fertility and produces weaker crops.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji oya nɔ odu tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwereɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi.

english: If I use chemical sprays to kill weeds on my field, will it poison the crops I want to harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ebaafee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni misumɔɔ ni makpa lɛ?

english: Selective chemical weedkillers only target weeds without harming specific crops like maize. However, using the wrong chemical or applying too much can damage crops and leave harmful residues, so correct chemical choice and proper dosage are essential.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ tsuɔ jwɛi pɛ he nii ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa awui. Shi kɛlɛ, tsofai ni ejaaa loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni sa kɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ halamɔ he miihia waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot if I leave them in the soil past their harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho kpamɔɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living storage organs. Once they reach maturity, leaving them in wet soil starves them of oxygen and exposes them to soil fungi, causing the starch inside the root to break down and decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso mli nibii ni kɛ wala yibii toɔ. Kɛ amɛdara kwraa lɛ Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa starch ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same land, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo béi baaba?

english: You can plant them together safely because they mature at different speeds. Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize has been harvested.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ amɛdaraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eyeɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sun exposure on their leaves to produce energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal rot and maximizing light exposure.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa kane lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by viruses carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early allows the new leaves to unfold properly and support pepper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ ajie amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni eda.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and ensuring good air circulation around the plants helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds when the rainy season starts late?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy, continuous rains. Planting after a single light rain risks seed failure if the dry weather returns before the roots establish.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ baafite kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba dani shishifãi lɛ je shishi.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure near the base helps restore leafy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you rotate or mix them with maize, they enrich the soil with natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa tsake loo okɛ ŋmãa futu mli lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly even though I apply fertilizer every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli daa be moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil is too acidic or lacks organic matter, plants cannot absorb nutrients effectively. Adding compost, crop residues, or agricultural lime helps improve soil health so fertilizers can work properly.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ loo ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and crinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap, or by a virus they carry. Spraying with organic neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides can help manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust in the plant center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Applying recommended pest treatments early in the morning or late evening targets the caterpillars effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Mulching your soil and keeping watering consistent helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary shade and keep the air humid, protecting the young cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong windstorms right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when bearing fruit. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden or bamboo fork prop prevents the tree from snapping under heavy winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni mli wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my yam mounds early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ato mra yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Weeds compete with young yam vines for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing them early ensures the yam plant has enough energy to build large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest so the roots do not become woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa lɛ, no lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeee tso?

english: Cassava is generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can carefully dig up one root to test; if it is firm, cooks soft, and is not overly fibrous or woody, the crop is ready.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu shishifã kome he nii ni oka kɛji eyɛ shiŋŋ, eyɛ mlɛo ni ebɛ tsɔne loo tso tsɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn brown and burn when there are no bigger shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under direct sunlight; planting tall shade trees or temporary crops like plantains protects them from excessive sun and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential mineral plants use to build healthy green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji mineral ko ni he hia ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains flooded my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy; when water covers the soil for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛmuɔ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop without forming fruit when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do I need to remove some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many shoots grow from the same plantain stool, they compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, which leads to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni jɛɔ plantain ŋmei kome mli lɛ miida lɛ, Ekɛ tsei ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha plantains lɛ aná ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do the leaves in the very middle of my maize plant look like they have holes eaten through them and ragged edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni etse lɛ?

english: This pattern of leaf damage is typical of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing point of the maize plant during the day to feed on the fresh inner leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ baai ni fiteɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ feɔ, ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does placing dried grass around the base of my crop plants help them stay green during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi awo he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material (mulch) blocks the sun's heat from reaching the soil, preventing water from evaporating quickly and keeping the roots cool and hydrated.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli (Mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of growing across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds yam vines up so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make plant food, while also keeping the leaves off the wet ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso lɛ nɔ koni ebaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Why are the top leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Tight upward leaf curling in tomatoes is usually a response to leaf-curl viruses carried by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, or a reaction to extreme heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji hetoo kɛha baai ni shwieɔ shi ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ, loo nɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa mli baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules, which enriches the soil with free nutrients when the plant roots break down.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai ni aheee nɔ ko be mli ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: If I notice one of my cassava plants has yellow, twisted leaves, should I remove it from the farm or leave it?
ga: Kɛji oyɔse akɛ ŋmei tso kome yɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mashi?

english: You should uproot and destroy the affected plant immediately far away from your farm. This stops Cassava Mosaic Disease from spreading through whiteflies to the rest of your healthy cassava plants.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ ni yɔɔ he ko ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmeii yɛji anɔ kɛya ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves get white spots and turn brown when the weather is very humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Humid weather encourages fungal diseases like maize leaf blight to grow. Fungus spores travel through moisture in the air and stick to wet leaves, causing brown patches and reducing growth.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ he hewalɛ. Fungal spores lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ ahe. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehaa dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I do not plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants fold upwards and wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves in extreme heat to slow down water loss through their pores. Giving them mulch around the base holds moisture in the soil and reduces this heat stress.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebaaha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures are too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly. Consistent watering and light shade can help the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents the bottom of the fruit from turning black and rotting.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ba daa lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ ni efite.

english: Why do my groundnut plants grow big leaves but have empty shells when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ baa agbo shi eshishifãi lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Empty pods happen when the soil lacks calcium during the time the plant forms its nuts underground. Adding calcium sources like agricultural lime or wood ash helps the pods fill out completely.
ga: Pods ni bɛ nɔ ko baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ calcium jɛɛhe tamɔ lime loo tso ashwishwɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ.

english: Why does adding too much chemical fertilizer make my crop leaves turn brown and look burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mitso lɛ mli lɛ haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ?

english: Excess fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil, which pulls water out of plant roots instead of feeding them. This dries out the leaves from the edges inward, making them look burnt.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ. ni haa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen from the topsoil and flood the root zone, preventing plants from absorbing food. Nitrogen gives leaves their rich green color, so without it, leaves turn pale yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse.

english: Why do weeds make my maize grow thin and produce smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha mi-abele lɛ miifee bibioo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds take those resources first, the maize plant lacks the energy needed to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha ŋwɛi, hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ jwɛi kɛ nakai nibii lɛ tsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ Abele bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know if a new maize seed variety will grow better on my farm than the old seeds I am used to buying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fe dumɔwui momo ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: New seed varieties are often bred to resist local diseases or handle dry spells better than older seeds. However, because soil and weather vary, it is best to test the new variety on a small patch of your field first to see how it performs before planting your whole farm with it.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui heei koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ loo amɛtsuɔ hulutsoo be he nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɛ srɔtoi. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni aka ŋmeii heei akwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko. yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii eha dani okɛdu oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Shade trees and food crops like plantains act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei kɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and grow. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the root zone or leaves the soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your plants properly gives each stalk enough space and food to grow strong and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot afternoon temperatures or dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the plant retain its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and get sticky during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves are caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or mealybugs that gather under the leaves to suck out the plant's juices. They multiply quickly in dry weather, so spraying early with neem water or recommended pest controls keeps them from weakening the crop.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ neem nu lɛ nɔ mra. Aloo, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkagbɔjɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and woody even though the plant leaves look big and healthy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ, shi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing big green leaves instead of feeding its underground tubers. Using balanced plant food with potassium encourages the crop to send nutrients down into building thick, starchy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji moŋ fe ni eeeha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso niyenii ni potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ amaje shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli tse ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground. As long as the plants stand back up in the cool evening, it is normal, but placing dry grass or mulch around the base helps keep the soil moist and cool longer.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ damɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, no lɛ ehi. Shi kɛ akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo The base lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my cowpea seeds failing to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep for the shoot to reach the surface, or if soil insects eat them. Buying certified seed stock and planting at the recommended depth ensures most seeds will sprout successfully.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli he ni ooohe ni odu yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ eshɛɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui babaoo akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds I save from my own harvest get damaged by insects in storage, while new packaged seeds stay clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui heei ni awo mli lɛ he tseɔ.

english: Packaged seeds from agro-dealers are thoroughly dried and often treated with safe protective coatings before sealing. Saved grains often carry invisible insect eggs from the field, so they must be completely dried and stored in airtight bags or containers to keep insects out.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni awo mli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ egbiɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni bei pii lɛ, akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe woɔ mli dani akɛtswaa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni ato lɛ woɔ kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ afɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi kwraa ni akɛto kotoku loo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take so many years before I can harvest any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ekpaa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that spends its first few years building a strong root system and trunk before it has enough energy to produce flowers and grow pods.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo dani etswaa shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi ni wa. dani enáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: How can I earn money from my land while I wait for my young cocoa trees to grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can plant fast-growing food crops like maize, cassava, or plantains between your young cocoa trees to give you food and quick income during the early years.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo plantains yɛ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ koni eha niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water very quickly in direct heat, so they need shade from larger plants to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops much more than my mature trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awui babaoo fe mitsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and leaves, so fast-growing weeds easily steal their sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before the young plants can establish themselves.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ aju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mlɛo dani tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off some branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji komɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or excess branches so the tree can focus its energy on growing healthy pods, while also allowing air and sunlight inside to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba mli koni tsɛŋemɔ hela akabote mli.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest on my land?
ga: Ani tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close forces the trees to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, which results in weaker trees and smaller overall harvests.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni anáa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my crops give a good harvest in the first year but produce less in the years after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops feed on nutrients in the soil every season, so if you do not replenish the earth with fertilizer or organic matter, the soil loses its richness and produces smaller yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa be. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi, ni ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but only a few turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they lack sufficient water or nutrients, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms before they can set into healthy pods.
