ga: Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ehe. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii Tutua fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, overly wet weather, especially when the farm is overcrowded and shaded too heavily.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔji lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why has my old cocoa farm stopped producing as many pods as it did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ kpa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo feemɔ tamɔ bɔ ni efee afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As tree crops age, their natural ability to produce fruit slows down, and old soil becomes worn out, meaning the farm needs pruning, soil treatment, or gradual replanting.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii lɛ baa shi. ni shikpɔŋ momo lɛ baafite Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afo ŋmɔji lɛ amli fiofio, akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to trim away some of the upper branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Trimming cocoa branches allows air and sunlight to pass through the tree canopy. This keeps the farm dry enough to prevent fungal diseases like black pod while encouraging the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Kookoo niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ hɔɔŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji anaa, yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hu hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can restore healthy plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same land continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize improves the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil and help the maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛye amɛbua ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When rain creates standing water around the plants, it smothers the roots and creates conditions for soil fungi to cause root decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu haa nu damɔɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ he, ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my young vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from drying out quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil moist helps flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and remaining tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by small insects like whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the plant from getting stunted and failing to produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehe hia ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee shwilafo ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete with each other for light, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small cobs rather than a healthy, full harvest.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ emuu ni mli wa lɛ

english: If I bury my crop seeds deep in the soil, will they grow bigger and stronger?
ga: Kɛ mifu mi yibii lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ani dumɔwui lɛ baafee wuji ni amɛhe wa?

english: Burying seeds too deep starves them of air and light, causing them to rot under the dirt before they can push through the surface. Seeds should only be planted at a shallow depth—usually twice their size—so they can easily sprout and reach the sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ pɛ. (bei pii lɛ, elɛɛmɔ ji shii enyɔ) koni eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my pepper crops very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in tall, weak plants that produce very small peppers. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and bear plenty of fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa nu he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why did the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout well this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests can lose their strength or carry diseases if they are not dried and stored under strict conditions. Buying certified seeds from a recognized agricultural distributor guarantees high germination rates and protects your field from seed-borne diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ loo ekɛ hela aba kɛji akɛ agbiko ni akɛtoko yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa amli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ooohe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni ale lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaabu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living canopy that protects the young trees until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop roots with dried grass or plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass—known as mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating in the heat. As the dry leaves rot over time, they also break down into rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni egbi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Baai lɛ hu fiteɔ, ni ehaa niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo baa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to grow healthy leaves. Applying well-rotted animal manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer feeds the soil and helps the leaves turn back to a deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eye ebua baabii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching prevents heat shock, allowing the flowers to stay on the plant and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo akafee nɔ ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Will letting weeds grow among my crops really hurt my harvest if I water the field well?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni maŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ nu wo ŋmɔji lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your plants' roots. Clearing weeds regularly ensures all the goodness in your soil goes straight into making your crops grow big and yield well.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I test if my soil has enough water for my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can test soil moisture by digging a few inches down into the root zone and squeezing a handful of soil into a ball. If the soil holds its shape without dripping wet water, it has good moisture; if it crumbles away into dry dust, your crops need immediate watering.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ okwɛ kɛtsɔ 2-3 inches ni ooofo kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ko ni ooofee bɔɔlu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ bɛ mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa. Kɛji etsɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo onibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are fully ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack. Harvesting at this time ensures the tubers are firm, full of starch, and not watery.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ, efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi bɔi fãmɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha bulbs lɛ afee shiŋŋ. Eyi kɛ starch ni nu bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Keeping some tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture so the young plants can survive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Shade loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha shade aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I measure the space between my seed holes instead of planting as many seeds as possible close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ ni kã dumɔwui akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough food and air to produce a large, healthy harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds around their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mishiɔ jwɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil nutrients they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts alongside my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for your maize while giving you two different food crops from the same land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ekɛ niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ he kome lɛ haa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge stems and leaf branches but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ tso agbo kɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai, shi ŋmei bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or excessive water, the plant spends all its energy growing upper leaves instead of roots. Balanced soil management helps the cassava store energy down in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo nu babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by fall armyworms hiding deep in the plant whorl. Applying targeted organic remedies or recommended insecticides early in the morning helps control them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, asraafoi a-armyworms ni egbee shi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to cut off lower branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the farm canopy. This reduces humidity inside the farm, preventing damp diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Tsoi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Tsi helai ni mli edɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil cool with organic mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from insects when I store it in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli?

english: Insects like weevils thrive in damp, unsealed environments. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until it is hard, then storing it in sealed, airtight bags starves pests of oxygen and keeps the grain safe for months.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni nɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ No sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and easily scorched by strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field before maize make the maize grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it uses that stored nitrogen to grow strong and dark green.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they fight over water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce a single, large bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo dara yɛ tso kome he lɛ Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ yibii agbo kome.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop plants with dried palm leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he? Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ewo mli?

english: Covering the ground, or mulching, protects the soil from direct sun rays. This stops water from evaporating quickly, keeps the crop roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching loo mulching buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akafee lasu oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these tiny bugs early stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ virusi ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaakpa curling lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips in a V-shape mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its deep green color.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ V su mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put tall bamboo sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by catching sunlight with their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves high into the light and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases can easily rot them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ ŋmɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaa amɛyaaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgboi oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of protecting itself from drying out. Leaves lose a lot of water to hot air, so shedding them helps the plant conserve moisture inside its stems and roots until rain returns.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ŋmei he koni ekagbi. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu babaoo kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot or the soil gets too dry. High temperatures prevent pollination from taking place, causing the plant to shed unpollinated flowers to save water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei akawo fɔfɔi amli pollen koni nu akafite.

english: Why is it better to grow sweet potatoes on raised mounds rather than flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ hi fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds create soft, loose soil where root tubers can expand easily without fighting hard earth. Mounds also keep excess rainwater draining away so the tuber roots do not rot.
ga: Gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akpee. Gɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tuber lɛ shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my crops growing much shorter and weaker now than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida kuku kwraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ fe bɔ ni amɛji afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Crops rely heavily on food nutrients hidden in the soil to grow tall and strong. Over time, continuous farming without adding manure or fertilizer wears out the soil, leaving crops hungry and unable to grow properly.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ waa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops look much greener and healthier than mine on the same land area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ hewalɛ fe minɔ̃ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Deep green leaves show that crops are getting enough nourishment, especially nitrogen, from well-cared-for soil. When farmers nourish their soil with organic manure or balanced fertilizers, their crops grow faster and greener.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli Beni okwaafoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni esaaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the crop is starving due to a lack of nutrients in tired soil, or that the soil is too dry. When soil loses its nutrients, plants cannot produce the green color needed to feed themselves.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the daytime heat even when the soil feels a bit damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ?

english: When soil gets worn out and hard, crop roots stay shallow and weak. Shallow roots cannot draw up enough water to protect the plant from hot sunshine, causing the leaves to drop and wilt.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ewa Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What makes my cassava tubers stay tiny even after staying in the ground for over a year?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nɔ ni fe afi ni mikɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, fertile soil full of nutrients to swell into big tubers. If the soil has lost its nutrients and become hard, the plant cannot store enough food underground to grow large roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baa nii ni niyenii kpakpai eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fiteɔ ni ewa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ato niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná shishifãi wuji.

english: Why are my vegetable plants dropping their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Crops drop their flowers when they are stressed by poor soil conditions. If the soil lacks minerals like phosphorus, the plant saves its remaining strength to stay alive rather than spending energy making fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ minerals tamɔ phosphorus Tso lɛ baahiɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli koni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why are my crops taking so much longer to mature and be ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: When soil fertility drops, crops spend a lot of time struggling to gather basic nutrients instead of growing quickly. Good soil nutrients speed up crop growth so you can harvest early.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ba shi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite amɛbe babaoo ni amɛkɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbua niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ anaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ oya. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni onyɛ okpa oya.

english: How does putting animal manure in the soil change the way my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloo ŋmei ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients and organic matter, keeping it soft and moist. This allows plant roots to spread easily, absorb food, and grow strong stems with heavy harvests.
ga: Koolooi aŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo, amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow so much better when I let my land rest for a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ miha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe be fioo ko lɛ?

english: Leaving soil to rest, or fallow, allows wild plants and leaf litter to decompose naturally. This process naturally restores nutrients and organic matter back into the soil, giving your next crops fresh food to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ koni ehi shi loo efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koo mli tsei kɛ baai amli jwɛi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛ niyenii hee.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more easily now than they did in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Just like people get sick when they don't eat well, crops grown in poor, degraded soil have weak defense systems. Healthy crops grown in rich soil can naturally fight off pest attacks and diseases better.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi hela mɔ amɛ kɛ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite ni ehiii nɔ lɛ bɛ hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii anɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much continuous rain on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them, and waterlogged soil starves the roots of the air they need to absorb food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aye hɔmɔ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm field make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, leaving natural plant food behind for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop plants with dry leaves during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry leaf mulch acts like a blanket that traps soil moisture, keeps root areas cool, and stops the harsh dry winds from baking the earth hard.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly and stop the plant from producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaaa miwo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which spread plant viruses and drain the plant's food supply, preventing fruit formation.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli ni ehaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ hoɔ. Koni akɛtsi yibiiwoo naa

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water stays trapped in heavy soil for too long, creating conditions for harmful fungus to attack the roots and destroy them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atutua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do caterpillars gather inside the deep center where new leaves are growing on my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ he ni baai heei miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide inside the central leaf funnel because the young leaves inside are soft, sweet, and shaded from hot sunlight and heavy rainfall.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Ejaakɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni amɛhaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he hɔɔŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear away all the plantain trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie dumɔwui fɛɛ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate foliage that burns easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing plantain leaves act as living umbrellas providing vital shade and cool air.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo, ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing at the bottom of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree grows large bunches.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the leaves to capture maximum sunlight for leaf food production while protecting the foliage from fungal diseases that thrive on damp soil.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni emɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha baa niyenii feemɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without turning into tomatoes when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making them sterile so they fall off because the plant cannot form seeds or fruit without fertilization.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. sterility No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui loo aduawai kɛji akɛ ekɛ fɔmɔ nii wooo mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food that keeps leaves green and healthy. It can also happen when too much rain washes nutrients away or drowns the roots, preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji tso niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark black spots at the bottom before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is growing. Irregular watering makes it worse because the plant needs steady soil moisture to carry calcium from the soil into the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ haa enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa ejaakɛ tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛná calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and roll inward during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during hot afternoons to shield themselves from excessive heat and stop water from evaporating too fast. However, if the leaves stay curled even in the cool morning, it is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking juices from the leaf undersides.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he, ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping maize and cassava allows you to maximize your farmland. Maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, while cassava grows slowly underneath and takes over the field after the maize is harvested, giving you two crops from one land area without them fighting for light early on.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ haa onáa shikpɔŋ ni obaanyɛ odu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Beni ŋmãa lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishi ni eŋɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ kɛha la mra.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seed yams too close to each other in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need space and lots of soil nutrients to grow big. If you plant them too close together, their underground roots will compete for food and water, which results in many small, thin tubers instead of large, valuable yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia he ko babaoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛji odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni jara wa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants need wooden sticks to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei ni amɛkɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Climbing bean varieties have weak stems that cannot support heavy pods on their own. Giving them sticks helps them grow upward toward sunlight, keeps the leaves and pods off the damp soil, and prevents diseases caused by mud and rot.
ga: Climbing bean henɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ tsei niji lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulu la mli. Buu baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. ni atsĩ helai ni sũ kɛ ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support, dropping the extras to save energy. However, heavy flower drop happens when the tree is stressed by dry Harmattan winds, lack of soil water, or attacks from insects like mirids.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Ekɛ fɔfɔi krokomɛi nɛɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, nu ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ tamɔ atatu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the growing leaf funnels of my young maize during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which attack the central growing tip of the maize plant because it is tender, sweet, and full of water. They hide deep inside the leaf whorl to stay safe from heavy rain, birds, and sprays while eating your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmeii ni miida yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná shweshweeshwe shihilɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, okpoi, kɛ shwiemɔ he beni amɛyeɔ onibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil has lost its power to grow good crops before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ dani adu?

english: If previous crops grew very slowly, turned pale green, or produced small yields, your soil is weak. You can also tell by looking at wild weeds—if weeds on the uncultivated land look stunt and yellow, the soil lacks the organic manure or nutrients your crops will need.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo Etsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ koo mli jwɛi ni oookwɛ lɛ hu nɔ. Kɛji jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark brown and rotting just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled from the ground, the root loses its connection to water and reacts quickly with air, causing a natural breakdown. Unlike yams, cassava has no protective skin, so it must be processed, eaten, or kept buried in damp sawdust within two to three days of harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome. ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ baa Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava bɛ ŋmei ni buɔ ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu he nii, aye, loo afu amɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli efɔ mli yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is ready for harvest or if I need to wait a few more weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa loo esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi krokomɛi?

english: Maize is mature when the silk on the cob turns dark brown and dry, and the leaves turn yellowish-brown. If you press a kernel with your fingernail and a clear or firm starch comes out instead of milky liquid, the maize is ready for harvesting.
ga: Abele lɛ eda kɛji siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ nyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse je kpo yɛ nu ni tamɔ mliki najiaŋ lɛ. Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How many months after planting can I expect my yams to be mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ? Ani manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ baagbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Most yam varieties in Ghana take between 6 to 9 months to mature after planting. You will know they are ready when the leaves and vines naturally dry up and turn yellow.
ga: Ghana ŋmeii babaoo heɔ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 dani amɛshwereɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ amɛfee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Plantains require direct sunlight to grow strong stems and produce heavy bunches. Dense shade from big trees limits sunlight and creates competition for soil nutrients, slowing down plantain growth.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii. Tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo ni mli wa lɛ haaa hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ. ni ekɛ akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by fungal or bacterial root diseases brought on by poor drainage. When water sits around the roots for too long, the roots drown, rot, and can no longer pump water to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛpomp nu kɛya baai lɛ amli dɔŋŋ.

english: Is it good for my crop yield if I grow beans together on the same land with maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil for the maize, while the tall maize stalks give climbing bean vines a structure to grow on.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha ŋmãa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ naa gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ.

english: Planting cassava repeatedly on the same plot drains essential nutrients from the soil and allows cassava-specific pests and diseases to build up, leading to smaller yields over time.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmei he pɔtɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my groundnut farm early in the first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut seedlings grow slowly at first and cannot easily compete with aggressive weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Early weeding allows the young crop to establish strong roots.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abɔ he akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the central whorl. Identifying this early allows you to control the pest before it damages the main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Enɛ ni oooyɔse mra Ehaa onyɛɔ oyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ hei titri ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my pepper plants after transplanting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ awo mli beni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Apply the first batch of fertilizer about 2 to 3 weeks after transplanting once the roots have settled, and a second batch when the plants begin flowering to encourage abundant fruit production.
ga: Okɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ afata he beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do I see so many new pests on my maize farm these days compared to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa tsɛŋemɔ helai heei lɛ? Nibii babaoo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɛnɛ kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe.

english: Pest populations increase over time due to changing weather patterns, planting the same crop continuously without resting the soil, and pests slowly building resistance to older chemical treatments.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafee tsofai momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe hewalɛ fiofio.

english: What causes the leaves of my young corn plants to have small holes and look chewed from the inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni okwɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ mli?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm or stem borers, which hide inside the central leaf funnel (the whorl) and eat the soft growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm loo stem borers lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei (ring) lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baa bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: At what stage of growth is my corn crop most at risk of being destroyed by pests?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli mi ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai?

english: Corn is most vulnerable during the early seedling stage when young leaves are tender, and again during the tasseling and cob-formation stages when pests feed on the developing ears.
ga: Abele ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishijee be mli beni baai bibii lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ cob feemɔ be mli beni kooloi ni yeɔ toi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plant is damaged by insects or suffering from a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ efite loo eyɛ tso hela ko?

english: Insects usually leave physical signs like bitten leaves, holes, or chewed stems, whereas plant diseases often show as yellowing leaves, spots, wilting, or rotted stems without visible chewing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ baai ni akɔmɔ, bu, loo tsei ni akɔmɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jieɔ amɛhe kpo akɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni anaaa ni amɛyeɔ.

english: How do I know the correct amount of pest medicine to spray on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni esa akɛ mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ falɛ ni sa?

english: Using too little pest medicine will fail to kill the insects, while using too much can burn your crop leaves; you should always use the exact measuring cap or container recommended by an extension officer or product label.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ egbeŋ kooloi lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso baai ashã lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii taakɛ nibii lɛ ahe adafitswaa najiaŋdamɔlɔ loo niŋmaa lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ.

english: If I spray my crop medicine and the insects disappear, why do they often come back after a short time?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni kooloi lɛ laajeɔ. Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pesticides often kill visible adult insects, but eggs buried inside stems or leaves can hatch later, or new pests can fly over from nearby farms if protection is not maintained.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda ni anaa lɛ. Shi wɔji ni akɛwoɔ tsei loo baai amli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sɛɛ mli. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela hee ko baanyɛ ajɛ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli aba kɛji abuuu he.

english: Is it better for me to spray my crop medicine early in the morning or in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ tsei anɔ leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when the weather is cooler, as heavy afternoon heat evaporates the medicine quickly and can burn crop leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ atsɔ oya ni eha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã.

english: Is it safe for me to harvest and eat my crops immediately after applying pest medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni maye amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii?

english: No, every crop medicine has a safe waiting period (pre-harvest interval) ranging from a few days to several weeks to allow the chemical to break down so the food is safe to eat.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni sa ni amɛkɛbaamɛ. Eheɔ he fɛɛ he kɛjɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashiɔ otsii babaoo dani akpaa ŋmaa lɛ dani tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ koni niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do pests attack weak plants in my farm more than the healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy, well-fed plants produce strong plant tissues and natural chemicals that discourage insects, while weak or water-stressed plants cannot defend themselves and attract hungry pests.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ jieɔ tso mli fãji ni mli wa kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni egbɔjɔ loo nu efo amɛhe lɛ nyɛɛɛ abu amɛhe ni amɛgbala kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Can changing the types of crops I plant each season help reduce pest attacks on my land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, alternating crops like corn with legumes breaks the food supply of specific pests, preventing pest populations from building up in the soil year after year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Baafite niyenii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi jɛɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ naa koni amɛkabu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do I need to raise the roof of my nursery shed higher instead of leaving it low to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ greenhouse lɛ yiteŋ moŋ fe ni mashi lɛ shi kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If a nursery shade is built too low, hot air and moisture get trapped right above the young plants. Raising the roof allows fresh air to circulate, keeping the temperature cool so fragile seedlings do not suffocate or burn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee hulutsoo lɛ shi tsɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baatsi tso bibioo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ awó tsũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. cool down temperature Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo loo amɛkashã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need a shade cover built over them in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa he ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out quickly under direct heat. A shade cover acts like an umbrella, filtering strong sunlight and protecting the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Hulu lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Efoɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I tell if the shade roof over my nursery plants is blocking too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi hulu la babaoo naa?

english: When crops get too little light under a low or thick shade cover, they grow tall, thin, and pale as they stretch toward the sky searching for light. Removing some cover or raising the structure helps them grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná la fioo ko pɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi loo ni mli wa shishi lɛ, Tsei lɛ daraa, amɛhe feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shĩa lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mli loo awo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings rot and die when heavy rain pools around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it chokes the roots, causing them to rot and killing the whole plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings collapse at the stem when I give them too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu babaoo ha amɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive water creates a damp environment where soil fungi thrive. These fungi attack the tender stems at the ground level, causing the plant to rot and fall over, a problem known as damping-off.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni sũ mli ŋmeii baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ tutuaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei fiteɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Enɛ ji naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ damping.

english: Why is it recommended to cover nursery beds with dry grass right after sowing small seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui bibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Covering the seedbed with grass shields the light soil from heavy raindrops that can wash away seeds or create a hard soil crust that prevents young shoots from coming up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ha dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni waaa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he, ni baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ loo efee shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why must I cover my cocoa beans with tarpaulins immediately when it starts to rain on the drying floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tarp haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ pɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans must stay completely dry to cure properly. Rainwater restarts moisture accumulation, causing dangerous black mold to grow, which ruins the beans and lowers their sale price.
ga: Gbimɔ: Esa akɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa koni etsa jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ abua ehe naa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ shwereɔ. Enɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ ni ebaaha jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What happens to my harvested maize if rain gets onto the grains while they are drying outside?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When water touches drying maize, it makes the grains absorb moisture again. This leads to mold growth, sprouting, and insect infestation, making the crop unsafe to eat or store.
ga: Kɛ́ nu tswa ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa, amɛshwereɔ ni ŋmeii baa amɛnɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ loo akɛtoɔ.

english: Why should I keep my harvested yam tubers inside a dry, covered shed instead of leaving them out in the open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ato tsũ ko ni egbi ni aha nɔ lɛ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ

english: Direct rain and sun damage yam skin and allow bacteria to enter. Storing tubers in a dry, covered structure protects them from water rot and keeps them fresh for months.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ sweet potato hewolo lɛ ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ bulb lɛ to he ko ni egbi ni aha nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu akafite, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to put a waterproof cover over our compost heaps during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mama ni nu nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away the valuable nutrients that break down inside the compost pile. Covering the heap ensures water does not carry away the goodness before you can put it on your farm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ lɛ eyaaa dani okɛwo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What does it actually mean if someone says my crop produce is organic?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ mi-nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli?

english: Organic produce means crops grown naturally using compost, animal manure, and natural pest control methods, without relying on synthetic fertilizers, weedicides, or harsh chemical sprays.
ga: Organic produce tsɔɔ tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛi tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni mli wa nɔ

english: Will spraying a little chemical on my sick crops mean my whole farm is no longer organic?
ga: Ani tsofai fioo komɛi ni mikɛbaafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efeŋ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli dɔŋŋ?

english: Using chemical sprays like fungicides to treat specific problem areas helps save your yield, but those treated crops cannot be sold as strictly organic. Your farm remains largely natural, but the specific chemical-treated produce loses its certified organic status.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ, tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii, tsuɔ nii kɛtsaa hei ni naagbai yɔɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite. Shi anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ nakai tsei ni atsa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ akɛ nɔ ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ kã he eji adebɔɔ nɔ babaoo. Shi nibii ni akɛ tsofai etsu nii lɛ laajeɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔɔ akɛ amɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I use natural manure for my soil if I occasionally use chemical sprays for crop diseases?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe helai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ bei komɛi amli

english: Yes, combining natural manure to build healthy soil with targeted chemical sprays only when severe disease breaks out is a smart approach called Integrated Pest Management. It keeps your soil fertile while protecting your income.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he koni akɛma shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ pɛ kɛji hela ni naa wa ba lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋaa ni ale lɛ akɛ integrated pest management. Eyeɔ ebuaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shika ni onáa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves start developing black or white spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa ŋmeii diji loo eyɛŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those spots are usually caused by fungal diseases. Fungi thrive in cold, wet, and humid weather, spreading rapidly across wet leaves and causing them to spot, yellow, or rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ baa. Fuŋ lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni edɔ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. ni ofee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my fruits look healthy at first but start rotting on the stem right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ shishijee mli shi amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: As plants grow dense with leaves, moisture gets trapped around the growing fruits. Fungal spores sitting quietly on the plant react to this wetness and cause the fruit to rot before it fully ripens.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da ni ehiɛ baai lɛ Moisture baakpɛtɛ ehe. aduawai ni miida Fungal spores ni fĩɔ shi dioo Tsei lɛ baahere nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ nɔ. ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ dani etsuɔ ​​jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I tell if my sick crop is damaged by insects or by a fungal disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii helai efite miŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves clear physical signs like holes in leaves or chewed stems. Fungal diseases usually show up as discolored spots, powdery coatings, dark patches, or wilting without any visible bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ bu yɛ baai amli loo tsei ni atsɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsake, nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ bɛ mli.

english: What does a fungicide actually do when I apply it to my sick crops?
ga: Mɛni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: A fungicide is a targeted medicine that kills or stops the growth of parasitic fungi causing diseases on your plants, allowing the crops to recover and protecting healthy leaves from getting infected.
ga: Fungicides ji tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni baagbe loo ebaakpa parasitic fungi ni kɛ hela baa otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ adalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe.

english: When is the best time to apply fungicide so I do not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii baatsu nii koni akafite shika?

english: Apply fungicide at the very first sign of disease spots or right before heavy rains begin. Waiting until the entire farm is rotting makes the chemical far less effective and wastes your money.
ga: Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ hela he okadi loo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaafite oshika.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying fungicide before I can harvest my crops to sell?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ?

english: Every fungicide has a waiting period called a pre-harvest interval, usually written on the container (often 7 to 14 days). You must wait this full time so the chemical breaks down and the food is safe for consumers.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni amɛkɛmɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani akpaa ŋmaa. Bei pii lɛ, aŋmaa enɛ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ nɔ (bei pii lɛ, gbii 7 kɛyashi 14). Esa akɛ omɛ be fɛɛ be ni tsofai lɛ afite ni niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ.

english: Can I prevent fungal diseases on my farm without buying chemical sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsi fungal hela naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miheee tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, by spacing your crops properly to let air flow through, clearing weeds regularly, using disease-resistant seeds, and removing infected plant parts early, you can prevent most fungal problems naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Kɛ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii. ni ojie tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Obaanyɛ otsi ŋmɔtɔ he naagbai babaoo anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is the difference between traditional seeds and the improved crop seeds people talk about?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ blema dumɔwui kɛ tsei dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni gbɔmɛi wieɔ he lɛ ateŋ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to withstand local pests, diseases, and dry spells while producing significantly higher yields per acre compared to traditional seeds saved from past harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii babaoo kwraa yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Why do some crop varieties perform well in one season but yield poorly in the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ko mli shi amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties react differently to weather changes like rainfall timing and heat; some varieties are designed for early rains while others handle mid-season drought better.
ga: Tsei henɔi srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli, tamɔ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ dɔlɛ. Afee srɔtoi lɛ ekomɛi kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, an essential nutrient plants need to produce chlorophyll and build strong stems and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee klorofil ni amɛfee tsei kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Will planting my seeds closer together help me get a bigger total harvest from my land?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ he lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller overall yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ejieɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct harsh sunlight and need temporary shade from larger trees or food crops like plantain to protect their leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. ni ehe miihia ni tsei wuji loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop plants to grow so slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your plants during their critical early growth stages.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otso lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are insects attacking my crops early in the season before the plants even flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be lɛ mli mra, dani tsei lɛ po fɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young leaves and fresh stems are soft and rich in sap, making them an easy, nutrient-dense food source for pests multiplying at the start of the rainy season.
ga: Baai bibii kɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull it from the ground, causing the plant to temporarily wilt to protect itself from drying out.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ agbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: How can improved farming techniques help me get more harvest without buying more land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli he ŋaai ni etee hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpã nii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: Using correct plant spacing, balanced fertilization, and high-yielding seeds allows each individual plant to reach its maximum potential on the land you already own.
ga: Kɛtsɔ Gbɛ ni Ja ni Akɛto Tsei Ateŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja Kɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni eshɛɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ momo lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves lose water too quickly. Providing shade plants like plantains or Gliricidia protects them from heat stress until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains loo glicidia ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to feed newer ones, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted compost helps keep the whole plant green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai heei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water in the soil to dissolve so the crop roots can drink it in. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn plant roots and waste the fertilizer since the plant cannot absorb dry chemicals.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wu nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni egbi lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way I point the buds when I plant cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji lɛ, ani gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, the tiny buds on the cassava stem cutting must always point upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle and bend awkwardly to grow upward, which weakens the plant and yields smaller cassava roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ yucca tso nine lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ koni ekwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a very common pest in Ghana. They hide deep inside the leaves at the center of the plant, requiring early treatment with suitable bio-pesticides or recommended sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ amɛ tee baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Esa akɛ atsa lɛ mra. kɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and planting virus-resistant seeds helps protect the tomato plants from getting damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Control Ni dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tomato tsei ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: When too many shoots grow from one plantain root, they fight with the main stem for water, light, and soil food. Leaving only 2 or 3 strong suckers leaves enough food for the mother plant to yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo jɛ plantain shishifã kome mli lɛ Ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ wuɔ koni ena nu, la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: How does covering the ground with dry grass help my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mi-vegetables lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, shielding the ground from hot direct sunlight to prevent soil water from evaporating quickly. It keeps the soil cool and slowly breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akatsɔ oya. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni fiofio lɛ Efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam vines for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Vine ŋmɔtɔ ni haa amɛkwɔɔ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves into the air where they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the plant make leaves green and feed the growing tuber underground, resulting in much bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai eŋɔli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for next season's maize?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?
