english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly microbes in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting maize after legumes allows the maize to feed on this natural soil food.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ haa abele lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning at the edges during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily when exposed to direct sunlight without shade crops like plantain or banana trees, which act as living umbrellas to keep the young plants cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei bɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade koni eha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ Harmatta hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve water, allowing the crop to stay alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants rot at the bottom when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nubu lɛ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water around cabbage stems starves the roots of air, allowing harmful water-loving soil bacteria to attack and rot the base of the plant.
ga: nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Kaabaji tsei babaoo tsɔ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my maize grow thin and tall without producing big cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli tse ni ekwɛɔ ni ebɛ toi wuji beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too closely, the stalks fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to grow weak and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraaa waa, ni dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu baa. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the ground, allowing them to absorb the very first rainfall faster than newly planted seeds and take over the land.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ nɔ, ni no haa amɛmɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of growing along the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni akɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eda lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight for growth while keeping the leaves off the damp soil where mold and fungal rot spread.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara yɛ be mli ni ehaa baai lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of key soil nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid weather when tree branches are too overcrowded to let sunlight and air pass through.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ́ tso niji lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off the lowest leaves of my tomato plants as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ be mli ni tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Pruning lower tomato leaves prevents rain from splashing soil-borne fungal diseases onto the leaves, keeping the main plant clean and healthy.
ga: O-tomato lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ akagbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ashwã baai lɛ anɔ. Ha tomato tso titri lɛ he atse ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my mango tree produce a huge harvest one year but very few fruits the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli, shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Producing a heavy crop consumes almost all of the tree's stored nutrients, forcing it to rest and produce fewer fruits the following year while it rebuilds energy.
ga: Nibii ni tsii ni anáa lɛ biɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ eto lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni ewo yibii fioo yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither when I clear all the big shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight because their delicate leaves dry out quickly. Shade trees shield young cocoa from extreme heat, keep the air humid, and protect the soil from losing moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni elaaje lɛ he.

english: Why does my plantain stalk die after bearing just one batch of fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo yibii kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and produce fruit only once. After harvesting, that main stem dies back naturally while transferring its remaining nutrients to the small sucker shoots growing around its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Tso titri lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ

english: Yam plants store energy in tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to capture maximum sunlight, prevents diseases from wet ground, and yields larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ bulbs lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Tsi hela naa kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni oha yitso agbo

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ edara kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ baai lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the growing center of young maize plants. They feed on leaves before the plant forms ears, which can severely stunt or kill the crop if left untreated.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ anɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani tsei lɛ woɔ toi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee mlɛo loo efite kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread viruses. As they feed on the underside of leaves, they drain nutrients and cause the leaf to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. be mli ni eyeɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive humidity. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy rather than trying to form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow on the bottom leaves while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green and healthy; when soil lacks it, the plant steals nitrogen from older bottom leaves to nourish new top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwie shi lɛ, tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas before maize help my next maize harvest grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with beneficial soil microbes to pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant dies, this trapped nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ amɛwo shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable stems with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai tsei ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that shades the soil from the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking root.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekawo shishifãi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves available nitrogen to newer top leaves, leaving the older bottom leaves starved and yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Shi shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni hɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔŋ aye amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and woody even though the leaves look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛji ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my young rice leaves turn reddish-brown and look stunted in flooded fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai lɛ miitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Reddish-brown leaves in flooded rice fields often point to iron toxicity, which happens when poor water drainage causes excess soluble iron to build up around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dade yɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ha dade ni mli tse ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites, thrips, or aphids, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but fail to form pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Insect pests like flower thrips or pod borers often attack and feed on the flower buds before they can develop into mature cowpea pods.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips loo pod borers. Bei pii lɛ, amɛtutuaa ni amɛyeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani amɛfeɔ tsina ŋmeii ni eda.

english: Why are my plantain stalks snapping and falling over easily during mild winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni waaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over easily when pests like root nematodes or banana stem weevils eat away the underground roots and corm, weakening the plant's hold in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo banana ŋmeii ye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes develop dark, sunken rotten spots at the bottom while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ yɛ hei ni egboi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni edaa lolo lɛ?

english: This is Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering or very dry soil conditions.
ga: Enɛ ji Blossom End Rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What makes the healthy green pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Clearing weeds and pruning trees helps air flow to dry out the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi mli kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown long before the harvest season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is commonly caused by Yam Anthracnose fungal disease or underground root-knot nematodes damaging the moisture flow from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato anthracnose loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my garden egg leaves and cause them to drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: White powdery spots are caused by Powdery Mildew, a fungal infection common during hot, humid days that starves the leaves of sunlight until they dry and fall off.
ga: Powdery mildew ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ gbii ni edɔ, ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ anine shɛɛɛ hulu la nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants pull nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my farm yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer for maize, improving soil fertility without extra chemical costs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato leaves curl during intense heat to reduce their surface area and prevent water loss through evaporation. Regular watering at the root level helps keep the plant hydrated during hot hours.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures cause heat stress in pepper plants, forcing them to drop blossoms to conserve water and energy. Providing light shade or spreading dry grass around the base helps keep the plant cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔii lɛ anɔ koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Ni akɛ hulutsoo loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once heavy fruit bunches grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that cannot naturally support the weight of a heavy fruit bunch during strong winds. Supporting the main stalk with a strong wooden prop or branched stick keeps it upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, enyɛŋ ekwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo tsei niji ni wa fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why must I stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight drives plant photosynthesis, which provides the leaves with energy to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la tsirɛɔ fotosintɛsis yɛ tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from sprouting and taking over your field.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni eha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many of their flowers to conserve energy for a few strong pods. However, excessive flower drop can be caused by dry spells, lack of shade, or insect pests damaging the blooms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo be, hulutsoo be ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ fe nine.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots, starving your crops even if rainfall is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves of my corn field?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the plant's growing center. Catching them early allows you to use appropriate pest control before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ hei ni edaa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsofa ni sa atsu nii dani amɛfite onibii.

english: How do I know which way is up when planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ?

english: Look closely at the stem for the small buds where old leaves used to grow; these buds should point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down causes poor sprouting and weak tuber development.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmeii bibii lɛ. He ni baai momoi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Cassava ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Staking lifts the yam vines off the ground so the leaves can trap maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the plant to produce more energy, which builds larger and healthier tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, receive too little shade, or are attacked by pests like mirids. Maintaining adequate shade trees and managing moisture helps flowers mature into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Nine shɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ fioo tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutuaa tso lɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain shishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main tree for water and soil nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make my land better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During intense heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting. As long as the soil is moist, the plant usually recovers in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital resources like sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, leaving your plants hungry and cramped.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ ni amɛhe afee shoo.

english: Why do my crop roots turn soft and rot when heavy rain sits on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots because they cannot breathe. Without air, root tissues die and begin to rot.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shwiemɔ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ No lɛ shishifã lɛ gboɔ ni ebɔi fitemɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots go dark and spoil just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living plant parts that continue to breathe heavily after harvest. Once cut from the main stem, natural chemical reactions start within 48 to 72 hours that cause blue-black streaking and rapid rotting unless the roots are processed, dried, or kept cold immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifã ji tso lɛ fã ni hiɛ ka ni ewaa lolo akɛ ebaamu beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ ko jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli, ni ekɛ bluu-diŋ ŋmɔlɔi kɛ fitemɔ oya baa. ja atsu shishifãi lɛ ahe nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ, agbi amɛ, loo awo friji mli.

english: How does keeping freshly cut vegetables in a cool shade or cool store keep them fresh for market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai heei ni akɛtoɔ hulutsoo be mli loo he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ehi shi ehee kɛha jara lɛ?

english: Once you harvest green vegetables, they lose water rapidly and burn through their natural sugars to stay alive. Keeping fresh produce cool slows down their breathing and water loss, which prevents them from wilting and keeps them crisp until they reach the buyer.
ga: Kɛji okpa aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ laajeɔ nu oya ni amɛshãa adebɔɔ mli sugars lɛ koni amɛhi wala mli. Kɛ́ ahã aduawai kɛ aduawai heei afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ehaa mumɔ kɛ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haaa amɛgboi, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: Why does slicing and drying fresh plantain or cassava right after harvest prevent them from rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akpa plantain loo cassava hee ni agbi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa amɛfite lɛ?

english: Spoiling happens because mold and bacteria thrive on the water inside fresh crops. Slicing and drying removes that moisture, creating a stable environment where harmful microbes cannot grow, which allows the dried product to store safely for months.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa ejaakɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ daa yɛ nu lɛ mli yɛ tsei heei amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ni agbi lɛ, ejieɔ nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛŋ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ nibii ni egbi lɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to protect themselves from drying out. Reducing the leaf area exposed to direct sunlight and wind conserves internal water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ́ ajie he ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots in my barn even when there is no soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural internal biological clock. After a few months of rest following harvest, the tuber automatically breaks its natural sleep period and uses its stored food energy and water to push out new shoots, seeking light and dirt to grow again.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni wala yɔɔ mli. Beni ajɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Yitso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mlijaa mli ewoɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe fãi amli. ni okɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ mli Taomɔ la kɛ muji ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my plantains are fully grown and ready to cut so they do not ripen too fast on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ edara ni esa akɛ afolɔ amɛ koni amɛkakwɛ oya tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fingers lose their sharp side angles and become full and rounded, and the dried flowers at the tips rub off easily. Harvesting at this stage ensures the fruit is mature but still firm and green enough to handle transport.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni nineshi nine fɛɛ nine sɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni eyi obɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaajie. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa aduawai lɛ edaa shi ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛwo he kroko.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels under stress, it sacrifices its flowers to save water and energy just to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ekɛ fɔfɔi baashã afɔle koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Lower tomato leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or when older bottom leaves are blocked from sunlight by dense foliage above. It can also happen when soil stays overly wet, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Tomato baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋwɛi tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense direct sun. Without tall shade trees to filter the sunlight and retain air moisture, the tropical heat evaporates water from the leaves faster than the young roots can absorb it from the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei kakadaji ni baatsi hulu la lɛ naa ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Tropical heat lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ feɔ la oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads become soft, watery, and smelly while still growing in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe yitsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, nu yɔɔ mli, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: This soft rot is caused by soil bacteria that enter the plant through tiny wounds left by insects or farm tools. Warm and overly wet conditions cause these bacteria to multiply fast, breaking down the head's cell walls into a watery, foul-smelling mush.
ga: Nɛkɛ soft rot hela nɛɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli helai ni baa tsei amli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii ni kooloi bibii loo ŋmɔ mli nibii feɔ lɛ anɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ haa nɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi nɛɛ ayiɔ babaoo oya. Efoɔ yitso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli ni shãa mɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for plant growth, or that the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving drainage helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by severe heat and dry weather. Protecting young plants from insects and keeping the soil moist helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my harvested yams coming out small and bent instead of long and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eda lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to stretch down and grow into long, straight tubers. Hard, compacted, or stony soil stops the tubers from expanding and forces them to bend.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekɛlɛ ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi ni ja. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ, loo ni tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni enyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, allowing ground fungi to attack the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni atswa lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree lacks water, when sucking insects attack the blossoms, or if there are not enough tiny insects like midges around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔii Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii, tamɔ mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop making peppers when the hot season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper feemɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Very high temperatures cause pepper plants to drop their flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy. Providing shade and keeping the soil moist during hot weeks helps the plants hold onto their flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea pods right after the flowers open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea pods attract insects like pod-boring caterpillars as soon as they form because the young pods are soft and full of sweet juices. Protecting the crop early with insect sprays or neem oil keeps the insects away.
ga: Bush bean pods lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ pod-boring ŋmeii kɛji amɛfee pɛ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ. Nibii ni abuɔ he mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why are my vegetable leaves covered in white sticky spots and small insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahe eyi kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: White sticky spots are usually honeydew produced by aphids or mealybugs that suck sap from your crop's leaves. This sap attracts mold, which damages the leaf and stops the plant from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji wuo ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ otso lɛ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ feɔ. Latex nɛɛ baagbala ŋmeii. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ efee niyenii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with strong wooden poles and planting them in deep, rich soil stops them from tipping over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ ni okɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plants naturally while also covering the ground to prevent soil drying out.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekagbi.

english: How should I store my cassava stem cuttings before planting so they do not dry out or spoil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmei niji ato dani madu? Koni tso lɛ akagbi loo ekafite.

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be stored upright in a shaded area, such as under a tree, with their base ends slightly buried in moist soil. Leaving them lying flat on dry ground or in direct sunlight dries out the buds and reduces their ability to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ ato shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, tamɔ tso shishi, ni akɛ shishifã lɛ naagbee awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo mli. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha yibii kpakpai aba?

english: A good cassava cutting should come from a mature plant that is 8 to 12 months old, be about the thickness of a adult's thumb, and contain at least 4 to 6 undamaged nodes or buds along the stem.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpa ni afo lɛ ajɛ tso ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni elɛɛmɔ tamɔ mɔ ko ni eda lɛ tsitsi nɔ lɛ mli. ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ niji loo ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni efiteee yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some of my cassava stems rot in the ground shortly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stem rot usually happens when cuttings are bruised or peeled during transport, planted in waterlogged soil without proper drainage, or cut with dirty tools that introduce fungal infections.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ yibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ aniji lɛ fã loo ajie amɛhe yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ majeɔ lɛ. Aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. loo ni akɛ nibii ni he tseee ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ ŋmɔɔ

english: Why do improved crop varieties produce much higher yields than our old traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe wɔ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved varieties are specifically bred by agricultural scientists to resist local pests and diseases, tolerate short droughts, and use soil nutrients more effectively to produce larger tubers or bigger grains.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi efɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Eŋmɛɔ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ gbɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji loo dumɔwui wuji

english: Is it safe for me to plant crop seeds or stem cuttings that I brought from another region of Ghana?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni mikɛjɛ Ghana kpokpaa kroko nɔ kɛba lɛ?

english: Bringing planting material from another region can accidentally introduce new pests and crop diseases into your local soil. It is safer to buy certified seeds locally or check with an extension officer to see if that variety suits your local rainfall and soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni akɛbaajɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei kɛ tsei ahe helai aba. eboteɔ omaŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ oshara mli Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli loo okɛ extension official ko akwɛ kɛji dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ sa kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ omaŋ lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ.

english: How do I know if a recommended seed variety will actually perform well on my specific farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Every variety has specific preferences for rainfall, soil type, and growing duration. Instead of relying only on the variety's name, ask an extension officer about its maturity period, disease resistance, and soil requirements to match your land.
ga: Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni esumɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, shikpɔŋ henɔ, kɛ be ni ekɛdaraa lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɛi pɛ nɔ lɛ Bi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔ lɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ he sane. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela kɛ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Which way up should I plant my cassava stem cuttings in the soil, and why does it matter?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the raised leaf scars (buds) pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to curve around to reach light, which weakens the plant and severely lowers root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baa lɛ he okadii ni awo nɔ (shishifãi) ​​lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi shi lɛ, ebaaha tsei heei lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni la aba. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How long after cutting a cassava stem do I have to plant it before it dies?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ dani egboɔ?

english: Cassava stems stay viable for up to 2 to 4 weeks if stored properly in full shade and moisture, but planting them within 5 to 7 days after harvesting gives the fastest sprouting and strongest early growth.
ga: Kasava tsei baanyɛ ahi shi otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛ́ adu yɛ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very bushy with lots of leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ŋmɔji, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or planting crops too close together makes the plant put its energy into growing tall shoots and heavy leaves instead of sending food down to swell the underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni tsii, moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni amɛwo shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: What makes my cassava leaves curl up and turn yellowish during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are main symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects or passed down through infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi titri. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo amɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni afolɔ mli lɛ Tsoi srɔtoi ni hela nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa.

english: Can I plant coconut trees together with cocoa on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei tsei kɛ kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, coconut trees grow tall and provide ideal light shade for cocoa trees below them, protecting cocoa leaves from harsh sun while allowing both crops to produce well on the same farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, akokoo tsei daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhaa kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hɔɔŋ ni sa. Buu kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow better under taller trees than in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive under larger trees. Overhead shade keeps the air cool, reduces water loss from the soil, and prevents harsh sunlight from burning cocoa leaves.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ashishi. Shade ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni otsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekashã kookoo baai lɛ

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if they get too much direct sunlight during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Excessive direct sunlight dries out the soil quickly, causes cocoa leaves to burn and turn yellow or brown, and can stunt pod development or kill young trees.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. ni ebaanyɛ etsĩ pod lɛ shweremɔ naa loo efite tsei bibii.

english: How does planting shade trees help control weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees block full sunlight from reaching the ground, which naturally slows down weed growth while keeping soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Do fallen cocoa leaves hurt my farm, or should I leave them on the ground?
ga: Ani kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui? Aloo esa akɛ mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: You should leave them on the ground. Fallen cocoa leaves decompose into rich organic fertilizer that improves soil quality and feeds neighboring crops like coconut trees.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ. Kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei tsei.

english: Can natural leaf mulch really help reduce the amount of chemical fertilizer I need to buy?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni eba tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ shi?

english: Yes, decomposing leaves add vital nutrients back into the soil and retain soil moisture, helping reduce your reliance and spending on synthetic fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egboi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Enɛ haa hiɛnɔkamɔ kɛ shika ni afiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between coconut and cocoa trees so they don't fight for space?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni ja ni ka ŋmei tso kɛ kakao tso teŋ lɛ? bɔni afee ni amɛkaye he akaŋ yɛ he ko he

english: Proper spacing ensures high coconut trees provide filtered shade without completely blocking sunlight or causing roots to compete for water and nutrients.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛnáa hulutsoo ni tsiii hulu lɛ naa loo ehaaa amɛshishifãi lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if two different crops I planted together are supporting each other well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei enyɔ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for dark green foliage, steady trunk growth, minimal signs of heat stress, and consistent flowering or pod production on both crops throughout the season.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. stable trunk growth Okadii fioo komɛi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa kɛ fɔfɔi loo pod ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Will mixing two different crops like cocoa and coconut on one plot reduce my overall harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ, tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei futu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: If planted with the recommended spacing, both crops can yield abundant harvests because they share sunlight and organic nutrients effectively rather than competing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji lɛ Tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo ejaakɛ amɛkɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhe baabɔ akaŋ.

english: How do officers measure or estimate the total yield quantity from my farm after harvest?
ga: Te onukpai lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛsusuɔ loo amɛbuɔ nibii fɛɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yield is estimated by counting healthy, harvestable pods or fruits per tree across selected sample plots on your farm and multiplying by the total tree population.
ga: Asusuɔ yibiiwoo he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ akpa tso fɛɛ tso nɔ yɛ shikpɔji ni ahala ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ abɔ he

english: Leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for strong green growth. This usually happens when rain washes nutrients deep out of reach or when fertilizer is not applied at the right stage.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ he ko ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he loo kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awoko mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my farm yield less maize every year when I plant it in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen naturally and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaha nitrogen aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away from the root zone before the plants can drink it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp, but not during heavy downpours, allows the roots to absorb the nutrients effectively.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains provides temporary shade and holds moisture, shielding the seedlings until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni ashiɔ amɛ kakadaŋŋ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Buu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit, making them top-heavy. Microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects often weaken the underground corm, causing the whole plant to uproot during high winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii ni haa amɛfeɔ tsii. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ajie yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner green leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai eŋɔli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the central funnel of the corn plant to feed on tender new leaves. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched larvae chew through the stem if left untreated.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ baatsɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or transmitting a virus. Damaging these sap-feeders early prevents the leaves from wrinkling and stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ mliki niyenii nɛɛ akpãtãmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkadara kwraa.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when exposed to extreme heat or sudden shifts between dry soil and heavy watering. The stress causes the plant to drop blossoms to conserve energy rather than set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo tsakemɔ ko ba trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil remains waterlogged for too long, typically due to poor land drainage or delayed harvesting in heavy rains. Excess water starves the roots of air, letting fungal rot set in.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. loo nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ amli nu afee shoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ baafite.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers refuse to sprout right away when I keep them for seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ mikɛwo dumɔwui amli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers enter a natural rest period called dormancy after harvest. The tuber naturally sleeps for a few months and will only begin to sprout when its internal clock signals that the wet planting season is near.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Yitso lɛ baawɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa nyɔji fioo komɛi. ni ebaaje shishi ekwɛ̃ pɛ kɛji ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees dry out and burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow faster and have wide leaves that provide the gentle shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli jɔ haa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant seeds very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots compete for the exact same nutrients and water in the soil, while their leaves block sunlight from one another, resulting in thin plants with small harvests.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil or are getting waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea when the soil is damp helps them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding wood ash or agricultural lime helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What is causing holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the growing point of maize. Spraying approved treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps keep them under control.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsaa hela lɛ baatsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend tying my tomato plants to wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Staking keeps plants upright so heavy fruits stay off wet ground where soil fungal diseases rot them. It also allows sunlight and air to reach every part of the plant.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, akɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ toɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni sũ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu shɛɔ tso lɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Should I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady after two or three good downpours. The first single rain can trigger sprouting, but a dry spell immediately after will kill the young seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃. Shi hulutsoo be ni baa yɛ no sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baagbe tsei bibii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to dig up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves dry up and fall off and cracks begin forming in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu, ni obaanyɛ ole be ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and bigger than my crops even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local soil and climate conditions, allowing them to absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛjieɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it better to spread fertilizer on my field by hand or use a spreading machine?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ miniji ashwã ŋmɔji amli loo mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ atsu nii?

english: Hand application works well for small farms, but broadcasting machines speed up the work on larger plots, save labor, and ensure fertilizer is spread evenly across your field.
ga: Nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔji bibii. Shi wiemɔ tsɔnei yeɔ ebuaa ni nitsumɔ yaa oya yɛ shikpɔji wuji anɔ. Save labor Ni okwɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding the right fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow green and produce good yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What happens to my fertilizer if heavy rains fall immediately after I apply it to my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away topsoil fertilizer before plant roots have time to feed on it, which wastes your money and leaves your crops without enough food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛye. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii anaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward instead of growing strong and bushy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wilt and die when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have weak, shallow roots that cannot drink water fast enough to replace what the hot afternoon sun evaporates from their leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛto nɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ efo kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does leaving dead dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi gbohii ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around crop stems with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, reduces weed growth, and traps moisture in the soil.
ga: Mulching around Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable plants curl up when tiny insects gather underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Tiny pests like aphids feed by sucking juice out of the leaves, causing the plant tissues to shrink and the leaf to curl inward.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids yeɔ nii kɛtsɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray liquid chemicals on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because cooler temperatures stop the liquid from evaporating quickly, giving the plant leaves time to absorb it.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ kpaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛnuɔ nu.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize or cassava on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop roots are getting enough oxygen in wet soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: If water stands in your field for days without draining, the soil loses air spaces, causing roots to rot and leaves to turn yellow from lack of oxygen.
ga: Kɛji nu ta oŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo ni nu hoɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains have soaked the ground so much that the roots are drowning and cannot soak up nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying balanced organic manure helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant doesn't get enough calcium or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly, preventing the plant from moving nutrients properly to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines produce the food that grows the underground tuber through their leaves. Lifting the vines up on stakes allows leaves to catch full sunlight and fresh air, leading to much bigger tubers and preventing leaf diseases caused by wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa yitsei lɛ daraa kwraa, ni etsĩɔ tsei ahe helai ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop roots with dry grass or husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or cocoa husks is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that shades the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the land, leaving the soil tired. Beans, cowpeas, and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Beans, cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot in the soil when water sits around the roots for too long without draining, especially during rainy seasons. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow at the edges and dry up before the fruit bundle matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai akui lɛ dara lɛ?

english: This is often caused by leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka or a lack of potassium food in the soil. Removing the infected leaves and adding wood ash or compost around the base gives the plant strength to finish maturing its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji baa mli ŋmɔtɔ helai tamɔ Sigatoka loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛ tso sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their young tiny pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Cocoa trees shed tiny young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—when they don't have enough water and nutrients to feed all the pods at once, or when sap-sucking insects like mirids attack them during dry periods.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel wilt. Beni amɛbɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaahã ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome, loo kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mirids lɛ tutua amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves look like holes have been chewed into them with small powder inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ nibii bibii bibii lɛ? Yɛ cone mli, ŋmɔ bu?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central stem of the plant during the hot part of the day and eats young leaves. Checking your field early allows you to catch and spray them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or banana trees next to them creates living umbrellas that shelter the young cocoa and keep moisture in the soil until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ feɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, overly damp, and shaded environments. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight reach the trunk and clearing weeds under the trees lowers humidity and helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ Fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are green caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center of my maize plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the young leaves at the center of the plant to feed on tender growth. Spraying recommended control agents early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed reaches them effectively before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai bibii amli yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛyeɔ hela lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow with green spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects and by planting stem cuttings taken from sick plants. You can keep your farm safe by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and using cuttings only from healthy plants.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies kɛ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ pɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does my land become hard like concrete after rain dries up, making my crops grow poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hard soil lacks organic matter, which keeps soil soft and spongy. Adding animal manure, compost, or leaving dried crop stalks on the field improves soil texture, allowing roots to spread easily and hold onto water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmeii. Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ashishifãi ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy nutrients out of the land, especially nitrogen. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and naturally put it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout even when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
