ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: The very first rain often moistens only the surface, while the deep soil underneath remains dry and scorching hot, causing seeds to dry out and die. It is safer to wait until rains become regular so the soil stays wet enough for seeds to germinate.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ waa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Placing too many seeds in one hole causes the plants to fight with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to develop strong stalks and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that travels down to make the tuber underground grow big. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light while protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ la ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ, kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu ni atsĩɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and covering the base with dry leaves helps maintain steady soil temperature and protects the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ baai ni egbi aha shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it better for me to plant nursery seedlings instead of just putting seeds directly into my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Nursery seedlings have already grown past their weakest baby stage in a protected environment. Planting strong seedlings gives them a much higher chance of surviving harsh weather, pests, and weeds compared to seeds planted directly in the open field.
ga: Nursery dumɔwui lɛ etsɔ amɛ gbekɛbiiashi be ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi amli kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do young seedlings often wither and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes shock because their delicate roots get disturbed and suddenly exposed to direct heat. To prevent this, transplant early in the morning or late in the evening, water them immediately, and give them a bit of shade for the first few days.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛshɛɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafee Transplant nɛɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ha nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni oha hulutsoo be fioo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow and curl up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather is extremely hot and dry, plants lose water faster than their roots can drink it. Curling their leaves is the plant's natural defense to reduce water loss and protect itself from burning in the sun.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he.

english: Plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like calcium. The plant drops flowers to save its own life when conditions are too tough to support fruit growth.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium lɛ, tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛhere amɛhe kɛji shihilɛi lɛ bafee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over hundreds of years to survive in poor soil and dry conditions. They aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, which is why clearing them early is essential.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ ekãa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight under the soil for water and nutrients, while their leaves fight for sunlight. Giving crops proper space allows each plant to get enough food and light to grow big and yield well.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la He ni sa ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to trim off some healthy-looking leaves and branches from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mifolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra lower leaves—called pruning—lets fresh air and sunlight reach the inside of the crop. It stops fungal diseases from spreading and forces the plant to send its energy into making bigger fruits rather than growing extra leaves.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ pruning. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ woɔ aduawai wuji ni ekwɛɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ baai krokomɛi.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for crops before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Good crop soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, and holds moisture without turning into sticky mud. Dark soil contains decayed leaves and natural matter that provide rich food for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ su tsuɔ, efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ baa ni fiteɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the exact same crop on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil healthy and starves crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ atsakemɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi.

english: It is best to water crops early in the morning or late in the evening. If you water during the hot afternoon, most of the water evaporates before roots can drink it, and wet leaves in scorching heat can easily burn or get fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ Nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo amɛná tsɛŋemɔ helai oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the leaves above ground look bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po lɛ,

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or stays too wet, cassava plants spend all their energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of storing starch in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the trees without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from water stress, lacks nutrients, or is attacked by tiny insects like mirids (akate) that damage the young flower stems.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu mli haomɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (akate) tutua lɛ, ni amɛfiteɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ekpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread leaf curl viruses, preventing the plant from absorbing light and water normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ leaf curling virus lɛ eshwaa Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ la kɛ nu bɔ ni sa.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot inside the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around the roots in poorly drained soil, creating conditions for soil fungi and microscopic worms (nematodes) to attack the soft skin of the yam.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa shihilɛi baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ. (nematodes) koni amɛkɛtutua ŋmeii ahewolo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten patches at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then very wet.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni efɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why is it important to leave specific distance between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he kroko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to spread roots and leaves so they do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in healthier plants and bigger harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ ebaa lɛ eshwa. Bɔni afee ni tsei akaye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sun. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees shade and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ náa hɔnɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do crops like maize grow better after I have grown beans or groundnuts on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni midu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting seeds after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains are regular and continuous for about two to three weeks so the soil accumulates enough moisture to keep young sprouts alive if a dry spell happens.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ aahu ni eya nɔ aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ abua ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi kɛji hɔmɔ shihilɛi ba.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep producing small shoots around the main stem, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ, ni esa akɛ mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers. If you leave too many, they steal water and nutrients from the main parent plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. You should prune most of them, leaving only one or two strong suckers to take over after harvesting the main stem.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji oshi lɛ yɛ nɔ babaoo Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ babaoo. 1-2 pɛ ni eshwɛɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii beni akpa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tall plantain trees keep falling over before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui kakadaji lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them easy for strong winds to push over. You can prevent this by using wooden props or bamboo poles to support the stems bearing heavy fruit.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni aduawai ni tsii babaoo yɛ nɔ, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli oya. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant plantains together with cassava on the same farm, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli loo béi baaba?

english: You can plant them together if you space them properly. Both crops need plenty of nutrients and water, so if planted too close, they will compete for soil space and light, leading to lower yields for both crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome kɛji okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná ŋwɛi, shikpɔŋ kɛ la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the trees and plant them in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni midu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains are often planted alongside young cocoa to provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist until the cocoa plants mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize crops growing weak and yellow when I plant them under mature plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu yɛ plantain ni eda shishi lɛ?

english: Maize requires full direct sunlight to grow healthy and strong. Mature plantain trees broad leaves block sunlight from reaching the ground, leaving the maize starved for light.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmã tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Plantains ni eda lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ bɛ la.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain tree turning yellow and drying up like a skirt around the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi tamɔ sɛkɛti ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This behavior is often caused by fungal diseases like Panama disease or severe nutrient deficiency. The disease clogs the plant's internal tubes, preventing water from reaching the leaves, which causes them to turn yellow and collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ Panama hela, loo niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ waa lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa. Ehaa nu shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkuɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my plantain plant is about to start producing a fruit bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-plantains lɛ baabɔi aduawai akui awomɔ?

english: A plantain tree produces around 30 to 40 broad leaves before flowering. Just before the fruit appears, the newest leaf grows noticeably shorter and narrower, followed shortly by a large flower bud emerging from the top center.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baawo baai ni mli kwɔlɔ aaafee 30 kɛyashi 40 dani amɛwo fɔfɔi, dani amɛwo yibii. Baai heei lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛmli etse yɛ gbɛ ni kadiɔ mɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ ji ŋmei agbo ko ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce smaller bunches after two or three years of harvesting on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛkpaa nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ

english: Plantains extract large amounts of nutrients from the soil with every harvest. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted, and without replenishing it with animal manure, compost, or fertilizer, the new plantains will produce smaller bunches.
ga: Plantains jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Be ni be hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni kɛji akɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, dumɔwui heei baawo jwɛi bibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up and dry out during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmath beaŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbi lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during dry weather to reduce surface area exposed to dry winds and conserve water. Without mulching around the roots or artificial watering during severe dry seasons, the plant slows down its growth to survive.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baa shi lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he. ni akɛ muji ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo akɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ tsuuu nii yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers pile dead plantain leaves and stalks around the base of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ buaa plantain baai kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ anaa yɛ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Piling organic material around the base acts as mulch, which traps moisture in the soil, keeps roots cool during hot periods, suppresses weeds, and decays over time to feed the plant natural nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni abua naa lɛ abɔle Shishitoo lɛ he baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei.

english: Why is my cassava taking over ten months to mature when I expected to harvest it much earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nɔ ni fe nyɔji nyɔŋma dani mi-cassava lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Ani akpaa gbɛ akɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ mra kwraa fe nakai?

english: Cassava stores its energy slowly in underground roots over time. Depending on the soil nutrients and crop variety, roots take between 8 to 14 months to fully develop, so giving it time produces larger and heavier tubers.
ga: Cassava toɔ hewalɛ fiofio. yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ Shishifãi lɛ heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 14 dani amɛdaraa kwraa. Enɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha lɛ be lɛ, ebaaha yitso lɛ agbo ni etsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that scorch easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them acts as a canopy to protect the young trees until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baatsu nii akɛ shade ni baabu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss. By shrinking the surface area exposed to the sun, the plant conserves water to survive hot periods.
ga: Abɛi baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa fɛ̃i ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ ajie he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi lɛ, ehaa tsei nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow, curling leaves usually indicate that the plant is under stress from tiny sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or is missing key nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji amli, loo akɛ niyenii titrii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing much smaller now than they used to years ago on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ dara kwraa fe bɔ ni amɛji afii komɛi ni eho nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting yams continuously on the same land drains key nutrients from the soil over time. Without letting the land rest or adding manure and fertilizer, the soil lacks the energy to produce large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potato be fɛɛ be yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii titrii ni he hiaa lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fataaa he.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving less energy for developing big fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni akɛbaawo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my young maize right after a short rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛfiteɔ mi-baby corn lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be ko sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm weather and early rains trigger armyworm eggs hidden in the soil or leaves to hatch quickly, sending caterpillars to feed on soft, growing maize leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa cutworm ŋmeii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ loo baai amli lɛ fɔɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain in March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ March mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heat spell before the rainy season truly begins. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni baa mra lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo bei asɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal essential plant food and fertilizer from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ tso niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings need to be planted facing upwards instead of just burying them any how?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ hiɛ kɛya ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni aaafu kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small buds or 'eyes' that must point towards the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots have to bend underground to find sunlight, which wastes energy and leads to poor root development and lower tuber yields.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ tsei lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna hulu la. ni fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do we cut seed yams into smaller pieces before putting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔfoɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii dani wɔfuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cutting healthy seed yams into smaller pieces, called setts, allows you to multiply your planting material so you can cover a larger farm. Treating the cut surfaces with wood ash protects the setts from rotting in the soil before shoots sprout.
ga: Sweet potato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afoɔ mli bibii bibii Atsɛɔ lɛ Sett. Ehaa okɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fataa he koni okɛha ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ tsu he ni afo lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaabu set lɛ he koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli dani ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting seedlings from heat and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my cassava mounds instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops need room for their roots to expand and their leaves to catch sunlight. When cassava mounds are packed too closely, the plants compete for soil nutrients and water, resulting in thin plants with small, weak tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ gbɛ koni shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli ni baai lɛ hu aná hulu la. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ni ato lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ yitsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, indicating that the soil needs fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use to conserve water during extreme heat. However, if the leaves are also sticky or spotted, it can mean tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are feeding on the sap.
ga: Leaf curling ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ wa lolo loo amɛhe ewo ŋmɔtɔ, Enɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies eye ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off mistletoe plants from the branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ mistletoe lɛ kɛjɛɔ kooko nine lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mistletoe is a plant parasite that attaches to cocoa branches and steals water and vital nutrients directly from the tree. Removing it early prevents it from weakening the branch, reducing cocoa pod production, or killing the tree.
ga: Mistletoe ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo niji ahe ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi niji lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɔjɔ. Ha cocoa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ aba shi loo ha tso lɛ agbo

english: Why are caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing point of young maize plants. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from sunlight while destroying the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ hei ni ŋmeii tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni okɛbu ohe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ofiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the cool morning allows plant roots to absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun causes quick evaporation. Afternoon watering can stress hot plants and waste water due to evaporation.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli dani hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adɔ fe nine ni amɛfite nu yɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil fast when stored in plastic bags right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo plastic kotokui amli beni mikpaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains hidden moisture. Storing it in airtight plastic bags traps heat and moisture inside, creating a humid environment where harmful mold and grain insects quickly multiply.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛ́ okɛwo plastic kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmaa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya.

english: How do I know if my farmland has good soil for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Cocoa trees thrive in deep, dark, well-drained soils rich in organic matter. Soil that holds some moisture during dry spells without turning into sticky, waterlogged mud is ideal for healthy root growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni efeee muji kɛ nu. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when direct sunlight hits them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh sunlight. Plantains or shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting seedlings from heat and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Black pod is a common fungal disease caused by high humidity and excess shade. Removing infected pods quickly and trimming heavy branches helps air flow through the farm to stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji fungal hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni hulutsoo ni fa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni afoɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛkpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the small side shoots growing on my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: These side shoots, called chupons, waste the tree's energy. Removing them encourages the cocoa tree to direct water and nutrients into growing healthy leaves, flowers, and cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ afã tsei nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ, fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ewoɔ cacao tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amaje cacao baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava has aggressive root systems that steal nutrients and water from young cocoa. It is better to use plantain instead, as plantain provides shade without competing heavily for food underground.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo bibii amli. Esa akɛ akɛ plantains atsu nii moŋ ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo ni akaŋshii babaoo bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii he.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cocoa trees use to conserve water during dry weather. Applying dry grass or leaves around the tree base as mulch helps soil retain moisture and reduces leaf loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni cacao tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni bɔle Tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsu nii akɛ mulch ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my crops need fertilizer to produce more fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Yellowish leaves, slow growth, and trees producing very few pods are clear signs that the soil is running low on vital nutrients that fertilizer can help restore.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo kɛ tsei ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua ni aku sɛɛ aba lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Many cocoa flowers naturally drop off due to heavy rains, dry spells, or lack of small insects needed for pollination. Healthy trees produce thousands of flowers so that enough will survive to form pods.
ga: Kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulutsoo be, loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha pollination Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi akɛ pods.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to each other to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their roots fight for nutrients and their branches block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing keeps trees healthy and reduces humidity that causes diseases.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ ni tsei aniji tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do tall weeds growing around my farm affect my cocoa yield?
ga: Jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te miŋmɔ lɛ saa mi kokoo yibiiwoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. They also hide pests and trap damp air that breeds fungal infections on your crop.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu. Amɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu teeɔ ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa onibii anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees just fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects or human assistance to transfer pollen to make fruit. If a flower is not pollinated within a day or two, the tree naturally drops it to save energy for other branches.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. aloo adesa yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli koni amɛwo yibii lɛ mli Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli Tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato niji krokomɛi ahe.

english: How does hand pollination actually work to give me more crop yield?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba?

english: Hand pollination means using a small tool or hand to move pollen directly from one flower to another. This guarantees that flowers get fertilized, producing far more healthy pods than waiting for wild insects alone.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ nibii loo niji bibii tsuɔ nii. Koni ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya ekroko nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baawo fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mli wa fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mɛmɔ kɛkɛ.

english: How do tiny insects help my cocoa flowers turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: Insects like midges live in moist farm leaf litter and carry pollen from flower to flower as they move around. This pollen transfer fertilizes the flower so it can grow into a cocoa pod.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ midges hiɔ baai amli yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. ni amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ beni amɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ. Nɛkɛ pollen ni akɛyaa he kroko nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Does heavy rainfall help or hurt the flowers on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ awui?

english: While trees need water to grow, heavy rain can wash away tiny pollinating insects and knock delicate flowers off the branches, which can reduce the number of pods that form.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia tsei koni amɛdara moŋ, shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ni etswa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha pods ni baa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: What causes my small cocoa pods to turn shriveled and black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa?

english: This is often caused by a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease or a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree discards extra pods it cannot afford to feed during dry or stressful weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela loo adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi loo ni haa mɔ haoɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshwieɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is too much open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, sensitive leaves that scorch under direct hot sun. They need partial shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to keep cool and hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni sũ lɛ mli ajɔ ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm soil is lacking nutrients for good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni baaha ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: If your tree leaves are turning yellow, growing very slowly, or producing very few small pods even when weather is good, the soil is likely depleted of nutrients like nitrogen and potassium.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdara blɛoo waa, loo amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii Fioo kwraa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi po. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu fɔɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium ni bɛ.

english: Will cutting away some of the branches on my cocoa trees actually help them grow more pods?
ga: Ani mi-cacao niji lɛ ekomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua cacao tso lɛ ni eda diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, pruning removes unneeded foliage so sunlight and air can reach the main trunk and branches. This keeps the tree healthy, reduces disease, and encourages fresh flowering.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa, ehaa helai baa shi ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi heei hewalɛ koni amɛwo.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing much less fruit than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural production slows down, and their roots become less efficient at pulling nutrients from the soil, leading to fewer flowers and lower yields.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii fioo pɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce lots of pods in one season but very few in the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be kome mli shi ewoɔ fioo pɛ yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees use a tremendous amount of energy to produce a large harvest. If they do not get enough water and fertilizer afterward, they need a resting season to rebuild energy before producing heavily again.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo nibii babaoo. Kɛji nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Amɛmiitao be ni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛtswa amɛhewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani amɛfee ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The crop pulls nitrogen from its older leaves at the bottom to feed the fresh leaves at the top, causing the bottom ones to fade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they have special microbes on their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the cowpeas are harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays behind as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa tsina ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight over sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This stress makes the plants grow thin and weak, resulting in small cobs and a lower total yield than properly spaced plants.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ Ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do you advise me not to grow tomatoes in the exact same spot on my farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu tomato yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously in one spot allows pests and diseases that love that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating your crops starves out those specific pests and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tso lɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense against losing water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and retains internal moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination. Dropping flowers allows the plant to save its energy when weather conditions are too harsh to support growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni ehiii Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ ehiii tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside when the heavy rains last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess rainwater fills all the tiny air pockets in the ground, suffocating the roots and allowing soil-borne fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes and small dark droppings inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu ko ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli

english: This destruction is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the soft center of young maize plants to feed on tender growth, leaving behind visible leaf damage and waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli koni amɛye ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Shi nibii ni efite ni anaa kɛ jwɛi yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or crop leaves on the soil surface around my growing vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo madu baai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ani aduɔ aduawai?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, shields the soil from hot direct sunlight. It traps soil moisture, keeps root systems cool, and helps suppress weed growth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and look weak when water settles on my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛ́ nu gbee miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plant roots require soil oxygen to absorb nutrients and water effectively. When soil remains waterlogged, the roots drown and stop working, causing the plant above ground to starve and stall in growth.
ga: Pepper tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ni amɛbaakpa nitsumɔ. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure helps restore nitrogen so the plants can grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center of the crop to eat the leaves; applying recommended control treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches them effectively.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ koni amɛye baai lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛyeɔ hela lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding agricultural lime or calcium-rich fertilizers prevents this issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ okwaayeli mli lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni calcium yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rain falls for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily and protects the tubers from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. ni nu hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni ehaa yitso lɛ fiteɔ

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients like nitrogen and lets crop-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crop yield even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops before your plant roots can absorb them, leading to weak growth and low yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ oya kɛ hewalɛ. dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ekɛ dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: Why is it important to plant plantain suckers next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ he hiaa No hewɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create natural shade, protecting the young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Will planting my crop seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for light, space, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing leaves room for each plant to grow thick stems and produce full, heavy fruits.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the flowers can turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience water stress during dry weather or when sap-sucking insects attack the tree. Maintaining shade, preserving soil moisture, and managing pests keeps flowers on the tree.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua tso lɛ. Shade care Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Ye obua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my vegetable garden soil moist during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a method called mulching—prevents the sun from evaporating soil water, keeping the roots cool and moist much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai shwie otsei lɛ anɔ—gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—baaye abua ni hulu la akafee nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of the crop seeds I plant in my backyard sprout quickly while others fail to come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni miduɔ yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ oya lɛ? Ani edaaa ekoŋŋ kwraa?

english: Seeds require a balance of moisture, soil air, and correct planting depth to germinate. Planting seeds too deep prevents them from reaching sunlight, while planting in dry or overly hard soil keeps them from getting the water needed to break out of their shell.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ, shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli egbi tsɔ loo ni wa tsɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ naaa nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfo kɛjɛ eshishifã lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cocoyam under the shade of big trees in my compound, or does it need full sunlight to grow well?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ mli lɛ ashishi? Aloo esa akɛ ená hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cocoyam actually thrives in partial shade and moist soil. Planting it under larger trees protects its big leaves from burning under strong afternoon heat while keeping the root area damp.
ga: Cocoa yam kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai wuji lɛ anaa yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifã lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my backyard food crops very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu niyenii yɛ sɛɛtsu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another, leading to weak stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings sometimes fall over and die just a few days after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by dampness-related fungal decay at the base of the stem when the soil stays overly wet, or because the seedling stem grew too thin and weak searching for light.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni kɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo akɛni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ la taomɔ mli hewɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my backyard crops turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves typically indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is either holding too much stagnant water or staying completely dry for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ sũ lɛ ená nu ni damɔ shi babaoo loo egbi kwraa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I harvest kontomire leaves from my backyard without killing the main plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa contomire baai kɛjɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ ni mifiteee tso titri lɛ?

english: Always cut only the outer, fully mature leaves near the base, leaving at least three or four young central leaves intact so the plant can continue to capture sunlight and produce new growth.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni eda ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ pɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, shi baai bibii 3 loo 4 yɛ teŋgbɛ koni tso lɛ aya nɔ aná hulu la ni ekɛ dalɛ hee aba.

english: Why are holes appearing on my kontomire leaves, and how can I protect them naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji miije kpo yɛ mi-contomire baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Holes are usually caused by leaf-chewing insects like caterpillars or beetles. You can handpick them off in the morning or spray the leaves with a mild liquid made from crushed neem leaves and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Obaanyɛ ojie amɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ leebi loo okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Akɛ neem baai ni atswa kɛ nu fee.

english: Why do my cocoyam leaves droop and dry up during the hotter months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cocoyam leaves broad surface areas lose moisture rapidly in intense heat. Drooping is the plant's natural reaction to conserve water when the soil lacks adequate moisture.
ga: Cocoa haa nu sɛɛ foɔ yɛ hei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Defoliation ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ koni ekɛbu nu he kɛji sũ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I make the hard soil in my backyard soft and rich for my food crops without buying commercial fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ afee blɛoo ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miniyenii tsei lɛ ni miheee jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can enrich hard soil by mixing in organic materials like decomposed kitchen waste, dry animal manure, and fallen leaves, which break down to loosen the soil and feed the roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ shĩa mli jwɛi ni egbo, kooloi amli jwɛi ni egbi, kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni okɛaafutu mli lɛ nɔ. ni baafite koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ niyenii aha shishifãi lɛ

english: What is the best time of day for me to water the food crops around my house during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo niyenii tsei ni bɔle mishia lɛ he lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply before the strong sun causes the water to evaporate from the ground.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli kwɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. When nitrogen is low or washed away by heavy rains, the plant cannot produce green pigment, which slows down its overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen faaa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi. Enɛ baaha dalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why is my yam growing very slowly even though we are getting good rainfall this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Water alone is not enough for heavy feeding crops like yam; they also require nutrient-rich soil. If the soil lacks essential minerals like potassium and phosphorus, the tubers cannot expand, regardless of how much rain falls.
ga: Nu pɛ faaa kɛha niyenii tsei ni tsii tamɔ sweet potatoes. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hu he miihia amɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus. Yitso lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ

english: Why do my crops yield less food every year when I plant maize on the exact same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Changing what you plant gives the soil time to recover and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nɔ ni oduɔ lɛ ni oootsake lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and cannot drain properly. The roots need oxygen from the air underground, and when submerged in waterlogged soil for too long, soil fungi and bacteria quickly attack and rot them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia shishifãi. ni kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Fungi kɛ bacteria ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense heat as a defense mechanism to conserve water. By curling, they reduce the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, usually uncurling again once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he. Curling haa baa lɛ nɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi. ni esumɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate them. Under extreme conditions, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo kooloi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ. yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa waa shishi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them alongside maize acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize, helping both crops grow better together.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my crops very close to each other, won't I get a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting crops too close together actually lowers your harvest. The plants end up competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller yields rather than healthy, fruit-bearing crops.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi. Esa akɛ tsei nɛɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa. Yɛ tso ni woɔ yibii kpakpai ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster and are naturally tougher than domestic crops. They aggressively absorb the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, effectively starving your crops of essential resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe shia tsei. Amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did some of my crop seeds fail to sprout after I planted them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep where air cannot reach them, or if the topsoil dries out completely after planting. Storing seeds in hot or damp places before planting can also destroy their vitality.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ dani aduɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ afite amɛshihilɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer (like urea) helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ urea) fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize seeds in straight lines rather than scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in lines gives every crop enough space to receive light, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier compared to scattering seeds randomly.
ga: Nibii ni yaa nɔ yɛ line mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa trukaa lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Clearing bushy shade, pruning extra branches to let sunlight in, and harvesting ripe pods regularly help stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ Atsemɔ nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he koni hulu la abote mli Ni tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are there tiny holes all over the leaves of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: Insects like beetles and caterpillars are eating the leaves to feed themselves. If left unchecked, they can destroy the leaves the plant needs to feed its pods, so spraying organic neem oil or approved pest controls early protects the crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii miiye baai lɛ koni amɛye amɛhe niyenii. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite baai ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛ e-pods lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa kroko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the ground is often caused by waterlogging in heavy soil or attacks by tiny worms called nematodes and fungi. Planting on high mounds with good drainage and using healthy seed yams prevents the tubers from rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes kɛ fungi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potatoes ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ, ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomatoes cracking open on top before they fully turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack open when water supply changes suddenly—such as a heavy downpour after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to split. Consistent watering prevents this problem.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. cause disintegration Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What causes my plantain trees to snap or fall over easily even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po?

english: Plantain trees often fall because banana stem borers or root nematodes have eaten away the inside of the stem and roots, weakening the base. Planting clean, treated suckers and supporting fruiting plants with bamboo poles keeps them standing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ banana tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo nematodes yeɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi lɛ. gbɔjɔmɔ shishitoo lɛ Tsobii ni he tse ni atsa amɛ kɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leaves but failing to form a tight round head in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when temperatures are too hot or when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces leaf growth instead of head formation. Planting during cooler months and using balanced fertilizer encourages firm heads.
ga: Kaabe nyɛŋ ajie eyitso kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bulbs. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nyɔji ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni bulb lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell underground cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the swelling tubers push against the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the cocoa trees build strength during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ maa hewalɛ emaa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and rot when they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Heavy tomato fruits cause unsupported stems to bend to the ground. When leaves and fruit touch wet dirt, moisture-loving fungal diseases easily attack and spoil them.
ga: Tomato yibii ni tsii lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ sɛɛfimɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji baai kɛ aduawai ta shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to make green leaves, especially after heavy rains wash nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Titri lɛ, beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do crop leaves burn and dry up when I put fertilizer right next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Placing them directly against stems without enough water pulls moisture out of the plant, causing burns on the leaves and roots.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Ekɛ shãa baa baai kɛ shishifãi anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and getting yellowish spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on cassava is caused by tiny whiteflies that pass a viral disease to the plant, preventing the leaves from absorbing sunlight to make big roots.
ga: Nibii ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei bibii yɛŋ mli. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli Enɛ haaa baai lɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni amɛfee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars hide inside the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworm caterpillars hide in the central funnel of maize plants because the tender young leaves inside offer fresh food and protection from hot sun and predators.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii hee kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming any peppers during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper efeee yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and the soil lacks water, pepper plants enter survival mode and shed their blossoms to save energy and protect themselves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ yaa wala mli ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my orange trees drop many small, green fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Babaoo dani ebatsɔ agbo?

english: Citrus trees naturally shed excess young fruits if the tree lacks enough water or food in the soil to mature all of them safely.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baajie yibii bibii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my yam vines produce plenty of dark green leaves but leave me with small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?
