english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes yams spend all their energy growing tall vines and leaves on top instead of sending food down into the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ tsei ahe tsei yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛya shi kɛya yitso lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start to spoil so quickly a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni mikɛfoɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once cassava is cut from the stem, air enters the root wounds and triggers natural chemical decay within two to three days unless processed or buried under damp soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo ŋmei kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shishifã lɛ mli ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsofai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Ja atsu he nii loo afu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and need partial shade during their first two to three years. Without shade crops like plantain or banana to protect them, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fioo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires high amounts of nitrogen to grow, and when the soil lacks it, the plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps rebuild soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that eats the growing shoots of maize plants. Spotting them early allows you to spray recommended organic treatments like neem extract or targeted pesticides before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ. Spotting them early Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. dani ekpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with insecticidal soap or neem oil prevents the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkafee nɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems from my harvest to plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old, avoiding stems with visible pests, mold, or damage. Stems cut from the middle portion of healthy plants sprout the strongest roots and give the best yield.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaa, ŋmeii, loo nɔ ni efite lɛ ahe. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ebaawo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: How long should I wait after the first rain before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until the rains are steady and the soil is moist to a depth of about 10 to 15 centimeters. Planting after just one early light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then die if a week of dry heat follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 mli. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa nɛɛ wo mli shikome pɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ otsi kome sɛɛ yɛ la ni mli egbi shishi.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or straw is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under hot weather, retains water longer, and prevents weeds from taking over and stealing nutrients from your tomato plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aŋɔ he ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ o-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they receive maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. It also prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil, resulting in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potatoes kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni eha amɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha tsei lɛ. Ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Maintaining consistent moisture and protecting plants from extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in full sunlight without any shade around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and stems that lose water quickly under strong sun. Fast-growing shade crops like plantain or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa trees from heat and retaining soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of bottom leaves usually means the maize plant lacks nitrogen. As the plant grows, it pulls stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with plenty of leaves, so why are the tubers under the ground so small?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo. Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or water, it puts all its energy into growing big branches and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. Pruning excess foliage and controlling soil nutrients helps the plant focus on swelling its tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bulb ni efuu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce so many flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when there are no insects or wind to assist with pollination. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni baaye abua kɛha pollination Kɛji pollination yeee omanye lɛ Tso lɛ hu baashwie fɔfɔi.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting or catching soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaaa baai lɛ akafite loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akamɔ amɛ

english: Why does my plantain tree bear small bunches of fruit when I allow many young shoots to grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishitoo wulu lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: All the shoots, or suckers, growing around the mother plant share the same root system and compete for water and plant food. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving only one or two allows the main trunk to yield larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi loo tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yɛ shishifã kome ni ekɛ ehe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha niji ni dara ni tsii aba tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and preventing the plant from growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee agbo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves or spreading a virus. Damaged leaves cannot perform photosynthesis properly, which stunts the plant's overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why does my maize farm yield cobs with missing kernels if dry weather hits right when the tassels appear at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: The tasseling stage is when maize reproduces through pollination. If the plant suffers from lack of water during this short window, the silk threads dry out before catching pollen, resulting in cobs with missing or underdeveloped kernels.
ga: Brush stage lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa fɔɔ kɛtsɔ pollination nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu be kukuoo ko lɛ Siliki lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ebuaa pollen naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni elaaje loo dumɔwui ni edako lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are present, even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni wɔyɛ jwɛi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb fertilizer, water, and soil nutrients much faster than your crops can. Removing weeds ensures that your crops get the full benefit of the fertilizer and moisture in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the legumes are harvested, this trapped nitrogen remains in the dirt to naturally feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nitrogen ni aŋã awo mli nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This usually happens when your soil is running low on nitrogen fertilizer. Maize plants naturally move available nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies are sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or that the crop is suffering from intense heat. Treating the plants for pests keeps leaves flat so they can trap sunlight to grow fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli Nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni emɔ hulu la lɛ mli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when weather conditions get too hot or when watering is irregular. When the plant feels stressed by extreme heat or dry soil, it drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha ewalayeli moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun but stand upright again by evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables droop in extreme heat as a natural defense to conserve water by reducing their exposure to direct sunlight. As long as the leaves recover by evening, the plant is managing stress, but staying limp into the evening means it needs urgent watering.
ga: Aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni akɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ hulu la ni baa shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tsei hu kɛ haomɔ miikpe. Shi shwiemɔ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots sprouting around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots act like extra mouths to feed, stealing water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛhaa niyenii. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ejuɔ lɛ nɔ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee fɔfɔi agboi ni tsii.

english: Why must I erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves high into the air and exposes them to sun, which feeds the plant and allows large, healthy tubers to develop underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When water stays trapped in the soil for too long after heavy rains, it starves the roots of oxygen, causing them to rot under the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Nu haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, this nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize crop and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster right after I apply fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds all plant life indiscriminately. If weeds are present, they will absorb the nutrients just as quickly as your main crops, so weeding your farm before or right after applying fertilizer ensures your crops get the food instead.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ niyenii ni amɛkwɛɛɛ amɛhe nɔ ko nɔ ko. Kɛji jwɛi yɛ lɛ, amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya nakai nɔŋŋ. kɛ otsei titrii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔ lɛ awo mli loo beni okɛ ŋmɔ lɛ awo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii moŋ.

english: How long will it take for my cassava to be ready for harvest after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi-cassava lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava takes between 9 to 12 months to mature fully depending on the variety, so it requires long-term planning for your land.
ga: Kɛjɛ bɔ ni ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ato ogboshinii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which crops should I plant if I need a harvest in a very short time?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa yɛ be kukuoo mli?

english: Vegetables like peppers, tomatoes, and leafy greens, or short-duration maize varieties can be harvested within 2 to 3 months, giving you fast food and income.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa aduawai tamɔ ŋmei, tomato, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli Aloo, abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa henɔi ni yeɔ be kuku yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni enɛ baaha oná niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛ shika ni onáa.

english: Can I leave my mature yams in the ground if I am not ready to harvest them yet?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmɔtɔ ni edara yɛ shikpɔŋ? Ni kɛji akɛ mifeee klalo akɛ makpa nii lolo hu?

english: Yams can stay in the ground for a short time after maturity, but leaving them too long during the dry season exposes them to pest attacks like termites and causes them to dry out.
ga: Atomɔ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kukuoo ko. beni edara kwraa sɛɛ Shi kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Enɛ baaha amɛná tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Why do my harvested fresh tomatoes spoil so quickly before I get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have a high water content and thin skin, making them soft and prone to rotting within days if kept in hot containers without good airflow.
ga: Tomato mli nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni ehewolo hu yɛ mlɛo. Tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsɛnsi ni mli edɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my maize if I plant late when the rainy season is almost over?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ sɛɛ mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Maize needs regular water when flowering and forming seeds; planting too late means the rains may stop early, leading to poor grain development and low yields.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa daa kɛ́ efɔ fɔfɔi ni ewo dumɔwui. Dumɔ ni aduɔ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa mra. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmaa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmãa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly during the hot dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi waa yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from intense sun heat, reducing the amount of water escaping from their leaves.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa seedlings on my land?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa seedlings should be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart so their roots and leaves have enough room to grow without choking each other for light and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa dumɔwui lɛ aaafee mitai 3.3 kɛjɛ amɛhe koni eha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ aná hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkajie la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɛɛ amɛdɛŋ.

english: How much maize harvest can I get from one acre of land?
ga: Abele enyiɛ manyɛ makpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: With good spacing, quality seeds, and proper care, one acre of farmland in Ghana can yield between 10 to 15 bags (100kg each) of maize.
ga: kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa kotokui 10 kɛyashi 15 (eko fɛɛ eko tsiimɔ ji kilogram 100).

english: Why do my young plantain suckers turn yellow under heavy sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain leaves are tender and lose water quickly; without shade from neighboring trees, hot sunshine burns them before their roots are fully established.
ga: Plantain baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ hulutsoo. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ aaawo shishifãi.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year when I grow crops on the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Crops pull food nutrients out of the earth as they grow, so planting continuously on the same land without adding manure or resting the soil drains its strength.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fataaa he loo akɛ sũ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaha ehewalɛ aba shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is overly waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their tender leaves dry out quickly; they need shade crops like plantains to protect them and keep the surrounding soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Black rotted bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, are usually caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge, tall leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing tall leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eniji lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: The very first rain usually heats up dry, hot soil without soaking deep enough, creating a steamy environment that bakes or rots seeds before they can establish roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli agbala bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ mli lasu baa loo ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛ shishifãi baa.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing tall and thin and falling over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa akɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the stalks to stretch thin as they fight each other for sunlight, making them too weak to hold heavy cobs or withstand winds.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli agbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔ ŋmei ni tsii lɛ mli loo amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or dry leaves around my pepper plants help them grow better during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi awo he lɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, reduces water evaporation, and slowly breaks down into natural soil food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too high, during dry Harmattan winds, or when the plant lacks sufficient water at the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my cabbage plants have small round holes and look like they are being eaten from underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni ayeɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishi?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by tiny green caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae, which hatch from eggs laid on the undersides of the leaves and feed on them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai ashishi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ

english: How do I know my plantain bunch is mature enough to cut before it starts turning yellow on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantains kuu lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ dani amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp, angular corners and become plump and rounded, and the dry flower tips break off easily.
ga: Plantain tsei akuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ efo ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya

english: Why is my land becoming dryer and making my crops produce less food than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni ehaa niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Desertification and changing weather cause the soil to lose its moisture and rich topsoil, making it harder for crops to take in water and nutrients needed to produce a good harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋa nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ haa shikpɔji lɛ anɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaana nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Is it possible for me to grow food crops on dry, empty land where nothing is currently growing?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but you need special crop varieties that survive with little water, or you must first improve the soil using leguminous plants to bring life back to dry land.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi tsei srɔtoi krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ he miihia bo. Aloo ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmeii atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛ wala aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do hot weather and dry soil make my cassava and yam roots stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa mi-cassava kɛ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: When the soil gets too hot and dry from environmental changes, plants spend their energy trying to survive the heat rather than expanding their roots and storing food underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi yɛ shihilɛ mli tsakemɔi ahewɔ lɛ Tsei baafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some of these new drought-tolerant crops taste different from our traditional local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa nɛɛ ahe ŋɔɔmɔ yɛ srɔto kwraa yɛ wɔmaŋ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Breeding crops to survive dry weather often alters their natural sugars, starches, or water content, which changes how they taste or feel in your mouth compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni afɔɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ tsakeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar, starch, loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni onuɔ he ehaa loo bɔ ni onuɔ he ohaa yɛ odaaŋ kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: Does a crop that survives harsh dry weather always taste as good as crops grown in good rain?
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni yeɔ wala yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ hu ŋɔɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Not always. Plants under water stress or those bred strictly for toughness often produce lower levels of natural sugars, which can make them taste less sweet or more bitter.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei ni yɔɔ nu shishi loo tsei ni akwɛɔ koni amɛfee shiŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ adebɔɔ mli sugar ni baa shi. Enɛ haaa ehiɛ afee shoo loo ehiɛ edɔ waa.

english: If a hardy crop grows very well in dry soil, does that mean it gives my family all the nutrition we need?
ga: Kɛji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eyeɔ ebuaa miweku lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni he hiaa wɔ lɛ?

english: No, many resilient crops provide mostly energy like carbohydrates, but lack essential vitamins, minerals, and proteins, meaning they cannot provide full nutrition on their own.
ga: Dabi, tsei babaoo ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi lɛ haa amɛ hewalɛ babaoo, tamɔ carbohydrates, shi amɛbɛ vitamini, mineral, kɛ protein ni he hiaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei nɛɛ nyɛŋ aha niyenii ni yeɔ emuu kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my children still get weak even when we harvest and eat plenty of high-yielding food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ wɔkpaa niyenii ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni wɔyeɔ lɛ?

english: Eating large amounts of a single high-yielding crop gives stomach fullness and energy, but without companion crops like leafy vegetables or beans, the body misses out on vital micronutrients needed for full health.
ga: Kɛ́ oye tso kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaaha omusuŋ ayi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ tsei ni fata he tamɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai loo ŋmeii bɛ lɛ, gbɔmɔtso lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ niyenii bibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa lɛ.

english: Why should I try to get improved seeds from specialized crop farmers instead of using seeds from my kitchen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni maná dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe nilelɔi adɛŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-kpataashi lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Specialized crop farmers use seeds specifically selected to withstand dry spells and diseases, giving you a much higher chance of a successful harvest than regular food seeds.
ga: Mɛi ni duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni ahala krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ kɛ helai shihilɛi anaa lɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa onáa hegbɛ ni fa babaoo akɛ obaakpa nii jogbaŋŋ fe niyenii dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ.

english: How can changing the type of crops I plant on my small farm help the whole country?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aye abua maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: When many farmers adopt high-yielding and resilient crops, it drastically increases the total food available in local markets, reducing food shortages and driving down prices for the entire nation.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo miitsɔ amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Niyenii ni faaa lɛ aba shi ni eha jara aba shi yɛ maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why do some crops grow fast in the field but spoil quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii komɛi ni aduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli, shi kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ lɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties focus all their energy on fast growth and high moisture yield, which makes their cells softer and more liable to rot quickly if not stored or processed right away.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ bɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmli wala yibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni kɛ́ akɛtooo loo atsuuu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite oya.

english: What is a cash crop, and how is it different from the food crops I grow to feed my family?
ga: Mɛni ji shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ niyenii ni miduɔ koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii lɛ he?

english: A cash crop is grown primarily to sell in the market for profit rather than for direct household consumption. While food crops like cassava and maize feed your family daily, cash crops like cocoa, cashew, or oil palm generate larger lump-sum income to pay for school fees, health care, and farm investments.
ga: Aduɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii titri koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei koni ana sɛɛnamɔ moŋ fe ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ shia tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ be mli ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ oweku lɛ daa gbi lɛ, shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa Aloo ŋmei fɔ baaha shika babaoo aba ni akɛwo skul nyɔmɔ? Tsofafeemɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli

english: How long do I usually have to wait before a new cash crop tree starts producing and giving me money?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani shika ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko aje shishi ewo yibii ni eha mi shika?

english: Tree cash crops like cashew, cocoa, or oil palm usually take between 3 to 5 years to start producing fruits, unlike seasonal food crops like maize or vegetables which yield income within 3 to 4 months.
ga: Tso mli shika nibii tamɔ cashew nuts, cocoa loo oil palm fɔɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 teŋ dani ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ni haa shika yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli lɛ he.

english: Can I plant food crops like plantain or maize on the same piece of land with young cash crop trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Planting food crops like plantains alongside young cash crops provides immediate food and quick income, while also offering beneficial shade to protect young tree seedlings from harsh sunlight.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ baaha aná niyenii kɛ shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if a new piece of land is suitable for growing crops before I spend money on seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ? Dani obaafite shika yɛ tsei dumɔwui ahemɔ mli?

english: Observe the color and feel of the soil, as well as the wild plants growing on it. Dark, loose soil that holds moisture well and supports tall, green natural vegetation is usually fertile and ready for farming.
ga: Kadimɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni enuɔ he ehaa. Nɔ ni fata he ji koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni fiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ asɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo ni esa akɛ adu.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they say a crop will 'take well' on my land this year?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛkɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ‘baaye nii jogbaŋŋ’ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi nɛɛ?

english: It means that the soil conditions, temperature, and expected rainfall on your land match what that specific crop needs to survive, grow strong roots, and produce a good harvest without dying off early.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ, latsaa, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ kɛ nɔ ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ kpãa gbee. eyɛ shishifãi ni wa ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai ni egbooo oya

english: What basic steps should I take to prepare fresh land before planting my crops for the first time?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa mihe hee lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: Clear tall brush and weeds, break up hard soil so young roots can spread easily, and avoid burning all the cleared vegetation so organic matter can stay in the soil to feed your crops.
ga: Jiemɔ tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ. Efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ ashãmɔ he koni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do certain cash crops like cashew grow better in transition areas like Kintampo than in heavy forest areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ cashew ŋmeii lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsakemɔ hei tamɔ Kintampo fe hei ni kooi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like cashew are hardy and have deep roots that thrive in areas with bright sunlight and moderate rainfall, making them better suited for dry transition zones than crops that require constant high humidity and heavy forest shade.
ga: Tsei tamɔ cashew wa ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulu babaoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe tsei ni biɔ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ koo mli hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my seeds right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early ensures that young roots get steady water while establishing themselves, making the crop strong enough to survive any unexpected brief dry spells later in the growing season.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi bibii lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be be mli ni amɛtoɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die early even when the topsoil looks dark and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ duŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Dark topsoil can be deceiving if there is a hard layer of rock or compacted clay beneath it that stops roots from going deep, or if the soil drains water too quickly during short dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ediŋ lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ kɛji akɛ tɛ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ shishi ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli shɔŋŋ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu egbi.

english: What can I do on my farm if the rains in my district become unpredictable or start late?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ loo ebaa blɛoo?

english: You can plant early-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties, and cover the soil around your plants with dried grass or leaves (mulching) to keep the moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni daa oya loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Ni okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough water during the hot, dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni nu hɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Crops show water distress by wilting or curling their leaves during the hottest part of the day. You can also test the soil by digging a few inches down; if the dirt feels dry and crumbles easily, your crops need water.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu he naagbai akpo kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ hu okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi ni oootsɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni efoɔ oya Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia nu.

english: How can I keep the soil moist without having to fetch water every single day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mikɛ nu shwieee shi daa gbi?

english: Covering the dirt around the base of your plants with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and traps moisture in the ground much longer.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my crops die when rainwater stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like humans do. When excess rainwater sits around the base of plants without draining away, it chokes the roots, preventing them from breathing and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni efooo. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for plant food like nitrogen, or it is getting too much or too little water. Adding well-rotted animal manure around the plants helps restore their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia tso niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. Koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egboi ni akɛaabɔle Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hewalɛnamɔ kpakpa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before they grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms often drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the watering consistent and feeding the plant helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my weak crops more than the strong ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy, well-fed plants produce natural defenses that ward off insects. When a crop is stressed by poor soil or lack of water, it becomes weak and easy for pests to eat.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni buɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe. Kɛji tsei miihao kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside them provides natural shelter and keeps the soil cool until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ko aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni sa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy ears of maize.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds away from my young crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei bibii amli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they quickly drink up water and steal soil food meant for your crops. Removing them gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaakwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu?

english: Early morning or late evening is the best time to water crops. Watering during these cooler hours allows the roots to absorb moisture before the hot sun can evaporate the water away.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Why does it take several years for my new cocoa trees to start bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso hee lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a strong root system and thick trunk to support heavy pods. During the first three to five years, the tree directs all its energy toward growing sturdy branches before it can nourish flowers and fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa eniji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ dani enyɛɔ ehaa efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trunk fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbee shi ni etsɔko ŋmɔtɔ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but it can only support a limited number of pods. The tree naturally drops excess flowers if it lacks water, soil nutrients, or enough tiny insects like midges to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi ebaanyɛ eŋɔ pods fioo ko pɛ. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nu bɛ ehe. niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ni baanyɛ afee amɛhe ŋmeii.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves from drying out completely. Planting permanent shade trees helps hold soil moisture and shields cocoa leaves from harsh sun.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛkagbi kwraa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning excess shade branches keeps air moving and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: As cocoa trees pass 20 or 30 years of age, their roots become less efficient at drawing nutrients from the soil. Pruning dead branches, applying fertilizer, or gradually replanting helps maintain strong yield over time.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso eye afii 20 loo 30 lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Niji ni egboi lɛ ni ooofolɔ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, loo ni ooodu ekoŋŋ blɛoo lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Unripe green pods have flat, under-developed beans with very low sugar content. If picked too early, the beans will not ferment properly, leading to a weak flavor and lower buying price.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edako lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshɛko lolo ni sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa kwraa. Kɛji ohala mra tsɔ lɛ Beans lɛ shwieŋ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa shi, ni jara ni akɛheɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Plantain leaves trap the natural heat and moisture needed for fermentation. This warm environment changes the internal bean color from purple to chocolate brown and develops the full cocoa flavor.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ nɛɛ tsakeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe su kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa tsokolate ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni oha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ kookoo

english: What happens if I leave my cocoa beans in the sun to dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Over-drying makes cocoa beans brittle, causing the shells to crack easily during handling. It also destroys the natural fats inside the bean, which reduces the quality and market value of your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi tsɔ lɛ, ehaa kookoo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa oya beni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ hu. Enɛ haa okpamɔ nii lɛ ahe sɛɛnamɔ kɛ jarayeli jara baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa beans get moldy when I store them for a short time after drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kɛ́ mikɛto be kukuoo ko lɛ? Beni egbi sɛɛ?

english: Mold grows when stored cocoa beans still contain hidden moisture inside. Beans must be dried thoroughly until they crackle when squeezed before putting them into sacks for storage.
ga: Mold lɛ daa kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni ato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee mli lolo. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaagbala kɛji akɛ ashɛre dani akɛwo kotokui amli koni akɛto.

english: Why is it bad to store my bags of dried cocoa directly on a concrete floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ kookoo kotokui ni egbi lɛ baato kɔnkrit nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concrete floors draw moisture up from the ground, which gets absorbed into the bottom bags of cocoa. Placing bags on wooden pallets keeps air circulating underneath and prevents dampness from ruining your crop.
ga: Kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. ni baabote kookoo kotoku ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ kotokui lɛ wo tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen is the key nutrient responsible for green leaf growth, and when the soil lacks it, the plant pulls what little nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baa eŋɔli lɛ daa. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tso lɛ heɔ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and gives pests that feed on cassava a permanent home. Changing crops every season gives the soil time to recover and breaks the pest cycle naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmei lɛ aná shia ni baahi shi daa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efoɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects seem to damage my crops more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warm, humid weather during the rainy season creates perfect breeding conditions for insects to hatch quickly, while soft fresh plant shoots give them plenty of food to eat.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa kooloi lɛ fɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaha amɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: Can I protect my vegetable crops from insects without buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni miheee tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni jara wa?

english: Yes, you can make natural sprays using water mixed with crushed neem leaves or hot pepper, or plant strong-smelling herbs around your field edges to scare away destructive pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ efutu mli lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. Aloo dumɔ tsofai ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa obɔle he. Edge ŋmɔji koni akɛshwie kooloi ni fiteɔ nii.

english: How does covering the ground around my crops with dry leaves help them grow?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ hamɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Covering the ground—known as mulching—works like an umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture in the ground so you water less, protects the soil from hot sun, stops weeds from growing, and rots over time to feed the plants.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni eha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away the good soil on my farm?
ga: Matsi nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaju shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ kɛya. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting fast-growing ground crops like cowpeas holds the soil together with their roots, while building small dirt mounds or ridges across slopes slows down running water so it sinks into the ground instead of carrying your topsoil away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome. be mli ni amaa gɔŋ bibioo loo ŋshɔkei yɛ gɔji srɔtoi anɔ Ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛya.

english: Why do some cocoa farmers leave tall trees standing inside their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ tsei kakadaji yɛ amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tall trees provide natural shade that protects cocoa trees from harsh direct sunlight, drop leaves that rot into rich plant food, and keep the cocoa farm cool during hot dry spells.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Baai ni egboi lɛ bafeɔ tsei aniyenii. kɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ

english: Why is it good to plant beans in the same farm right next to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ mi ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans have special roots that trap natural nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the nearby maize while allowing you to harvest two different crops from the same plot of land.
ga: Beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How does animal manure help my crops grow better than untreated soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe sũ ni atsuuu he nii?

english: Animal manure feeds beneficial living organisms in the soil and improves the soil's ability to hold water, releasing essential nutrients slowly to your crops over a long period.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa sũ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kpo fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Hot afternoon sunlight causes water to evaporate rapidly from the plant's leaves and the surface of dry soil. Adding organic compost or dry plant material into the soil helps it hold onto moisture like a sponge so plants stay hydrated longer.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost loo tsei ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ tamɔ sponji. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of letting full sunlight reach the crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahã hulu lɛ ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants naturally grow under taller forest trees. Shade trees protect young cocoa from scorching sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist during dry periods, and extend the productive lifespan of your cocoa trees.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ashishi yɛ kooi ni kɛlɛ lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ wala sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Are all big trees good to keep as shade trees for cocoa, or can some trees hurt my crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji hi akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ akɛ hulutsoo kɛha kookoo? Aloo tsei komɛi baanyɛ aye midumɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: Not all trees are safe for cocoa. Some trees attract pests like mealybugs that spread the cocoa swollen shoot virus, while others steal too much water. It is best to plant recommended shade trees like Terminalia ivorensis (Emeri) or Albizia.
ga: Jeee tsei fɛɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha kookoo. Tsei komɛi gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ mealybugs ni gbɛɔ cocoa bud virus lɛ eshwaa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi Nu babaoo ni amɛjuɔ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ adu, tamɔ Terminalia ivorensis (Emeri) loo Albizia.

english: Does a mature cocoa farm still need shade trees, or is shade only necessary for young plants?
ga: Cocoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo lolo. Aloo ani hulutsoo he miihia tsei bibii pɛ?

english: Young cocoa needs heavy shade to survive, but mature cocoa still needs light, scattered shade (about 30-40% canopy cover) to protect the soil from drying out and prevent heat stress on the pods.
ga: Kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni ehi shi. Shi cocoa ni eda lɛ hu he miihia ni ená hulutsoo ni mli tse, ni egbɛ eshwa (aaafee 30-40% yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ) koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi ni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa seedling to mature and start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ daa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take about 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, while improved hybrid varieties can mature and produce pods within 2 to 3 years if well managed.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a tree on my farm is mature enough to give proper shade to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: A shade tree is mature when it has developed a broad leaf canopy high above the ground, allowing filtered sunlight to pass through without letting harsh direct heat burn the crops below.
ga: Shade tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he kɛji amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Enɛ haa hulu la ni atsɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaaa la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to shed extra flowers, but severe flower drop happens when there are not enough pollinating insects (midges), or when the tree is stressed by drought or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei baawo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollinators (intermediaries) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: What happens to my crop trees during the dry Harmattan season, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu amɛhe?

english: Dry Harmattan winds cause soil to dry quickly and make crop leaves wilt. Having permanent shade trees and covering the soil around the base of your plants with dry leaves (mulching) retains soil moisture.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ehaa tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo daa ni akɛ baai ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: This usually happens due to transplant shock and direct sun exposure. Young seedlings need fast-growing shade plants, like plantains, put in place before transplanting to shield them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ implant lɛ he shoofeemɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni adu dani adu amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ amɛhe.

english: Why is it recommended to plant plantains on the same plot before planting cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create an instant shelter for fragile young cocoa plants. They also yield food and quick income for your household while the cocoa grows.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa cacao tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ shĩa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛhaa oshia lɛ niyenii kɛ shika oya hu yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best way to spend my crop budget to make sure my new trees yield well in the future?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ midumɔ shika lɛ atsu nii koni mitsei heei lɛ awo yibii kpakpai wɔsɛɛ?

english: Invest your money in high-quality hybrid seedlings from certified nurseries, buy appropriate fertilizers, and secure good shade plants to establish a healthy farm early on.
ga: Okɛ oshika awo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli. Hemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni otao tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baaha ofee ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mra.

english: Why do so many flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges to carry pollen from flower to flower to form a pod. If the flowers do not get pollinated, the tree drops them to save energy for new flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi he miihia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛkɛ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ koni amɛfee pods. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollination Tso lɛ baashi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha fɔfɔii heei.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers encouraging us to hand-pollinate our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ ni wɔkɛ wɔdɛŋ awo kookoo tsei amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Natural insect pollination only fertilizes a small fraction of cocoa flowers. Doing it manually transfers pollen directly to the right flower parts, allowing the tree to produce significantly more pods than relying on insects alone.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ haa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ. Nɛkɛ nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nɛɛ haa pollen yaa hei srɔtoi. of flowers tɛ̃ɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe ni ekɛ ehe aaafɔ̃ kooloi bibii pɛ anɔ.

english: How does the weather affect whether my crop flowers turn into actual fruits?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi saa mitso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Crops react heavily to rain and sunshine. A short dry period followed by rain signals the plant to bloom, but too much heavy rain or severe drought can wash away pollen or dry up flowers before they set fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii waa. be kuku ni akɛgbiɔ Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, ni etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi loo fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ ahe dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do experts tell me to cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi miikɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes extra branches to let sunlight and fresh air reach the center of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing large pods instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aya tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees yielding fewer pods now than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe bɔ ni amɛwo afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their stems and roots become less efficient at carrying water and nutrients from the soil. Older trees require specialized pruning, grafting, or eventual replanting to restore high yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda Kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baabi ni afolɔ amɛ, atswa amɛ, loo adu amɛ ekoŋŋ koni amɛná yibii babaoo.

english: Will planting my cocoa trees closer together give me a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting trees too close makes them compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving each tree enough space allows it to grow a strong trunk and branch canopy that yields far more pods.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛhe mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji ni mli wa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I don't leave shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mishiii tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under intense sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting the young plants from extreme heat and keeping soil moisture steady.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ daa.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Clearing heavy weeds and pruning thick branches helps airflow dry out the farm so the fungus cannot grow and destroy your crop.
ga: Black pods ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ babaoo kɛ tsei ni afoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebɔleɔ ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ni efiteee onibii.

english: How do weeds growing around the base of my trees harm my harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, soil nutrients, and fertilizer intended for your crops. They also create a damp shelter for insect pests and disease spores that can move onto your crop trees.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii Amɛfeɔ shĩa ni mli ejɔ hu kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ aya otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks food and needs fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crops show signs like yellowing leaves, slow growth, and small or dropping fruits. Applying the right fertilizer restores essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so the crop can produce full yields.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ Tso lɛ baajie okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, edalɛ blɛoo, kɛ aduawai bibii loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ fɛɛ

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip, it usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves the little nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves to survive, leaving the old bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that takes the same specific food out of the ground every season. Planting it repeatedly drains those nutrients completely and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to smaller yields each year.
ga: Abele ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ lɛ, nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fioo daa afi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rains get very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe just like they need water. When rain sits on flat, hard soil without draining, it drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that cause fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni wa ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni kɛ tuber rot baa lɛ aba.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the start of the rainy season is uncertain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii? Akɛni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee bɛ faŋŋ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Planting after just one single shower is risky because the soil can dry up quickly. You should wait until the rain is strong enough to keep the top layer of soil moist continuously for two to three days before sowing your seeds.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nu ni ashwie shi shikome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ anɛ waa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme afternoon heat or lack of regular water. The plant drops the flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted even though the green vines on top grow tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛtsake eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep, and loose soil to push downward and swell easily. If the soil underneath is too hard, stony, or not mounded high enough, the tuber cannot expand smoothly, resulting in small, deformed shapes regardless of how green the leaves look.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he miihia sweet potato koni ekɛtsi shi ni efuu oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo atooo he kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔ ni sa lɛ Tubers lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ bibioo ni ehiii bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ha.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and small green worms crawling underneath them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ cabbage baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shishi

english: Those holes are made by caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by small moths. They eat the tender cabbage leaves for food, but spraying the leaves early with soapy neem water or organic pest control stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Buji lɛ ji ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bibii fɔ̃ɔ amɛwuji amli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ kaabeji baai bibii. Shi kɛ́ okɛ neem samla loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ oya lɛ, ebaaha amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from under the leaves. This sap-sucking stresses the plant and can spread viruses that stunt its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi Nɛkɛ nu ni nuɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni haa edara lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do I need to spread and dry my harvested maize thoroughly in the sun before putting it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mashwã ni mahã egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize holds moisture inside the grains. If stored wet in bags, mold and dangerous fungi like aflatoxin grow rapidly, ruining the grain for food or sale and attracting hungry insects like weevils.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ toɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ni mli ewo fɔ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ daa oya. Dumɔwui ni akuɔ mli koni aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ ni egbalaa koolooi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I prune old leaves and extra shoots from my plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai momoi kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi plantain ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dry leaves and extra side shoots steal valuable food and water from the main plantain tree. Trimming dead leaves and leaving only two or three strong shoots directs all the plant's energy toward producing large, heavy fruit bunches faster.
ga: Baai ni egbi kɛ sɛɛ tsei krokomɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Baai ni egboi ni afoɔ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni tsii oya.

english: What is the difference between a straight fertilizer and a blended fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: A straight fertilizer contains only one main nutrient for plants, like just nitrogen or just potassium. A blended fertilizer mixes different straight fertilizers together so your crops get a complete diet of multiple nutrients at once.
ga: Niyenii titri kome pɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi feɔ ekome ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii srɔtoi shikome.

english: I hear people talking about KCL fertilizer; what does it actually do for my crops?
