ga: Mi nu ni mɛi miiwie KCL ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Mɛni diɛŋtsɛ etsuɔ ​​ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: KCL stands for Potassium Chloride, which supplies potassium to your plants. Potassium helps crops build strong stems, withstand dry weather, fight off diseases, and produce bigger, heavier fruits and seeds.
ga: KCL damɔ shi kɛha Potassium Chloride, ni haa otsei lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa ŋmeii ni wa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Ekɛ helai srɔtoi wuɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni dara ni tsii.

english: What is MAP fertilizer and how does it help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji MAP ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: MAP stands for Monoammonium Phosphate. It provides both nitrogen and phosphorus, which help young crops build strong root systems early on and grow healthy green leaves.
ga: MAP damɔ shi kɛha Monoammonium Phosphate, ni haa nitrogen kɛ fɔsfɔs fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa mra. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa

english: Why can't I just apply one single type of fertilizer to all my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops need a balanced diet of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium to thrive. Using only one single fertilizer usually leaves out other essential nutrients, which can slow down growth and lower your harvest yield.
ga: Niyenii ni ja ni nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛshwere. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli, ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Can I mix different straight fertilizers like KCL and Ammonium Phosphate together myself?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ KCL kɛ ammonium phosphate afutu mli?

english: Yes, you can blend straight fertilizers together before applying them. Combining them in the right amounts gives your crop all the necessary nutrients in one go, saving you time and effort.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja afutu mli dani okɛwo mli. Kɛ́ okɛ bɔ ni sa futu mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Enɛ haaa okɛ obei kɛ omɔdɛŋbɔɔ akafite.

english: Which nutrient helps my young crops grow strong roots right after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Phosphorus, which is found in fertilizers like Ammonium Phosphate or MAP, is key for root development. It helps young plants establish deep, healthy roots so they can absorb water and nutrients effectively.
ga: Fosforo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ammonium phosphate loo MAP mli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is cocoa feed and why is it special for cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo niyenii? Ni mɛni hewɔ eji nɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛha cacao tso lɛ?

english: Cocoa feed is a custom fertilizer mix specifically designed for the needs of cocoa trees. It supplies the exact balance of nutrients cocoa trees require to blossom heavily and produce healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa feed ji tsofa ko ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ pɔtɛɛ aha cocoa tso lɛ hiamɔ nii. Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni he hiaa cacao tso lɛ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni wa aba.

english: Why is cocoa-specific fertilizer sometimes hard to find in our local farming communities?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ ewa akɛ aaana ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli yɛ wɔ akutsei ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Specialized fertilizers like cocoa feed are often produced in central facilities and distributed through specific supply programs, which can cause delivery delays reaching rural agro-dealers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi, tamɔ kookoo niyenii yɛ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni ajaa kɛtsɔɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛheɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni akɛhaa akrowai amli okwaayeli jalɔi lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do my crop leaves stay pale or yellowish even after applying basic fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mikɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are missing a specific nutrient that your current fertilizer does not provide. Blending your fertilizer with other nutrients like nitrogen or potassium can solve this imbalance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni o-fertilizer ni okɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɛɛ haaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium futu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsake nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee nɛɛ.

english: How does using the right fertilizer blend make my crops better for the market?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Properly blended fertilizers give crops all the nutrients they need to produce larger, healthier, and better-looking yields, which attract better buyers and higher prices at the market.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni no gbalaa mɛi ni heɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How deep should I bury my seeds when I am planting maize?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep (roughly the depth of your thumb). If you plant them too deep, the young shoot will run out of energy before reaching the light; if planted too shallow, birds might eat them or the hot sun will dry them out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 (aaafee oshishifa lɛ mlibotemɔ). Kɛji odu amɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Young shoots lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha amɛgbi.

english: Why is it wrong for me to plant many seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ madu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted together in one hole, the young plants will fight each other for water, light, and nutrients in the soil. Spacing them out allows each plant to build strong roots and produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei bibii wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa shishifãi ni wa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often should I water my vegetable nursery during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-nursery lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young seedlings need steady moisture. Water them twice a day—once early in the morning before the sun gets strong, and once in the cool evening—so the soil stays moist without drying out the delicate roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Nu shii enyɔ daa gbi. Leebi maŋkpa dani hulu lɛ mli wa Ni ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ mli Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akagbi.

english: Is it good to water my crops in the hot afternoon when the sun is bright?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu shwane mli beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is better to avoid afternoon watering. The hot sun causes most of the water to evaporate before the roots can drink it, and water droplets left on leaves can act like small heat glasses that scorch the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he yɛ shwane mli. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo glase bibii. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and stay weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If your soil looks pale, dry, or dusty, and crops planted there in the past had thin stalks or yellow leaves, the soil lacks nutrients. Adding compost or fertilizer restores food to the soil for healthy growth.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbi, loo eyɛ sũ ni tsei ni eho lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo baai ni miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant the maize grains I bought from the local market for cooking?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ koni mikɛfee niyenii?

english: Market grains are meant for eating and may be old, damaged, or poor varieties that produce low yields. Using certified seeds from an agro-dealer ensures high germination rates and protection against common diseases.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji niyenii ni ayeɔ ni ekolɛ egbɔ, efite, loo eji nɔ ni ehiii ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni ehaa helai ni afɔɔ namɔ baa lɛ hu baa.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to grow after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if heavy rains wash them away, if insects eat them underground, or if they were planted too deep for air to reach them.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie dumɔwui lɛ, Kɛji kooloi ye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a protective shield that keeps them cool while their roots establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ he waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ baa.

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's natural way of saving water during dry periods. As long as the stems stay healthy, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishi wa lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How many rubber trees can I realistically plant on my acre of land in Ghana?
ga: Rɔba tsei enyiɛ diɛŋtsɛ manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: On a standard acre, you can plant between 100 and 200 rubber trees depending on your spacing. Proper spacing gives each tree enough room, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow strong and produce good latex.
ga: on standard area Obaanyɛ odu gum tsei 100 kɛyashi 200, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni okɛ ohe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ nu kpakpa aba.

english: How much rubber yield can I expect from my farm once the trees mature?
ga: Rɔba ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛji tsei lɛ eda kwraa?

english: A well-managed rubber farm can produce anywhere from 800 to over 1,500 kilograms of rubber per hectare every year, provided the trees are healthy and tapped correctly.
ga: Rɔba ŋmɔ ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ajie rɔba kilogram 800 kɛyashi nɔ ni fe 1,500 yɛ hectare kome mli daa afi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni atswa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my rubber trees turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rubber trees naturally shed their leaves during the dry season to conserve water in their stems. This is normal behavior, and fresh green leaves will sprout as soon as the rains return.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ amɛtsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why is it important to hire a trained tapper rather than just any farm worker to cut my rubber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aŋɔ mɛi ni atsɔse amɛ ni amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ moŋ fe ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi kɛkɛ ni amɛfolɔ mi rɔbɔt tsei lɛ?

english: Tapping requires precise skill to cut through the outer bark without damaging the tree's inner growing layer. An untrained worker can permanently scar or kill the tree, while a trained tapper protects the tree so it produces latex for over 20 years.
ga: Tapping biɔ ŋaa pɔtɛɛ ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fãi lɛ amli ni efiteee tso ni miida lɛ mligbɛ fãi lɛ. Nitsulɔi ni atsɔseee amɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee tsei ahe tsɔi loo amɛgbe amɛ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛi ni atsɔse amɛ ni tswaa tsei lɛ buɔ tsei lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛfee latɛs nɔ ni fe afii 20 sɔŋŋ.

english: Will cutting the bark of my rubber tree damage it permanently?
ga: Ani gum tso lɛ yibii ni aaafo lɛ baafite nii kɛya naanɔ?

english: Not if it is done properly. When done by a trained tapper, only a thin layer of outer bark is sliced off, allowing latex to flow while giving the tree time to regenerate fresh bark over a few years.
ga: Dabi kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ tapper ni atsɔse lɛ fee lɛ, kponɔgbɛ ŋmei bibioo ko pɛ baahi. pɛ ni afolɔ koni latɛs lɛ ajɛ mli yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ be ni ekɛfee ŋmei hee hee yɛ afii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune the lower branches of my young rubber trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ gum tsei bibii lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lower side branches forces the young rubber tree to grow a smooth, straight main trunk. A smooth trunk is necessary because it gives tappers a clean surface to cut when the tree matures.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha gum tsei bibii lɛ afee tso titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ja. Tso lɛ yitso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia ejaakɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni abaanyɛ afo mli beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does latex flow better from rubber trees in the early morning than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Rubber trees have high water pressure inside their trunks during the cool morning. As the sun heats up during the day, water evaporates through the leaves, reducing the pressure and causing latex flow to slow down.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ yɛ nu ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛtso lɛ mli yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli Nu lɛ tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli, ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when my young rubber tree is big enough to start producing latex?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-rɔba tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi latɛs feemɔ?

english: A rubber tree is ready for tapping when its trunk trunk measures about 50 centimeters around at a height of one meter from the ground, which usually happens around 5 to 7 years after planting.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaatswa amɛ kɛji amɛshishifã lɛ dalɛ shɛ aaafee sɛntimita 50, ni ji aaafee mita 1 kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni bei pii lɛ ebaa yɛ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can a rubber tree bark regrow after it has been cut for latex collection?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ beni afo lɛ koni ebua latɛs lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Yes, rubber tree bark naturally grows back over 7 to 10 years, provided the initial cuts were shallow and did not destroy the living cambium layer underneath.
ga: Hɛɛ, rɔbɔt tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 mli, kɛji akɛ shishijee ŋmei lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni efiteee cambium ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Since rubber trees take years to start producing, how can my family earn money while waiting for the trees to grow?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ yibii shishi. Te miweku lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ana shika yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni rɔbɔt tso lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: In the first 3 years while the rubber trees are small, you can intercrop fast-yielding crops like plantain, cassava, or maize between the rows to feed your family and generate income.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 lɛ mli be mli ni rɔba tso lɛ ji bibioo lɛ Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ plantains, cassava loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ koni okɛha oweku lɛ niyenii ni oná shika.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their delicate leaves burn easily in full direct sunlight. Keeping mature shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural shield from strong heat and wind while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies heavily on to grow green and healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or a balanced nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmãa damɔɔ nɔ waa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ni akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy bushes but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given excessive nitrogen, they spend all their energy growing stems and foliage above ground instead of storing nutrients in subterranean tubers. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage root development.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aha lɛ nitrogen babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with small dirt-like powder inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji lɛ? yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the daytime to eat young leaves. Applying organic treatments like crushed neem seed solution or targeted spraying early in the morning reaches the pest inside the shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem dumɔwui ni atswa. loo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa. baaha kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aná

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the plant experiences heat stress or severe dry soil, or when there are not enough insects to pollinate them. Regular watering and spreading dry leaves around the base keeps the root zone cool and prevents flower loss.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai ni egbi lɛ nɔ daa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Konu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afite.

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the soil rapidly, suppresses weed growth, and gradually decomposes into natural plant food that enriches your soil over time.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need maximum sunlight to make energy for expanding their underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into the air, improving sunlight exposure and preventing fungal diseases caused by contact with damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly into the seed hole on the day I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afɔseɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds already contain enough natural energy to germinate, and strong chemical fertilizer directly touching a seed can burn the tender initial root. It is safer to wait a few weeks after the seedling emerges and has functional roots before applying fertilizer nearby.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ momo. Ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot during the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This destruction is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, humid, and overly shaded environments. Pruning excess branches lets sunshine and fresh air circulate through the farm, drying out the pods and slowing fungal spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ, ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying leaves with soapy water or neem oil controls these insects and stops leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni ekpa baai lɛ ashishijee.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods now than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Just like human beings get weaker as they age, cocoa trees lose their high yield capacity after about 20 to 30 years. Old trees spend most of their energy maintaining their large stems rather than making pods, which means they need to be pruned back or replaced with new seedlings.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni adesai gbɔjɔɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Cocoa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ yɛ aaafee afii 20 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei agboi anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afo tso lɛ sɛɛ loo atsake dumɔwu lɛ.

english: What does it mean when people say I should run my cocoa farm like a business?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko kɛɛ esa akɛ makwɛ kookoo akɛ jarayeli nitsumɔ?

english: Running a farm like a business means tracking your expenses and crop yields, investing in farm maintenance, and planning ahead to replace old trees so that your farm continuously makes a profit rather than just giving you seasonal pocket money.
ga: Jarayeli okwaayeli tsɔɔ shika ni afiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ he saji. Ni akɛ shika awo ŋmɔ mli saamɔ mli kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni akɛtsake tsei momoi. Koni oha oŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ be fɛɛ be Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha bo be mli shika ko kɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies and cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains and permanent shade from tall forest trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil while they grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ hulutsoo ni hiɔ shi daa kɛjɛɔ koo mli tsei kakadaji amli. Koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees as close together as possible to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe bɔ ni manyɛ koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight over nutrients in the soil and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly ensures each tree gets enough food, water, and air to produce heavy pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni tsei ahe baai tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii, nu, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but they shed many of them if the tree is stressed by a lack of water, missing soil nutrients, or if there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebaafɔ fɔfɔi babaoo kɛji akɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a survival mechanism. When water is scarce in the dry season, the tree intentionally drops its leaves to conserve moisture inside its trunk and branches so it doesn't dry out completely.
ga: Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Beni nu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ amli lɛ he koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads fast in cool, wet weather. If your farm is too dark or overcrowded, air cannot flow through, allowing moisture to stay on the pods and encourage the fungus to grow.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ loo eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu hiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: What is that green leafy plant growing high up on my cocoa tree branches, and why is it harming my yield?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ enaa minitsumɔ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii lɛ?

english: That is mistletoe, a parasitic plant. Its roots grow directly into your cocoa tree's branches to steal food and water, which drains energy away from producing pods and can eventually kill the branch.
ga: No ji tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ mistletoe. ni ji tso ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ Eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kookoo niji anɔ koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ pod feemɔ mli, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ nine lɛ agbo.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra or overgrown branches—called pruning—allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree. It also stops the tree from wasting food on unnecessary leaves, directing energy into growing larger, healthier pods instead.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ—ni atsɛɔ lɛ pruning lɛ—haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu koni tso lɛ akafite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e tsɔɔ he wami ɔ blɔ konɛ e pee podhi nɛ a he wa nɛ a ngɛ he wami ɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni maná tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Tired soil usually shows in your crops through pale or yellowish leaves, thin trunks, slow growth, and trees that produce tiny pods. Adding fertilizer or compost returns missing nutrients to the ground so the plants can feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo yɛ onibii amli kɛtsɔɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. kɛ tsei ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni elaaje lɛ ku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I grow short-term vegetables like tomatoes and peppers alongside my main long-term crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu aduawai ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ? Kɛfata mi be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ he.

english: Vegetables grow and yield quickly, providing you with continuous income and food to sustain your family while you wait for long-term cash crops like cocoa to mature or recover from a bad season.
ga: Aduawai daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya. Enɛ haa onáa shika kɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa ni okɛkwɛɔ oweku lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ shika ni akɛbaatsu nii be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ loo ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ kɛjɛ bei ni ehiii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What are the benefits of planting root crops and vegetables together instead of relying on just one crop?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ shishifãi kɛ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ he kome moŋ fe ni aaadu tso kome lɛ he?

english: Mixing different crops reduces your risk of total loss. If disease or poor weather affects one crop like cocoa, resilient root crops and fast-growing vegetables ensure you still have food to eat and crops to sell.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ebaafite kwraa lɛ baa shi. Kɛji hela loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ ye tso pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ kookoo, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ amɛhe oya kɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya Enɛ baaha oná niyenii ni oye kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Is cassava a good crop to plant if I want a reliable harvest during difficult dry seasons?
ga: Ani ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa kɛji akɛ ehe miihia ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni wa mli?

english: Yes, cassava is a very tough crop that can tolerate poor soil and dry conditions. It stores its energy underground in tubers, making it a dependable backup crop when weather conditions are harsh.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa waa ni baanyɛ adamɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa. Ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ yitso lɛ mli. Ehaa efeɔ tso ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu.

english: Why does cocoyam grow much better in shady and damp areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoyam has broad, soft leaves that easily lose moisture under harsh sun. Moist soil and gentle shade prevent the plant from drying out, allowing it to build strong, healthy roots.
ga: Cocoyam yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shishifãi ni mli wa, ni mli wa.

english: Why do my yam vines need clean mounds and plenty of sunlight to grow big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa gɔŋ ni he tse kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their green leaves to trap sunlight and convert it into energy. Keeping mounds free of weeds ensures that all water and soil nutrients go directly into feeding the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛ tsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii fɛɛ yaa ŋtayaai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do root crops like yam and cassava take so much longer to harvest than leafy vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii heɔ be babaoo dani akpaa fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ?

english: Vegetables direct their energy into quick surface leaves and fruits, while root crops spend months building deep, heavy underground storage tubers full of starch, which takes much more time.
ga: Aduawai kɛ hewalɛ yaa baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ. ni heɔ be babaoo fe nakai

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small, wrinkled fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive heat and dry soil cause pepper plants stress. When stressed, the plant conserves water and energy, resulting in smaller fruits or flowers dropping off early.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ pepper tsei lɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei buɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants get leaf spots and rot quickly after continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ baa nɔ tsɔi ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tomatoes dislike soggy soil and high humidity. Rain splashing on wet soil transfers fungal spores onto lower leaves, which can cause the plant leaves and stems to rot.
ga: Tomato sumɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ fungal spores lɛ yaa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ agboi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees failing to produce many pods even though they have green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ wooo ŋmeii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ baai eŋɔli moŋ?

english: Cocoa trees need a balanced combination of adequate shade, soil nutrients, and pest protection. Too much shade, nutrient shortages, or insect damage at flowering can stop pod development even if leaves look healthy.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo ni sa ni akɛfutuɔ amɛhe. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe Shade babaoo ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha pod lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa po.

english: How can growing food crops help revive my farm's income when my cocoa yield is low?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli shika lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ be mli ni kookoo ni anáa lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Food crops like peppers, tomatoes, and root crops give you immediate harvests throughout the year, keeping cash flowing into your household even when your cocoa trees are going through an off-season or recovering.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tomato, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa shika baa oshia lɛ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale kɛji akɛ cacao tsei lɛ yɛ amɛ be ni amɛtsuuu nii loo amɛmiiya hiɛ po.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants start turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the food it needs to grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year lead to smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Cassava removes specific nutrients from the soil as it grows. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients, so rotating your field with legumes like cowpeas helps put goodness back into the earth.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ. Kɛ́ odu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii woɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ kpakpafeemɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Planting tall shade trees or fast-growing plantains next to them acts like an umbrella, protecting the young cocoa from burning heat and keeping the soil damp.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei kakadaji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with few leaves when I plant them under dense trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ baai fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to make energy and expand its roots under the ground. When planted in deep shade, the crop stretches upward trying to reach the light, leaving it weak with small tubers.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia Yucca koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni egbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be mli kwɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔɔ koni ekɛ la aha. Shi tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and making the whole plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young leaves. Sprinkling or spraying the plants with a mixture of neem leaf extract and water helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu kɛ nu ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ loo okɛshwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack sufficient water in the soil. Regular watering at the root zone and keeping mulch around the stems protects the plants from heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ nu awo shishifãi lɛ ahe daa ni okɛ sũ awo he. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing very small and thin even though the leaves above ground look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deeply cultivated soil mounds to expand their roots. If the ground is too hard or compacted, the tubers cannot grow big even if the top leaves appear fine.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Bulb lɛ nyɛŋ adara agbo eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are mature and ready to be dug up from under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are usually ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up. You can check by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown or black markings, the crop is ready.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi gbimɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Saved seeds can fail to sprout if they were stored with too much moisture or damaged by insect pests like weevils. Drying seeds properly in the sun and storing them in airtight containers protects their ability to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ akakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii efite amɛ. Hulu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ nitoo yɛ tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ he.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm cause my crops to grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops all the food and moisture in the soil, allowing them to grow faster and produce more.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential food found in compost or fertilizer that helps crops build strong, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why is it helpful to plant beans in the same land alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which feeds the soil and provides natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ, ni eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so I can get more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to small, weak crops.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to come up out of the soil at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they were planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil dried out completely, or if the seeds were old and damaged before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa, loo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni efite dani adu.

english: Why do yam vines need to climb up tall wooden sticks to yield big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to generate energy; lifting the vines onto stakes exposes more leaves to the sun and keeps them away from rot on the wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee hewalɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo naa tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass traps moisture in the soil under the hot sun, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off unnecessary branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ wɔ kokoo tsei lɛ aniji ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches allows light and fresh air to reach the cocoa trunk, which reduces black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce bigger pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa babaoo shɛɔ kookoo lɛ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering, which prevents the flowers from successfully forming fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper in the exact same soil where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-tomato lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes suffer from the same soil diseases; planting them in the same spot year after year lets pests and diseases build up in the ground.
ga: Helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ nɔŋŋ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ tomato yeɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii kɛ helai akabote mli. Ebaanyɛ ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil right around the base of the stem starts to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: How do I choose the best crop variety to plant on my farm when there are so many options available?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaakwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Be mli ni nibii babaoo yɛ ni abaanyɛ ahala mli?

english: You should select crop varieties based on your local soil type, rainfall patterns, and local market demand. High-yielding or disease-resistant varieties perform best when matched correctly to your local environmental conditions.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei srɔtoi ni damɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli he hiamɔ nii Nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some tomato varieties turn bright red quickly while others take a much longer time to change color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato komɛi feɔ tsuru ni mli tse oya nɛkɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo dani amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe su.

english: Different tomato varieties have different genetic traits that control their ripening speed. Some are bred to mature quickly to beat dry weather, while others ripen slowly to give farmers a longer shelf life for market sales.
ga: Tomato henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi ni kudɔɔ bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Afɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi koni amɛshwere oya koni amɛye shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anɔ kunim. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwereɔ blɛoo. Koni eha okwaafoi lɛ aná shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Will seeds grown inside a greenhouse perform the exact same way if I plant them out in my open field?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafee amɛnii tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli?

english: Not always. Greenhouse plants are protected from harsh weather, pests, and heavy rains. Planting those same seeds directly in an open field exposes them to natural outdoor stress, so you must ensure the variety is adapted for open-field conditions.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Abuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe. Dumɔwui nɛɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛkpeɔ adebɔɔ mli haomɔi ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: Why do vegetables grown inside a greenhouse structure look greener and healthier than those in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouse structures shield plants from extreme heat, direct sunlight, and excess rain, allowing them to conserve water and leaves to retain high levels of chlorophyll without environmental stress.
ga: Greenhouse gbɛjianɔtoi buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine. Ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ nu he, ni amɛbaa lɛ hu nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ klorofil ni fa babaoo mli ni shihilɛ mli haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to make a farming plan instead of just planting as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔ moŋ fe ni madu nii kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: A seasonal plan helps you align crop growth stages with expected rainfall and peak market prices. Planting without a timeline can cause your crops to flower during dry spells or harvest when market prices drop.
ga: Be mli gbɛjianɔtoo yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ tsei adalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni akpaa gbɛ kɛ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. Dumɔ ni aduɔ ni be bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli loo akpa amɛ be mli ni jara nɔ jara baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow strong at the beginning but then stop growing before they produce any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwere waa yɛ shishijee mli shi no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa shweremɔ dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Crops need different plant nutrients at different stages. They use nitrogen early for leaf growth, but require phosphorus and potassium to form strong roots and flowers. Growth stops if nutrient levels drop during flowering.
ga: Tsei biɔ tso mli niyenii srɔtoi yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Akɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii mra. yɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mli Shi ehe miihia lɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium koni enyɛ efee shishifãi kɛ fɔfɔi ni wa. Dalɛ baakpa kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly during the hottest parts of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to reduce their surface area exposed to the sun. This is a natural defensive reaction that slows down water loss and keeps the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of turning them into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or drought stress. When temperatures get too high, pollination fails, and the plant drops the unfertilized flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ haomɔ kpe. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Ni tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves turning yellow mean the soil is hungry or if my crop has a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ loo hela emɔ mitso lɛ?

english: Nutrient hunger usually causes whole leaves or lower leaves to turn an even yellow shade. Disease symptoms typically show up as yellow spots, irregular patches, leaf curling, or dark brown spots on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ haa baai muu lɛ fɛɛ loo baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ po. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ he okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds keep sprouting on my land even after I have completely cleared the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds leave thousands of dormant seeds buried under the soil for years. Clearing or turning over the ground brings these hidden seeds to the top, where sunlight triggers them to grow again.
ga: Jwɛi haa dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni egboi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ loo atsakeɔ lɛ baaha nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ aya ŋwɛi. Hulu la lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure around the plants can help fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ Tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop every year drains the same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the dirt. Changing crops each season, like switching between maize and groundnuts, keeps the soil rich and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ tsakemɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa helai lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves with sticky, sawdust-like powder inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on young crops. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or approved chemicals when the worms are small prevents major harvest losses.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛtsu nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii beni kooloi lɛ darako lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ ŋmaa nibii wuji ni baafite lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves crumpling up and developing patchy yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by planting stems taken from sick plants. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties stops this disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly loo ŋmeii ni miida ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot while still attached to the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid conditions with little sunlight. Pruning leafy cocoa branches to let air and sunlight in, alongside removing affected pods immediately, keeps the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ. Kookoo baai ni akɛ baai shwieɔ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli kɛfata he lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ajie nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark, sunken, and rotten as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, efoɔ, ni egboɔ beni edara lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, which often happens when soil water levels fluctuate wildly. Watering your vegetables regularly and adding lime or organic matter to the soil stops this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-vegetables lɛ amli daa ni okɛ lime loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni enɛ akafee.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy green branches but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwereɔ shi ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put all their energy into leaves rather than flowers and pods. Avoiding heavy chemical nitrogen fertilizers on leguminous crops allows them to naturally flower and produce higher yields.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ Tsofai ni tsii ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees when setting up a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe beni miito ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight and require shade to survive their early years. Fast-growing plantain suckers provide natural shade and retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Plantain tsei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines wilt during the hot afternoon even when there is moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, yam leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it, causing temporary wilting. Placing dry grass mulch over the planted heaps keeps the soil cool and helps the roots absorb water steadily.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Sweet potato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni egbi ha dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do different sellers and farmers call the same seed by different local names like 'pue' or 'pearl'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nihɔɔlɔi kɛ okwaafoi tsɛɔ dumɔwu kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi srɔtoi tamɔ ‘pue’ loo ‘pearl’ lɛ?

english: Local seed names often vary by dialect, region, or physical characteristics like shape and color. Knowing the crop's growing habits and features helps you identify the right variety regardless of what local name traders give it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutsoŋ dumɔwui agbɛi srɔtoi yɛ wiemɔ, kpokpaa, loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ sui tamɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni onibii lɛ daa kɛ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oyoo tso henɔ ni sa. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi lɛ tsɛɔ lɛ amɛha lɛ,.

english: If I plant very small crop seeds, will the harvest also produce small crops?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwu bibioo ko kwraa Ani kpamɔ lɛ hu baaha ŋmɔshi nibii fioo aba?

english: Not necessarily. Seed size does not determine the final crop size. Many small seeds are bred to grow into full-sized plants, often offering good tolerance to dry conditions and specific soil types.
ga: Halamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ dalɛ etsɔɔɔ naagbee dumɔwui lɛ dalɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui bibii babaoo koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛŋmɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe gbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to plant saved seeds from the local market or certified seeds from an extension officer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ loo dumɔwui ni extension official ko ema nɔ mi?

english: Certified seeds are tested for high germination rates and disease resistance, while local saved seeds are cheaper but may give unpredictable crop sizes and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jara waaa. Shi ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ adalɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo aba shi.

english: Can seeds that grow well in drier neighboring countries like Burkina Faso also produce well on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Burkina Faso ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Yes, crops adapted to drier northern climates like Burkina Faso often do very well in dry regions of Ghana because they require less water and mature faster during short rainy seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi, tamɔ Burkina Faso lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana hei ni nu egbi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu fioo pɛ he hiaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: What happens to small dry-zone crop varieties if my land receives too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni baa dry zone tsei bibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ?

english: Crops adapted to dry areas can suffer from root rot or fungal diseases if they sit in excess water, so they require land that drains water quickly or raised mounds.
ga: Tsei ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo hei ni nu bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya loo gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why is some farmland much easier to dig and clear than other lands nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi amli ŋmɔji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ waaa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Yɛ akutso lɛ mli?

english: Soil ease depends on texture and organic matter. Sandy or loamy soils stay loose and soft, making land preparation easy, whereas clay soils harden when dry and become heavy when wet.
ga: Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ha lɛ damɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ he saamɔ feɔ mlɛo Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ wa kɛji egbi, ni eyɛ tsii kɛji edɔ.

english: How does hard, heavy soil affect the way my crops grow?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsii lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard soil makes it difficult for roots to spread out and find nutrients, leading to stunted growth, thin stems, and smaller harvests compared to softer land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger on one section of my land than on another section of the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli fe ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli he kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality varies across a single field due to differences in soil depth, moisture retention, underground rocks, and past decomposition of organic material.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ he fɛɛ he. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ hewɔ lɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji, tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni eho lɛ amli fitemɔ.

english: Which type of land is best for planting small grain crops?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha dumɔwui bibii adumɔ?

english: Small grain crops generally perform best on light, well-drained soils where their fine root systems can easily grow without getting logged with excess water.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshishifãi kpakpai lɛ baanyɛ adara oya kɛji nu babaoo bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a new crop variety will produce a high yield on my specific land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hee ko baawo yibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Matching the crop's growth period with your local rainfall pattern and soil type is key. Planting a small test plot first allows you to observe how the plant behaves before committing your whole field.
ga: Ehe hia akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ be kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ ato he. Kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni ooodu Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa dani okɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help your maize turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested after three to four months, leaving plenty of space and time for the slow-growing cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 sɛɛ, ni ehaa ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ naa he kɛ be babaoo koni ekwɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What is eating small holes into my cabbage leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Small holes are usually caused by caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, eating the leaves. You can protect your cabbage by spraying natural neem leaf extract or appropriate pest control solutions early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ diamondback ŋmei ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu cabbage he kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I decide the exact day to start sowing seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui lɛ he kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain. Wait until the rain falls steadily two or three times within a week so the soil stays deep-wet, ensuring your seeds do not dry out after sprouting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the soil becomes too dry or when the air temperature gets extremely hot. Giving your plants regular water at the root and mulching the soil keeps the ground cool so fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ sũ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛtsu nii.

english: Can I save some of the hybrid maize seed I harvest this season to plant next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended to plant saved seeds from hybrid crops. Second-generation hybrid seeds usually give much lower yields and weak plants; buying fresh hybrid seeds each season gives you the full harvest yield.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ ni ji hybrid dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni ooohe yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha oná ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers sometimes turn hard and woody instead of soft when cooked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo kɛ́ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody if they are left in the ground too long past their maturity stage or if the plant suffers through extended drought. Harvesting at the right time prevents the roots from becoming tough.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ fe fɔmɔ be lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ais.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize in the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the specific soil nutrients maize needs and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ baaho. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the young pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark, and excessively humid conditions. Pruning excess shade branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight dry out the pods and reduce fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be fe nine. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ amli ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive in tough environments, so they drink water and suck up soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing food from your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant my food crops on land that was previously dug up for illegal gold mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu miniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni be ko ni eho lɛ ajieɔ shika tsuru yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Land damaged by illegal gold mining (galamsey) loses its fertile topsoil and often contains heavy chemicals. Before planting, the land must be leveled, toxic soil removed or treated, and organic compost added over time to rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ (galamsey) lɛ efite lɛ baafite eshikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ tsofai ni tsii yɔɔ mli. Dani abaadu lɛ, esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Jiemɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ poizin lɛ kɛjɛ mli loo tsa nɔ. ni okɛ organic compost afata he yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and wilting when I water them with water from a river near a mining site?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsuɔ shika tsuru lɛ yɛ lɛ shwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: River water near illegal mining sites is often contaminated with heavy metals and chemical residues. This polluted water damages root systems, preventing the crop from taking up nutrients and causing leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ ewo faa mli nu ni bɛŋkɛ hei ni ajieɔ shika tsuru yɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ. ni haa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains, the sun scorches the leaves and dries out the root area, causing young seedlings to die.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tso bibioo lɛ gbele.

english: Why do green cocoa pods turn dark black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a soil-borne fungus that thrives in high humidity and excessive shade. Pruning dense branches to let in airflow and sunlight helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ shade ni fa fe nine mli. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before they turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to shed many flowers because they produce more blooms than they can feed. However, excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks water, nutrients, or proper insect pollination.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ejaakɛ amɛfɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii, loo nibii ni sa ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning purple and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple kɛ yellow yɛ green ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen, which maize needs for leafy growth, while purple leaves show a shortage of phosphorus needed for root and stem strength. Applying the right balance of fertilizers fixes this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ lɛ Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baa ni ji purple lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves above ground but very tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and branches instead of sending nutrients down to build large roots. A balanced nutrient approach encourages proper tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ eniji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji Niyenii mli hewalɛ gbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tuber lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting beans or groundnuts in the same field as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the ground, providing free natural food for crops like maize planted alongside or after them.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow and collapsing from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by fungal or bacterial wilt diseases that attack the internal water pathways of the plantain stem, cutting off water supply to the leaves even if the soil is wet.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fungal loo bacteria wilt ni tutuaa plantain tsei lɛ amli nu gbɛi lɛ. Efoɔ nu ni akɛmajeɔ baai lɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the roots of my crops help them survive during hot dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and keeps moisture near the roots longer during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing smaller pods now even though I haven't changed my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni mitsakeko mishikpɔŋ lɛ lolo?
