english: As cocoa trees grow older, their roots exhaust the essential nutrients stored in the ground. Even if the land looks unchanged, the soil loses its natural strength over years of farming, which leads to smaller pods unless you restore soil fertility with compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da Amɛshishifãi lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni tsakeee moŋ Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ mli. This leads to smaller pods. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ku sɛɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings on the exact same land where my old cocoa trees just died?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni mikookoo tso momo ni egbo etsɛko lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, but old cocoa land often lacks key nutrients and can harbor soil diseases from the previous crop. You should clear old diseased roots, let the land rest or plant cover crops for a while, and enrich the soil before putting in new seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momo amli, ni ebaanyɛ efee shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni jɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli lɛ jɛɛhe. Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ be fioo. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ dani amɛdu dumɔwui heei.

english: How do I know if my cocoa land has run out of nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ efo mi-kokoo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If your trees show pale or yellowish leaves, grow slowly, drop young pods prematurely, or yield far less than they used to, it is a strong sign that the soil nutrients have been depleted and need replenishment.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo, loo ewoɔ ŋmɔŋ oya, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo fe tsutsu lɛ Eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etã ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How long can a single cocoa tree keep producing good yields before it becomes too old?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso kome baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: Cocoa trees usually produce their best yields between 10 and 25 years of age. After about 25 to 30 years, production naturally declines, and the tree becomes more prone to diseases, meaning it may need to be pruned back heavily or replaced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25. Yɛ aaafee afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ lɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni helai baanyɛ amɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni afolɔ amɛ waa loo atsake amɛ.

english: Why do new hybrid cocoa varieties produce pods faster than the old types our parents planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo heei ni akɛfutu mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe kookoo henɔi momo ni wɔfɔlɔi du lɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa seeds are specially bred to grow stronger root systems quickly and absorb nutrients better, allowing them to start producing pods in about two to three years, compared to older varieties that took up to five years.
ga: Afee kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ewaje amɛshishifãi lɛ oya ni eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Akɛ enɛ toɔ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii enumɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Excess water sits on the pods when air cannot circulate, so pruning extra shade branches and harvesting mature pods regularly helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he. No hewɔ lɛ, niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmeii ni edara ni akpaa daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: During the Harmattan, strong winds and high heat cause trees to lose water faster than their roots can drink it. Trees shed leaves to save moisture and protect themselves from drying out completely.
ga: During harmattan Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi ni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: How do tall shade trees help my cocoa farm, and won't they steal food from my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛjuŋ niyenii kɛjɛŋ minibii lɛ amli?

english: Shade trees act as protective umbrellas against harsh sunlight and hot winds, while their falling leaves decay into rich natural fertilizer. While they share soil space, the protection and moisture they provide far outweigh the nutrients they use.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ. Shi hebuu kɛ fɛ̃i ni amɛhaa lɛ fa kwraa fe niyenii ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do many cocoa flowers drop off the tree without ever growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Flowers will also drop naturally if the tree is under stress from drought, poor soil food, or extreme heat.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa

english: What is the best month of the year to plant new cocoa seedlings in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni abaanyɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time is at the beginning of the major rainy season, usually around May or June. This gives young roots several months of steady rainfall to establish deep in the soil before the dry season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee May loo June. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ naa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be nyɔji babaoo koni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat because their leaves dry out faster than their roots can take up water. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shelter and retains soil moisture while the young trees build strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa mɔ náa shihilɛhe be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa

english: Why do my maize plants develop ragged holes in the leaves and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf funnel of the plant to feed on tender new growth. Checking the central funnels early and applying appropriate pest control prevents the caterpillars from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when air temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically. High heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing fertilization and causing the blossom to drop off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava tubers when I plant cassava on the exact same farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava absorbs large amounts of nutrients, especially potassium, from the soil each season. Planting cassava repeatedly in the same spot without resting the land or rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas starves the soil and leads to smaller yields.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo, titri lɛ potassium, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Cassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli kɛtsɔ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Plantain suckers compete directly with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main stem and one or two healthy suckers ensures that the plant directs its energy into producing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and remaining very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips. Removing infected plants early and controlling these insect pests prevents the virus from spreading across the rest of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ni akudɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall with green leaves but produce small or empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Aloo nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: Using only nitrogen-rich fertilizer (like urea) causes the plant to focus all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of grain development. Crops require a balanced mix of nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, to form full and heavy cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ urea) pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ he nii. Yɛ dumɔwui ni baa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni ja he miihia Tsei. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium fata he Koni aná ŋmei ni eyi obɔ ni tsii

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil if I plant right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ fioo lɛ? Klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: The first light rain often only wets the top layer of soil, which triggers the seed to start sprouting, but the deeper soil remains dry. If dry weather follows immediately, the tender sprout dries out or rots underground before it can emerge.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi loo amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛbaaje kpo.

english: Why do my harvested yams decay in storage even though they looked healthy when dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛto eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ atsa lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Minor cuts or bruises made by harvesting tools create entry points for microscopic fungi and bacteria. Storing yams in a cool, airy barn on raised racks and handling them gently prevents soft rot from setting in.
ga: Nibii bibii ni afolɔ loo atswaa ni nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ kɛbaa lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai bibii ni anaaa lɛ baa. Too atomo yɛ shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ. ni emɔ mli blɛoo Enɛ baaye abua ni loo lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water collects on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air within the soil to survive. Standing water cuts off oxygen to the root zone, suffocating the roots and allowing destructive soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is fertile without sending it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse ni mikɛmajeee laboratori?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark brown or black, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well, and contains earthworms or soft insect activity. Dark green weeds growing naturally on the land also signal rich soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ, efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo hu yɛ jɛmɛ. Jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds strip moisture from broad plantain leaves faster than the roots can drink from the dry ground. Placing dry grass or fallen leaves around the base (mulching) keeps the soil cool and retains water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni akɛaabɔle shishi lɛ he (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to plant wood poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tso ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need sunlight on their leaves to produce food that feeds the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground, maximizing sunlight absorption and preventing ground rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ

english: How does planting cowpeas between my maize rows help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpea roots capture nitrogen gas from the air and transfer it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the neighboring maize plants while preventing weeds from covering the ground.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, jwɛi ni akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of leaves. Spraying the leaves with natural neem seed oil or mild soapy water helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui amli fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree lacks moisture or when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) in the soil shade to pollinate them. Maintaining moderate shade keeps the environment humid enough for pollination.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ mli loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ. Shade ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shihilɛ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa kɛha pollination.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for a single strong generation; saving seeds from the harvest results in weak plants with smaller yields and irregular growth in the second season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ foɔ mli krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ kome ni he wa. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or permanent shade trees to cover them and keep the soil moist while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa daa koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs fertilizer before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If your soil looks pale, feels dry and hard, or if crops from your last harvest grew slowly with yellowing leaves, the soil lacks key nutrients. Adding animal manure, compost, or crop fertilizer helps rebuild soil fertility for healthy plant growth.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse Enuɔ he akɛ egbi ni ewa Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ da blɛoo ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmei ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well. Maize grows quickly and can be harvested in a few months, while cassava grows more slowly and takes over the space after the maize is harvested, giving you two crops from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why is it important to wait for the major rainy season before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ dani adu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings require moist soil to sprout roots and fresh leaves. Planting during the dry season will cause the cuttings to dry out and die before they can establish themselves.
ga: Cassava tso ni afo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni shishifãi kɛ baai heei akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛma shi.

english: What causes tiny holes in my vegetable leaves and how can I stop it safely?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ aduawai ahe baai amli lɛ baa ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa amɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars feeding on your crops. You can protect your crops by spraying a natural mixture made from crushed neem leaves and water, which repels insects without poisoning the food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa kɛ nu fee lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii ni ekɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji baaa

english: Why should I cut down excess branches from large shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming shade tree branches allows healthy airflow and balanced sunlight to reach the cocoa plants below. Too much shade traps excess moisture, which leads to fungal diseases like black pod rot.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli, ni hulu la ni sa lɛ shɛɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod rot baa.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from previous harvests, especially hybrid varieties, lose their strength and yield less grain each season. Certified seeds are specially selected to grow faster, resist local diseases, and produce bigger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli Titri lɛ hybrid henɔi Ebaafite hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why do the leaves of my garden eggs curling up during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in dry weather is a plant's way of conserving water to survive intense heat. However, it can also attract tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, so giving the plants adequate water helps them recover.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Shi kɛlɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii hu. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I tell when my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and climbing vines begin to yellow and wither naturally. This shows the plant has stopped growing above ground and stored all its energy inside the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my farm prevent my crops from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your planted crops get all the food they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I clear my land without burning the bush before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi lɛ dani maduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning strips the soil of vital natural food and destroys beneficial organisms that keep the land rich. Allowing cleared bush to decompose naturally adds valuable organic matter back into the soil, helping it retain moisture and nutrients for your crops.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei bibii ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni amɛfite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ekɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it helpful for my farm if I grow cowpeas or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are legume crops that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer, nourishing the surrounding soil and helping cereal crops like maize grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds as close together as possible so I can harvest more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in weak plants and tiny yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to grow full and productive.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from a agricultural dealer instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ dɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, a he dumɔwuhi nɛ a je nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ yi.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and dry conditions while producing high yields. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over generations, often leading to weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is missing nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Applying urea fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and keeps the maize growing healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Urea loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants need to be tied to wooden stakes off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tso ko he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are soft and tend to bend or break under the weight of growing fruit. Staking holds the plants upright, keeping the leaves and fruit off the wet soil where fungal diseases quickly spread.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛkumɔ yɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ tsiimɔ shishi. Tso lɛ ni akɛaama shi shiŋŋ Tsi baai kɛ aduawai anaa koni amɛkahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛkwɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants rely on their leaves catching maximum sunlight to generate energy, which is stored in the tuber under the ground. Staking the vines elevates the leaves to get full sunshine and air, leading to larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baai ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ. ni abaato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni ená hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools in heavy soil and cannot drain away, suffocating the tubers. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. suffocate the head Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani ebafeɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from water stress or extreme heat during hot spells. Giving the plants consistent moisture and mulching around their base keeps the soil cool so flowers can form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nu mli haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ mli fũu be fɛɛ be ni akɛ sũ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into my cabbage leaves, and how can I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ majie amɛ kɛjɛ mihe?

english: These caterpillars hatch from eggs laid on cabbage leaves by moths and feed on the foliage to grow. You can control them naturally by picking them off early in the morning or spraying a liquid mixture made from crushed neem tree leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛwuji amli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii anɔ, amɛkãa kaabe baai anɔ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛdara. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oootsi amɛhe leebi maŋkpa loo nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ efutu lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil, or that waterlogged soil is suffocating the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava rot is caused by fungi or bacteria in the soil, which spreads rapidly when the field holds too much stagnant water or when tubers are left unharvested long past maturity.
ga: Kassava fitemɔ jɛɔ ŋmei loo muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ bafee he ni ekã shi tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni akpaaa amɛ kɛyashi amɛdara kwraa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I plant maize on the same piece of land continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa jɛmɛ be ni ekɛtsa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and twist during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to conserve moisture when the air is dry, but it is also a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are sucking the juice from the leaves while the plant is heat-stressed.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi. Shi eji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites hu he okadi. Amɛmiimu nu kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yɔɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures become too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there are not enough insects around to transfer pollen within the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ebɔle amɛhe Pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛya fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger yield if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks and tiny or missing ears of maize.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my yams grow twisted and thin instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potatoes lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand easily. If the soil is hard, compact, or full of stones, the tubers struggle to penetrate and become bent or stunted.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Yitsei lɛ amlibotemɔ wa ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe.

english: Why did many of the seeds I sowed fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛko shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the soil dries out completely, if underground pests eat them, or if the seeds were too old and dead before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛgboi dani adu.

english: How do weeds reduce the amount of food my crop produces?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ haa niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your crops, effectively starving your plants and hiding pests that attack your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa onibii lɛ teeɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain beside them creates shade and traps moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔs tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the stem looks thick and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny pests called nematodes or stem borers attack the root base underground. Without healthy roots anchored in the ground, the heavy fruit load and wet soil cause the tree to blow over in the wind.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ dumɔwui anɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo mlai. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Yibii ni tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhiɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ amli.

english: Why is my maize growing so slowly and looking pale even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns roots by cutting off air. Plant roots need oxygen to breathe and suck up nutrients from the soil, so waterlogged maize becomes pale and stops growing.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni afoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛjie niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa shweremɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tight and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on the leaves, they pass the virus, which stunts the plant's growth and prevents it from bearing good fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji ŋmeii ye baai Amɛbaagbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa ni etsi enaa koni ekawo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves and vines on my yam mounds turn black and dry up in the middle of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii akuu lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly in warm, wet weather. Rain splashing on the leaves spreads the fungus, causing the vine to die back early before the yam tubers can grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose kɛbaa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ha wain tso lɛ agbo dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over my cowpea leaves just a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young cowpea leaves attract caterpillars and beetles that hatch early in the season to feed on soft leaves. Inspecting leaves early and spraying neem leaf extract can stop the insects before they destroy the crop.
ga: Cowpea baai bibii lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fɔɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni neem baa lɛ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kooloi lɛ anaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning watery and rotting in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rot to spread. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop all their flowers without forming any peppers during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper efeee yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot, pepper flowers experience heat stress and cannot pollinate properly. The plant drops the unpollinated flowers to save water and energy until cooler weather returns.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of small flowers, but almost none of them turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ eko kwraa tsakeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them, along with steady soil moisture. If midges are absent or the tree is suffering from dry spells, the unpollinated flowers simply dry up and fall off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. kɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he Kɛji akɛ teŋdamɔlɔ ko bɛ loo tso lɛ miina hulutsoo be. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there is too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct heat. Sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly, so planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them acts as a natural umbrella to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ nakai tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during rainy season storms when they are bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden fork or bamboo stake prevents wind and soft rain-soaked soil from knocking it down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu agbo ko kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli loo ŋmei ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekajɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ enɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ egbee shi.

english: Yellowing leaves on growing maize usually indicate that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the crop needs for green leafy growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes in the previous season helps keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants shed their flowers before growing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers fall off primarily due to attacks by tiny pests like thrips and flower borers that feed on the buds, or because of severe heat stress. Protecting the plants with targeted pest control during the early flowering stage helps save the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ cowpea fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ fɔfɔi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ tutuamɔ. aloo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei ahe ni abuɔ he kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee be lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem starts to swell and crack open from the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ daa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso titri lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni mli elɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves dry and off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases while catching maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal hela naa yɛ be mli ni onine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and making the plants stunt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites sucking the sap from the undersides of leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the farm early for sucking insects stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Okwaafoi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Bɔni afee ni egbala kooloi bibii lɛ, etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the roots pull up calcium properly.
ga: Rot diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops in the heat of the afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu shwane loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the soil absorbs moisture before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it. Afternoon watering wastes water and can stress hot leaves with sudden temperature changes.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ nu ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ahe afee shoo yɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them while their roots establish during the first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes and tiny green worms inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the fall armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft center leaves of maize plants. Early detection and applying recommended control measures help protect the crop before it gets destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani akpataa amɛhiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or whiteflies that suck the sap from tender leaves and spread viruses, which stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ akpa.

english: Which direction should I point the buds when I plant my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it difficult for roots and branches to grow properly, leading to low yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi kɛ tsei aniji baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts or beans improves the soil for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This leaves natural nutrients behind that help feeding future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni baaye abua ni aha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer directly onto the dry soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve properly so roots can absorb it safely. Putting chemical fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots and damage the crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my crops start wilting in the hot afternoon even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Sandy or low-organic soils lose water quickly through heat and evaporation. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps hold moisture in the ground for longer periods.
ga: Shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔji ni nɔ bɛ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and rot before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, which often happens when watering is uneven or dry spells occur while fruits are developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ba be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can make food. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and off the hot ground, helping the plant grow large tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la kɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees produce very small bunches when many shoot stems grow around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ekomɛi shwereɔ bibii waa beni tsei babaoo shwereɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a main plantain stem, they compete for food and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only two or three, giving the main tree enough energy to make large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ kui wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the farm is waterlogged. Adding fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo afee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves curl up and dry out during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ Harmattan be mli ni nu lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry air and intense sun suck water out of young leaves faster than the roots can pull it from the ground, forcing the plant to drop or curl leaves to save moisture.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ashwie shi loo ebɔle ebaai lɛ ahe koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when the ground feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes tomato leaves to lose water faster than stems can pull it up from the roots. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself and recovers once the afternoon cools down.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tomato baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ shwane mli fɛ̃i ba.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without growing into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when weather gets extremely hot or when water supply is irregular. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and survive the weather stress.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Tso nɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ejo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔ naa foi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the farm is covered in thick shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need controlled sunlight to produce food for flowering and pod development. Excess shade reduces pod growth and traps damp air that encourages black pod disease.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni akudɔ amɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ. Shade ni fa fe nine lɛ haa pod lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flood the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil with water, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, soil fungi attack the weakened roots and cause tubers to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fungi tutuaa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ tuber rot baa.

english: Why does my yam vine dry up and turn brown after climbing the stake?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikwɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn brown and dry out when the tuber underground has finished storing food and reaches full maturity, showing that the yam is ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ blɔfo ni amɛbaagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ gbeɔ niyenii ni amɛtoɔ naa ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa.

english: Why do insect pests spread faster when I plant only maize across my whole land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ midu ŋmãa pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting a single crop gives specific pests an endless food source with no barriers. Mixing different crops confuses pests and stops them from easily destroying the whole farm.
ga: Tso kome ni aduɔ lɛ haa kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa niyenii ni bɛ naagbee, ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi futu mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ afutu amɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds sprout back so quickly right after I clear and clean my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie he lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie asleep deep in the soil for years. Clearing the land exposes the soil to sunlight and rain, which triggers all those hidden seeds to wake up and grow together.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ ateshi ni amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into strips when there is a strong storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are designed with soft tear-lines so wind can pass through them easily. Splitting prevents the heavy wind from snapping the main trunk or uprooting the whole plant.
ga: Afee plantain baai lɛ kɛ yaafo okadii koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Niji ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekakumɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ loo ekajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shishi.

english: Why do I see some farmers building net-covered structures over their crops, and what do they do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa okwaafoi komɛi ni miitswa ŋshɔŋlooi koni amɛkɛha amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ? Ni te amɛfeɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Net-covered structures, often called shade houses or net houses, shield delicate crops from direct scorching sun, heavy rainfall, and destructive insects, helping plants grow healthier without heavy chemical spraying.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ehà nɔ Bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ hulutsoo tsũi loo trellis greenhouses. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ koolooi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii shwieee nɔ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how does it help crops grow better than in an open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: A greenhouse is a frame covered with transparent plastic or glass that creates a controlled environment. It keeps out pests, retains warmth and moisture, and allows you to grow high-value crops all year round regardless of outside weather.
ga: Greenhouse ji tsɔne ko ni akɛ plastic loo glase ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni haa shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ kooloi ni woɔ mɔ mii la lɛ kɛyaa Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be hiɔ shi ni ehaa oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the main difference between growing crops under a mesh net cover versus inside a plastic greenhouse?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ashishi kɛ plastic ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: A mesh net primarily provides shade and keeps out larger insect pests while letting rainwater and air flow through freely. A plastic greenhouse fully encloses the plants to control temperature, moisture, and rainwater completely.
ga: Nɔ titri ni haa ŋshɔŋlooi feɔ hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi wuji ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ oya. Plastic greenhouse bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni enyɛ ekwɛ hulutsoo, fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why are some crops grown inside enclosed structures while crops like maize and yam grow fine in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ tsei komɛi yɛ tsũi ni agbe naa lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Delicate vegetable crops like tomatoes, sweet peppers, and nursery seedlings are easily damaged by heavy rain, hot sun, and insect pests. Tougher field crops like maize and yam are naturally built to survive normal open-air conditions.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ aduawai tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato, bell pepper, kɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ oya. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa lɛ ateŋ ekomɛi ji ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ. Abɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛhi shi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ amli.

english: Is it necessary to build permanent cement bases when constructing a protective crop shelter?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ama simenti shishitoo ni baahi shi daa kɛ́ ama ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhe?

english: No, permanent cement foundations are not strictly required. While concrete makes the frame stronger against strong winds and rot, simple wooden posts or bamboo frames anchored securely in the ground work well for smallholder budgets.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa kwraa akɛ afee simenti shishitoo ni hiɔ shi daa. Shi kɛlɛ, kɔnkrit haa tsɔne lɛ mli waa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ fitemɔ he. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo ŋmeii ni akɛfi shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ okwaafonyo bibioo ko shika he gbɛjianɔtoo mli.

english: Will putting a net cover over my crop nursery protect my young seedlings from harsh sunlight?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: Yes, shade nets act like protective canopies for young seedlings. They block harsh sun rays that scorch tender shoots and soften the impact of heavy raindrops that can break weak stems.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shade net lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni shãa tsei bibii lɛ anaa, ni amɛhaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ baa shi.

english: Why did my plantain farm fail to produce good bunches even after I put in so much effort?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ wooo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ mihe wo mli waa moŋ

english: Plantains often fail due to poor soil fertility, prolonged dry spells without irrigation, infestation by root-damaging nematodes, or diseases like Black Sigatoka that destroy the leaves before the fruit matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Be kakadaŋŋ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ ni nematodes ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ loo helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka ni fiteɔ baai lɛ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How can I prevent my plantain suckers from getting wasted or dying off after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite loo amɛkagbo yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can protect plantains by using clean, disease-free suckers, planting in deep organic-rich soil, mulching around the base to keep soil moist, and clearing weeds that compete for water and nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu plantains ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ Mulch abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ajie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown long before the fruit is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Premature drying of plantain leaves is usually caused by leaf spot diseases or lack of water and nutrients. Removing affected bottom leaves regularly helps keep the disease from spreading to healthy foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ plantain baai lɛ agbiɔ oya ji leaf spot disease loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend new modern farming styles instead of the traditional ways our elders used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi heei baa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔɔfee nɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ Ni wɔ onukpai lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Modern techniques help farmers adapt to changing weather patterns, declining soil quality, and new pests. These methods aim to produce higher yields on smaller pieces of land while protecting crops from crop failure.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ŋaai yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa shi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei Gbɛi nɛɛ ayiŋtoo ji ni amɛná yibii babaoo yɛ he ko bibioo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off my land before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly. Leaving existing shade trees or interplanting with fast-growing crops like plantain creates a protective canopy that helps young cocoa plants survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni yɔɔ momo ni haa hulutsoo baa loo adu tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually show that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to build foliage and stay strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-composted animal manure helps the leaves turn healthy and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ehe awa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or excess water, the plant focuses its energy on expanding stems and leaves above ground. As a result, less food is redirected to the root system to build thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or uneven watering. If the weather is too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve water rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai.

english: Why does heavy rain cause my cowpea plants to lose their blossoms and produce fewer pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall physically knocks delicate flowers off cowpea stems and washes away pollen before insects can fertilize them. Additionally, waterlogged soil stresses the root system, prompting the crop to drop its flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ dani kooloi bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛboteɔ gbalashihilɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hu haa shishifãi lɛ anɔ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli agbee shi.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the main stem to produce a much larger cluster of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee plantains kuu ko ni da kwraa.

english: What happens if I sow my maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the stems to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller cobs or plants that fail to produce cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei loo tso lɛ bafeɔ bibioo kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni anyɛɛɛ afee ŋmei ko kwraa.

english: Does tying my yam vines to wooden stakes really help me harvest bigger yams?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi diɛŋtsɛ ni makpa sweet potatoi wuji?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves high into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture plant food. The energy generated by the leaves travels down into the ground to produce larger, heavier tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni fata staking he ji baai ni awóɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee tsei aniyenii. Hewalɛ ni baa lɛ jieɔ lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji ni tsiimɔ aba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from young leaves, or by viral diseases they transmit. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf curling from spreading across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of the small young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the trunk before maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ ekomɛi batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This usually happens due to 'cherelle wilt,' which is the tree's natural way of dropping extra pods it cannot feed, or due to black pod disease caused by high humidity and poor airflow. Pruning unnecessary branches helps lower humidity and reduces pod losses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ ‘Cherelle wilt’, ni ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ eshwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛɛɛ eye lɛ. aloo yɛ black pod hela ni jɛɔ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii mli baa lɛ hewɔ Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafolɔ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi ni ebaaha pod ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as main food for the plant, or the roots are getting choked by too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure and improving soil drainage helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe titri. Aloo nu babaoo efo shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he, ni aha sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when the hot sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause tomato plants to stress and shed their flowers to save energy. When flowers drop, fruit cannot form, so watering regularly and providing partial shade during very hot weather helps keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi lɛ Yibii nyɛŋ afee. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because heat burns their soft leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving some big trees or planting plantains around young cocoa creates protective shade and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my pepper leaves, and how do I protect my farm from them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-pepper baa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the crop. Clearing surrounding weeds where pests live and spraying safe, recommended insecticides early in the morning can protect your pepper plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ bu yɛ baai amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛshwieɔ nɔ shweshweeshwe. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ leebi be mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu o-pepper tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow tall and thin with very tiny roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The cassava uses all its energy stretching upward to reach light, leaving no food to develop big, healthy roots underground.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kasava lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni ekɛ ehe shwieɔ shi koni emɔ la lɛ nɔ. Eshiii niyenii ko yɛ esɛɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa aba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it good for my farm if I plant groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is very good because groundnuts capture natural food (nitrogen) from the air and put it into the soil. This feeds the maize naturally while giving you two different harvests from the same plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than the yam crops I planted on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe sweet potato tsei ni miyɛ ni mikwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally stronger and faster at stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients than farm crops. Clearing weeds early while your yam plants are young stops the weeds from choking the crop and stealing its food.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya kɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Be mli ni sweet potato tsei lɛ darako lolo Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛjuɔ amɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to plant vegetables this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, and holds moisture without turning into a sticky pool of mud. Adding organic compost or dried animal manure makes poor soil rich and healthy for vegetables.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha aduawai.

english: Why are the tips of my cassava stems turning black and dying back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yitsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Black tips and dying stems on cassava are signs of a plant disease called anthracnose, usually brought by farm pests or infected planting materials. Using clean, disease-free stems for planting stops the sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Tips diji kɛ tsei ni miigboi ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ ji tso hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo dumɔ nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli tsu nii beni oduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I know that my plantain bunch is full and ready to cut down?
