ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ eyi obɔ ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Plantain is ready to harvest when the individual fruits look plump and rounded instead of flat or sharp-edged. Also, the dry flower ends at the tip of the plantain fingers will snap off easily when touched.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛfata he lɛ, fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ plantain niji ahe lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Officer, why are the young leaves on my new cocoa trees turning brown and drying up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso hee lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily scorch. Planting plantain or shade trees next to them provides cover and preserves moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni aaadu yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehiɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Sir, why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight and airflow, along with removing infected pods early, helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Officer, what is causing tiny worms to eat the leaves inside the center fold of my maize plants?
ga: Ofisa: Mɛni haa ŋmei bibioo ko tamɔ nɛkɛ? Ye baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: That is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that burrows into the leaf whorl of maize. Catching them early and applying approved insecticides or ash-and-sand mixtures into the whorls can protect your crop yield.
ga: No baafee Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo sũ kɛ ŋã ni akɛfutu mli yɛ ring lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Sir, why do small insects cause the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites that transmit plant viruses. Spraying soapy water or recommended bio-pesticides early can control these insects before they damage the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites ni hiɛ tsei amli helai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Abaanyɛ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Officer, why does my cassava plant have plenty of thick leaves but only small, thin roots under the ground?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ mli tse waa shi eshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of tuber development. Using balanced fertilizers that contain potassium helps the plant store energy in the roots to produce bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛwo ŋmei shishifãi wuji.

english: Sir, how can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to plant maize without paying for a lab test?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa ni miwooo lab mli kaa he nyɔmɔ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well without staying soggy, has plenty of earthworms, and grows vigorous wild weeds. If weeds look stunted or yellow, the soil likely needs organic compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ. ni edaa ni etsɔɔ koo mli jwɛi ni mli wa Kɛji jwɛi lɛ je kpo akɛ egbɔjɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Officer, should I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year, or should I wait?
ga: Ofisa Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo esa akɛ mamɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can scorch newly germinated seeds in the hot, dry soil before the full rainy season begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baa shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Sir, why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before they turn into actual pods?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed, but heavy flower drop happens due to water stress, poor pollination, or insect damage. Proper weeding, soil moisture, and maintaining beneficial insects help more flowers set into pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. pollination ni ehiii loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Officer, how many shoots should I leave around one plantain stem to get big bunches?
ga: Plantain tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ onukpa lɛ ashi koni ená tsei babaoo?

english: It is best to keep only three shoots per stand: the main bearing plant (mother), one medium shoot (daughter), and one small shoot (granddaughter). Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohiɛ ŋmeii 3 yɛ shidaamɔhe fɛɛ shidaamɔhe: ŋmeii titri kome (nyɛ), ŋmeii teŋgbɛ kome (biyoo), kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome (nabi yoo). Shikpɔŋhosomɔi ni woɔ yibii fe nine lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: Sir, why are the bottom fruits on my tomato plants turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil moisture consistent through mulching helps the plant absorb the calcium it needs.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulching tsuɔ nii daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow fast. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of specific nutrients that maize relies on, and it allows soil pests and diseases to build up, leading to smaller yields each season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Crops cannot absorb dry fertilizer through their roots. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant's roots or evaporate into the air before the crop gets a chance to use it.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛtsu nii.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct heat. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and produce small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When weeds grow uncontrolled, your crops starve because they must share limited resources.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ dara ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ejaakɛ esa akɛ amɛja nibii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for root space and sunlight, causing all of them to grow tall and weak instead of strong and full.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi amli he kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyiɔ obɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if left in waterlogged ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil starves cassava roots of oxygen and creates conditions where fungal diseases grow, causing the tubers to rot beneath the ground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks next to my yam vines for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo emasɛi lɛ? Vine ŋmɔtɔ ni haa amɛkwɔɔ?

english: Yam plants need sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sunlight and protects them from soil pests.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: What causes tiny holes and chewed edges on my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves and feed on them, which weakens the plant if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without turning into peppers during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause stress to pepper plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy and stay alive rather than spending energy producing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I plant them in a sunny open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to heat and cannot withstand direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong stem and leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest so they do not rot?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni amɛgboko?

english: Most improved cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. When the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, the tubers under the ground are mature and ready to be harvested.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Tubers lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, high heat, or an imbalance in nutrients. Giving the plants consistent water and avoiding excessive nitrogen during flowering encourages fruit set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ gĩ trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa waa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen babaoo he yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to make raised dirt mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and warm soil to expand into large, healthy tubers. Making raised mounds breaks up hard earth, improves drainage during heavy rains, and gives the tubers space to grow smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli edɔ koni etsɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ agbala. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. ni oha yitso he lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm reduce the size of my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, light, and soil nutrients. When weeds crowd your crops, they steal essential food, causing the crops to remain small and produce lower yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle onibii ahe lɛ Ebaaju niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally refreshing the field for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee hejɔɔmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Curled or twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Controlling these small pests early stops the leaves from crumpling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ loo efoɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do small beetles bore holes into my dried maize grains after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli beni mikɛwo he ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs inside the corn kernels. Thoroughly drying maize before storage and keeping it in airtight bags or sealed containers suffocates the pests and protects the grains.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto kotoku loo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot dry spell before regular rains start. Waiting until the rainy season has fully established ensures young sprouting seeds will not dry out and die.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ fɛɛ mli koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger when I use irrigation during the dry season compared to relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔ nu pɛ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Irrigation gives crops a steady, controlled supply of water without the dry spells that stress plants. When plants do not suffer from water stress, they spend all their energy growing larger and producing higher yields, even though setup costs are higher.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ daa ni akudɔɔ amɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni haa tsei haoɔ lɛ akpee Beni nu he haomɔ enaaa tsei anɔ hewalɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa moŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop turn yellow when rain floods my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded with water, it starves the roots of air. Plant roots need air to breathe and absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, so suffocating roots cause the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants roll up into tight tubes on very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which stops water from evaporating out of its leaves too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehe he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying, rather than using energy to grow fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do my green leafy vegetables start producing flowers and seeds early instead of growing big leaves in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai wuji yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat signals to the plant that its survival is threatened. The plant rushes to produce flowers and seeds quickly so it can reproduce before the heat kills it, rather than focusing on leaf growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ ewala eba oshara mli. Tsei kɛ oyaiyeli woɔ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui oya koni amɛfɔ dani latsaa lɛ akpata amɛhiɛ. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma tsohi nɛ a daa a nɔ.

english: Why are the fruits on my crop smaller when I plant many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leaving less food for each individual plant to build big fruit.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii fioo koni ewo yibii ni da.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after a big rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over centuries to absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops, allowing them to jumpstart their growth as soon as rain falls.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my fragile young crop seedlings need artificial shade structures, but older plants do fine in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ni aná hulutsoo gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ? Shi tsei ni edara lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young seedlings have very tender leaves and weak, shallow roots that cannot drink water fast enough to replace what the hot sun burns off, while mature plants have deep roots to keep themselves hydrated.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto hulutsoo najiaŋ. Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ koni eha gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli ajɔ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot and soft-spoil so quickly while being transported in wooden crates to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ beni akɛwoɔ tso adekai amli kɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh crops continue to breathe and produce heat after harvest. Packing them tightly in heavy wooden crates crushes the bottom fruits, creating injuries and heat build-up that speed up bacterial decay on the road.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ ehee yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso adekai ni tsii wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaakumɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa mɔ pilaa kɛ dɔlɛ ni haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why does my harvested cassava spoil in just a few days after digging it up from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a hard protective skin like Yams. Once detached from the plant, internal chemical reactions begin instantly to seal root damage, which rapidly turns the flesh dark and unusable within two to three days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ ŋmei ni wa tamɔ cassava. Kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ he Tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ekɛtsiɔ shishifã ni efite lɛ naa. Enɛ baafee duŋ oya ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in the clear sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and need protection from harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them keeps the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebiɔ ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor soil nutrients. Maintaining adequate shade and keeping the soil covered helps the tree retain its flowers until tiny pods form.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa he. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa.

english: How much of my harvest income should I keep to maintain my farm for the next season?
ga: Nikpamɔ mli shika enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛto koni mikɛkwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: It is best to set aside a portion of your crop earnings right after harvest to cover essential expenses like buying seeds, fertilizers, tools, and paying for weeding labor before spending on personal needs.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajara shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fã ko mli koni akɛwo shika ni he hiaa tamɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, nitsumɔ dadei, kɛ nitsumɔ ni akɛbaatsu jwɛi ahe nii dani akɛtsu nii yɛ mɔ diɛŋtsɛ hiamɔ nii ahe.

english: Can I use waste from my poultry coops to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi atsu mli sũ ni efite lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, poultry manure is a rich natural fertilizer that adds organic matter and nutrients to the soil. However, it should be dried or composted first so it does not burn the plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ashishifã ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ agbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ koni akashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in wet, dark, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight into the tree canopy helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why is my farm giving me smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every year drains specific soil nutrients. Rotating your crops or planting legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi. Nibii ni aduɔ loo ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and supports strong cob growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will cutting off branches from my fully grown cocoa tree reduce the amount of pods I get?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Pruning unnecessary or dead branches actually increases yield because it allows air and sunlight to reach the trunk, encouraging new pod formation and reducing plant diseases.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmeii heei feɔ ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baa shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up water and soil nutrients instantly. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing light, food, and water from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛnu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju la, niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow and dry up when the plant lacks sufficient water and nitrogen. When soil moisture drops, the roots cannot absorb nutrients effectively, causing lower leaves to wither first.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nu kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ he. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi lɛ Shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agbi klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is suitable for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ?

english: Cassava grows best in loose, well-drained sandy loam soil where root tubers can expand easily. If water pools on your land for days after rain, the soil holds too much water and will cause the cassava roots to rot.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli mlɛo. Kɛji nu damɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu babaoo mli ni ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living umbrellas that shield the cocoa and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ni elaaje baa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity encourage fungal diseases like late blight. Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil onto lower leaves, causing black spots and leaf decay.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ baai ni fiteɔ baa.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the center of my maize plants, and how do they get there?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te fee tɛŋŋ ni amɛyashɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Moths, like the Fall Armyworm moth, lay eggs on young leaves. Once hatched, the caterpillars crawl into the central whorl of the maize plant to feed on tender growing tissues.
ga: Kplukai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ, woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Kɛji akɛ efɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miida blɛoo lɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after maize naturally restores soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if my plants look like they are growing fine?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni mitsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are hardier than cultivated crops, silently stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight from the soil, which ultimately reduces the size and weight of your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dioo. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii baa shi.

english: Why do seeds saved from my hybrid maize harvest yield much less when I plant them next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu lɛ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum performance in the first generation only. Replanting saved seeds results in weaker plants with uneven growth and lower yield potential.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Eyɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the green vines turn yellow and dry up completely. This signals that the plant has finished growing foliage and stored all its energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi kwraa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ baai lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: If I put artificial light on my nursery crops at night, will it help them grow faster or harm them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ kanei ni akɛfee nibii wo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Ani ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya loo ebaaye amɛ awui?

english: Crops need a natural balance of day and night. While light helps plants make food during the day, continuous light at night disrupts their natural resting cycle, causing stress that can weaken or even kill delicate young plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ afee ekome yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ gbi mli moŋ, shi La ni yaa nɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ gbalaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbe amɛ po baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when exposed to direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops have tender leaves and small roots that cannot pull up water fast enough to replace what evaporates in full sun. Without shade to protect them, severe heat and intense light dry out their leaf tissues until they burn and die.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto nɔ ni efo yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ Kɛji hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni baabu he Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ agbi ni eha eshã ni egbo.

english: Why do my crops wilt when I suddenly cut down all the large shade trees on my farm at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops get used to the moist, cool climate created by shade trees. Removing all shade suddenly shocks the plants by exposing them to strong heat, drying winds, and intense sunlight before they have time to adapt.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ batsɔmɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni mli ejɔ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ feɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo fɛɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ he afee shoo kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni ekɛbaawo mli lɛ nɔ dani ená be ni ekɛtsake ehe.

english: Is it safe to water my vegetable crops during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooha aduawai nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering under strong afternoon sun can shock hot plant roots with cool water, and any water drops left on leaves can rapidly heat up and scorch the plant before the soil actually absorbs the moisture.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha tso ni mli edɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ akpokpo kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ adɔ oya ni eshã tso lɛ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers during a sudden spell of extreme heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni ba trukaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops face sudden environmental stress like hot dry spells, they focus their remaining water and energy on keeping the main plant alive rather than spending energy on producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi kpeɔ trukaa, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: If my crops look weak, why shouldn't I apply a massive amount of fertilizer all at once to save them?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fataa he shikome koni eye ebua nakai tsei lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer at once burns the plant roots and draws moisture out of the plant, turning leaf tips brown and causing more harm than good to an already stressed crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ naagbai babaoo baa tsei ni ehao momo lɛ anɔ fe nɔ ni hi.

english: Do my crops process food and grow mainly during the day or at night?
ga: Ani niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni aduɔ yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli?

english: Crops capture light energy to manufacture food during daytime sunlight hours, but they actually do much of their growing and fruit building during the dark hours of the night using stored energy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ la hewalɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii yɛ hulutsoo be mli, shi tsei babaoo yeɔ amɛbe diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin in heavy shade but fail to make big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ miiya hiɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Shi amɛnyɛŋ amɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Without enough sunlight, a crop spends all its energy stretching upwards toward the light to survive, leaving no extra energy to store away and grow thick root tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpã kɛtee ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ eshwɛɛɛ hewalɛ ko ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli tse ni akɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my crop is dying from a lack of water versus too much heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ nu ni faaa loo dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine hewɔ?

english: Crops suffering from drought will stay wilted even during the cool morning hours, whereas heat-stressed plants with enough soil water only wilt during peak afternoon heat and bounce back by nightfall.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni hɔmɔ emɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ agbi yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hulutsoo haoɔ amɛ ni nu fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baagboi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli pɛ, ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my nursery plants suffer if I remove their shade netting all at once instead of gradually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-nursery tsei lɛ naa amanehulu kɛji mijie shade netting lɛ fɛɛ shikome moŋ fe ni mafee fiofio lɛ?

english: Plants adjust their leaf thickness and moisture levels to suit their environment. Uncovering them completely without a gradual transition exposes tender leaf tissue to sudden high light levels, causing sun scorch and plant collapse.
ga: Tsei tsakeɔ baa lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ latsaa koni ekɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akpã gbee. Gbelemɔ ni yeɔ emuu ni tsakemɔ fiofio bɛ mli lɛ jieɔ baa bibii lɛ akpo kɛyaa la ni naa wa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni tsei shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my soil need to hold water for my crops to grow well during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi nu mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil acts like a sponge that stores water for roots to drink between rains. If the soil cannot hold moisture, the plant roots dry out and cannot absorb the nutrients needed to produce healthy crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni ekɛ nu toɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛnu kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do young crop seedlings suffer more from a lack of water than fully grown plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa nu ni faaa fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young plants have small, delicate roots that stay near the surface where soil dries out fast. Older plants have deeper root systems that can search far underground to find stored water.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ atao nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some types of soil dry out quickly while others stay wet for days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔji komɛi gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwieɔ shi gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has loose, large particles that let water drain straight through, while clay or dark organic soil has tiny spaces that trap and hold onto water for a long time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni haa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. koni akɛ nu ato be kakadaŋŋ

english: How does covering my farmland with dried leaves help keep water in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi ha he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground creates a shield against the hot sun. This prevents soil water from evaporating into the air, keeping moisture right where the plant roots can reach it.
ga: Mulching haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ gbɛ. Koni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ hei ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aya lɛ.

english: Why do government extension officers come to collect water and soil samples from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli extension nitsulɔi lɛ miibua nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Testing allows experts to examine the hidden health of your soil and water. The results show what nutrients your farm lacks so the government can give you the right advice to improve your harvest.
ga: Kaa haa ŋaalɔi leɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ kɛ onu lɛ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ ha yɛ teemɔŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baatsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni nɔyeli lɛ anyɛ aha bo ŋaa ni ja koni oha onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does testing the water I use for irrigation help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ kaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Water can contain hidden salts or chemicals that harm plants. Testing ensures the water is safe so your crops can drink freely and thrive without getting scorched or diseased.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmei loo tsofai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni yeɔ tsei awui yɛ nu mli. Kaa haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe. No hewɔ lɛ, onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ anu nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni shãaa loo hela emɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: How can agricultural research help me get a better harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmaa kpakpa kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Research identifies crop varieties and farming methods best suited for your local climate. Applying these proven methods protects your crops from failure and improves your farming business.
ga: Feemɔ niiamlitaomɔ koni ona tsei srɔtoi kɛ okwaayeli gbɛi ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Gbɛi ni ana he odaseyeli nɛɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he, ni ehaa okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I keep caring for my crops continuously instead of leaving them to grow on their own after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya nɔ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need ongoing support through weeding, watering, and protection. Abandoning them midway allows weeds and pests to steal their food and water, leading to poor yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ hebuu nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ fã lɛ, jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stunt even when there is plenty of water on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off their air supply. Roots need a balance of water and air in the soil to breathe and pull up food.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to keep weeding my cocoa farm every season even when the trees are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ daa afi kɛji tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Weeds constantly compete with cocoa trees for soil moisture and nutrients. Regular weeding ensures all available water goes directly into supporting your cocoa pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ be fɛɛ be kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyeɔ ebuaa o-cocoa pods lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the rice seeds I buy at the local market are good enough to plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good seeds are clean, heavy, and free from holes or discoloration. You can test them by putting them in a bucket of water; healthy seeds will sink to the bottom, while weak or insect-damaged seeds will float to the top and should not be planted.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai ahe tse, amɛhe wa, ni bu loo amɛhe su tsakeee. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu baagi ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui kpakpai baagbee shi kɛya shishi. Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni kooloi efite lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ.

english: Why does my harvested grain turn into dust and spoil after I put it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli ewo sũ ni efite beni mikɛwo nibii atoohe kotokui amli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That dust is caused by tiny insects called weevils that eat the grain from the inside out. If your grain is not completely dried in the sun before bagging, the moisture left inside allows insects and mold to multiply quickly and destroy your crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ sũ baa. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmei. ni yeɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo nɔ Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ egbiko yɛ hulu mli dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, Fɛ̃i fɛɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ mli lɛ baaha kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo aya hiɛ oya ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some extension officers say we should clean or treat our seeds before putting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ wɔtsumɔ dumɔwui ahe loo wɔtsu he nii dani wɔdu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds from the market or previous harvests often carry tiny insect eggs or fungal diseases on their skin that you cannot see. Treating or cleaning seeds removes these hidden threats so the young crop doesn't rot underground before sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ, kooloi bibii bibii yɔɔ mli. Aloo, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ekpɛtɛ hewolo lɛ he yɛ he ni onyɛɛɛ ona lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni abaatsa loo atsuu he lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ gbeyeishemɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ kɛya. Enɛ ji koni tsei bibii lɛ akagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure straight onto my crop plants as soon as I clean my poultry house?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie tsina tsina shĩa lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and hot, which will burn the roots and stems of your young plants. You should pile the manure in a shaded area for a few weeks to let it rot and cool down into dark compost before spreading it on your farm.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ otsii fioo komɛi koni eha egbo ni edɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ mli dani okɛgbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ ŋmei?

english: Cassava needs soft, loose soil where its tubers can easily grow big underground. If water sits on top of your land like a pond for days after rain, or if the soil is hard rock and heavy clay, cassava tubers will rot or stay very small.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia cassava. Eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nubu gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji tɛ ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii Kasava shishifãi lɛ egbo loo amɛji bibii waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though rain has been falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is missing essential nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. While water keeps the plant alive, adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the food it needs to turn green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Eyɛ mli akɛ nu haa tsei hiɔ shi moŋ, Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do insect pests destroy my crops more when I plant the same crop in the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: When you plant the same crop every season, insect pests stay in that soil and wait for their favorite food to appear again. Changing crops every season starves the pests and breaks their breeding cycle.
ga: Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɛɔ niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa lɛ ni eba ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi lɛ ni ebaafite bɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the crop seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally excel at stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because they are adapted to survive tough conditions, they will quickly starve your planted crops unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amɛhe esa yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jumɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛbaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni odu lɛ oya. Ja ojie amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need full sunlight to make energy for flowering and producing fruit. When planted under deep shade, the plant stretches upward searching for light instead of using its energy to produce pepper pods.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie amɛhe kpo ni amɛtao la moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee pepper pods.

english: Why do my crop flowers fall off without growing into fruit during very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress the plant, causing it to shed its flowers to save water and stay alive. Watering early in the morning and keeping the soil covered with dried grass helps the plant retain moisture and keep its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛshwie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: If my maize crops look healthy now, can I stop spraying them with pest medicine, or do I have to keep spraying until harvest?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo bianɛ Ani manyɛ makpa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ maya nɔ mafɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Stopping pest treatment early can allow hidden insects or eggs to multiply quickly and destroy your yield. You should follow the full recommended spraying schedule rather than stopping as soon as the plants look green.
ga: Kpaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii. Esa akɛ onyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoi fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ asɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, ke tso ɔ pee eŋɔli pɛ ɔ, kpa.

english: If I put half the recommended dose of pesticide on my pepper plants to save money, will it still protect them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ fã ni awo he ŋaa lɛ wo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ koni mikɛ shika akafite hu? Ani ebaaye ebua lolo ni ebu pepper tsei ahe?

english: Applying less than the recommended dose does not kill all the pests; it leaves the strongest ones alive. These surviving pests can then multiply and become resistant to the chemical, making future outbreaks harder to control.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ fɛɛ. Ehaa mɔ ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ hiɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ wala nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛfɔɔ bii ni amɛfeɔ mɛi ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ tsofai. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ abaakwɛ helai ni baaje kpo wɔsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to spray my cocoa trees repeatedly for black pod disease instead of just spraying them once when I see the rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔkɛ tsofa afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ shii abɔ koni wɔkɛtsa black pod hela lɛ moŋ fe ni wɔbaashwie tsofa shikome beni wɔna akɛ aduawai lɛ egbo lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads continuously during the rainy season. One spray only kills active fungus at that moment, so regular treatments are needed to maintain a protective shield on new and growing pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Spray kome pɛ baagbe tsɛŋemɔ hela ni tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɛɛ pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni atsa amɛ daa koni akɛbu gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ ahi shi.

english: My cassava leaves turned yellow, but after applying plant medicine they look green again; can I safely stop the treatment now?
ga: Mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Shi beni akɛ tso tsofa tsuɔ nii lɛ Ebatsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ. Ani manyɛ makpa tsofafeemɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe bianɛ?

english: Green leaves mean the plant is recovering, but the underlying disease or pest may still be present in smaller amounts. Stopping treatment too early often causes the sickness to return worse than before.
ga: Baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihe ejɔ. Shi hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lolo yɛ fioo fioo mli. Bei pii lɛ, tsofafeemɔ ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa shi fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: What should I do if my crop shows signs of rot again right after I finish the full cycle of recommended chemical treatment?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jie ŋmɔtɔ he okadii akpo ekoŋŋ beni migbe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ naa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When sickness returns immediately after treatment, the pest or fungus may have developed resistance or environmental conditions favor new infection. You should consult an officer to switch to a different type of plant medicine or use complementary cultural methods.
ga: Beni hela lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ tsamɔ sɛɛ Ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo ŋmei lɛ nyɛŋ eye hela lɛ nɔ loo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hi kɛha helai heei. Esa akɛ okɛ onitsulɔi lɛ agba sane yɛ tso tsofa kroko ni oootsake loo gbɛi krokomɛi ni akɛfataa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛtsu nii lɛ he.

english: What will happen to my cocoa farm's yield if I gradually reduce the amount of fertilizer I apply every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji miba nɔ fiofio? Ani abaajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ daa afi?

english: Gradually reducing fertilizer without replacing lost soil nutrients causes the soil to deplete over time. As a result, crop yields will steadily drop and the trees will become weaker and more prone to diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ fiofio ni akɛ sũ mli nibii ni elaaje lɛ etsakeee lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi. ni tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni helai nyɛɔ emɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why does my yam crop seem to wither when I suddenly stop giving it plant food mid-season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa amɛ niyenii hamɔ trukaa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams require a steady supply of nutrients during tuber formation. A sudden stop in nutrient supply causes severe shock to the plant, forcing it to drain energy from its leaves to survive, which stunts root growth.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia sweet potato yɛ be mli ni efeɔ tuber lɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ ni akpaa trukaa lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ ni naa wa baa tso lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Do crops like tomatoes get dependent on synthetic fertilizers, making them collapse if I stop using them?
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tomato lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ anɔ. Ni ani ebaafite kɛji mikpa ekɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Crops do not get addicted, but heavy reliance on synthetic fertilizers can degrade natural soil microbial life. When you suddenly stop applying fertilizer, the depleted soil cannot support the plant until organic health is restored.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ jeee nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli. Shi kɛ́ akɛ he fɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ anɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ aba shi. Kɛji okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ trukaa Kɛyashi be mli ni bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tsei.

english: If I want to stop using chemical sprays on my farm completely, can I just stop today or do I need to phase them out slowly?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miisumɔ ni makpa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kwraa hu? Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɛnɛ loo esa akɛ makpa fiofio?

english: Stopping chemical sprays abruptly without having alternative organic protections ready leaves crops vulnerable. Transitioning gradually allows natural beneficial insects and biological soil activity time to rebuild.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akpaa trukaa ni nɔ kroko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ oshara mli. Tsakemɔ lɛ baaba fiofio. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ naa be kɛ be ni amɛkɛbaatswa shikpɔŋ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm come back stronger if I reduce the weedicide amount or apply it incompletely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa waa ekoŋŋ kɛji miba tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ loo mikɛtsuuu nii kwraa lɛ?

english: Applying too little weedicide weakens weeds without killing their roots. This allows them to recover quickly, produce seeds, and outcompete your crops for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni efiteee amɛshishifãi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waaa oya. dumɔwui afeemɔ ni oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant maize or cocoa if I need money quickly?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa loo kookoo kɛji shika he miihia mi oya?

english: Maize is a short-term crop that matures in just 3 to 4 months, offering fast cash to meet immediate needs. Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that takes 3 to 5 years to yield, but it provides steady income for decades once it starts producing.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, ni ehaa anáa shika oya koni akɛtsu hiamɔ nii ni he hiaa oya lɛ ahe nii. Cocoa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani anáa, shi ebaaha aná shika ni yaa nɔ daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akɛ abɔi ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to grow cassava alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Growing cassava or food crops with young cocoa provides immediate food and income during the years you wait for cocoa to mature. The short-term crops also protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight.
ga: Cassava loo niyenii ni akɛ cocoa bibii baadu lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afii ni okɛbaamɛ ni cocoa lɛ agbɔ lɛ amli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ hu buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he.

english: How can I make sure I get good profit from my corn farm this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: To maximize profit, use high-yielding certified seeds, apply fertilizers at the correct stages, clear weeds early so they do not steal nutrients, and plant right at the start of the rains.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo Kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ atsu nii. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ he ni sa. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. bɔni afee ni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ

english: If I harvest my maize, will the same plant grow back and give me another cob?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmãa Ani tso lɛ nɔŋŋ baakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmãa ekoŋŋ?

english: No, maize is an annual plant that completes its full life cycle in one season. Once the stalk produces its cobs and dries, it dies, and you must plant new seeds for the next harvest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ji tso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa afi ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ kwɛ̃ ni egbi lɛ, egboɔ ni esa akɛ odu dumɔwui heei kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why can I leave cassava in the ground for a long time, but maize must be harvested right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abaanyɛ ashi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ shi esa akɛ akpa ŋmei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores its food reserve in underground roots that stay fresh in moist soil for up to two years. Maize stores its food in dry grains on above-ground cobs, which rot or get destroyed by pests if left on the field after ripening.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli, ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashiɔ afii enyɔ. Abele toɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi mli yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. ni baafite loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: How does a dry cassava stick grow into food after I put it in the soil?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ adu ŋmei ni egbi lɛ akɛ niyenii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small living nodes along their length. When buried in moist soil, these nodes sprout roots downwards into the earth and shoot green leaves upwards, with the roots swelling over time into edible cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛlɛɛmɔ mli kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni ayeɔ.

english: How long can cassava roots remain safely in the ground before they spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe dani amɛgboi?

english: Most cassava varieties can stay safely in the soil for 12 to 24 months. However, if left too long, the roots become hard, woody, lose starch quality, and eventually rot.
ga: Kasava babaoo baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 24. Shi, kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfeɔ tamɔ tsei, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ

english: Can I plant corn on land where I just cleared an old farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ momo ko mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cleared farm soil is often rich in organic matter, making it great for fast-growing crops like corn that need plenty of nitrogen to yield well.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ni biɔ nitrogen babaoo koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why does my soil become weak after I plant maize and cassava on it many times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ beni midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shii abɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize and cassava absorb high amounts of soil nutrients quickly to produce their food. If you replant them continuously without adding fertilizer, animal manure, or rotating with legumes like cowpea, the soil loses its fertility.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa gbalaa niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛji akɛ oya nɔ odu ekoŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli.

english: Can I take part of the corn I harvested and plant it as seed for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eko ni madu akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: You can, but harvested grains often produce lower yields and weaker plants in the second generation. Purchasing fresh, high-quality certified seeds ensures high yields and uniform crop growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha yibii babaoo aba ni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the dirt naturally, making the soil fertile again for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the sap and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate pesticides keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni sa tsu nii lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of maize plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended insecticides or neem extracts protects the growing point of the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei akutsei amli lɛ. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, causing fungal infections. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the roots dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. kɛ fungal infection baa Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Yam vines need to catch direct sunlight to produce energy and grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing diseases and maximizing sunlight exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why should I cut away some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ babaoo tsɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and heat. Keeping taller shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain protects young cocoa from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops yield less even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for the fertilizers and natural nutrients in the soil. Even with enough rain, crops will starve if weeds are stealing their food.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ Dumɔwui hu yeɔ hɔmɔ kɛji jwɛi ju amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees protect them from direct sun and strong winds while keeping the surrounding air and soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting trees too close together causes their roots and leaves to fight for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every tree enough room to grow big and reduces the spread of farm diseases.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa ni ehaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: When cocoa trees lack sufficient soil food, their leaves often turn yellowish, growth slows down, and they produce very few pods. Applying fertilizer restores missing soil nutrients so the tree can produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni elaaje yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo nibii ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: What can I feed my crops if I cannot afford chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ maha niyenii kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You can feed your soil using organic material like compost, decomposed animal manure, or fallen leaves. As these materials break down, they release natural nutrients into the soil and help keep it moist without extra cost.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ Kɛ́ nibii nɛɛ fite lɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi?

english: Cutting off extra or weak branches—a practice called pruning—allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ—haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds stop my cocoa plants from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitsi mi cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by taking away water, light, and soil nutrients meant for your crop. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your cocoa trees get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii yɛ mli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi daa lɛ, ehaa cacao tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: This blackening is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning excess branches for sunlight, and removing infected pods quickly helps control its spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni ji black pod lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. weeding Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ bɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree experiences stress from dry weather, poor soil food, high heat, or pest damage. Giving trees adequate shade and maintaining soil fertility helps keep flowers attached until pods form.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui Tso lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How does hot, dry weather affect my cocoa trees?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ saa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During the hot, dry season, trees lose moisture quickly, causing leaves to wilt or drop and young pods to shrink. Leaving dry leaves on the ground around the tree trunk acts as mulch to trap soil moisture.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi Eshiɔ baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.
