english: How do I tell when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color, usually turning from green or red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting pods at full color ensures maximum bean quality and prevents them from over-ripening and rotting.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Pods ni akpa ni yɔɔ sui fɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ baa. ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ fe nine ni amɛkafiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when I clear all the big trees and plantain suckers around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ lolo beni mijieɔ tsei kɛ ŋmeii ni edara ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa shoots are very tender and burn easily under direct sunlight. Growing plantains or keeping shade trees around them provides temporary cover from harsh sun and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ loo hulutsoo ni akɛhaa he fɛɛ he Tso lɛ baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa be kukuoo ko. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How do I stop my plantain trees from falling over when heavy wind or rain hits my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi midumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni naa wa ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them vulnerable to strong winds. You can prevent them from falling by supporting the stem with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles firmly anchored into the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Obaanyɛ otsi enaa koni ekagbee shi kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo tso ni wa ni akɛfi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni oookɛfi tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant nutrients away from the main stem. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tso wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize needs in large amounts to grow. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the season will solve this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn plants look like they have tiny holes eaten through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii ni ayeɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Checking plants early and applying neem seed extract or appropriate pesticides directly into the plant funnel helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots thin and small even though the leaves above ground look bushy and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are crowded, cassava focuses its energy on growing tall leaves instead of growing tubers under the ground. Giving crops proper spacing and avoiding excess nitrogen late in the season helps tubers swell.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ baai kakadaji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni sa ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ he yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto stakes instead of letting them grow on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up into the sunlight, allowing the plant to generate more food for the root, resulting in larger yam tubers and reducing rot from wet ground contact.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo amɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji. ni eha fitemɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods helps air flow and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why does my farmland turn hard like rock after it rains, making it hard for seeds to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ani ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui akɛ amɛakwɛ̃?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure. Adding compost or leaving crop residues on the soil helps keep it loose, retains moisture, and makes it easy for crop roots to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of plant food like calcium cause tomato plants to drop flowers to save energy. Watering regularly and mulching the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and prevents flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tsei amli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishi daa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I prepare my land so that it produces a bigger harvest next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Clearing the land properly and mixing organic matter like compost into the soil restores essential nutrients, helping crops feed better and produce higher yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I clear big rocks and tree stumps from my land before bringing in a tractor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tɛi wuji kɛ tsei akui kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ trakta lɛ aba?

english: Heavy farm machinery needs smooth, open pathways to plow evenly without breaking equipment or damaging the structure of your soil.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni tsii lɛ koni amɛtsu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛfiteee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ loo amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii.

english: Why is it better to expand my farm step-by-step rather than clearing all the land at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ magbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli fiofio moŋ fe ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Setting up your field gradually lets you manage labor costs effectively, learn how your land reacts to new techniques, and prevent severe crop loss if rain pattern changes.
ga: He ni oyɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo fiofio lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasemɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ ŋaai heei ahe ni otsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ naa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi tsake.

english: Can machines do all the work on my farm without me checking on the crops regularly?
ga: Ani tsɔne ko baanyɛ atsu nitsumɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa?

english: While machines handle heavy tasks like tilling, human care is essential to spot crop diseases early, check soil moisture, and make practical decisions machines cannot make.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsɔnei tsuɔ nitsumɔi ni tsii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii lɛ, gbɔmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ he miihia koni ana ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai mra. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha ni okpɛ yiŋ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni tsɔnei nyɛŋ akpɛ

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures equal spacing between plants so they do not fight for sunlight and water, while also making weeding and machine passage much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ekɛ hulu la kɛ nu etswaaa akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi kɛ tsɔne gbɛi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant the same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil; rotating crops gives the land a rest and helps maintain strong soil productivity.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ mli wa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural survival response where the plant reduces its surface area to trap moisture and prevent water loss during intense heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo hetoo ni tsei baa shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu ni laajeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do cassava roots rot when water collects and stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa ni ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air from the soil space to breathe; standing water chokes the root system, causing decay and inviting fungal diseases that destroy the harvest.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baa.

english: How does breaking up hard soil before planting help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mifoɔ mli dani miduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Loosening hard soil allows crop roots to dig deeper into the ground where moisture stays hidden, keeping the plant alive even when rain stops for weeks.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa otsii komɛi po sɛɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with strong roots that absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, which is why early clearing is needed to give your crops room to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli wa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni oha otsei lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying whenever I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni majie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn easily under direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, cooling the environment and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves but produce tiny, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi ani eyɛ yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of roots. Proper plant spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to store starch downward in the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ebaahe be dani baa kɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ starch toɔ bulbs lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam plants need long wooden stakes for their vines to climb instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for tuber growth. It also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu. Tsi fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during light windstorms, even when they are carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa waa mli lɛ? Kɛ́ ewo yibii po

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can easily be weakened by underground pests like root nematodes or weevils. Supporting heavy fruiting stems with bamboo props and keeping the base clean stops them from toppling over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo weevils baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Nibii ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ kɛ shishitoo lɛ ni ahaa ehe tseɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes and powdery droppings inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfee powda yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of young maize to feed on tender leaves. Checking fields early allows you to spot and treat them before they destroy the plant's growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ashishi koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni okwɛɔ lɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ onaa amɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stem before they can form small green tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛmiitsɔ tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering cause stress to tomato plants, making them shed their blossoms to conserve water. Mulching the soil and keeping it evenly moist helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Mulching kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my chili pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves. Controlling these tiny insects early stops the new leaves from crumpling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaye abua ni baai heei lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize turning yellow in a V-shape and dying before the corn ears form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele toi jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the center of lower maize leaves is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs high nitrogen to stay green and produce full ears, which can be corrected with nitrogen fertilizer or rich compost.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ aba. Abaanyɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ajaje enɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension official lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When harvested, their roots and fallen leaves decompose, releasing natural fertility into the soil that feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Shishifãi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ. Jiemɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni haa niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot spell before regular rains truly start. Sowing too early causes seeds to sprout and then dry up and die in the hot, dry soil due to a lack of follow-up rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Leaving or planting taller shade trees provides a natural canopy that lowers temperatures, retains soil moisture, and protects fragile young cocoa leaves from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni obu kookoo baai bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small, thin tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or have excess nitrogen in the soil, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storage roots. Giving plants enough space and balanced nutrients ensures the energy goes down into making thick tubers.
ga: Beni tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai anɔ moŋ fe ni ebaabua shishifãi anaa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa ekɛ hewalɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ afeemɔ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize stalks turning yellow in a 'V' shape while the plants are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant starves and takes nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing upper leaves and developing cob, causing the lower leaves to die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ haa ŋwɛi baa ni miida kɛ ŋmãa ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ gboiɔ oya.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and stake my yam vines on tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni mafo he ko ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. Lifting the vines on stakes helps leaves catch light while keeping them off wet soil where fungal diseases quickly breed and rot the foliage.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni miida. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfite oya lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants dry up and fall off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni pepper ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Shedding blossoms is the plant's survival response to conserve moisture and energy during dry or stressful periods.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Defoliation ji tso lɛ wala shihilɛ hetoo koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo haomɔ be mli.

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main stem and one small successor allows the mother plant to focus all its strength into bearing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ tso titri kome kɛ seshi kome pɛ hiɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ ehewalɛ wuji ni tsii lɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ he nii.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce few pods when I apply heavy nitrogen fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nitrogen ŋmeii ni tsii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans naturally feed themselves nitrogen from the air through friendly bacteria in their roots. Adding high-nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into growing leaves only, reducing the overall number of flowers and bean pods.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yeɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaalaka tso lɛ ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ayibɔ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my cashew blossoms wither and turn black during the hot dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture rapidly from delicate flowers, while sucking insects like tea mosquito bugs attack soft blooms. Protecting the farm boundary with windbreak trees and monitoring for pests preserves the flowers for nut formation.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Akɛ tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ abuɔ ŋmɔ husui ahe kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni ŋmeii afee.

english: Tightly curling tomato leaves are often a sign of viral infections spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies, or a defensive reaction to severe heat and drought. Controlling insect vectors and keeping soil consistently moist keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo nɔ ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he. Koolooi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots soft-rot and turn dark when rain collects and sits in my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ bua ehe naa ni eta miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need to breathe air in the soil. Waterlogging chokes off oxygen supply to roots, causing them to drown and creating ideal conditions for destructive soil fungi to attack and rot the plant base.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa amɛboteɔ nu mli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ atutua tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do animals and insects keep digging up and eating my seeds right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi bibii shwieɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Newly planted seeds are soft, moist, and packed with nutrients, making them an easy meal for birds, rodents, and insects. Protecting seeds with proper planting depth, seed treatments, or physical covers prevents pests from destroying them before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, edɔ ni niyenii eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa okpoi, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi niyenii feɔ mlɛo. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ. dumɔwui akwɛmɔ loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa he Enɛ baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What causes my young crop shoots to look chewed off or disappear overnight?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre loo amɛmiilaaje nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Nocturnal pests like cutworms, grasshoppers, or small rodents feed on tender young stems at night because the shoots are soft and easy to eat. Regular field monitoring and early pest control measures are required to protect vulnerable young plants.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli kooloi tamɔ cutworms, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii bibii yeɔ tsei bibii gbɛkɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni eyeli waaa. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ ŋmɔ mli daa kɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa mra. Koni akɛbu dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ahe

english: Why do some of my crops fail to sprout even after I put them in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds require a balance of moisture, proper temperature, and air to sprout. Planting too deep, planting in dry soil before steady rains, or using damaged seeds can prevent them from germinating properly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ. hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa yɛ shweremɔ mli dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Aloo dumɔwui ni efite ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How do I know if I am planting my seeds at the right depth in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: As a general rule, seeds should be planted at a depth equal to two or three times their width. Planting too deep starves the seed of energy before it reaches sunlight, while planting too shallow leaves it exposed to birds and heat.
ga: Taakɛ eji mla lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛlɛɛmɔ lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ dumɔwui lɛ aye hɔmɔ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ kɛ okpoi aná hulutsoo.

english: Why do my crops need space between them instead of planting many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hiaa ni gbɛ ahi amɛteŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets what it needs to grow strong and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is suitable for farming before I start clearing it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha okwaayeli dani mabɔi nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ?

english: Good farmland generally has dark, rich soil, stays moist without being waterlogged for days, and supports healthy wild plants. High-quality soil provides essential nutrients that crops need to grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni baa nii. Ehiɔ shi ni nu bɛ mli gbii babaoo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ koo mli tsei Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall in one section of my land but stay short and weak in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi amɛfeɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa yɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Soil composition varies across a single field due to differences in soil depth, nutrient levels, water drainage, or past land use, causing crops to behave differently depending on where they are planted.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ he fɛɛ he. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ hewɔ lɛ niyenii mli nibii srɔtoi, nu ni hoɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ he ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the afternoon even when the soil still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: During the hottest parts of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Drooping is a natural defense mechanism to conserve water, and leaves usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: How does the start of the rainy season in Ghana affect when I should plant my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ be ni jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ saa be ni esa akɛ madu mitsei lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need consistent moisture to establish roots after germinating. Planting too early before rains are regular can cause seeds to dry out in the hot soil, while planting at the right time ensures steady growth.
ga: Tsei lɛ taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛfee shishifãi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ, dani nugbɔ nɛ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ be naa baaha dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to take up water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops. Regular weeding is necessary so your crops do not get starved.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. It often happens when heavy rains wash soil nutrients deep beyond the reach of young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ ebaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni mli wa lɛ he kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: How does putting dry grass on the soil around my crops help them handle dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ naa eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight. It keeps the ground cool, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from stealing moisture from your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaju nu ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when rain water stands on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the ground for too long, oxygen gets trapped out, causing the roots to suffocate and rot under the soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen lɛ ŋmɛɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso afɔ sweet potato wain tso nɔ koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers. Lifting them off the damp ground also prevents fungal diseases from spreading onto the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛjie amɛhe tsei lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs agboi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ owó amɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants curling up and falling off before producing any pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or sudden dry conditions. Tiny sucking pests like thrips can also attack the flowers, causing the plant to drop them to protect itself.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na dɔlɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa. Nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips hu baanyɛ atutua fɔfɔi. Ha tsei agbee shi koni obu ohe he.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl inward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling in the hot sun is a defense mechanism. The tomato plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, helping it hold onto internal water until temperatures drop.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: How do groundnut pods end up growing under the ground when the flowers bloom on top of the stems?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, it develops a growing stem called a peg. This peg naturally bends downward and pushes into the soil, where the pod expands and matures.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Ebaafee tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg. Nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ baabɔle ehe kɛya shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ehe baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Pods lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ni amɛdara kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I cut down all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? kookoo tso muu fɛɛ

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive under moderate shade, which protects them from harsh sunlight and heat. Without shade, the trees become stressed and are more easily attacked by insect pests like mirids.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya.

english: Why should I remove excess suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If you allow too many suckers to grow together, they fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil. Cutting off extra suckers leaves enough food for the main stem to grow a heavy, healthy plantain bunch.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ plantain tsei akuu ko ni tsii ni he wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves of my young oil palm seedlings turn pale green when planted in very sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil loses nutrients quickly whenever it rains because it cannot hold water well. Pale leaves mean the palm seedling lacks essential plant foods like magnesium and nitrogen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ magnesium kɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and dry up after I spray chemical weedkiller on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weedkillers can burn or stress crops if applied in wrong quantities, sprayed in high heat, or if the chemical is not suitable for that specific crop variety.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo aha tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni esaaa mli. Akɛ la ni mli wa shwieɔ nɔ loo kɛji tsofai lɛ esaaa nakai tso lɛ henɔ lɛ

english: Can using the wrong pesticide on my vegetables make the plant disease worse instead of curing it?
ga: Ani tsofa ni ejaaa ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsa lɛ?

english: Yes, using improper chemicals can kill beneficial insects that naturally control pests, damage the plant's natural defenses, and allow diseases to spread faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuuu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛyeɔ kooloi bibii anɔ lɛ. Efiteɔ tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Tomato plants often shed flowers when daytime temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: I applied fertilizer to my pepper plants, so why are they growing only big leaves without making any peppers?
ga: Mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ amɛduɔ baai wuji pɛ ni amɛfeee chili ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Using fertilizers high in nitrogen makes plants focus all their energy on growing tall, green leaves rather than producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ jwɛŋmɔ hiɔ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my bean leaves turn light green and wilt even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water in the soil drowns the roots, stopping them from breathing and taking up nutrients, which causes the plant to look weak and wilted.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi. Ehaaa enyɛ emu ni enine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo.

english: Why is my maize growing so stunted and small in patches across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted patches are usually caused by underground soil pests attacking the roots or parasitic weeds like Striga attached to the maize roots beneath the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ loo jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ Striga ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa shishifãi ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava during dry periods is usually caused by small pests like green mites or whiteflies that suck the sap out of leaves when conditions are hot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli loo ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ

english: What causes white powdery spots to appear on the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powder jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: The white spots are a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads fast in humid weather when crops are planted too close together.
ga: Hela yɛŋ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die suddenly in the nursery right after coming out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo trukaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni eje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings often die from 'damping-off,' a root rot disease caused by too much moisture and poor water drainage in the nursery soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛjɛɔ 'Damp', ni ji shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my green orange fruits fall off the tree before they get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Citrus fruits often drop early due to fruit fly attacks, prolonged water stress during hot spells, or a lack of plant nutrients during fruit growth.
ga: Citrus aduawai lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya yɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu mli haomɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ yɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and fuel plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei náa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ aná tsofa.

english: How does planting beans on my farm help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nutrient remains in the ground to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Niyenii mli nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture is uneven. High heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to conserve energy for survival instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds before the bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy stems. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden fork or bamboo stake gives the plant extra balance against rainstorms and strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛfee ŋtayaai loo ŋtayaai ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa trees curling up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, brown young cocoa leaves are often damaged by sap-sucking pests like capsids or scorched by direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains and using recommended pest control protects the tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my cowpea leaves after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: White spots are a sign of powdery mildew, a plant disease that spreads easily when weather is warm and humid. Spacing your crops properly allows air to flow between plants, which keeps leaves dry and stops the fungus.
ga: He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji powder mildew he okadi. Enɛ ji tso hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my pepper seedlings while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Pepper dumɔwui be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from young pepper plants. Clearing them early prevents your peppers from becoming weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi o-pepper lɛ naa koni ekagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so it does not spoil under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. Leaving tubers in waterlogged soil too long can cause them to become tough or rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛwa loo amɛgboi.

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is hard, compact, or full of rocks. Making high, soft soil mounds gives the roots space to expand smoothly downwards.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ agbɛ ashwã shi jogbaŋŋ kɛya shi.

english: Why do my cabbage heads remain loose and leafy instead of forming a hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bɔɔlu ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads stay soft when they lack consistent water, full sunlight, or nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering and good manure encourage the inner leaves to pack tightly into a firm head.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ nu shwie amɛmli daa. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ jɛmɛ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa baaye abua ni mligbɛ baai lɛ afee ekome ni efee bulb ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains protects them from the harsh sun and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees are mature enough to withstand full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant gets enough energy to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu he akaŋ. Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baa, ni enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually show that the plant is short of nitrogen, which is a vital food for growth. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant pulls what is left from its oldest bottom leaves to feed the new green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ heɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This extra nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow smaller and yield less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are aggressive, stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from your crops. When weeds crowd the field, your crops starve and cannot produce full, healthy harvests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Kɛ jwɛi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the farm stays flooded with rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa abɔɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When excessive rainwater sits on the farm for too long, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and curl up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates wet, humid conditions that help fungal diseases like blight grow fast. Water splashing up from the wet soil onto the leaves spreads fungal spores, causing leaf spots and curling.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. Nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baai anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa. Ehaa baai lɛ amli tsɔi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to stress caused by intense heat, lack of water, or poor insect pollination. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy and protect its own survival.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli baa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Eshiɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ebu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he.

english: Yam vines need to stretch their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight for making food. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, promoting bigger underground tubers and preventing leaf diseases caused by soil moisture.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ afee amɛbaai lɛ asɛɛgbɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ yaa hiɛ ni etsiɔ baa helai ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer the tender, soft leaves growing in the central funnel of young maize plants. They hide deep inside the funnel during the day to feed safely away from heat and birds.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hoppers lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni niyenii lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger and faster when I add manure to the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛyaa oya kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Manure adds essential nutrients and organic matter back into the earth, which feeds the soil and gives plants the energy they need to build strong roots, stems, and fruits.
ga: Manure kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi, tsei, kɛ aduawai ni wa.

english: Why do crops planted in dark soil usually give better yields than those in light sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark soil holds more organic matter, nutrients, and water, providing a constant food supply for roots to build larger, healthier fruits and seeds.
ga: Shikpɔji ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ nu babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii daa koni amɛwo aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do cocoa trees pull food from the ground all the way up to the pods on the trunk?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cacao tsei lɛ náa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli?

english: Roots take up water and dissolved soil nutrients, then the tree pumps this liquid food upward through small channels under the bark directly to nourish the developing pods.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni ji nu nɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: What makes cocoa beans inside the pod grow full and heavy instead of flat?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ daa ni eyiɔ obɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Beans become full and heavy when the tree absorbs enough soil nutrients to store energy and natural fats inside each seed during its growth period.
ga: Nuts eyi obɔ ni etsii kɛji tso lɛ ejie niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔji ato dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa seeds have so much oil inside them compared to seeds of other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔ babaoo yɔɔ kookoo yibii amli kɛ akɛto dumɔwui krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa seeds store natural oil and fat as a rich energy reserve so that a newly planted seed has enough strength to sprout and grow strong leaves before making its own food.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔ kɛ fɔji toɔ akɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa dani akɛtsu nii kɛhoo nii.

english: Is it bad for my cocoa crop if the beans inside have a high fat content?
ga: Ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ?

english: No, natural fat is actually essential energy for the cocoa plant to thrive, and beans high in good fat produce the rich chocolate flavor and weight buyers pay for.
ga: Dabi, adebɔɔ mli fɔji ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni haa cacao tsei lɛ daraa. Ni ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ haa tsokolate lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ muji ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ woɔ he nyɔmɔ.

english: How does the quality of my soil affect the taste of my harvested cocoa beans?
ga: Te bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha tɛŋŋ lɛ saa mikookoo ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ he?

english: Rich soil provides balanced nutrients that the tree uses to create natural fats and compounds in the beans, directly improving the rich flavor of the harvested crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ lipids kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ nut lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni mli wa lɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa crop need nutrient-rich soil to produce good pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli he hiaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Producing pods requires a massive amount of plant energy; without rich soil, the cocoa tree cannot draw up enough raw materials to build healthy, plump beans.
ga: Pods ni afeɔ lɛ biɔ tso hewalɛ babaoo waa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii bɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their leaves when the weather becomes dry and sunny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: When water in the soil becomes scarce, cocoa trees drop leaves to save moisture and energy, protecting their main trunk and roots until the rains return.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he. Buu tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I check if my cocoa beans have good fat content while drying them on the mats?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ mli fɔ kpakpa yɛ mli beni migbiɔ yɛ tsɔne nɔ lɛ?

english: Well-nourished beans with good fat content feel plump, have a solid brown center when cut open, and leave a faint oily glaze when rubbed between your fingers.
ga: Nuts ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni fɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ayɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni wa kɛji afo mli. ni eshiɔ fɔ fioo kɛji akɛ okɛwo oniji ateŋ.

english: Why should I buy improved crop seeds instead of just planting the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, handle dry spells better, and produce much higher yields than saved seeds, giving you more food and profit for the same amount of land.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Etsuɔ shɛɛ saji ni egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato lɛ Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ niyenii babaoo kɛ sɛɛnamɔi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature faster than others, and how does that help me if the rains stop early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi shwereɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ oya?

english: Early-maturing crop varieties complete their growth cycle quickly, allowing you to harvest a full yield before the rainy season ends and drought sets in.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ gbeɔ dalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ nikpamɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee ni hɔmɔ baa.

english: What happens to my maize crop if it does not get enough water when the flowering tassels start showing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most critical time for maize; if the plant lacks water during this stage, the cobs cannot fill with grains, leading to empty or stunted cobs.
ga: Be ni fɔfɔi fɔɔ lɛ ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ Cob lɛ hu nyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmaa lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo loo amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning or in the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the crop roots to absorb moisture before the hot sun evaporates the water, preventing heat stress and leaf burning.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ baa shãa naa.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during prolonged dry weather to save water and protect its tubers underground until moisture returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress, poor soil nutrients, or lack of water, as the plant tries to conserve energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nu ni bɛ be mli ni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing good fruit when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients, forcing them to spend energy growing tall to reach light rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ dalɛ hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ atsu nii koni amɛná la moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How does planting my crops in straight rows help me get a bigger harvest than scattering seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmaa babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal space, light, and air, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and manage water.
ga: Row planting haa tsei fɛɛ naa he ko, la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tamɔ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ nu he nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my crops need fertilizer or if my soil already has enough nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa momo?

english: Yellowish leaves, slow growth, or small stems usually mean your crops lack nutrients, whereas healthy green foliage and strong stems show the soil is well-nourished.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni daa blɛoo, loo tsei bibii tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop spots and rot when there is too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive wetness creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases to spread on leaves and fruit, which damages the plant unless the soil drains well and leaves can dry out.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã baai kɛ aduawai anɔ. Enɛ baafite tso lɛ. Ja shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni baai lɛ baanyɛ agbi.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants stops it from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni ekagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to put my maize seeds in the ground when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You should wait until the rain falls steadily two or three times and the soil stays wet below the surface. Planting too early after just one light rain can cause seeds to dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow in the middle while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-shape along the middle of lower leaves means the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure early in the plant's growth helps restore its deep green color and boosts grain yield.
ga: Su ni tamɔ V ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the plants suffer from extreme heat or sudden dryness in the soil. Mulching around the base with dried grass helps keep the soil moist and cool so flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Fɔfɔi baanyɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to swell into large tubers. Building high mounds loosens the earth so roots can grow easily and protects the yams from rotting in waterlogged soil during heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ adara oya ni akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting directly on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets light and air in, and removing infected pods quickly keeps the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ duŋ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does my groundnut farm produce green leaves but empty shells underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai eŋɔli shi ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the top layer of soil to fill out their pods. If the soil lacks calcium, the plant grows healthy leaves but produces empty pods, often called 'pops'.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni mli wa shi ebaawo ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ enɛ 'pop'.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my tomato seedlings after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep roots and seeds already hidden in the soil, allowing them to grab water and fertilizer faster than crop seedlings. Early weeding during the first month gives your crop a head start to grow taller than the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atoɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: How deep should I bury oil palm seedlings when transplanting them to the main field?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ, te esa akɛ afu amɛ kɛyashɛ he ko tɛŋŋ?

english: Oil palm seedlings should be buried so the base of the stem sits level with the surrounding ground. Burying them too deep smothers the growing tip, while planting too shallow exposes roots to drying sun.
ga: Esa akɛ afu mu tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni tso lɛ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ekome. Kɛ́ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss and save energy. It is a natural self-defense mechanism, and the plant will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: When maize is planted too close, the roots and leaves compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and smaller, underdeveloped corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni edako lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen, preventing flowers from fertilizing properly. When fertilization fails, the plant drops the unused flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tso lɛ baashi fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly into shapes like cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or from a virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my corn leaves turn yellow along the middle while the outer edges stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing inside corn leaves is a sign that the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. The plant steals nutrients from older parts to feed new growth, causing the yellow pattern.
ga: Abɛi baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen. Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi baa

english: How do I tell if my groundnuts are fully grown and ready to pull out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves start turning yellow and drying up, and when the inside of the groundnut shell turns dark brown with full seeds inside.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Ni kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local soil conditions, so their roots quickly absorb surface moisture and nutrients faster than farm crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Yam tubers twist when the soil underneath is too hard, rocky, or compacted. Building soft, raised mounds of soil gives the tuber space to push down straight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha tuber he lɛ ashɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi.

english: Why do my watermelon vines produce many yellow flowers, but only a few actually grow into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai?

english: Watermelons produce male flowers (which only supply pollen) and female flowers (which grow into fruit). Only female flowers that get pollinated by insects like bees will turn into watermelons.
ga: Watermelon woɔ fɔfɔi hii. (ni woɔ pollen pɛ) kɛ fɔfɔi yei (ni daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai) Fɔfɔi yei pɛ ni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ pollen woɔ mli lɛ bafeɔ watermelon.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow, it usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps them regain their green color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my field make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a family of crops that take nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped food stays behind in the earth to nourish whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei akuu ko ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Niyenii ni atsĩ naa lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in full sunlight to make food. When you give them stakes to climb, the leaves catch more sunlight, which allows the plant to send energy down to grow larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ oha amɛkwɔ Baai lɛ baaná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground, and heavy bunches of fruit make them top-heavy. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop helps hold the tree up until the fruit is ripe.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni aduawai ni tsii baaha tso lɛ tsii waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyashi eyibii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the field for too long, the roots suffocate and rot, which is why cassava grows best on mounds or well-drained soil.
