ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack open on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato skins split open when the plant gets a sudden heavy amount of water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water very quickly and expands faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomato hewoloi lɛ tswaa kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and weaker even if I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal food, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Because weeds grow very fast, they take up the nutrients in the soil before your crops have a chance to feed on them.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛyeɔ.

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which hides deep inside the growing center of the maize plant to eat tender leaves before they unfold. Treating the crop early protects the growing tip so the plant can mature.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebuɔ tso lɛ naji ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight and cannot survive without shade. Planting food crops like plantains around them creates a umbrella of shade that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. ni enyɛŋ ehi shi kɛji hulutsoo bɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil becomes too dry. The plant drops the flowers to save its water and energy so that the whole plant does not die from heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Enɛ ji koni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli.

english: Is it good to plant other crops like cashews together with my cocoa trees?
ga: Nibii krokomɛi tamɔ cashew nuts ni aduɔ Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi kɛ mi cacao lɛ?

english: Yes, planting other crops alongside cocoa is called intercropping. It helps you make maximum use of your farmland and gives you extra crops to sell so you do not rely only on cocoa.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ akɛ intercropping. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ kookoo pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers plant cashew trees on the same farm as their cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ cashew tsei yɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛduɔ amɛ kokoo lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew trees are hardy and can withstand drier conditions than cocoa. Planting them together provides a reliable extra source of income if bad weather or disease affects the cocoa yield.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ fe kookoo. Hefatalɔi adumɔ haa anáa shika babaoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hela ni ehiii lɛ saa kookoo feemɔ he.

english: What are the benefits of mixing fast-growing crops with long-term trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni daa oya kɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ he lɛ he?

english: Fast-growing crops produce harvest and quick cash early on, which supports your family and pays for farm maintenance while you wait for long-term tree crops like cocoa to mature.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ woɔ ŋmaa mra kɛ shika mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ oweku lɛ nɔ ni owoɔ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ he nyɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: What happens to my income if I plant only cocoa and the crop gets ruined by disease?
ga: Mɛni baa shika ni mináa lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ miduɔ kookoo pɛ ni helai kpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: If you rely solely on cocoa and disease strikes, you risk losing all your income for the season. Combining crops gives you a financial safety net.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ kookoo kɛ hela pɛ nɔ Okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ obaafite shika fɛɛ ni onáa kɛha be lɛ. Nibii ni okɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa onáa shika he shweshweeshwe.

english: When cocoa trees get old, they produce very few pods, dry up easily, and do not respond well to fertilizer. This is a sign that the old trees need to be cut down and replaced with fresh seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko eda lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ, egbiɔ oya, ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afo tso momo lɛ ni akɛ dumɔwu hee awo najiaŋ.

english: Where can I get the money to cut down my old cocoa trees and plant new ones?
ga: Nɛgbɛ maná shika ni mikɛfolɔ kookoo tsei momoi ni mikɛdu eheei?

english: You can plant alternative cash crops like cashews or food crops on part of your land to generate steady profits first, then use that money to clear old cocoa trees and buy new seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu shika ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ cashew nuts loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ona sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nakai shika lɛ ajie cacao tsei momoi lɛ ni ohé dumɔwui heei.

english: Can I use the cash I make from selling cashews to rebuild my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shika ni mináa kɛjɛɔ cashew ŋmeii ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ ama mi-cocoe ŋmɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, using income earned from hardy cash crops like cashews is an excellent way to fund farm labor, purchase tools, and buy new cocoa hybrid seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, shika ni jɛɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa tamɔ cashew nuts mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ nɔ. hɔɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni ohé hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei

english: How long should I watch my new crop grow before deciding to expand or add another crop?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa dani makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ matsake loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he?

english: You should observe your new crop for a few seasons to ensure it is surviving well in your soil and climate. Once you confirm it is growing successfully, you can comfortably invest in adding other crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli bei fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ebaahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Kɛji oma nɔ mi akɛ eye omanye lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ shika awo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli. hejɔɔmɔ

english: How can I protect myself financially if my main farm crop dies suddenly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mihe yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ gbo trukaa?

english: You protect yourself by practicing crop diversification—growing a mix of cash crops and food crops so that if one crop dies, the remaining crops keep bringing in money.
ga: Obuɔ ohe he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amlijaa ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔ. koni kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome gbo Tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ aya nɔ amɛkɛ shika aba.

english: Why should a cocoa farmer consider growing cashews as a backup crop in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ kookoo okwaafoi asusu cashew dumɔ he akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cashews thrive well in warm, dry regions, require less water than cocoa, and have a strong market demand, making them a safe backup crop during dry spells or low cocoa harvests.
ga: Cashews kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi. Nu fioo he miihia fe kookoo ni eyɛ jarayeli nibii babaoo Enɛ haa efeɔ sɛɛfimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, hot sunlight because their leaves dry out easily. Planting shade crops like plantains provides cover and creates a cooler, moist environment that protects the cocoa seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for green leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or animal manure helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fataa he. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know which direction to place cassava stem cuttings in the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted with the raised growth buds or nodes pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the plant to waste energy turning roots and shoots around, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ ni edaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ haa efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsakeɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This natural nitrogen feeds the soil and improves the growth of nearby maize crops without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni eekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to stretch up toward the sun to produce food for the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, prevents rot and diseases, and helps the crop produce larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛkpã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji

english: Tomato flowers usually drop due to extreme heat or irregular watering during the flowering stage. Hot weather kills the pollen inside the blossoms, preventing fruits from forming and causing the flowers to dry up and fall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ agbo. Ehaa aduawai baa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture in the soil during dry spells, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha onibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up into small wrinkled balls?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu bibii ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or thrips, or by viruses carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early stops the curling and helps new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baai heei daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several weeks of dry heat before the full rains arrive. Seeds sown right after the first rain may germinate quickly and then die from heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa naagbee. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ oya, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant in a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Select maiden suckers that have thick bases and narrow, sword-like leaves rather than broad leaves. These suckers have strong root bases with plenty of stored energy to grow fast and produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Halamɔ tsei bibii ni shishigbɛi lɛ mli tse kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ klante lɛ moŋ fe baai ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ shishitoo ni wa ni hewalɛ babaoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do some cassava varieties stay hard and tough when I boil them, while others become soft and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji mikɛ amɛ shã lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi yɛ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava varieties have different starch and water contents. High-starch varieties are bred for gari or industrial processing and stay firm when boiled, while table cassava varieties absorb water easily and soften quickly when cooked.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ yɛ starch kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni starch fa yɛ mli lɛ koni akɛfee gari loo nitsumɔhei. ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ ahoo lɛ yɛ be mli ni okpɔlɔ nɔ ŋmei henɔi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni efeɔ blɛoo oya kɛji akɛ ahoo lɛ.

english: Why is my local flint maize much harder to grind than the yellow hybrid maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ flint ŋmãa ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ wa waa fe ŋmãa ni ji yellow hybrid lɛ?

english: Flint maize has a thick, glassy outer shell designed by nature to resist insects and store well, whereas hybrid or dent maize has a softer, starchier center that crushes easily.
ga: Flint ŋmãa yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa ni mli tse ni tamɔ glase ni adebɔɔ fee koni ekɛ kooloi akabote mli ni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni hybrid loo dimpled corn lɛ yɛ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fãa oya.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant save moisture and prevent itself from drying out during high temperatures.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaaa egbi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when my farm stays flooded with rain for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nu efo miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water displaces air in the soil, suffocating root systems. Without oxygen, roots cannot pull essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Extreme heat or water stress damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing fruit set and causing the unfertilized flowers to drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Tsĩ aduawai anaa koni amɛkamɔ ni eha fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ agbo

english: Why does adding salt help keep my harvested vegetables fresh for longer without rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mikpamɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee lɛ?

english: Salt draws out excess water from plant tissues through osmosis, creating an environment where bacteria and fungi cannot live and spoil the food.
ga: Nu lɛ gbalaa nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli kɛtsɔɔ osmosis nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ baa ni muawai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɛɛ ahi shi ni ehaa niyenii fiteɔ.

english: Why must I ferment my harvested cocoa beans under banana leaves before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-kookoo ni akpa lɛ woɔ banana baai ashishi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the seeds to kill the bitter taste, destroy the pulp layer, and unlock the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color before sun-drying.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa dumɔwui lɛ mli dɔɔ koni ejie ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. efiteɔ tsokolate lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbeleɔ tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni tsuɔ waa lɛ mli dani egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up thin and crooked instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji mlɛo ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, deep soil mounds to expand easily. Compacted or stony soil physically restricts tuber expansion, resulting in misshapen tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi tuber lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ naa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why does my plantain sucker take so long to bear fruit if I leave weeds growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain suckers lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young plantains for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients, slowing down the crop's growth and delaying fruit development.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ dumɔwui bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hu sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods crack open and spill seeds on the ground before I finish harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbalaa ni amɛshwieɔ dumɔwui amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani migbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpamɔ naa lɛ?

english: Mature cowpea pods naturally burst open when they get very dry to spread their seeds. Harvesting early in the morning while the pods are slightly moist from dew prevents seed loss.
ga: Cowpea ŋmeii ni eda lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛgbi waa koni amɛgbɛ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwã. Nikpamɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli edɔ fioo kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the growth stage helps the crop regain its green color and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every time I plant maize on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients from the soil every season. If you grow it repeatedly on the same spot without a break, the soil gets tired and exhausted. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with nitrogen and keeps it healthy.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii daa be. Kɛ́ odu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni sũ faaa lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to push long wooden sticks into the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso kakadaŋŋ ko? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward direct sunlight to produce energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to direct its energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha tsei kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother tree. By cutting them down and leaving only one or two strong suckers for the next harvest, your main plantain stem grows faster and produces bigger bunches.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ amɛ ni oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. O plantains titrii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaawo panicles wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites living under the leaves. Spraying early with natural neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticide stops the insects before they stunt the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ kpaa gbee dani amɛhaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of proper insect pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby can help lower the heat stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsei ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, strong sunlight and wind. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted beside them during their early years to protect their delicate leaves until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other on the ridge?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmei ko nɔ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their leaves fight for sunlight and their roots fight for nutrients and space underground. Giving them proper distance allows each plant to form thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso awo bulbs ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass and leaves on the soil around their vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai aŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. The dry grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly rots to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Hay tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for me to sow my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain falls steadily enough to moisten the top layer of soil deeply. Sowing seeds after just one light rainfall can cause the seeds to germinate and then dry up and die if the sun returns for several days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba gbii babaoo.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stay short even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɛ eshwa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for building strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the plant's growth helps it regain its green color and produce large cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ koni amɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: How do leguminous crops like soybeans help improve the soil for other crops I plant later?
ga: Te ŋmeii tamɔ soybeans haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni miduɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Soybeans and other legumes have tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop leaves and roots decompose after harvest, they release this natural food into the earth, making it richer for crops like maize.
ga: Soybean kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and protect itself from heat, which is normal behavior. The plant goes dormant above ground while keeping the cassava tubers alive under the soil until the rains return.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ baai yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes maize stalks to produce flowers at the very top before the cobs form on the side?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ dani ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛgbɛ?

english: The flower at the top is the tassel, which produces pollen that gets blown by the wind onto the soft silks of the lower cobs. This pollination process is essential because without it, the cob will not form any corn grains.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji tsitsi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ pollination gbɛ nɛɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ kɛji ebɛ lɛ, The cob lɛ ewooo ŋmãa ŋmãa ko kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry out and die when I plant them in open sunlight without plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni dumɔwui bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains around them creates living shade and keeps the air humid so the young cocoa trees can survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni ŋɔɔ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants and leaving ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu ni mli ewo muji lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworms, which hide inside the leaf funnel of young maize plants to feed on soft tissue. Early treatment by applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract directly into the central leaf funnel stops them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall flukes, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Mra be mli tsamɔ Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grains spoil quickly and attract insects when I store them in my crib?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbalaa kooloi bibii kɛbaa mihe kɛji mikɛto ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when they are stored while still holding too much moisture, which attracts weevils and causes mold to grow. Thoroughly drying the harvested cobs in the sun until the seeds are hard reduces water content and protects the grain during storage.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ akɛto ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo eshwɛ. Enɛ baagbala ŋmeii kɛba ni ebaaha ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ mli wa lɛ, no haa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to lift yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food that travels down to form big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, exposing them to light while preventing leaf diseases caused by wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ekpɛɔ ni atsĩɔ tsei ahe helai ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and applying balanced organic manure helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo tsei amli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa fata he lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin stalks and produce very small cobs when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ shishi tsei bibii ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo ebɔ he yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the roots and leaves compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Planting seeds with proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough room and food to develop strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my crops grow better when it rains compared to when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Rainwater covers the entire field evenly and carries natural nitrogen from the air, which nourishes the soil better and reaches deeper roots than light surface watering by hand.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ fe kɛtsɔ nine ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fioo lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my crops from dying during dry periods when water is scarce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii akagboi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni nu faaa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dried leaves or straw (mulching) acts like a blanket, trapping moisture in the dirt and stopping the sun from drying out the roots quickly.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) koni etsu nii tamɔ blanket. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do crop roots stay close to the surface when I only water the top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ? Beni mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Roots always grow toward moisture. If you only wet the top layer of dirt, roots stay near the surface, making plants fragile and weak against strong sunshine and dry winds.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be kɛya ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji okɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwie shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ oya.

english: How do I tell if my crops are suffering from too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Too much water makes the soil soggy and drowns the roots, leading to soft, yellowing leaves, while too little water makes the leaves turn crisp, brown, and curl upward to save moisture.
ga: Nu babaoo haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nu fioo tsɔ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: Why is it important to perform farm activities like weeding step-by-step instead of all in one day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafee ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ fiofio lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ o je e tsuo ngɛ ligbi kake mi.

english: Doing farm tasks step-by-step keeps you from getting overwhelmed and ensures weeds are removed before they can steal critical water and sunlight from young crops.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mli nitsumɔ ni oootsu lɛ fitsofitso lɛ haaa onu he akɛ ogbɔjɔ ni ejieɔ jwɛi lɛ dani amɛjuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ.

english: Why should I try to complete my field preparations before the main rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni masaa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Preparing land early creates a soft, well-aerated bed for seeds so that as soon as the rains start, the seeds can germinate quickly without getting washed away by heavy torrents.
ga: He lɛ he saamɔ mra Ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ. koni kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ kɛkɛ Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ eŋɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Early morning or cool evening is best because lower temperatures allow soil to soak up the water fully without the hot midday sun evaporating it into the air.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ shwieee kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before it rains or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right before a light rain so the moisture melts the fertilizer into the soil for the roots, but avoid applying it before heavy downpours that wash it away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fioo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwie.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun even if the ground was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil, causing leaves to temporarily wilt to reduce water loss until the air cools down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ baai lɛ agbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the plant nutrients in my farm's soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away fertile topsoil and carry valuable nutrients deep beyond the reach of crop roots, which is why planting on ridges or using cover crops helps protect soil quality.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa aya shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ loo nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do some farmlands refuse to grow crops properly while neighboring lands produce plenty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli hei komɛi kpooɔ ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Soil quality varies from plot to plot. Some lands 'reject' crops because the soil lacks essential nutrients, holds too much or too little water, or is too acidic, while neighboring plots may have healthy, fertile soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ. Shikpɔŋkukuji komɛi ‘kpooɔ’ ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu babaoo loo fioo ni ahiɔ mli loo eyɛ acid tsɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni hi ni baa nii.

english: What does it mean when people say a piece of land 'does not accept' crops?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ko ‘kpɛlɛɛɛ’ nidumɔ nii anɔ lɛ, mɛni etsɔɔ?

english: When land 'does not accept' crops, it means the soil conditions are unsuitable for plant growth, causing seeds to either fail to germinate or plants to stunt and die before yielding fruit.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ ‘kpɛlɛɛɛ’ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ esaaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ loo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow fine in the beginning but stop growing and turn yellow after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli shi amɛkpaa shweremɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants initially feed on stored nutrients inside the seed. Once those run out, if the soil lacks the necessary plant food, the crops starve, stop growing, and turn yellow.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ jeɔ shishi eyeɔ niyenii kpakpai ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ nakai shikpɔji lɛ etee Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaye hɔmɔ, amɛbaakpa shweremɔ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I check if a new piece of land is good for crops without risking all my money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ mishika fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: Before investing heavily, you can plant a small test patch with fast-growing crops to observe how the land behaves, or contact an agricultural extension officer to examine the soil for you.
ga: dani okɛ shika babaoo awo mli Obaanyɛ odu kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ enii ehaa Aloo okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko abɔ koni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eha bo.

english: Is it wise to plant a small section of my field first to test if crops will survive there?
ga: Esa akɛ odu he bibioo ko. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni akɛka kɛji ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baahi shi loo ebaahi shi?

english: Yes, planting a small test plot allows you to observe how crops perform in that specific soil without risking your entire season's budget and effort on unknown land.
ga: Hɛɛ, kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni aduɔ. Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ be muu fɛɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aleee nɔ lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Why is farming on land I have never used before so financially risky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsuuu nii dã lɛ nɔ okwaayeli ji shika he oshara lɛ?

english: New land is unpredictable because you do not know its soil quality or history. Without prior testing, you might spend money on seeds and labor only to discover the soil cannot support crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hee ji nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba ejaakɛ oleee bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha loo eyinɔsane. Kɛji akɛ kaa ko bɛ dani afee lɛ Obaanyɛ ofite shika yɛ dumɔwui kɛ nitsumɔ he pɛ ni ona akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I avoid spending all my savings on a farm only to get no harvest at the end of the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ shika fɛɛ ni mikɛto lɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná ŋmaa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee pɛ?

english: You can protect your investment by gathering knowledge about the soil beforehand, testing small areas first, and matching the right crop to the specific soil type rather than planting blindly.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nilee ni obaabua naa kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Kaa he bibioo ko okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu shwilafoi

english: What causes a farmer to lose their entire investment during the very first year on new land?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaafoi lɛ fiteɔ amɛshika fɛɛ ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: First-year total losses usually happen when a farmer plants a large area without testing the soil first, leading to crop failure if the land turns out to be infertile or unsuitable for that crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni laajeɔ fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ baa beni okwaafoi duɔ shikpɔji wuji ni amɛkaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bafee nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli loo esaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither and die even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Rainfall alone is not enough; if the underlying land has hard underground layers, toxic mineral levels, or lacks nutrients, crops will fail even with good rain.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ tsũ ni wa Eyɛ minerals ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po.

english: How can I know which specific crops will do well on my farm before buying seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: You can determine crop suitability by looking at the natural weeds and trees already growing on the land, asking nearby farmers about their experience, or getting a quick soil test from an extension officer.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ko sa ha kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Bi okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amɛ niiashikpamɔi. Aloo ná shikpɔŋ lɛ he kaa oya kɛjɛ extension nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ.

english: How should I pack and store my yams after harvest so they do not spoil before reaching the market?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ, te esa akɛ afee tɛŋŋ awo sweet potatoes lɛ amli ni akɛto koni ekafite dani eyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yams have delicate skin that bruises easily during movement. When bruised, rot-causing bacteria and fungi enter through the cuts. Packing them carefully with dry straw or sawdust in ventilated crates protects them from skin damage and moisture accumulation during transit.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ enyiɛ. Kɛji akɛ fã ko ni egbo lɛ Bacteria kɛ fungi ni kɛ gangrene baa lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmeii ni egbi wo adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hewolo ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baabua amɛhe naa yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ he.

english: Why do my yams lose weight and become soft if I leave them in the sun after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are living tubers that continue to breathe and lose water. Direct sunlight causes high heat, making the yam sweat out its internal moisture rapidly, which leads to shrinkage, weight loss, and softness.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo.

english: What is yam 'curing', and why should I do it before moving my crop to storage?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘tsamɔ’ ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee enɛ dani mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii aya he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Curing involves keeping freshly dug yams in a warm, shaded, and well-ventilated spot for a few days. This process allows minor cuts and skin scratches to heal naturally by forming a thick protective skin layer, preventing diseases from infecting the tuber.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tsamɔ he ji sweet potato ni atsa ehee lɛ ni akɛtoɔ. Shi yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ gbii fioo. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fãji bibii kɛ ŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ tsaa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ hewolo nɔ fã ni mli tse ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni efeɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni helai akabote yitso mli

english: Why do yam leaves turn yellow and dry up when the crop is almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ kpamɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a natural sign that the yam plant has matured. As the plant completes its life cycle, it stops producing new leaves and redirects all remaining nutrients and energy down into the underground tuber to make it large and starchy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ eda. Kɛ tso ko gbe ewala shihilɛ naa lɛ Ebaakpa baai heei ni eeefee lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ baa shi kɛya ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes or poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso loo tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground and spreads the leaves out to receive direct sunlight, which maximizes food production through photosynthesis and leads to bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tso ji tso ko ni kwɔɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii feɔ babaoo kɛtsɔɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots after a few months even without water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ ni nu bɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural dormant period after harvest. Once this internal dormancy period ends naturally, the tuber uses its stored energy and starches to sprout shoots in preparation to grow a new plant.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ wɔɔhe be lɛ ba naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Bulbs lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛ starch tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛsaa amɛhe kɛha tsei heei adumɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow misshapen and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ efite ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand downward through the soil as they grow. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the developing tuber cannot push straight through and bends around obstacles. Planting yams in deep, loose mounds allows straight tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii ni edara lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni amɛbɔle gbɛtsii nibii ahe. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my yams rot underground if there is too much rain late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive water in the soil deprives the underground tuber of oxygen. When soil stays waterlogged, rot-causing fungi thrive in the wet conditions and invade the yam tissues under the ground.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baaná hɔmɔ. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ Fɛ̃i ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. ni etutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fãji lɛ.

english: Why do white insects gather on the skin of my stored yams, and do they harm the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui?

english: These are scale insects that suck juice from the yam skin. They dry out the tuber, weaken its structure, and leave marks that lower the selling price at the market.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ahewolo nɔ nu lɛ. Amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. egbɔjɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni eshiɔ nibii ni haa jara ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baa shi

english: If I cut a large yam tuber into pieces to plant as seed, how do I stop the cut pieces from rotting in the soil?
ga: Kɛji mifo sweet potato tuber agbo ko mli bibii koni mikɛdu dumɔwui Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni afo lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: A cut yam sett leaves fresh plant tissue exposed to soil fungi. Dusting the cut surfaces with dry wood ash and letting them dry in the shade before planting seals the wound and protects the sett from rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli fãji heei lɛ naa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ ni egbi lɛ shwie he ni afo lɛ nɔ ni oha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi pilamɔ lɛ naa ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why do my tomatoes crush and rot so quickly when I transport them from my farm to the market in deep wooden crates?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli fãa ni egboɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have soft skin and continue to ripen and generate heat after harvest. When packed tightly in deep crates, the heavy weight from top layers crushes the bottom fruits, while trapped heat rapidly speeds up spoilage during transit.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni edɔɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛwo adeka ko ni mli kwɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Muji ni tsii ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa fitemɔ yaa oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn dark blue and spoil just two days after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ bluu ni mli edɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is detached from its root system, it undergoes rapid natural oxidation called post-harvest physiological deterioration. It must be consumed, sold, or processed into products like gari within 48 hours to prevent the starch from spoiling.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli gbala kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli oksideshin mli oya waa. Atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ, ni esa akɛ aye, ahɔ̃ɔ loo afee lɛ nɔ ko tamɔ gari yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli koni ashikiŋsha lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside my barn during storage even when I harvested them clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akɛtoɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa lɛ ni ehe tse moŋ

english: Yams rot in storage primarily due to tiny, unseen scratches caused by harvesting tools like hoes. Microscopic fungi enter through these wounds, and high humidity in the storage space allows the rot to spread from one tuber to another.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ nitoohe titri lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii ahewɔ. Nɔ ni anaaa ni jɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ nibii tamɔ ŋmei mli baa lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ boteɔ pilamɔi nɛɛ amli. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ bulb kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits split wide open in the field before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst open when heavy rain follows a long dry period. The vine rapidly absorbs a large amount of water, causing the soft inner flesh of the fruit to expand faster than the outer rind can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Wein tso lɛ gbalaa nu babaoo oya. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or dry soil conditions. The plant sheds flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture and energy until environmental conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my garden eggs become soft, bitter, and wrinkled when left in the sun at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs (eggplants) lose water quickly through their skin when exposed to sunlight. As moisture evaporates, natural bitter compounds become concentrated inside the fruit, and the skin hardens to slow down further water loss.
ga: Eggplant (Eggplant) shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ ehewolo nɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, nibii ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. ni hewolo lɛ baafee shiŋŋ koni ekɛ nu kroko ni baa shi lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still attached to the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Spores travel through rain splashes, so removing affected pods early prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Spores lɛ tsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the key nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and improves cob size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmei lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and droop around the main stem before the bunch fully forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ mihe lɛ? Tso titri lɛ dani kuu lɛ feɔ kwraa?

english: This leaf wilt is often caused by root-damaging pests or fungal soil diseases like Panama disease. Damaged roots cannot draw enough water up the stem, forcing the plant to drop its outer leaves to conserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Panama hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baa. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛya tso lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ajie esɛɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right when they look mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kaaba yitsei lɛ tswaa trukaa beni kaaba lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cabbages split when they take in an excess of water near the end of their growth cycle. The inner leaves continue to grow rapidly and push against the tightly bound outer head until the structure cracks open.
ga: Kaabaji fiteɔ kɛji enine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ beni ebɛŋkɛɔ edalɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfi amɛhe waa lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear all the large trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because intense direct sunlight scorches their leaves and quickly dries out the topsoil. Keeping shade trees or planting tall food crops like plantains provides the cool environment and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure restores the green color and helps the stalks grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ adara waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, skinny plants and small tubers instead of big, heavy roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yitso bibioo yɔɔ mli yɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which spreads easily in damp, dark conditions. Pruning extra branches and clearing underbrush lets sunlight and air in to dry the pods faster and slow down the disease.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ amli kɛ amɛhe ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya ni ehaa helai sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my previous maize harvest yield less than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Commercial seeds are specially bred hybrids that produce high yields in their first planting, but their saved offspring lose those strong genetic traits, leading to smaller cobs and lower yields.
ga: Jarayeli dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Shi seshibii ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite nakai fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or a lack of water, which prevents proper pollination. Keeping the soil moist and mulched helps the plant retain its flowers so fruit can develop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do you recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally restoring fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much even when my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing underground roots that steal water and fertilizers right out of the soil before your crop roots can reach them, slowing down your harvest growth.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni daa oya. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Enɛ baaha nikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and dry out during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture out of leaves faster than roots can suck water from the dry ground. The plant curls its leaves to reduce its surface area and save what little water it has left.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baafolɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛ nu fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I cut off the unnecessary lower branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Removing weak lower branches prevents the tree from wasting energy on non-producing stems, redirecting nutrients into growing bigger pods while making it harder for pests to climb up.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. Niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji amli Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ewaa ahaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive and can dry out or burn under strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that create temporary shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi loo amɛshã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa be kukuoo mli hɔɔŋ baa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni obu kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do we have to build high soil mounds to plant yams instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔma gɔji ni kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick underground. Building high mounds loosens the soil deep down, making it easy for the tubers to expand without resistance, while also protecting them from rotting in waterlogged soil after heavy rains.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ama lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli fitemɔ hu naa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Does it really matter which direction I insert cassava cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo?

english: Yes, direction matters because the buds on the stem cutting must point upward toward the sky. If you plant cassava cuttings upside down, the roots and shoots struggle to emerge correctly, leading to weak growth and low tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia ejaakɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do groundnut flowers drop to the ground and push themselves into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are unique because their fruit develops underground. Once the flower above ground is pollinated, it forms a small stem called a 'peg' that bends downward and buries itself in the soil, where the actual groundnut pod matures.
ga: Eyɛ srɔto kwraa akɛ ŋmeii yɛ ejaakɛ amɛyibii lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie amɛhe lɛ Amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni amɛkotoɔ shi ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or waterlog the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu lɛ tsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Plantain trees do not have a deep, strong taproot to anchor them deep in the ground; their roots grow shallowly near the surface. When the bunch of plantains grows heavy, the tree becomes top-heavy and needs wooden poles for support to prevent it from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baaha amɛfi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni plantains lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsei akwɛ nɔ koni akaje shishi.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants curling up and dropping off before producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips and aphids. Maintaining steady soil moisture and managing insect pests helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ aphids ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a defense response to heat stress or excessive moisture, but if the leaves are also yellowing and twisted, it is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo hulutsoo ni fa fe nine he. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛtsake Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my vegetable beds help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables saatsoi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective shield against the sun. It prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the number of weeds competing for water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa nu he akaŋ lɛ ayibɔ baa shi

english: Why is it important to weed my cowpea farm when the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: When cowpea plants are young, their root systems are weak. Clearing weeds early stops the weeds from stealing water, light, and nutrients, allowing the cowpea to grow quickly and spread its leaves over the soil to block future weeds.
ga: Beni tsina tsei lɛ ji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii, ni ehaa tsina ŋmei lɛ daa oya ni egbɛɔ ebaai lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Are all fungi and tiny organisms in my farm soil harmful to my crops?
ga: Fungi kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, not all fungi cause rot or disease. Many microscopic organisms in the soil are positive agents that work like natural helpers, helping plant roots absorb water and essential nutrients so your crops grow stronger.
ga: Dabi, jeee ŋmeii fɛɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii loo hela aba. Nibii bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nibii ni hi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni onibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why can't I see the helpful organisms in the soil that support my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mana nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni fiɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: These beneficial fungi are extremely tiny—so small that they are completely invisible to the naked eye. Even though you cannot see them, millions of them live around crop roots forming unseen networks that feed the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ faaa kwraa. Eyɛ bibioo kwraa bɔ ni hiŋmɛi enaaa lɛ kwraa. Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ po. Shi amɛteŋ akpekpei abɔ yɛ ni hiɔ tsei shishifãi ni feɔ tsɔne ko ni anaaa ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I increase the number of friendly microscopic organisms in my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Adding organic matter like well-rotted manure, compost, and decaying plant leaves to your field gives these microscopic positive agents the food and shelter they need to multiply and keep your soil alive.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egboi fata osɛɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ nibii bibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛkwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do good fungi in the soil help my cassava or yam plants feed themselves?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua o-cassava loo sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛna amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii?

english: Friendly microscopic fungi attach themselves to crop roots and extend far into the soil like tiny threads. They gather hidden water and soil nutrients from places the root cannot reach and pass them directly into the plant.
ga: Naanyo ŋmei ni yɔɔ bibioo lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei shishifãi ahe ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kpãai bibii. Amɛbuaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtee hei ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ anaa, ni amɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ ŋɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops stay greener during dry spells when the soil has good organic matter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ? Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli?

english: Beneficial soil microbes hold liquid and moisture around plant roots like microscopic sponges, allowing your crops to survive longer when rain is scarce.
ga: Sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ toɔ nu kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ tsei shishifãi ahe tamɔ sponji bibii. Ye obua onibii ni okwɛ̃ lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ faaa.

english: Can friendly organisms in the soil protect my crops from diseases?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: Yes, positive fungal agents occupy the space around root tissues and consume available food, preventing bad germs and root-rot diseases from establishing themselves on your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, fungal nibii ni hi baaye he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ahe fãji kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ niyenii Enɛ tsiɔ helai fɔji kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkabua amɛhe naa yɛ onibii amli.

english: Are there different families of helpful fungi working in agricultural soil?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji anɔ lɛ awekui srɔtoi yɛ?

english: Yes, helpful soil microbes belong to distinct families. Some specialize in extending root reach for water and fertilizer, while other families specialize in attacking harmful pests and bad soil diseases.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ jɛ wekui srɔtoi amli. Mɛi komɛi le shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ be mli ni wekui krokomɛi He esa waa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuamɔ mli.

english: What happens to the invisible beneficial organisms in my soil if I burn my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba bɔɔ nii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni anaaa ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ? Kɛji mishã ŋmɔ lɛ dani midu nii?

english: Burning your field heats up the topsoil and destroys these tiny, delicate positive organisms. Without them, your crops lose their natural root partners and will rely much more heavily on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Oshia lɛ ni oooshã lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli adɔ ni ekpata nibii bibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahiɛ. nɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ Kɛ amɛbɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hefatalɔi ni amɛbaatsɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ babaoo.

english: Will spraying heavy chemical fungicides hurt the good organisms living in my farm soil?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye nibii kpakpai ni hiɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui?

english: Yes, strong chemical fungicides often kill beneficial soil fungi along with the bad ones. Using chemicals carefully and only when necessary helps protect the natural positive agents that keep your soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbeɔ sũ mli ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ hu. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ be mli ni ehe miihia pɛ lɛ baabu adebɔɔ mli nibii kpakpai ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has these invisible positive organisms working for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni anaaa nɛɛ ni tsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Although you cannot see the organisms themselves, strong root systems, rich dark soil around roots, and healthy crop growth with less need for excessive chemical inputs are clear signs that beneficial microbes are active.
ga: Kɛji bo diɛŋtsɛ onyɛɛɛ ona adebɔɔ lɛ po Shi shishifã lɛ mli wa. Shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ. Ni tsei ni daraa jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai babaoo he ehiaaa lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ miitsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in the direct open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full sunlight because their soft leaves burn and lose water quickly. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in cold, damp weather. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and air into the farm helps keep the pods dry and prevents the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the bunches start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem borers. Supporting the trees with bamboo wooden props and keeping the base clean prevents them from snapping under heavy loads.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni aha shishitoo lɛ he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ yɛ muji ni tsii shishi.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant steals food from its old bottom leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baa lɛ adalɛ yɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ.

english: Why are my rice plants producing empty heads with no grains inside at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ woɔ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?
