english: Empty rice heads are usually caused by stem borer insects eating the inside of the plant stalk, or by severe dry weather while the plant was flowering, preventing the grains from filling up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni haa ŋmãa yibii lɛ eyiɔ obɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack upward due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams rot in the soil soon after I plant them during the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot when planted in waterlogged soil that lacks good drainage. The excess water attracts fungal diseases that enter through any cuts on the seed piece before it has a chance to sprout roots.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni boteɔ dumɔwu lɛ fã ni afo lɛ mli dani enáa hegbɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the underside of the leaf, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. When the plant feels stressed, it sheds its flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my sweet orange tree drop its young green fruits before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Citrus trees shed young fruit when they do not get enough water during hot periods, or when fruit flies lay eggs inside the young fruits, causing them to turn yellow and fall off early.
ga: Orange tsei woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Aloo beni aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ aduawai bibii amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains to shelter them, the intense sun scorches their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to grow.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha amɛná hulutsoo lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ agbi.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving holes behind?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ bu yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and eat the young leaves, which can ruin the crop if not treated early with appropriate organic or chemical controls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ mra. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and twisting into strange, crumpled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Your cassava likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings for planting is the best way to prevent this from happening.
ga: Ekolɛ o-kasa lɛ yɛ kasa mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering patterns during the fruiting stage.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli ni ejaaa.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce tiny cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When the crop is harvested, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from rotting quickly while they are in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya be mli ni miyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are damaged during harvest or stored in hot, damp places. Storing undamaged yams off the ground on raised bamboo shelves in a well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps them cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛfite yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni edɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ atomɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ ato shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmei adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa edɔ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops so much if I do not clear them early enough?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa kɛji minyɛɛɛ majie amɛ oya bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your plants need to build strong stems and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that bakes the topsoil. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the young roots will burn and die before the steady rains fully begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ Shishifãi bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ kwraa.

english: Why are my sweet potato roots small and thin instead of fat and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ fɔ ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need loose, heap-mounded soil to expand easily. If the soil is too hard or packed down, or if the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant grows big green leaves instead of fat tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni ebɔle ehe koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Tso lɛ baaná baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ fɔ bulbs najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the surrounding trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and hot dry winds. They need shade crops like plantains or larger trees above them to keep the air humid and protect their delicate leaves from getting scorched.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize is starving for nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Without enough food or when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients, the plant loses its green color and cannot grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-ŋmã lɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ laajeɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same spot every season make my harvest smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously exhausts the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests and diseases to build up in large numbers in that area.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ sũ mli helai buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and look lifeless during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during extreme heat to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them retain moisture until the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or insect attacks. When stressed, the plant tries to save energy by shedding its flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛtsɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up growing short, crooked, and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji, ni ebɔle ehe, ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow crooked when the soil underneath is too hard, compact, or filled with rocks. Yam roots require soft, loose, deep, and high earth mounds to push downward easily.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baakɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Sweet potato shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni etsilɛ, ni mli kwɔ, ni kɛlɛ koni amɛtsi kɛya shi mlɛo.

english: Covering the ground with dried plant materials creates a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating into the air, and stops weeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: How do weeds growing close to my cassava plants slow down the growth of the tubers underground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal the sunlight, water, and soil fertilizers meant for your crop. When weeds crowd your cassava, the plant lacks the energy needed to build big, heavy starch roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi eyi ŋmei lɛ mli obɔ lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji ni tsii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei.

english: If I cut off some of the leafy stems from my tomato plants, won't that destroy the crop?
ga: Kɛ mifo tomato tso ko baai lɛ ekomɛi lɛ, Ani no efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Pruning away excess leaf stems actually helps the plant because it stops wasting food on unnecessary leaves and sends all its strength into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ejaakɛ ekpaa niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli lɛ fitemɔ. ni okɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Can I leave the roots of my harvested crop in the ground so new shoots grow back without replanting seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ ni miduuu dumɔwui heei?

english: Certain crops like sugarcane, pineapples, and cassava can regrow from their old roots or stems after harvest, which saves you the expense and effort of purchasing and planting new seeds every time.
ga: Tsei komɛi, tamɔ shɛ̃, anana, kɛ cassava, baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ shishifãi momo loo tsei ashishifãi amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haaa oná shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni okɛheɔ dumɔwui heei ni okɛduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why is it so difficult to find available farm workers between November and January?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaana ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi yɛ November kɛ January teŋ lɛ?

english: November to January is the peak harvest and crop processing season in Ghana, meaning almost every farmer needs extra hands at the same time. Because workers get overwhelmed with demand across multiple farms, hiring labor becomes very difficult and expensive during these months.
ga: Alemle kɛyashi January ji be ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nitsumɔ be ni fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo baahiɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kroko yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ jɛ nitsulɔi babaoo ni ataoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo amli lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nitsulɔi ni aaaná lɛ wa ni ejara hu wa yɛ nɛkɛ nyɔji nɛɛ amli.

english: Can I clear land and start planting new crops in October?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mabɔi tsei heei dumɔ yɛ October mli?

english: Starting new crop fields in October is risky because it directly precedes the dry Harmattan season. New seedlings will struggle to survive without sufficient rains, and farm labor will be too busy with end-of-year harvesting to help you manage new fields.
ga: Oshara yɛ ŋmɔji heei ni aaaje shishi yɛ October mli lɛ hewɔ ejaakɛ etsɔɔ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui heei baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe baawo ŋmaakpamɔ mli tsɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua bo ni okwɛ ŋmɔji heei anɔ.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth as the year comes to an end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Towards the end of the year, rainfall reduces significantly and dry winds set in. Plants naturally slow down their growth and focus energy on ripening existing fruits or surviving the dry season rather than putting out fresh leaves or shoots.
ga: Yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswaa. Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni miikwɛ̃ loo amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo jeɔ baai aloo tso ɔmɛ a he.

english: Why shouldn't I start major new farm activities late in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijeɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi heei ni he hiaa shishi yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Major activities like clearing or planting late in the year overlap with the busiest harvest period. Trying to start new projects when farm labor is already overworked often leads to incomplete work, abandoned fields, and wasted money.
ga: Nitsumɔi wuji tamɔ tsei ahe nitsumɔ loo tsei adumɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ kɛ kpamɔɔ be ni mɛi babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ kpãa gbee. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni aje nitsumɔ hee shishi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii fe nine Bei pii lɛ Enɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ni eshɛɛɛ he baa. ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni ashi kɛ shika ni elaaje

english: Why is it harder to prepare my soil for planting in December than in the middle of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa kɛha dumɔ nii yɛ December mli lɛ wa fe afi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: By December, the dry season hardens the soil, making clearing and tilling physically exhausting for workers. Additionally, farm hands are already busy harvesting existing crops, making land preparation much slower and more difficult.
ga: Beni shɛɔ December lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa nitsulɔi lɛ ahe jɔ̃ɔ amɛhe. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ akpamɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ he saamɔ yaa hiɛ fioo ni ewaa.

english: What happens if I delay my harvest past October?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ kpamɔ lɛ shwie October sɛɛ?

english: Delaying your harvest pushes your field work into the November to January period when labor is scarce. You risk crop spoilage on the field because farm hands will be overworked and unavailable to help you gather your produce in time.
ga: Okpamɔ lɛ ni oootsi sɛɛ lɛ baatsi oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ kɛya November-January mli. ni ji nitsulɔi ahe nitsumɔ he be Okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ obaafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmɔ mli niji baatsu nii fe nine ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua bo ni okɛ ŋmaa lɛ abua naa yɛ be naa.

english: Why do my farm workers get exhausted and slow down during the end-of-year months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ ahe ejɔ amɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: End-of-year farm work combines hot, dry Harmattan weather with heavy crop harvesting demands. Workers often become overwhelmed by back-to-back heavy labor across many fields, causing them to tire out quickly.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ kɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ kɛ hiamɔ ni yɔɔ akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ feɔ ekome. Bei pii lɛ, nitsumɔ ni wa ni yaa nɔ yɛ nitsumɔi babaoo mli lɛ yeɔ nitsulɔi anɔ kunim. Enɛ haa amɛshãa oya.

english: Why do many Ghanaian crops mature and require harvesting at the exact same time late in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Ghana tsei babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he ni akpaa amɛ yɛ be kome mli yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Most crops depend on the major rainy season earlier in the year to grow. Because they are planted around the same time when rains start, their growth cycles finish together late in the year, creating a single massive peak season for harvesting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Ejaakɛ adu lɛ yɛ be kome too mli ni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dalɛ be lɛ fɛɛ baa naagbee yɛ afi lɛ naagbee. ni no haa efeɔ be ni akɛkpaa nii babaoo

english: How does the dry season between November and January affect my daily farm routine?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ November kɛ January teŋ lɛ saa mi daa gbi nibii ni mifeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During this period, crop care shifts from planting to harvesting and protecting mature crops from drying out. Daily work becomes focused on gathering mature yields quickly before weather damage or labor shortages occur.
ga: Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmaakpamɔ nɔ. ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi Daa gbi nitsumɔ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ anaabuamɔ oya nɔ dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi afite loo nitsulɔi ahe ehiaaa.

english: When is the worst time for me to expand my farm size?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni ehiii fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The worst time to expand is right before or during the November to January period. Trying to manage extra acres when labor is scarce and weather is dry puts extra pressure on you and your workers, often leading to poor yield on the new section.
ga: Be ni ehiii fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ agbɛ ashwã ji dani November kɛ January loo yɛ teŋ. Mɔdɛŋ ni ooobɔ koni okwɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre krokomɛi anɔ yɛ be mli ni nitsulɔi faaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ kroko baa bo kɛ onitsulɔi lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haaa nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fã hee lɛ mli.

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots and leaves to spread out and produce larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Look closely at the small buds or leaf nodes along the stem. These buds should point upwards toward the sky, not down toward the soil, so the new shoots can easily grow above ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. loo baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Etsɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, retains soil moisture longer, and prevents weeds from taking nutrients away from your pepper plants.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the top layer of soil into gutters and streams before roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or before a light drizzle.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko eba.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get damaged if I water them during the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ afɔ tomato baai anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, efiteɔ lɛ?

english: Water droplets sitting on leaves act like small magnifying glasses under intense afternoon sun, scorching the foliage. It is best to water crops near their roots early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa ni shãa baai lɛ shishi lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy green growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Curled and yellow-patched leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem varieties prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest grow as well as bought hybrid seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu edaaa lɛ? Kɛ hybrid dumɔwui ahemɔ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yield and strength in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwã koni tso lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe awa.

english: My tomato plants are producing plenty of flowers, but why are the flowers dropping off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime heat is too extreme or when the soil dries out completely, which stresses the plant. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during very hot days helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks next to my yam vines as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso lɛ ato he lɛ? Sweet potato wain tso be mli ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight. Staking the vines allows the leaves to catch full sunlight, which generates the energy the plant needs to grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. Controlling these insects with organic sprays like neem oil helps new leaves grow back flat and normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, tamɔ neem fɔ lɛ ye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baa heei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛdaraa tamɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the same patch of land where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he ni mibua ŋmeii anaa yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases. Planting them in the same spot year after year lets disease germs build up in the soil and attack your new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii jɛ tsei aweku kome mli, ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua onibii heei lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and soft roots that dry out quickly under intense sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa protects them from harsh sunlight until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Young cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass or mulch keeps the root zone cool and slows down water loss.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo mulch ha tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants usually show readiness when their lower leaves turn yellow and naturally drop off, typically 9 to 12 months after planting. You can also gently dig up the soil near the base of one plant to check the thickness of the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛhesaamɔ lɛ kpo kɛ́ amɛshishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ Ofo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso kome shishi lɛ he fiofio hu koni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ mli wa ha.

english: Why is it important for me to clear all weeds from my land before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and will steal water, sunlight, and plant food from your young seedlings. Clearing weeds before planting gives your crops full access to everything they need for a strong start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ tsei niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ dani oduɔ lɛ haa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look tired during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni etɔ amɛ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in extreme heat to conserve water and protect themselves from intense sunlight. Once the temperature drops in the evening or they receive water, they usually bounce back.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ loo enáa nu. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grown inside a greenhouse grow taller and faster than the same crops planted in my open farm outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ daa ni amɛyaa oya fe tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Greenhouses maintain a warm, humid environment while protecting crops from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, and strong winds. This controlled environment allows plants to spend all their energy growing rapidly rather than fighting bad weather.
ga: Greenhouses haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ nɛɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa baawu lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant starves its older bottom leaves so it can send the remaining nutrients to feed the new top growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ gbeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje ŋwɛi tsei heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high, when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade trees to protect their delicate leaves from direct, harsh sunlight and to keep the surrounding soil moist while their root systems are still developing.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very tiny roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to one another, their roots compete heavily for food, light, and water. This competition leaves the plants with too little energy to swell and grow large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli waa. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look pale and sickly even though I pour plenty of water on them every morning and evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ? Nu babaoo Daa leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ?

english: Overwatering fills all the air spaces in the soil with water, which smothers the roots. Without air, the roots decay and cannot absorb food, causing the plant to starve despite the wet soil.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why does trimming off extra leaves and side shoots from my tomato plants help me get bigger tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa tomatoi wuji lɛ?

english: Removing non-essential shoots prevents the plant from wasting nutrients on extra leaves, directing all its food energy straight into expanding the fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, no tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa shweremɔ mli.

english: Why do insects attack and damage my crops much more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warm weather speeds up the breeding cycle of pests, causing their populations to explode quickly. In contrast, heavy rains during the wet season naturally wash insects off plants and destroy their eggs.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ gbalashihilɛ mli oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛyibɔ ​​tee hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ enɛ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ kooloi bibii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ amɛwuji.

english: Why does my cabbage plant collapse and wilt during the afternoon even when the ground around it is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi moŋ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Midday wilting in wet soil usually means harmful soil fungi or pests have damaged the plant's roots, stopping them from pumping enough water up to keep pace with the heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛpomp nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛye dɔlɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I buy cassava stems from the market, why do some produce very big tubers while others produce small ones under the same care?
ga: Kɛji mihe ŋmei kɛjɛ jara nɔ Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji waa lɛ? Tsei komɛi woɔ bulb bibii kɛ hiɛdɔɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Different cassava varieties naturally have different genetic strengths. Some varieties are specifically bred for high tuber production or disease resistance, while others are older local strains. Using certified, high-yielding stem varieties gives you a more predictable and uniform yield.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Amɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛi srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Atsɔse henɔi komɛi pɔtɛɛ koni amɛfee snobby loo helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe. yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni eda. Kɛ okɛ stem henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii ni yaa nɔ daa ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba.

english: How do I choose the best maize variety to plant when there are so many types sold in the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu? Be mli ni nibii babaoo yɔɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Your choice should depend on the rainfall pattern in your area. Short-duration maize varieties are best for areas with short rainy seasons because they mature fast, while long-duration varieties are better for regions with long, heavy rains to maximize yield.
ga: Esa akɛ nɔ ni obaahala lɛ adamɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Abele henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ koni aná yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some types of pepper plants survive long dry seasons while other types die off quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Certain pepper varieties have deeper root systems and leaf features that retain moisture better during drought. Selecting drought-tolerant varieties helps ensure your crop survives extended dry spells in Ghana.
ga: Pepper henɔi komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni ooohala lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ amli.

english: Why can't I just save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next season instead of buying new ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui heei

english: Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for maximum yield in their first generation. If you plant saved seeds from that harvest, the next generation loses its strength, resulting in unequal plant sizes, weaker crops, and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafite hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ adalɛi lɛ jeee ekome. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: Why do my tomato plants perform poorly when I plant them on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or beans resets soil nutrients and breaks the cycle of soil diseases.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake tomato. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: I planted all my pepper seeds on the same day, so why are some growing fast while others haven't even sprouted yet?
ga: Miduɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi po ekwɛko lolo lɛ?

english: Seeds sprout unevenly due to small differences in planting depth, soil moisture, or seed quality. Keeping your seedbed uniformly moist and planting at a consistent shallow depth encourages all seeds to sprout around the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ bɔ ni adu lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ yɛ srɔto fioo Dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ he lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ daa lɛ woɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees keep producing pods for many years while my maize dies completely after just one harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kwraa yɛ kpamɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is an annual crop designed by nature to finish its entire lifecycle in one season. Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that builds a strong root and trunk structure to continually produce fruit for decades if properly maintained.
ga: Abɛi ji afi ŋmɔshi nibii ni adebɔɔ fee koni egbe esɛɛkuu lɛ fɛɛ naa yɛ be kome mli. Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni woɔ shishifã kɛ shishifã ni mli wa koni eya nɔ ewo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain tree grow small shoot 'children' around its base, and should I let all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ‘bɔɔlu’ bibii ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ maha amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Plantain trees produce suckers to naturally multiply. Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main mother plant for nutrients; removing extra suckers and keeping only 2 or 3 strong ones ensures bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii kɛha adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛkɛ tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ajie ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi agbo aba.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant several seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to build a thick stem and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newer top leaves to survive, indicating that you need to apply nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he.

english: Is it better for my farm if I burn the weeds after clearing, or should I leave them on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mishã jwɛi lɛ beni mijie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ loo esa akɛ mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cut weeds on the ground as mulch protects your soil from drying out under the hot sun and slowly decomposes into organic food for your crops. Burning destroys valuable soil nutrients and leaves the ground bare and dry.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaabu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni fiofio lɛ ebaafite ni etsɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ gbiŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and crack easily just a few days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil turns hard and dry when it lacks organic matter like compost or decayed plant material. Adding animal manure or crop residues helps the soil act like a sponge, holding moisture much longer after it rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbiɔ kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ. Koolooi amli ŋmeii loo tsei amli ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Ehiɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: How deep should I put my maize seeds into the ground when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: You should plant maize seeds about two to three centimeters deep, which is roughly the length of your thumb tip to the first knuckle. Planting too deep prevents the seed from coming up, while planting too shallow lets birds eat it or rain wash it away.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 2-3, ni ji aaafee ŋmãa lɛ naa kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi aye amɛ loo nugbɔ baaho dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava and maize very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. Giving proper distance allows both crops to grow big and produce high yields.
ga: Kɛ́ abua tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green growth. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure will feed the plants and turn them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔ nii lɛ amli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The best time is two to three weeks after planting, once the seeds have sprouted and formed strong roots, and only when the soil is moist. Applying fertilizer to dry soil or too early can burn the young roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa Ni beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni egbi tsɔ loo oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with tiny white insects underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The leaf curling is caused by tiny pests called whiteflies that suck sap from the plant and spread diseases. Spraying your crops with neem leaf water or a safe crop spray helps control them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai srɔtoi eshwãa Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why am I supposed to remove the bottom leaves of my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Removing the lower leaves keeps them from touching the wet soil, which stops fungal diseases from splashing onto the plant during rain. It also lets fresh air flow through the plant to keep it healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii helai akashwie tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme sun, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo tsei niyenii ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so fast after I put them in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they get wounded during harvest or are stored in warm, damp places. Storing undamaged yams in a shaded, well-ventilated barn off the ground on wooden racks keeps them dry and preserves them.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji amɛpila yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛgbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have a special relationship with natural helpers in the soil that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the legume crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, providing free plant food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ suɔmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛha adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa yɛ sũ mli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nitrogen ni ato lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ eji tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-corn feed ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to put fertilizer right against the main stem of my young crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer acts like strong salt. If it touches the tender stem directly, it draws moisture out of the plant and burns its outer skin, which can stunt or kill the crop instead of feeding it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo ni mli edɔ. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ Ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli ni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ ashã. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛgboi yɛ niyenii najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants looking like someone shot tiny holes right through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tamɔ mɔ ko ni etswa bu bibii kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and chew through the soft, rolled-up leaves. As the leaf grows and unfolds, those chews turn into rows of visible holes.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwieɔ baai bibii ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ Beni baai lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Nakai ŋmɔlɔi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Very small insects like whiteflies or thrips suck the sap from the leaves and spread a virus into the plant. This virus damages the plant's leaf cells, causing them to twist upward and preventing the crop from absorbing sunlight properly.
ga: Kplukai bibii waa tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ fiteɔ tso baa mli wala yibii. Enɛ haa baa mli wala yibii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes or garden eggs on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato loo ŋmeii yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests and soil diseases that feed specifically on tomatoes stay behind in the soil after harvest. If you plant tomatoes there again, those waiting pests will immediately attack the new crop; changing to a crop like corn starves those pests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tomato tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu tomato yɛ jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ Nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miimɛ lɛ baatutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of big leaves but give me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in soil rich in leafy food, it sends all its energy upward to make leaves instead of sending energy downward into the roots to swell the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, Etsuɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee ŋmei. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e ha nɛ tsɔwi ɔmɛ nɛ a bli.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: The mother plantain tree has to share water and food with every small shoot around it. By removing the extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones, all the nourishment goes into growing a bigger, heavier bunch of fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ kɛ tsei bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ aja enu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashiɔ niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ baaha aduawai lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee shwiili.

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the damp ground so they can catch more sunlight to make food. It also keeps the leaves dry, which prevents rotting diseases from taking over the crop.
ga: Staking jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhoo nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ hu ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni fiteɔ lɛ akaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: When water becomes scarce in the dry season, the cocoa tree drops its outer leaves on purpose to reduce water loss through evaporation, allowing the trunk and roots to survive until the rains return.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ kponɔgbɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits when the heat gets very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the sticky pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from being naturally fertilized. When fertilization fails, the plant sheds the flower to save its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfɔ bii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ baaja amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow root systems and cannot reach deep underground water. During the dry season, intense heat causes leaves to lose moisture quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains and putting dry leaves around the base (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛ baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ (mulch) lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn brown and shrivel up when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ? Ni eji nɔ bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: When small cocoa pods shrivel and dry up, it is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree naturally sheds pods it cannot feed due to lack of nutrients, or because insects like capsids have bitten the young pods.
ga: Kɛji kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwie shi ni amɛgbi lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ‘cherel wilt’, ni baa beni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni nyɛɛɛ aye nii yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ hewɔ. aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ hewɔ

english: Why is it important to cut away extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or weak branches so sunlight and air can circulate freely through the farm. This reduces moisture that causes fungal diseases and helps the tree send its nutrients directly to producing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ mli.

english: How can I prevent black pod disease from destroying my cocoa harvest when heavy rains start?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ black pod hela lɛ naa koni ekafite kookoo feemɔ beni nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, dark conditions. You can protect your farm by picking ripe pods quickly, removing infected pods from the trees, clearing weeds, and applying approved fungicides before the heavy rains begin.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ooobua naa oya lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ tsei amli ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛhaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my maize leaves to develop long, light-colored streaks?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ ahe baa lɛ miifee ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Light streaks on maize leaves are usually caused by Maize Streak Virus, which is spread by leafhopper insects, or by a lack of nutrients in the soil. Using improved seed varieties and applying appropriate fertilizer helps crops stay green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Maize Streak Virus, ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baa lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to apply fertilizer so it doesn't wash away from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akashwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist but not soaking wet, usually shortly after the rainy season starts when plants are actively growing. Applying fertilizer during heavy downpours washes the nutrients away before roots can drink them.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ feɔ be kukuoo ko. Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ, ni ji be mli ni tsei miida lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ amɛ.

english: What is the benefit of planting beans or groundnuts on the same land as my main crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii titri yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ he?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that enriches the ground for other crops while giving you an additional harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa anáa nibii krokomɛi hu.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit compared to other farms in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Slow plantain growth usually happens when the soil lacks nutrients, when too many suckers are competing around one mother plant, or when microscopic worms (nematodes) attack the roots. Removing extra suckers allows the main plant to get full nourishment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain ni daa blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmeii babaoo fa tsɔ ni miitswa akaŋ kɛha tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ, loo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii (Nematodes) tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: How can I keep insects from eating my harvested maize and beans while in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moisture inside stored grains. To protect your crop, dry the grains thoroughly in the sun until they are hard, and store them in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) or clean containers that prevent insects and air from entering.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. koni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni okɛto kotoku ko ni vacuum tsiɔ mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo nɔ ko ni mli tse mli koni kooloi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a cry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves. When the soil lacks nitrogen or when heavy rain washes it away, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed the new growth, turning the bottom leaves yellow first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ biɔ nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oootsɔ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are naturally forest plants that burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Without tall trees or plantains to provide shade, the hot sun dries out the leaves faster than the young roots can draw water from the soil, causing the seedlings to overheat and wither.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ji koo mli tsei ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the leaves of my young maize and leaving small dark droppings inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni etse ehe yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That is the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that loves to hide in the tender center leaves of maize plants. They feed during cooler parts of the day and hide deep inside the plant where rain and birds cannot easily reach them, leaving behind hole damage and powdery waste.
ga: No ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmei tsei ahe baai bibii amli lɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ekɛ ehe tee tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ Nugbɔ kɛ okpoi nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe mlɛo. Eshiɔ bu kɛ sũ ni efite yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before I even dig them up for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifolɔ amɛ po koni mikɛkpa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when the soil holds too much water and lacks air, usually from heavy rains on poorly drained soil or fungal diseases. The waterlogged soil suffocates the roots, allowing soil fungi to enter and break down the cassava tubers into mush.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ loo ŋmeii hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ gbálaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops fail to grow well if I plant maize on the exact same patch of land for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil without giving it time to recover. It also creates a permanent home for pests and soil diseases that target maize, making each new harvest weaker than the last.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ hu feɔ shia ni hiɔ shi daa. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ hee fɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ he waaa fe naagbee nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce much bigger tubers when I give them tall wooden poles to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwereɔ bulbs wuji babaoo beni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ha amɛ lɛ? Ha amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines store energy in their underground tubers through sunlight caught by their leaves. When they climb tall poles, the leaves spread out widely in the light instead of clumping on the damp ground where they catch diseases and stay shaded.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni tswaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Beni amɛkwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã la lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakpɛtɛ amɛhe yɛ kui amli yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Biɛ ji he ni amɛbaaná hela ni amɛha hulutsoo.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds die in the soil even after I planted them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The first rain of the season is often a temporary shower that quickly dries out under the hot sun. If seeds absorb that initial moisture and start sprouting, they will dry out and die as soon as the topsoil bakes before the true, steady rainy season sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwu lɛ ŋɔ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni ebɔi shweremɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛ, dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni ebaa daa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or uneven watering. When daytime temperatures get too high, the pollen inside the flower dies before it can fertilize the plant, causing the flower to dry up and snap off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛgbiɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ dani enyɛɔ ehaa tso lɛ shwereɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in between my maize help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of crops that have tiny soil organisms living in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and feed it into the earth. As they grow, they naturally enrich the soil around them, sharing natural fertilizer with nearby crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei ni yɔɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛbaawo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli hewalɛ. Amɛji adebɔɔ mli nibii. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jaa nɔ.

english: Why is a small plant with purple flowers causing my maize nearby to turn pale and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Minɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpa dalɛ?

english: That purple-flowered plant is Striga, also known as witchweed, which is a parasitic weed. Its roots attach directly to the roots of your maize underground and steal the water and food right out of the maize plant before it can use them to grow.
ga: Tso ni yɔɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed, ni ji jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant too many seeds close together in one area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Why do I need to make raised soil mounds before planting seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Raised mounds loosen the soil so that yam tubers can easily expand underground, while also preventing roots from rotting due to standing water during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Select mature stems from healthy, high-yielding plants that are 8 to 18 months old, using cuttings taken from the middle portion of the stem rather than the soft top or woody bottom.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ amli, ni okɛ tsei ni afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ hɛ mi nɛ ngɛ blɛoo loo e sisi nɛ a kɛ tso pee.

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, which restores fertility for future crops without needing extra fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my growing maize crops turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to grow green leaves, or that waterlogged soil is preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of covering the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ mulching he Mɛni ji miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, holds moisture in the ground, stops weeds from taking over, and cools the soil under hot sunshine.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ masɛi?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa plant's first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ cacao tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning rather than at mid-day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Watering in the morning allows the soil and plant roots to absorb moisture before the strong afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate into the air.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants have small holes that look like ragged tears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? No tamɔ yaafo ni ekumɔ?

english: Small holes in young leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the funnel of the plant and eat the tender leaves before they fully open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or suffer from irregular watering while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛnaa nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight. They require temporary shade plants, like plantains or bananas, planted alongside them to act as umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and soft before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp conditions. Keeping your farm weeded and pruning excess tree foliage helps air flow through and keeps the pods dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is lacking nutrients for my crops to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?
